> R7.3 / OBL-DEP-1 / E12 question.**

> checksum-verified bincode 1.3.3 / serde 1.0.228 sources (no new retrieval). No build, test, node
> run, malformed-input execution, downloaded-code execution, probe, or operational-secret access.

## 0. Carried A42.1 qualifications (applied here, no separate pass)

- **Conditional capacity needs *both* grant and growth assumptions.** A `with_capacity(n)` **request**
  does not equal an `n`-byte actual-capacity ceiling: the initial allocation grant may round up, and
  later `push` growth may exceed it. Any capacity bound below is stated conditionally on **both**.
- **Pinned std/allocator source can answer implementation questions** (not automatically
  execution-only); **observed RSS** remains a runtime question.
- **`Vec<u8>` growth / `String::from_utf8`:** `from_utf8` *consumes* its `Vec` (no second buffer);
  reallocation during `push` growth may occur **in place or by move**, so old/new buffer overlap is a
  **possibility, not a universal event**. (No `String` appears in the Timeout schema; the point
  applies to the `signature: Vec<u8>` growth path.)

## 1. Admission ordering and effective options

Two inbound call sites in `binary_consensus_loop.rs`, both with the constant
`MAX_INBOUND_TIMEOUT_FRAME_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (= 64 KiB, `:309`):

| Arm | Decode | Guard order | Effective options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Timeout** | `:6988–6991` `deserialize::<TimeoutMsg<[u8;32]>>(&bytes)` | explicit `bytes.len() > 64 KiB → drop` precheck (`:6975–6987`); **sender binding `bind_sender` runs AFTER decode** (`:7001`); `drop(bytes)` on success (`:6996`) | `bincode::options()` (DefaultOptions) `.with_limit(64 KiB)` `.with_fixint_encoding()` |
| **NewView** | `:7197–7200` `deserialize::<TimeoutCertificate<[u8;32]>>(&bytes)` | transport-origin admission `gate.authorize_origin(origin)` runs **BEFORE decode** (`:7158–7170`); explicit `bytes.len() > 64 KiB → drop` precheck (`:7183–7196`); `drop(bytes)` on success (`:7206`) | same |

**Preserved R7 result:** the **explicit `bytes.len() > 64*1024` prechecks enforce the input cap**;
`with_limit(64 KiB)` is a **bytes-read counter limit, not a heap budget** (it bounds total input
consumed, so a length prefix declaring more than can be read within 64 KiB errors when the counter is
exceeded — it does **not** cap the speculative `with_capacity`). **Effective options differ from the
outer free `deserialize`:** these use `options()` + `with_limit` + `with_fixint_encoding` with **no
`allow_trailing_bytes()`**, so DefaultOptions' default **rejects trailing bytes** (fixint, LE). The
outer free-function options are **not** transferred. Only the guards needed for decode exposure are
traced: Timeout's self-declared `validator_id` is bound to the authenticated origin **after** decode
(the decode allocation happens for any origin that reaches this arm); NewView's origin admission
**precedes** decode (an unauthorized origin cannot trigger the TC decode allocation). Downstream F5
signature verification, F7 high-QC admission, retention, and engine mutation are **out of scope**.

## 2. Actual instantiated schemas and minimum encoded sizes (fixint)

`ValidatorId(pub u64)` (`ids.rs:29`) → **8 B**. `QuorumCertificate<[u8;32]>` (`qc.rs:29–35`):
`block_id [u8;32]` (32 B inline) + `view u64` (8) + `signers Vec<ValidatorId>` (8-B `u64` len + 8·n) →
**min 48 B**, each signer **8 B**.

`TimeoutMsg<[u8;32]>` (`timeout.rs:72–84`): `view u64`(8) + `high_qc Option<QC>` (1-B tag; +≥48 if
`Some`) + `validator_id ValidatorId`(8) + `suite_id u8`(1) + `signature Vec<u8>` (8-B len + 1·m) →
**min 26 B** (high_qc None, empty signature); each signature byte **1 B**.

`TimeoutCertificate<[u8;32]>` (`timeout.rs:231–246`): `view u64`(8) + `high_qc Option<QC>`(1; +≥48) +
`signers Vec<ValidatorId>`(8 + 8·s) + `signed_timeouts Vec<TimeoutMsg>`(8 + Σ≥26) + `timeout_view
u64`(8) → **min 33 B** (all empty). Field order: view, high_qc, signers, signed_timeouts,
timeout_view.

**Logical vs authenticated certificate.** The decoded `QuorumCertificate<[u8;32]>` here is the
**logical/wire** type (a `signers: Vec<ValidatorId>` list + `block_id` + `view`); it is **not** an
authenticated/retained certificate — membership/quorum/signature checks are the separate downstream
F5/F7 and engine steps, not part of this decode.

**Zero-input elements — checked, none found.** Every reachable collection element has a nonzero
minimum encoded size: `QC.signers` element = 8 B; `TimeoutMsg.signature` element = 1 B; `TC.signers`
element = 8 B; `TC.signed_timeouts` element ≥ 26 B. So each collection's element count is ≤
`bytes_read_remaining / min_element`, and under the 64 KiB read cap the **total filled logical
content across all nested collections is O(64 KiB)**.

**Fixed Vec-nesting (not input-dependent).** Within a `TimeoutCertificate`: `TC.signers` (depth 1),
`TC.high_qc.signers` (depth 1, via `Option<QC>`), `TC.signed_timeouts` (depth 1), and within each
`signed_timeouts[i]`: `.high_qc.signers` (depth 2) and `.signature` (depth 2). Max Vec-nesting depth
= **2**, fixed by the schema. `TimeoutMsg` alone has max depth 1 (`high_qc.signers`, then
`signature`).

## 3. Simultaneously-live storage (per A42.1-C1: completed siblings persist)

bincode/serde decode fields and elements **sequentially**, so at any instant only the collections on
the **current active nesting path** hold an un-input-backed **speculative** `with_capacity` reservation
(each ≤ `min(declared, floor(1 MiB / size_of::<T>))`, i.e. **≤ 1 MiB of bytes regardless of element
layout**). Because `TC` field order decodes `high_qc` and `signers` **before** `signed_timeouts`, by
the time `signed_timeouts` is decoding, `TC.high_qc.signers` and `TC.signers` are **already complete**
(input-backed). Within `signed_timeouts`, exactly **one** `TimeoutMsg` is current, and within it
exactly **one** inner `Vec` is actively reserving at a time (`high_qc.signers` completes before
`signature` begins). Therefore the **concurrent speculative over-reservation** is at most:

- **TimeoutMsg decode:** 1 active inner `Vec` → **≤ 1 MiB** speculative, + O(P) backed.
- **TimeoutCertificate decode:** `TC.signed_timeouts` outer `Vec` (≤ 1 MiB) **+** the current
  `TimeoutMsg`'s one current inner `Vec` (≤ 1 MiB) → **≤ 2 MiB** concurrent speculative, + O(P) backed.

**But completed siblings persist (A42.1-C1).** Each **completed** `signed_timeouts[0..i]` and each
completed `QC.signers`/`signature` remains **live with its actual capacity (including spare from
growth)** for the life of the decoded value. These are **input-backed** (each required ≥ its nonzero
min input to fill; a sub-vector that cannot be filled aborts the whole decode), so their **total
content is O(P) ≤ O(64 KiB)**, but their **capacity** is conditional on the growth/allocator
assumptions (A42.1-C2). Inline `Vec`/`Option` headers inside a completed `TimeoutMsg`/`QC` struct are
already counted in that struct body — not double-counted.

## 4. Success and failure cases

| Case | Allocation behavior | Peak live (symbolic) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Oversized declared count, short input** | the Vec's cautious `with_capacity` (≤ 1 MiB bytes) is allocated **before** elements read; fill then hits the 64 KiB read-limit / slice end → **decode `Err`** | completed prior fields (O(P)) + the ≤ 1 MiB speculative reservation of the current collection (+ outer ≤ 1 MiB if inside `signed_timeouts`) |
| **Truncation inside a nested signer/signature `Vec`** | inner `Vec` reserves ≤ 1 MiB speculative, `next_element` fails on exhausted input → whole decode `Err` → entire partial value dropped | completed `signed_timeouts[0..i]` (O(P), backed) + TC earlier fields (O(P)) + ≤ 2 MiB concurrent speculative, then dropped |
| **Late failure after completed entries** | earlier allocations already performed; `Err` returns; Rust cleanup drops the partial `P2pMessage`/TC | same as above; **ordinary error cleanup does not establish immediate RSS reduction** (freed heap may be allocator-retained; RSS unmeasured) |
| **Valid, fully populated, ≤ 64 KiB** | all collections filled from real input (total content O(P) ≤ 64 KiB); no un-backed speculative remains at completion; success path runs **`drop(bytes)`** freeing the ≤ 64 KiB input buffer before downstream | O(P) backed content + capacities (conditional on growth) |
| **Trailing input** | DefaultOptions **rejects trailing bytes** (no `allow_trailing_bytes`) → a valid message followed by extra bytes → **decode `Err`** | whatever was allocated up to the trailing-byte detection, then dropped |

**Decode-work vs other costs (separated):** visitor work for one call is O(bytes read) ≤ O(64 KiB)
plus the per-collection allocation operations; this is **separate from** downstream cryptographic
verification (F5 signature checks, F7 high-QC admission), later retention, and runtime CPU cost, none
of which are counted here.

**Owned input buffer vs decode storage.** `bytes` is the already-owned encoded frame (≤ 64 KiB); the
decode borrows it as `&bytes` and creates **separate** owned structures. During decode both are live
(overlap); on **success** both arms explicitly `drop(bytes)` (`:6996`, `:7206`) to avoid overlapping
the encoded frame with the decoded working set; on **error** `bytes` and the partial value drop at
scope end.

## 5. Supported conclusion (R7.3 / E12 inner-decoder question)

For one `bincode::options().with_limit(64 KiB).with_fixint_encoding().deserialize::<T>(&bytes)` with
`T ∈ {TimeoutMsg<[u8;32]>, TimeoutCertificate<[u8;32]>}` and symbolic read-bounded input `P ≤ 64 KiB`:

- **Logical decoded contents:** **O(P) ≤ O(64 KiB)** — every nested collection element consumes a
  nonzero minimum of input (checked: ≥ 1 B for signatures, ≥ 8 B for signer ids, ≥ 26 B for inner
  timeouts); input is capped by the explicit precheck **and** the `with_limit` read counter.
- **Speculative initial reservation requests:** each active collection requests
  `min(declared, floor(1 MiB / size_of::<T>))` ≤ **1 MiB of bytes**; concurrent speculative requests
  are bounded by the active nesting path — **≤ 1 MiB (TimeoutMsg), ≤ 2 MiB (TimeoutCertificate)** — by
  field order and sequential element decode. This bound does **not** cover completed siblings.
- **Actual capacities:** ≥ contents; **conditional** on explicit initial-grant **and** growth
  assumptions (not pinned here); completed collections retain capacity incl. spare.
- **Allocator behavior / process RSS:** **not pinned / UNMEASURED**.

A single numerical peak is **not** invented and no growth multiplier is assumed. The source result is:
backed content O(≤ 64 KiB) + at most ~1–2 MiB concurrent un-backed speculative reservation (serde
cautious cap × active-path depth ≤ 2), with capacity/allocator/RSS terms explicitly conditional or
unmeasured — **sufficient to finish this bounded source review without execution**.

## 6. Disposition

Both inner schemas, the admission ordering (Timeout binds sender after decode; NewView admits origin
before decode), allocation lifetimes (speculative vs backed; completed siblings persist; success-path
`drop(bytes)`), the enumerated failure cases, and the supported symbolic accounting are documented.
**No genuinely unresolved source question remains** for this sub-boundary: the outer (A42/A42.1) and
inner (A43) decoder allocation/work reviews are both closed at the source level. Remaining residuals
are classified **separately**: actual container capacities (conditional on the std `Vec` growth
policy / allocator — a pinned-source implementation question, not covered here), and process RSS /
runtime CPU / liveness (**runtime, UNEXECUTED**).

The ≤ 1 MiB-per-collection serde cautious reservation is a **bounded** request (R7/E12 accounting
family); A43 does **not** mint a finding from it and infers **neither exhaustion nor safety**. This
does **not** close the broader **OBL-DEP-1 / E12** obligations (whole-node queues, concurrent
connections, aggregate memory) — explicitly out of scope. **A1-F3, A17-F1, A21-F1**, timeout
authentication, and consensus safety are **not** reopened; **A21-F1**'s hand-written
proposal-decoder identity (reservation before validation) remains separate from serde's bounded
post-length-prefix cautious reservation. **C5** remains **OPEN**; runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**.

> **Layer A42.1 — correction of A42's allocation accounting and disposition (internal v1.121).**
> Scope **Public DevNet**, pinned at HEAD `18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b` /
> root tree `5b6c543435ac017dd8372c93f48be397899db14a` / branch `claude/exciting-keller-a05rwc` /
> origin `https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND.git`. Read-only source audit. No build, test, node run,
> malformed-input execution, probe, or implementation. Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5** remains
> **OPEN**. All obligation identities, finding IDs, aliases, and original obligation definitions
> preserved; no global index rewrite. Superseded A42 statements are marked `[SUPERSEDED-A42 → A42.1-Cx]`.
> **No plan-file was written this pass.** This completes the bounded schema/visitor source review;
> A43 is **not** started and no completed decoder/crypto/transport investigation is reopened.

## Retained from A42 (supported, unchanged)

Exact dependency provenance (bincode 1.3.3, serde/serde_core/serde_derive 1.0.228, checksums verified
vs `Cargo.lock`); the generic `Vec<T>` seq visitor path including `Vec<u8>` (not `deserialize_bytes`);
`String`'s slice-availability check; the per-variant schema and minimum encoded sizes; **no
zero-input collection elements** (u8=1, u16=2, `RestoreCatchupBlock`=90, `PeerInfo`=41 bytes); **fixed
nesting depth ≤ 2**; discriminator validation **after** a full decode. The §0 A41 carry-forward
corrections also stand.

## C1 — Reservation requests vs total heap `[SUPERSEDED-A42 → A42.1-C1]`

**Exact initial capacity request.** For each `Vec<T>`, serde requests
`capacity = min(declared_count, floor(1 MiB / size_of::<T>()))` (`serde_core private/size_hint.rs:12–22`,
integer/floor division; `0` for a ZST element). This is a **request passed to `Vec::with_capacity`**,
distinct from the container's eventual capacity and from allocated memory.

**What the "at-most-two-active-collections" argument actually bounds — corrected.** A42 used the
fixed nesting depth (≤ 2) to assert "≤ 2 MiB un-backed overhead." That argument bounds **only the
concurrently *speculative initial reservation requests*** — at most two collections are mid-decode at
once (one outer + one current inner), so at most two un-input-backed initial `with_capacity` requests
(each ≤ 1 MiB) are outstanding **at the instant of a truncation**. It does **not** bound all spare
capacity, nor peak allocated memory: **completed inner collections remain live** — each completed
`RestoreCatchupBlock` pushed into the outer `Vec` still **owns its `qc_signer_indices` buffer**, and
each completed `PeerInfo` still owns its `address` `String`, **including any spare capacity** left by
growth. Those completed buffers are not "the current speculative request," so the ≤ 2 bound says
nothing about them; they accumulate for the life of the decoded message.

## C2 — Explicit separated accounting (replaces the unconditional peak-heap claim) `[SUPERSEDED-A42 → A42.1-C2]`

A42's single inequality `Peak ≤ C_backed·P + D·PREALLOC + allocator_overhead` is **withdrawn** as an
asserted peak-heap bound (it hid unknown growth/allocator terms inside one symbol and relied on the
unverified "~1.5–2× doubling" transient, also **withdrawn** — std `Vec`'s growth factor is
implementation-defined and not pinned by this source review). Replace it with layered accounting that
keeps four levels separate, for one `bincode::deserialize::<P2pMessage>(payload)` with symbolic
payload length `P`:

| Level | What it is | Bound (supported) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **(a) Logical decoded contents** | sum over all decoded elements of their logical in-memory size (e.g. `Vec<u16>` content = 2·count; `String` content = byte length; block/peer struct bodies) | **input-proportional: O(P)** — every retained logical byte required ≥ a proportional input byte (no zero-input element); this is the justified, preserved result |
| **(b) Source-level reservation requests** | the `with_capacity` requests serde issues | each active collection requests `min(declared, floor(1 MiB/size_of::<T>))`; **≤ 2 un-input-backed requests outstanding at once** (C1); completed collections' earlier requests already serviced |
| **(c) Actual container capacities** | `Vec`/`String` `capacity()` after growth, incl. completed buffers' spare capacity | `≥` their contents; **not pinned** without the `Vec`/`String` growth/reallocation policy; total-capacity asymptotic is **conditional** — *if* every container's capacity ≤ `c`·its content for some growth constant `c`, *then* total capacity `≤ c·O(P) + ≤2·(1 MiB)` initial speculative; `c` is **not** established here |
| **(d) Allocator allocation / retention** | allocator rounding, free-list retention after frees | **not pinned** (allocator-dependent) |
| **(e) Process RSS** | resident set | **UNMEASURED** |

Components to count (without double-counting): the **outer `Vec` buffer** (capacity ≥ its element
count); **completed inner buffers** (each completed block's `qc_signer_indices`, each completed peer's
`address` `String` — live, with spare capacity); the **current partial element** (its in-progress
inner collection's speculative reservation, ≤ 1 MiB); **`String` storage** of the current field;
**reallocation temporaries** during any `Vec`/`String` growth (old+new buffer briefly co-resident — a
transient whose factor is unpinned); and **error-path allocations** (see C3). Do **not** separately
re-count a block's/peer's inline `Vec`/`String` header bytes — those are already inside the outer
element's struct body counted in (a).

## C3 — String and late-failure wording `[SUPERSEDED-A42 → A42.1-C3]`

Replace A42's "allocates exactly `len` / cannot over-allocate" with the **supported** property: the
`SliceReader` **rejects a declared byte length that exceeds the remaining slice before copying**
(`get_byte_slice`: `len > self.slice.len()` → `Err(unexpected_eof)`, `bincode de/read.rs:47–54`), so a
`String`/byte field cannot consume a declared length that is not actually present. This bounds the
**copied length** by available input; it does **not** fix the resulting `String`/`Vec` **capacity**
(`to_vec()`/`from_utf8` may allocate capacity ≥ the copied length) nor the **allocator footprint**.

**Late failure.** A decode error can occur **after** earlier elements/fields of the same message have
already allocated (e.g. several completed blocks, then a truncated inner `Vec<u16>`). Those earlier
allocations were already performed; the final `Err` returns and the partially-built `P2pMessage` is
dropped (ordinary Rust cleanup frees the owned buffers at the language level). Ordinary error cleanup
does **not** establish immediate **RSS** reduction — freed heap may be retained by the allocator; RSS
is **unmeasured**.

## C4 — Known source cap vs missing deployment inputs `[SUPERSEDED-A42 → A42.1-C4]`

A42 treated the payload bound `P` as "a separate concern" as if unknown. Correct: there **is** a known
source-level ceiling on the enclosing transport frame — `MAX_TRANSPORT_CIPHERTEXT = 16 * 1024 * 1024`
(16 MiB) (`qbind-net/framed_io.rs:21`), enforced on the inbound read: `read_transport_frame` rejects
`len > MAX_TRANSPORT_CIPHERTEXT` with `InvalidData` **before** reading the ciphertext
(`framed_io.rs:109–122`). This is an established **source fact**, not a runtime-only unknown.

Bounding caveats (kept exact): this cap is on the **ciphertext** length. The bincode `payload` that
`decode_frame` feeds to `deserialize` is the **decrypted** inner frame's body (after AEAD removal and
the inner 5-byte `discriminator || len` prefix), so the two lengths are **related but not equal** —
`P` is bounded **above** by the ciphertext cap (plaintext ≤ ciphertext) but the exact
ciphertext→payload conversion (AEAD tag/nonce, inner framing) is **outside this bounded scope**. So
`P < 16 MiB` as a known upper bound, kept **symbolic** for exact-overhead purposes; the cap is **not**
equated with the bincode payload length and **not** with total heap. Target/layout/toolchain
(`size_of::<RestoreCatchupBlock>()`, `size_of::<PeerInfo>()`, `Vec` growth factor, allocator) remain
**assumptions or measurements requiring execution**, separate from this source fact.

## C5 — Disposition `[SUPERSEDED-A42 → A42.1-C5]`

R7.3 / E12 records an **accounting / evidence** question. A42 framed the ≤ 1 MiB serde cautious
reservation as "the same oversized-reservation family already tracked under R7/E12." Corrected: the
serde reservation is a **bounded, element-size-divided** initial request
(`min(declared, floor(1 MiB/size_of::<T>))`) and the accounting question **does not, by itself,
establish that it is an oversized-allocation vulnerability**. A42.1 does **not** mint a finding from
this reporting correction and infers **neither exhaustion nor safety**. **A21-F1 remains a separate,
preserved finding** — the *hand-written* proposal decoder that reserves **before** body/binding
validation is a distinct pattern from serde's bounded, post-length-prefix cautious reservation; the
two are not merged.

**Established vs conditional vs unmeasured (summary):**
- **Established source properties:** generic `Vec<T>` seq path (incl. `Vec<u8>`); cautious request
  `min(declared, floor(1 MiB/size_of::<T>))`; `String` slice-availability rejection before copy; no
  zero-input element; fixed nesting ≤ 2; ≤ 2 concurrent speculative reservations; discriminator check
  after decode; transport ciphertext cap 16 MiB; logical decoded contents O(P).
- **Conditional capacity bound:** total container capacity ≤ `c·O(P) + ≤2·1 MiB` **only under** an
  explicit `Vec`/`String` growth-factor assumption `c` (not pinned here).
- **Unmeasured:** actual allocator behavior, reallocation transients, peak RSS, and any
  exhaustion/liveness outcome — **UNEXECUTED**.

This is sufficient to finish the bounded schema/visitor source review. Broader **OBL-DEP-1 / E12**
obligations (inner payload decoders, aggregate/whole-node memory, runtime measurement) remain
**separate and open** and are **not** re-queued under generic wording. **C5** remains **OPEN**;
runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**.

> **Layer A42 — schema-specific allocation and decode-work accounting for one outer P2P message
> (internal v1.120); addresses the outstanding R7.3 / OBL-DEP-1 / E12 source question.**

> root tree `5b6c543435ac017dd8372c93f48be397899db14a` / branch `claude/exciting-keller-a05rwc` /
> origin `https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND.git`. Third-party **source** audit (read-only retrieval
> of exact crates.io archives authorized; unpacked under `/tmp/a40_crates`, **no downloaded code
> executed**, no malformed input run). No build/test/node run/probe/implementation. Runtime remains

## 0. Carried A41 corrections `[SUPERSEDED-A41 → A42-§0]`

1. **`zeroize_derive 1.4.3 ZeroizeOnDrop` mechanism stated precisely.** The `ZeroizeOnDrop` derive
   generates a `Drop` impl that brings `::zeroize::__internal::{AssertZeroize, AssertZeroizeOnDrop}`
   into scope and invokes **field-wise `zeroize_or_on_drop()`** (`zeroize_derive/src/lib.rs:100–113`,
   expansion `:573–581`) — **distinct** from the deprecated `#[zeroize(drop)]` path, which generates a
   direct `fn drop(){ self.zeroize() }` (`:44–66`). The supported conclusion is unchanged: each field
   of the decoded `fips204::PrivateKey` receives ordinary-`Drop` zeroization.
2. **Physical-lifetime wording withdrawn.** A41's table phrase "persists in the stack frame until
   overwritten" is **withdrawn**. The supported statement is: the repo-owned `sk_array: [u8; 2560]`
   has **no explicit source-level erasure** (no `zeroize`/`Drop`), and dropping a plain byte array is
   **not** zeroization; physical copies, storage location, and remanence are **unmeasured**. A41's
   closed decoded-key source question is **not** reopened.

## 1. The inspected boundary (one invocation)

`p2p_tcp.rs::decode_frame(frame: &[u8])` (`:177–202`):

```
if frame.len() < 5 { Err("frame too short") }                      // header guard
len = u32::from_be_bytes(frame[1..5]) as usize
if frame.len() < 5 + len { Err("frame truncated") }                // payload-present guard
payload = &frame[5..5+len]                                         // BORROWED slice of the owned frame
msg: P2pMessage = bincode::deserialize(payload)?                   // the decode under study
match (&msg, discriminator) { … }                                  // discriminator check AFTER decode
```

- The **input `payload` is a borrowed sub-slice of the already-owned `frame`** — the decode does
  **not** copy the input; it allocates new owned structures from it. The already-owned frame is kept
  separate from decode-created allocations (per scope).
- The 1-byte discriminator is validated **after** a full successful decode, so a discriminator-mismatch
  frame still pays the entire decode allocation/work before rejection.
- `len` (≤ u32) is bounded by `frame.len()` (the payload must be present), so the decode's input
  length `P = len` is capped by the transport frame size — a **separate transport-buffer concern**
  (excluded here). Inner Proposal/Vote/Timeout/NewView/DAG payload decoders, downstream queues,
  retained state, and connection aggregation are **out of scope**.

## 2. Provenance and effective decode options (verified)

`.crate` SHA-256 verified against `Cargo.lock` **before** reading: **bincode 1.3.3** (`b1f45e94…`),
**serde 1.0.228** (`9a8e94ea…`), **serde_core 1.0.228** (`41d385c7…`), **serde_derive 1.0.228**
(`d540f220…`). The free function used by `decode_frame` is:

```
pub fn deserialize<'a,T>(bytes) -> Result<T>  =
    DefaultOptions::new().with_fixint_encoding().allow_trailing_bytes().deserialize(bytes)
```
(`bincode/src/lib.rs:177–185`). Effective options: **fixint** (collection/seq lengths and `u64`/`u32`
are fixed-width; a `Vec`/`String` length prefix is an 8-byte `u64`), **little-endian**, byte
**limit = Infinite** (the free function sets none — consistent with R7.2–R7.3's established "slice
deserialize uses `Infinite`"). The 64 KiB Timeout/NewView prechecks (R7.2) are not on this outer
path (they guard the *inner* decoders). These are retained prior conclusions, **not** new findings.

## 3. Actual visitor paths (not assumed)

- **`Vec<T>` (incl. `Vec<u8>`)** uses the serde generic **seq** path, **not** `deserialize_bytes`:
  `Vec<T>::deserialize` → `deserialize_seq(VecVisitor)` (`serde_core de/impls.rs:1135–1176`);
  `VecVisitor::visit_seq` does `Vec::with_capacity(size_hint::cautious::<T>(seq.size_hint()))` then a
  `push` loop (`:1157–1168`). bincode `deserialize_seq` reads the `u64` length and yields exactly that
  many elements with `size_hint() == Some(len)` (`bincode de/mod.rs:344–351, 321–323`). Thus every
  `Vec<T>` performs a **cautious initial reservation** = `min(declared_len, 1 MiB / size_of::<T>())`
  (`serde_core private/size_hint.rs:12–22`, `MAX_PREALLOC_BYTES = 1 MiB`) **before** any element is
  read, then grows by `push` as elements decode.
- **`String`** (`PeerInfo.address`) uses `deserialize_string` → bincode `read_string` → `read_vec` →
  `get_byte_buffer(len)` → `SliceReader::get_byte_slice(len)` which **rejects `len > remaining`
  before any copy** (`bincode de/read.rs:47–54`), then `to_vec()` allocates exactly `len` bytes. So a
  `String` **cannot over-allocate** beyond bytes actually present in the slice — distinct from the
  `Vec<T>` seq path, which **can** over-reserve up to the 1 MiB cautious cap before consuming input.
- **Scalars / fixed arrays**: `u16`/`u32`/`u64` are fixint (2/4/8 B, inline); `NodeId([u8;32])`
  (`p2p.rs:75`) and the `[u8;32]` id fields decode as **exactly 32 fixed bytes, inline, no heap, no
  length prefix**; `Option<u64>` = 1 byte (None) or 9 bytes (Some).

## 4. Per-variant allocation / decode-work accounting

Encoding prefixes (fixint): outer `P2pMessage` tag `u32`=4 B; inner enum tag `u32`=4 B; each `Vec`
length `u64`=8 B. "Min element" = minimum encoded bytes to successfully decode one element.

| P2pMessage variant | Heap collections (nesting) | Min element bytes | Min full-message bytes | Over-reservable before truncation? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Consensus(Proposal/Vote/Timeout/NewView)(Vec<u8>)` | one `Vec<u8>` (depth 1) | u8 = **1 B** | 16 B (empty) | yes — cautious ≤ **1 MiB** |
| `Consensus(RestoreCatchupRequest)` | none (scalars + `[u8;32]`) | — | 50 B fixed | no |
| `Consensus(RestoreCatchupResponse)` | `Vec<RestoreCatchupBlock>` → per block `Vec<u16>` (depth 2) | block = **90 B**; `u16` = **2 B** | 59 B (0 blocks) | yes — outer + current inner, each cautious ≤ 1 MiB |
| `Dag(Batch/BatchAck/BatchCertificate/BatchRequest/BatchResponse){data: Vec<u8>}` | one `Vec<u8>` (depth 1) | u8 = **1 B** | 16 B (empty) | yes — cautious ≤ 1 MiB |
| `Control(Heartbeat){view:u64,timestamp_ms:u64}` | none | — | 24 B fixed | no |
| `Control(PeerExchangeRequest){max_peers:u32}` | none | — | 12 B fixed | no |
| `Control(PeerExchangeResponse){peers: Vec<PeerInfo>}` | `Vec<PeerInfo>` → per peer `String` (depth 2) | `PeerInfo` = **41 B** | 16 B (0 peers) | outer `Vec` cautious ≤ 1 MiB; inner `String` **not** over-reservable |

**Every reachable collection element consumes ≥1 input byte** (u8=1, u16=2, `RestoreCatchupBlock`=90,
`PeerInfo`=41). **No element consumes zero input bytes.** This is now *demonstrated* for the actual
types and the actual fixint options (R7.3 required demonstration, not assumption). Consequently the
decoded element **count** of any one collection is ≤ `remaining_input / min_element`, and the
**content** retained is `O(consumed input)`.

**Allocations before a truncated input is rejected.** For each in-progress `Vec<T>`, the cautious
`with_capacity` (≤ `min(declared, 1 MiB/size_of::<T>)`) is allocated **before** elements are read, so
up to ~1 MiB of un-backed capacity exists per in-progress collection at the instant of truncation.
`String`/byte reads do **not** over-allocate (availability-checked). A final decode error does **not**
undo allocations already performed, but on error the whole partially-built `P2pMessage` is dropped.

**Simultaneously live.** The outer `P2pMessage` has exactly **one** active variant, so one active
collection chain. Because the schema nesting depth is **fixed at ≤ 2** (never input-dependent), at
most **two** collections are "reserved but not yet input-backed" at once: the outer `Vec` capacity and
the single current inner collection (`Vec<u16>` or `String`). Completed elements already pushed into
the outer `Vec` are **input-backed** (each required ≥ its min element bytes of real input to complete;
a block/peer that cannot complete aborts the whole decode). Temporary owned copies (`String`,
`Vec<u8>`, block/peer structs) are distinct from the borrowed input slice.

## 5. Supported per-call bound

For one `bincode::deserialize::<P2pMessage>(payload)` with payload length `P` (`P ≤` transport frame
cap — a separate concern):

> **Peak live heap(one decode)  ≤  C_backed · P  +  D · PREALLOC  +  allocator_overhead**

- `C_backed · P` — content backed by actually-consumed input (`C_backed` a small constant ≥ 1 from
  struct padding / `size_of::<element>` vs encoded size; every retained byte required proportional
  input).
- `D · PREALLOC` — the un-backed cautious over-reservation: `D` = schema nesting depth **≤ 2 (fixed)**,
  `PREALLOC` = **1 MiB** (serde cautious cap). So the un-backed initial-reservation overhead is
  **≤ ~2 MiB per decode**, **not** multiplicative in `P` (no per-element amplification, because every
  element consumes ≥1 input byte and only the current in-progress collection at each of the ≤2 depths
  holds an un-backed reservation).
- `allocator_overhead` — allocator rounding, `Vec` growth transients (amortized doubling, transient
  ~1.5–2× during growth), peak RSS — **not pinned by source**.

**Assumptions / exact missing facts (named, not estimated):** the transport frame cap that bounds `P`
(transport-buffer scope, excluded); exact `size_of::<RestoreCatchupBlock>()` / `size_of::<PeerInfo>()`
(layout-dependent — sets the cautious cap divisor and `C_backed`, but each cap is ≤ 1 MiB regardless);
`Vec` reallocation/growth factor and allocator behavior; and peak RSS — all require layout pinning or
execution. A single numerical byte total therefore **cannot** be fixed here; the **structural** bound
above (`O(P)` backed + ≤ 2 MiB fixed-depth over-reservation) is the supported source result. No
source-answerable work is deferred to the runtime queue.

## 6. Disposition

**R7.3 outer-message decode question answered to the supported extent.** The outer `P2pMessage`
variants each decode into a **fixed-depth (≤ 2)** collection structure under `bincode 1.3.3` fixint /
Infinite-limit options and serde 1.0.228's cautious (≤ 1 MiB) seq reservation; **every reachable
collection element consumes ≥ 1 input byte** (demonstrated per type), `String`/byte reads are
availability-checked (no over-allocation), and the per-call peak live heap is bounded by
`O(P) + ≤2 MiB` un-backed over-reservation plus unpinned allocator/RSS terms. The discriminator check
occurs after decode, so decode cost is paid before a mismatch is rejected.

**Kept separate:** one-call decoded allocation/work (this layer) · subsequent handling/retention of a
decoded message · whole-node concurrency (many handlers/queues) · runtime memory/CPU outcomes
(**UNEXECUTED**). The ≤ 1 MiB cautious over-reservation per `Vec` is the **same oversized-reservation
family already tracked under R7 / E12**; A42 **refines** its schema-specific bound rather than
discovering a new defect — **no finding is minted or forced** (duplicate-checked: no independently
distinct, source-supported defect beyond the tracked reservation family). **A21-F1** (hand-written
proposal-allocation, an *inner* decoder) and **A17-F1** (catch-up state authentication) retain their
identities and are **not** reopened. This does **not** close **OBL-DEP-1 / E12** or the broader
resource audit; the inner payload decoders, aggregate/whole-node memory, and runtime measurement
remain open. **C5** remains **OPEN**; runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**.

## 0. Carried A40 corrections `[SUPERSEDED-A40 → A41-§0]`

1. **`getrandom_backend` removed from getrandom 0.2.16's unresolved-input list.** Verified: the string
   `getrandom_backend` does **not** appear anywhere in `getrandom 0.2.16/src/` — that custom-backend
   cfg selector belongs to getrandom **0.3.x**, not the pinned 0.2.16. A40's §4 inclusion of
   `getrandom_backend` among the unresolved build inputs is **withdrawn**. The genuine unresolved
   inputs remain: deployed **target triple**, the effective resolved **feature set**, build-time
   `RUSTFLAGS`, and the identity of the **compiled binary**.
2. **fips entry-point error propagation distinguished from getrandom OS-backend behavior.** The
   inspected Linux backend (`linux_android_with_fallback.rs`) is not a single syscall: it does
   `sys_fill_exact(dest, getrandom_syscall)` with a `use_file` (`/dev/urandom`) fallback when the
   syscall is unavailable (`:13–20`), and `sys_fill_exact` handles interrupted/partial reads. A40
   should not have flattened this to a bare syscall. The **supported** conclusion is unchanged and
   narrower: a **final** `OsRng::try_fill_bytes` error (after getrandom's own internal fallback/retry
   handling) propagates as `Err` to the fips entry points and then to QBIND, producing **no successful
   cryptographic output**. A40's completed API→RNG→failure-consumer review stays closed; randomness
   and platform analysis are **not** restarted.
3. **Proposal/Vote authorization cross-reference corrected.** A40 §0 cited **A19-F1** for "absent
   production Proposal/Vote authorization". That is wrong: A19-F1 is the **remote-signer-selector**
   finding and retains that identity. The actual prior admission evidence is the **production
   consensus-loop wiring** `proposal_vote_authority: None` (`main.rs:6148`) plus the admission
   contract that production proposal/vote signing consults **only** `proposal_vote_authority`, where
   `None` yields no authority (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:736–752, 918, 941–950`) — the Run-422
   proposal/vote admission established in the prior consensus-admission layers. A40 §0's substantive
   point (the `:4881`/`:5272` completion calls do not establish selected-binary invocation) stands on
   that evidence.

## 1. Provenance (verified)

Reused the A40 checksum-verified `fips204 0.4.6` archive, and retrieved the zeroization dependencies,
each `.crate` SHA-256 verified **against `Cargo.lock` before** reading:

| Package | Version | `.crate` SHA-256 (matches Cargo.lock) | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fips204` | 0.4.6 | `c9fb5a36…0b15` ✓ (A40) | defines `PrivateKey`, `SerDes`, derives |
| `zeroize` | 1.8.2 | `b97154e6…88d0` ✓ | `Zeroize`/`ZeroizeOnDrop` traits + array impls |
| `zeroize_derive` | 1.4.3 | `85a5b415…852e` ✓ | derive macros generating the `Drop` impl |

`fips204 0.4.6` depends on `zeroize` (manifest), and QBIND leaves `fips204` default features on
(A40). Source conclusions below are at the **package-source** level; effective build configuration
and deployed behavior are **not** asserted from a name or trait alone.

## 2. Dependency key-object erasure (the retained A17.1/A18 question) — RESOLVED at source level

`fips204::ml_dsa_44::PrivateKey` (**`types.rs:19–27`**):

```
#[derive(Clone, Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
pub struct PrivateKey<const K, const L> {
    pub(crate) rho: [u8; 32], cap_k: [u8; 32], tr: [u8; 64],
    s_1_hat_mont: [T; L], s_2_hat_mont: [T; K], t_0_hat_mont: [T; K],
}   // where  struct T([i32; 256])  also #[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]  (types.rs:52–54)
```

- `zeroize_derive 1.4.3` `ZeroizeOnDrop` generates `impl Drop { fn drop(&mut self){ … self.zeroize() } }`
  (`zeroize_derive/src/lib.rs:94–109`); the `Zeroize` derive zeroizes each field.
- `zeroize 1.8.2` implements `Zeroize for [Z; N]` (`src/lib.rs:369`) and `ZeroizeOnDrop for [Z; N]`
  (`:379`), so the `[T; L]`/`[T; K]` arrays zeroize element-wise and each `T([i32;256])` zeroizes its
  256 `i32`s.

**Evidenced source disposition:** the dependency-owned decoded `PrivateKey` object **is overwritten
on ordinary `Drop`** — every secret-bearing field (`rho`, `cap_k`, `tr`, `s_1`/`s_2`/`t_0` hat_mont
arrays) is zeroized when the object leaves scope, including the post-construction `?`-return error
paths. This resolves the "uninspected/dependency-owned" status A39.1-C3(4) left open: the decoded
key object has a real source-level erasure mechanism. (`zeroize` uses volatile writes + a compiler
fence; A41 does not test actual memory remanence — see §4.)

## 3. Ownership chains for the three wrappers

`try_from_bytes(sk: [u8; SK_LEN]) → expand_private(ETA, &sk) → PrivateKey` (`fips204 lib.rs:421–424`)
takes the serialized array **by value**; `[u8; 2560]` is `Copy`, so the wrapper's `sk_array` is
**bit-copied** into the dependency. The three QBIND wrappers (`ml_dsa44.rs`) are structurally
identical in secret handling:

| Wrapper | sk→sk_array copy | PrivateKey construction | explicit erasure of repo copy? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `derive_public_key` | `:362` | `:366` → `get_public_key()` `:370` | **none** |
| `sign` (allocating) | `:420` | `:424` → `try_sign` `:428` | **none** |
| `sign_into` (caller-buffer, library/test-only per A39.1) | `:497` | `:500` → `try_sign` `:505` | **none** |

The three wrappers import `zeroize` only for the `ValidatorSigningKey` derive (`:32`, `:181`); **no
wrapper calls `.zeroize()` or `drop()` on `sk_array`** on any path.

## 4. Ownership / erasure table

`object → creation/copy/move → owner → erasure mechanism → paths covered → limitation`

| Object | Creation / copy / move | Owner | Erasure mechanism | Paths covered | Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Original secret bytes** `sk: &[u8]` | borrowed (no copy by the wrapper) | the **caller**. Via `ValidatorSigningKey` (`ml_dsa44.rs:181` `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]`, `bytes: Vec<u8>`) the owner is erased on its own drop; a raw `Vec`/slice passed to the static methods depends on that owner | `ValidatorSigningKey::Drop` → `bytes` zeroized (owner-dependent) | owner's own drop | not erased by these wrappers; a non-`ValidatorSigningKey` caller has no guarantee here |
| **Repo-owned `sk_array: [u8; 2560]`** | `sk.try_into()` copies the secret bytes into a fixed array | wrapper stack frame | **NONE** (plain `[u8;N]`, no `Drop`, no explicit `zeroize`) | **none** — not erased on success or returned-error | persists in the stack frame until overwritten; also `Copy`-duplicated into `try_from_bytes`. **Repo-owned gap** → maps to A10-F1/E18 |
| **Dependency deserialization input** `sk: [u8; SK_LEN]` (the by-value `try_from_bytes` parameter) | bit-copy of `sk_array` | dependency fn frame | **NONE** (plain array; `expand_private(&sk)` borrows, returns; dropped as no-op) | none | dependency-owned transient copy of the full serialized secret, **not** zeroized |
| **Decoded `PrivateKey` (`secret_key`)** | built by `expand_private` from `&sk` | wrapper local | **`ZeroizeOnDrop` → `Drop` zeroizes all fields** (§2) | ordinary scope-end drop on success **and** post-construction error returns | does not erase the serialized copies above or earlier keystore intermediates; process `exit()`/`abort` would skip `Drop` (not asserted to occur) |
| **Derived `PublicKey`** (`derive_public_key`) | `get_public_key()` | wrapper local → returned bytes | `ZeroizeOnDrop` on the struct; returned bytes are **public** | n/a | public material, not a secret-erasure concern |
| **Signature** (`sign`/`sign_into`) | `try_sign` result | returned / copied into `out` | n/a | n/a | not secret |

**Distinctions held separate (per the stated discipline):**
- **Source-level copying vs physical copies:** the table records source-level moves/copies
  (`sk→sk_array`, `sk_array→try_from_bytes`); A41 does **not** claim a specific number of physical
  memory copies (compiler elision, register/stack spills unknown).
- **Ownership transfer vs zeroization:** `try_from_bytes` taking `sk` by value is a copy/transfer,
  **not** an erasure of the source array.
- **Ordinary Drop vs skip-destructor paths:** `PrivateKey::Drop` runs on ordinary function return;
  `std::process::exit`/`panic=abort` elsewhere would skip it — not asserted to happen here.
- **Erasing one owner vs earlier copies:** the `PrivateKey` `ZeroizeOnDrop` erases the **structured
  object only**; it does **not** reach the repo-owned `sk_array`, the by-value `try_from_bytes`
  serialized copy, or keystore-stage intermediates.
- **Library/compiler guarantee vs observed remanence:** `ZeroizeOnDrop` is a source/library
  guarantee; A41 makes **no** claim about observed memory remanence, residual-secret lifetime,
  exploitability, or extraction.

## 5. Disposition

**Resolved (evidenced source disposition):** the retained dependency-owned key-object erasure
question is answered — `fips204 0.4.6 PrivateKey` carries `Zeroize + ZeroizeOnDrop` (verified against
`zeroize 1.8.2` / `zeroize_derive 1.4.3`, checksums matched), so the decoded private-key **object** is
zeroized on ordinary `Drop`. A **protected dependency object does not** protect the repository-owned
`sk_array` (no erasure mechanism in the wrapper), the by-value serialized `try_from_bytes` input copy,
or earlier keystore intermediates.

**Mapping.** The repo-owned `sk_array` non-erasure is an existing-family secret-handling
sub-observation under **A10-F1 / E18** (repo-owned key-material lifetime), **not** a new finding
(duplicate-checked: same in-memory-secret-lifetime gap family already tracked; no independently
distinct defect is asserted). Encrypted-format provisioning (OBL-KEY-1b writer, A26) stays **separate
and unchanged**; obligation properties are not reassigned.

**What this does NOT close.** The positive `PrivateKey` destructor result does **not** close **A10-F1**,
**E18**'s runtime obligations, or **C5**. Only the specific A39.1-C3(4) sub-observation (the
`fips204::PrivateKey` erasure status, previously "uninspected") is updated to "ZeroizeOnDrop at source
level". Secret erasure as a **runtime/memory** property remains **UNEXECUTED** — no memory test is

## 0. Carried A39.1 corrections `[SUPERSEDED-A39.1 → A40-§0]`

These corrections do **not** reopen the consensus/journal audit.

## 1. Exact dependency provenance (verified)

Retrieved the exact crates.io package archives and verified each SHA-256 **against `Cargo.lock`
before** reading contents (strong provenance — package archive, not a git tag or rendered source,
and not a deployed binary):

| Package | Version | `.crate` SHA-256 (matches Cargo.lock) | Randomness deps (from its manifest) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fips204` | 0.4.6 | `c9fb5a36…0b15` ✓ | `rand_core 0.6.4`, sha2, sha3, zeroize |
| `fips203` | 0.4.3 | `c8bdb645…a280` ✓ | `rand_core 0.6.4`, sha3, subtle, zeroize |
| `rand_core` | 0.6.4 | `ec0be479…6922e` ✓ | `getrandom 0.2.16` (via its `getrandom` feature) |
| `getrandom` | 0.2.16 | `335ff9f1…8592` ✓ | cfg-if, libc, wasi |

**Feature configuration (from the package manifests).** Both fips crates declare
`default = ["default-rng", …]` and `default-rng = ["rand_core/getrandom"]`
(`fips204 Cargo.toml:111–117`, `fips203 Cargo.toml:42–48`). QBIND declares `fips204 = "0.4"` /
`fips203 = "0.4"` with **no `default-features = false`**, so **`default-rng` is enabled**, which
turns on `rand_core`'s `getrandom` feature (making `rand_core::OsRng` available). QBIND declares
**no** direct `rand_core`/`getrandom` dependency and sets **no** getrandom feature (`js`/`custom`/
`rdrand`/`linux_disable_fallback`), **no** `getrandom_backend` cfg, and **no** `.cargo/config`
RUSTFLAGS (verified in-tree). The chain is identical for both primitives:
**fips20x → rand_core 0.6.4 → getrandom 0.2.16** (not getrandom 0.3.4, which is resolved for an
unrelated crate elsewhere in the tree).

## 2–3. Four operations: API → RNG → randomness request → failure consumer

For each, the QBIND wrapper boundary (already reviewed A39/A39.1) hands off to the dependency entry
point below. Every randomness request on the production path uses the **fallible** `try_fill_bytes`
interface, which returns `Result`; the deterministic internal routine runs **only after** the random
bytes are obtained, so **no operation can return a successful cryptographic result after a failed
randomness request**.

| # | QBIND call | Dependency entry → delegate | RNG type & request | Fallible? | Failure translation | Determinism note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `MlDsa44Backend::generate_keypair` → `ml_dsa_44::try_keygen()` | `traits.rs:44 try_keygen()` → `try_keygen_with_rng(&mut OsRng)` → `KG::try_keygen_with_rng` (`lib.rs:241`) → `ml_dsa::key_gen(rng, ETA)` (`ml_dsa.rs:33`) | `rand_core::OsRng`; one 32-byte `xi` via `rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut xi)` (`ml_dsa.rs:41`) | **Yes** | `.map_err(\|_\| "KeyGen: Random number generator failed")?` → QBIND `ConsensusSigError::Other` | `key_gen_internal(eta,&xi)` deterministically **expands the random `xi`** (`ml_dsa.rs:44`) — standard FIPS-204, **not** a fixed-seed fallback |
| 2 | `MlDsa44Backend::sign`/`sign_into` → `PrivateKey::try_sign(msg,&[])` | `traits.rs:156 try_sign()` → `try_sign_with_rng(&mut OsRng, msg, ctx)` (`lib.rs:268`) | `OsRng`; one 32-byte `rnd` via `rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut rnd)` (`lib.rs:283`) | **Yes** | `.map_err(\|_\| "ML-DSA.Sign: random number generator failed")?` → QBIND `ConsensusSigError::Other` / `BoundedMlDsa44SignError::BackendFailed` | hedged signing: `sign_internal(…, rnd, false)` runs after `rnd` filled; the deterministic-signing variant (rnd={0}^32) and `try_sign_with_seed`/`DummyRng` are **separate APIs QBIND does not call** |
| 3 | `MlKem768Backend::generate_keypair` → `ml_kem_768::KG::try_keygen()` | `traits.rs:54 try_keygen()` → `try_keygen_with_rng(&mut OsRng)` → `ml_kem_key_gen(rng,…)` (`ml_kem.rs:150`) | `OsRng`; two 32-byte values `d`,`z` via `rng.try_fill_bytes` (`ml_kem.rs:158,162`) | **Yes** | `.map_err(\|_\| "Alg 19: Random number generator failed for d/z")?` → QBIND `CryptoError::InternalError` | `ml_kem_key_gen_internal(d,z,…)` deterministically expands random `d,z` (`ml_kem.rs:170`); `keygen_from_seed` is a separate unused API |
| 4 | `MlKem768Backend::encaps` → `EncapsKey::try_encaps()` | `traits.rs:213 try_encaps()` → `try_encaps_with_rng(&mut OsRng)` (`lib.rs:206`) → `ml_kem_encaps(rng,…)` (`ml_kem.rs:226`) | `OsRng`; one 32-byte message `m` via `rng.try_fill_bytes` (`ml_kem.rs:226`) | **Yes** | `.map_err(\|_\| "Alg 20: random number generator failed")?` → QBIND `CryptoError::InternalError` | — |

**RNG interface — fallible vs infallible (source-established).** `rand_core 0.6.4 OsRng`
(`os.rs:65–71`): `try_fill_bytes(dest) → getrandom(dest)?; Ok(())` (**fallible**, maps error to
`rand_core::Error`), whereas `fill_bytes(dest)` **panics** on error (`os.rs:61–64`). **All four
operations call `try_fill_bytes`**, never `fill_bytes`; a getrandom failure therefore propagates as
`Err` to QBIND and **does not** reach the panicking interface. (A40 does not assert dependency
panic-freedom in general — it establishes that the inspected randomness requests use the fallible
path; it does not inspect every internal `.unwrap()`. The one `rng.try_fill_bytes(…).unwrap()` found
in `fips203 k_pke.rs:287` is inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, not the production keygen path, whose
`k_pke_key_gen` "no longer relies on rng".)

**Boundary back to QBIND.** Each dependency `Err(&'static str)` is mapped by the already-reviewed
QBIND wrappers (A39/A39.1) to a typed error; for `sign_into` the caller's output buffer is left
unchanged on a returned error. No fallback RNG, retry, or value substitution exists **in the
dependency entry points**; QBIND-side fallback was already found absent on the inspected chains.

## 4. Platform / build bounding of getrandom 0.2.16

Backend is selected by target triple in `getrandom 0.2.16 src/lib.rs:237+` (`cfg_if!`). The public
`getrandom(dest) -> Result<(), Error>` (`lib.rs:370`) is **fallible** on every target.

- **Conditional source conclusion (server targets):** on a **Linux** target with
  `target_arch ∈ {x86_64, aarch64, arm, powerpc, powerpc64, s390x, x86}` or `target_env = musl`, and
  with the default `linux_disable_fallback` *off* (QBIND sets no such feature), the selected backend
  is **`linux_android_with_fallback`** (`lib.rs:261–304`): the `getrandom(2)` syscall with a lazy
  `/dev/urandom` `use_file` fallback. On **macOS** the backend is `getentropy` (`lib.rs:241–248`);
  other Unixes map to `getrandom.rs`/`getentropy.rs`/libc variants as listed.
- **Not established (missing build inputs, named):** the deployed **target triple**; the effective
  cargo **feature set** actually resolved for getrandom in the production build graph (QBIND enables
  none, but A40 did not resolve the entire transitive graph); any `--cfg getrandom_backend=…`,
  `linux_disable_fallback`, or RUSTFLAGS supplied at build time; and the identity of the **compiled
  binary**. A40 does **not** claim the audited binary used any particular OS backend, and surveys no
  unrelated platforms.
- **Not established (runtime):** OS entropy availability/quality, early-boot blocking behavior, and
  uniqueness across restarts — **UNEXECUTED**; getrandom's own docs note first-call boot-time blocking
  and rare mis-configuration failure, but deployed behavior is not sampled here.

## 5. Bounded disposition — R-DEP-1

**Answered to the extent retrieved source supports:** for all four operations the pinned dependencies
(`fips204 0.4.6`, `fips203 0.4.3`, each via `rand_core 0.6.4` → `getrandom 0.2.16`, checksums verified
against `Cargo.lock`) acquire randomness from **`rand_core::OsRng`** (selected by the fips crates'
`default-rng` default feature, which QBIND leaves enabled), through the **fallible** `try_fill_bytes`
→ `getrandom(dest) -> Result` interface; a randomness failure is returned as `Err` and propagated to
QBIND's wrappers, and **no successful cryptographic output is produced after a failed randomness
request**. Deterministic internal expansion of a freshly-sampled random seed (`key_gen_internal`,
`keygen_from_seed`-shaped internals) is standard algorithm structure and is **distinct from** a
fixed-seed fallback or from entropy-failure handling. The production randomness path uses the
fallible interface throughout, not the panicking `OsRng::fill_bytes`.

**Kept separate (unchanged):**
- **R-DEP-1 residual now narrowed to platform/build:** the deployed getrandom **backend** is a
  conditional source conclusion pending the named build inputs (target triple, resolved features,
  cfgs/RUSTFLAGS, the binary). Not closed.
- **Runtime entropy availability/quality and uniqueness:** **UNEXECUTED** — not established by source.
- **Algorithm correctness / constant-time (R-DEP-2):** **not performed** this pass.
- **Secret erasure, key provisioning, transport replay/nonces, custody integration:** existing
  dispositions (OBL-KEY-1b/OBL-SIGN-1b/A26; transport A11-F1 and related; A19-F1/H04-F1) **unchanged**.

**OBL-DEP-2a / OBL-DEP-2b are not redefined and not declared complete here.** A40 addresses the
R-DEP-1 dependency-source question only. **No finding is required or forced**; no distinct defect is
asserted (the fallible-interface + no-output-on-failure behavior is a non-defective observation).
Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5** remains **OPEN**. The general dependency backend-correctness /
constant-time / runtime audit is **not** begun.

Run-035"), (b) over-classified the bounded caller-buffer signing API as a selected-binary production
op, and (c) over-stated several evidence properties. A39.1 corrects each with complete bodies and the

## C1 — Corrected key-generation and certificate-signing routes `[SUPERSEDED-A39 → A39.1-C1]`

**There is a second in-binary keygen route A39 missed: the `qbind-node identity` DevNet operator
subcommand, implemented in the node executable.** Executable trace:

```
main.rs:2018–2024  (intercept `identity` token BEFORE flag parsing/config; Run-375)
  → identity_cli::dispatch(raw)                     (main.rs:2022; exits with its code at :2023)
    → mint_devnet_root()                            (identity_cli.rs:290)
        → MlDsa44Backend::generate_keypair()        (pqc_devnet_helper.rs:54 → fips204 try_keygen)
    → MlKem768Backend::generate_keypair()           (identity_cli.rs:307 → fips203 KG::try_keygen)
    → issue_leaf_delegation_cert(&spec, &root.root_sk)   (identity_cli.rs:321)
        → ml_dsa_44_sign_digest(root_sk, &digest)   (pqc_devnet_helper.rs:221–223 → MlDsa44Backend::sign → fips204 try_sign)
```

**Error consumers (complete bodies read):**

- `mint_devnet_root()` keygen `Err` → `eprintln "root keygen failed"` + `return EXIT_IO`
  (`identity_cli.rs:290–296`).
- ML-KEM-768 keygen `Err` → `eprintln "ML-KEM-768 keygen failed"` + `return EXIT_IO`
  (`identity_cli.rs:307–313`).
- cert-signing `Err` → `eprintln "issue leaf cert failed"` + `return EXIT_IO`

  `DevNetCertError::SigningFailed` (`pqc_devnet_helper.rs:221–223`) which the dispatcher converts to

**Classification.** The `qbind-node identity` path is a **DevNet operator subcommand implemented in
the node executable** (Run-375), DevNet-only (MainNet/TestNet generation refused inside the
dispatcher — `identity_cli.rs` role/network guards, e.g. `EXIT_REFUSED` at `:256`). It is **distinct
from**: (i) normal consensus operation (which performs **no** keygen — validator keys are *loaded*,

tests/examples. A39's "the only in-binary keygen is Run-035" is **withdrawn**: there are **two**

## C3 — Tightened evidence wording `[SUPERSEDED-A39 → A39.1-C3]`

1. **Returned-Err handling (narrowed).** Supported statement: *each wrapper does not turn a returned
   dependency `Err` into a successful cryptographic output* (it maps `Err` to a typed error and, for
   `sign_into`, leaves `out` unchanged). A39.1 does **not** infer dependency panic-freedom, abort
   behavior, or the absence of outer-layer retries — those are not established by reading the wrappers.

   buffer is left unchanged (`ml_dsa44.rs:487–515`). (Scoped to the returned-error case per item 1.)

   on successful encaps the shared secret is **stored in a zeroizing container** (`SharedSecret::new(ss)`,
   `handshake.rs:387`). A39.1 does **not** assert immediate erasure of the pre-wrap value.
4. **`sk_array` vs `fips204::PrivateKey` separated.** The repository-owned `sk_array` stack copy

   the dependency type's destruction/erasure behavior remains **uninspected** (cross-ref secret
   handling OBL-KEY-1b / OBL-SIGN-1b / A26, not double-counted).

   the supported narrower statement: **`crates/qbind-crypto/Cargo.toml` declares no direct
   `rand`/`getrandom`/`rand_core` dependency**; RNG reaches the primitives only transitively through

   &[])` still receives the **message and (empty) context** arguments — only the RNG is not an

## C4 — Completion and disposition

For every inventoried wrapper the repo-owned
**operation → dependency-API → caller → guard → failure-consumer** chain is now supported:

- **Randomness ops:** ML-DSA `try_keygen`/`try_sign`, ML-KEM `try_keygen`/`try_encaps`, each a
  dependency API without an explicit RNG argument; no repository-owned RNG/seed; no direct RNG
  dependency in the crate manifest.
- **Keygen reachability:** DevNet operator subcommand (`qbind-node identity`) and the Run-035
  diagnostic harness in-binary; operator cert-mint helper; otherwise test/fixture. Normal consensus
  operation performs no keygen.
- **Signing reachability:** production consensus signing uses the **allocating** proposal/vote/timeout
  APIs off a **prepared/admitted, journal-bound** reservation, each **fail-closed** on `Err` (counter
  + refuse-to-emit/transmit, no panic/retry/substitution on the inspected chains); the **bounded
  caller-buffer** API has **no production caller** on the searched boundary.
- **Encaps reachability:** selected-binary KEMTLS `ClientHandshake::start` via `StaticCryptoProvider`,
  `Err` → `NetError::KeySchedule` propagated, no fallback suite, shared secret stored in a zeroizing
  container only after success.
- **No wrapper turns a returned dependency `Err` into successful output.**

On this basis the **repo-owned randomness-integration / failure-propagation sub-boundary of
OBL-DEP-2a** is marked **complete**. Held **separate and open**: dependency-internal RNG / getrandom
backend selection (**R-DEP-1**), backend algorithmic correctness and constant-timeness (**R-DEP-2**),
secret-erasure of repo-owned `sk_array` and dependency-owned key objects (cross-ref OBL-KEY/SIGN),
and deployed OS entropy quality / uniqueness across restarts (**R-RUNTIME-1**, UNEXECUTED — **not**
established by source). OBL-DEP-2a / OBL-DEP-2b are **not redefined**; OBL-DEP-2b (unvendored
dependency internals / deployed entropy) stays separate. **No new finding is required or forced** by
these report corrections; all existing finding IDs, aliases, obligation identities, and dispositions
are preserved. Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5** remains **OPEN**. The dependency-internals audit
is **not** begun.

# QBIND Security Findings Register

> **Layer A39 — in-tree cryptographic randomness integration and failure propagation (internal v1.116), under OBL-DEP-2a.**
> Scope **Public DevNet**, pinned at HEAD `18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b` /
> root tree `5b6c543435ac017dd8372c93f48be397899db14a` / branch `claude/exciting-keller-a05rwc` /
> origin `https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND.git`. Read-only source trace. No build, no test, no
> harness/helper/node execution, no probes, no signer/HSM connection, no operational-secret
> inspection. Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5** remains **OPEN**. All 54 obligation identities,
> finding IDs, aliases, and dispositions preserved; no global index rewrite.

## A39 scope and single source question

**What randomness operations do QBIND's real cryptographic wrappers request, through which dependency
APIs, and what do their callers do when those operations fail?** Repo-owned integration is kept
separate from dependency internals and deployed entropy quality. Resolved dependency versions
(verified against `Cargo.lock`, not inferred from `crates/qbind-crypto/Cargo.toml`'s `"0.4"` ranges):
**`fips204 0.4.6`** (`Cargo.lock:1324–1327`), **`fips203 0.4.3`** (`:1312–1315`); `getrandom 0.2.16`
(`:1377`) and `0.3.4` (`:1388`), `rand_core 0.6.4`/`0.9.5` both resolved. `qbind-crypto/Cargo.toml`
declares `fips204`/`fips203`/`zeroize` only — **no direct `rand`/`getrandom`/`rand_core` dependency**.

## Carried-forward A38.1 wording clarifications (narrow; governance not reopened)

- **CF-1 (A38.1-C1).** The *second* local-candidate governance-execution consumption **call**
  (`main.rs:3558`, `LocalPeerCandidateCheck` surface) **is reachable** after the shared preflight
  returns `Ok(Some(decision))`; only its **`Err(reason)` arm (`:3565`)** is unreachable under the
  unchanged-input assumption (identical decision/carrier/policy, surface-independent routing). The
  earlier `?`-enforced consume still exits at `:3589` on a fail-closed.
- **CF-2 (A38.1-C3).** The drain's **no-trust-mutation** conclusion is scoped to the established
  **file-absent** `drain_candidate.bundle` rejection; the **separately-conditioned file-present
  mutating pipeline** (requiring an additional local-filesystem write capability) is preserved as a
  distinct branch, not reopened (A12-F1 untouched).
- **CF-3 (A38.1-C3).** Live inbound `0x05` **propagation** is a **separate configured downstream
  effect** (`--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-propagation-enabled`); the universal "NEVER
  propagated" phrasing is withdrawn — the validation-only dispatcher never *applies*, but propagation
  is a configurable effect distinct from apply.

## 1. Bounded operation inventory

All real wrappers live in `crates/qbind-crypto/src/`. Every primitive randomness entry point is a
`try_*` form; **no wrapper supplies a repository-owned RNG or seed** — a whole-crate scan found no
`try_*_with_rng`, `from_seed`, `OsRng`, `thread_rng`, `getrandom`, or `rand*` use in
`qbind-crypto/src/` or on the signing/handshake caller paths. The RNG is therefore selected
*inside* the dependency (fips203/fips204 default), at the dependency boundary.

| Op | Wrapper (file:line) | Dependency API | Randomness source | Input checks before op | Error translation | Apparent-success on failure? | Reachability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ML-DSA keygen | `MlDsa44Backend::generate_keypair` (`ml_dsa44.rs:386–394`) | `fips204 ml_dsa_44::try_keygen()` | dep-internal (no-arg form); none repo-supplied | none (no inputs) | `Err → ConsensusSigError::Other("ML-DSA-44 keygen failed")` | **No** — `try_*` `Result`, no fabricated key | test/fixture (`validator_signer`, `keystore`, `signer_loader:443`, `genesis_consensus_authority:1504`, `bundle_signing_ratification` tests); diagnostic-binary harness (`main.rs:8799`, Run-035 forged-injection) |
| ML-DSA sign (allocating) | `MlDsa44Backend::sign` / `ValidatorSigningKey::sign` (`ml_dsa44.rs:412–433`, `235–237`) | `fips204 PrivateKey::try_sign(msg, &[])` (hedged/randomized) | dep-internal; none repo-supplied | `sk.len()==2560`; `PrivateKey::try_from_bytes` decode | `Err → ConsensusSigError::Other("ML-DSA-44 signing failed")` | **No** — returns `Err`, no sig fabricated | **selected binary** (`LocalKeySigner::sign_proposal/sign_vote/sign_timeout*`, `validator_signer.rs:370–404`) |
| ML-DSA sign (caller-buffer) | `MlDsa44Backend::sign_into` / `ValidatorSigningKey::sign_into` (`ml_dsa44.rs:479–515`, `264–270`) | `fips204 PrivateKey::try_sign(msg, &[])` | dep-internal; none repo-supplied | `out.len()>=2420` **first** (`:489`), then `sk.len()==2560` + decode | `Err → BoundedMlDsa44SignError::{OutputTooSmall,InvalidKey,BackendFailed}`; **`out` left unchanged** | **No** — `out` written only after a complete signature exists (`:509–511`) | **selected binary** (`LocalKeySigner::sign_vote_into`, `validator_signer.rs:416–437`) |
| ML-DSA sign (digest helper) | `ml_dsa_44_sign_digest` (`ml_dsa44_signature_suite.rs:101–103`) | → `MlDsa44Backend::sign` | dep-internal; none repo-supplied | delegates | `Err → CryptoError::InvalidSignature` (collapses backend/RNG failure into InvalidSignature) | **No** | operator tool (`pqc_devnet_helper.rs:221`, dev/offline cert mint) + tests |
| ML-KEM keygen | `MlKem768Backend::generate_keypair` (`ml_kem768.rs:92–100`) | `fips203 ml_kem_768::KG::try_keygen()` | dep-internal; none repo-supplied | none | `Err → CryptoError::InternalError("ML-KEM-768 keygen failed")` | **No** | operator tool (`identity_cli.rs:307`, `pqc_devnet_helper.rs:54`) + tests |
| ML-KEM encaps | `MlKem768Backend::encaps` (`ml_kem768.rs:124–146`) | `fips203 EncapsKey::try_encaps()` (randomized) | dep-internal; none repo-supplied | `pk.len()==1184`; `EncapsKey::try_from_bytes` decode | `Err → CryptoError::InternalError("ML-KEM-768 encapsulation failed")` | **No** | **selected binary** (KEMTLS `ClientHandshake::start`, `qbind-net/handshake.rs:375–377`, via `StaticCryptoProvider`) |

**Not a randomness op, recorded for completeness.** `MlKem768Backend::decaps` (`ml_kem768.rs:148–182`)
requests **no** randomness; FIPS-203 implicit rejection makes a corrupted ciphertext return a
*pseudo-random* shared secret (a dependency property, confirmed by the repo's own test
`ml_kem768.rs:248–268`), not a wrapper-level apparent-success-on-failure. `MlDsa44Backend::verify` /
`derive_public_key` and `MlDsa44SignatureSuite::verify` are deterministic (no randomness).

**Provider/trait dispatch accounted for.** The ML-KEM encaps path is reached through the
`KemSuite`/`CryptoProvider` trait, not a direct call: `p2p_node_builder.rs:413,415` registers
`MlKem768Backend::new()` (KEM) and `MlDsa44SignatureSuite::new(sig_suite_id)` (signature) into a
`StaticCryptoProvider`; `ClientHandshake::start` resolves `cfg.crypto.kem_suite(id)` (`handshake.rs:367–371`)
then calls `.encaps(...)`. This establishes **selected-binary** reachability for encaps and for the
signature-suite verify path — not merely that the APIs exist.

## 2. Failure consumption (one level up the inspected chains)

| Randomness-op failure | Immediate consumer | Action on failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ML-DSA sign (vote/proposal/timeout) | `LocalKeySigner::{sign_proposal,sign_vote,sign_timeout,sign_timeout_with_chain_id,sign_preimage}` (`validator_signer.rs:344–404`) | `.map_err(\|_\| SignError::CryptoError)` → **propagate/refuse**; no panic, no retry, no value substitution, no alternate backend |
| ML-DSA sign_into | `LocalKeySigner::sign_vote_into` (`validator_signer.rs:416–437`) | suite check first (`SuiteMismatch`); then `BoundedMlDsa44SignError::{InvalidKey,BackendFailed} → BoundedSignError::BackendFailed`; **`out` unchanged**; propagate |
| ML-KEM encaps | `ClientHandshake::start` (`qbind-net/handshake.rs:375–377`) | `.map_err(\|_\| NetError::KeySchedule("kem encaps failed"))?` → **propagate/refuse**; no fallback suite, no zero/constant shared-secret substitution; `SharedSecret` zeroizing wrap applied only **after** success (`:385–387`) |
| ML-DSA/ML-KEM keygen (tools) | `identity_cli.rs:307–313` (→`EXIT_IO`); `pqc_devnet_helper.rs:54–56`/`221–223` (→`String`/`DevNetCertError::SigningFailed`); `main.rs:8799–8809` (→`eprintln FATAL` + `exit(1)`) | **propagate/refuse**; no panic-through, no substitution |

**Fallback explicitly investigated (not assumed).** On the inspected chains there is **no** silent
downgrade and **no** fail-open: the signer does not swap to a dummy/alternate backend on crypto
failure, and the handshake does not fall back to another suite or a fixed secret. The `ValidatorSigner`
trait does admit other implementations (remote/HSM signer); those backend-selection paths are the
subject of existing findings (**A19-F1** authority RemoteSigner selector ignored; **H04-F1/E17**
validator remote-signer unwired; `hsm_pkcs11.rs:482,512` are commented-out stubs, no live PKCS#11
sign) — **cross-referenced, not reopened and not double-counted**. This absence claim is **scoped to
the inspected `LocalKeySigner` + `ClientHandshake::start` + operator-tool chains**.

**Caller-buffer output contract on failure.** For `sign_into` the **wrapper** promises and performs:
capacity checked before signing; `out` written only after a complete signature exists; on **any**
error `out` is left **unchanged** (`ml_dsa44.rs:487–515`; forwarded verbatim by
`validator_signer.rs:426–436`). The wrapper does **not** itself zeroize `out`, the `sk_array`
stack copy, or the decoded `fips204::PrivateKey` on failure; the `fips204` key type's own
`ZeroizeOnDrop` behavior is **dependency-owned and not inspected here** (cross-ref secret-handling
**OBL-KEY-1b / OBL-SIGN-1b / A26**, not double-counted).

## 3. Evidence levels separated

A call to `try_keygen` / `try_sign` / `try_encaps` establishes **API selection only**. It does **not**
establish, and A39 does **not** assert: OS entropy availability/quality, key/nonce uniqueness across
restarts, cryptographic correctness, constant-time execution, or any deployed behavior. Stopping at
the exact dependency boundary, the **named residuals** are:

- **R-DEP-1.** fips204 0.4.6 / fips203 0.4.3 select their RNG **internally** (the no-arg `try_*`
  forms); which `getrandom` backend/version (`0.2.16` vs `0.3.4`) is reached on each primitive path,
  and the OS entropy source, are **dependency-internal and unverified** here (unvendored source is
  **not** automatically unavailable — it is simply not inspected this pass; stays under
  **OBL-DEP-2b**, separate).
- **R-DEP-2.** Backend algorithmic correctness, constant-timeness, and hedged-vs-deterministic
  signing internals — **out of scope** (no backend/constant-time analysis, no platform entropy
  audit, no runtime fault injection).
- **R-RUNTIME-1.** Deployed entropy quality / uniqueness across restarts — **UNEXECUTED**; not
  established by source.

## 4. Preserved / distinguished (no double-count)

- **Primitive randomness vs transport handshake fields.** `client_random` (`handshake.rs:320,346`) is
  **caller-provided** to `ClientHandshake::new`, not drawn by a `qbind-crypto` wrapper — it is a
  **transport handshake field**, excluded from the primitive-randomness inventory and cross-referenced
  to the transport analyses (A5-F1 / A11-F2 / A13.1), not counted here.
- **AEAD nonce scheduling** (`chacha20poly1305.rs`) is a transport **nonce schedule**, not a primitive
  randomness request — excluded from this inventory; transport replay/nonce and configuration analyses
  preserved unchanged.
- **Keystore provisioning / secret ownership** (A10-F1/E18, OBL-KEY-1b, A26) preserved; the
  `sk_array`/decoded-key handling note above is cross-referenced there, not a new finding.
- **Consensus admission / signing-journal** analyses (A17-F1, QBIND-A1-F003) preserved; the `SignError`
  produced by the signer is consumed by those already-reviewed consensus paths.
- **Remote/HSM implementation gaps** (A19-F1, H04-F1/E17) preserved as the backend-selection context
  for the fallback investigation above.

## A39 bounded disposition

For every inventoried wrapper the repo-owned integration is established: the randomness-requesting
operations are the three `try_*` primitive entry points (ML-DSA `try_keygen`/`try_sign`, ML-KEM
`try_keygen`/`try_encaps`); **no wrapper supplies its own RNG/seed**; each checks inputs before the
operation; each maps a dependency `Err` to a typed error and **none can return an apparently
successful cryptographic result on failure**; the caller-buffer path leaves `out` unchanged on error.
On the **selected-binary** chains (consensus signing via `LocalKeySigner`; KEMTLS encaps via
`ClientHandshake::start`) and the **operator-tool** chains (identity CLI, devnet helper) the failure
is **propagated/refused** — no panic, retry, value substitution, or backend downgrade on the inspected
paths. Keygen reachability is predominantly **test/fixture** and **operator-tool**; the only in-binary
keygen is the Run-035 forged-injection **diagnostic** harness (`main.rs:8799`), which exits closed.

This completes the **OBL-DEP-2a** sub-boundary *in-tree cryptographic randomness integration and
failure propagation* for the repo-owned layer, with the dependency/runtime residuals **R-DEP-1 /
R-DEP-2 / R-RUNTIME-1** named and left open at the dependency boundary. **OBL-DEP-2b** (unvendored
dependency internals / deployed entropy) remains **separate and open**. **No finding is minted or
forced; no blanket cryptographic-security verdict is issued.** Other unreviewed
integration/secret-handling questions are preserved unchanged. Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5**
remains **OPEN**.

# QBIND Security Findings Register

> **Layer A38.1 — correction of the A38 composed invocation and enforcement analysis (internal v1.115).**
> Scope **Public DevNet**, pinned at HEAD `18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b` /

> harness/helper/node execution. Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5** remains **OPEN**. All 54

> This layer **corrects A38**; A38's superseded statements are marked `[SUPERSEDED-A38 → A38.1-Cx]`.

## A38.1 scope

A38 treated `main.rs:1905` (ReloadCheck surface) and `main.rs:3558` (LocalPeerCandidateCheck surface)
as two **independent** route-level surfaces, and concluded that the local peer-candidate route's
governance-execution verdict is **logged-only / advisory** (A38 surface-2 row and disposition). A
complete read of the composed caller + shared preflight shows that framing is **wrong**. A38.1
corrects the invocation composition, the enforcement claim, the two negative-caller groundings, the
effect/dependency wording, and the live-`0x05` classification. It mints **no finding**, closes **no**
contract question, and reopens **nothing** (A12-F1 untouched).

---

## C1 — Corrected local-candidate composed trace `[SUPERSEDED-A38 → A38.1-C1]`

**The execution hook at `main.rs:1905` lives inside the shared preflight, not on a separate
reload-check route.** `preflight_run_132_validation_only_v2_marker_check` (`main.rs:1774–1913`) has a
**single definition** and is called from **two** CLI routes: the reload-check route (`:3102`) and the
local peer-candidate-check route (`:3522`). Inside it, after the Run-130 v2-ratification verify
(`:1812–1825`, `?`), the Run-165/167 governance-**proof** gate
(`preflight_v2_validation_only_marker_check_with_governance_proof_load`, `:1861–1879`, `?`), and the
pure Run-182 on-chain hook (`:1896–1899`), it runs the governance-**execution** consumption:

```
consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome(&decision, …selector, …load,
    GovernanceExecutionRuntimeSurface::ReloadCheck)          // main.rs:1905–1909
    .map_err(run_220_governance_execution_consumption_marker_error)?;   // :1911
Ok(Some(decision))                                            // :1913
```

The `?` converts a governance-execution **fail-closed** into `Err(MutatingSurfaceMarkerV2Error)`.

**On the local peer-candidate-check caller (`main.rs:3522–3590`):** the `match` on the preflight
result routes that `Err` to the **`Err(marker_err)` arm** (`:3580–3590`), whose body is
`eprintln "[binary] Run 132: VERDICT=invalid …"` **followed by `std::process::exit(1)` at `:3589`**.
That arm is mutually exclusive with the `Ok(Some(decision))` arm (`:3528–3576`) that contains the
**second** consumption — the `LocalPeerCandidateCheck`-surface call at `:3558`. So a
governance-execution fail-closed in the shared preflight **exits the process (1)** at `:3589` and
**never reaches** the `:3558` call.

**The `:3558` logged-only arm is unreachable after the earlier hook succeeds, under an unchanged
policy.** Both consumptions pass the **same** `&decision` (the `Ok(Some(decision))` value returned by
the preflight), the **same** `ctx_data.governance_execution_policy_selector`, and the **same**
`ctx_data.governance_execution_load`; they differ **only** in the `surface` argument
(`ReloadCheck` vs `LocalPeerCandidateCheck`). The per-surface routers are **surface-independent**:
`route_loaded_governance_execution_to_reload_check_callsite_decision`
(`pqc_governance_execution_payload_carrying.rs:1090–1095`) and
`route_loaded_governance_execution_to_local_peer_candidate_check_callsite_decision` (`:1129–1134`)
both delegate to the **identical** `route_callsite_decision` (`:1067–1083`) with **no** surface
branch; the decision is a pure function of `(policy, carrier, expectations, trust_domain)` via
`malformed_payload_shortcircuit` → `absent_or_available_decision` (`:1029–1048`) → `run_211_evaluate`
(`:1052–1063`). Therefore reaching `:3558` means the `ReloadCheck`-surface consume at `:1905` already
returned `Ok` (Proceed); with identical inputs the `LocalPeerCandidateCheck`-surface consume returns
`Ok` as well, so the `Err(reason)` arm at `:3565` is **not reachable** in that composed path.

**Corrected conclusion.** *Preserved as a local code fact:* the `:3565` arm, in isolation, only
`eprintln`s (no `exit`, no mutation). *Withdrawn:* A38's inference that the **local-candidate route
therefore treats governance-execution failure as advisory**. The route's governance-execution
enforcement is the **`exit(1)` at `:3589`** (via the shared preflight's `ReloadCheck`-surface `?`),
which fires **before** the `:3558` arm is reachable. No environment-changing actor is invented to
force the `:3565` branch; absent a mid-flight policy/environment change it is dead in this
composition.

**Final consumer (`Run077Result::exit_code()`, `:3639–3646`).** When the governance block passes
(or is skipped), control falls through to `eprintln!(verdict_line)` (`:3639`) and
`std::process::exit(Run077Result::Ran{…}.exit_code())` (`:3640–3646`). `exit_code()`
(`pqc_peer_candidate_binary.rs:331–339`) returns **0 only for `PeerCandidateOutcome::Validated`**, **1
otherwise**, and **1 for every `Refused`**. So the terminal exit is 0 on a clean Validated pass and 1
on any non-Validated outcome; a governance-execution fail-closed does **not** reach this consumer
because it has already exited at `:3589`.
