# QBIND Security Findings Register

> **Layer A38 — remaining governance-execution invocation boundaries (internal v1.114).**
> Scope **Public DevNet**, pinned at HEAD `18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b` /
> root tree `5b6c543435ac017dd8372c93f48be397899db14a` / branch `claude/exciting-keller-a05rwc` /
> origin `https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND.git`. Read-only source trace. No build, no test, no
> harness/helper/node execution. Runtime remains **UNEXECUTED**; **C5** (production cryptographic
> custody / signing-lifecycle obligation) remains **OPEN**. All 54 obligation identities, finding
> IDs, aliases, and dispositions preserved; no global index rewrite.

## A38 scope

One source question, applied to the **four remaining governance-execution runtime surfaces** that
A36.1 explicitly deferred (`_a361_layer.md`-equivalent §C1 note: *"remaining runtime surfaces
(reload-check, local peer-candidate-check, inbound `0x05`, peer-driven drain) are **not** reviewed"*):

> For each entry point, **when does a configured governance-execution requirement actually reach an
> enforcing decision, and what happens when invocation is skipped?**

The governance-execution runtime machinery is the Run-213/215/217/220/224/226 arming path
(`GovernanceExecutionRuntimeArmingConfig`, `consume_surface` →
`consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome`), **distinct** from the Run-163/165/167/169
governance-**proof** carrier path (`with_governance_proof_carrier`). A38 traces only the
**execution** machinery. The governance-proof path is out of scope here (last touched A25).

The node binary has exactly **four** `consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome` call
sites (`main.rs:952, 1297, 1905, 3558`), reached with exactly four of the seven representable
`GovernanceExecutionRuntimeSurface` values:

- `main.rs:952` → `ReloadApply` (mutating; covered by A36)
- `main.rs:1297` → `StartupP2pTrustBundle` (mutating; covered by A35/A35.1)
- `main.rs:1905` → `ReloadCheck` (**A38 surface 1**)
- `main.rs:3558` → `LocalPeerCandidateCheck` (**A38 surface 2**)

The surfaces `LiveInbound0x05` and `PeerDrivenDrain` (A38 surfaces 3 and 4) have **no**
`consume_run_220` call site in the node binary (confirmed by exhaustive grep of `main.rs`; the only
`PeerDrivenDrain*` tokens in `main.rs` are the unrelated Run-150 `PeerDrivenDrainPolicy` constructor
at `:3989–4090, 8376–8395`, not the execution surface). Their preflights
(`preflight_live_inbound_0x05`, `preflight_peer_driven_drain`) and routers
(`route_loaded_governance_execution_to_live_inbound_0x05_callsite_decision` /
`…peer_driven_drain_callsite_decision`, `pqc_governance_execution_payload_carrying.rs:1143, 1160`)
are reachable **only** through `arm_surface` (`pqc_governance_execution_runtime_arming.rs:366, 390,
393`) → `consume_surface` (`:522–535`), and `consume_surface` for these two surfaces is invoked
**only from tests/examples**, never from the node path.

## Shared consumption semantics (`consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome`, `main.rs:1065–1130`)

For every surface that *is* invoked, the node-path consumer builds expectations from the marker
candidate with an **empty binding** — `expected_proposal_id: String::new()` (`:1092`), empty
`expected_decision_id` / `expected_candidate_digest` / `expected_governance_proof_digest` /
`expected_replay_nonce`, fixed `GovernanceAction::Rotate` / `LocalLifecycleAction::Rotate`
(`:1094–1095`), `expected_effective_epoch: 0` / `now_epoch: 0` (`:1102, 1104`) — then
`GovernanceExecutionRuntimeArmingConfig::from_cli_or_env(selector).unwrap_or_default()`
(`:1106–1109`, default = `Disabled`), then routes through
`wire_governance_evaluator_runtime_callsite_without_evaluator_context(&arming, surface, …, false)`
(`:1120–1127`) → `.map(|_| ()).map_err(|fc| fc.reason)`. Per the in-source Run-226 note
(`:1110–1119`): the binary marker metadata **cannot construct a real evaluator request/response**
(no proposal/decision binding), so the **no-evaluator-context** wiring is used — default
`Disabled` + absent carrier **short-circuits to the legacy bypass BEFORE the evaluator stage**, and
every **present** carrier **fails closed BEFORE any mutation**. This reaffirms the register's
standing result (A35–A37.1): **the hook never positively accepts a supplied carrier on the binary
path** — it either bypasses (`Disabled` + `Absent`) or fails closed.

## The four surfaces — invocation / result / effect

| # | Surface | Hook invoked on node path? | Site | Result handling | Furthest effect of a fail-closed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Reload-check (`--p2p-trust-bundle-reload-check`) | **YES** | `main.rs:1905–1911` | `consume_run_220(…ReloadCheck).map_err(run_220_…marker_error)?` — `?`-propagated out of the validation-only preflight | Err aborts the **validation-only** check and is surfaced operatorially; **no** marker/sequence/trust mutation on either outcome (preflight contract `runtime_arming.rs:231–234`: caller MUST drop outcome) |
| 2 | Local peer-candidate validation (`--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-check`) | **YES** | `main.rs:3558–3575` | `match … { Ok(())=>{}, Err(reason)=> eprintln "[run-220] VERDICT=invalid …" }` — **logged only** | A log line. **No `process::exit`, no mutation.** Strictly weaker than the co-located v2 authority-marker conflict at `:3580–3590`, which prints `VERDICT=invalid` **and `std::process::exit(1)`** |
| 3 | Inbound `0x05` peer-candidate processing | **NO** | — (no `consume_run_220(…LiveInbound0x05)` in `main.rs`) | not reached on the live path | n/a — a configured requirement is **never consulted** on the live `0x05` node path |
| 4 | Peer-driven drain (Run-153 drain-once) | **NO** | — (drain block `main.rs:8194–8456` uses `with_governance_proof_carrier`, not the execution preflight) | not reached on the drain path | n/a — a configured requirement is **never consulted** on the drain node path |

### Surface 1 — Reload-check (invoked, validation-only)

`main.rs:1905–1911`, inside the v2 reload-check preflight (returns `Ok(Some(decision))` at `:1913`).
The consume result is `?`-propagated: a fail-closed becomes an `Err` that aborts the validation-only
reload-check and is reported operatorially. Because the reload-check surface is validation-only
(`preflight_reload_check` docstring `runtime_arming.rs:231–234`: *"no marker write, no sequence
advance, no live trust swap, no session eviction, no Run 070 call"*), the decision gates **no
mutation** in either direction. Under the default policy (`Disabled` + `Absent` carrier) the
decision is the legacy-bypass **Proceed** (`Ok`); it is never a positive accept.

### Surface 2 — Local peer-candidate validation (invoked, logged-only)

`main.rs:3558–3575`. A fail-closed is **translated to a `VERDICT=invalid` log line only** — the arm
does **not** call `process::exit` and performs no mutation. This is materially weaker than the
sibling v2 authority-marker conflict branch at `:3580–3590`, which both logs `VERDICT=invalid` and
calls `std::process::exit(1)`. So on this surface, even a `ProductionGovernanceRequired` /
`MainnetGovernanceRequired` fail-closed produces **no process-level or state-level consequence** —
only an operator-visible log. (Validation-only is preserved; the observation is that the
governance-execution verdict here is advisory where the adjacent marker verdict is enforcing.)

### Surface 3 — Inbound `0x05` peer-candidate processing (not invoked on the live path)

No `consume_run_220(…LiveInbound0x05)` exists in `main.rs`. The live inbound `0x05` dispatcher
(`main.rs:7902–8019`) performs only: (a) the **Run-123 validation-only authority-marker conflict
check**, itself gated by the ratification gate (`:7909–7932`) and **SKIPPED on the DevNet legacy
path** when the gate is not invoked (`:7925–7931`); and (b) the **Run-147 non-applying staging
queue** (`:7948–8019`), which the in-source contract states *"NEVER applies, NEVER persists
sequence, NEVER writes the authority marker, NEVER mutates LivePqcTrustState, NEVER evicts
sessions"* (`:7941–7944`). **No governance-execution preflight runs here.**

This is a **documented** limitation, not an inference: `preflight_live_inbound_0x05` carries the
**A8 live-config limitation** docstring (`runtime_arming.rs:315–326`): *"the live inbound `0x05`
runtime path **does not yet thread** a per-connection governance-execution policy from its live
config; this wrapper exposes the policy injection at the source/test level … Wiring the armed policy
into the live `0x05` runtime config is … **deferred to Run 218**."* Consequence: a configured
governance-execution requirement (including the fail-closed `ProductionGovernanceRequired` /
`MainnetGovernanceRequired` policies) **never reaches an enforcing decision** on the live inbound
`0x05` node path — the requirement is simply not consulted there. There is no positive apply on this
surface regardless (staging is non-applying), so no bundle is activated here; but the specific claim
"a configured execution requirement gates live `0x05`" is **false on the current binary**.

### Surface 4 — Peer-driven drain (not invoked on the drain path)

The Run-153 drain-once block (`main.rs:8194–8456`) attaches governance material via
`.with_governance_proof_carrier(governance_proof_load, governance_policy)` (`:8332–8335`) on the
`ProductionV2MarkerCoordinator` and invokes `try_drain_once_shared` (`:8425–8434`). That carrier is
the **governance-proof** path (Run-165/167), **not** the governance-execution preflight: there is no
`preflight_peer_driven_drain` / `consume_run_220(…PeerDrivenDrain)` call anywhere in the drain path.
`preflight_peer_driven_drain` (`runtime_arming.rs:348–360`, MainNet-refusal-preserved docstring
`:344–347`) is reachable only via `arm_surface`/`consume_surface` from tests/examples.

**Additional drain gating that IS present (kept separate from the execution-hook question):**

1. The drain fires only when `--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-drain-once` is armed **and** the
   shared staging queue exists (`:8194–8195`) **and** a baseline `LivePqcTrustState` is present
   (`:8212–8214`; else `drain-once skipped … no mutation` `:8443–8448`).
2. MainNet peer-driven apply is **refused unconditionally** at drain-once invocation
   (`:8388–8394`, `std::process::exit(1)`), and again at apply-policy construction (`:8403–8409`).
3. **The established missing `drain_candidate.bundle` handoff is preserved.** The drain invocation
   builder reads candidate material from `scratch_dir.join("drain_candidate.bundle")`
   (`main.rs:8235–8249`), a per-process scratch path under `std::env::temp_dir()`. No node-path
   producer writes that file from the staging queue; the drain consumes the **in-memory** shared
   staging queue via `try_drain_once_shared`, while the `ProductionDrainInvocationBuilder` is
   constructed against a `candidate_path` that the node never populates. This remains the
   previously-recorded drain handoff gap. **A network sender cannot create that file** — it is a
   local filesystem path owned by the process. Any file-present branch would require an **additional
   local filesystem write capability** (an operator or a co-located process placing
   `drain_candidate.bundle` in `qbind-run153-drain-scratch-<pid>`), which is a distinct precondition
   and is **kept separate from A12-F1** (the NoV2 drain-coordinator fallback). A38 does not assume
   this capability and does not demonstrate a file-present drain.

Consequence: a configured governance-execution requirement **never reaches an enforcing decision**
on the peer-driven drain node path; the drain's governance gate (such as it is) is the separate
governance-proof carrier, and the drain is independently blocked by the unpopulated
`drain_candidate.bundle` handoff and the MainNet refusal.

## A38 bounded disposition

- **Surfaces 1 and 2 (reload-check, local peer-candidate-check):** the governance-execution hook
  **is invoked** but is **validation-only**. Under the default `Disabled` + `Absent` policy it is a
  legacy-bypass `Proceed`; a present/required carrier fails closed, but on surface 2 that fail-closed
  is **logged-only** (no `exit`, no mutation), and on surface 1 it aborts a check that mutates nothing
  either way. Neither surface demonstrates a positive accept, and neither gates a state mutation.
- **Surfaces 3 and 4 (inbound `0x05`, peer-driven drain):** the governance-execution hook is **not
  invoked on the node path at all**. The preflights exist and are exercised only at source/test
  level; live `0x05` wiring is explicitly **deferred to Run 218** (documented A8 limitation), and the
  drain path routes governance through the separate **proof** carrier, not the execution preflight.
  A configured execution requirement is **never consulted** on these two surfaces. Fail-closed
  protection against a positive apply on these surfaces comes from **other** mechanisms (non-applying
  staging; `current_auth = None` / `proposal_vote_authority = None`; MainNet unconditional refusal;
  the unpopulated `drain_candidate.bundle` handoff), **not** from the governance-execution hook.
- This **grounds and extends the A36.1 unresolved contract/integration candidate** (required-policy
  hook non-invocation, no documented exception) across all four remaining surfaces: on surfaces 3–4
  the non-invocation is **total on the node path** (stronger than the skip-branch non-invocation
  A36.1 recorded for the mutating surfaces), and on surfaces 1–2 the invoked hook is non-enforcing
  (validation-only / logged-only). Recorded under **OBL-GOV-2** (open overall) as the completion of
  the A36.1-deferred surface review. **No new finding ID is minted and none is forced** — this is a
  contract/wiring observation on an already-tracked obligation, not a newly-demonstrated
  node-boundary defect; nothing is dismissed, and the remaining execution-wiring evidence (Run 218
  for live `0x05`; a node-path execution consumer for the drain) stays **separately outstanding**.
- **Remaining source questions (named, bounded):** (a) the live inbound `0x05` runtime
  execution-policy threading is unimplemented pending **Run 218** (`runtime_arming.rs:315–326`);
  (b) no node-path consumer invokes `preflight_peer_driven_drain` / `consume_run_220(…PeerDrivenDrain)`
  for the drain — the unread would-be consumer does not exist in `main.rs`. Both are recorded as
  deferred/unimplemented, not as unread branches in reachable code.

## A37.1-C1 Corrected scenario table `[SUPERSEDED-A37 → A37.1-C1]`

| Scenario | Command / capture | Status handling | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **216 S1 / 227 S1** (`--help`) | `set +e; node --help; HELP_RC=$?; set -e` (216:103, 227:121) | **genuine**, **asserted `== 0`** (`[[ -eq 0 ]] \|\| fail`, 216:104, 227:122) | `--help` exits 0 (and, with the surface check, hides the selector) — a **help** command, not a trust-bundle operation |
| **216 S2–S10 / 227 S2–S4** | `( node --print-genesis-hash … ) >log 2>&1 \|\| true; rc=$?` (216:96,111–115; 227:114) | **MASKED** — `\|\| true` makes the OR-list exit 0, so `rc=$?` reads 0; the node's **actual** exit status is unchanged but **not captured** | only `assert_surface_silent` (negative-log) on a **print-genesis early-exit** path |
| **227 S5** (`fixture-governance-allowed`) | `set +e; node --print-genesis-hash … bogus-free selector; S5_RC=$?; set -e` (227:136) | **genuine status recorded** (rc=1), **no success assertion** (only surface-silent) | nothing about enforcement; a recorded unasserted rc |
| **227 S6** (invalid selector) | `set +e; node … bogus-policy; S6_RC=$?; set -e` (227:140) | **genuine**, **asserted non-zero** `[[ -ne 0 ]] \|\| fail` + `assert_grep 'invalid governance-execution policy selector'` + `assert_grep 'no marker write; …; no Run 070 call'` (227:142–145) | invalid selector → non-zero + the Run-217 rejection + no-mutation message (a **valid** check) |
| **216 S8** (invalid selector) | `… \|\| true; S8_RC=$?` + `assert_surface_silent` (216:113) | **MASKED** (no genuine rc assertion, unlike 227 S6) | only negative-log; 216 has **no** genuine invalid-selector rc assertion |

`|| true` masks the **OR-list** exit status (forcing a subsequent `$?` to 0); it does **not** change the node's
actual exit. **Negative-log checks alone** (`assert_surface_silent`) establish neither successful **parsing**,
**precedence**, nor **enforcement** — only the absence of forbidden strings. **Help**, an **earlier refusal**
(e.g. invalid-selector `exit(1)`), and a **`--print-genesis-hash` early-exit** are each distinct from a **real
trust-bundle startup/reload/SIGHUP operation**, which none of these node commands reach.

## A37.1-C2 Regression status → final verdict (status-to-verdict trace) `[SUPERSEDED-A37 → A37.1-C2]`

In both harnesses, `run_test_target` / `run_lib_test` wrap `cargo test` in `set +e … set -e`, capture `rc`, write
`${EXIT_DIR}/test_${target}.rc`, and `printf 'test:…\trc=%d\n' "$rc"` into `TEST_VERDICTS` — but **never `fail`/exit
on `rc != 0`** (216:145–166, 227 equivalent). The summary prints `for v in "${TEST_VERDICTS[@]}"` (216:197,
227:258) and then an **unconditional** `echo "verdict: PASS"` (216:201, 227:262) — the overall verdict is **not
computed from** the recorded regression `rc`s.

**Finite static counterexample (no claim any historical test failed):** build, helper (`helper_rc==0`), S1 help
(`HELP_RC==0`), 227 S6 invalid-selector assertion, and the denylist all succeed → control reaches the regression
loop → one `cargo test` target returns `rc=1` → `run_test_target` records `test:Xrc=1`, `set -e` is restored
without a `fail`, the loop continues → the summary prints `test:Xrc=1` **and** `verdict: PASS`. The emitted overall
`PASS` therefore **does not reflect** a regression-test failure it records.

**Disposition (assessed separately from the governance hook-invocation candidate; duplicate-checked):** this is a
genuine **evidence-harness assurance defect** — the Run-216/227 "verdict: PASS" does not aggregate the
regression-test statuses it reports, so a failing regression would not flip the verdict. It is **harness/evidence
tooling**, **not** a QBIND node/protocol vulnerability, and is **not** dismissed merely for being a harness: it
**weakens the independent trust** that can be placed in the recorded Run-216/227 `PASS`. Recorded as a bounded
**evidence-assurance observation**; **no node-security finding ID is forced** (it matches no existing node finding
by mechanism — distinct from A19-F1/A23-F1/A25-F1 — and is an evidence-integrity issue, not a node-boundary
defect).

## A37.3 Claim → actual-assertion table (HEAD harness)

All node scenarios invoke `target/release/qbind-node` with **`--print-genesis-hash`**, which prints the genesis
hash and **exits early** — **before** any startup trust-bundle / reload / SIGHUP processing, so the
governance-execution hook is **never reached** by these node commands.

| Claimed property | Actual command / call | Route exercised | Assertion type | Establishes | Does NOT establish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default = Disabled; flags accepted | `qbind-node --print-genesis-hash --env … [selector]` (216 S2–S10; 227 S2–S5) | CLI parse + `--print-genesis-hash` early-exit | **masked** exit (`\|\| true; rc=$?`) + `assert_surface_silent` (negative-log) | CLI accepts the flags; no forbidden text in the print-genesis-hash log | hook invocation on a real operation; a real exit status (masked) |
| Invalid selector fails closed | `qbind-node --print-genesis-hash --env devnet --…-policy bogus` (227 S6) | Run-217 selector validation (`main.rs:2052`) | **genuine + asserted**: `[[ S6_RC -ne 0 ]]` + `assert_grep 'invalid governance-execution policy selector'` + `assert_grep 'no marker write; no sequence write; … no Run 070 call'` | invalid selector → non-zero exit + the Run-217 rejection + no-mutation message | that any *valid* selector drives the hook on a real operation |
| Selector still parses | `… --…-policy fixture-governance-allowed` (227 S5) | CLI parse + early-exit | **genuine but NOT rc-asserted** (`S5_RC=$?`, recorded rc=1, only surface-silent) | the flag parses without forbidden surface text | nothing about enforcement (rc=1 recorded, unasserted) |
| `--print-genesis-hash` behavior | `qbind-node --print-genesis-hash` | genesis-hash print path | log/exit capture | the print path runs | trust-bundle startup/reload path (not reached) |
| Policy reaches seven preflight wrappers; fixtures evidence-only; production unavailable | release-built **helper** corpus (216 tables pass=86; 227 tables pass=144) | **direct library/helper execution** | positive helper-table verdicts | the **library** functions behave as tabulated | that the **node** invokes those functions on a real startup/reload/SIGHUP operation |
| No forbidden enforcement text | `denylist` across captured logs | negative-log grep | PASS (patterns empty) | the captured logs lack forbidden strings | that enforcement occurred (absence of forbidden text ≠ successful enforcement) |
| Regression invariants | `cargo test -p qbind-node …` (216/227 test lists) | unit/integration tests | **genuine** `cargo test` rc (no `\|\| true`) | the named test targets pass **at the recorded revision** | node-operation hook invocation; current-HEAD execution |

**Key separations:** CLI parsing, invalid-selector rejection (Run-227 S6, genuine), `--print-genesis-hash`
behavior, **direct library/helper execution** (helper corpus), and **source-symbol presence** are all exercised;
**actual startup/reload/SIGHUP hook invocation** and **mutation-or-refusal at the intended trust-bundle boundary**
are **not** exercised by the node commands (all early-exit via `--print-genesis-hash`). A helper's direct call is
**not** transferred into evidence that the node invokes that function on a real operation.

## A36.1-C1 Contract closure withdrawn → unresolved candidate `[SUPERSEDED-A36 → A36.1-C1]`

A36 concluded the required-policy non-enforcement on skipped paths is "documented-and-matched" and "not an
unresolved candidate." Reassessed against the four separated propositions:

1. **Selector/parser guarantees** — a present value parses or the process `exit(1)`s at Run-217 (`main.rs:2052`);
   absent → `Disabled` (`pqc_governance_execution_policy_surface.rs`). **Established.**
2. **Invoked-hook guarantees** — a present carrier fails closed (policy gate / class / binding), Disabled+Absent
   bypasses, evaluator-unavailable; no positive acceptance (A36, retained). **Established.**
3. **Does the binary guarantee hook invocation covers the requested operation?** **NO.** `consume_run_220…` is
   reached only on the ratification-gate **Invoke** + v2-sidecar + authority-marker/data-dir path. On the
   ratification-gate **Skip** (DevNet no-opt-in, `main.rs:6886–6904` / reload-apply `:4492–4497`), the SIGHUP
   `ratification:None` branch (`pqc_live_trust_reload.rs:1127–1140`), and the missing-authority-marker early return
   (`:1357–1365`), the apply proceeds via the legacy path and the hook is **never invoked** — the selected policy
   is **not consulted** for that operation.
4. **Documented exception permitting skip under a selected required policy?** **NOT established.** The docs state
   the selected policy "reaches **all seven** production preflight contexts (source/test level)" and
   "missing/malformed/invalid material fails closed **under an explicit policy**" (RUN_215 §128–145; RUN_217
   §107–125); RUN_226 §68–101 lists the `consume_run_220…` call sites and documents only the **default** `Disabled`
   + legacy no-governance-execution compatibility (Run-214) as a bypass. **No** document states that an **explicit
   required** policy may be silently non-consulted on the ratification-skip / missing-marker branches; the only
   documented skip is the default-compatibility path, and the CLI qualifies the whole selector as "source/test
   selector wiring only … release-binary evidence deferred to Run-216/227."

A documented default-compatibility path, a hidden flag, and a source/test label do **not**, by themselves,
establish proposition 4. Therefore A36's categorical conformity / "not-a-candidate" conclusion is **withdrawn**.

**Disposition — explicitly unresolved contract/integration candidate (not forced to a finding).** There is a gap
between the documented "the selected policy reaches all seven preflight contexts / fails closed under an explicit
policy" and the executable fact that the governance-execution hook is **not invoked at all** on the
ratification-skip / `ratification:None` / missing-marker branches, with **no documented exception** for a selected

## A36.1-C2 Concrete lifecycle traces `[SUPERSEDED-A36 → A36.1-C2]` (replacing the prerequisite list)

**Reload-apply, explicit required policy, hook skipped (DevNet).** `--p2p-mode p2p` + `--p2p-trust-bundle <baseline>`
+ `--data-dir …` + `--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-execution-policy=production-governance-required`, **without**
`--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-enforcement-enabled`. Startup: Run-217 validates the selector (valid → OK); the
baseline bundle is loaded/validated. Process-start reload-apply (`main.rs:4450–4529`): `ratification_gate_decision`
→ **Skip** (DevNet no opt-in) → falls through to `apply_validated_candidate_with_previous` (Run-070/073) **without
the v2 marker preflight** → `consume_run_220(ReloadApply)` **not invoked** → the required policy is **not consulted**
→ candidate applied to the **process-local** `LivePqcTrustState`; `NoActiveSessionsEvictor` request (no sessions);
Run-055 sequence commit; **no v2 marker decision** to persist (A36.1 / A36-B). **Furthest effect:** process-local
trust swap + persistent sequence record — **without** governance-execution enforcement despite the required policy.
(Process-local; does not modify another node. The persistent sequence/marker files survive process exit; the
in-memory live state does not.)

**SIGHUP, explicit required policy, boot-to-trigger.** Startup gating (Run-074, `main.rs:4838–4879`): **Unix**;
`--p2p-mode p2p`; `--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-enabled` **paired with** `--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-path
<PATH>`; **mandatory** `--p2p-trust-bundle <BASELINE>` (each else FATAL `exit(1)`). The required selector is validated
at Run-217; the mandatory baseline bundle is loaded and validated at startup; a **startup-refused** configuration
never reaches the handler. In `run_p2p_node`, the `LiveReloadController` is constructed, **capturing** the resolved
`governance_execution_runtime_arming` (the required policy), the ratification config, and the authority-marker
config; the SIGHUP handler is installed after P2P startup. On a later SIGHUP trigger (`pqc_live_trust_reload.rs:912+`):
- if `self.config.ratification` is **present** and the re-read candidate is a **v2** sidecar **and** an
  authority-marker context was captured at construction → the v2 marker preflight runs → `consume_run_220_sighup`
  **consults** the captured required policy → present carrier **fail-closed** (no mutation of the running node's
  shared state) / Disabled+Absent bypass;
- if `ratification` is **None** (`:1127–1140`) **or** the authority-marker context is absent (`:1357–1365`, DevNet
  no-data-dir/no-opt-in) → the apply takes the legacy branch → the hook is **not invoked** → the required policy is
  **not consulted** → the candidate is applied to the running node's **shared** trust snapshot (+ a **real**
  eviction request — a request, not proof of session termination).

**v1-at-startup → v2-at-trigger (verified, not assumed):** the sidecar version is re-read at **trigger** time
(`:923–929`), so a v2 candidate can appear at trigger even if the startup baseline was v1. But the v2 marker
preflight is still gated by the **authority-marker context captured at controller construction**; if startup did not
establish that context (e.g. DevNet v1 baseline, no opt-in / no data-dir), a v2 trigger candidate hits the
missing-marker early return (`:1357–1365`) → legacy apply → hook **not** reached. So the v1→v2 transition does
**not** by itself enable the governance-execution hook — the **first missing step** is the startup-time
authority-marker/ratification context capture, which bounds the reachability claim.

## A36.1-C3 Two-stage sidecar-loading account `[SUPERSEDED-A36 → A36.1-C3]`

Both mutating surfaces load governance-execution status in **two separate** operations, not one shared parse:
- **Startup** (`main.rs:534–542`): the versioned ratification dispatcher first; then a **separate** `std::fs::read`
  + `serde_json::from_slice` for the governance-execution sibling — I/O or non-JSON failure maps to **Absent**.
- **SIGHUP** (`pqc_live_trust_reload.rs:923–959`): **stage 1** `load_versioned_ratification_with_governance_proof_from_path`
  (→ V1 / V2 / typed error / None); **stage 2** (only on the V2 arm) a **separate** second
  `std::fs::read(path).ok().and_then(|b| serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&b).ok())` →
  `governance_execution_load_status_from_optional_sidecar_value`.

| Case | Resulting status / outcome |
| --- | --- |
| **First-load failure** (ratification sidecar I/O / JSON / unknown-schema / malformed) | typed ratification refusal; the **second read is not reached** (earlier failure preserved) |
| **Second-read I/O or JSON failure** | `.ok()` / `.and_then(…ok())` → `None` → **`Absent`** governance-execution status (**not** Malformed) |
| **Absent / null sibling** (valid JSON, no `governance_execution`) | **`Absent`** |
| **Malformed present sibling** | **`Malformed`** |
| **Available carrier** | **`Available`** |
| **Outer branch that never performs these reads** (`self.config.ratification == None`; or startup not on the invoke+v2 path) | neither load performed; hook not reached |

Under an **explicit required policy** (where the hook **is** invoked), `Absent` → `RequiredButAbsent` fail-closed,
`Malformed` → fail-closed, `Available` → fail-closed (A36.1-A). So a **second-read I/O/JSON error ≠ Malformed** — it
is **Absent**, and not every file/JSON error is a malformed-carrier rejection. The two reads of the same path are a
TOCTOU-**shaped** surface, but **no exploitable race is asserted**: no capability or ordered changing-file sequence
is established or executed, and under an explicit policy the net is fail-closed regardless.

## A36.1 Carried A35.1 corrections

**C-A `[SUPERSEDED-A35.1 → A36.1-A]` (ordered guards in `evaluate_governance_execution_policy`,
`pqc_governance_execution_policy.rs:1074–1252`).** A35.1-C2's "Available → WrongProposalId (any policy)" is
corrected to the actual ordered outcomes for a present carrier under the startup/reload expectations
(`expected_proposal_id = ""`):
- **Disabled** → `GovernanceExecutionDisabled` at the **policy gate** (`:1084`), **before** any binding.
- **ProductionGovernanceRequired / MainnetGovernanceRequired** → `classify_production_policy_rejection` (`:1087–1089`),
  **before** binding.
- **Fixture / EmergencyCouncilFixture** → fall through to class-availability (`:1098`), class↔policy match (`:1117`),
  MainNet-fixture refusal (`:1126`), unsupported-action (`:1131`), **structural well-formedness** (`:1147`,
  `is_well_formed` requires nonempty proposal_id/…), suite/env bindings, and **only then** the proposal-ID binding
  (`:1234–1242`). An **empty** supplied ID fails well-formedness; a **nonempty** ID cannot equal the empty startup
  expectation → `WrongProposalId`. So the refusal reason is **policy-specific**, not one universal guard.
- The unavailable evaluator (`ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`) is **still invoked** after a consumption
  failure, and the final integration result preserves the **consumption** rejection

**C-B `[SUPERSEDED-A35.1 → A36.1-B]` (persistence wording).** The startup ratification **Skip** branch
(`main.rs:6886–6904`) may reach the Run-055 sequence handling (`:6918–6927`) and `trusted_roots` merge
(`:7140–7185`), but it derives **no v2 marker decision** ("the marker file is NOT written from unratified state").
**Sequence** effects and **marker** effects are kept separate: the Skip branch exercises sequence/roots, not marker
persistence.

**C-C `[SUPERSEDED-A35.1 → A36.1-C]` (parse vs env-read errors).** `governance_execution_policy_env_selector`
(`pqc_governance_execution_policy_surface.rs:278–283`) maps `std::env::var` **read** errors (unset / non-unicode)
to `Ok(None)` (→ absent → `Disabled`), while a **present-but-invalid** value yields a typed **parse** error. A
stable process environment does not itself prove every read *succeeds* with the same value — but the bounded
conclusion holds: a CLI-supplied selector is the same string both times (deterministic parse → identical), and a
CLI-absent selector yields the same env read result on both passes absent a process-environment change (no
environment-changing attacker is invented).

## A36.2 The two reload routes — comparison table

| Aspect | Process-start reload-apply | SIGHUP live reload |

| Production entry / state owner | `main()` startup; `ProductionLiveTrustApplyContext` over a **fresh, process-local** `LivePqcTrustState::initialize_from_loaded_bundle` (`main.rs:4450–4461`); **`NoActiveSessionsEvictor`** (no active sessions at process start) | `LiveReloadController` constructed during `run_p2p_node`; operates on the **running node's shared** live trust state; a **real** P2P session evictor |

| Outer invocation gates / v1-v2 / early returns | `ratification_gate_decision` (`:4498`): DevNet Skip (no opt-in) → legacy Run-070/073 apply, **hook not invoked**; Invoke + v2 sidecar → `preflight_run_134_v2_marker_decision` (early `Ok(None)` for v1/no-data-dir) → consume | `ratification: None` apply branch (`:1127–1140`) → legacy `apply_validated_candidate_with_previous`, **hook not invoked**; missing `authority_marker` (`:1357–1365`) → `Ok(None)`, hook not reached; v2 marker preflight present → consume |
| Expectation provenance | inline: candidate-derived env/chain/genesis/fingerprint/sequence/suite + fixed `Rotate` + **empty** proposal/decision/digest/nonce + zero epochs (A35) | `governance_execution_expectations_from_v2_candidate` (`:1605+`): same shape — `expected_proposal_id = ""`, placeholders, fixed `Rotate` |
| Consumption / evaluator / final result | `wire_…without_evaluator_context` (ReloadApply surface) → Disabled+Absent `ProceedLegacyBypass`; else fail-closed per A36.1-A; evaluator invoked, result preserves consumption rejection | `wire_…without_evaluator_context` (Sighup surface) → **identical** outcome logic |
| First possible downstream effect | **process-local** snapshot prep → swap → (NoActiveSessions) eviction request → Run-055 sequence commit → conditional v2 marker persist | **running node's shared** snapshot prep → swap → **real eviction request** → sequence commit → conditional v2 marker persist |

**Joint satisfiability:** both hook-invoked configurations are satisfiable only under: ratification gate **Invoke**
(DevNet needs `--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-enforcement-enabled`), a **v2** sidecar, and an authority-marker/
data-dir context. For **SIGHUP** specifically, the node must have passed startup and be running under the selected
policy — a configuration that startup refuses never reaches the signal handler. The governance-execution **outcome
logic is identical** across startup, reload-apply, and SIGHUP (same `wire_…without_evaluator_context`); the
**material differences** are the **effect scope** (process-local vs running-node-shared), the **evictor**
(no-op vs real), and the **policy-resolution time** (re-resolved vs captured) — not the acceptance/refusal result.

## A36.3 Effect boundaries (bounded traces)

- **reload-apply, Disabled+Absent (bypass):** validation → **process-local** snapshot prepare → swap →
  `NoActiveSessionsEvictor` eviction request (no active sessions to terminate) → Run-055 sequence commit →
  conditional/idempotent v2 marker persist. Affects **only this process's** live trust state; it does **not**
  modify another running node. Furthest effect: process-local trust swap + sequence/marker.
- **reload-apply, present carrier (fail-closed):** `consume_run_220(ReloadApply)` returns `Err` **before** any
  Run-070 apply / swap / eviction / sequence / marker (the hook runs before those mutations) → apply refused. (A
  refusal here precedes those effects; it does not prove the process performed no **earlier** writes — e.g.
  baseline load/validation already ran.)
- **SIGHUP, Disabled+Absent (bypass):** validation → **running node's shared** snapshot prepare → swap → **real
  eviction request** → sequence commit → conditional v2 marker persist. An eviction **request** is **not** proof
  every session terminated. Affects the running node's shared trust snapshot.
- **SIGHUP, present carrier (fail-closed):** `consume_run_220_sighup…` returns `Err` → the mutating preflight
  fails closed **before** swap/eviction/sequence/marker; the running node's shared state is unchanged by this
  reload.
- **ratification Skip / ratification:None / missing-marker (hook not invoked):** the legacy apply path runs
  **without** the governance-execution hook; existing bundle validation / ratification (where it executes) / marker
  / local-issuer checks are **not** transferred onto these branches — on Skip, ratification is **not** verified and
  no v2 marker is written (A36.1-B), while the apply/sequence/roots may still proceed per the documented DevNet
  legacy path.

## A36.4 Applicable policy contract

The CLI selector contract (`cli.rs:1139–1193`) is explicit: **hidden, disabled-by-default**, "**Run 215 is
source/test selector wiring only**," `production-governance-required` → "**fails closed because no real governance
execution engine is implemented**," `mainnet-governance-required` → "**fails closed**," fixtures are
"DevNet/TestNet **evidence-only**," and an explicit block of **NOT**-claims ("NOT a real governance execution
engine … NOT an autonomous-apply / apply-on-receipt / peer-majority authority claim … NOT sufficient to enable
MainNet peer-driven apply"); invalid values are a typed parse error (never silent `Disabled`).

- **Exact applicable promise / scope limitation:** the selector promises **fail-closed** behavior for the
  required policies and **evidence-only fixture** behavior otherwise, scoped as **source/test wiring** with release
  evidence deferred (Run-216). It does **not** promise real governance-execution acceptance or that it gates apply
  **independently** of the ratification gate.
- **Whether the selected route enforces it:** **Yes.** On both reload routes, when the hook is invoked a present
  carrier **fails closed** (matching the contract), and Disabled+Absent bypasses (documented Run-213/214
  compatibility). When the hook is **not** invoked (ratification Skip / `ratification:None` / missing marker), the
  apply proceeds via the **documented** legacy path — within the selector's stated scope (it does not claim to gate
  those).
- **Configuration/capability:** the selector affects apply only when the v2-marker preflight runs
  (ratification-gate Invoke + v2 sidecar + authority-marker/data-dir).
- **Furthest supported consequence:** present carrier → apply refused before mutation; Disabled+Absent → apply
  proceeds, gated by the *other* mechanisms (real ratification signature where invoked, anti-rollback), not by
  governance execution.

**Disposition:** the observed behavior **conforms to the documented contract** (fail-closed / source-test / not an
engine). This is therefore **documented-and-matched behavior**, **not** a violated contract and **not** an
unresolved candidate. **No finding minted** (and none suppressed — the contract is explicit and the implementation
matches). **Duplicate check by mechanism:** distinct from **A19-F1** (a selector *parsed but ignored with no
effect*; here the governance-execution selector **is honored** where invoked — fail-closed — and its
non-invocation on the skip path is the documented ratification-gate behavior, not a silently-ignored selector),
from **A23-F1** (signing-key↔ratification-target binding), and from **A25-F1** (Run-163 fixture byte-equality
governance-**proof** assurance). A bounded operator-facing **assurance note** is recorded (an operator who sets a
required governance-execution policy on DevNet-no-opt-in gets the documented legacy skip, not an apply-block) —
classified as documented behavior, not a finding.

## A35.1-C1 Outer-gate coverage corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A35 → A35.1-C1]`

A35's "startup continues only through Disabled+Absent" conflated **hook bypass** with **hook never invoked**. The
**ratification gate** controls whether the gate body (which contains the preflight **and** the governance-execution
hook) runs at all: `ratification_gate_decision(env, operator_opt_in)` (`pqc_ratification_policy.rs:156–174`) →
MainNet/TestNet **Invoke**; **DevNet → `Skip(DevnetNoOperatorOptIn)` unless** `--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-
enforcement-enabled`. `main.rs:6695` runs the gate body only `if startup_gate_decision.should_invoke()`; the
**Skip** branch (`:6886–6904`) explicitly **does not verify ratification, derives no marker, and never invokes the
governance-execution hook** — yet startup **continues** to the Run-055 sequence check (`:6918–6927`) and the
`trusted_roots` merge (`:7140–7185`). Even when invoked, `preflight_run_136_v2_marker_decision_for_startup` returns
`Ok(None)` **early** (`:1196–1210`) for a v1/absent `ratification_v2` or a missing `--data-dir`, **before** reaching
`consume_run_220` (`:1297`) — so the hook is not invoked there either.

**Outer-gate table (DevNet unless noted):**

| Config | Ratification gate | Hook (`consume_run_220`) invoked? | Furthest source-supported effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DevNet, **no** ratification opt-in | **Skip** | **No** (gate body skipped) | continues to Run-055 sequence check + `trusted_roots` merge — **no ratification verified**, **no marker written** |
| DevNet, opt-in, **v1**/no-v2 sidecar | Invoke | **No** (`preflight_run_136` is v2-only; v1 uses the Run-105 path) | v1 Run-105 gate + Run-120 marker; no Run-220 |
| DevNet, opt-in, v2 sidecar, **no `--data-dir`** | Invoke | **No** (preflight `Ok(None)` at `:1203`) | no marker; no Run-220; no Run-055 persistence (data-dir unset) |
| DevNet, opt-in, v2 sidecar, `--data-dir` set | Invoke | **Yes** (`:1297`) | the inner matrix (A35.1-C2) applies |
| MainNet / TestNet | **Invoke** (always) | per v2/data-dir as above | gate always invoked |
| `--consensus-authority-from-genesis` | n/a | n/a | **FATAL `exit(1)`** (A32 `main.rs:5405`) — aborts startup; **not** a skip that permits continuation |

**Selecting a "required" governance-execution policy does NOT force hook invocation:** the ratification-gate Skip
(DevNet no-opt-in) bypasses the whole gate body **regardless** of the governance-execution policy selector, so a
`ProductionGovernanceRequired`/`Mainnet…` selection on a DevNet node without ratification opt-in has **no effect** —
the hook never runs. A35's universal statement is corrected: startup also continues through the **ratification-gate
Skip** path (hook **never invoked**, ratification **not** verified), which is distinct from the Disabled+Absent
**bypass** (hook invoked, inside a path where ratification **was** verified). The genesis route is FATAL-refused,
not a continuation-permitting skip.

## A35.1-C2 Consumption / evaluator / returned rejection reconstructed `[SUPERSEDED-A35 → A35.1-C2]`

`integrate_governance_evaluator_runtime_consumption` (`…evaluator_runtime_integration.rs:268–408`): (1) `consume_surface`;
(2) if `is_legacy_bypass()` (Disabled+Absent → `NoGovernanceExecutionSupplied`) → **return `ProceedLegacyBypass`
before the evaluator**; (3) otherwise it **invokes the evaluator** `evaluate_governance_decision_source` (`:310`,
the `ProductionDecisionSourceEvaluatorInterface` = `ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`) **even after a consumption
that already fail-closed**, then (4) returns **`RuntimeConsumptionFailClosed(outcome)`** (`:397`) **preserving the
consumption-level rejection**. So A35's "present carrier reaches the evaluator → fail-closed on unavailable context"
is corrected: the evaluator is invoked, but the **final** integration outcome for a present carrier preserves the
**consumption** rejection.

**Startup expectation contradiction (the primary, binding-level reason):** startup sets
`expected_proposal_id = String::new()` (`main.rs:1092`), but `GovernanceExecutionInput::is_well_formed`
(`pqc_governance_execution_policy.rs:428–438`) requires `proposal_id` (and decision_id, digests, nonce, …) **nonempty**,
and the Run-211 validation (`:1234–1242`) requires `input.proposal_id == expected_proposal_id` **and**
`decision.proposal_id == expected_proposal_id`. With `expected_proposal_id = ""`, a **well-formed** Available carrier
(nonempty proposal_id) can never equal `""` → `WrongProposalId`; an input crafted with `proposal_id = ""` to match
fails `is_well_formed`. **Therefore no Available carrier can reach `ProceedAccepted` on the startup route** — for an
**unsatisfiable consumption binding** reason that is **independent of** (and prior to) the unavailable evaluator.

**Inner outcome table (hook invoked; per policy × load status):**

| Load \ policy | Disabled | Fixture / EmergencyCouncil (DevNet fixtures) | Production / Mainnet required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Absent** | consume=bypass → **`ProceedLegacyBypass`** → `Ok` | consume=`RequiredButAbsent` → evaluator invoked (unavailable) → **`RuntimeConsumptionFailClosed`** → `Err` | same → **`Err`** |
| **Malformed** | consume=fail-closed (malformed) → evaluator invoked → **`RuntimeConsumptionFailClosed`** → `Err` | same → `Err` | same → `Err` |
| **Available** | not bypass → consume rejects (**`WrongProposalId`**, unsatisfiable empty-`expected_proposal_id` binding) → evaluator invoked (unavailable) → **`RuntimeConsumptionFailClosed`** → `Err` | same (`WrongProposalId` binding) → `Err` | same → `Err` |
| **Invalid selector** | FATAL `exit(1)` at Run-217 (A35.1-C3) — never reaches the hook | — | — |

So **no supplied carrier receives positive acceptance** through the invoked hook — now for the corrected,
**two-independent-reasons** basis: (a) **unsatisfiable consumption binding** (empty `expected_proposal_id` vs the
nonempty-required, equality-bound input) and (b) **unavailable evaluator** (`ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`).
These are kept separate: (a) would reject an Available carrier even with a working evaluator. Positive binary
acceptance is deferred (Run-221/227).

## A35.1-C3 Selector-validation bound corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A35 → A35.1-C3]`

The early invalid-selector rejection (Run-217, `main.rs:2052`, `exit(1)`) is retained, but with precise bounds:
the early-resolved arming value (`_run_217_…`) is **not** the value later passed to the hook — the hook **re-resolves**
from `ctx_data.governance_execution_policy_selector` (the captured CLI string, `main.rs:585`) via
`from_cli_or_env` **again** at `:1106`. The two resolutions necessarily agree **under these assumptions**: (i) a
CLI-supplied selector is the **same string** both times (captured once in `ctx_data`), so a **parse** of that string
is deterministic → identical result; (ii) a CLI-**absent** selector makes the resolver read the **process
environment** on both reads, which are identical **provided the running process's environment is unchanged between
them** — the normal case (an ordinary external shell cannot mutate a running process's environment; no
environment-changing attacker is invented). Distinguishing **selector parse errors** (deterministic on a fixed
string) from **environment-read errors** (only divergent if the process env itself changed): under (i)/(ii), the
`.unwrap_or_default()` at `:1109` is a **validated defensive dead-path**. This qualification is **not** turned into a
new vulnerability — no concrete admitted path mutates the process environment mid-run.

## A35.1-C4 Effect language and disposition reassessed `[SUPERSEDED-A35 → A35.1-C4]`

**Effect language.** A35's examples — loading genesis, verifying ratification, computing a marker decision — are a
**read**, a **computation**, and an **in-memory mutation** respectively; they do **not** by themselves demonstrate
earlier **filesystem writes**, and equally A35 must not be read as proving the process performed **no** earlier
writes. Actual persistence on the startup path is the Run-055 sequence write (`check_and_update_sequence`) and the
conditional/idempotent v2 marker persist — which occur **after** the hook on the invoked path, **or** (per C1) on
the Skip branch **without** the hook. Reads/computation/in-memory state are kept distinct from persistence.

**Disposition reassessed against the corrected premise.** A35's "no finding warranted" is **not** frozen: the
premise changed (a required governance-execution policy does **not** force invocation; the ratification-gate Skip
bypasses the whole body). Reassessing — for a candidate finding there must be an **applicable contract**, an
**admission/effect trace**, a **capability scope**, and a **duplicate check**:
- **Applicable contract:** the governance-execution selector is a **hidden, source/test** DevNet/TestNet selector
  (A35 variants), and the DevNet ratification-gate Skip is **documented** ("preserves pre-Run-105 DevNet behaviour …
  NOT a passed ratification", `main.rs:6886–6893`). No documented contract promises that a DevNet governance-execution
  "required" policy is enforced **independently of** ratification opt-in. So **no applicable independent contract is
  established as violated** on DevNet.

  continues to sequence/roots without ratification verify or governance-execution enforcement) is an

- **Duplicate check:** distinct mechanism from A24-family / A25-F1 (governance **proof**) and from the unwired-
  authority residuals; no existing ID matches this governance-**execution** gate-skip composition.

**Decision:** **no finding minted** — but for the **corrected reason** (hidden source/test selector + documented
intentional DevNet ratification skip ⇒ no independent applicable contract shown violated), **not** A35's original
reason (which addressed only the invoked-hook path). Recorded as a precise **operator-facing assurance observation**
under **OBL-GOV-2**: *on the selected binary, the governance-execution policy selector is gated behind
ratification-gate invocation; under the documented DevNet no-opt-in Skip it has no effect, and startup proceeds to
Run-055 sequence/`trusted_roots` without ratification verification or governance-execution enforcement.* This is

Run-221/227) kept **distinct from unexecuted-runtime**.

## A35.3 `.unwrap_or_default()` resolution (main.rs:1109)

`from_cli_or_env` returns `Err(GovernanceExecutionPolicySelectorParseError)` on an invalid selector, and
`.unwrap_or_default()` would fall back to **`Disabled`** (default; test `default_runtime_arming_is_disabled:585`).
**However, the same selector value is validated fail-closed earlier** at the Run-217 gate (`main.rs:2052`, in
`main()`), which runs **before** `main()` invokes `run_p2p_node` (`:6152`) → the preflight (`:6784` → `:1176`) → the
`:1297` consume. An invalid selector therefore **`exit(1)`s at `:2052` before `:1109` is reached**; the only values
that reach `:1109` already parsed `Ok` (or both-absent → Disabled). So on the startup route the `.unwrap_or_default()`
**cannot discard a reachable policy error** — it is a **validated defensive dead-path**, not a silent downgrade.
(Traced the same selector value and call order; not assumed from the comment.)

## A35.4 Policy / load-status matrix — Public DevNet startup

| Load status \ policy | `Disabled` (default) | Fixture / EmergencyCouncil / Production / Mainnet (explicit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Absent carrier** | `NoGovernanceExecutionSupplied` → **`ProceedLegacyBypass`** → `Ok` → startup continues (A25 control) | `GovernanceExecutionRequiredButAbsent` → **FailClosed** → startup aborts before mutation |
| **Malformed sibling/carrier** | **FailClosed** (parser/routing fail-closed, independent of the bypass, which is absent-only) | **FailClosed** |
| **Well-formed Available carrier** | not a bypass (`is_bypassed` = absent-only) → reaches evaluator stage → **FailClosed** (`ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`, no bindable evaluator context) | reaches evaluator stage → **FailClosed** (expectation placeholders cannot match; evaluator unavailable) |
| **Invalid selector** | **FATAL `exit(1)` at Run-217 (`:2052`)** — never reaches `consume_run_220` | same |

Distinctions held: the governance **hook is invoked** (consume_run_220) only when the outer gates admit the preflight;
an **outer gate** (no v2 sidecar / no `--data-dir` / genesis-refusal) **skips the hook**; the **hook returns a bypass**
only for `Disabled`+`Absent`; **no "supplied carrier accepted" path exists** (every present carrier fails closed);
**startup continues to protected effects only on the Disabled+Absent bypass** — i.e. with governance-execution
**not enforced**, the effects gated by the *other* mechanisms (real ratification signature, Run-163 proof policy,
Run-055 anti-rollback), not by governance execution.

## A35.5 Expectation-provenance table (`main.rs:1087–1104`)

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `expected_environment`, `expected_chain_id`, `expected_genesis_hash`, `expected_authority_root_fingerprint`, `expected_authority_domain_sequence`, `expected_suite_id` | **authenticated candidate** (`decision.candidate()`, derived from the verified v2 ratification) |

| `expected_proposal_id`, `expected_decision_id`, `expected_candidate_digest`, `expected_governance_proof_digest`, `expected_replay_nonce` | **empty-string placeholders** |
| `expected_on_chain_proof_digest`, `expected_custody_attestation_digest` | **`None` placeholders** |
| `expected_effective_epoch = 0`, `now_epoch = 0` | **zero placeholders** |

These expectations are **consumed only on the present-carrier path**, which **fails closed before any mutation** (the
placeholders cannot match a real carrier and the production evaluator is unavailable). On the `Disabled`+`Absent`
**bypass** path they are **not** meaningfully evaluated (the legacy bypass short-circuits before the evaluator stage).

## A35.6 Provenance and effect boundary

A **reachable acceptance** on this route is **only** the `Disabled`+`Absent` `ProceedLegacyBypass` → it establishes
**permitted absence** of governance execution — **not** authorization, **not** evaluator approval, **not** cryptographic
verification, **not** field-consistency acceptance of a carrier. On `Ok(())`, the preflight returns
`Ok(Some(decision))` and startup proceeds to the named downstream effects: **Run-055 sequence update**
(`check_and_update_sequence`), **v2 marker persistence** (`persist_accepted_v2_marker_after_commit_boundary` —
conditional/idempotent: a no-op when `should_persist` is false), and **in-memory `trusted_roots` preparation** — all
distinct from, and preceding, actual **P2P/service startup**. These effects are gated by the *other* mechanisms, not by
governance execution. A **fail-closed** hook result (`Err`) returns via `.map_err(…)?` **before** the sequence/marker/
roots of this preflight — but (per the stated caution) this does **not** prove the process performed no **earlier**
writes: boot-genesis load, the real ratification verification, and the in-memory marker-decision computation already ran
before `consume_run_220`.

## A35.7 Disposition

| Behaviour | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| `Disabled`+`Absent` → `ProceedLegacyBypass` → startup continues | **Intentional bypass** (Run-214 legacy compatibility, preserved bit-for-bit) |
| Any present (`Available`) carrier → FailClosed at the evaluator stage | **Unavailable implementation** — the binary cannot bind a Run-222 evaluator context (`ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`); positive binary acceptance is explicitly **deferred to Run-221/227** |
| Explicit policy + `Absent` → `RequiredButAbsent` FailClosed; `Malformed` → FailClosed | **Implemented fail-closed refusal** (no silent downgrade) |
| Invalid selector → `exit(1)` | **Implemented fail-closed startup refusal** (Run-217) |
| `.unwrap_or_default()` at `:1109` | **Validated defensive dead-path** (Run-217 dominates) — not a silent error-discard |

**Net:** a configured governance-execution policy on the startup route **does not accept or act on any supplied
governance-execution carrier** — it either **bypasses** (`Disabled`+`Absent`) or **fails closed** (every present
carrier, every absent-under-explicit-policy, every malformed, every invalid selector). Positive governance-execution
enforcement is **unavailable implementation** (deferred), not a violated contract and not silent acceptance. **No new
finding** is warranted (intentional-bypass + unavailable-implementation + implemented fail-closed refusals; the
`unwrap_or_default` concern is resolved as a validated dead-path). This is **not** transferred to the Run-163 proof
(A24–A26), the real ratification signature, or custody selectors.

## C1 — Withdraw the unsupported view-ordering conclusion `[SUPERSEDED-A34 → A34.1-C1]`

A34 called the proposal/justification view ordering "unnecessary under lock-monotonicity + A31 commit ordering."
The cited checks establish only: `safety_decision` compares the **justification view against the locked view**
(`hse.rs:2150`); `try_commit_with_qc` compares the **stored views of B, P, G** (`hse.rs:1886`). Neither establishes
any relationship between the **embedded QC's certified block/view** and the **proposal's parent/view**, nor proves
that omitting such a relationship preserves safety. The grep showing no proposal-view↔justify-view check is
evidence of absence **within its search scope**, not evidence the check is unnecessary.

**Superseded wording** ("unnecessary," "not needed," "absent by design") → **"No enforcing check for the embedded
QC ↔ proposal parent/view relationship was identified in the inspected engine path; its necessity and security
consequence remain an explicit protocol-invariant/proof question."** The **observed equal/higher-view predicate
acceptance** (`Safe(ViewSufficiency)` on `justify_qc.view >= locked.view`) is preserved as a fact; it is turned
into neither a vulnerability claim nor a safety assurance.

## C2 — Correct the finding threshold `[SUPERSEDED-A34 → A34.1-C2]`

A34 required an "effect-to-finality trace" before a finding could be recorded. That is **withdrawn** — it is not
the standing audit standard. The standing separation is:

1. **Applicable contract / invariant.**
2. **Source-confirmed enforcement difference.**
3. **Admitted input and bounded effect.**
4. **Production reachability.**
5. **Further security consequences and severity.**

A demonstrated contract violation may support a bounded library/integration finding **without** a
conflicting-finality demonstration; equally, **a different API's contract does not automatically bind this engine
path.** Reassessed parent/QC observation on that basis:
- (1→2) `verify_block_proposal` (`lib.rs:839`) **explicitly** checks `qc.block_id == parent_block_id`; the
  inspected verified-ingestion engine path (`ingest_verified_proposal` → `register_block_with_admission` →
  `safety_decision`) **does not** — a source-confirmed enforcement difference.
- (3) the conditional trace (C4) reaches **internal self-voting**.
- (4) current production authority wiring (`proposal_vote_authority=None`, `current_auth=None`) **blocks that
  handler path** (fail-closed).
- (1, unresolved) the **missing link** is whether `parent_block_id == justify_qc.block_id` is an **applicable
  security requirement of this engine path** — `verify_block_proposal` is a **different API**, so its contract does
  **not** by itself establish that `ingest_verified_proposal` violates **its** contract.

**Disposition:** because the applicable-requirement question for the engine path is unresolved, this is **retained
as an unresolved security candidate under OBL-CONS-9** — **not dismissed** (lack of finality evidence is not the
reason), and **not minted** (no established engine-path contract to violate yet; not forced, not auto-classified
under A17-F1). It would become a mintable bounded finding if the engine-path requirement is established by spec or
by an existing applicable contract.

## C3 — Correct "self-certifying own_qc" `[SUPERSEDED-A34 → A34.1-C3]`

A34's "commits rely on self-certifying `own_qc`" is replaced. Precisely: `on_qc` (`hse.rs:1797–1799`) **attaches a
logical QC** to the block node (`blocks.get_mut(&qc.block_id).own_qc = Some(qc)`); `try_commit_with_qc` checks
**`own_qc` presence** (`own_qc.is_none() → return`) and the **stored block view/height** conditions
(`g_view<p_view<b_view`; `g_height>committed_height`; `g_view>committed.view`). It does **not** independently
re-authenticate endorsements. **Authentication is assumed from the earlier admission route** that formed/attached
the QC (ordinary verified ingestion of votes; local self-vote bookkeeping; catch-up per-signer `on_vote` — A17-F1
scope). The already-reviewed distinctions among those routes are preserved and not reopened.

Consequently, A34's argument "no commit-effect trace because commits use self-certifying `own_qc`" is restated:
the commit predicate consumes `own_qc` **presence + stored view/height**, with endorsement authentication assumed
upstream; the safe-voting `justify_qc` and the commit-predicate `own_qc` are distinct objects, so the parent↔QC
observation is a safe-voting-path question, not resolved or excused by the commit predicate.

## C4 — Bound the finite witness accurately `[SUPERSEDED-A34 → A34.1-C4]`

A34's T1 is **downgraded to a conditional predicate trace** (not "jointly satisfiable" in production). The
`ingest_proposal` gate order (`bhse.rs:4610–4639`) and `safety_decision` fix the required premises:

| Premise | Source gate | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Epoch match | `:4611` | `proposal.epoch == current_epoch` |
| Receiver current view | `:4619–4628` | the **proposal advances** `current_view` to `view` if higher (resetting `voted_in_view`); `view < current_view` rejected — so the receiver need **not** have pre-advanced; receiving the proposal advances it |
| Correct proposer | `:4631` | `from == leader_for_view(view)` — the Byzantine proposer must **be** the leader for that view |
| Not already voted in the view | `:4637` | `voted_in_view == false` (true after a fresh advance) |
| Receiver lock | `safety_decision:2150` | needs `justify_qc.view >= locked.view`; the receiver need **not** have **installed the embedded QC as its lock** — only its existing lock's view matters |
| Candidate distinct / retention / slot | `ingest_verified_proposal` / `register_block_with_admission` | retention + block-slot admission (verified path) |
| Authentic QC + signer set | stated premise | authentic over the QC's **actual** certified statement; no forgery, no fixture substitution |
| Admitted snapshot + outer proposal signature | `bcl.rs` snapshot + `verify_proposal_msg_with_domain` | **required; unwired in production** |

So **holding or receiving the QC does not require** the receiver to have pre-advanced its view (the proposal
advances it), nor to have installed that QC as its lock (safety compares justify vs the **existing** lock); it
**does require** not having voted in the (post-advance) view and the proposer being that view's leader. Because
the **supplied snapshot is unwired in production** (fail-closed reject), **the full witness is not jointly
satisfiable on the selected binary** — it is a **conditional predicate trace** whose furthest effect, under the
supplied-snapshot path with the premises above, is an **internal self-vote**.

**Control (comparison case, not a correctness proof):** `parent_block_id == qc.block_id` and
`proposal.view > qc.view`, `qc.view >= locked.view` → the honest `Safe(ViewSufficiency)` self-vote. Labeled a
comparison, not evidence of protocol correctness.

## C5 — Repair remaining-work classification `[SUPERSEDED-A34 → A34.1-C5]`

Adding a live-path parent check is **not** called "missing implementation" — a possible remediation is not evidence
the implementation violates its contract. Classification separated:

- **Source facts established:** `verify_block_proposal:839` checks parent↔QC-block and is **unwired** in qbind-node;
  the verified-ingestion engine path performs no such check; no proposal-view↔justify-view check exists in the
  inspected path; the conditional self-vote trace (C4); production fail-closes before this handler.
- **Applicable specification / invariant unresolved:** whether `parent_block_id == justify_qc.block_id` (and any
  proposal-view/justify-view relationship) is a **required** security invariant **of this engine path**.
- **Proof or counterexample needed:** a protocol argument or a multi-node Byzantine schedule deciding whether the
  `ViewSufficiency` short-circuit is safe on the live path absent the binding (out of scope here; a passing
  experiment would **not** constitute a general safety proof).
- **Runtime validation:** **UNEXECUTED.**
- **Implementation work required:** only **if** the invariant above is established — not asserted here.

**OBL-CONS-9 remains SOURCE-PARTIAL** with its original scope; completed source traces (A31/A32/A33/A34) preserved.
The parent/QC and view-ordering questions are **resolved to this disposition** (unresolved security candidate /
open invariant) and are **not** re-queued as further authentication or missing-check search; broader safety is not
declared complete.

## A34.1 A33 correction ledger (concise; supersedes the cited A33 statements)

**A. Actual production rejection** `[SUPERSEDED-A33 → A34.1-A]`. The current binary wires
`proposal_vote_authority = None` (`main.rs:6148`) **and** `current_auth = None` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3140`).
So the effective Proposal/Vote authority is `None`, reaching the **Required-policy rejection at `bcl.rs:6423–6434`**
("verification context unavailable"), assuming earlier transport/binding/decode gates pass. **D7-A1**
(`:6323–6337`) is the **distinct** case of a *supplied* authority **without** current authorization. A33's
description of D7-A1 as the universal production first rejection is withdrawn; neither branch is "first before the
earlier transport/binding/decode gates."

**B. Absent QC is selection, not error recovery** `[SUPERSEDED-A33 → A34.1-B]`. At `bcl.rs:6612–6645`, a **retained
verified QC = `None` selects `engine.on_proposal_event` directly** (not a fallback); a verified-entrypoint **error
returns** with **no** legacy fallback. An absent-QC proposal can take the direct legacy entry **even under Required
policy with an otherwise-admitted supplied snapshot** — distinct from (i) the current binary (which supplies **no**
snapshot) and (ii) LocalFixtureUnsigned. For absent QC, `proposal.qc.as_ref().map(...) = None`, so with an existing
lock **no justification-view comparison can succeed** and `safety_decision` takes the **ancestry branch** (Safe
only if the parent chain reaches the locked block; else Unsafe). Direct public-engine calls are separate from
handler-selected calls.

**C. Evidence is relative and non-authorizing** `[SUPERSEDED-A33 → A34.1-C]`. A `VerifiedQuorumCertificate` records
**successful verification against the trusted inputs supplied at that call**. Its private fields prevent ordinary
construction outside the defining module; they do **not** independently establish trustworthy provider selection,
present authorization, persistent freshness, or production activation. (No production mock-backend vulnerability is
implied or claimed.)

**D. Unwired authorization fails closed** `[SUPERSEDED-A33 → A34.1-D]`. The production path is **rejected before
downstream checks** (fail-closed), not "operating with authorization checks absent."

A33's supported authentication composition (outer-sig ⟂ embedded-QC verification; exact evidence↔wire-QC match;
chain/epoch binding; verifier-constructed `VerifiedQuorumCertificate`) is preserved.

## A34.2 The two relationships — contract / enforcement table

Producer (honest leader, `on_leader_step`, `bhse.rs:4066–4081`): `parent_id = locked_qc().block_id (|| committed)`
and `justify_qc = locked_qc()`, so an honest leader sets **`parent_block_id == justify_qc.block_id`** — a
**producer convention**, not a receiver guarantee.

| Property | Required by protocol/API? | Honest-producer convention? | Checked by the selected-binary receiver? | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **(1)** `proposal.header.parent_block_id == embedded QC block_id` | **Yes, by one API** — `verify_block_proposal` (`lib.rs:824–847`): `qc.block_id != parent_block_id → BlockHeaderMismatch` (`:839`) | **Yes** (producer sets both from `locked_qc`) | **No** — `verify_block_proposal`/`evaluate_proposal_for_vote`/`decide_and_record_vote`/`hotstuff_decide_and_maybe_record_vote` have **no qbind-node production caller**; the live path (`ingest_verified_proposal` → `register_block_with_admission` → `safety_decision`) performs **no** such check | **Enforced only by an UNWIRED library API + convention; absent on the live path** |
| **(2)** `proposal.view` strictly `>` / constrained vs `justify_qc.view` | **No** — no API requires it | n/a | **No** — `safety_decision` compares `justify_qc.view` to **`locked.view`** (not to `proposal.view`); no receiver check of proposal-view vs justify-view exists (grep-confirmed absent) | **Unnecessary under the lock-monotonicity invariant** |

Live-path justification derivation: on the **verified** path `register_block_with_admission` (`hse.rs:1606–1610`)
sets `justify_qc = QuorumCertificate::new(evidence.certificate().block_id, evidence.certificate().height,
evidence.signers())` — derived from the authenticated evidence, but **not tied to `parent_id`**. `safety_decision`
then uses `justify_qc.view` for the `ViewSufficiency` short-circuit (`hse.rs:2150`, inclusive `>=`), **without**
consulting `justify_qc.block_id` or requiring it to equal the parent.

## A34.3 Finite source traces

Membership `M = {0,1,2,3}` (unit weight, `q = ceil(2·4/3) = 3`); state: existing lock `L = QC(block_L, view=5)`;
receiver `current_view = 6`; authentic QC signatures are a **stated premise over the QC's actual certified
statement** (no forgery, no fixture substitution). Stages kept separate: (1) handler admission; (2) engine
registration + earlier mutations; (3) safe-voting decision; (4) vote bookkeeping/action; (5) outbound
authorization/signing/handoff; (6) any later QC/commit.

| Trace | Jointly satisfiable prereqs | First rejection / furthest supported effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **T1: valid QC certifying X ≠ proposed parent Y** (`qc.block_id=X, qc.view=6 ≥ 5`; `parent_block_id=Y`) | epoch=authorized, leader `from=leader_for_view(6)`, view=6, not-voted, M-membership, retention/slot ok; **authorization snapshot** required | **Production:** rejected at stage 1 (effective-pv `None`, `bcl:6423–6434`) — not reachable. **Implemented (supplied-snapshot) path:** stages 1–2 pass (outer-sig ok; embedded-QC of X authentic; `evidence==qc`; chain/epoch ok; registered with `parent_id=Y`, `justify_qc=QC(X,6)`); stage 3 `safety_decision` → `justify_qc.view 6 ≥ lock 5` → **`Safe(ViewSufficiency)`, ancestry NOT walked, Y never compared to X** → stage 4 **self-vote** (furthest effect). **No parent↔QC-block rejection** (`verify_block_proposal` unwired). **No stage-6 commit trace** (commits use self-certifying `own_qc` + parent chain, not `justify_qc`). |
| **T2: justify_qc.view == proposal.view (6,6) and > (7 vs 6)** | as above | `safety_decision` compares justify (6 or 7) to **lock (5)** only → `Safe(ViewSufficiency)` in both; **no proposal-view/justify-view rejection** (relationship 2 absent by design) |
| **T3a: absent QC, no lock** | no `locked_qc` | `safety_decision` step 1 → **`Safe(NoLock)`** → self-vote |
| **T3b: absent QC, existing lock** | lock `L` present; `justify_qc = None` | step 3 skipped (no justify_qc); **ancestry walk**: reaches `block_L` → `Safe(Ancestry)`; else → **`Unsafe`** (no vote) |
| **T4: control (intended relationships)** | `parent_block_id == qc.block_id = X`, `qc.view=6 ≥ 5` | all checks consistent → `Safe(ViewSufficiency)` → self-vote (the honest-producer case) |

A generated self-vote (stage 4) is **not** a signed or transmitted vote (stage 5 outbound signing/authorization is
separately gated, A26/A27/A29.1 — and the production authorization is unwired). An accepted predicate is **not**
conflicting finality. The unwired production authorization remains a reachability boundary; its implementation is
not invented here.

## A34.4 Bounded disposition and remaining evidence category

**Relationship (1) parent_block_id ↔ QC block_id — unresolved specification/proof assumption (not forced finding).**
The equality **is** an intended API property (`verify_block_proposal:839`) and an honest-producer convention, but
the API that enforces it is **unwired** and the selected binary's live proposal path does **not** check it; the
`ViewSufficiency` short-circuit trusts `justify_qc.view` without binding the QC to the parent. This is a
**source-established live-path divergence** (not erased by its lack of production reachability, and **not**
dismissed under A17-F1 or the unwired-authority residual). However, the furthest supported acceptance-and-effect
trace stops at a **self-vote on the snapshot-gated, non-production-reachable implemented path** (T1): there is
**no** finite trace to a commit or conflicting finality (commits rely on self-certifying `own_qc` + the parent
chain, A31), and demonstrating a safety violation would require a multi-node Byzantine schedule that is **out of
scope**. So **no new finding is minted** (no demonstrated violated security property with a finite effect trace to
finality) and the issue is **not dismissed**: it is recorded as a precise OBL-CONS-9 residual.
**Exact missing evidence / remaining category:** either (a) **missing implementation** — wire a receiver check
binding `parent_block_id == justify_qc.block_id` into the live path (e.g. inside `ingest_verified_proposal` /
`register_block_with_admission` before `safety_decision`), or (b) a **protocol proof / Byzantine-schedule
experiment** showing the `ViewSufficiency` rule is safe on the live path absent that binding. This is **not**
re-queued as generic "more source review" — the source question is resolved to this boundary.

**Relationship (2) proposal.view vs justify_qc.view — unnecessary under a supported invariant.** The implemented
safe-voting rule gates `justify_qc.view >= locked.view` (the monotonic lock is the reference, not the proposal
view), and the commit predicate separately enforces strictly-increasing `B/P/G` views via self-certifying
`own_qc` (A31). No receiver check of proposal-view vs justify-view is present **or needed**; a proposal-view/justify
-view gap is permitted by design. **Disposition: unnecessary under lock-monotonicity + the A31 commit ordering.**

**Tests (inspected, not executed):** `crates/qbind-consensus/tests/consensus_verify_tests.rs` asserts
`verify_block_proposal` rejects `qc.block_id != parent_block_id` with `BlockHeaderMismatch` (`lib.rs:840`) — but it
exercises the **unwired** library API, **not** the binary's `ingest_proposal`/`safety_decision` path; it therefore
establishes the API property, **not** live-path enforcement. The engine safety/proposal tests assert the
`safety_decision` branch outcomes and the verified-QC handoff (A32/A33), not the parent↔QC binding on the live
path.

## A33.1 Carried A32 qualifications (additive corrections, verified)

1. **Reachability ≠ a contained call.** `ingest_proposal` enforces `safety_decision` (A32), but that is a
   downstream implementation detail, not selected-binary admission. Production wires `current_auth = None`
   (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3140`). First rejecting branch: **present authority, no current authorization** →
   the snapshot `None` arm under Required → **D7-A1 "current authorization unavailable — no current-authorization
   owner wired"** (`bcl.rs:6323–6338`), `return` before outer-signature verify (`:6353`), embedded-QC verify
   (`:6439`), and any engine entry. **Absent authority** (no verification context) → under Required → "verification
   context unavailable" (`bcl.rs:6324`/`:6423`). Predicate execution is **not** production-reachable merely
   because the handler contains the call.
2. **Finding attribution.** A17-F1 covers **restore-catch-up**'s missing endorsement verification. Automatic
   attribution of **every legacy proposal's empty-signer justification** to A17-F1 is **withdrawn** — the legacy
   `ingest_proposal` justify-QC projection is a **different route**; absent a matching finding record and
   mechanism, the legacy-proposal empty-signer case is an **open question**, not a duplicate of A17-F1.
3. **Mutation order.** `ingest_proposal` performs **future-view advancement/reset** first: `if view >
   current_view { current_view = view; proposed_in_view = false; voted_in_view = false }`
   (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4619–4622`) — **before** the current-view and leader checks (`:4626`, `:4631`). A
   proposal for a future view thus **advances `current_view` and resets the flags with no rollback** even if the
   subsequent leader check returns `None`. Distinguish **legacy insert-then-evict** registration (`register_block`
   may evict the just-inserted candidate under slot pressure — candidate persistence is **not** universal) from
   the **verified** path's candidate-retention guarantee (`register_block_with_admission` reserves retention +
   a block slot by evicting **other** blocks, never the candidate). These view/flag mutations **lack rollback**.
4. **Implemented rule, not a proof.** `justify_qc.view >= locked.view` is the **implemented** safe-voting rule;
   source comments and predicate tests do **not** establish a full HotStuff safety proof.
