## A33.2 Ordered admission map — three classifications

**1. Selected binary at this revision (actual startup inputs, first rejection).** Inbound Proposal under the
production Required policy with `current_auth = None`: the handler matches the current-authorization snapshot
(`bcl.rs:~6280`) → `None` arm → **D7-A1 reject "current authorization unavailable"** (`:6330`), `return`. The
outer-signature verifier, the embedded-QC verifier, the freshness ticket, and both engine entrypoints are **not
reached**. **First rejection = D7-A1.** (The self-vote / `safety_decision` enforcement that A32 located is
therefore not exercised on the production inbound route.)

**2. Implemented handler with explicitly supplied authorized context (conditional/library/test — production does
NOT supply it).** With a bound snapshot `snap`, the ordered chain is:
`epoch == snap.authorized_epoch()` (`:6294`, else D7-A2 reject) → **outer-signature** `verify_proposal_msg_with_domain`
(`:6353`; recomputes the canonical v2 preimage from the message + trusted domain; wire-chain gate before crypto;
Err → reject) → **every present embedded wire QC** verified via `verify_quorum_certificate_with_domain` under the
**same admitted `snap`** (`:6439+`; a valid outer signature does **not** excuse an invalid embedded QC) → **freshness**
ticket confirmation → **entrypoint selection** (`:6612`): `Some(verified)` → `on_verified_proposal_event`
(`bhse.rs:4393`) → `ingest_verified_proposal` (`:4520`) → `ingest_proposal` with evidence → `register_block_with_admission`
(retain verified justification) → `safety_decision` → self-vote; **on verified-entrypoint error → fail-closed, NO
legacy fallback** (`bcl.rs:6648`). This path authenticates the justification end-to-end, but **production never
supplies the snapshot**.

**3. Direct legacy engine entry (caller responsibilities, absent guarantees).** `on_proposal_event` (`bhse.rs:4213`)
→ `ingest_proposal` with `verified_evidence = None`: the justify-QC is the **logical-only** wire projection
`QuorumCertificate::new(wire_qc.block_id, wire_qc.height, vec![])` — **empty signers, no authentication**;
`safety_decision` then trusts `justify_qc.view`. Caller must authenticate the QC; this entry does **not**. Reached
only on the **absent-QC / LocalFixtureUnsigned** (non-Required) passthrough — **not** the production Required route.

| Property | Where / status |
| --- | --- |
| Outer proposal signature validity | **Enforced** — `verify_proposal_msg_with_domain` (`bcl.rs:6353`), on the snapshot-gated path |
| Embedded QC constituent signatures, membership, quorum, chain, epoch | **Enforced** — `verify_quorum_certificate_with_domain` → `verify_quorum_certificate_core` (`qc_verify_domain.rs:959–1127`), every present embedded QC under the admitted `snap` |
| Exact verified-evidence ↔ embedded-wire-QC correspondence | **Enforced** — `ingest_verified_proposal` `evidence.certificate() != qc → EvidenceCertificateMismatch` (`bhse.rs:4538`); whole `WireQuorumCertificate` incl. bitmap + signatures |
| Derivation of stored QC view/block_id/signers | **Enforced (verified path)** — the retained `VerifiedQuorumCertificate` carries verified `certificate` (block_id, height→view) and verified `signers`; the verified path derives justification from evidence, never the wire projection. **Legacy path:** derived from the unauthenticated wire projection (empty signers) |
| Proposal parent ID ↔ justified (QC) block ID | **Absent explicit check** in the traced bodies — neither `ingest_verified_proposal` nor `safety_decision` requires `proposal.header.parent_block_id == qc.block_id`; the QC authenticates its own certified block, which is not required equal to the proposal's parent. Assumed-by-protocol; see residual |
| Ordering between proposal view and justification view | **Absent explicit check** of `proposal.view` vs `justify_qc.view`; `safety_decision` compares `justify_qc.view` to `locked.view` only. Assumed-by-protocol; see residual |
| Authorization generation + engine/verifier membership agreement | **Enforced on the supplied-snapshot path** (engine-context correspondence + `snap.authorized_epoch`/verifier membership); **ABSENT in production** — no `current_auth` snapshot is generated/wired (`:3140` → D7-A1) |

## A33.4 `VerifiedQuorumCertificate` construction boundary

The type has **private fields** (`qc_verify_domain.rs:521–529`). Its **only** constructor is
`verify_quorum_certificate_with_domain` (`:878–911`), which runs `verify_quorum_certificate_core`
(wire-chain gate, epoch gate, membership span, `ceil(2W/3)` voting-power threshold, and **vote-signature
verification**, `retain_signers = true`) **before** building the struct. Therefore **possession of a
`VerifiedQuorumCertificate` guarantees** its constituent signatures verified, met the threshold under the recorded
membership, and are bound to the recorded chain/epoch/domain. The only other `-> VerifiedQuorumCertificate` site
(`binary_consensus_loop.rs:22341`) is a `#[cfg(test)]` helper that returns the verifier's output — there is **no
struct-literal bypass** outside the module. Retention/resource admission (`reserve_verified_justification`,
`reserve_block_slot_for_new`) performs **no** cryptographic verification; it is byte/slot accounting only.

## A33.5 Finite case table (first rejection / furthest supported effect)

| Case | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Required policy, missing authority / current authorization | **D7-A1** "current authorization unavailable" (`bcl.rs:6330`) or "verification context unavailable" (`:6423`) — **first production rejection**, before any verify/engine step |
| Valid outer proposal, **invalid embedded QC** | rejected at `verify_quorum_certificate_with_domain` (`:6439+`); a valid outer signature does **not** rescue it (supplied-snapshot path) |
| Valid QC, **mismatched supplied evidence** | `ingest_verified_proposal` → `EvidenceCertificateMismatch` (`bhse.rs:4538`) |
| Valid QC whose **block_id ≠ proposed parent** | **no rejection on this axis** — the traced path has no parent↔QC-block identity check; the QC authenticates its own block; furthest effect is admission of a proposal whose justification is not its parent (assumed-by-protocol; residual) |
| Justification view equal / higher than lock | `safety_decision` → `Safe(ViewSufficiency)` (inclusive `>=`, A32), ancestry skipped |
| **Absent embedded QC** | verified path refuses (`MissingEmbeddedQc`, `bhse.rs:4532`) — routed to legacy entry instead; **no-lock/bootstrap** → `safety_decision` `Safe(NoLock)`; **existing lock** → legacy `justify_qc` (logical-only) compared to lock, else ancestry/Unsafe |
| Verified-entrypoint refusal | **fail-closed, NO legacy fallback** (`bcl.rs:6648`) |
| Direct legacy entry with logical justification | `safety_decision` trusts the unauthenticated `justify_qc.view`; **separated from network admission** (reached only on the non-Required/LocalFixtureUnsigned passthrough, not the production Required route) |

**Tests inspected (not executed):** the engine proposal/safety tests assert the happy-path verified handoff
(`inbound_proposal_verified_qc_handoff_total`) and the `safety_decision` branch outcomes; they assert the
predicate/handoff behaviour under **supplied** evidence/snapshots and do **not** establish that production supplies
a snapshot, nor the parent↔QC-block / proposal-view ordering relationships, nor Byzantine-schedule safety.

## A33.6 Disposition and residuals

- **No new finding.** The proposal-specific authentication is **implemented and well-composed**: outer-signature
  verification is independent of embedded-QC verification; the embedded QC is verified under the admitted
  snapshot; `VerifiedQuorumCertificate` possession guarantees verification (private fields, single verifier
  constructor); exact evidence↔wire-QC correspondence and chain/epoch binding are enforced; a verified-entrypoint
  failure does not fall back to the legacy path. The entire verified chain is **gated behind the
  current-authorization snapshot, which production leaves unwired** (`:3140` → D7-A1 reject) — this is the SAME
  **IMPLEMENTATION-REQUIRED** residual recorded in A30.1 (no production `AuthorizedProposalVoteSnapshot` supplier),
  **not** a new defect. The legacy logical-only path is **Required-rejected** in production and is a route
  distinct from A17-F1 catch-up.
- **Named source residuals (exact, not "review more deeply"):** within the implemented (snapshot-gated) verified
  path, two relationships are **not explicitly enforced** by the traced bodies — **(a) proposal
  `parent_block_id` ↔ embedded QC `block_id`** identity, and **(b)** any ordering between `proposal.view` and
  `justify_qc.view`. They are assumed-by-protocol on a path that is **not production-reachable** today; the exact
  unread relationship to resolve, should a production snapshot supplier be wired, is whether
  `on_verified_proposal_event`/`ingest_verified_proposal` (or an earlier caller) must bind the embedded QC's
  certified block to the proposal's parent before `safety_decision` consumes the justification view. This matters
  because `safety_decision`'s `ViewSufficiency` short-circuit trusts `justify_qc.view` without that binding.
- **Separation preserved:** source (this pass) vs dependency vs runtime (UNEXECUTED) vs missing-implementation
  (the unwired snapshot) are kept distinct. No Byzantine-schedule / full safety-liveness claim is made.

**OBL-CONS-9 → SOURCE-PARTIAL** (unchanged status, sub-boundary advanced): the proposal-justification
authentication + parent-binding sub-boundary is now resolved to its caller/implementation boundaries (production
first-rejection D7-A1; implemented-but-snapshot-gated verified chain; legacy unauthenticated route; the two named
binding residuals). The commit predicate (A31) and safe-voting predicate/enforcement (A32) sub-boundaries remain
complete. Broader conflicting-vote schedules and full safety/liveness remain outstanding and are not moved or
manufactured. **A17-F1, A1-F3, A33-F1** preserved and untouched; duplicate check finds no distinct violated
property with an admission-and-effect trace, so nothing is minted or suppressed.

All 54 obligation identities, finding IDs, and aliases preserved (no global index rewrite). Runtime remains
**UNEXECUTED**; **C5** remains **OPEN**.

## A32.2 Exact safe-voting rules and caller selection

**`safety_decision(block_id)`** (`hse.rs:2128–2177`) — the single authoritative predicate; branch order:
1. `locked_qc` is `None` → **`Safe(NoLock)`** (returns before any candidate lookup).
2. candidate `blocks.get(block_id)` is `None` → **`Unsafe`** (ancestry unverifiable).
3. `block_node.justify_qc` present ∧ `justify_qc.view >= locked.view` (**inclusive `>=`**) → **`Safe(ViewSufficiency)`**
   — **short-circuits; the ancestry walk is skipped**.
4. else **unbounded** ancestor walk over `parent_id` links until `current.id == locked.block_id` →
   **`Safe(Ancestry)`**, or break on no-parent-link / missing-parent → **`Unsafe`**.

**`is_safe_to_vote_on_block`** (`hse.rs:2111`) = thin wrapper `matches!(safety_decision(_), Safe(_))`.

**`bounded_safety_decision(block_id, max_hops)`** (`hse.rs:2198–2247`) — identical branch order and `>=`
short-circuit, but a **bounded** walk: `SafeNoLock` / `CandidateAbsent` / `SafeViewSufficiency` /
`SafeAncestry{hops}` (`hops==0` ⇒ candidate IS the lock) / `BoundExhausted` (at `max_hops`) / `NoParentLink` /
`ParentAbsent`; never calls the unbounded predicate first; finite on a cyclic graph.

**`BasicHotStuffEngine::is_safe_to_vote_at_height(justify_qc_view)`** (`bhse.rs:5061`) — a **separate scalar**
helper: no block lookup, no ancestry; `locked_height().is_none()` → true; `Some(jv) if jv >= locked_view` → true;
else false. (Height/view scalar only.)

**Actual caller selection (verified):**
- The **production inbound proposal** path uses the **unbounded** `safety_decision` (`bhse.rs:4700`, §A32.3).
- `bounded_safety_decision`'s only non-test caller is the **RUN-422 safety-record-store** observation
  `observe_checks_locked` (`safety_record_store/owner.rs:2096`, step "9d"), not the core vote path.
- `is_safe_to_vote_on_block` and `is_safe_to_vote_at_height` have **only test callers**
  (`tests/run_422_d7d2_signing_state_recovery_tests.rs`; `tests/m5_timeout_view_change_tests.rs`).
Comments are not treated as executable guarantees; one helper is not substituted for another.

## A32.3 Proposal data and enforcement provenance

**Inbound Proposal (`ingest_proposal`, `bhse.rs:4602–4760`):** gates (A28.1) epoch (`:4610`), current-view
(`:4627`), leader `from == leader_for_view(view)` (`:4631`), not-already-voted (`:4636`); derives `block_id` and
`parent_id` (`[0xFF;32]` sentinel → `None`); parses the **legacy** `justify_qc` as
`QuorumCertificate::new(wire_qc.block_id, wire_qc.height, vec![])` — **empty signers (logical-only, not
authenticated; A17-F1 scope)** — while the **verified** entrypoint derives justification from **verified retained
evidence** inside the engine (`register_block_with_admission`), never from the wire projection; registers the
block; then **enforces `safety_decision(&block_id)`** (`:4700`): **`Unsafe` → `return None` (no vote, no
observation)**; **`Safe(branch)` →** optional hook (`None` legacy/verified → proceed; `Observe`/`Gate` →
observe/gate, refusing without self-voting if the candidate was evicted) → **self-vote `on_vote`** (bookkeeping)
→ QC may form → `on_qc` → commit (A31). **Mutations before a later refusal:** `register_block` adds the candidate
node **before** `safety_decision`; the node persists even on `Unsafe`; the self-vote mutation occurs **only** on
`Safe`. Outbound signing/broadcast is the separately Required/journal-gated stage.

**Legacy leader self-vote (`on_leader_step`):** the leader constructs its own proposal (parenting to its
`locked_qc`) and self-votes via `state.on_vote` (`:4154`) **without a distinct `safety_decision` call** — safety
is structural to the self-built proposal (it extends the leader's own lock), a route difference from the inbound
path's explicit re-check.

**Owning / gated / scalar routes:** `on_leader_self_vote_detailed` (owning, `on_qc@1405`),
`on_vote_detailed_effect_gated` (effect gate), `bounded_safety_decision` (RUN-422 observation), and the scalar /
wrapper helpers are **not** the core production vote-casting path.

**Parent↔justification binding and QC authentication — where enforced / assumed / absent / not reached:**
- `safety_decision` compares `block_node.justify_qc.view` to `locked.view` and walks `parent_id` links; it does
  **not** verify that `justify_qc` *refers to the parent block* (no parent↔justify-block identity check), and it
  does **not** re-authenticate the `justify_qc`'s signers. QC **authentication** is therefore **assumed** by this
  predicate and **enforced elsewhere**: on the **verified** path by the engine's retained-evidence admission; on
  the **legacy** path the `justify_qc` is logical-only (empty signers, **A17-F1**). Whether the production inbound
  path reaches the legacy projection at all is bounded by the Required-authorization gate (A26/A29.1) — not
  invented or enabled here.

## A32.4 Finite boundary-case table (source reasoning only)

| Case | `safety_decision` result (first deciding branch) |
| --- | --- |
| No lock, candidate **absent** | **`Safe(NoLock)`** — step 1 returns before candidate lookup |
| Existing lock, candidate **absent** | **`Unsafe`** — step 2 |
| `justify_qc.view < locked.view`, ancestry not reaching lock | **`Unsafe`** — step 4 chain breaks |
| `justify_qc.view == locked.view` | **`Safe(ViewSufficiency)`** — inclusive `>=`, ancestry skipped |
| `justify_qc.view > locked.view` | **`Safe(ViewSufficiency)`** — ancestry skipped |
| `justify_qc.view < locked.view`, ancestry path **reaches** lock | **`Safe(Ancestry)`** — step 4 finds `locked.block_id` |
| Missing ancestry (chain breaks / parent absent before lock) | **`Unsafe`** |
| Bounded path traversal limit | **`BoundExhausted`** (only `bounded_safety_decision`; the unbounded `safety_decision` has no hop limit and walks to genesis) |

**Admitted non-descendant via `ViewSufficiency`:** this is the **intended justification-view branch** of the
HotStuff rule (progress when `justify_qc.view >= locked.view` even without directly extending the locked block),
**not** a demonstrated safety failure. Its soundness rests on the `justify_qc.view` being a trustworthy
authenticated value (verified path) and on lock monotonicity + quorum intersection (A29.1 arithmetic) — required
authenticated inputs and caller guards that are **assumed here, not re-proved**. **Conflicting finality is not
inferred from predicate acceptance alone.**

**Tests inspected (not executed):** `tests/run_422_d7d2_signing_state_recovery_tests.rs:1301–1553` assert
`is_safe_to_vote_on_block` outcomes across a simulated crash/restore (safe/unsafe per lock state);
`tests/run_422_retained_decision_observation_tests.rs:289–389` assert `bounded_safety_decision` branch/hop
outcomes; `tests/m5_timeout_view_change_tests.rs:955–976` assert the scalar `is_safe_to_vote_at_height` boundary
(`>=` inclusive, below-lock unsafe). They assert the **predicate's branch outcomes**; they do **not** establish
production enforcement wiring beyond `ingest_proposal`, nor Byzantine-schedule safety.

## A31.1 Exact commit predicate and mutation order

`HotStuffStateEngine::on_qc(qc)` (`hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1782–1805`), **mutations first, in order**:
1. **Lock mutation** (`:1787–1794`): `replace_lock = locked_qc.is_none() || qc.view > locked_qc.view`; if so
   `locked_qc = Some(qc.clone())`. (Occurs **before** any commit decision and **persists** even if commit is
   later refused.)
2. **QC attachment** (`:1797–1799`): if `blocks.get_mut(&qc.block_id)` exists, `node.own_qc = Some(qc.clone())`.
   (Attaches `own_qc` to B's node; also persists regardless of commit outcome.)
3. `try_commit_with_qc(qc)` (`:1802`); returns `Ok(())`.

`try_commit_with_qc(qc)` (`:1828–1937`) — **read-only until the final commit block; no partial mutation before a
return**:
- **B** = `blocks[qc.block_id]`; `return` if absent or `B.own_qc.is_none()`; `b_view = B.view` (`:1830–1839`).
- **P** = parent of B: `return` if `B.parent_id` is `None`, P absent, or `P.own_qc.is_none()`; `(p_id, p_view)`
  (`:1841–1861`).
- **G** = parent of P: `return` if `P.parent_id` is `None`, G absent, or `G.own_qc.is_none()`;
  `(g_id, g_view, g_height)` (`:1863–1883`).
- **Views strictly increasing** (`:1886`): `return` unless `g_view < p_view < b_view` — **strictly increasing,
  NOT consecutive** (gaps permitted; no contiguity check).
- **Height monotonic** (`:1892–1895`): `height_ok = committed_height.is_none() || g_height > committed_height`.
- **Should-commit** (`:1897–1916`): `committed_block.is_none()` → true; `committed_id == g_id` → **false
  (same-block, no re-commit)**; else `blocks.get(committed_id)` → `Some(c)` → `g_view > c.view`; **`None` (prior
  committed block absent from the tree) → `true` ("allow commit to move forward")**.
- **Commit** (`:1918–1936`) iff `should_commit && height_ok`: `committed_block = g_id`,
  `committed_height = g_height`; push `CommittedEntry{block_id:g_id, view:g_view, height:g_height}` to
  `commit_log` only if `last.block_id != g_id`; then `evict_commit_log_if_needed`.

**Distinctions recorded:** block existence + parent linkage are required for B/P/G; the predicate checks `own_qc`
**presence** only, **not** authenticated endorsement (authentication is the vote-admission route's job, §A31.2);
views are **strictly increasing, not consecutive**; commit uses **G.height** for `height_ok` and **G.view** for
the view comparison (both monotone vs the prior commit); same-block is rejected; a **prior committed block absent
from the tree** skips the view check and relies on `height_ok` alone; and the predicate verifies the B←P←G
ancestry **among themselves** but performs **no descent check** linking **G to the previously committed block** —
it advances on **numerical** monotonicity only (ancestry preservation across commits is not re-checked locally).

**"Committed" scope:** this is the in-memory `committed_block`/`committed_height`/`commit_log` effect only — it
does **not** by itself establish durable persistence, transaction execution, network agreement, or finality.

## A31.2 Caller / admission table

`on_qc` is reached only through `ingest_vote_and_form_qc` producing `Ok(Some(qc))` (`on_vote_detailed:1701–1715`;
gated variant `on_vote_detailed_effect_gated:1718+`) and the self-vote path (`:1405`); `pacemaker.rs:456` drives
ticks. The sim harness (`hotstuff_node_sim.rs`) and tests are separate.

| QC-producing route | How `on_qc` is reached | Vote-admission authentication (boundary) | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Local leader / self-vote** | leader step → self-vote → `ingest_vote_and_form_qc` → `on_qc` (`:1405`) | the self-vote is the local signer's; outbound broadcast is separately Required/journal-gated (A26/A27/A29.1) — **internal engine mutation may precede outbound refusal** | **selected-binary**, local |
| **Ordinary inbound Proposal/Vote** | inbound vote → `on_vote_detailed` → `on_qc` | Proposal/Vote **Required**-authorization + journal refusals already established (A26/A27/A29.1) gate *processing*; a refused outbound does not unwind a prior engine mutation | **selected-binary**, inbound |
| **Restore-catch-up** | `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` → `register_block` + per-signer `on_vote` (`:4008–4018`) → QC forms → `on_qc` | QC signers are **logical-only** ids validated against local M (`qc.validate`), **A17-F1** scope — not wire-signature-verified here | **selected-binary**, catch-up (A17-F1) |
| **Guarded / gated library** | `on_vote_detailed_effect_gated` applies the QC only if `gate.allow(self, qc)` (`:1718+`) | caller-supplied gate | **library/guarded** |
| **Direct engine API / init-restore setters** | `set_locked_qc` / `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` set state directly | no commit decision; **initialization/restore**, not an ordinary commit | **library/init** — distinct from a production commit |

The commit predicate relies on each route to have authenticated the votes that formed the QC; it re-checks only
`own_qc` **presence**. The **A1-F3** TC-setter lock route and **A17-F1** catch-up logical-QC admission are
boundaries — not reopened, and not transferred between routes. Initialization/restore setters accepting
constructed state are **not** automatically a production exploit.

## A31.3 Finite boundary-case table (source reasoning only)

| Case | First rejecting predicate / permitted effect |
| --- | --- |
| Missing ancestor (B/P/G absent) or missing `own_qc` on any of B/P/G | **`return` (no commit)** at the respective `blocks.get`/`own_qc.is_none()` guard (`:1830–1883`); lock + `own_qc`-on-B mutations from `on_qc` still stand |
| Equal or decreasing B/P/G views | **`return`** at `g_view < p_view < b_view` (`:1886`) |
| Increasing but **non-consecutive** B/P/G views | **permitted** — strict-increase only; commit proceeds to the monotonicity checks |
| Candidate `g_height ≤ committed_height` | **`return`/no-commit** via `height_ok = g_height > committed_height` (`:1892–1895`) |
| Recommitting the same block (`committed_id == g_id`) | **no-commit** (`should_commit = false`, `:1900–1902`) |
| Prior committed block **absent from the tree** | view check **skipped**, `should_commit = true` (`:1908–1912`); commit proceeds **iff `height_ok`** — height monotonicity is the only backstop |
| Higher-view/higher-height G whose **descent from the prior commit is not established** | **permitted by the local predicate** (no ancestry check; commits on `g_view > committed.view ∧ g_height > committed_height`). Whether such a non-descendant G can be **admitted** (accumulate a B←P←G chain each with a quorum QC) is governed by the **safe-voting / lock rules at the caller**, **not** this predicate — see §A31.5. **Not** a demonstrated conflicting-finality attack: admitting a conflicting 3-chain would require defeating those unreviewed safe-voting rules; the state is synthetic here. |

**Caller guarantee vs local gap.** The one place the local predicate lacks a check is cross-commit **ancestry**;
before declaring a defect, the governing guarantee is the proposal/vote **safe-voting** discipline (lock-based
`is_safe_to_vote` and proposal parent-linkage), which determines whether a competing 3-chain's QCs can form at
all. That boundary is **named, not traced** here (§A31.5); no finding is forced from a synthetic non-descendant
state. **Tests inspected, not executed:** engine commit tests assert 3-chain happy-path commit and monotonic
no-backward-commit; they do **not** establish ancestry preservation against an adversarial competing chain (that
is the safe-voting property, untested here).

## A30.1-1 TC verifier vs the complete F7 admission path `[SUPERSEDED-A30 → A30.1-1]`

A30 correctly noted `high_qc_eq` (`timeout_verify.rs:449–457`) compares only `view`/`block_id`, but wrongly
extrapolated that the **composed** path omits QC authentication (and that a future caller must add a
`verify_quorum_certificate` call). The actual F7 composition (within `admit_f7_retained_high_qc_with_budget`,
reached only for `high_qc = Some` with a snapshot, after the epoch/membership gates of A29.1-1):

1. **Retained-proof lookup** — `engine.state().retained_qc_for_timeout_projection(logical_qc)`
   (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:1575–1588`; impl `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:2324–2357`): matches the **logical QC**
   (`block_id`, `view`, `signers`) to a locally-retained `VerifiedQuorumCertificate` requiring
   `node.justify_qc == Some(logical)` ∧ `certificate.block_id == logical.block_id` ∧
   `certificate.height == logical.view` ∧ `evidence.signers() == logical.signers` (ascending-bit order; rejects
   duplicates/reordering); absent → `MissingRetainedProof`, ambiguous → `AmbiguousRetainedProof`, over-scan →
   `ScanLimitExceeded`.
2. **Resource/working-set checks** (`:1589–1602`) → `TemporaryWorkingSetExceeded`.
3. **Re-verification** — `reverify_quorum_certificate_with_domain(certificate, &verifier.signing_domain,
   snapshot.authorized_epoch(), &verifier.validators, key_provider, backend_registry)`
   (`:1603–1612`; `qc_verify_domain.rs:916–937` → `verify_quorum_certificate_core:959–1127`): on the **retained
   wire certificate** (signature material), gating wire-chain-id, epoch, membership-span, positive/representable
   voting-power **threshold**, and **vote-signature verification**; failure → `ReverificationFailed`.
4. **Admission → confirmation → engine effect** (A29.1).

**Logical QC vs retained wire certificate.** The logical QC carries `block_id`/`view`/`signers`; the **retained**
`VerifiedQuorumCertificate` carries the signature material that step 3 re-verifies. `high_qc_eq` is **one
verifier's intentionally-limited responsibility** (reference match against the evidence maximum), not the whole
authentication; the "signer bitmap" comment in `timeout_verify.rs` is a scope note for *that* function, not the
composed path's actual fields. **Withdrawn:** "a future caller must simply add `verify_quorum_certificate`" —
existing downstream re-verification already accounts for it. An authorization snapshot **alone** is insufficient:
the retained-evidence lookup and every remaining guard (steps 1–3) must also pass. **A1-F3 stays SOURCE-GATED on
the TC-setter route; no new finding is minted from `high_qc_eq`'s limited scope.**

## A30.1-3 Evidence-binding and ordering statements corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A30 → A30.1-3]`

- **Evidence view check:** the actual guard is `ev.view != tc.timeout_view` (`timeout_verify.rs:410`), **not**
  `evidence.view == tc.view`. `tc.view` is kept distinct as the checked **immediate-successor target** (engine
  `on_timeout_certificate` requires `tc.view > current_view` to advance).
- **Timeout signature preimage** (`timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id`, `timeout.rs:157–188`):
  `domain_tag(chain_id, Timeout) ‖ view(8, LE) ‖ [ high_qc.block_id(32) ‖ high_qc.view(8, LE) | 40 zero bytes if
  None ] ‖ validator_id(8, LE)`. The timeout signature therefore **authenticates the signer's reported QC
  reference** (its `block_id`+`view`) and the signer's own `view`/identity — it does **not** attest the reported
  QC's **endorsements** (those are re-verified separately in A30.1-1 step 3). "Authentication of a reported QC
  reference" and "verification of that QC's endorsements" are distinct and performed by different stages.
- **Tie ordering (precise):** the producer `maybe_tc_for` selects `high_qc = select_max_high_qc(view_entries
  .values())` (HashMap-values order) and then `signed_timeouts.sort_by_key(|t| t.validator_id)`
  (`timeout.rs:699–701`); the TC carries that `high_qc` plus the **sorted** evidence vector. A verifier recomputes
  `select_max_high_qc(evidence.iter())` over the **received sorted vector** and requires `high_qc_eq`. For a tie
  between **different `block_id`s at the same top view**, the producer's HashMap-order pick may differ from the
  sorted-vector derivation, so the producer's own TC can trip `HighQcMismatch` at verifiers. All verifiers use the
  **same** received sorted vector deterministically — they do **not** independently reorder it; the potential
  mismatch is between the producer's selection order and the sorted-evidence derivation. (Source reasoning only;
  no execution or exploit claim.)

## A30.1 Stage 1 — producer → signed timeout → emission

`BasicHotStuffEngine::create_timeout_msg` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4978–4980`):
`let high_qc = self.state.locked_qc().cloned(); TimeoutMsg::new(self.current_view, high_qc, self.local_id)`. The
timeout carries the producer's **current `locked_qc`** (Some if a lock exists, else None) — it is **not** forcibly
stripped. `maybe_emit_view_timeout_with_auth` (`bcl.rs:7534+`) constructs it (`:7638–7639`), checks engine/signer
identity, then runs **F7 before signing** on `timeout_msg.high_qc` (`:7648`). Both production callers pass
**`current_auth = None`** (`:3290`, `:3438`). Prerequisites kept visible: the view-timeout pacer/backoff
(`ticks`/`view_state`/`backoff`), `restore_mode_active`, a signer (suite resolved at `:7626`), and an outbound
facade for broadcast.

| Local lock | Timeout `high_qc` | F7 (A29.1-1) under production `current_auth = None` | Emission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **none** (`locked_qc = None`) | `None` | `admit` → `NoQc` (no snapshot consulted) → pass | **signed + locally ingested + broadcast** (given pacer/restore/signer/facade prereqs) |
| **present** (`locked_qc = Some`) | `Some` | `admit` with `snapshot = None` → **`AuthorityUnavailable`** → `return` | **refused before signing** (not emitted) |
| *(supplied snapshot)* | `Some` | `admit` + epoch/engine↔verifier/timeout-context/chain checks | emitted if all pass — **library/test-only; no production supplier of the snapshot exists** |

So honest production nodes emit **only `high_qc = None`** timeouts; a present-lock timeout is fail-closed at F7
before signing. (A29.1's F7 result is carried, not re-audited; no Proposal/Vote journal/`Required` gate is on the
Timeout path.)

## A30.2 Stage 2 — aggregation → selected high-QC → evidence verification

- `TimeoutAccumulator::maybe_tc_for` (`timeout.rs:674`) forms a TC from the per-view, validator-keyed distinct
  timeouts once `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp` (M-quorum), selecting the high-QC via `select_max_high_qc`.
- `select_max_high_qc` (`timeout.rs:490–508`): picks the reported `high_qc` with the **strictly greatest** `view`
  (`qc.view > max_view`); on a **tied** top view the **first-encountered** QC wins (iteration-order-dependent
  over the entries map — **not** a content-deterministic tie-break; comments are not relied on).
- `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (`timeout_verify.rs`): unique tc.signers (`:384–390`), evidence
  `validator_id`s == tc.signers set (`:392–405`), per-evidence view == tc.view + signature verification under
  **V** + `saturating_add` V-weight (`:408–423`) + `two_thirds_vp(V)` (`:425`); then **Step 5** recomputes
  `derived_max = select_max_high_qc(evidence)` and requires `high_qc_eq(derived_max, tc.high_qc)` else
  `HighQcMismatch` (`:433–438`).

**Distinctions (recorded exactly):**
- *authenticated transport sender* — `authorize_origin(origin)` (NewView) / `bind_sender` (Timeout): who submitted the frame.
- *distinct timeout signers meeting quorum* — V-quorum of **timeout** signatures (`:408–425`).
- *reporter whose high-QC is selected* — the **single** max-view reporter (`select_max_high_qc`); **not** a quorum.
- *endorsement evidence for that QC itself* — **`high_qc_eq` compares only `view` and `block_id`** (`:449–457`),
  and the source is explicit that it **does NOT** validate the high-QC's signer bitmap/signatures ("that is the
  existing `verify_quorum_certificate` boundary … intentionally untouched"). So a V-quorum of timeout signatures
  does **not** imply a quorum reported or **endorsed** the selected QC; the TC path confirms the selected high-QC
  matches the evidence max-by-(view,block_id) but **does not authenticate the high-QC's own quorum** (deferred to
  an unwired-on-this-path `verify_quorum_certificate`).

**Input cases:** all-None → `derived_max = None`, `high_qc_eq(None, None) = true` (accepted, carries no QC);
one-present → that QC selected, must equal `tc.high_qc` by (view, block_id); tied-highest-view → `select_max_high_qc`
keeps the first-encountered (order-dependent), and `high_qc_eq` accepts any evidence-reported QC sharing that
(view, block_id) — a tie between **different** block_ids at the same top view would make the producer's selection
order-dependent and could trip `HighQcMismatch` at a verifier that derived a different representative. Library
construction (a hand-built TC) is kept separate from a production acceptance trace (which additionally passes F7
and engine-M validation).

## A30.3 Stage 3 — receiver → lock installation → next consumer

`on_timeout_certificate` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5154–5199`): `tc.validate(self.state.validators())` (M:
membership + dedup + M-quorum); if `tc.view <= current_view` → `Ok(current_view)` (**stale, no advance, no lock
change**); else, **if `tc.high_qc = Some`**, install it when the existing lock is **absent** *or* its view is
**strictly higher** (`:5169`, `None => true, Some(locked) => tc_high_qc.view > locked.view`) — the
"no-existing-lock" case is an install, not only "strictly higher" (A29.1 qualification carried); then advance
`current_view = tc.view`. The installed `locked_qc` is the next proposal's justification (`leader_for_view`
proposal parents to `locked_qc.block_id`). With `tc.high_qc = None` there is **no** lock update.

## A30.4 Producer-to-consumer data-flow table

| Hop | Mechanism (source) | Carries | Governing check | Production (current_auth=None) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| produce | `create_timeout_msg` (`bhse:4978`) | `high_qc = locked_qc` (Some/None) | — | — |
| emit | `maybe_emit…` F7 before sign (`bcl:7648`) | timeout `high_qc` | F7: None pass / Some→`AuthorityUnavailable` | **Some refused before signing** |
| sign+broadcast | signer + facade (`bcl:7534+`) | signed timeout | signer/facade present | only None-high_qc emitted |
| receive timeout | `verify_timeout_msg`(V)→F7→`on_timeout_msg`(M) (`bcl:7032/7065/7100`) | one signer + its high_qc | V-membership+sig; F7; M-accumulate | Some-high_qc timeout → F7 reject |
| aggregate | `maybe_tc_for`+`select_max_high_qc` (`timeout:674/490`) | TC with max-view high_qc | M-quorum of timeouts | TC high_qc = max of **admitted** (None in prod) |
| verify TC | `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (V) (`timeout_verify:378–440`) | TC + evidence | V-quorum + `high_qc_eq`(view,block_id only) | high_qc **own quorum not validated here** |
| F7 (TC) | `admit/confirm_f7_high_qc` (`bcl:1514/1490`) | `tc.high_qc` | None pass / Some→`AuthorityUnavailable` | **Some refused** |
| install | `on_timeout_certificate` (M) (`bhse:5154`) | `tc.high_qc` | `tc.validate(M)`; set_locked_qc if Some&(no-lock\|higher) | **reached only with None → no lock update** |

## A30.5 Two bounded traces

**(a) Admissible no-high-QC TC (production-reachable).** `tc.high_qc = None`, signers `S ⊆ M∩V` meeting
`q(M)`/`q(V)`, evidence covers `S`, target view > receiver current view. V-verify: `derived_max = None`,
`high_qc_eq(None, None) = true` → Ok. F7: `admit` → `NoQc` (no snapshot needed) → pass. Engine
`on_timeout_certificate`: `tc.validate(M)` Ok, `tc.view > current` → advance (`Ok(to_view)`); `high_qc = None` ⇒
**no `set_locked_qc`**. **Furthest effect: a view advance with no TC lock update.**

**(b) Present-high-QC attempt (first production refusal).** `tc.high_qc = Some(qc)`. V-verify may accept (if
`high_qc_eq` matches the evidence max, even though `qc`'s own quorum is not validated here). **F7 `admit` with
production `current_auth = None` → `AuthorityUnavailable` → return — this is the first actual refusal on the
selected binary.** The production trace **stops here**: `on_timeout_certificate` / `set_locked_qc` is never
reached in production. *Downstream (library/test only, with a supplied snapshot — not production-reachable):* F7
`Some` path would additionally require epoch/engine↔verifier/timeout-context/chain agreement; only then would the
engine install `qc` as the lock (if absent or higher). This is described separately and is **not** called
production-reachable.

## A29.1-1 F7's conditional authorization requirement `[SUPERSEDED-A29 → A29.1-1]`

A29 stated "F7 refuses when current authorization is absent" as a blanket rule. Corrected from the complete
bodies (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:1514–1567` admit, `:1490–1503` confirm):

| `high_qc` / snapshot | `admit_f7_retained_high_qc` | `confirm_f7_high_qc_before_effect` | First rejecting guard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **`None`** (any snapshot) | `let Some(logical_qc) = … else { return Ok(NoQc) }` (`:1547–1549`) — **no snapshot consulted** | `(NoQc, None, _) => Ok(())` (`:1498`) — **permitted without a snapshot** | **none** (passes; authorization not required) |
| **`Some`, no snapshot** | `let Some(snapshot) = … else { return Err(AuthorityUnavailable) }` (`:1557–1559`) | `_ => Err(OperationSubstituted)` | **`AuthorityUnavailable`** (snapshot-absent check) |
| **`Some`, with snapshot** | `snapshot.owner().admit()` ticket, then `current_epoch == authorized_epoch` ∧ engine↔verifier ∧ engine↔timeout-context membership ∧ chain-id (`:1560+`) | `present.confirm_before_effect(qc, …)` | first failing membership/epoch/chain/ticket/evidence check |

So F7's authorization requirement is **conditional on `high_qc = Some`**. For a `high_qc = None` certificate the F7
stage passes with no snapshot/authorization. A1-F3's TC-setter scope is preserved (F7 governs the retained
high-QC admission, not the TC signature set).

## A29.1-2 Three TC route traces repaired (messages vs certificates) `[SUPERSEDED-A29 → A29.1-2]`

- **Inbound Timeout** (`bcl.rs:6993–7115`): `bind_sender(claimed)` (single self-declared sender) → single-message
  **V** membership + signature verification via `verify_timeout_msg` (`:7032`) → F7 (`:7065–7090`) →
  `engine.on_timeout_msg` under **M** (`:7100`, accumulate; `maybe_tc_for` may form a TC). A single Timeout's
  admission does **not** require a V **quorum** (it is one signer's message, not a certificate); only a
  **subsequently formed TC** receives the certificate checks (V-quorum + engine M-validation).
- **Inbound NewView** (`bcl.rs:7142–7358`): uses **`gate.authorize_origin(origin)`** BEFORE decode/F5/engine
  (`:7159–7170`) — a NewView is a multi-signer TC with **no single self-declared sender**, so the Proposal/Vote/
  Timeout `bind_sender` claimed-sender comparison is **not** invented here (the source says so explicitly). Then
  evidence verification under **V** (`verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`, `:7255`), F7 (`:7294–7309`), and
  engine validation under **M** (`on_timeout_certificate`). A29's "bind_sender" for route 2 is withdrawn.
- **Local TC helper** (`apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view_with_auth`, `bcl.rs:7875–7978`): V-verify (`:7886`,
  Err→return) → F7 admit (`:7908`) → F7 confirm (`:7920`) → `engine.on_timeout_certificate` under **M**
  (`:7938`) → **only if an outbound facade exists** (`:7961`) serialize (`bincode::serialize`, `:7964`) and
  `broadcast_consensus_msg(NewView)` (`:7967`). Four **distinct** failure branches: engine rejection (`:7951`),
  missing facade (`:7961`), serialization failure (`:7975`), send failure (`:7969`). **"Local NewView broadcast
  is gated by `current_auth`" is withdrawn** as a universal claim: `current_auth` here is consumed **only** by
  F7 (and thus only matters for `high_qc = Some`); the Proposal/Vote `Required`-authorization gate
  (`admit_outbound_action`) and the signing-reservation **journal** gate are **not** on this separate TC path.

**Engine application vs view advance** (`on_timeout_certificate`, `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5154–5199`):
`tc.validate(self.state.validators())?` (M) then `if tc.view <= self.current_view { return Ok(self.current_view) }`
— a **stale/non-advancing** TC returns `Ok(current_view)` **without advancing**; only `tc.view > current_view`
advances (`Ok(to_view)`) and may update `locked_qc` (only when `high_qc = Some` and strictly higher). A
successful `Ok(_)` therefore does **not** imply a view advance. A `broadcast_consensus_msg` success is a broadcast
**attempt/handoff** (`outbound_new_views_sent++`), **not** confirmed network delivery.

## A29.1-3 Dual-membership rule stated precisely; witness repaired `[SUPERSEDED-A29 → A29.1-3]`

For the unit-weight memberships at this revision, certificate acceptance **and application** under both sets
requires a single distinct signer set `S` to satisfy **all** of:

- `S ⊆ M ∩ V`,
- `|S| ≥ q(M)` where `q(M) = ceil(2·W_M/3)` (threshold computed over **M**),
- `|S| ≥ q(V)` where `q(V) = ceil(2·W_V/3)` (threshold computed over **V**),

alongside valid signatures, evidence binding, target-view checks, and the route-specific guards above. The
threshold is **not** recomputed over `M ∩ V`; `q(M)` and `q(V)` are each computed over their own full membership,
and `S` must meet both. "Evidence-set equality" means **TC signer IDs == evidence IDs** (`timeout_verify.rs:392–405`),
**not** equality with the entire `V` membership. This rule is scoped to **certificate acceptance/application** —
not to every intermediate engine mutation, nor to an individual Timeout broadcast.

**Repaired witness** (`M = {0,1,2,3}` from `num_validators=4`; `V = {0,1,2,4}` from configured keys;
`q(M) = q(V) = ceil(8/3) = 3`), with **`high_qc = None`** in the TC and its signed evidence, genuine valid
signatures, an admitted transport origin, matching timed-out views, a valid successor target **above** the
receiver's current view, and jointly satisfiable startup/config prerequisites (V local-membership + static-peer
coverage per `peer_key_provider.rs:371–428`):
- **`S = {0,1,2}`** — `⊆ M ∩ V = {0,1,2}`, `|S| = 3 ≥ q(M)=3` and `≥ q(V)=3`: passes V-verify **and** engine
  `tc.validate(M)` → **accepted**; target > current view ⇒ a **view transition** (`Ok(to_view)`). Because
  `high_qc = None`, **no `locked_qc` update occurs** (the `Some` branch at `bhse.rs:5169` is not entered).
- **`S = {0,1,2,4}`** — `4 ∈ V` but `4 ∉ M`: passes V-verify (all V-members, `|S|=4 ≥ 3`) but engine
  `on_timeout_certificate` → `tc.validate(M)` → `NonMemberSigner(4)` → **rejected** (no view advance).

**"Possibly updates `locked_qc`" is withdrawn from this mismatched-membership witness:** the witness uses
`high_qc = None`, so there is **no TC lock update**. A present (`Some`) high-QC would instead encounter the F7
authorization/membership checks (A29.1-1). No safety violation and no network-wide liveness failure is established
by either outcome (an accepted view transition is not a safety break; a rejected certificate is not a demonstrated
liveness failure).

## A29.1-4 Quorum-intersection arithmetic corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A29 → A29.1-4]`

Positive mathematical total `W`, exact-arithmetic assumptions; distinct signers; `q = ceil(2W/3)`.
- **Overflow caveat preserved.** Non-saturated addition alone does **not** ensure the implementation expression
  `2 * total` cannot overflow; the constructor total is `saturating_add` but `two_thirds_vp` multiplies
  `2 * total` unchecked (overflow at `total ≥ 2^63`), with the deployed overflow-check behavior **not** fixed by
  the committed profiles — A27.1's bounds and deployed-profile qualifications are retained.
- **`weight(Q₁ ∩ Q₂) ≥ 2q − W` is a lower bound, not the actual overlap.** The residue values
  `2q − W ∈ { W/3 (W≡0), (W+2)/3 (W≡1), (W+4)/3 (W≡2) }` are the **minimum** guaranteed overlaps; A29's "overlap
  is exactly W/3" is **withdrawn** (actual overlap can be larger).
- **`2q − W > F` is a sufficient worst-case honest-intersection guarantee**, not an "iff": it guarantees that even
  the **minimum** overlap contains honest voting power; it is not claimed necessary. A29's unqualified "iff" is
  **withdrawn**.
- **`W − F ≥ q`** characterizes whether **all** honest voting power can numerically meet the threshold; it does
  **not** prove protocol liveness (message availability, scheduling, and the full HotStuff argument are separate).
- **Preserved:** the residue calculations above (as lower bounds) and the unit-weight identity: for `N = 3f+1`
  with `f = ⌊(N−1)/3⌋`, `ceil(2N/3) = 2f+1 = quorum_size`.

No full HotStuff proof or new Byzantine schedule is asserted.

## Part 1 — bounded A28.1 corrections

### P1-A — "every receiver check rejects corrupted/substituted IDs" withdrawn `[SUPERSEDED-A28.1 → A29-P1A]`

`QuorumCertificate::validate` (`qc.rs:83–115`) checks the **received** IDs' membership, uniqueness, and
accumulated weight; it has **no knowledge of their pre-truncation values**. Predicate acceptance ≠ production
admission. *Small example:* engine set M = {0, 1, 2, 65538}. A catch-up block exports signer `65538` as
`65538 as u16 = 2` (`bcl.rs:8415`); the receiver widens it back to `ValidatorId::new(2)` (`:8488`). If `{0,1,2}`
is a quorum (e.g. N≈4, q=3), `qc.validate(M)` sees `{0,1,2}` — **all members, distinct, quorum met → Ok** — even
though the *original* signer was `65538`. So `qc.validate` does **not** reject a truncation-collided id that lands
on a valid member; it validates the post-truncation values. (This is a constructed illustration of the predicate
boundary, not a demonstrated production admission — honest exports are separately bounded in P1-B, and an
attacker-supplied catch-up QC is validated only against the **local** M, i.e. it can assert only local members.)

**Requester/responder binding kept separate.** For catch-up request/response, `bind_sender(claimed)`
(`bcl.rs:6150–6154`, `gate.authorize(origin, claimed)`) compares the *self-declared* (post-truncation) VID to the
**authenticated transport origin**: if the origin retains a high VID, its truncated claimed VID `≠ origin` → the
production binding gate **rejects**. This sender comparison applies to the **one** declared requester/responder
field only; it is **not** transferred to every QC signer (signers are not transport-origin-bound).

### P1-B — producer-side export derivation (replaces the export-range argument) `[refines A28.1-C2]`

Default selected-binary chain (verified): `BasicHotStuffEngine::new` → `HotStuffStateEngine::new(validators)`
(`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2017`) selects **default** limits; `max_votes_per_view = 256`
(`vote_accumulator.rs:122`); vote insertion drops over-cap votes (`:431`, "new votes are dropped" `:179`);
`maybe_qc_for` (`vote_accumulator.rs:514–540`) builds a QC from the accumulated **distinct** voters (≤256) and
returns `Ok(None)` on `InsufficientQuorum`; `own_qc` is set only for blocks that reached a valid QC;
`export_restore_catchup_blocks` (`:3894`) exports only suffix blocks with `own_qc.is_some()` (`:3911/3917`) and
derives the proposer from the engine leader schedule.

Derivation (unit weights, `W = N`): a QC forms only if `ceil(2N/3) ≤ (distinct voters ≤ 256)`, i.e.
`ceil(2N/3) ≤ 256 ⇒ N ≤ 384` (N=384: `ceil(768/3)=256 ≤ 256` ✓; N=385: `257 > 256` ✗). Dense member IDs are then
`0..=383 < 2^16`, so **honest** exports from this default path carry un-truncated proposer/signer IDs.
Initialization (`new` → default limits) and the inspected **unchanged-membership** epoch transition
(`bcl.rs:9062–9063`, reuses the current engine set) introduce no bypass of this premise.

**Scope (explicit).** This bound is for **honest exports from the default path** only. It does **not**: establish
a global validator-count cap (a larger `N` simply never forms a QC / never exports — not a rejection of the set);
bound requester/responder **local** IDs (those come from `local_validator_id`, not the QC path); or **authenticate
incoming catch-up QCs** (an inbound catch-up response's `qc_signers` are validated only against the **local** M by
`apply_restore_catchup_blocks` → `qc.validate`, so a sender can assert only local members — **A17-F1 preserved**).
The response **block-count** cap (`RESTORE_CATCHUP_MAX_BLOCKS_PER_RESPONSE`) is distinct from the signer-ID range.

### P1-C — execution attributions corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A28.1 → A29-P1C]`

- `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4815` is in **`ingest_proposal`** (enclosing fn `:4602`), **not** `on_leader_step`.
  Its actual entry gates (reached before the self-vote at `:4815`): epoch match (`:4610`), current-view match
  (future-view advance `:4618–4622`; else reject `:4627–4629`), and **proposal is from the expected leader**
  (`from != leader_for_view(view) → None`, `:4631–4634`). So this self-vote is cast only in response to a
  valid, current-view, correct-leader proposal.
- The selected binary's **first** production rejection of an otherwise-eligible outbound proposal/vote is
  `admit_outbound_action`'s **Required + absent current-authorization** check: `None` snapshot +
  `requires_context()` → `record_no_snapshot_unavailable` + `OutboundAuthAdmission::Rejected`
  (`bcl.rs:5604–5610`), evaluated at the top of the outbound handler (`:5842`) → `continue` **before** the
  guarded signer/journal call (`:5878`). The **missing-journal** refusal (A26/A27) is an **additional** refusal
  reached only by calls that already passed current-authorization — **not** today's first production rejection.
- **Outbound suppression ≠ no engine mutation.** `ingest_proposal` / `on_leader_step` mutate local engine state
  (view advance, vote/propose flags, accumulator) **before** the outbound authorization/journal gates; a
  suppressed broadcast does not unwind those local mutations.

OBL-CONS-7's disposition is updated **only** with this replacement reasoning (P1-B producer bound, P1-C
attributions); the completed constructor and producer inventory (A28) are preserved.

## Part 2 — OBL-CONS-8 (two finite sub-questions)

### Q1 — what the implemented threshold establishes under one fixed membership

**Assumptions (explicit):** one common membership with a fixed weight assignment, total voting power `W` (distinct
signers, non-saturated `u64` totals); Byzantine voting power `F`; honest validators do not sign conflicting
messages at the same (view, step). Predicate: a quorum is any signer set with weight `≥ q`, where
`q = ceil(2W/3)` (`validator_set.rs:494`; `qc.rs` / `timeout*` consume it).

- **Minimum overlap of two quorums.** `|Q₁ ∩ Q₂|_weight ≥ 2q − W`. With `q = ceil(2W/3)`:
  `W ≡ 0 (mod 3)`: `2q − W = W/3`. `W ≡ 1`: `(W+2)/3`. `W ≡ 2`: `(W+4)/3`. So overlap `≥ W/3` always, strictly
  `> W/3` when `3 ∤ W`.
- **Overlap contains honest power** iff `2q − W > F`. For `W ≡ 0`: `F < W/3` (strict, since overlap is exactly
  `W/3`); for `3 ∤ W` a small positive margin exists (`(W+2)/3` or `(W+4)/3 > F`). This is the safety-relevant
  condition (an honest validator in the intersection does not double-sign).
- **Honest power alone forms a quorum** (liveness-relevant) iff `W − F ≥ q = ceil(2W/3)`, i.e.
  `F ≤ W − ceil(2W/3) = ⌊W/3⌋`. For `W ≡ 0`: `F ≤ W/3`.
- **Integer-rounding / unit-weight.** With unit weights `W = N` and the classic `f = ⌊(N−1)/3⌋`: for `N = 3f+1`,
  `ceil(2N/3) = 2f+1 = quorum_size` (`:483–486`) — the count predicate and the voting-power predicate coincide at
  `N ≡ 1 (mod 3)`; at other residues `ceil(2N/3)` is the governing power threshold while `2f+1` is a separate
  count helper.

These are the arithmetic conditions only. The two conditions above are each shown **sufficient** (not proven
necessary). They are separate from cryptographic admission (signatures), the Part-1 vote-cap restriction (which
bounds *distinct voters per view*, not the threshold), actual message availability, and a full HotStuff
safety/liveness proof — none of which is claimed here.

### Q2 — which membership governs TC acceptance when M ≠ V

**Sets:** **M** = dense engine membership (`build_uniform`, `self.state.validators()`); **V** = configured
timeout-verification membership (`peer_key_provider`, `ctx.validators`). Startup prerequisites: V enforces local
membership + static-peer key coverage (`peer_key_provider.rs:371–428`); inbound frames are transport-origin-bound
(`bind_sender`).

| Route | Ordered gates (first → last) | Does one set's threshold suffice? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Inbound Timeout** | `bind_sender` (origin) → `verify_timeout_msg` under **V** (`bcl.rs:7032`) → F7 `admit/confirm_f7_high_qc` (`:7065–7090`; refuses when current authorization absent) → `engine.on_timeout_msg` under **M** (`:7100`; accumulator + `maybe_tc_for`, M-quorum). | **No** — V-verification gates entry, but TC *formation* is under M. |
| **2. Inbound NewView/TC** | decode (`:7200`) → `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` under **V** (`:7255`; V-membership set-equality + V-quorum, `timeout_verify.rs:384–405,425`) → F7 (`:7294–7309`; refuses when current authorization absent) → `engine.on_timeout_certificate` under **M** (`bhse.rs:5154`, `tc.validate(self.state.validators())` = M-membership + dedup + M-quorum). | **No** — passing **V** does not suffice; the engine **re-validates under M**; `high_qc=Some` additionally may update `locked_qc` only if higher, `high_qc=None` advances view without a lock update. |
| **3. Locally formed TC** | `maybe_tc_for` forms under **M** (`:7107`) → `apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view_with_auth` re-verifies under **V** (`:7886`, `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence(..., ctx.validators=V)`) → broadcast gated by `current_auth`. | **No** — a locally-formed (M) TC must also pass **V** before broadcast, and broadcast is authorization-gated. |

So **both M and V conditions apply on every route** — effectively `M ∩ V` governs end-to-end TC
formation/acceptance/broadcast; passing a single set's threshold never suffices. The established production **F7
refusal when current authorization is absent** is preserved (its signature analysis is not reopened).

**One jointly-satisfiable mismatch (illustration).** `static_peers = 3 ⇒ num_validators = 4 ⇒ M = {0,1,2,3}`;
operator configures `--validator-consensus-key` for IDs `{0,1,2,4}` ⇒ `V = {0,1,2,4}` (local membership + peer
coverage satisfiable with these IDs). `q = ceil(2·4/3) = 3`.
- A TC signed by `{0,1,2} ⊆ M ∩ V` meets `q=3` in both → passes V-verify **and** engine M-validate → **accepted
  view transition** (furthest effect: the receiving node advances its view / possibly updates `locked_qc` if
  `high_qc` is higher). An accepted view transition is **not** by itself a safety violation.
- A TC signed by `{0,1,2,4}` passes **V** (all V-members, 4 ≥ q) but **fails M**: `on_timeout_certificate` →
  `tc.validate(M)` → `NonMemberSigner(4)` → **rejected** (furthest effect: no view advance on this node). A
  rejected certificate is **not** by itself a demonstrated network-wide liveness failure.

No signature forgery, assumed bypass, or runtime execution was used; the mismatch is an operator-configuration
property, and the furthest source-established effects (accepted view transition / rejected certificate) are
recorded without extrapolation to safety or liveness.

## A28.1-C1 Proposer-check attribution corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A28 → A28.1-C1]`

A28 credited the selected-binary leader path with the checked `u16::try_from` → `ProposerIndexOverflow`
(`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3597–3604`). That checked conversion belongs to **`try_propose_gated_owning`** — a
**different** path. The selected binary's leader tick instead calls `engine.try_propose()`
(`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3683`) → `try_propose → on_leader_step` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4937–4938`), which
uses **unchecked, truncating** casts:

- `:4123` — `proposer_index: self.local_id.0 as u16` (proposal construction).
- `:4177` — `validator_index: self.local_id.0 as u16` (vote construction).
- `:4815` — `validator_index: self.local_id.0 as u16` (the owning envelope's self-vote).

The transfer of `ProposerIndexOverflow` protection to this path is **withdrawn**. These casts silently truncate a
`local_id ≥ 2^16`. Per the required stage separation, an unchecked cast **alone** proves neither emission nor an
accepted identity substitution:

| Stage | Status on this path |
| --- | --- |
| Reaching the conversion | yes, when the local node is leader for the view (`is_leader_for_current_view`) |
| Constructing an action | yes — a `BroadcastProposal`/vote action with the truncated index |
| Internal engine effects | local engine state only |
| Passing outbound authorization/signing | **gated** — the outbound Proposal/Vote broadcast runs the journal-aware guarded signer, which **fails closed when the journal is `None`** (production; A26/A27) and otherwise requires the Run-420 `Required` authorization; no emission of a truncated-index proposal/vote is established in production |
| Sending bytes | not established (blocked by the prior stage in production) |
| Receiver acceptance | not reached |

The existing Run-420 `Required` / current-authorization restrictions are preserved. Truncation requires an
operator-configured `local_id ≥ 2^16`; its furthest established local effect on this path is **action
construction**, with outbound emission gated.

## A28.1-C2 ID-conversion inventory completed (with receiver guards)

`ValidatorId` is `ValidatorId(u64)`; wire identity fields are `u16`. Inventory (source value/type → admission/range
bound → conversion → outbound prerequisites → receiver checks → furthest established effect):

| Site | Source → conv. | Outbound prereq | Receiver check | Furthest established effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bhse.rs:4123` proposer_index | `local_id.0: u64` → `as u16` (unchecked) | journal-gated signing (fail-closed `None`) | inbound proposal `bind_sender` (`bcl.rs:6198`) + conditional membership (C3) | action construction; emission gated |
| `bhse.rs:4177/4815` vote index | `local_id.0` → `as u16` (unchecked) | journal-gated signing | inbound vote `bind_sender` | action construction; emission gated |
| `bcl.rs:8352` requester idx | `local_validator_id.0` → `as u16` (unchecked) | `RestoreCatchupRequest` broadcast (not signed) | `bind_sender(claimed)` binds to authenticated origin BEFORE servicing (`bcl.rs:7373–7385`); self-skip widen-back `req... as u64` (`:8389`) | request serviced only if sender-bound |
| `bcl.rs:8403` responder idx | `local_validator_id.0` → `as u16` (unchecked) | `RestoreCatchupResponse` broadcast | `bind_sender(claimed)` before applying (`bcl.rs:7391–7405`) | response applied only if sender-bound |
| `bcl.rs:8414` exported block proposer | `b.proposer.0: u64` → `as u16` (unchecked) | response broadcast; `RESTORE_CATCHUP_MAX_BLOCKS_PER_RESPONSE` export cap | widen-back `ValidatorId::new(.. as u64)` (`:8486`) → `apply_restore_catchup_blocks`: `block.proposer` checked **by identity** against `leader_for_view(view)` → `WrongProposer` (`bhse.rs:3983`); `block_id` bound to proposer/view/parent (`BlockIdMismatch`) | corrupted/substituted proposer **rejected** |
| `bcl.rs:8415` exported QC signer idxs | `v.0: u64` → `as u16` each (unchecked) | response broadcast | widen-back `ValidatorId::new(.. as u64)` (`:8488–8490`) → `QuorumCertificate::new(...).validate(self.validators())` (membership + dedup + ≥2/3; `NonMemberSigner`/`InsufficientQuorum`) | corrupted/substituted signer **rejected** |

**Binding gate** (`bind_sender`, `bcl.rs:6150–6154`): `Some(gate) => gate.authorize(origin, claimed)` binds the
self-declared id to the authenticated transport origin; `None => Ok(claimed)` (passthrough when no gate). The
Run-418 request/response gates (`bcl.rs:7373–7409`) apply it **before** counting or servicing. **IDs are used as
identity values** (leader-schedule equality, QC membership, sender binding), **not positional indices**. The
`u16` round-trip is lossless for ids `< 2^16`; for ids `≥ 2^16` it is lossy, and every traced receiver check
(`bind_sender`, `leader_for_view` equality, `qc.validate` membership) **rejects** a corrupted/substituted id
rather than accepting it. Truncation is therefore asserted **neither harmless nor exploitable** in the abstract —
each path's furthest effect is recorded with its rejecting guard.

## A28.1-C3 Membership-guard scope corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A28 → A28.1-C3]`

A28's "local membership is enforced within each set" is narrowed:
- **Timeout-verification set:** local membership **is** established by the key provider
  (`peer_key_provider.rs:371–399`, `LocalKeyMissing` fail-closed).
- **Dense engine set:** `BasicHotStuffEngine::new`/`assemble` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2015`) receives and
  **stores `local_id` separately** from `validators`; there is **no construction-time guard** that
  `local_id ∈ validators`. Consumer behavior with an out-of-range `local_id`: `is_leader_for_current_view()` =
  `leader_for_view(view) == local_id` is **never true** (the leader schedule contains only set members), so the
  node **never proposes** — a bounded, fail-silent effect, no crash. This is distinct from a sparse *member* of
  the verification set. (No enforcing startup guard found; the bounded absence and its consumer behavior are
  recorded.)

**"Genesis loader is the only reconciliation location" withdrawn** `[SUPERSEDED-A28]`. Two further engine/verifier
membership comparisons exist, both via `validator_membership_matches` (**ids AND voting weights**, not counts):
- `binary_consensus_loop.rs:1565–1566` — F7 retained-QC path; reached only after a retained-QC **ticket** is
  obtained (else `AuthorityUnavailable` refusal `:1561`), then gated on epoch equality, engine↔verifier and
  engine↔timeout-context membership, and chain-id.
- `binary_consensus_loop.rs:6488–6491` — inbound proposal path; reached only when a QC/snapshot verifier context
  (`snap`) is present, gated on membership match **and** `current_epoch == snap.authorized_epoch`; mismatch →
  `inbound_proposal_engine_context_mismatch_total` reject.

Both are **conditional runtime** comparisons (prerequisites: an authorized/retained context — distinguishing
*absent high-QC* → comparison not reached; *present high-QC with no current authorization* → earlier
authority/epoch refusal; *context eligible to reach the comparison* → membership predicate runs). They do **not**
establish an unconditional **startup** engine==verify equality guard. (The completed F7-signature analysis is not
reopened beyond this attribution.)

## A28.1-C4 Bounds applied at the correct stage; disposition

Distinct caps/constraints, kept separate (no cross-transfer):
- **Validator-count admission cap:** none source-enforced; `num_validators = static_peers + 1`; bounded only by
  the allocation/representation premise (A27.1-C4 / A28) — **not** a numeric guard, and **not** applicable to
  identity *values*.
- **Vote-accumulator cap:** `ConsensusLimitsConfig` (`vote_accumulator`) bounds per-view vote/entry counts — a
  **different** stage; it is **not** transferred to local identity fields or proposal construction.
- **QC-formation constraint:** `qc.validate` membership + dedup + ≥2/3 (the gate the catch-up signers meet).
- **Export prerequisite:** `RESTORE_CATCHUP_MAX_BLOCKS_PER_RESPONSE` caps blocks per catch-up response.
- **Allocation premise:** engine `Vec`/`HashMap` of `N` entries.

An exported certified block's size bound derives from its **actual** production path
(`export_restore_catchup_blocks` + the per-response cap + `qc.validate` on apply), not from the vote-accumulator
cap and not from any local-identity field.

**OBL-CONS-7 completion (corrected).** The constructor + admission reachability question (A28.2 A–D) remains
**SOURCE-COMPLETE**; this pass **adds** the ID-conversion sub-trace, which is bounded: lossless for ids `< 2^16`;
for the leader-tick proposal/vote the truncated field's emission is **gated** (journal fail-closed); for the
catch-up path every widened field is **rejected** at the receiver by an identity/membership guard. **Named
residual local source question** (not moved to multi-node runtime merely for eventual multi-node consequence):

outbound signing gate to emit a truncated-index proposal/vote* — bounded today by the journal-fail-closed signing
gate (A26/A27) and the Run-420 `Required` authorization; the exact rejecting guard is the signing gate, named
here. No local caller/bound is left unnamed.

Quorum-intersection sufficiency and multi-node TC/engine≠verify effects remain under **OBL-CONS-8** (not
reviewed). Duplicate check: QBIND-A1-F003 (journal) and A21-F1/QBIND-A1-F001 (decoder allocation) are distinct.

## A28.2 OBL-CONS-7 — degenerate/sparse admission to the selected binary

### A. Constructor behavior (`ConsensusValidatorSet::new`, `validator_set.rs:396–423`)

| Input case | Generic library constructor | Production producers admit? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Empty input** | **REJECT** — `"validator set must not be empty"` (`:414–416`) | n/a (rejected) |
| **Duplicate validator IDs** | **REJECT** — `"duplicate ValidatorId"` via `index_by_id` (`:405–407`) | also rejected upstream: `peer_key_provider` `DuplicateValidatorId` (`:362–366`); `build_uniform` emits distinct `0..N` |
| **Zero-weight members** | **ACCEPT** — no `voting_power` validation; `total_vp` via `saturating_add` (`:404–412`) | **not produced** — both producers assign `voting_power: 1` |
| **Non-empty all-zero-total** | **ACCEPT** — `total_vp = 0`; `two_thirds_vp = 0` (`:491–495`); `acc ≥ 0` trivially met | **not produced** — unit weights ⇒ `total = N ≥ 1` |
| **Sparse / non-contiguous IDs** | **ACCEPT** — IDs are `HashMap` keys; no contiguity requirement (`:404–412`) | engine: **never** (dense `0..N`); timeout-verify: **yes**, from operator-chosen `--validator-consensus-key` VIDs |
| **IDs outside the engine's dense `0..N`** | **ACCEPT** — any `u64` id | engine: **never**; timeout-verify: **yes** (operator config) |

Rejection vs normalization vs acceptance: the constructor **rejects** empty and duplicates; it does **not**
normalize/dedup beyond the first-duplicate rejection; it **accepts** zero/sparse/out-of-range. Weighted-library
behavior (non-unit `voting_power`) is retained as constructor-accepted but **has no selected-binary producer**
(A27.1-C2).

### B. Production provenance and membership agreement (two sets traced independently)

- **Engine set.** `num_validators = static_peers.len() + 1` (`main.rs:5503` LocalMesh, `:6170` P2P) →
  `build_uniform_validator_set` → dense IDs `{0 .. N−1}`, unit weights. Leader schedule is positional into the
  **sorted** ID list (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2079 sorted_leader_ids`, `:2395 leader_for_view = leaders[view % n]`).
- **Timeout-verification set.** `peer_key_provider` (`main.rs:5919`) enforces, before building:
  **duplicate-ID rejection** (`:362–366`); **local membership** (`:371–399`: explicit local key cross-checked
  against the signer, or signer-derived local key inserted, or `LocalKeyMissing` fail-closed); **static-peer
  coverage** (`:402–428`: every `--p2p-peer vid@addr` must have a configured key; bare `addr` fails closed).
  IDs = configured consensus-key VIDs (operator-chosen, possibly **sparse**).

**Properties enforced / NOT enforced (first-hand):** within each set — local membership ✓, static-peer coverage ✓,
duplicate handling ✓. **Across the two sets** — no production (non-genesis) startup guard enforces **count
equality** or **full ID-set equality** between the engine set (`{0..N−1}`) and the timeout-verify set (configured
VIDs). Equality holds only when the operator configures `--validator-consensus-key` with exactly `{0..N−1}` and
`N = static_peers + 1`. Agreement is **not** inferred from both being unit-weight or from matching counts; and two
independently-built sets are **not** themselves a defect.
- The one place an engine/verifier membership check exists is inside
  `load_verify_and_build_genesis_authority(…, num_validators)` (`main.rs:5835`), which is on the
  `--consensus-authority-from-genesis` branch — **startup-blocked**: that flag is FATAL-refused
  (`main.rs:5405–5417`, "before P2P service construction and before any consensus task starts, across every
  network mode, no override"). So that reconciliation is **not** reached in production.
- **LocalMesh vs P2P (kept distinct):** LocalMesh multi-validator notes that **multi-node inbound message
  ingestion is not wired into the binary path** (`main.rs:5565–5569`) — the binary drives leader proposal only,
  so the timeout-verify set is not exercised on inbound TCs there. The P2P path wires inbound routing
  (`BinaryConsensusLoopIo`), so `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` gates inbound TCs against the
  timeout-verify set.
- `main.rs:8798` (`for i in 0..num_validators`) is the Run-035 **forged-injection test harness** keygen (keys
  "NOT registered with any production provider"), not a production producer.

### C. Sparse-ID consumers and representation

- **IDs as identity / map keys.** `ConsensusValidatorSet` stores `index_by_id: HashMap<ValidatorId, usize>` and a
  `Vec`; lookups are `index_of`/`contains` (identity), not raw-ID positional indexing. `ValidatorId` is
  `ValidatorId(u64)` with `as_u64()`. Sender identity is checked by value: `on_timeout_msg` rejects
  `from != timeout.validator_id` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5099`); votes route via
  `try_admit_vote(claimed_sender.as_u64(), …)` (`:3383`).
- **Leader/proposer check (positional into sorted IDs).** `leader_for_view(view) = leaders[(view % n)]` over the
  **sorted** ID list — sparse-safe and identity-preserving; the leader route first checks
  `is_leader_for_current_view()` (`:3588`, `NonLeader` refusal).
- **Wire narrowing (u64 → u16), checked.** When the local node proposes, `proposer_index =
  u16::try_from(self.local_id.as_u64())` (`:3597–3604`): a local ID `> u16::MAX (65535)` is **fail-closed** with
  `LeaderRouteRefusal::ProposerIndexOverflow` (no UB, no silent truncation). This is the single relevant
  narrowing in the admission path; it is guarded.
- **Count/collection bound.** `num_validators = static_peers.len() + 1`; the engine `Vec` of `N` entries is an
  allocation-bounded quantity (no source-enforced numeric cap; same target-dependent premise as A27.1-C4).

### D. Bounded disposition

| Case | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Empty set | **Rejecting guard** — constructor `:414–416` (and `num_validators ≥ 1` always) |
| Duplicate IDs | **Rejecting guard** — constructor `:405–407`; producer `:362–366` |
| Zero-weight / all-zero-total | **Not reachable in production** — no selected-binary producer emits non-unit weight; constructor-accepted only on the weighted-library path (no binary consumer) |
| Sparse / out-of-dense-range IDs in the **engine** set | **Not reachable** — `build_uniform` always emits dense `{0..N−1}` |
| Sparse / out-of-dense-range IDs in the **timeout-verify** set, and engine≠verify disagreement | **Operator-configuration-reachable** (not authenticated remote input): the operator independently chooses `validator_id`, `--p2p-peer` set, and `--validator-consensus-key` VIDs, and no non-genesis startup guard enforces engine==verify ID-set/count equality. Leader selection and sender checks are sparse-safe; the sole wire narrowing (`proposer_index` u16) is fail-closed. **Precise unresolved boundary:** whether an operator-misconfigured engine≠verify set yields a multi-node **safety/liveness** effect requires a multi-node admission-and-effect trace — **queued to OBL-CONS-8**, not asserted here. |

Separations held: **operator configuration capability** (choosing mismatched sets) ≠ **peer capability** ≠
**authenticated consensus input**. A configuration mismatch is **not** turned into a remote exploit — no
admission-and-effect trace from authenticated remote input to a disagreement-driven effect is established at this
revision (and LocalMesh does not even wire inbound ingestion). **No new finding** is warranted (operator-config
property, no violated contract established without the queued multi-node effect trace); duplicate check:

## A27.1-C3 Quorum mathematics corrected `[SUPERSEDED-A27 → A27.1-C3]`

A27 called `two_thirds_vp` the "standard >2/3" quorum. Corrected: `ceil(2W/3)` (`validator_set.rs:494`,
`(2*total).div_ceil(3)`) with the predicate `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp` implements a **≥2/3 (inclusive)** threshold,
**not uniformly >2/3**. Small-total distinction (`two_thirds_vp(W)`):

| `W` | `ceil(2W/3)` | `2W/3` | admitted `acc` vs `2W/3` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 2 | 2 (exact) | `acc ≥ 2` admits **exactly 2/3** (inclusive) |
| 6 | 4 | 4 (exact) | `acc ≥ 4` admits **exactly 2/3** |
| 9 | 6 | 6 (exact) | `acc ≥ 6` admits **exactly 2/3** |
| 4 | 3 | 2.67 | `acc ≥ 3` strictly exceeds 2/3 |
| 5 | 4 | 3.33 | `acc ≥ 4` strictly exceeds 2/3 |

So when `W ≡ 0 (mod 3)` the threshold equals exactly `2W/3` and the `≥` predicate admits the exact-2/3 boundary;
otherwise `ceil` rounds up and the admitted power strictly exceeds `2W/3`. The **count** helper `quorum_size =
2f+1` (`:483–486`, `f = ⌊(n−1)/3⌋`) is a **separate**, count-based quantity and is not the voting-power predicate.
The intended fault model (`n = 3f+1`) is stated separately and **no protocol defect is declared from the formula's
spelling** (nor is it declared universally safe). **Remaining boundary (named, not claimed resolved):** whether a
`≥2/3`-inclusive voting-power threshold yields sufficient quorum **intersection** under the intended fault model
(especially at the exact-2/3 boundary for `W ≡ 0 (mod 3)`), and degenerate/small-set behavior, are **queued to
OBL-CONS-7** — not resolved here and not folded into OBL-CONS-6.

## A27.1-C4 Overflow disposition bounded precisely `[refines A27]`

Retained (demonstrated): constructor `total` and all signer accumulation **saturate**
(`validator_set.rs:409`, `qc.rs:102`, `timeout_verify.rs:423`, `timeout.rs:450`, `maybe_tc_for`); the sole
unchecked op `2 * total` (`:494`) overflows above `u64::MAX/2`.

Corrections:
- **Deployed overflow-check behavior is not established by committed profiles** `[SUPERSEDED-A27 → A27.1-C4]`.
  A27 inferred "release wraps / dev-test panics" from the absence of `[profile.release]`/`overflow-checks` in
  `Cargo.toml`. Withdrawn: the committed profiles do **not** establish the **deployed** build's effective
  `overflow-checks` (a deployer may set `overflow-checks = true` in release or via `RUSTFLAGS`). Stated precisely:
  the overflow's *effect* (panic vs two's-complement wrap to a spuriously-low threshold) depends on the
  **effective** overflow-check setting of the actual build, which the repository alone does not fix.
- **Saturation ≠ semantic preservation.** `saturating_add` prevents a *wrap* in those additions, but does **not**
  by itself preserve mathematical voting-power semantics: a saturated `total`/`acc` at `u64::MAX` is no longer the
  true sum, so saturation bounds the panic/wrap hazard without proving the quorum comparison remains numerically
  faithful at extreme weights.
- **Selected-binary unit-weight routes — allocation premise, not a source check.** Under unit weights,
  production `total = N` (validator count). Reaching `N > u64::MAX/2 = 2^63 − 1` would require > 2^63 distinct
  `ValidatorSetEntry` (each with a `Vec` slot + `HashMap` index entry), i.e. a quantity of memory no realistic
  target can allocate. This is a **target-dependent allocation/representation premise**, explicitly **not** a
  **source-enforced validator-count check** (there is no `checked_mul`, count cap, or guard in `two_thirds_vp`);
  it is not asserted as an unconditional all-platform invariant.
- **Caller-supplied weighted library sets — observation retained.** The `2*total` overflow (and aggregate-`acc`
  saturation) remain a real property of the weight-preserving library path with a caller-supplied non-unit-weight
  set whose total exceeds `u64::MAX/2`; this is **not dismissed** merely because that path has no selected-binary
  consumer at this revision. Applying the register's existing classification and duplicate policy, it is recorded
  as a **bounded library observation under OBL-CONS-6** (open library issue; no selected-binary reachability
  established; unexecuted runtime) — **no new ID or severity** is required to complete this correction.
