## A27.2 OBL-CONS-6 — quorum voting-power arithmetic, callers, weight provenance, disposition

Primary bodies read first-hand: `qbind-consensus/src/validator_set.rs` (constructor `:396–423`, `f`/`quorum_size`
`:473–486`, `two_thirds_vp` `:491–495`, `has_quorum` `:500–513`); `qc.rs:83–115`; `timeout_verify.rs:408–431`;
`timeout.rs:454`; `driver.rs:101–107`; weight producers; `Cargo.toml` profiles.

### A. Arithmetic contract (checked / saturating / ordinary separated)

| Quantity | Operation (source) | Arithmetic kind | Overflow behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total voting power (constructor) | `total_vp = total_vp.saturating_add(info.voting_power)` (`validator_set.rs:409`) | **saturating** | caps at `u64::MAX`; cannot panic |
| Threshold `two_thirds_vp` | `(2 * total).div_ceil(3)` (`:494`) | **ordinary** (unchecked `*`; `div_ceil` safe) | **only unchecked op**; overflows when `total > u64::MAX/2` |
| Accumulated signer VP | `acc.saturating_add(entry.voting_power)` (`has_quorum:508`, `qc.rs:102`, `timeout_verify.rs:423`) | **saturating** | saturates to `u64::MAX` |
| Count helpers | `f = (n.saturating_sub(1))/3` (`:479`); `quorum_size = 2*f+1` (`:485`) | saturating sub / ordinary (small `usize`) | `f ≤ (n-1)/3` ⇒ `2f+1 ≤ n`; no realistic overflow |

**Duplicate handling per consuming path:** constructor rejects duplicate `ValidatorId` (`:405–407`).
`qc::validate` **dedups** signers via a `HashSet` (`DuplicateSigner`, `qc.rs:94–96`) — the safety-critical QC
path. `has_quorum` (`:500–513`) does **not** dedup its input iterator (a repeated id double-counts; unknown ids
ignored as 0). `timeout_verify` (`:408–423`) iterates `evidence` with no explicit duplicate-`validator_id`
dedup (a repeated evidence entry would double-count via `saturating_add`; distinctness relied on upstream) —
recorded as a per-path difference, not asserted as a defect.

**Static boundary table** (`two_thirds_vp = (2·total).div_ceil(3)`):

| `total` | `two_thirds_vp` | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (non-empty all-zero-weight set) | 0 | degenerate: any `acc ≥ 0` meets it — **not produced** (every producer sets weight 1; constructor rejects empty) |
| 1 / 2 / 3 | 1 / 2 / 2 | normal |
| `N` unit (realistic) | `ceil(2N/3)` | standard >2/3 voting-power quorum |
| `u64::MAX/2` = 9 223 372 036 854 775 807 | `2·total = u64::MAX−1` (no overflow) | last safe total |
| `> u64::MAX/2` | **overflow** | **panic** (overflow-checks on) / **wrap → spuriously-low threshold** (overflow-checks off) |
| signer `acc` sum `> u64::MAX` | — | `acc` **saturates** to `u64::MAX` ⇒ `≥` any threshold |

**Overflow-checks / panic settings.** `Cargo.toml` defines only `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.test]` and sets
**no `overflow-checks`** key and **no `[profile.release]`**. Under Rust defaults: dev/test → overflow-checks
**on** (the `2·total` overflow **panics**); release → overflow-checks **off** (it **wraps** to a spuriously-low
threshold). Thus the mathematical overflow at `total > u64::MAX/2` is **mathematics**; the *effect* (panic vs
silent wrong-low threshold) is **conditional on the build profile**.

**Intended quorum/fault assumptions.** Classic BFT `n = 3f+1`; count quorum `2f+1` (`quorum_size`); voting-power
quorum `ceil(2·total/3)` (`two_thirds_vp`). The threshold formula is the standard >2/3 voting-power rule — **not
a defect by itself**; no protocol defect is inferred from the formula alone.

### B. Caller completeness (production vs test/sim)

| Consumer (source) | Class | Validator-set source | Pre-threshold checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qc::validate` (`qc.rs:106`) | **production** (QC validation) | consumer-supplied `ConsensusValidatorSet` (unit-weight producers below) | membership + **dedup** (HashSet) before threshold |
| `timeout_verify::verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (`timeout_verify.rs:425`) | **production** (node loop `:7255/:7886`) | same | per-evidence `verify_timeout_msg`, mixed-view guard, membership |
| `timeout.rs:454` | **production** (timeout cert) | same | membership/accumulation |
| `driver.rs:106` `self.set.has_quorum(ids)` | library wrapper (driver) → `has_quorum` | driver's set | none beyond `has_quorum` (no dedup) |
| `validator_set.rs:512` | internal (`has_quorum` body) | — | — |
| `safety_record_store/validate.rs:370,460` (`ctx.two_thirds_vp()`) | **separate type** (RUN-422 safety-record store) — **excluded OBL-STO-2b**, not `ConsensusValidatorSet` | n/a | n/a |
| `tests/*`, `validator_set.rs` unit tests | test/sim | test fixtures | n/a |

Node-binary reachability: the production consensus loop consumes quorum arithmetic via `verify_timeout_msg` /
`verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:7032/7255/7723/7886`, all < the
`#[cfg(test)]` boundary `:9439`) and QC verification. Function-name similarity / comments / re-exports were not
treated as caller evidence.

### C. Admitted-weight provenance

**Every in-tree validator-set producer sets `voting_power: 1` (uniform/unit).** Production producers:
`build_uniform_validator_set` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:713–722`, weight 1); genesis authority
(`genesis_consensus_authority.rs:407`, weight 1, comment "voting-weight binding is out of scope for this
genesis-static DevNet run"); `peer_key_provider.rs:434` (weight 1). Test/sim producers:
`validator_config.rs:357` (explicitly "test-only helper; production code may use different logic"),
`timeout_verification_bridge.rs:687` (test helper), `forged_injection.rs` (Run-035 "opt-in dev/test-only"
harness), and the `safety_record_store/owner/model.rs` TEST-ONLY model. Non-unit weights appear **only** in
`validator_set.rs` unit tests (small values, e.g. `validator_set_has_quorum_weighted:1547`).

→ Weights are **uniform (unit)** in every wired path. **No stake-derived or externally-configurable weighting is
wired** anywhere; the `ValidatorSetEntry.voting_power` field and the weight-aware helpers exist, but the
first missing integration boundary for weighted/stake voting power is that **no producer binds a non-unit
weight** (genesis comment defers it explicitly). Under unit weights, production `total` = validator **count**
`N`, and the supported bound is an **allocation/representation premise** — constructing a set with
`total > u64::MAX/2` would require ~9.2×10¹⁸ distinct `ValidatorSetEntry` (each with a unique id, a Vec slot, and
a HashMap entry), which is not allocatable — **not** a source-enforced numeric guard (there is no `checked_mul`
or bound check in `two_thirds_vp`).

### D. Disposition

**Bounded containment argument per production route.** For `qc::validate`, `timeout_verify`, `timeout`, and
`driver::has_quorum`: each consumes a **unit-weight** `ConsensusValidatorSet` whose `total` equals the validator
**count**, which is bounded far below `u64::MAX/2` by allocation infeasibility; constructor `total` and all
signer accumulation are **saturating**; QC dedups signers; the all-zero-weight degenerate `total = 0` set is
**not produced** (every producer sets weight 1, constructor rejects empty). Therefore, at this revision, **no
production route can drive `2·total` to overflow or produce a spuriously-low/degenerate threshold.**

**Classification (no forcing).**
- *Open library issue:* the **unchecked `2 * total` multiply** in `two_thirds_vp` (`validator_set.rs:494`) is a
  latent weighted-library arithmetic hazard — reachable only by constructing a **non-unit-weight** set whose
  total exceeds `u64::MAX/2`, with effect conditional on the build profile (panic vs silent wrap). This is a
  **callable library property**, not a production-reachable one.
- *Production reachability:* **none** at this revision — contained by unit weights + allocation infeasibility +
  saturating accumulation, as above.
- *Unexecuted runtime consequence:* **UNEXECUTED** (no node run; no overflow observed).

**Existing-finding / ID check.** No existing finding specifically covers quorum voting-power overflow
(QBIND-A1-F001/A21-F1 is a decoder *allocation* bound — distinct). **No new finding is minted:** the hazard is
not production-reachable here (so forcing a finding would overstate it), and the production routes are contained;
minting an ID for an unreachable, profile-conditional library multiply would be forcing. The observation is
recorded under **OBL-CONS-6** as a bounded library note, explicitly separated from production containment. The
degenerate all-zero-weight adjacency is queued to **OBL-CONS-7** (not produced here). Severity is **not forced**;
runtime remains unexecuted.

## A26.1 Bounded carried-forward refinements to A25-F1 (local; indexes not rebuilt; startup trace not repeated)

A25-F1 keeps its stable ID and its **assurance-scoped, severity-unresolved** disposition. Four refinements:

1. **Comparison with A23-F1 corrected** `[A26 refines A25-F1]`. A23-F1's concrete mechanism is the **missing
   equality between the bundle's verifying signing key K and the ratification target key T** (register §28
   / line "A23-F1 (signing-key/ratification-target binding)"). It is **not** a Run-188 custody-class enum
   equality. A25-F1 (Run-163 governance proof satisfied by a public-data byte pattern) and A23-F1 therefore do
   **not** share the same concrete root cause; any linkage is thematic only (authorization weakened by
   insufficient binding/verification), not a shared mechanism. The "shared root cause with A23-F1" phrasing in
   A25.2 is withdrawn.
2. **Documented guarantee vs auditor-inferred expectation** `[A26 refines A25-F1]`. The operator surface
   (`cli.rs:869–920`, `--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-proof-required`) is **`hide = true`, disabled-by-default**,
   documented as "**source/test selector wiring only … release-binary … evidence is deferred to Run 172**", and
   explicitly disclaims "**NOT** a governance execution engine, **NOT** an on-chain governance proof, **NOT** a
   KMS/HSM custody claim, **NOT** a validator-set rotation primitive, **NOT** sufficient to enable MainNet
   peer-driven apply." So the shipped surface **does** carry caveats. A25's "no operator-facing caveat" is
   narrowed: the "independent governance authorization" assurance was an **auditor-inferred expectation**, not a
   **documented guarantee that is violated**. A25-F1 stands only as: an operator who enables the hidden flag
   expecting an independent cryptographic governance authorization would be mistaken; the code documents the
   limitation rather than promising the assurance.
3. **Ratification-signature trust anchor scoped** `[A26 refines A25-F1/A25.1-A2]`. The genuine ML-DSA-44
   verification (`verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2`) is anchored to the authority loaded from the
   **configured external genesis file** (`main.rs` `genesis_cfg.authority`), i.e. the
   `bundle_signing_authority_roots` of that genesis. A25 does not thereby restore any boot-genesis / pinning
   equivalence — that remains unresolved. Inability to **forge fresh** signed content does **not** imply
   inability to **supply an existing authentic** ratification; replay of a pre-existing authentic ratification
   is a separate question guarded only by the per-domain anti-rollback sequence, not closed here.
4. **Run-055 sequence vs marker authority-domain sequence kept distinct** `[A26 refines A25.1-C2/C3]`. In the
   A25 startup trace, `loaded.bundle.sequence` (the Run-055 trust-bundle anti-rollback sequence,
   `check_and_update_sequence`) is a **different value** from the marker's `authority_domain_sequence`. A set
   `--data-dir` alone does **not** make either check succeed: C2/C3 additionally assume the **persisted state is
   compatible** (no rollback / same-sequence-equivocation) and that **I/O succeeds**. The marker persist is an
   **advancing write** only when `should_persist` is true; otherwise it is an **idempotent no-op**
   (`persist_accepted_v2_marker_after_commit_boundary`). The A25 "accepted ⇒ writes happen" step is thus
   conditioned on these assumptions.

**Method.** Repository-wide scoped searches for key/secret writers (`fs::write`/`File::create`/`.seal(` over
key material, `generate_keypair`, `private_key_hex`, `*.sk.bin`), plus first-hand reads of `keystore.rs`,
`signer_loader.rs`, the example helpers, `identity_cli.rs`, and the authority-custody / KMS-HSM / remote-signer
modules. `qbind-node/Cargo.toml` declares exactly one `[[bin]]` (`qbind-node`, `src/main.rs`); everything under
`examples/` is a separate example binary, not the node.

### Writer table — entry point → format/property → writer fn → production-caller status → persistence → unresolved

| Entry point | Format / property | Writer (file:line) | Production-caller status | Persistence / perms | Unresolved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `identity_cli::dispatch` (`qbind-node identity`) | **authority/custody transport** — ML-KEM-768 leaf **secret** key `leaf.kem.sk.bin` (+ public cert/identity JSON); root ML-DSA-44 signing key held in memory, **never written** | `identity_cli.rs:1208`, SK write `:379–388` | **PRODUCTION-REACHABLE** from the binary (`main.rs:2019–2025` intercepts argv `identity`→`dispatch`→`exit`), but **DevNet-only, fail-closed** on any other env (`identity_cli.rs` `if env != "devnet" → EXIT_REFUSED`) | `fs::write` then `set_permissions(0o600)` (cfg(unix)); create→chmod window | not a **consensus** key; entropy `MlKem768Backend::generate_keypair` |
| `devnet_consensus_signer_keystore_helper` (example) | **plaintext validator keystore** `{"suite_id":100,"private_key_hex":"…"}` (operational ML-DSA-44 **consensus** secret key) | `examples/devnet_consensus_signer_keystore_helper.rs:51` (keygen `:77–78`, write `:86–89`) | **NOT** reachable from `qbind-node` (example bin only); operator-runnable DevNet tooling, labelled "evidence/test helper only … DEVNET-EPHEMERAL" | `fs::write` then `set_mode_0600` (cfg(unix); `.pk.hex` not chmodded); create→chmod window | keypair entropy real (`MlDsa44Backend::generate_keypair` → `fips204::ml_dsa_44::try_keygen`, OS entropy); **plaintext at rest** |
| `devnet_pqc_root_helper` (example); `run_419`/`run_421` drivers (examples) | authority/custody transport — ML-KEM-768 leaf **secret** key `*.kem.sk.bin`; root signing key never written | `examples/devnet_pqc_root_helper.rs:78` (`:116–120`); `run_419…:196`, `run_421…:207` | **NOT** reachable from `qbind-node` (example bins) | `fs::write` then `set_permissions(0o600)` cfg(unix); create→chmod window | no consensus key |
| `key_rotation_cli::init_key_rotation` | **key-adjacent metadata, NO secret** — `KeyRotationEvent` JSON holding only the **new PUBLIC key** + validator id/epoch/role | `key_rotation_cli.rs:164`, write `:197` | library fn exported via `lib.rs`; **no `[[bin]]`** and **0 non-defn callers**; doc references a `qbind-key-rotation` binary not declared in-tree | pretty JSON; no KDF/secret | whether rotation-event emission ships as a bin elsewhere (writes only a public key regardless) |
| `keystore.rs` test helpers | plaintext (`:994`) and **EncryptedFsV1** (`:1006`) | `write_keystore_file:994`, `write_encrypted_keystore_file:1006` | **`#[cfg(test)]` only** (boundary `:984`) | **deterministic** salt/nonce (see below); `File::create` (umask, no chmod) | — |
| `tests/t153_encrypted_keystore_integration_tests.rs` | EncryptedFsV1 | `:60–95` | **test-only** | deterministic salt/nonce; `File::create` no chmod | — |

### EncryptedFsV1 writer — entropy / KDF / serialization / permissions (the only in-tree encrypted *writers* are test-only)

Production `keystore.rs` (lines 1–959) **decrypts/reads only** — `FsValidatorKeystore` / `EncryptedFsValidatorKeystore`
expose `new` + `load_signing_key` + parsers; **no `fs::write`/`File::create`/`.seal(` in the production region**.
The only encrypted *writers* are the `#[cfg(test)]` helpers, and their randomness is **deterministic**:

- **salt** (`keystore.rs:1020–1029`): `// For tests, use a deterministic "random" salt based on entry_id` — bytes copied from `entry_id`.
- **nonce** (`keystore.rs:1031–1040`): `// For tests, use a deterministic "random" nonce` — `entry_id` bytes reversed, `wrapping_add(1)`.
- **No `OsRng` / `thread_rng` / `fill_bytes` anywhere in `keystore.rs`** (scoped grep = 0).
- **KDF**: `derive_key_pbkdf2(passphrase, &salt, kdf_iterations)` (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256; `qbind-crypto/src/kdf.rs:69` `pbkdf2_hmac::<Sha256>`); tests pass `DEFAULT_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 100_000` (`kdf.rs:20`); `PBKDF2_SALT_SIZE = 16`, nonce = 12.
- **AEAD / serialization**: ChaCha20-Poly1305 `seal` → hand-written JSON `{version,suite_id,aead,kdf,kdf_iterations,salt_hex,nonce_hex,ciphertext_hex}`.
- **Permissions**: `File::create` (umask-dependent; **no** `set_permissions`/`0o600`).

→ **Do not infer production entropy from these**; they are deterministic test fixtures.

### Production load boundary (where consensus keys must come from instead)

The `qbind-node` binary **never provisions a consensus signing key**; it **loads** one (`signer_loader.rs`,
Run-032: "reuses the existing keystore primitives … does NOT invent a new keystore format, does NOT clone or
expose private keys"): from `config.signer_keystore_path`, entry id `validator-{N}`; encrypted-keystore
passphrase read from env `QBIND_VALIDATOR_KEY_PASSPHRASE`. Only `LocalKeystorePlain` / `LocalKeystoreEncrypted`
load backends are wired; `RemoteSigner` / `HsmPkcs11` / `LoopbackTesting` are not wired for loading here
(→ delegate to external systems). `validator_config.rs` is read-only (0 writers). Consensus signing keys are
therefore provisioned **externally** (operator tooling such as the plaintext example helper, or an external
KMS/HSM/remote-signer).

### Scoped negatives (searches, not filenames/comments)

- No **production** consensus signing-key (`private_key_hex` / `suite_id 100`) writer: all `private_key_hex`
  writer hits are `#[cfg(test)]` (`keystore.rs`, `t153`) or the example helper; no `src/` non-test writer.
- Authority-custody / KMS-HSM / remote-signer modules (`pqc_authority_custody.rs`,
  `pqc_authority_kms_hsm_backend.rs`, `pqc_production_kms_hsm_custody_backend.rs`,
  `pqc_remote_authority_signer.rs`, `pqc_production_remote_signer_backend.rs`) write **zero** `fs::write`/`File::create`;
  they are abstractions/verifiers/fixtures delegating custody to external KMS/HSM/remote-signer systems.
- Custody/KMS/remote-signer **release-binary example helpers** (run_204/206/294/296/195/189…): 0 secret-key
  indicators (fixtures/tables only).
- `qbind-remote-signer/src/main.rs`: 0 `generate_keypair`/`fs::write`/`File::create`/`private_key_hex` — not a provisioner.

**A26.2 conclusion.** The in-tree **encrypted-format** validator-keystore writer is **absent in production/operator
scope** (only deterministic `#[cfg(test)]` writers exist); the only operator-runnable **consensus-key** writer is
the DevNet-ephemeral **plaintext** example helper; the only **production-reachable** key-material writer is the
DevNet-only `identity` subcommand writing a **KEM transport** secret key (not a consensus key). Encrypted
provisioning is an **external** boundary. This **answers OBL-KEY-1b**.

## A26.3 Question B — signing-journal integration inventory

**ANSWER: NO.** At the pinned HEAD, the running node's signer paths do **not** execute anti-equivocation
admission before signing. The journal type, its full reserve/consume/record API, the durable storage backend
trait (production-implemented), and even **journal-aware production signer wrappers** all exist — but the
production node **never constructs a journal** and threads a literal **`None`** into every signer call site, so
the admission-before-signing code is **never reached**; the journal-aware outbound path **fails closed instead**.
The module's own header states it (`signing_reservation_journal.rs:26–28`: "It does **not** wire any production
activation path. Production startup never initializes a journal").

### Interface inventory

- **`signing_reservation_journal.rs`** = THE anti-equivocation journal (`pub mod`, `lib.rs`). `SigningReservationJournal`
  (`:2146`); `::initialize(store, limit)` (`:2350`) / `::open(store)` (`:2411`); **`reserve_for_sign(position,
  binding)`** (`:2611`) = the admission call (persists a `Reserved` record *before* the signer runs; returns
  FreshlyReserved / ExactRetryRetained / Conflict / **PotentiallySigned** / Exhausted / LiveCapacityExhausted);
  `consume_for_signing` (`:4122`); `record_signed_result` (`:4180`). `SigningKind` (`:128`) = **Proposal, Vote only
  (no Timeout)**. Backend trait `SigningJournalStorage` (`:1258`) with synced writes (`put_signing_record_synced`
  `:1267`).
- **`signing_journal_admission.rs`** = **NOT** anti-equivocation admission. `pub(crate)` module; header: "NO
  production caller yet … isolated implementation-and-test path." It admits **fixed-capacity memory buffers**
  (retrieval/reserve/publish workspace) through the existing `SharedAccountant`; a **separate** mechanism.
- **`safety_record_store/`** = a **separate** generic safety-record store + `SharedAccountant` ledger + a
  TEST-ONLY model (`owner/model.rs`, `#[cfg(test)]`, header "TEST-ONLY, NOT wired … no production caller"). Holds
  `TimeoutCert` retained-record types. **Not** the anti-equivocation journal — kept distinct (per task caution).

### Caller trace (grep evidence; production region vs tests)

- `reserve_for_sign(` production call sites: `binary_consensus_loop.rs:4755` (proposal), `:5179` (vote) — both
  inside the journal-aware guarded family. All other callers are `#[cfg(test)]` / `tests/` / the TEST-ONLY
  `owner/model.rs` mirror / the `d7d10` integration test.
- The journal is threaded as **`Option<&SigningReservationJournal>`** from the top production entry
  `run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` (`:2805`, reached from `main.rs`) and is **always `None`** in production:
  `run_binary_consensus_loop` → `…_with_io(…, None)` (`:2786`); `do_leader_tick` call sites (`:3223`, `:3378`)
  pass `None` (arg annotated "no signing-reservation journal wired in production").
- `guarded_sign_proposal_for_broadcast` (`:4370`) unwraps the Option at **`:4421–4432`**: on `None` it increments
  `outbound_proposal_journal_unavailable_total`, prints "outbound proposal **NOT signed** (signing-reservation
  journal unavailable) — **fail-closed**", and **returns before `reserve_for_sign`** (`:4755`). The vote path is
  equivalent. So in production, `reserve_for_sign` / `consume_for_signing` / `signer.sign_*` on this path are
  **unreachable**.
- The non-journal direct family `sign_proposal_for_broadcast` / `sign_vote_for_broadcast` (`:5356` / `:5449`,
  under `#[cfg(test)]` blocks at `:5355` / `:5448`) has **no production caller** (callers are tests).
- **Construction**: every `SigningReservationJournal::initialize|open` site (`:12840`, `:26570`, `:26573`,
  `:27711`) is **beyond the `mod tests` boundary (`:9439`)** → **zero production construction**.
- `signer_loader.rs` and `p2p_node_builder.rs`: **zero** journal references (grep = 0). The node's
  signer-loading/construction path knows nothing of the journal.
- Timeout signing never involves the journal (`SigningKind` has no Timeout). A separate direct-signing path in
  `hotstuff_node_sim.rs` is a test-oriented harness.
- Storage substrate IS production: `impl SigningJournalStorage for RocksDbConsensusStorage` (`storage.rs:1456`)
  and `InMemoryConsensusStorage` (`:1764`) are non-test — the synced-write capability is wired, but **no journal
  object is ever built over it** in production.

### Per-path bucket classification

| Path | (a) exists | (b) lib/test invocation | (c) prod construction | (d) prod admission-before-sign | (e) persistence-before-release | (f) restart recovery + fail-closed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SigningReservationJournal` (reserve/consume/record) | **YES** | **YES** (model mirror, journal tests, d7d10 test) | **NO** | **NO** (always `None` → guarded path fails closed before `reserve_for_sign`) | library only (never exercised in prod) | library only (`open` reloads; `Reserved`-without-continuation → `PotentiallySigned`/refuse) — never wired |
| `signing_journal_admission.rs` workspace admission | YES | YES (cfg(test)) | NO | n/a (memory-buffer admission, not a sign gate) | n/a | n/a |
| `safety_record_store` | YES | YES | partial substrate | n/a (generic store, not the journal) | n/a | n/a |

### First missing integration boundary (single)

`run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2805`) would need to (1) **construct** a
`SigningReservationJournal` via `::initialize(store, limit)` / `::open(store)` over the production
`RocksDbConsensusStorage` (which **already** implements `SigningJournalStorage`, `storage.rs:1456`), most naturally
supplied through `p2p_node_builder.rs` / `signer_loader.rs` (both currently hold **zero** journal references), and
(2) pass **`Some(&journal)`** instead of the literal `None` at `do_leader_tick` (`:3223`, `:3378`) and the inbound
handler. The earliest single gate the binary hits today is the **`None` arm at `:4421–4432`** (proposal) and its
vote equivalent: a constructed journal must flow to those unwraps before `reserve_for_sign` (`:4755` / `:5179`)
can ever execute. Until that construction + `Some` wiring exists, no anti-equivocation admission runs before
signing; the guarded outbound paths **fail closed (do not sign)** under the `None` journal.

### Durability / recovery nuances (explicit, un-inferred)

- The backend methods are `*_synced`; the module asserts `WriteOptions::set_sync(true)` / WAL flush
  (`journal.rs:32–35`) — **actual fsync was not verified** at the RocksDB byte level.
- The module **explicitly disclaims** rollback/clone resistance (`journal.rs:22–25`: "provides **no** durable
  anti-rollback anchor … The record checksum detects corruption only; it is not authentication and not rollback
  protection"). **Rollback/clone resistance must not be inferred from disk persistence.**
- The recovery test `tests/run_422_d7d2_signing_state_recovery_tests.rs` does **not** construct the journal; its
  header states "a passing test here confirms *missing* protection — it never establishes signing-state
  continuity."

**A26.3 conclusion — confirms and refines QBIND-A1-F003.** The anti-equivocation signing journal is **present but
unwired**: API, journal-aware guarded signer wrappers, `Option` plumbing, a fail-closed `None` arm, and a
production `SigningJournalStorage` backend all exist, but the journal object is **never constructed or threaded**
in production, so admission/persistence/recovery never run — the production outbound Proposal/Vote path fails
closed rather than signing with (or without) the journal. Timeout signing has no journal variant. This matches
QBIND-A1-F003 ("journal unwired") and sharpens it: the missing boundary is construction + `Some`-threading at
`run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io`, not merely absent call sites. **No new finding** (QBIND-A1-F003 applies;
RUN-422 component internals remain the excluded OBL-STO-2b thread).

## A25.1 Concrete startup scenario — joint satisfiability and ordered acceptance trace

**Scenario (one DevNet startup configuration).** `environment=Devnet`; outer ratification
enforcement explicitly invoked; `--data-dir` set; an otherwise-valid signed trust bundle and an
authentic v2 **Rotate** ratification (real authority-root ML-DSA-44 signature); a compatible
predecessor authority marker; Run-163 `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive` enabled
(`--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-proof-required`); a supplied `governance_authority_proof` sibling;
the **separate** governance-**execution** policy `Disabled` with its carrier **absent**.

**Joint satisfiability.** These coexist with no earlier rejecting guard:
- `--data-dir` set + `Devnet` ⇒ the Run-055 sequence-persistence precondition is met
  (`main.rs:7140–7169`: only TestNet/MainNet without `--data-dir` FATAL-exit; DevNet-with-`--data-dir`
  proceeds with anti-rollback active).
- A v2 sidecar routes to the v2 preflight `preflight_run_136_v2_marker_decision_for_startup`
  (`main.rs:6784`), which runs the real v2 ratification verifier directly and **skips** the v1
  Run-105 gate (`main.rs:1143–1144, 6810`) — so the two ratification gates do not both fire.
- Governance-execution `Disabled` + absent carrier is the documented legacy-bypass default and does
  not conflict with Run-163 being `Required` (independent selectors; §B).

**Prerequisite honesty.** Authentic ratification/bundle possession is an explicit prerequisite.
Authoring the `governance_authority_proof` sibling does **not** grant it: the sibling is parsed out
of the sidecar JSON *before* `BundleSigningRatificationV2` is deserialised
(`pqc_ratification_input.rs:350–354, 369`) and is **not a field of that struct** nor of its signed
preimage (`bundle_signing_ratification.rs:1314–1408` fields; `:1404–1407` `signature` is
"ML-DSA-44 over `sha3_256(v2_canonical_preimage(self))`"; preimage layout `:1414–1433` enumerates
only struct fields). Therefore adding/changing the sibling **does not change the signed ratification
preimage and does not invalidate the authority signature** — and conversely cannot forge or alter
the signed rotation facts.

### Ordered trace — input/provenance → executed check → selected outcome → next consumer

| # | Input / provenance | Executed check (source) | Selected outcome (this scenario) | Next consumer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## A25.2 Disposition — finding A25-F1

**Security contract of the additional Run-163 requirement.** By its naming and shape — a policy
literally called `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`, an operator selector
`--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-proof-required`, a `governance_authority_proof` carrying an
`issuer_authority_class` (`GenesisBound` / `EmergencyCouncil`) and an optional
`GovernanceThreshold{approvals, required, total}` — the control **promises an independent governance
authorization**: evidence that a governance authority (potentially multi-party, meeting a quorum)
separately authorized this lifecycle action, over and above the single bundle-signing authority root
that signed the ratification.

**What the shipped verifier actually delivers.** The production-wired verifier is
`fixture_issuer_signature_verifier()` (`main.rs:1260`). `verify_governance_authority_proof`
(`pqc_governance_authority.rs:503–761`) resolves to a chain of **equality comparisons** of the
proof's self-declared fields against the `candidate` / `trust_domain` — both derived from the
**already-authenticated** ratification and all **public** values — plus a **self-declared** optional
threshold (`:734–749`, `approvals >= required`, no verified signer set) and an issuer-signature
check that is a **public-data byte pattern** (`:296–313`: recompute
`b"qbind-run163-gov:" ‖ class.tag() ‖ ":" ‖ authority_root_fingerprint ‖ ":" ‖ candidate_v2_digest ‖
":" ‖ sequence.to_be_bytes()` and compare bytes — **concatenation + equality, not a cryptographic
signature**). It binds **no** secret key distinct from (or even equal to) anything, and **no**
verified approver set.

**Capability/effect analysis.**
- *Does it bypass or weaken the real authorization?* **No.** The authenticated ratification
  ML-DSA-44 signature (A2) is an independent, upstream, fail-closed gate; the proof sibling is
  outside its signed preimage (A25.1), so enabling/supplying a proof cannot forge, alter, or skip
  it. A party lacking the authority private key still cannot produce an acceptable ratification.
  The proof is additionally **bound to the authenticated candidate** (A7 equalities), so it cannot
  authorize anything the ratification does not already authorize. **No distinct authorization
  defect.**
- *Does it deliver the independent governance assurance it advertises?* **No.** Any party holding
  the (already-required) valid ratification can compute every equality value and the public-data
  issuer byte pattern, and omit or self-declare the threshold — so the "governance authority proof"
  adds **zero** independent authorization assurance on the shipped verifier.

**Classification: operator-facing assurance gap** (source-established). The additional Run-163
requirement, as shipped and production-wired, provides the *appearance* of an independent
governance-authorization control while delivering none. This is **not** a distinct authorization
escalation (nothing is bypassed; the real ratification signature still gates and the proof is
candidate-bound), and **not** merely "intentional fixture without a contract": although the code
labels the verifier a fixture with production evidence deferred (Run 172/221/227), the operator-facing
selector is wired into the production binary startup path with **no surface-level signal** that the
check is non-cryptographic, which is precisely what creates the operator-assurance contract it fails
to meet.

**Duplicate / root-cause comparison.**
- **A23-F1 / E23** (trust-bundle K≠T custody governance-class gate = enum equality, not
  authorization) — **shared root cause**: governance/authority "verification" implemented as
  structural / public-data comparison rather than cryptographic authorization. A25-F1 is the **same
  root-cause family on a different surface** (startup marker-acceptance governance-proof gate vs
  custody-attestation gate) with a distinct concrete mechanism (public-data byte-pattern issuer
  signature + self-declared threshold).
- **A19-F1** (authority RemoteSigner selector ignored) — **shared pattern**: an operator-facing
  selector advertises an enforcement/authorization property the wired path does not deliver. A25-F1
  differs in that the selector *is* honoured (the policy genuinely gates, §A24.1) but what it gates
  on is non-cryptographic.
- **A8-F1** (program authorization gap) — related authorization-surface theme but a different
  subsystem; not the same root cause.

**Decision: mint distinct stable ID `A25-F1`** — *Operator-facing governance-proof assurance gap:
the production-wired `--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-proof-required` startup control is satisfied by a
public-data byte pattern (shipped fixture issuer-signature verifier) and a self-declared threshold,
delivering no independent governance authorization beyond the already-verified ratification
signature.* Cross-referenced to **A23-F1 (root cause)** and **A19-F1 (selector-assurance pattern)**.
A distinct ID (not folded into A23-F1) is warranted because the surface, the operator control, and
the concrete mechanism differ; the shared root cause is recorded explicitly rather than by merging.

**Severity / runtime uncertainty (explicit).** Severity is **uncertain** and is scoped to
**assurance/operational**, not demonstrated authorization bypass. Runtime consequences are
**UNEXECUTED**: no live mutation, networking, or root replacement was exercised. The verifier is
acknowledged scaffolding (production implementation deferred), so A25-F1 may describe pre-production
behaviour; it is nonetheless a **source-established** gap because the selector is production-wired
with no operator-facing caveat. Lack of runtime execution does not erase the source-established
behaviour; equally, public-data verification alone does **not** prove the surrounding authenticated
authorization was bypassed — and here it is not (the ratification signature stands).

## A25.3 Narrow carried-forward reporting corrections

1. **C5 meaning restored** `[A25 corrects A24.1]`. C5 denotes the **production cryptographic
   custody / signing-lifecycle** obligation. A24.1's layer text labelled "C5 (consensus
   liveness/safety)" — that redefinition is withdrawn. C5 remains **OPEN** on its custody/signing
   criteria.
2. **ActivateInitial verification corrected** `[A25 corrects A24.1-C3/C5]`. `ActivateInitial` is
   proof-**optional only when the context is `Unavailable`**. When a proof is `Available`/`Supplied`
   it is **still verified** — `evaluate_governance_marker_gate` runs the `Supplied` branch
   (`pqc_governance_authority.rs:1013–1027`) **before** any policy/action branch, regardless of
   action. A24.1's unconditional "`ActivateInitial` would short-circuit to `NotRequiredNoProof` even
   under this policy" holds **only** for the `Unavailable` context; with a supplied proof even
   `ActivateInitial` is verified (→ `Accepted`/`Rejected`).
3. **"Does not establish authorization" scoped.** That statement applies **only** to the additional
   Run-163 governance **proof** under the shipped fixture verifier. The **separate** real
   ratification ML-DSA-44 signature (`verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2`,
   `bundle_signing_ratification.rs:~2044`) **is** a genuine cryptographic authority authorization and
   remains verified and fail-closed; A25 does not weaken that statement.
4. **Fixture mechanism terminology.** The fixture issuer-signature mechanism is a **public-data byte
   pattern** (domain-tag ‖ public fields, concatenation + byte equality), explicitly **not** a
   cryptographic signature. This replaces the "checksum / byte-equality" phrasing used in A24.1-C6.

These corrections do not reopen unrelated audits and do not rebuild the 54-ID coverage index.

## A24.1 corrections

Each correction cites executable source at HEAD and marks the superseded A24 statement
`[SUPERSEDED-A24 → A24.1-Cn]`.

### C1 — Withdraw "production startup ctx always sets `governance_proof_load = Absent`" `[SUPERSEDED-A24 → A24.1-C1]`

A24 asserted the production startup builder hardcodes `GovernanceProofLoadStatus::Absent`,
making the schema gap total. The executable path refutes this:

- **`crates/qbind-node/src/pqc_ratification_input.rs:350–367`** — a v2 sidecar's optional
  `governance_authority_proof` sibling is parsed into one of three states: **`Absent`** (sibling
  missing or JSON `null`), **`Available(proof)`** (sibling present and well-formed → typed
  `GovernanceAuthorityProof`), or **`Malformed(e)`** (sibling present but unparseable).
- **`pqc_ratification_input.rs:489–497`** — the Run-169 versioned dispatcher's **v2 arm** returns
  `V2 { ratification, governance_proof }`, carrying the loaded status out (v1 arm, line 422, is
  always `Absent` — v1 never defined the carrier).
- **`crates/qbind-node/src/main.rs:508–523`** — the startup builder's **V2 arm (516–519)**
  propagates the loaded `governance_proof` into `governance_proof_load`. Only the **V1 arm (514)**
  and the **no-sidecar arm (522)** hardcode `Absent`.
- **`main.rs:1264–1278`** passes `&ctx_data.governance_proof_load` (the real status) into the
  startup preflight.

**Corrected statement.** When an operator supplies a v2 ratification sidecar containing a
well-formed `governance_authority_proof` sibling, the startup status is **`Available(proof)`**, not
`Absent`. The "always Absent / total wire-schema gap / unreachable-`Supplied`" conclusion is
withdrawn. The carrier exists, is parsed, and is propagated to the gate on the production startup
`--p2p-trust-bundle` route.

**Root-cause note (documentation defect, not a reachability fact).** A stale doc comment at
**`crates/qbind-node/src/pqc_governance_authority.rs:938–941`** still reads "the v2 ratification /
marker wire material does NOT carry governance proof fields (documented schema gap)." That comment
predates the Run-167/169 sibling wiring traced above and is contradicted by it. It is the likely
source of A24's error. Recorded as a **stale/misleading source comment** (a documentation defect in
the shipped tree), explicitly distinct from any runtime weakness.

### C2 — Correct the `Available → Supplied` mapping; the fixture verifier IS reachable with a proof `[SUPERSEDED-A24 → A24.1-C2]`

**`crates/qbind-node/src/pqc_governance_proof_wire.rs:349–357`** —
`GovernanceProofLoadStatus::governance_proof_context(verifier)` maps `Available(proof)` →
`GovernanceProofContext::Supplied { proof, verifier }`, and `Absent | Malformed(_)` →
`GovernanceProofContext::Unavailable`.

**`pqc_governance_authority.rs:1013–1027`** (`evaluate_governance_marker_gate`) — a `Supplied`
context invokes `verify_governance_authority_proof(proof, candidate, trust_domain,
persisted_sequence, verifier)` **before any policy branch is consulted**. Therefore the shipped
`FixtureIssuerSignatureVerifier` wired at **`main.rs:1260`** (`fixture_issuer_signature_verifier()`)
**is reached with a real proof** on the production startup route whenever the sidecar supplies a
well-formed sibling — under **both** `NotRequired` and `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`. A24's
"fixture verifier never reached with a proof" is withdrawn.

### C3 — Correct the policy / malformed-proof matrix `[SUPERSEDED-A24 → A24.1-C3]`

A24 framed the gate as "no-op under `NotRequired`, else unconditional fail-closed." The precise
matrix (`pqc_governance_authority.rs:914–928, 997–1036`; `pqc_governance_proof_surface.rs:80–81`):

| Load status | `NotRequired` | `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`, action ∈ {Rotate, Retire, Revoke, EmergencyRevoke} | `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`, action = ActivateInitial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Available(proof)` | verified → `Accepted` / `Rejected` | verified → `Accepted` / `Rejected` | verified → `Accepted` / `Rejected` |
| `Absent` | `NotRequiredNoProof` (no-op) | `RequiredButMissing` → **Err** | `NotRequiredNoProof` (no-op) |
| `Malformed` | `NotRequiredNoProof` (treated as absent) | `RequiredButMissing` → **Err** | `NotRequiredNoProof` (treated as absent) |

Corrections encoded:

- **`Malformed` does not universally reject.** It folds to `Unavailable`
  (`pqc_governance_proof_wire.rs:344–356`) and is treated as absent; it fails closed **only** when
  the policy `requires_proof_for` the candidate's action. The deliberate `Malformed → Unavailable`
  fold is documented at `pqc_governance_authority.rs:344–348`.
- **A supplied proof is verified even under `NotRequired`** (the gate verifies any `Supplied`
  context before the policy branch, `:1013–1027`). `NotRequired` is not a blanket "ignore the
  proof."
- **`requires_proof_for` (`:917–928`)**: `NotRequired` → false for every action;
  `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive` → true only for Rotate/Retire/Revoke/EmergencyRevoke, **false for
  `ActivateInitial`**. So even under the Required policy, a genesis-bound `ActivateInitial`
  candidate needs no proof.
- **The MainNet refusal is separate and unchanged.** It lives at the calling surface
  (`pqc_peer_candidate_apply` upstream binary gate; surface doc `pqc_governance_proof_surface.rs:92–97,
  159–165`); the governance-proof policy neither enables MainNet peer-driven apply nor bypasses any
  environment/ratification gate. The outer ratification-enforcement policy
  (`main.rs:544–549`: Strict on MainNet; AllowLegacyUnratified only on TestNet/DevNet behind the
  `--p2p-trust-bundle-allow-unratified-testnet-devnet` flag) remains a **distinct** gate from this
  governance gate and is not re-litigated here.

### C4 — Correct downstream enforcement attribution (the proof gate vs Run-182 vs Run-220) `[SUPERSEDED-A24 → A24.1-C4]`

A24 attributed independent startup-blocking to the Run-182 on-chain-governance call-site. Corrected
by three distinct carriers on the startup `--p2p-trust-bundle` path:

1. **The actual Run-163 proof enforcer** is
   `preflight_v2_marker_decision_with_governance_proof_load` at **`main.rs:1264–1278`**, whose
   `Result` is propagated by `?` (line 1278). Its Layer-3
   (`pqc_authority_marker_acceptance.rs::decide_v2_marker_acceptance_with_lifecycle_and_governance:1864–1880`)
   maps `RequiredButMissing{action}` → `Err(GovernanceAuthorityRequiredButMissing)` and
   `Rejected(outcome)` → `Err(GovernanceAuthorityRejected)` (startup aborts), while
   `NotRequiredNoProof | Accepted(_)` → `Ok(decision)` (startup proceeds). **This** is the path that
   enforces the proof at startup.
2. **Run-182** (`invoke_run_182_startup_p2p_trust_bundle_callsite_onchain_governance_marker_decision`,
   called at `main.rs:1288–1291`, defined `1310–1348`) is a `fn … ()` with **no return type**; the
   decision it computes is stored in **`_outcome` (line 1346) and discarded**, and its context is
   built with **`proof: None`** and empty/zero `expected_governance_*` fields (`1333–1345`). It is a
   source-reachability hook, **not** an enforcing gate. A24's claim that Run-182's returned decision
   "independently blocks startup" is withdrawn — no rejecting operation is wired from it.
3. **Run-220** (`consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome`, `main.rs:1297–1303`) **is**
   enforced (`.map_err(run_220_governance_execution_consumption_marker_error)?`), but it carries the
   **separate** `governance_execution` sidecar status (`main.rs:524–543`,
   `GovernanceExecutionLoadStatus`, surface `GovernanceExecutionRuntimeSurface::StartupP2pTrustBundle`)
   — a different wire carrier from the Run-163 `governance_authority_proof`. **Do not conflate it
   with the Run-163 proof gate.** Its own semantics are out of this pass's bounded scope beyond
   recording that it is distinct and separately propagated.

### C5 — Bounded static startup trace (one lifecycle-sensitive action under `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`)

Operator starts the node with `--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-proof-required` **or**
`QBIND_P2P_TRUST_BUNDLE_GOVERNANCE_PROOF_REQUIRED=1`
(`pqc_governance_proof_surface.rs:120–196`, OR-combined) **and** a v2 ratification sidecar
(`--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification <path>`) whose candidate resolves to a `Rotate` action:

1. `main.rs:510` → `load_versioned_ratification_with_governance_proof_from_path` → V2 arm
   (`516–519`) sets `governance_proof_load` to the sibling's status.
2. `main.rs:1261–1263` → `policy = RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`.
3. `main.rs:1264–1278` → `preflight_v2_marker_decision_with_governance_proof_load(inputs{update_source:
   StartupLoad}, policy, &governance_proof_load, &fixture_verifier)?`.
4. `pqc_governance_proof_surface.rs:104` → `governance_proof_context` (Available→Supplied;
   Absent/Malformed→Unavailable).
5. `decide_v2_marker_acceptance_with_lifecycle_and_governance:1850` (Layers 1+2 anti-rollback +
   lifecycle) then `:1864` Layer-3 `evaluate_governance_marker_gate`.
6. `requires_proof_for(Rotate) = true` (`:920–926`):
   - proof `Absent`/`Malformed` → `RequiredButMissing` → **`Err` → `?` at `main.rs:1278` → startup
     aborts** (fail-closed; no marker persist, no sequence write, no trust swap — persist is a
     separate post-commit step, `pqc_authority_marker_acceptance.rs:1898–1909`).
   - proof `Available` → `verify_governance_authority_proof` → `Accepted` (**Ok → startup
     proceeds**) or `Rejected` (**Err → aborts**).

The gate therefore **enforces at node startup** on this route. (A genesis-bound `ActivateInitial`
candidate would short-circuit at step 6 to `NotRequiredNoProof` even under this policy.)

### C6 — Reassess the security boundary (reachable, but cryptographically hollow)

The corrected boundary is **not** "unreachable gate / schema gap" (A24). It is: *the gate is
reachable and control-flow-enforcing, but what the shipped (default) verifier enforces is not issuer
authorization.*

- **`FixtureIssuerSignatureVerifier::verify_issuer_signature`
  (`pqc_governance_authority.rs:296–313`, builder `:280–293`)** recomputes
  `expected = b"qbind-run163-gov:" ‖ class.tag() ‖ ":" ‖ authority_root_fingerprint ‖ ":" ‖
  candidate_v2_digest ‖ ":" ‖ authority_domain_sequence.to_be_bytes()` — **every input is a public
  or candidate-derived field carried in the proof/trust-domain** — and checks
  `proof.issuer_signature == expected` by **byte equality**. This is a deterministic checksum over
  public data, **not** a secret-key / asymmetric signature verification. Any party able to author the
  v2 sidecar can compute the matching `issuer_signature` and pass the signature gate
  (`:752–753`). `fixture_issuer_signature_verifier()` is the verifier wired at `main.rs:1260` — i.e.
  the **shipped default**, not merely a test harness.
- **The optional threshold (`:734–749`)** compares the proof's **self-declared** `approvals >=
  required` (`is_met()`); it binds no verified signer set, and when the proof omits `threshold`
  (`None`) there is **no threshold check at all**.

**Net effect.** Enabling `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive` raises the startup bar from "nothing" to
"a correctly-formatted, self-certifying sidecar," and verifies a supplied proof even under
`NotRequired` — but it does **not** establish that the ratification was authorized by a governance
authority, because the signature check is key-free and the threshold is self-declared. This is the
accurate characterization of the Run-163 governance-proof sub-boundary, superseding A24's
reachability-centred conclusion.

**Disposition (no forcing).**
- **No new finding ID is minted, and no existing ID is renamed, re-severitied, or closed.** This
  pass corrects A24's reachability conclusion and sharpens the boundary characterization under the
  **OBL-GOV-2** governance obligation / the Run-163 governance-proof sub-boundary. It updates **only**
  that sub-boundary.
- The weakness is **source-established and reachable** and is **not** dismissed on "fixture" or
  "missing runtime" grounds (the fixture verifier is the shipped default, wired at `main.rs:1260`).
- Reachability **alone** does not demonstrate an unauthorized **live** state change: the outer
  ratification-enforcement policy (`main.rs:544–549`), the environment/MainNet refusal at the calling
  surface, and the Run-055/070 trust-apply + marker-persist pipeline remain **separate** and
  **UNEXECUTED** in this read-only audit. The claim recorded is precisely: *the governance gate is
  reachable and enforcing, but the shipped verifier it enforces is a public-data checksum, not an
  authorization proof.*
- **Affirmed from A24 (not superseded):** the fixture byte-equality observation and the
  optional-declared-threshold observation. **Superseded from A24:** the "always Absent / total
  schema gap / unreachable-`Supplied`" reachability conclusion (C1–C2), the universal
  malformed-reject framing (C3), and the Run-182-independently-blocks-startup attribution (C4).

## A24.1 Reporting corrections (affirmed + extended)
The A1-F1, A7-F1 (= QBIND-A1-F005), and evidence-precedence corrections were applied in **A23 §A23.1** (in the
preserved master below) and are **affirmed unchanged**: A1-F1 = *SOURCE-ADDRESSED (production timeout/TC paths
reject absent verification context before effects; caller inventory completed in A5; behavioral validation
unexecuted)* — the historical context-absent bypass is the hazard gated, not current behavior; **A7-F1 defect** =
`verify_transaction_auth` accepts empty `tx.auths` and lacks distinct-signer/threshold/authority checks (opaque
ingestion is reachability, not the defect), **QBIND-A1-F005 ≡ A7-F1** (no double count); §25.2 ledger authoritative
for historical identities, **not** automatically for current-HEAD dispositions (A22.1 statuses provisional where
current-revision evidence is unidentified; embedded earlier-lineage A19/A23/A26/A30 references are not current-pass
evidence); unvendored ≠ unavailable (A7.1 retrieved pinned serde). **Extension `[A24.1]`:** the **governance-proof
selector IS consumed** at startup (`main.rs:1261-1263` via `governance_proof_policy_from_cli_or_env(
ctx_data.governance_proof_required_selector)`), so this mechanism is **distinct from A19-F1's ignored remote-signer
selector** — the governance selector genuinely selects a policy; its limitation is elsewhere (§A24.2-E).

## A24.2 (Q-A) Admission and policy — startup dispatcher order

Startup (`main.rs:1260-1278`) selects `fixture_issuer_signature_verifier()` + `policy =
governance_proof_policy_from_cli_or_env(selector)` and calls `preflight_v2_marker_decision_with_governance_proof_
load(inputs, policy, &ctx_data.governance_proof_load, &verifier)` (`pqc_governance_proof_surface.rs:98-106`), which
builds `context = proof_load.governance_proof_context(verifier)` then `decide_v2_marker_acceptance_with_lifecycle_
and_governance`.
| Stage | Behavior / first rejection |
|---|---|
| Outer ratification gate + data-dir prereq | per Run-105/106 (precede this decision; unchanged, A19.1/A20) — this governance decision is only reached when the ctx was built |
| Policy selector | `GovernanceProofPolicy`: **default `NotRequired`** (hidden selector `--p2p-trust-bundle-governance-proof-required` / env, OR-combined, disabled-by-default, **Non-MainNet-enabling**); `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive` requires a proof for Rotate/Retire/Revoke/EmergencyRevoke, **ActivateInitial stays optional** (`:917-928`) |
| **Proof-load status at startup** | **`GovernanceProofLoadStatus::Absent` — always, on the production startup ctx** (`main.rs:508-522`: the v2 ratification/marker wire carries **no** governance-proof fields — documented schema gap). So `context = Unavailable` on the real route |
| `Absent` under `NotRequired` | `GovernanceMarkerGate::NotRequiredNoProof` → governance layer is a **no-op** (anti-rollback + lifecycle decision stands) |
| `Absent` under `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive` + sensitive action | **fails closed** → `GovernanceAuthorityRequiredButMissing{action}` (startup refused) |
| `Malformed` | sidecar-malformed → rejected (fail closed) |
| `Supplied` (fixture/test path only; **not** the production startup ctx) | verified by the supplied verifier (§A24.3) |

**Lifecycle sensitivity:** `requires_proof_for` gates only the four sensitive actions under the Required policy;
ActivateInitial never requires a proof.

## A24.3 (Q-B) What is authenticated — verifier checks in order

`verify_governance_authority_proof` (`pqc_governance_authority.rs:503-761`), executed order:
1. `OnChainGovernance` class → `UnsupportedOnChainGovernance` (fail-closed).
2. structural well-formedness (non-empty required fields + **non-empty issuer_signature**).
3. suite: issuer-signature suite PQC (`UnsupportedIssuerSuite`/`NonPqcSuiteRejected`); authority-root suite PQC.
4-5. trust-domain binding — proof **and** candidate vs `trust_domain` (env/chain/genesis/authority-root/root-suite) — **equality**.
6. candidate-digest: `proof.candidate_v2_digest == candidate.latest_ratification_v2_digest` — equality.
7. sequence: `== candidate.latest_authority_domain_sequence`; `< persisted_sequence` → `ReplayRejected`.
8. lifecycle-action: `== classify_candidate_lifecycle_action(candidate)`.
9. class-authorizes-action: GenesisBound → any; EmergencyCouncil → EmergencyRevoke only; OnChain → unsupported.
10. key binding: `proof.active_key == candidate.active_key`; per-action new/revoked-key equality.
11. **threshold (OPTIONAL)**: `if Some(threshold)` → `is_well_formed` (`required>=1, total>=required, approvals<=total`) + `is_met` (`approvals >= required`); **`None` skips it**. `approvals` is a **caller-supplied `u32` count — NOT a tally of independently verified distinct signers**.
12. **issuer signature**: `signature_verifier.verify_issuer_signature(proof, trust_domain)`.

**The production verifier is `FixtureIssuerSignatureVerifier` (`:296-313`):** it recomputes
`expected = "qbind-run163-gov:" ‖ class.tag() ‖ ":" ‖ authority_root_fingerprint ‖ ":" ‖ candidate_v2_digest ‖
":" ‖ sequence_be` and checks `proof.issuer_signature == expected` — a **byte-equality over bytes derived
entirely from public fields** the proof's constructor already sets. **This is not a cryptographic, key-bound
signature verification; it binds no private-key possession.** Approvals are declared, not derived from verified
signers; the threshold is optional. **Every "expected" value traces to the candidate or the caller-supplied
`trust_domain`** — equality is **consistency, not independent authentication**. (The surrounding **real
bundle-signature + ratification** checks on the outer v2 path are unchanged and preserved; this governance gate is
an *additional* layer, not a replacement.)

**Answer (Q-B):** the gate authenticates **field consistency** (+ optional declared threshold) via a **fixture**
issuer-verifier — it does **not** establish issuer authorization.

## A24.4 (Q-C) One acceptance/rejection trace (static, UNEXECUTED)
**Target:** a lifecycle-sensitive action (e.g. Rotate) under `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive`, with a valid
predecessor marker + valid v2 ratification prerequisites. **Result: the trace is blocked at the proof-load guard.**
On the production startup ctx, `governance_proof_load` is **`Absent`** (schema gap, §A24.2), so for a sensitive
action `requires_proof_for(Rotate)=true` + context `Unavailable` → `evaluate_governance_marker_gate` returns
`RequiredButMissing{Rotate}` → `MutatingSurfaceMarkerV2Error::GovernanceAuthorityRequiredButMissing` → **startup
fails closed before any acceptance**. **Capability note:** this holds without assuming authority keys, filesystem
permissions, or an authentic ratification — the wire simply carries no proof field to supply. **Public-data-derived
fixture material does NOT satisfy the gate on the production startup route**, because the route never supplies a
proof at all (the fixture consistency-check is only reachable on the `Supplied` fixture/test path, where it
establishes consistency, not authorization). Under the default `NotRequired`, the same transition's governance
layer is a **no-op** (`NotRequiredNoProof`). **Subsequent gates:** even a hypothetical governance-accept would
still pass through **Run-182** (`invoke_run_182_startup_p2p_trust_bundle_callsite_onchain_governance_marker_
decision`) and **Run-220** (governance-execution runtime-arming consumption) before the decision is returned
(`main.rs:~1285-1296`), each able to reject before any mutation — so no downstream acceptance is claimed here.

## A24.5 (Q-D) Consumer and effect
The governance-aware wrapper `decide_v2_marker_acceptance_with_lifecycle_and_governance`
(`pqc_authority_marker_acceptance.rs:1841-1881`) composes **Layer 1+2** (`decide_marker_acceptance_v2_inner` =
anti-rollback compare + Run-159/161 lifecycle validation — this **reads the persisted marker** at
`inputs.marker_path`, `:426`) then **Layer 3** (`evaluate_governance_marker_gate`). It is **non-mutating but not
"no I/O": it reads the persisted marker**; the **only disk write** is the separate
`persist_accepted_v2_marker_after_commit_boundary` (`:1898-1909`, no-op unless `should_persist`), called **after**
the commit boundary. The startup consumer (`main.rs`): preflight `decision` → **Run-182** → **Run-220** →
`Ok(Some(decision))`; the accepted decision then gates (downstream, separately) **marker/sequence persistence**,
**preparation of the `trusted_roots` vector** (`main.rs:7172-7185`, A20), and **P2P startup**. **Boundary
established:** the governance-proof gate is one **preflight-acceptance** layer in the marker-decision chain
(anti-rollback + lifecycle + governance, under the outer ratification gate + Run-182/Run-220); it is **not itself
a mutation authorizer**. Startup conclusions are **not** transferred to SIGHUP / reload-apply / peer-driven drain
(those share `decide_v2_marker_acceptance_with_lifecycle_and_governance` but with differing inputs/sources — e.g.
`update_source`, differing ratification configs — and are **queued under OBL-GOV-2**, not asserted here).

## A24.6 (Q-E) Disposition — no new finding forced
**Answer to the bounded question:** on the selected binary's v2 trust-bundle startup route, requiring a governance
proof establishes **only consistency of supplied fields, not issuer authorization** — and, more strongly, a proof
is **never supplied at startup** (v2 wire schema gap → `Absent`), so under the **default `NotRequired`** the gate
is a **no-op** and under the hidden `RequiredForLifecycleSensitive` selector a lifecycle-sensitive transition
**fails closed**. The production `FixtureIssuerSignatureVerifier` performs **byte-equality over public-data-derived
bytes** (consistency, not key-bound authorization); the threshold is optional with a **declared** approvals count.
**Classification:** an **intended fixture/library boundary** plus a **documented schema gap** (no governance-proof
fields on the v2 wire) and a **documented deferral** ("production-surface proof-carrying evidence deferred to
Run 172"). **No reachable deployed authorization bypass is demonstrated** on the startup route: the gate is either
a no-op (NotRequired) or fail-closed (Required+Absent); the fixture consistency-check is never reached with a
proof in the selected binary. **Duplicate check:** distinct from **A23-F1** (bundle-signer/ratification-target
mismatch), **A8-F1** (on-chain program authorization gap), and **A19-F1** (ignored remote-signer *selector* — the
governance selector, by contrast, **is consumed**). **No new ID minted** (no violated security contract and no
reachable weakness demonstrated; the behavior matches the intended source/test contract). Recorded as an answered
**OBL-GOV-2** sub-boundary, cross-referenced to OBL-SIGN-1b; **A23-F1 unchanged**. **Tests (inspected, not
executed):** `run_163`/`run_165`/`run_167`/`run_171`/`run_173`/`run_182`/`run_220` governance-proof/marker tests
exercise the policy selector, proof-load status (Absent/Available/Malformed), the fixture verifier's
byte-equality, threshold well-formedness/met, and the RequiredButMissing fail-closed — **none establishes a real
key-bound issuer signature or a `qbind-node` Supplied-proof startup path.** **C5 remains open.**

**Genuinely separate (queued under existing obligations, not opened here):** a **real** issuer-signature verifier
(Run-172 deferral) → OBL-GOV-2 / OBL-SIGN-1b; the differing SIGHUP/reload-apply/drain governance inputs → OBL-GOV-2;
provisioning/rotation/attestation/journal → OBL-SIGN-1b custody-lifecycle / OBL-KEY-1b / OBL-STO-2b.

## A24.7 A23 carry-forward qualifications (verified, incorporated)
1. **Custody freshness is optional** (`validate_authority_custody_attestation` gate 14): both timestamps **absent
   → proceeds**; an incomplete pair (one set, one unset) or `expires <= freshness` or out-of-window → **rejects**.
2. **Marker decisions are non-mutating but read the persisted marker** — "pure/no I/O" is too broad:
   `decide_marker_acceptance_v2_inner` reads `inputs.marker_path` (`:426`); the only write is
   `persist_accepted_v2_marker_after_commit_boundary` (`:1898-1909`).
3. **Governance evaluation lives in the governance-aware wrapper** `decide_v2_marker_acceptance_with_lifecycle_and_
   governance` (via `evaluate_governance_marker_gate`), **not** in bare `decide_marker_acceptance_v2`.
4. **The marker path folds two lifecycle-rejection variants for compatibility** (`pqc_authority_marker_
   acceptance.rs:1799-1805`): `InitialActivationAfterPersistedRejected` and
   `V1PersistedV2CandidateNotSupportedHere` are **not** treated as startup-refusing lifecycle rejects (back-compat:
   re-issued `Ratify` on accepted advancement + the Run-131 v1→v2 migration path). **Not every lifecycle rejection
   refuses startup** — only those two are folded, surrounded by the anti-rollback compare that enforces the safety
   properties. All other lifecycle rejects do refuse.

The 54 obligation identities/definitions are unchanged; only the OBL-GOV-2 startup-governance sub-boundary
disposition and the §A24.1 corrections are updated. No global index rebuild; no historical evidence treated as

## A23.2 Ordered gate table

**Lifecycle validator `validate_v2_lifecycle_transition` (`pqc_authority_lifecycle.rs:291-469`):**
| # | Case | First rejecting op / outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | structure | `candidate.validate_structure()` → `StructurallyMalformedRejected` |
| 2 | trust-domain env/chain/genesis/authority-root/root-suite | **equality vs `trust_domain`** → `Wrong{Environment,Chain,Genesis,AuthorityRoot}Rejected` |
| 3 | PQC suite (root + active signing key) | `is_pqc_lifecycle_suite` → `NonPqcSuiteRejected` |
| 4 | prior-record version | V1 persisted + V2 candidate → `V1PersistedV2CandidateNotSupportedHere`; malformed V2 → `StructurallyMalformedRejected` |
| 5 | idempotency | `candidate == prev` (bit-for-bit) → `Idempotent` |
| 6 | no prior | `ActivateInitial` → `InitialActivationAccepted`; else → `UnsupportedLifecycleActionRejected` |
| 7 | prior, sequence | `cand.seq < prev.seq` → `LowerSequenceRejected`; `== ` (non-idempotent) → `SameSequenceConflictingDigestRejected` (equivocation) |
| 8 | prior, higher-seq action | `Rotate`: `previous_key` must equal `prev.active` (`WrongPreviousKeyRejected`) + `check_active_key_not_revoked_or_retired` → `RotationAccepted`; `Retire`: must preserve `prev.active` → `RetirementAccepted`; `ActivateInitial` → rejected |

**Custody validator `validate_authority_custody_attestation` (`pqc_authority_custody.rs:465-707`):**
| # | Check | Kind / first reject |
|---|---|---|
| 1-4 | env/chain/genesis/authority-root | **equality vs `trust_domain`** (attestation + candidate) → `Wrong*` |
| 5 | `bundle_signing_key_fingerprint == candidate.active_bundle_signing_key_fingerprint` | binds attestation↔candidate → `WrongSigningKeyFingerprint` |
| 6-8 | `candidate_digest` / `authority_domain_sequence` / `lifecycle_action` == **expected_** | **equality vs caller-supplied expected** → `Wrong*` |
| 9 | `governance_authority_class == expected_governance_authority_class` | **enum equality to caller-supplied expected** (→ `CustodyAttestationMalformed`) — **not** governance authorization |
| 10-12 | `custody_attestation_digest` non-empty; `custody_key_id` non-empty; `== expected_custody_key_id` (when Some) | **presence + equality; the custody digest is NOT cryptographically verified** |
| 13 | `custody_suite_id == PQC_LIFECYCLE_SUITE_ML_DSA_44` | equality to constant → `UnsupportedCustodySuite` |
| 14 | freshness/expiry window (both set; `fresh<expires`; `fresh<=now<expires`) | `now_unix` **caller-supplied** → `CustodyAttestationExpired`/`…Malformed` |
| 15 | custody class | `Unknown`→rejected; `RemoteSigner`→`RemoteSignerUnavailable`; `Kms`→`KmsUnavailable`; `Hsm`→`HsmUnavailable`; `FixtureLocalKey`/`LocalOperatorKey`→continue |
| 16 | MainNet | fixture/local → `Fixture/LocalCustodyRejectedForMainNet` (before policy) |
| 17 | production policy | → `Production/MainNetProductionCustodyUnavailable` (no real backend) |
| 18 | policy×class×env | `FixtureOnly`/`DevnetLocalAllowed`/`TestnetLocalAllowed` + fixture/local + DevNet/TestNet → `AcceptedFixture/LocalOperatorCustody`; else `PolicyRefusesCustodyClass` |

**Acceptance is reachable only for `FixtureLocalKey`/`LocalOperatorKey` under a matching DevNet/TestNet policy,
non-MainNet, with all equality/presence/suite/freshness gates satisfied. KMS/HSM/RemoteSigner custody classes all
fail closed ("Unavailable"). There is no cryptographic custody or signature/attestation verification anywhere.**

## A23.3 Input-provenance and cross-layer binding

| Input | Supplied by | Trust requirement | Checked how |
|---|---|---|---|
| `persisted` prior record (`Option<PersistentAuthorityStateRecordVersioned>`) | **caller** (an argument) | **must already be trusted** — the `Persistent…` type name does **not** establish it was loaded from trusted durable storage within these functions | used for anti-rollback/idempotency compare only |
| `candidate` state | caller | the subject under validation | structure + trust-domain + sequence/action gates |
| `trust_domain` (env/chain/genesis/authority-root/suite) | **caller** | **must already be trusted** | equality target for lifecycle + custody |
| `expected_candidate_digest/action/sequence/governance_class/custody_key_id` | **caller** | **must already be trusted** | equality targets (custody gates 6-9,12) |
| `policy`, `now_unix`, custody evidence (attestation) | caller | policy/time caller-set; attestation is the validated (untrusted) input | equality/presence/freshness |

**Cross-layer binding (`validate_lifecycle_governance_custody_and_backend`):** the **custody** arguments
(attestation, candidate, expected_*) and the **backend** arguments (identity, request, response,
backend_expected) are **independent**; the wrapper does **not** cross-check that the backend request/response
refer to the same candidate/digest/action/sequence/key as the custody attestation. **That cross-layer
association is a caller responsibility**, not enforced here. Within each layer, bindings are equality against
caller-supplied `expected`/candidate fields; **equality is consistency, not independent authentication.**

## A23.5 Bounded composition traces (static, UNEXECUTED)
- **Which class/policy reach the backend verifier** (`validate_lifecycle_governance_custody_and_backend`): only
  after lifecycle **and** custody accept — i.e. fixture/local custody class + `FixtureOnly`/`DevnetLocalAllowed`/
  `TestnetLocalAllowed` + non-MainNet + all bindings; the Run-203 backend verifier then runs (itself accepting
  only a fixture KMS/HSM response under a fixture backend policy, per A21).
- **Can a direct fixture-backend acceptance satisfy the full composition?** Only if the caller **also** supplies a
  mutually-consistent lifecycle+custody set (valid candidate transition + fixture/local custody attestation +
  matching `expected_*` + DevNet/TestNet policy). All values are **caller-supplied fixtures**; no cryptographic
  authentication is involved.
- **First rejections:** `is_peer_driven_apply_preflight && MainNet` → `MainNetPeerDrivenApplyRefused`; lifecycle
  reject → `LifecycleOrCustodyRejected`; custody reject (KMS/HSM/RemoteSigner class, production policy, MainNet,
  or any binding mismatch) → `LifecycleOrCustodyRejected`; backend reject → `BackendRejected`.
- **Jointly-satisfiable acceptance** exists only as an **all-fixture, all-caller-supplied** construction on
  DevNet/TestNet; it demonstrates **field consistency among caller-supplied values**, not custody possession or
  governance authorization.

## A23.6 What `validate_lifecycle_governance_and_custody` establishes
**Establishes (given caller-trusted inputs):** the candidate is a structurally-valid, trust-domain-bound,
PQC-suite, sequence-monotonic lifecycle transition (Initial/Rotate/Retire with key-continuity), **and** the
custody attestation's fields are consistent with the candidate + the caller-supplied `expected_*` values + a
non-empty custody digest + the ML-DSA-44 custody suite + an in-window freshness, for a **fixture/local** custody
class under a matching DevNet/TestNet policy.
**Must already be trusted (not established here):** `persisted`, `trust_domain`, and every `expected_*` value —
all caller-supplied; `persisted`'s `Persistent…` type is **not** proof of a durable-storage load.
**Does NOT establish:** cryptographic custody (custody digest only non-empty), **governance authorization** (gate
9 is enum equality to a caller-supplied class — the real governance-proof verifier is the separate Run-163
`verify_governance_authority_proof`, **not** invoked here), real KMS/HSM possession (those classes are
"Unavailable"), or the authenticity of the prior/candidate/trust-domain/expected inputs.

## A22.1 Bounded completion of A21's client trace (six questions)

**(a) Transport injection vs acceptance.** `MockKmsHsmCustodyTransport` (`:953-1008`) is a **test double**
implementing `KmsHsmCustodyProviderTransport`; `scripted`/`respond`/`always_fail` store caller-supplied
`Result<ProductionCustodyResponse, ProductionCustodyError>` and `submit` (`:997-1008`) returns them in order.
`[SUPERSEDED-A21 →A22.1(a)]` the blanket "accepts an injected response" wording: separate four stages —
**transport receipt** (the mock returns the supplied object) → **successful submission result**
(`submit_custody_signing_request` wraps it in `SubmittedCustodyRequest` **only if** the size check passes,
`:1592-1604`) → **verification acceptance** (`verify_custody_response` must pass all gates) → **downstream
authorization** (none — no node consumer, §A22.1(f)). The mock proves none of the later stages and **does not
make a real provider exist**.

**(b) Actual size enforcement.** `response_size_estimate` (`:645-649`) sums **exactly three** fields:
`signature_commitment.len() + attestation_digest.len() + transcript_digest.len()`. **Omitted:** request-id echo,
bound_request_digest, backend_id, provider_id, key_id, nonces, freshness/expiry, and the envelope framing.
**Timing:** checked at `:1594-1597` **after** `transport.submit` has already returned a fully-constructed
in-memory `ProductionCustodyResponse` (post-receipt). **Comparison:** `> PRODUCTION_KMS_HSM_CUSTODY_MAX_RESPONSE_
BYTES` (64 KiB). **Outcome:** `Err(ProductionCustodyMalformedResponse)`. This is a **typed partial-field estimate
on an already-allocated object**, **not** a total-response-size or pre-allocation/pre-decode bound (there is no
real I/O to bound).

**(c) Expected-value provenance.** `backend_expectations` (`:450-478`) composes `BackendExpectations` from: the
**spec/config** (`self.*`: custody_class, lifecycle_action, candidate_digest, authority_domain_sequence, key_id,
primary signing-key fingerprint, custody_attestation_digest, request/response nonces); the **request**
(`expected_request_digest = request.request_digest()`); the **response**
(`expected_response_digest = response.response_digest()`); and both (`expected_transcript_digest`). In verify
(`:1655-1669`) these feed the Run-203 verifier. **What independently binds the request:** the spec/config-supplied
expected values (candidate digest, key id, nonces, fingerprint, sequence, lifecycle) checked by equality against
request/identity fields. **What merely recomputes consistency:** `expected_response_digest` is derived **from the
response itself** (so that equality is tautological), and `expected_transcript_digest` is recomputed from
identity+request+response — these establish **self-consistency, not independent authentication**.

**(d) Direct vs composed verification.** The normal path `evaluate_custody_backend` (`:1723-1736`) = `submit` then
`verify`. `submit_custody_signing_request` guarantees: a size-checked response, and `SubmittedCustodyRequest.
request_id == request.request_id` (`:1587,1599-1604`). When `verify_custody_response` is called **directly** with
a hand-built `SubmittedCustodyRequest` (its fields are public), those submit-time guarantees are **not**
pre-established, but verify **re-derives** request/response/transcript digests and **re-checks**: 3-way request-id
correlation (`:1641-1645`), provider/key match (`:1646-1653`), the Run-203 fixture binding (`:1662-1672`), and
transcript equality (`:1681-1683`). So a direct caller must still satisfy every equality/binding; the only values
it cannot self-satisfy are the **spec-supplied** expectations (candidate digest, key id, nonces, fingerprint,
sequence) — unless that caller also controls the spec (a fixture/test construction, no authentication proven).

**(e) The `ProductionCustodyAccepted` fallback arm (`:1712-1719`).** `[SUPERSEDED-A21 →A22.1(e)]` for treating the
"Unreachable" comment as proof. `ProductionCustodyProviderKind` has **8** variants (`:97-115`); `is_production()`
(`:138-146`) is **only** the 4 `Production*`. Step 1 (`:1632-1638`) rejects `is_production()`; step 5 explicitly
handles `FixtureKms`/`FixtureHsm`; the `_ =>` arm therefore catches **`Disabled`/`Unknown`**. Via the **normal
build→submit→verify path**: unreachable — `to_backend_kind()` maps `Disabled→BackendKind::Disabled`,
`Unknown→BackendKind::Unknown` (`:165-172`), which the Run-203 verifier rejects (`UnknownBackendRejected`), so no
`Disabled`/`Unknown` provider yields an accepted Run-203 outcome. Via a **direct `verify_custody_response` call
with an internally-inconsistent, caller-constructed envelope** (Run-295 `provider_kind ∈ {Disabled,Unknown}` while
the Run-203 `backend_response.backend_kind ∈ {FixtureKms,FixtureHsm}` and all spec bindings satisfied): the arm
**can fire**, returning a `ProductionCustodyAccepted` **enum value to the constructing caller**. **Assessment
against the API contract and actual callers:** reaching it requires a caller that violates the envelope's own
`provider_kind ↔ backend_kind` consistency, and the result is an **in-memory outcome with no production
consumer** (§A22.1(f)). **No security consequence is established**; this is a **latent library/API imprecision**
(the "Unreachable" comment is strictly inaccurate), **not a vulnerability** and **not a finding**.

**(f) Integration boundary (auditable caller inventory).** `[SUPERSEDED-A21 →A22.1(f)]` narrowing "four
startup-file greps." A **crate-wide** grep (`crates/qbind-node/**`) for `evaluate_custody_backend` /
`verify_custody_response` / `submit_custody_signing_request` / `recover_custody_request_window` /
`ProductionKmsHsmCustodyBackend` / `KmsHsmCustodyProviderTransport` returns references in exactly: **the defining
`src/` module itself**; `examples/run_296`, `examples/run_298`; `tests/run_295`, `tests/run_297`. **No other
`src/` file** references them, and there is **no `Box<dyn …Custody>` / `Arc<dyn …Custody>` dynamic dispatch** in
node `src/` (grep empty). The composing trait is `GovernanceProductionKmsHsmCustodyBackend` (`:1264`), implemented
only by this module's own struct, constructed only in those examples/tests. **Conclusion (bounded):** no
`qbind-node` production path constructs or invokes the custody backend; consumers are two examples + two tests.
**Remaining edge:** this is a name/type/trait grep across the crate + a dyn-dispatch check, not a full symbolic
call-graph; a transitive path through an uninspected wrapper is not exhaustively disproven, so the negative is
scoped to "no direct or dyn-dispatched caller in `crates/qbind-node/src` outside the defining module."

**Recovery (`recover_custody_request_window`, `:1738-1772`).** Requires a **caller-supplied** `prior: Option<&
SubmittedCustodyRequest>` (None → `NoPriorRequest`). Compares in memory: different `request_id` → NoPriorRequest;
same id + different key_id → `ConflictingKeyHandleForSameId`; same id + different request envelope digest →
`ConflictingRequestForSameId`; same request + different response digest → `ConflictingResponseForSameRequest`;
byte-identical → `IdempotentReplayOfSameRequest`; else → `AmbiguousRecoveryFailClosed`. It is an **in-memory
comparison against caller-supplied prior state** — **not** a durably stored/enforced record, and **not** restart/
rollback/clone resistant. The grep-verifiable helpers (`:1779-1799`: default-is-disabled, mainnet-refuses-fixture,
never-falls-back = `true`) are **self-asserted constants documenting intent**, not proofs.
