| Storage | `global: Option<ConnTokenBucket>` + `per_address: HashMap<RemoteAddr, ConnTokenBucket>` | sharded `[RwLock<HashMap<PeerId, TokenBucket>>; 16]` |
| Builder field | `abuse_dos_runtime_config: Option<…>` **default `None`** (`p2p_node_builder.rs:938`) | installed **unconditionally** (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1750-1751`) |
| Install gate | `if Some(cfg) && cfg.connection_limiter_enabled()` → `set_abuse_dos_runtime_state` (`:1712-1722`); CLI-gated at `main.rs:8072-8087` | `build_deployed_inbound_per_peer_limiter()` (`from_optional_config`, default `1000` msg/s + `100` burst) → `set_inbound_per_peer_limiter` |
| **Default production posture** | **DISABLED** (no CLI flag → `None` → accept path admits unconditionally; even if installed with `disabled_default`, `check` returns `ConnectionLimiterDisabled` and touches no state) | **ENABLED** (active on every P2P node; buckets accumulate) |
| Admission call | accept loop `state.should_admit(peer_addr, now)` (`p2p_tcp.rs:999-1015`), **before** KEMTLS | read loop `limiter.allow_node(&source_peer, now)` (`p2p_tcp.rs:1504-1509`), **after** a frame decodes |
| Deployed vs library | deployed (`TcpKemTlsP2pService`) | deployed (`TcpKemTlsP2pService`); the `AsyncPeerManagerImpl`/`net_service` per-peer path is **never spawned by `main.rs`** (library/test-only, per the adapter module doc) |

MainNet is refused for the connection limiter (`check` → `MainNetRefused`; `from_config` → `Err(MainNetRefused)`),
and an enabled-but-nonsensical config fails **closed** at construction (`validate`).

## A16.2 Exact keys and insertion boundaries

**Connection limiter — key includes the source port.** `check_inbound` builds
`key = RemoteAddr::new(remote.to_string())` (`runtime.rs:199`); `SocketAddr`'s `Display` is **`ip:port`**, so the
per-address key is **(ip, port)**, not (ip). `ConnectionRateLimiter::check` (`config.rs:572-619`): MainNet/
disabled/invalid guards first; then the **global** bucket (`get_or_insert_with` + `try_consume`) — **a
globally-rejected connection returns `ConnectionRateLimited` before any per-address insertion** (`:599-601`);
only on global success, **and only when `per_address_rate_window` is `Some`**, does it
`state.per_address.entry(remote.clone()).or_insert_with(…)` (`:604-612`). The default/compatibility config leaves
`per_address_rate_window = None` + `max_connections_per_address_window = 0` (`config.rs:262-263`), so **no
per-address entries exist unless the operator selects an enabled profile with a per-address window** (e.g.
`public_devnet_recommended`: `Some(1s)` / `5` per addr, `:292-293`). A per-address-rejected connection reuses the
same existing key (self-limited), so it adds no new key beyond the first.

**Message limiter — first-eight-byte NodeId key.** `bucket_key(node_id) = PeerId(u64::from_be_bytes(node_id
.as_bytes()[..8]))` (`deployed_inbound_per_peer_limiter.rs:163-168`) — the **first 8 bytes of the 32-byte
NodeId, big-endian**. Two distinct NodeIds sharing their first 8 bytes **share a bucket** (documented coarse
selector, not an identity/auth claim). `allow_node → allow_key → PeerRateLimiter::allow`, which does
`buckets.entry(*peer).or_insert_with(|| TokenBucket::new(…))` (`peer_rate_limiter.rs:321-323`) — **insert on
first sight**. The call site (`p2p_tcp.rs:1489-1509`) runs **only after `decode_frame` returns `Ok(msg)`** — a
structured `P2pMessage`; `0x05` peer-candidate frames `continue` earlier and a decode error `break`s, so **neither
inserts a message bucket**. **Connection acceptance alone does not insert a message bucket**: insertion requires a
completed KEMTLS handshake + registration **and** at least one decodable structured frame.

**Identity layers kept distinct** (not assumed): handshake acceptance (KEMTLS completes) → registered NodeId,
which is a **repeatable registry NodeId only** under Required/Optional + `mutual_auth_complete` + a map entry
(else a **temporary session NodeId** = `sha3_256(domain ‖ local_validator_id ‖ session_counter ‖ peer_addr)`);
the limiter key is derived from **whatever NodeId was registered**, authenticated or temporary. The limiter does
**not** require binding-map membership or a consensus key — it runs on the registered NodeId regardless of
authenticated consensus origin / consensus authorization (those are separate, Run-418).

## A16.3 Entry lifetime and cleanup

| Path | Connection limiter | Message limiter |
|---|---|---|
| Insert | `per_address.entry().or_insert_with` on first allowed (ip:port) with a per-address window | `buckets.entry().or_insert_with` on first decodable frame from a NodeId-first-8 key |
| Refill | `ConnTokenBucket::refill` tops up tokens in place | `TokenBucket::refill` tops up tokens in place |
| **Expiry** | **none** — refill is not expiry; the entry is never dropped on token recovery | **none** — same |
| Remove | none in this module | `PeerRateLimiter::remove_peer` exists (`:343-350`) **but has no production caller** (callers are: `peer_rate_limiter.rs` tests; `net_service.rs:306` on a *different* `self.peers` registry in the non-deployed path; `async_peer_manager.rs` tests) |
| Prune / cap / clear | **none** | **none** (no cap; `NUM_SHARDS=16` is concurrency sharding, not a cardinality bound) |
| Owner-drop | state dropped only with `PublicDevnetAbuseDosRuntimeState` (service lifetime) | shard maps dropped only with `PeerRateLimiter`/`DeployedInboundPerPeerLimiter` (service lifetime) |

**Distinctions enforced:** **refill ≠ expiry** (tokens recover; the map entry stays); **map length ≠ allocated
capacity** (`HashMap` retains backing capacity even if entries were removed — but here they are not removed, so
length grows monotonically); **session lifetime ≠ limiter-owner lifetime** (a `read_loop` break on disconnect/
same-NodeId replacement/eviction removes **nothing** from either limiter map — confirmed the read loop never calls
`remove_peer`); **dropped handle ≠ completed cleanup** (dropping a `PeerConnection`/aborting a loop does not prune
limiter state). **No production insertion has a matching production removal for either limiter map.**

## A16.4 Finite, jointly-satisfiable retention traces (symbolic)

**(a) Message-limiter retention — default-enabled, strongest subcase.**
- *Actor/config:* a peer that can reach the listener and complete KEMTLS; **no certificate needed** for a
  temporary-session inbound (Disabled/Optional modes); default limiter active.
- *Trace:* connection *i* → handshake completes → registered NodeId `N_i` (temporary session id when unmapped;
  distinct per connection because `session_counter` increments) → peer sends ≥1 frame that `decode_frame`s to a
  `P2pMessage` → `allow_node(N_i)` → `entry(bucket_key(N_i)).or_insert(TokenBucket)` → on disconnect the entry
  **remains**.
- *Accounting:* distinct keys `D_msg` ≤ min(2⁶⁴, number of such connections over node lifetime); retained bytes ≈
  `D_msg × (size_of::<PeerId>() = 8 + size_of::<TokenBucket>() ≈ 32 + per-entry HashMap overhead)`, **symbolic**
  (std `HashMap` layout/load-factor not pinned). The **1000 msg/s per-bucket** limit bounds *per-key arrivals*, not
  the *number of keys* → **a rate limit does not bound retained cardinality.** Entries persist after contributing
  connections end.
- *Collision floor:* first-8-byte collisions merge keys, so cardinality saturates at ≤ 2⁶⁴ distinct buckets — a
  finite but astronomically large ceiling; coarse keying reduces distinctness only for NodeIds colliding in 8
  bytes.

**(b) Connection-limiter per-address retention — config-gated.**
- *Config prerequisite:* operator supplies an enabled abuse/DoS config with `per_address_rate_window = Some(..)`
  (CLI-gated; **off by default**).
- *Trace:* each inbound that passes the **global** budget and reaches the per-address step inserts a bucket keyed
  by **`ip:port`**; because the port varies per connection, **a single source IP yields many distinct keys**. No
  pruning → entries accumulate.
- *Accounting:* retained keys bounded by the count of globally-admitted distinct `ip:port` over lifetime; the
  global token bucket throttles the **insertion rate**, not the **retained count**. Symbolic bytes as in (a).
- *Counterexample:* a connection rejected by the **global** bucket inserts **no** per-address entry (§A16.2).

**Cumulative vs simultaneous:** in both, retained entries can far exceed simultaneous connections, because
nothing removes an entry when its connection ends. **Separately**, neither trace establishes a physical outcome:
**no OOM, exhaustion, consensus effect, or executed attack is claimed** (E25).

## A16.5 Metrics storage is separate from limiter storage (resolves, not reopens)

`PeerNetworkMetrics.peers: RwLock<HashMap<PeerId, PeerCounters>>` is **capped at `MAX_TRACKED_PEERS = 128`**
(`metrics.rs:423,532`): `ensure_peer_entry` returns `false` and bumps `overflow_peer_count` once `len() >= 128`
(`:580-583`), and `inc_rate_limit_drop` folds beyond-cap drops into an aggregate `overflow.rate_limit_drop`
counter (`:751-765`). **This cap is on the metrics map, not the limiter.** The deployed message limiter's own
bucket map (`PeerRateLimiter` shards) has **no** such cap. So: **a cap on metrics entries is not a cap on limiter
entries** (the limiter is uncapped), and conversely **not every peer-indexed map is unlimited** (the metrics map
is bounded at 128). Direct vs indirect metric influence: the limiter **indirectly** drives
`qbind_net_per_peer_drops_total{reason="rate_limit"}` via `inc_rate_limit_drop(key)` (bounded by the 128-cap +
overflow counter) and its own self-contained `drops` AtomicU64; **no global response-size bound is asserted**
(producer cardinality limits such as 128 bound a *metric family*, not the overall `/metrics` body).

## A16.6 A15 carry-forward (A24-F1/E24 preserved; qualifications folded, HTTP audit not reopened)
- **Allocation accounting uses actual capacities.** The A15 request-processing figures are the allocated
  capacities `cap(request_line)`, `cap(header_line)`, and `cap(parts) × size_of::<&str>()` (16 B/entry on a
  64-bit target) — **not** the raw lengths R/H/T (which are content sizes, not capacities). An async handler has
  **task/future storage**, not a dedicated thread stack (correcting the A15 "task stack" phrasing).
- **EOF can complete `read_line`.** A terminating EOF completes the request-line read and allows subsequent
  tokenize/route **without a trailing newline**; handler termination also includes **runtime teardown**, not
  solely client closure or a socket error.
- **Response length derives from node state, not the request — but is not peer-independent.** The `/metrics` body
  size is produced from node counters, which peers **do** influence; distinguish **producer cardinality limits**
  (e.g. metrics' 128-peer cap, §A16.5) from a **response-size guarantee** (none asserted).
- **Slow-reader blocking depends on the complete response and transport buffering.** Do **not** treat
  `M ≤ send-buffer + receive-window` as a guaranteed completion rule; whether a non-reading client blocks the
  write depends on the full response and available buffering, which are unverified.
- These refine A24-F1/E24 wording and **do not close it**.

| **Connection-rate per-address map** | **PRESENT but config-gated.** `ip:port` keys (port included), no pruning when enabled; **off by default** (no CLI enable → no state). |

## A15.1 Activation and exposure prerequisites

**Configuration → enablement.** Production builds the config with `MetricsHttpConfig::from_env()`
(`main.rs:4991`), which reads `QBIND_METRICS_HTTP_ADDR` (`metrics_http.rs:136-162`):
| Env state | Result | Server |
|---|---|---|
| **unset** | `Self::disabled()` (`enabled=false`, placeholder `127.0.0.1:0`) | **disabled (default)** |
| set, **invalid** `SocketAddr` | WARNING logged → `Self::disabled()` | **disabled** |
| set, **valid** `ip:port` | `{bind_addr=addr, enabled=true}` | **enabled**, binds `addr` |

The **sentinel for "disabled" is the `enabled` bool**, not the address (`disabled()` still stores a placeholder
`127.0.0.1:0`); enablement is never inferred from the address. `spawn_metrics_http_server_with_crypto`
(`:258-276`) returns a **no-op `tokio::spawn(async {})`** when `!enabled` (`:264-267`); only when enabled does it
`run_metrics_http_server` → `TcpListener::bind` → accept loop.

**Bind interface = operator-chosen, not code-restricted.** `parse::<SocketAddr>()` accepts **any** interface —
`127.0.0.1:9100` (loopback) **or** `0.0.0.0:9100` (all interfaces). The code does **not** force loopback; whether
the listener is reachable off-host is the operator's `QBIND_METRICS_HTTP_ADDR` choice. **Configured address ≠
observed reachability** (binding proves a socket, not external exposure; that depends on the chosen interface +
host firewall, unobserved here).

**Authentication / admission: none present.** `handle_connection` (`:388-465`) performs **no** authentication,
token check, source-address allow-list, or TLS. This is a **separate plain-HTTP `TcpListener`** — the P2P
KEMTLS handshake, cert/auth gates, per-peer/connection rate limiters, and frame-size limits live on the
`TcpKemTlsP2pService` and **do not** apply here. **`[SUPERSEDED where historical text implies P2P controls cover
/metrics →A15.1]`**: no shared protection; the endpoint's only gate is the `enabled` flag + the operator's bind
choice.

## A15.2 Request processing and resource bounds (per stage, first limiting boundary)

Ordering in `handle_connection`: (a) `read_line(request_line)` → (b) header-skip loop → (c) tokenize+route
decision → (d) render (only for `GET /metrics`) → (e) `send_response`. Headers are read/consumed **before** the
method/path is ever examined, so **no routing rejection bounds the read phase**.

| Stage | Source | Application limit? | First effective boundary | Allocation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Request line** | `read_line(&mut request_line)` `:398-401` | **none** | `\n` or EOF (or Io error) | `request_line: String` grows to the bytes-until-`\n` = **R** (unbounded by app) |
| **Headers** | loop `header_line.clear(); read_line(&mut header_line)` `:404-414` | **none** (no count, no size, no total-bytes cap) | blank line (`\r\n`/`\n`) or EOF (`bytes_read==0`) | **one** reused `header_line: String`; `clear()` keeps capacity, so memory = **H_max** (largest single header), **not** Σ headers; **count N_h unbounded** = cumulative read work, not growing memory |
| **Tokenize** | `request_line.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<&str>>()` `:417` | n/a | — | the `&str` slices borrow `request_line` (no text copy), but the **`Vec` itself allocates** ~**T** pointer/len pairs (T = token count ≤ R) |
| **Route** | `parts.len()<2`→400; `method!="GET"`→405; path→200/404 `:418-462` | this is the **first application rejection**, but it is **after** (a)+(b) | 400/405/404/200 | small |
| **Render** | `format_metrics_output` `:450,468-488` | n/a | — | output `String` = **M** = metrics cardinality — **server-side, not client-controlled**; production uses `CryptoMetricsRefs::new()` (empty) so the optional crypto/DAG renderers are **off** (base `metrics.format_metrics()` only, `:476-487`) |
| **Per-connection** | `BufReader::new(&mut stream)` `:394`; detached task `:364` | — | — | tokio `BufReader` default buffer ≈ **8 KiB**; plus socket/fd + task stack; **×C** concurrent connections |

**Confirmed absent at HEAD** (A24-F1 core, revalidated PRESENT): request-line length cap; per-header size cap;
header count cap; total-request-bytes cap; concurrent-handler cap; read-duration, write-duration, and overall
handler-lifetime deadlines. `read_line` in **tokio 1.49.0** reads until newline/EOF with **no length limit**
(documented `AsyncBufReadExt` behavior), confirming the unbounded request-line/header growth.

**Retained-capacity vs cumulative vs occupancy vs RSS (kept distinct):** `request_line` = per-connection growth
to R; `header_line` = retained capacity H_max (reused), while many headers are **cumulative processing work**
(N_h iterations), not growing memory; concurrent **occupancy** = Σ over C live connections of
(≈8 KiB + R_i + H_max_i + T_i·ptr); **measured RSS** is **not** established here (no runtime; allocator/target
layout unverified → symbolic bounds R, H_max, N_h, T, C, M used).

## A15.3 Bounded scenarios and counterexamples

Prereq for all: endpoint **enabled** (`QBIND_METRICS_HTTP_ADDR` set valid) and reachable on the chosen interface.

| Scenario | Source-supported behavior | Finite accounting | Exit condition | Unresolved (runtime) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Long request line** (no `\n`) | `read_line` appends until `\n`/EOF | `request_line` → R bytes; token `Vec` → up to ~R/1 entries on tokenize (only reached if a `\n` eventually arrives) | client `\n`, EOF, or Io error | physical memory outcome of large R; whether RSS is reclaimed after the short-lived handler returns |
| **One large header** | single `read_line` into reused buffer | `header_line` capacity → that header's size H; retained for the (short) connection only | blank line / EOF | peak H vs. buffering |
| **Many short headers** | loop iterates per header | memory stays ≈ H_max (reused buffer); **N_h unbounded** = CPU/time | blank line / EOF | sustained-work impact unmeasured |
| **Stalled / slow sender** (dribble, never completes) | each `read_line` **awaits with no timeout** | handler parked; holds 1 socket/fd + ≈8 KiB BufReader + current Strings | **only** client close / EOF / socket error | slow-loris-style accumulation across many connections; count bounded by OS fd limits, **not** by the app |
| **Concurrent connections** | every `accept` → `tokio::spawn(handle_connection)` **detached**, **no semaphore** (`:364-368`) | occupancy O(C); C bounded by OS accept/fd limits, not app | per-connection exit above | aggregate memory/fd pressure unmeasured |
| **Slow response reader** | `send_response` `write_all`+`flush`, **no write deadline** (`:510-515`) | body M is bounded (server-side) | if **M ≤ socket send-buffer + client recv window**, `write_all` **completes without the client reading**; only **M > buffering** parks the handler on a non-reading client | exact buffer sizes/target-dependent |

**Do not over-claim (counterexamples honored):** absent application limits do **not** equal infinite physical
memory, a **guaranteed OOM**, a process crash, or a consensus halt — the metrics server is a **separate task/
listener**; any process-level effect is unquantified and undemonstrated here. A write without a deadline is **not**
proof every non-reading client blocks it: for the small, server-sized metrics body it may drain into OS/socket
buffers and complete; blocking requires a body exceeding available buffering.

## A15.4 Ownership and shutdown

| Entity | Owner | On shutdown signal (`metrics_shutdown_tx` dropped) |
|---|---|---|
| **Listener task** | `metrics_handle` (`main.rs:5003`) | `run_metrics_http_server_with_listener` `select!` takes `shutdown_rx.changed()` → `break` → `Ok(())` (`:377-384`); `metrics_handle.await` at `main.rs:5463` observes **listener-task** completion (result discarded with `let _`) |
| **Connection handlers** | **detached** (`tokio::spawn` handle dropped, `:364`) | **not** joined, cancelled, or tracked; an in-flight handler (e.g. a stalled sender) **keeps running** after the listener stops |
| **Handler sockets/buffers** | each handler task | dropped when that handler returns/errors — **not** on listener shutdown |
| **Shared metrics** | `Arc<NodeMetrics>` cloned per connection (`:362`) | clones drop as handlers end |
| **Runtime / process** | `#[tokio::main]` | detached handlers terminate only at **runtime teardown / process exit** |

**Separation enforced:** a returning `metrics_handle.await` proves the **listener task** completed; it does **not**
prove all **handlers** completed (they are detached and undrained). **Listener shutdown ≠ runtime teardown ≠
process termination.** No handler-drain/join/cancel exists on this path.

## A14.1-C1 — External-observability claim corrected (A14 §A14.5)

**A14 §A14.5 wrote:** "the repository ships **no** such check" (external progress check) and "The repository ships

Prometheus alert:

  `expr: up{job="qbind-node"} == 1 and changes(qbind_consensus_committed_height[10m]) == 0`, `for: 10m`,
  `severity: page`, runbook `RUNBOOK.md#qbindconsensusnoprogress`. It sits in the **ENABLED** group
  `qbind-devnet-observability` ("every expr uses a metric verified present in a release-binary scrape"),
  documented in `ALERT_RULES.md:22,48` and `RUNBOOK.md` ("Correlate … a stalled view with no commits suggests a
  quorum/liveness fault … escalate").

**But the following distinctions are preserved, and none of them closes A15-F1:**

| Layer | Status at HEAD | Note |

It does **not** detect the consensus-**task exit** as such |

**Corrected conclusion:** A15-F1's core — **no in-process task supervision/recovery** — is independently supported

## A14.1-C2 — Run-096 unexpected-exit "production example" withdrawn (A14 §A14.3, §A14.4)

**A14 presented** the Run-096 arm refusal as a config-gated production example: §A14.3 row "Internal fatal →
return/break" cites "Run-096 arm refusal → `return BinaryConsensusLoopProgress::default()`", and §A14.4's second
example says a "`--reconfig`-style CLI intent with a non-monotonic/invalid `target_epoch` (e.g. against a restored
engine)" reaches it. **`[SUPERSEDED-A14 →A14.1-C2]`** — **no production CLI route reaches the task's arm refusal
at this HEAD.** Full route traced:

1. **CLI gate** `derive_reconfig_proposal_from_cli_flag` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:502-520`): `None→Ok(None)`;
   `target==0 → Err(TargetEpochZero)`; `is_mainnet → Err(MainnetRefused)`; else `Ok(Some(target))` with
   **`target ≥ 1`**.
2. **main** (LocalMesh `main.rs:5538-5553`; P2P `main.rs:8509-8524`): on `Err` it prints "FATAL" and
   **`std::process::exit(1)` before spawning** — so `target==0`/mainnet never reach the task; on `Ok(Some)` it
   sets `cfg.with_reconfig_proposal(target)`.
3. **Loop prelude** (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2812-2878`): engine constructed with **`current_epoch: 0`**
   (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2099`; the field is documented "always EpochId(0) and static" at `:1356-1358`);
   optional `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` sets **`current_view`** only and **does not touch
   `current_epoch`** (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2654-2677` — verified directly; the A14 reliance on the
   "restored engine advanced epoch" code comment is **not** used as evidence); no production pre-arm caller of
   `set_current_epoch` exists (its only in-loop callers are `#[cfg(test)]`), and `transition_to_epoch` runs only
   later, after a committed reconfig.
4. **Arm** `set_pending_reconfig_next_epoch(target)` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2286-2301`): refuses only on
   `target==0` or `target ≤ current_epoch`. With `target ≥ 1` and `current_epoch == 0`, **`target > 0` always
   holds → arm succeeds** → the refusal `return` at `binary_consensus_loop.rs:2891-2902` is **not reached**.

This holds for **both** LocalMesh and P2P (same prelude). **Withdrawn** as a demonstrated production trigger.

**Retained as a defensive/library-path observation**, with exact prerequisites: the engine-layer
`set_pending_reconfig_next_epoch` second gate refuses when a **direct caller** passes `target==0` or
`target ≤ current_epoch` with `current_epoch ≥ 1` — a state **no production CLI pre-arm path produces at HEAD**.
**Run-096 test bodies inspected (not executed):** `run_096_zero_target_epoch_refused_by_engine_layer`
(`tests/…:179-198`) is a **direct engine** test — it calls `engine.set_pending_reconfig_next_epoch(0)` and
asserts `PendingReconfigIntentError::TargetEpochZero`, **bypassing the CLI gate and never spawning the loop**;
`run_096_single_validator_reconfig_commits_and_persists` (`:80-121`) **spawns the loop** with a **valid** target
and asserts commit+persist (the arm succeeds, not refuses); the CLI-gate unit tests (`:207-253`) cover
`None`/`0`/mainnet/valid. So the task-internal refusal `return` is **not** exercised by any spawn-the-loop test
with a nonzero target; only the engine layer's `target==0` check is, directly.

## A14.1-C3 — Concrete storage-failure witness (replaces A14 §A14.4's assumed "committed epoch transition")

A14 §A14.4 *assumed* "a committed canonical epoch transition." A14.1 establishes one **jointly-satisfiable**
configuration and an **ordered source trace** that reaches it before the storage write, distinguishing **internal
engine effects** from **outbound forwarding**.

**Configuration (single-validator LocalMesh, DevNet):** valid local identity; `num_validators = 1`;
`--data-dir` set so `cfg.consensus_storage = Some(..)` (Run-093 handle; absent handle ⇒ no persistence per
`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2974-2977` and `main.rs:8500-8503`); `--devnet-reconfig-proposal-next-epoch=1`;
non-mainnet. Spawned via `spawn_binary_consensus_loop` (`main.rs:5590`, io = `None`, so
`verification_policy = Required`, `proposal_vote_authority = None` per `binary_consensus_loop.rs:2931`).

**Ordered trace (static; not executed):**
1. CLI accepts `target=1` (`≠0`, non-mainnet) → `cfg.with_reconfig_proposal(target_epoch=1)` (`main.rs:5538-5547`).
2. Loop prelude: engine `current_epoch = 0`; arm `set_pending_reconfig_next_epoch(1)` → `1 > 0` → **Ok, armed**.
3. Leader-step tick → `do_leader_tick` → **`engine.try_propose()` runs unconditionally**
   (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3683`) and emits a `BroadcastProposal` carrying `payload_kind=RECONFIG,
   next_epoch=1` plus the paired self-`BroadcastVote`. The **`Required` / `proposal_vote_authority=None` gate
   applies ONLY at the outbound boundary** `forward_actions_to_facade` (`:3763-3765`), which the io=`None` path
   **never calls** (`outbound = None`). **Internal engine state advances regardless of the authorization
   policy** — this is the internal-effect vs outbound-forwarding distinction.
4. With `num_validators = 1`, across the required leader-step ticks the engine's own self-votes form the QC chain
   and **commit** the reconfig block internally (HotStuff commit-chain depth not re-derived here; single-validator
   commit+persist of a reconfig is corroborated — **not** solely established — by
   `run_096_single_validator_reconfig_commits_and_persists`, which asserts a persisted epoch).
5. Post-tick `maybe_transition_epoch_from_committed_block` (`:9007-9086`) sees the committed `RECONFIG` header,
   checks `next_epoch(1) > current_epoch(0)`, and calls `engine.transition_to_epoch(EpochId(1), same_validator_set)`
   — sequential `0→1` with the **same** validator set (no external governance provider required) → **succeeds** →
   `current_epoch = 1`.
6. `maybe_persist_engine_epoch_transition` (`:3340-3353` tick branch; body `:8723`): `current_epoch(1) >
   last_persisted_epoch(0)` → attempts the atomic epoch-transition write via the storage handle. **A local
   storage write failure** (disk full / I/O error / permissions) returns `Err` → `eprintln!("… FATAL …")` →
   `epoch_persistence_failed = Some(e)` → `break`.
7. Post-loop (`:3517-3551`): `final_progress = progress.lock().clone()` (**no error field**) → logs
   "Run 094 epoch persistence FAILED — fail-closed exit" → returns `final_progress`.
8. **Owner behaviour:** task ends; `JoinHandle` resolves `Ok(progress)`; `consensus_handle` is **not awaited until
   operator `ctrl_c`** (`main.rs:5596`) and its result is then discarded; **no supervision/restart**; the process
   continues (LocalMesh parked on `ctrl_c`).

**Prerequisite classification (kept distinct):** config prerequisites = single-validator + `--data-dir`
(storage wired) + `--devnet-reconfig-proposal-next-epoch=1`; the triggering fault = a **local storage write
failure** at persistence — explicitly **not** attacker-triggered and **not** relabelled as a remote exploit.
**Unresolved/qualified step:** the exact HotStuff commit-chain depth (how many ticks to commit) was not
re-derived; production reachability of the commit is grounded in source (unconditional `try_propose`,
single-validator engine, successful `transition_to_epoch`) and **corroborated** by the test, **not inferred from
the test alone**. Runtime UNEXECUTED.

*(A second, transition-layer variant: if `transition_to_epoch` itself rejected a committed reconfig, the loop
takes the `reconfig_transition_failed` fatal branch (`:3328-3335`) instead — same unsupervised-exit shape. For
single-validator `0→1` the transition succeeds, so the persistence branch is the witnessed one.)*

## A14.1-C4 — Lifecycle and evidence wording tightened (A14 §A14.1–§A14.3, §A14.7)

1. **Missing failure fields ≠ unobservable completion.** A14 §A14.1/§A14.3 wrote that a fatal exit is "invisible
   to any value an observer could read" and the struct's lack of an error field makes failure unobservable.
   **`[SUPERSEDED-A14 →A14.1-C4]`** Precisely: `BinaryConsensusLoopProgress` (`:695-709`) has **no error field**,
   so the returned value **does not encode the failure *reason***; it does **not** make **task completion**
   itself unobservable. Completion is observable (the task ends; the `JoinHandle` resolves). What is lost is the
   **reason**, available only via the stderr "FATAL"/"fail-closed exit" logs.
2. **An await that returns observes completion; discarding the result loses handling, not observation.** A14
   §A14.2/§A14.3 framed `let _ = consensus_handle.await` as if no completion is observed.
   **`[SUPERSEDED-A14 →A14.1-C4]`** At shutdown the `await` **does observe task completion** (it returns
   `Ok(progress)` or `Err(JoinError)`); binding to `let _` discards **outcome handling**, not the completion
   itself. The actual A15-F1 gap is narrower and must be stated as such: **during operation the handle is not
   awaited at all** (both production paths park on `ctrl_c` first), so completion is **not observed while the
   node runs**; and even the shutdown-time await **discards** the outcome. Keep this distinct from (a) normal
   cooperative shutdown and (b) the awaits of the **other** workers (`run035_handle`, `snapshot_handle`,
   `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown`), which are separate completions.
3. **Panic outcome is conditional on the *effective* strategy.** A14 §A14.3 reasoned from "no `panic=\"abort\"`
   in any `Cargo.toml`" + bare `#[tokio::main]`. **`[SUPERSEDED-A14 →A14.1-C4]` (hardened, not reversed):** those
   establish only the **committed source** defaults; they do **not** establish the **deployed binary's** build
   settings (a `RUSTFLAGS=-C panic=abort`, profile override, or custom allocator/`-Zbuild-std` could change it).
   State conditionally: **under an unwind strategy** a task panic yields `Err(JoinError)` (discarded at the
   shutdown await, process continues); **under an abort strategy** the process aborts. Which holds in deployment
   is **unverified here**.
4. **Negative test-coverage claims scoped to inspected bodies.** A14 §A14.7 said tests "**none** assert an
   in-process supervisor … (there is none to assert)." **`[SUPERSEDED-A14 →A14.1-C4]`** Scope it: **in the test
   bodies inspected this pass** (`run_096_*`, `b5`, `b9`, `b10`, `c4_b6`), none asserts an in-process
   supervisor/watchdog/restart. This is **not** proof no such regression test exists anywhere in the tree; an
   absent supervisor **could** be exposed by a future/other failing regression test. The static **source**
   finding (no supervisor in `main.rs`) is what carries A15-F1, independent of test enumeration.
5. **Receiver-ownership precision.** A14 §A14.2/§A14.4 said "the consensus task owns **only** the receiver."
   **`[SUPERSEDED-A14 →A14.1-C4]`** The task owns the inbound **`mpsc::Receiver`** among its **consensus-wiring**
   handles; it of course also owns its **engine**, its **`BinaryConsensusLoopConfig`**, its clones of the
   **progress `Arc`** and **`metrics` `Arc`**, and (P2P) the **outbound facade** and **inbound stats**. The
   transport-decoupling argument (§A14.4) rests specifically on the **receiver** drop closing the inbound
   channel so `ChannelConsensusHandler::try_send` fails and only logs (`p2p_inbound.rs:506-520`); the other
   owned resources drop with the task and do not alter that conclusion.

## A14.1-D A15-F1 disposition after A14.1
**A15-F1 — OPEN, PRESENT at HEAD (static-supported; availability / in-process observability). Stable ID retained;
no new/duplicate ID.** The finding is **unchanged in substance**: in both production paths the consensus task's
`JoinHandle` is not awaited during operation (only at `ctrl_c`, then discarded), no in-process watcher/health-
check/restart exists, and the returned value encodes **no failure reason**. A14.1 corrects the **supporting
evidence**: an **example external** height-stall alert (`QbindConsensusNoProgress`) **does** ship (symptom-level,
not task-specific, deployment-unobserved, no in-process recovery → **does not close A15-F1**); the Run-096
arm-refusal is **not** a production trigger (retained as a defensive/library path); the storage-failure witness
is now **concrete** (single-validator reconfig → committed transition → local storage write failure); and the
lifecycle wording is tightened (completion observable, reason not; panic conditional on effective strategy; test
claims scoped; receiver-ownership precise).

## A14.1 Current-source disposition for A15-F1

**A15-F1 — OPEN, PRESENT at HEAD (static-supported; availability / observability).** In **both** production
startup paths the spawned consensus task's `JoinHandle` is awaited **only during operator-initiated shutdown**,
its result is **discarded**, the returned-progress `Arc` is bound to an **unused `_progress`**, and there is **no
in-process watcher, health-check, or restart** of the task. The task's return type carries **no failure field**,
so a fatal exit is invisible to any value an observer could read — it is signalled **only by a stderr log**.
This matches the historical hypothesis; it is revalidated as a current source fact, not an executed runtime
observation.

Scope qualifier: this is an **availability / in-process-observability** finding. It is **not** an authentication
bypass, **not** a consensus-safety defect, and **not** a remote exploit on its own; the single bounded reachable
exit example (§A14.4) is a **local** storage/config condition.

## A14.2 Caller / owner inventory (production vs test)

**Production (non-test) callers — exactly two, both in `qbind-node/src/main.rs`:**

| Path | Call site | Helper | Handle binding | Progress binding | Handle observed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LocalMesh** (single-validator, io=None) | `main.rs:5590` | `spawn_binary_consensus_loop` | `consensus_handle` | **`_progress` (unused)** | **only at shutdown**: `let _ = consensus_handle.await;` after `ctrl_c` (`:5593-5596`) |
| **P2P** (configured, io-wired) | `main.rs:8684-8685` | `spawn_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` | `consensus_handle` | **`_progress` (unused)** | **only at shutdown**: `let _ = consensus_handle.await;` after `ctrl_c` (`:8702-8706`) |

All other call sites are **tests** (`crates/qbind-node/tests/…`) or the internal delegation
`run_binary_consensus_loop → run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2786`).

**Observer search (the `_progress`-unused caveat was tested, not assumed):** `consensus_handle` appears in
`main.rs` **only** at its spawn and its single shutdown `await` (`:5590,5596,8684,8706`) — **no `tokio::select!`
arm, no `JoinHandle::is_finished()` poll, no watchdog/supervisor/restart** (grep for
`watchdog|supervis|restart|health_check|is_finished` in `main.rs` finds none against this task). **No production
reader** of `BinaryConsensusLoopProgress` fields exists (the returned `Arc` reaches only the unused `_progress`;
the task holds the only writing clone). The `node_metrics: Arc<NodeMetrics>` passed into the loop is updated
continuously (**diagnostics**, scrapeable via the opt-in metrics endpoint) — that is an **external** signal, not
in-process supervision (§A14.5).

**Owners that are independent of the consensus task** (so they are unaffected by its exit — see §A14.3):
`node_context` holds the `TcpKemTlsP2pService` (listener/accept) and `demuxer_handle`; the
`ChannelConsensusHandler` **sender** is held by the demuxer (plus a default-inert Run-035 clone,
`main.rs:6185`); the consensus task owns only the **receiver** `consensus_inbound_rx` (`main.rs:6177`, cap 256).
`P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown(node_context)` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:2247-2265`) is invoked **only at `main.rs:8714`**,
after `ctrl_c` and after the consensus `await` — never from a consensus-task exit.

## A14.3 Lifecycle table — completion vs failure vs process termination

Loop signature: `run_binary_consensus_loop[_with_io](…) -> BinaryConsensusLoopProgress`
(`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2778-2811`) — a **bare progress value, not a `Result`**. Spawn helpers return
`JoinHandle<BinaryConsensusLoopProgress>` (`:9394-9396,9420-9422`). The struct
(`:695-709`) has fields `ticks / proposals_emitted / commits / committed_height / current_view / inbound` —
**no error/failure field.** Final value: `let final_progress = progress.lock().clone(); … final_progress`
(`:3517,3551`); the fatal-error locals `epoch_persistence_failed` / `reconfig_transition_failed`
(`:2980,2986`) are **only logged** (`:3518-3529`) and reduced to `.is_some()` booleans in the exit log line —
they are **never written into the returned value or the progress `Arc`.**

| Lifecycle event | Source branch | Return type / JoinHandle result | Failure in returned progress? | Logging | Owner (main) response | Restart? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Expected cooperative shutdown** | `shutdown_rx.changed()` → `break` (`:3119-3125`, no-io `:3367+`) | returns `final_progress`; handle → `Ok(progress)` | no (clean counters) | "Shutdown signal received after N ticks" | the shutdown `await` returns; node proceeds to `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown` | n/a (intended) |
| **Unexpected normal return** | configured `max_ticks` cap → `break` (`:3355-3362`); production leaves `max_ticks=None` so this is a **test/characterization** path | returns `final_progress`; handle → `Ok(progress)` | no | "Reached max_ticks=…, stopping." | **none during operation** (main parked on `ctrl_c`); result discarded at shutdown | **no** |
| **Internal fatal → return/break** | Run-096 arm refusal → `return BinaryConsensusLoopProgress::default()` (`:2891-2902`); epoch-transition Err → `break` (`:3182-3189,3328-3335,3481`); epoch-persistence Err → `break` (`:3194-3206,3340-3353,3498`) | returns progress (default/last); handle → **`Ok(progress)`** (NOT `Err`) | **no** (error dropped; only `.is_some()` logged) | "FATAL: …" then "… FAILED — fail-closed exit: …" | **none** (handle unobserved until shutdown; result discarded) | **no** |
| **Panic under unwind** | committed strategy is **unwind** (no `panic="abort"` in any `Cargo.toml`); bare `#[tokio::main]` (`main.rs:2008`); task **not** wrapped in `catch_unwind` | handle → **`Err(JoinError)`** at the shutdown `await`; **process continues** (unwind caught at task boundary) | n/a (no value) | tokio's default panic report to stderr | **none**; `let _ = …await` **discards** the `Err` | **no** |
| **Process abort / exit** | `std::process::exit(1)` exists only in unrelated startup gates (e.g. Run-035 `main.rs:8762,8773`); `std::process::abort()` only in `safety_record_store/owner/model.rs` (a separate SIGABRT-on-violation subsystem) — **not** on the consensus path | whole process ends | n/a | that subsystem's own logs | n/a | n/a |
| **Running but not progressing** (liveness stall) | loop keeps selecting/ticking; `ticks` advances while `commits`/`committed_height` stall | task **alive**; handle unresolved | no (counters just plateau) | per-tick metrics/log continue | **none** (progress `Arc` unread in production) | **no** |

**Separations enforced:** a "FATAL" log is **not** proof the process exits (the three fatal branches `return`/
`break` the **task** and the process keeps running); a bare-progress return is **not** an application-level
`Err`; **unwind panic** (committed default) is kept distinct from **allocator/`process::abort`** (a different
mechanism, not on this path); a **possible build override** to `-C panic=abort` via `RUSTFLAGS` is **unobserved
and out of scope** (the committed profiles do not set it); and the **deployed binary's** actual behaviour is
unobserved (static only).

## A14.4 What survives an unexpected consensus-task exit (P2P)

On a consensus-task exit **without** operator `ctrl_c`, nothing calls `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown`, and the task's
only owned consensus resource — the inbound **receiver** — drops. `ChannelConsensusHandler::handle_consensus_msg_from`
(`p2p_inbound.rs:506-520`) then does `self.sender.try_send(…)`; on the now-closed channel it returns `Err` and
the handler **only logs** `"[P2P Inbound] Failed to forward consensus message (channel full or closed)"` and
returns — **no transport shutdown, no connection close, no health flag, no error propagation.** Staged outcome:

| Stage | After consensus-task exit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Listener bound | **survives** | `TcpKemTlsP2pService` owned by `node_context`, not dropped |
| Handshake possible | **survives** | accept task independent of the consensus task |
| Transport traffic processed | **survives** | read/write loops + demuxer owned by `node_context` |
| Consensus messages accepted into the engine | **stops** | receiver dropped → `try_send` fails → logged + dropped |
| Consensus progress | **stops** | engine no longer driven by inbound; no commits advance |

So the node continues to **present as "up"** (listener, handshakes, metrics) while consensus is **dead and
unsupervised** — the core A15-F1 gap. **Transport availability must not be read as consensus health.** (Separately:
under the production `Required` policy with `proposal_vote_authority=None` — `main.rs:8673-8682`,
`binary_consensus_loop.rs:742-749` — inbound Proposal/Vote are already rejected fail-closed and outbound
suppressed even when the task is **healthy**; that liveness gate is **independent** of A15-F1 and is not counted
as its effect.)

**One bounded, jointly-satisfiable unexpected-exit example (local, not remote).**
- **Trigger:** Run-094 epoch-persistence write failure. On a committed canonical epoch transition, the tick/inbound
  branch calls `maybe_persist_engine_epoch_transition(engine, storage, …)`; a storage write error returns `Err`,
  logged `"FATAL"`, `epoch_persistence_failed = Some(e)`, `break` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3340-3353`), then
  post-loop `"Run 094 epoch persistence FAILED — fail-closed exit"` (`:3518-3522`) and a normal `Ok(progress)`
  return.
- **Config prerequisites:** a node with `cfg.consensus_storage = Some(..)` (Run-093 handle wired) **and** a reached
  canonical epoch transition (e.g. a committed reconfig block).
- **Capability prerequisite:** a **local storage write failure** (disk full / I/O error / permissions) at the
  persistence instant. This is explicitly a **local storage/config failure**, **not** relabeled as a remote
  exploit.
- **Consequence (unexecuted):** the consensus task ends `Ok`; `consensus_handle` is unobserved until `ctrl_c`;
  no supervisor/restart; transport stays up per the table above. Runtime UNEXECUTED.

A second, purely config-gated example is the **Run-096** startup refusal (requires a `--reconfig`-style CLI intent
with a non-monotonic/invalid `target_epoch`, e.g. against a restored engine): logs `"FATAL"`, returns
`BinaryConsensusLoopProgress::default()` at startup (`:2891-2902`) — again a clean task exit, process alive.

**Panic / hang without a demonstrated trigger are conditional lifecycle analyses only:** a panic inside the
engine/tick would unwind to `Err(JoinError)` (discarded), and a "running but not progressing" hang is possible in
principle, but **no trigger is demonstrated here**, and A21-F1 / A33-F1 are **not reopened** to supply one.

## A14.5 Diagnostics vs supervision

Four distinct layers, only the first of which exists in-process for this task:

| Layer | Present at HEAD? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Diagnostic emission** | **yes** | per-tick/exit stderr logs; continuous `NodeMetrics` updates; final "Loop exit:" summary (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3530-3550`) |
| **Owner-side detection** | **no** | handle awaited only at shutdown and discarded; progress `Arc` unread; no `is_finished`/`select!` watcher (§A14.2) |
| **Alerting / automatic shutdown** | **no (in-process)** | no code converts a consensus-task exit into a node shutdown or alert |
| **Recovery / restart** | **no** | no respawn of the consensus task anywhere |

The metrics endpoint is **operator-opt-in** (and relates to carried A24-F1, not reopened); whether an **external**
process manager restarts the node is **deployment-dependent and unobserved** — no repository-defined supervisor or
deployment health-check for this task was found. Detection via metrics requires an external scraper comparing e.g.
`ticks`/`commits` deltas; the repository ships **no** such check.

- **`shutdown()` awaiting a task ≠ proof of completion.** Confirmed here: `consensus_handle.await`'s result is
  **discarded** (`let _`), and `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown` **aborts** the demuxer with a 5 s timeout then relies on
  **drop** for the transport (`p2p_node_builder.rs:2254-2261`) — awaiting/aborting does not establish clean
  completion.
- **Dropping senders must account for retained clones and queued/active commands.** The
  `ChannelConsensusHandler` sender has a retained Run-035 clone (`main.rs:6185`) and a 256-deep queue; the
  task-exit cleanup reasoned about here is the **receiver** drop, which closes the channel for `try_send`.
- **A fatal-error `blocking_send` can wait behind backpressure.** Carried from A13.1 (secure_channel
  `reader_worker`'s `tx.blocking_send(Err(e))` can block on a full async channel); not re-audited here.
- **Read-loop exit releases its own resources but does not guarantee whole-session cleanup.** Carried verbatim
  from A13.1-C2; consistent with §A14.4 (a sub-loop/task exit does not tear down peers.
- **`pqc_active` configured-map requirement applies to Required/Optional; Disabled keeps its separate
  `client_random` resolver.** Carried verbatim from A13.1-C5; not re-audited here.

## A13.1-C1 — Outcome and receive-counter corrections (A5-F1)

**C1a — Four branches separated (the A13 "inevitable chain" is withdrawn).**
A13 §A13.2 (v1.74:56-60) wrote that a framing loss' "failure surfaces **later** when a misframed frame reaches
`decrypt_app` and the AEAD tag check fails (fatal → teardown)," and §A13.0 dispositioned A5-F1 as
"desync → later AEAD/decode failure → **this connection torn down**." **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C1]`** The
consequences after a desync are **conditional, not a single inevitable chain**, and they are four distinct
events that must not be collapsed:

1. **Framing loss** — `read_transport_frame` (`framed_io.rs:109-137`) `read_exact`s the 5-byte header then the
   payload; a timeout after ≥1 consumed byte discards those bytes, and `recv_app` (`secure_channel.rs:415-418`)
   starts a **fresh** read with no retained offset. This alone changes only the *next read position*; it does
   not by itself reject, exit, or close anything.
2. **Frame rejection** — the next misframed read resolves to **one of two sub-cases** (see C1b), each a distinct
   rejecting boundary with a distinct counter effect.
3. **Worker exit** — a *fatal* `Err` (anything not `TimedOut`/`WouldBlock`) makes `reader_worker`
   (`secure_channel.rs:691-695`) send the `Err` and `break`; the async `read_loop` then observes that `Err` from
   `channel.recv().await` and `break`s (`p2p_tcp.rs:1527-1530`). **This ends the read side only.**
4. **Socket closure** — is a *separate* event with its own owners and timing (see C2); it does **not** follow
   from read-side exit on a **registered** session.

**C1b — Receive-counter table corrected.** A13 §A13.2 row "Complete frame + decode/AEAD failure" assigned
"**receive counter +1** (next_nonce before open)" to a single conflated "decode/AEAD" outcome
(v1.74:54). **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C1]`** The counter advances **iff execution reaches
`direction.open` → `next_nonce()`**. `next_nonce` (`session.rs:68-75`) **reads the current counter `n`, then
stores `n+1`**, and `open` (`:84-89`) calls it **before** `aead.open`, so the store **is not rolled back on AEAD
failure**. Rejections that occur *before* `open` never call `next_nonce`:

| Receive outcome | Where | Reaches `open`? | Receive counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TransportFrame::decode` too-short / payload-truncated | `transport.rs:49-60` | no | **unchanged** |
| oversized length (`len > 16 MiB`) rejected pre-alloc | `framed_io.rs:117-122` | no | **unchanged** |
| unexpected `msg_type` (not APP) | `decrypt_app_frame` `transport.rs:92-94` | no | **unchanged** |
| AEAD open **attempted** and **fails** (tag mismatch) | `open` `transport.rs:95` → `session.rs:84-89` | **yes** | **n → n+1** (store precedes the failure) |
| AEAD open succeeds | same | yes | **n → n+1** |

So a desynced read can terminate the reader **without advancing the receive counter at all** (decode-size or
`msg_type` rejection), or **with a single advance** (if it reaches `open`). Partial-read / no-progress-timeout
cases (A13 §A13.2 rows) remain **unchanged counter** — that part of A13 was correct and is retained.

**C1c — Scope wording corrected.** A13 §A13.2 ended "Effect is **connection-local; other peers unaffected**"
(v1.74:59). **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C1]`** Replace with: **direct connection-local disruption is established
(framing loss on this one connection, re-traced to source); broader effects — including whether and how quickly
other peers are affected — are not demonstrated** (no runtime, no topology model). "Not demonstrated" is not
"shown absent."

---

## A13.1-C2 — Ownership and cleanup corrected (A6-F1 and general teardown)

**C2a — The two ownership domains are different objects.** `SecureChannelAsync` (`secure_channel.rs:570-577`) is
a `Clone` handle holding **`write_tx: mpsc::Sender<WriteCommand>`** and **`read_rx: Arc<Mutex<Receiver<…>>>`** —
it owns **no socket**. The **socket** is owned by the **`Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>`** created in `try_new`
(`:628`) and shared only by the two blocking workers (`:631-640`). These are distinct; dropping
`SecureChannelAsync` handles and releasing the socket are **not the same event** and need not be simultaneous.

**C2b — Counterexample: a reader-failed *registered* session is not cleaned up by the read side.** A13 §A13.4
row "Reader failure / remote EOF" claimed the failure drops "the last `SecureChannelAsync` clone ⇒ channel
Arc → socket closed; writer_worker ends on closed `write_rx`," release condition "**prompt, on the error**"
(v1.74:102). **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C2]`** For a **registered** peer this is false. `read_loop`'s `break`
(`p2p_tcp.rs:1518,1523,1529`) **does not** remove the `peers` entry and **does not** touch the write side; there
is **no `Drop` on `PeerConnection`** (`:339-369`). Therefore, after the reader fails, the following remain
**alive**: the **`peers` map entry**; the outbound **`tx`/`raw_tx`** senders it holds; the **write loop** (still
awaiting `recv()` in its `select!`); the **writer_worker**; and the **socket**. The reader failure ends the
**`reader_worker` + async `read_loop` only**. There is no source-supported "prompt, on the error" whole-session
cleanup here.

**C2c — Where socket release actually comes from.** The socket (last `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>`) drops only
when **both** blocking workers exit:
- **`writer_worker`** (`:705-751`) exits when its outer `rx.blocking_recv()` returns `None` — i.e. **all**
  `write_tx` senders have dropped (which requires the `peers` entry gone *and* every `SecureChannelAsync` clone
  dropped) — **or** on a fatal send error / poisoned mutex.
- **`reader_worker`** (`:649-698`) exits when `read_tx` is closed/dropped or on a fatal read error.

Hence the socket is released via **`shutdown(self)`** (drops both channels, then **awaits** both handles —
`:382-394`; its own doc at `:383-387` notes dropping *both* outbound channels is required for the write loop to
exit), via **eviction** (C3), or via **same-NodeId replacement** (C2d) — **not** by a read-loop exit on a still-
registered session.

**C2d — A6-F1 restated precisely.** Same-NodeId `peers.write().insert(node_id, conn)` (`:1426`) ignores the
displaced `PeerConnection`, which is dropped: its `tx`/`raw_tx` close (displaced **write loop** exits) but its
`read_handle`/`write_handle` are **detached, not aborted**. The displaced **read loop task**, its
`SecureChannelAsync`, the two blocking workers, and the socket **linger** until the *remote* side EOFs or errors
(the reader loops on `TimedOut`/`WouldBlock` indefinitely while the remote is silent). This is the one
source-supported **cumulative, connection-local retention** schedule (one lingering displaced read-side per
replacement); **no** measured exhaustion, guaranteed permanent leak, or consensus effect is claimed.

**C2e — Withdrawn wording and clarified distinctions.** The following A13 §A13.4 phrasings are **withdrawn as
unsupported timing/universality claims `[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C2]`:** "**prompt, on the error**" (v1.74:102);
"**shortly after, as the channel Arc refcount reaches zero**" (v1.74:105); and any reading of A13 that implies a
reader failure makes the owners "all gone" or that **every** teardown waits on a remote EOF (EOF is the release
condition for the *detached/displaced* case specifically, not a universal rule). Five states kept explicit and
non-interchangeable: **detach** (drop a `JoinHandle` → task keeps running) · **abort request** (`abort()`,
effective only at an `.await`) · **observed completion** (`await` the handle) · **blocking-worker exit** (when
its channel end drops or it hits a fatal error) · **socket destruction** (last `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>`
drop). Finally, the two I/O workers are **two `spawn_blocking` *tasks*, which may be *queued*** on the blocking
pool, **not necessarily two *executing* OS threads** at any instant — "two threads per session" overstates
concurrency; capacity/queuing is a pool property, unquantified here (bare `#[tokio::main]`, not vendored).

---

## A13.1-C3 — Cancellation during an active write retry

A13 §A13.4 "Registry eviction" row said `abort()` "cancel[s] the **async** tasks" and that the blocking thread
"exits when `read_tx`/`write_rx` drop," with release "**shortly after**" (v1.74:105). **`[SUPERSEDED-A13
→A13.1-C3]`** for the timing and for the implicit claim that eviction promptly stops the writer. Precise
behaviour:

- **`evict_all_sessions`** (`p2p_tcp.rs:1789-1833`) drains `peers`, drops `tx`/`raw_tx`, and calls
  `read_handle.abort()` + `write_handle.abort()` (`:1818-1819`). These handles are the **async** `read_loop` /
  `write_loop` tasks only.
- The blocking **`reader_worker`/`writer_worker`** handles were **discarded at spawn** in `try_new` (`:632-634`,
  `:638-640` — the `spawn_blocking` return values are dropped → detached from birth); nothing holds them, and
  **`abort()` cannot reach them regardless**.
- Per tokio **1.49.0** (pinned): `JoinHandle::abort()` takes effect only the **next time the task yields at an
  `.await`**; it has **no effect on a running `spawn_blocking` task** ("the task will continue running"); and
  **dropping** a `JoinHandle` **detaches** (the task keeps running in the background). Confirmed from
  authoritative docs this pass (read-only).
- **`writer_worker`'s WouldBlock inner retry** (`secure_channel.rs:725-733`) sleeps 1 ms and `continue`s,
  **re-locking the mutex and re-calling `ch.send_app(&data)` without first checking** a dropped caller, a closed
  `write_rx`, or a dropped `response` oneshot. The inner loop exits **only** on `Ok(())`, a **non-`WouldBlock`
  fatal `Err`** (→ breaks inner, sends result, then breaks the outer loop → worker terminates), or — inside
  `send_app`/`seal` — **`NonceOverflow`** at `counter == u64::MAX` (`session.rs:70-72`), which surfaces as a
  fatal `Err`. A command already handed to the worker by `blocking_recv()` is therefore run **to completion or
  fatal error** even if the async side was evicted meanwhile.

**Consequence (unexecuted):** eviction stops the async loops, but a `writer_worker` **actively retrying a
WouldBlock write cannot be preempted by `abort()`**; the socket is released only once that worker reaches an
exit condition and the `reader_worker` has also exited (C2c). No claim is made about how often this window is
hit at runtime.

---

## A13.1-C4 — A11-F2 state table and config corrections

**C4a — Stored-counter semantics (nonce-used ≠ stored-counter).** Re-stated with the stored counter `n` **before
the seal**, per `next_nonce` (`session.rs:68-75`: read `n`, store `n+1`, return `make_nonce(flag,sid,n)`):

| Write event | `send_app`→`seal`→`next_nonce` | **Nonce used** | **Stored counter after** | Wire result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First `send_app(data)` | 1st `next_nonce` | **`nonce(n)`** | **`n+1`** | frame built from `nonce(n)` |
| Partial write, then `WouldBlock` | — | — | `n+1` (unchanged by the failed `write_all`) | **stale bytes of frame(`n`) left on the wire** |
| WouldBlock retry re-calls `send_app(data)` | 2nd `next_nonce` | **`nonce(n+1)`** | **`n+2`** | **new** frame built from `nonce(n+1)` |
| Each further WouldBlock retry | next `next_nonce` | `nonce(n+k)` | `n+k+1` | re-encrypted afresh each time |

The retry **re-encrypts the plaintext under a fresh nonce** (it does not resume the original ciphertext/offset).
`nonce(n)` and `nonce(n+1)` are **distinct** → this is **not A11-F1 nonce reuse**; A11-F2 stays a separate
finding. "Nonce used" (the value fed to AEAD) and "stored counter" (the next-to-issue value) are tracked as
**separate quantities** above; A13 §A13.3's single "sender counter c→c+1" column conflated them
**`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C4]`**.

**C4b — DummyAead can also disrupt framing.** A13 §A13.3 (v1.74:85-87) said the desync/teardown consequence is
"**specific to the real ChaCha20-Poly1305 path**" because DummyAead "reproduces the same bytes and there is no
tag to fail." **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C4]`** The **framing** disruption is **not** exclusive to real AEAD: a
*partial write* leaves a **truncated length-prefixed prefix** of frame(`n`) on the wire, and the retried
**full** frame(`n+1`) follows it. The receiver's `read_transport_frame` parses the stale 5-byte header/length
first and consumes the wrong byte count — a **framing/length desync independent of the AEAD tag**. Under
DummyAead there is no *tag* failure, but the receiver still misparses subsequent frame boundaries. The *tag*-
check failure is specific to real AEAD; the *framing* disruption is common to both.

**C4c — Write-timeout configuration (both paths set it; `try_new` changes only the read timeout).** A13 §A13.3
(v1.74:79-82) said "`try_new` sets only the 100 ms read timeout; it does not re-set the write timeout — **so
inbound/outbound differ**." Corrected **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C4]`**: `configure_socket`
(`secure_channel.rs:196-204`) sets `nodelay`, `set_read_timeout(DEFAULT_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS)`, **and
`set_write_timeout(DEFAULT_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS)`**, and it is called on **both** the **dial** path
(`connect`, `:242`) and the **accept** paths (`:292`, `:337`) — so the established write timeout is
`DEFAULT_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS` on **both** sides, not an inbound/outbound asymmetry. `try_new` (`:618-621`)
overrides **only** the **read** timeout to 100 ms (and **propagates** that error via `?`), leaving the write
timeout as configured. Two residual conditionals remain: (i) each `configure_socket` call uses **`.ok()`
(`:197,200,203`), silently discarding a failed syscall**, so the *effective* write timeout is "installed unless
the syscall failed"; and (ii) whether a stalled write surfaces as **`WouldBlock`/`EAGAIN`** (triggers the retry)
or **`TimedOut`** (fatal, no retry) is **platform-dependent** — the reader's own comment notes Linux may return
`EAGAIN` for a socket timeout (`:674-676`). Exact per-platform `SO_SNDTIMEO` mapping **not verified from an
authoritative source here → left conditional.**

---

## A13.1-C5 — Repeatable-identity prerequisite corrected

A13 §A13.4 (v1.74:90-93) stated the inbound NodeId is "**deterministic per peer**" and that the `pqc_active`
branch uses "`derive_node_id_from_pubkey(cert.leaf_kem_pk)`." **`[SUPERSEDED-A13 →A13.1-C5]`** The installed
inbound identity resolver (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1533-1561`) does **not** derive the `pqc_active` NodeId from the
leaf public key; it performs a **configured peer-map lookup**, and a missing mapping yields **no repeatable
identity**:

- **Required / Optional** (`:1536-1552`): if `!mutual_auth_complete` → **`None`**; else take
  `verified_peer_validator_id` (`None` if absent) and `parse_test_validator_id_from_cert_validator_id` (`None`
  if unparseable); then —
  - **`pqc_active` → `resolver_peer_node_ids.get(&vid).copied()`** (`:1549`): a repeatable registry NodeId
    **only if `vid` is present in the configured peer map**; a **missing entry → `None`**.
  - **not `pqc_active` → `Some(derive_test_node_id_from_validator_id(vid))`** (`:1551`, documented test-grade).
- **Disabled** (`:1553-1558`): `parse_test_validator_id_from_client_random(client_random)` (self-asserted,
  test-grade) → `Some(derive_test_node_id_from_validator_id(vid))`.

When the resolver returns **`None`**, the accept path falls back to a **temporary session NodeId** =
`sha3_256(INBOUND_SESSION_DOMAIN_TAG ‖ ":" ‖ local_validator_id ‖ session_counter_be ‖ peer_addr)`
(`p2p_tcp.rs:1161-1183`) — **not cryptographically bound to the dialer and not repeatable** across reconnects
(the counter changes). The four questions A13 blurred, separated:

| Property | Holds when | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Handshake acceptance** | KEMTLS completes under the configured mode (independent of registry identity) | `accept_kemtls_async_with_peer_init` `p2p_tcp.rs:1140-1142` |
| **Repeatable registry NodeId** | Req/Opt + `mutual_auth_complete` + parseable cert `vid` + (**`pqc_active`:** `vid` **in** `resolver_peer_node_ids`; **else** derive) | `p2p_node_builder.rs:1543-1557` |
| **Temporary NodeId fallback** | resolver returns `None` (no resolver, auth incomplete, unparseable, **or `vid` absent from the map**) | `p2p_tcp.rs:1161-1183` |
| **Authenticated consensus origin** | a **separate** resolver binds a verified-cert origin; `None` ⇒ ingress gate **fails closed** | `p2p_tcp.rs:1191-1194`, Run 418 |

The **registry identity resolver** (which NodeId a session registers under) and **Run-418 consensus
authorization** (whether a frame carries an authenticated origin) are **distinct resolvers with distinct
inputs**; A6-F1's same-NodeId replacement concerns the **former only**. A6-F1's replacement therefore presumes a
peer that resolves to a **repeatable registry NodeId** (map-backed in the `pqc_active` deployment); a peer that
falls to the temporary-NodeId path does **not** collide on insert and is outside A6-F1's precondition.

## A13.2 A5-F1 — receive-frame progress across retry
Route: `SecureChannelAsync::try_new` (`secure_channel.rs:608-646`, sets the **established** read timeout to
**100 ms** and **propagates** the config error via `.map_err(...)?` at `:621` — unlike the handshake's `.ok()`-
ignored config) → `reader_worker` loop (`:649-698`, `recv_app` under the mutex; TimedOut/WouldBlock =
**non-fatal**, sleep 1 ms + retry; other `Err` = fatal → send + break) → `recv_app` (`:415-418`,
`read_transport_frame` then `decrypt_app`) → `read_transport_frame` (`framed_io.rs:109-137`) → `decrypt_app`
→ receive counter `next_nonce()` (`session.rs:68-89`, increments **before** the AEAD open).

| Case | Consumed bytes | Retained framing state | Buffers | Counter | Retry branch | Next read position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **No frame bytes (no-progress timeout)** — *counterexample* | 0 | none to lose | header buf freed on `Err` | unchanged | non-fatal retry | **at a real frame boundary** — no desync |
| **Partial header** (1-4 of 5) | 1-4 header bytes **discarded** | none (fresh call) | freed on `Err` | unchanged | non-fatal retry | **mid-frame** → next `read_exact(5)` misreads remaining header+payload → **desync** |
| **Complete header + payload timeout** *(preferred: partial-read details certain)* | 5 header + 0..len-1 payload **discarded** | none | `Vec::with_capacity(5+len)` (≤16 MiB) freed on `Err` | unchanged | non-fatal retry | **mid-payload** → next call reads remaining payload as a "header" → **desync** |
| **Partial payload** | 5 header + k payload **discarded** | none | freed | unchanged | non-fatal retry | mid-payload → **desync** |
| **Complete frame + decode/AEAD failure** | whole frame consumed | n/a | freed | **receive counter +1** (next_nonce before open) | **fatal** (not TimedOut) → send `Err` + break | connection torn down |

**Separation:** loss of framing (partial cases) does **not** by itself fail AEAD or close the socket **at that
instant** — the reader keeps retrying; the failure surfaces **later** when a misframed frame reaches
`decrypt_app` and the AEAD tag check fails (fatal → teardown). A no-progress timeout loses nothing. Effect is
**connection-local**; other peers unaffected. The established read-timeout error is **propagated** (`:621`),
distinct from the handshake config whose errors are ignored (A12.1).

## A13.3 A11-F2 — write retry, ciphertext, and counter state
Route: `writer_worker` (`secure_channel.rs:700-751`) → `send_app` (`:401-405`) → `encrypt_app` →
`c2s/s2c.seal` (`session.rs:77-82`, `next_nonce()` then AEAD seal) → `write_transport_frame`
(`framed_io.rs:88-97`, `write_all` + `flush`).

| Event | Plaintext | Ciphertext/offset | Sender counter | Receiver counter | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zero-progress write error (0 bytes written) | retained in `data` | frame(c) encoded, not on wire | already c (seal ran) | unchanged | if WouldBlock → **retry re-encrypts** as frame(c+1); if TimedOut/other → fatal break |
| **Partial write + WouldBlock** | retained | **stale bytes of frame(c) on the wire**; retry builds **frame(c+1)** afresh | c→**c+1** | — | wire = partial(c)+full(c+1) → **receiver desync** → AEAD fail (connection-local) |
| Successful write | consumed | frame(c) fully sent | c | advances on receive | normal |
| Retryable WouldBlock | retained | re-encrypted each retry | **advances per retry** | — | platform-dependent (below) |
| Non-retryable TimedOut/other | retained | not re-sent | c (seal ran once) | — | fatal break → connection terminates |

**Retry re-encrypts anew** (does not preserve ciphertext/offset): each WouldBlock retry calls
`send_app(&data)` → fresh `seal` with `next_nonce()`. **Advancing to c+1 is a new nonce, NOT A11-F1 reuse.**
Consequence is **connection-local**: a partial-write-then-WouldBlock leaves stale frame(c) bytes on the wire
and re-sends frame(c+1), desyncing the receiver → AEAD failure → teardown of **this** connection. Prerequisite:
the write path must yield **WouldBlock** (not TimedOut). **Socket timeout semantics (left conditional):** the
established socket is **blocking** (`set_nonblocking(false)` pre-handshake) with a write timeout of 10 s from
the handshake `configure_socket` (`try_new` sets only the 100 ms **read** timeout; it does **not** re-set the
write timeout — so inbound/outbound differ); on platforms where `SO_SNDTIMEO` yields `TimedOut` the retry does
**not** trigger (fatal break, no re-encryption); on platforms where it yields `WouldBlock`/`EAGAIN` (noted in
the reader comment `:674-676`) the retry **does** trigger. Exact per-platform mapping **not verified from
authoritative source here → left conditional.** **DummyAead vs real:** under `DummyAead` (XOR, nonce ignored)
re-encryption reproduces the same bytes and there is no tag to fail; the desync/teardown consequence is
specific to the real ChaCha20-Poly1305 (`pqc_active`) path.

## A13.4 A6-F1 — replacement, worker ownership, and cleanup
**Repeatable NodeId:** inbound NodeId is derived by the B8 identity resolver from the dialer's verified cert /
on-wire hints — deterministic per peer (test-grade: `derive_test_node_id_from_validator_id(N)`; pqc_active:
`derive_node_id_from_pubkey(cert.leaf_kem_pk)`), so a reconnecting peer resolves to the **same** NodeId →
triggers `peers.write().insert` replacement (`p2p_tcp.rs:1426`, displaced value **ignored**). Owners per
`PeerConnection`: peers-map entry; outbound `tx`/`raw_tx` (feed the write loop); `read_handle`/`write_handle`
JoinHandles; and (held by the detached read/write loop tasks) the `SecureChannelAsync` → reader_worker +
writer_worker **blocking threads** → shared `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>` → **socket**.

| Event | Owners that disappear | Owners that remain | Release condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Registered idle session** | — | all | normal `shutdown(self)` (drop channels + **await** handles, `:382-394`) or eviction |
| **Displaced idle session** (same-NodeId insert) | peers-map entry; `tx`/`raw_tx` closed ⇒ **write loop** exits; JoinHandles **detached (no abort/await)** | **read loop task**, `SecureChannelAsync`, **both blocking workers**, **socket** | remote **EOF / fatal read error / AEAD-decode failure** — **NOT** a timeout (reader loops on TimedOut forever) ⇒ a silent-but-open remote lingers **indefinitely** |
| **Reader failure / remote EOF** | reader_worker (fatal `Err`→break); read loop observes `Err`→ends; dropping last `SecureChannelAsync` clone ⇒ channel Arc→socket closed; writer_worker ends on closed `write_rx` | — | prompt, on the error |
| **Writer failure** | writer_worker (fatal break); write loop ends | **read loop + reader_worker + socket** (not driven by the write side) | until the read side independently fails/EOFs |
| **Full downstream queue** | — | all (read loop `inbound_tx.send(..).await` backpressures; connection held, frames not dropped) | when the consumer drains or the connection errors |
| **Registry eviction** (`evict_all_sessions`) | peers-map drained; `read_handle.abort()`+`write_handle.abort()` (`:1818-1819`) cancel the **async** tasks; `tx`/`raw_tx` dropped | the **blocking workers** until the channel Arc drops (abort cancels async tasks at await points; a `spawn_blocking` thread is not force-cancelled mid-call — it exits when `read_tx`/`write_rx` drop) + socket until then | shortly after, as the channel Arc refcount reaches zero |

**Distinctions kept explicit:** dropping a JoinHandle = **detach** (task keeps running); `abort()` = **request**
cancellation (cooperative, at await points; does not force a `spawn_blocking` thread); awaiting = observe
completion; terminating a blocking worker = when its channel end drops; closing the socket = when the last
`SecureChannelAsync`/channel Arc drops. Do **not** infer cleanup from a counter, registry removal, an "evicted"
result, or `is_established()`. **One source-supported retention schedule:** a peer repeatedly reconnecting under
the same NodeId while each prior socket stays **open and silent** leaves one displaced read-side (socket + two
blocking threads + channel) per replacement, each released only on that socket's EOF/error — **cumulative,
connection-local retention**, with **no** claim of measured exhaustion, guaranteed permanent leak, or consensus
failure. **A31-F1 overlap** (its SIGHUP eviction uses the abort path) is **narrowly referenced**, not reopened.

## A13.5 Box::leak disposition (carried A12.1 qualification)
`Connection::handle_handshake_frame` `Box::leak(Box::new(self.crypto.clone()))` (server arm
`connection.rs:282-283`, client arm `:332-333`). **Register check:** no existing finding (A5-F1/A11-F2/A6-F1/
A4-F1/A21-F1/R7) covers this specific site/cause → it **remains a separately-tracked open question** (not
minted as an ID in this pass pending a bound/consequence demonstration). Precise characterization: the leak is
at the **handshake-frame-processing** sites, which occur **once per processed ClientInit/ServerAccept**,
**including attempts later rejected** (the leak precedes `handle_client_init`, so a cert-rejected or
malformed-cert handshake still leaks) — **not** once per TCP accept, and **not** on the earlier cheap rejection
paths that never reach `handle_handshake_frame`. **Per-invocation vs cumulative vs shared ownership:** each
invocation leaks **one small `Box<Arc<dyn CryptoProvider>>`** (a pointer-sized box holding a **cloned Arc
handle**; cloning the `Arc` **bumps a refcount — it does NOT duplicate the provider**). So the per-invocation
cost is small (box + one retained Arc strong-count), but it is **cumulative and unreclaimed** over the process
lifetime (grows with processed handshake frames incl. rejected attempts), and it keeps the shared provider's
strong-count from ever reaching zero. **Not dismissed because a comment documents it**; its consequence
(slow cumulative small-allocation retention) is bounded per-invocation and **unexecuted** at runtime.

## A13.6 A12.1 qualifications folded into this ledger
- "Optional without a certificate" **includes v2 with an empty certificate** (`handshake.rs:1103` requires
  `version>=v2 && !client_cert.is_empty()`; an empty cert falls to the no-cert branch) — not reducible to
  "Optional-v1."
- Certificate rejection is **not universally cheap**: suite/parse checks and (when roots are configured) a
  real ML-DSA **signature verification** precede decapsulation (`parse_and_verify_client_cert`), so some
  rejected inputs still pay signature-verify cost before the (avoided) decaps.
- A **blocking-worker limit** (tokio `max_blocking_threads`) does **not** establish a **queue-length cap**;
  the exact numeric default is omitted (pinned tokio 1.49.0, bare `#[tokio::main]`, not vendored/verified).
- **Failure to configure a timeout does not establish the effective socket setting**: the handshake path
  `.ok()`-ignores config errors (effective timeout then uncertain); the established path **propagates** the
  error (`secure_channel.rs:621`). Stated precisely, not assumed.
- **Box::leak** per §A13.5 (per-invocation small box incl. rejected attempts; cumulative; Arc clone ≠ provider
  duplication; separately tracked, no ID yet).

## A13.7 Evidence, test coverage, remaining obligations
- **A5-F1:** mechanism/caller path per §A13.2. Config: established session on any P2P node (not LocalMesh).
  Attacker capability: a connected peer that stalls mid-frame (or a lossy link). First rejecting boundary:
  none on the partial cases (retry resumes); teardown only when a misframed frame later fails AEAD. Consequence:
  connection-local desync→teardown; **no** cross-peer/consensus effect. Tests inspected (not run):
  `net_session_tests.rs`/`full_channel_roundtrip_tests.rs` cover success/roundtrip; **no mid-frame-timeout /
  desync assertion**. Runtime: UNEXECUTED.
- **A11-F2:** per §A13.3. Config: established session; the WouldBlock branch is platform-conditional. Attacker:
  a slow/backpressuring receiver (or a link inducing partial writes). Consequence: connection-local
  counter-advance + wire-desync→teardown; **not** nonce reuse (A11-F1). Tests: roundtrip tests only; no
  partial-write-retry assertion. Runtime: UNEXECUTED; platform mapping left conditional.
- **A6-F1:** per §A13.4. Config: a P2P node accepting repeat connections from a repeatable NodeId. Attacker:
  reconnect under the same NodeId leaving the old socket open+silent. Consequence: cumulative connection-local
  retention (lingering displaced read-side). Tests: eviction/roundtrip tests exist; **no** same-NodeId
  replacement-cleanup assertion. Runtime: UNEXECUTED.
- Kept separate: connection-local disruption (A5-F1/A11-F2) · cumulative retention (A6-F1, Box::leak) ·
  authentication bypass (none claimed here) · consensus effects (none claimed here).

| **A4-F2** | **OPEN — INTEGRATION/ASSURANCE GAP (unchanged kind, corrected framing).** The **cookie** pre-gate is unwired (`cookie_config: None`), so no cookie challenge/retry is exercised on either production endpoint; distinct from the **cert** pre-gate, which *is* present under Required/Optional.
