## A12.1.2 Correction 1 — handshake ordering and crypto configuration
**[SUPERSEDED-A12]** "KEM decapsulation runs before any certificate gate and always runs." The actual order in
`handle_client_init_inner` (`qbind-net/src/handshake.rs:966-990`) is **`verify_client_cert_if_required` (:974-
975) THEN `kem.decaps` (:987-989)** — the inline comment states cert verification runs "BEFORE KEM
decapsulation to fail closed on invalid cert." The no-cookie production entry `handle_client_init`
(`:1235-1249`) delegates straight to `handle_client_init_inner`; `connection.rs:265-312` server arm calls
`handle_client_init` (`:286-288`).

| Mode (`verify_client_cert_if_required`, `:1079-1114`) | Order & earliest rejection (before decaps) | Reaches decaps? |
|---|---|---|
| **Disabled** (deployed default, A6.1) | `Ok((None,false,None))` — **no cert gate** (`:1084-1086`) | **Yes**, on the first ClientInit (no cheap pre-gate) |
| **Required** | `version<v2` → `UnsupportedProtocolVersion` (`:1090-1092`); empty cert → `ClientCertRequired` (`:1093-1095`); else `parse_and_verify_client_cert` → reject on parse / untrusted root / bad signature / expired / revoked — **all before decaps** | **Only** after a cert passes |
| **Optional + cert present (v2)** | `parse_and_verify_client_cert` → reject on invalid before decaps (`:1103-1107`) | Only after cert passes |
| **Optional + no cert (v1/empty)** | `Ok((None,false,None))` (`:1108-1110`) — no gate | **Yes** |

**Real vs test-grade:** on the production-honest `pqc_active` path the decaps is real ML-KEM-768 (expensive) and
`parse_and_verify_client_cert` is a real ML-DSA-44 verify; on the test-grade path `DummyKem` decaps is cheap and
`DummySig` verify is vacuous — so the "gate before an expensive op" analysis is meaningful only under
`pqc_active`. **Client PoP distinction preserved:** even a verified client cert (Required) proves signature +
validity, **not** possession of the cert's private key (A2-F1). **Net A4-F2 effect:** the missing pre-gate is
specifically the **cookie** one; under Required/Optional-with-cert the **cert** gate already rejects an
invalid/absent cert before decaps, so the ungated-decaps DoS surface is the deployed-default **Disabled** (and
Optional-v1), not a universal "decaps before any gate."

## A12.1.3 Correction 2 — resource lifetime and timeout bounds
Distinct resource classes (previously conflated):
| Class | Acquired at | Bounded by |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted socket (fd) | `listener.accept()` (`p2p_tcp.rs:986`) | OS fd/backlog; released on drop |
| Async task | `tokio::spawn` per socket (`:1032`) | none (unbounded per-socket spawn) |
| **Queued blocking closure** | `spawn_blocking` (`secure_channel.rs:1061`) **before** the closure runs | tokio `max_blocking_threads` (closures wait here **with no socket timeout yet**) |
| **Executing handshake** | inside the closure, after `configure_socket` (`:337`) | per-I/O 10 s read/write timeout **only here**, and only if `set_read_timeout` succeeded (`.ok()` ignores errors) |
| Established-session workers | `spawn_peer_handlers` read/write loops | eviction (`evict_all_sessions`) |

**[SUPERSEDED-A12]** "released at 10 seconds" (unconditional): the 10 s per-I/O timeout is set **inside the
blocking closure** (`configure_socket`, `secure_channel.rs:337`), so it does **not** bound time a closure spends
**queued** awaiting a blocking-pool thread, and because config errors are `.ok()`-ignored (`:199-203`) a failed
`set_read_timeout` leaves the executing read with **no** timeout (potential indefinite hang on a silent peer).
It is a per-read timeout, **not** an accept-to-release deadline. **[SUPERSEDED-A12]** the "~45-hour worst case
per connection": reframed as a **finite slow-progress illustration** (frame-size × per-read timeout, *only when
the timeout is in effect*), **not a proven per-connection deadline**; the **missing parameter** is any absolute
whole-handshake deadline.

**Limiter taxonomy (corrected, kept separate):** **arrival-rate** = optional Run-362 limiter (default off);
**occupancy** = **none** at the app layer (`connections_current` is a gauge, never a reject cap, `p2p_tcp.rs:
1196,1727`); **blocking-worker** = tokio `max_blocking_threads` — the runtime is bare `#[tokio::main]`
(`main.rs:2008`) with no explicit setting; **the numeric default is omitted here** (pinned tokio 1.49.0 source
not vendored/verified, per instruction), with the qualitative point that it bounds **concurrent executing
handshakes**, not accepted sockets or the queue; **OS** = fd/backlog. A limiter reached after handshake
completion cannot protect earlier handshake allocation; the only pre-decaps app check is the (default-off)
Run-362 admit.

**Allocation ownership — `Box::leak` (new precise note, no ID):** `Connection::handle_handshake_frame`
**`Box::leak(Box::new(self.crypto.clone()))`** on the server arm (`connection.rs:282-283`) and the client arm
(`:332-333`) **intentionally leaks** one `Arc<dyn CryptoProvider>` box per handshake frame processed (required
because `AeadSession` needs `'static`; see the struct-level doc). Therefore **socket/task cleanup ≠ release of
every allocation**: the leaked Arc box persists for the process lifetime, one per connection, unbounded across
many connections. Checked existing IDs: not covered distinctly by A4-F1/A21-F1/R7; recorded as a **bounded,
documented design artifact / report correction**, **not** minted as a new ID, and aggregate-memory is not
reopened.

## A12.1.4 Correction 3 — authentication at registration and cookie integration
**[SUPERSEDED-A12]** the resource table's blanket "authenticated: Yes" at registration. At the registration
point (`p2p_tcp.rs:1186-1210`), `consensus_origin` is `resolver.and_then(|f| f(&peer_init))` and is **`None`**
when no resolver is installed or the session did not authenticate (`:1191-1194`); the peer is then registered
regardless (`connections_current.fetch_add` `:1196`; `spawn_peer_handlers(..., consensus_origin)` `:1199-1210`).
**Corrected:** at registration the **transport AEAD session is established**, but the **consensus-authenticated
origin may be `None`**; under **Disabled** there is no verified client identity at all; under **Required/
Optional-with-cert** the client cert is verified (signature + validity) **without PoP** (A2-F1). "Established"
≠ "consensus-authenticated."

**Cookie integration, both production endpoints:**
- **Server dispatch:** production builds `ServerHandshakeConfig { cookie_config: None }` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:
  2180`) and the accepted path uses the no-cookie `handle_client_init` (`secure_channel.rs:352`); the server
  **never issues a `ServerCookie`**. Peer IP, cookie config and time are **not** propagated into any cookie
  verify on this path (the cookie verifier `handshake.rs:894-917` binds `client_ip`/time but is only reached
  via `handle_client_init_with_cookie`, which production never calls).
- **Client handling:** the production dialer (`ClientHandshake::start` / `handle_server_accept`) consumes a
  `ServerAccept`, not a `ServerCookie`; there is **no production client challenge/retry** loop wired, so even if
  the server issued a cookie challenge the dialer would not complete the exchange on this path.
- **Distinction:** this is **missing cookie ENFORCEMENT** (the cookie pre-gate is absent end-to-end), which is
  separate from **missing preceding validation** — the **cert** validation gate *is* present (§A12.1.2) under
  Required/Optional. **Setting `cookie_config` alone would not complete integration**: it also needs the client
  ServerCookie/retry exchange and the server-side peer-IP/time propagation. **Library vs production:**
  `m6_dos_cookie_protection_tests.rs` exercises the cookie library path (challenge→verify, IP/time binding);
  **no non-test production caller** wires it (grep). A4-F2 = integration/assurance gap, **not** a demonstrated
  exploitable cookie defect. (No tests executed.)

## A12.1.5 Correction 4 — A12-F1 scope preserved; privilege claim corrected
A12-F1 (NoV2 marker-verification bypass of the apply policy's required-v2 check) is **retained separately from
A23-F1** (K≠T binding), with its **present-drain-file** prerequisite and **UNRESOLVED severity**.
**[SUPERSEDED-A12]** any implication that controlling the drain scratch file (`<temp>/qbind-run153-drain-
scratch-<pid>/drain_candidate.bundle`) is necessarily a **lesser** privilege than modifying operator
configuration — whether writing that file is easier or harder than editing `--p2p-trust-bundle`/genesis/config
**depends on deployment filesystem permissions** (temp-dir ACLs, shared vs dedicated host, process uid), which
are not established here. Kept separately described (not folded into A12-F1): the missing file→staged-candidate
identity binding and the skipped local-leaf/issuer checks (`local_leaf_cert_bytes: None`). Also retained from
A11.1: `try_apply_staged_peer_candidate` takes `&mut dyn V2MarkerCoordinator` (`pqc_peer_candidate_apply.rs:
782-789`) — **no** implemented `None`-rejection branch; the corrected receive order (policy dispatch → inner
temp-file write/validation → attempted removal `pqc_trust_peer_candidate.rs:743` → outer marker checks →
staging/optional propagation); and `fp=…;seq=…` is candidate metadata (a fingerprint), **not** proof of v2
marker verification.

## A12.3 Accept → handshake → registration trace + resource/admission table
Selected binary (configured listening P2P node, not LocalMesh): `TcpKemTlsP2pService::spawn_accept_loop`
(`p2p_tcp.rs:963`) binds `TcpListener` (`:932`) → `listener.accept()` loop (`:986`) → optional Run-362 admit
check (`:999-1015`) → `tokio::spawn` per socket (`:1032`) → `set_nonblocking(false)` (`:1133`) →
`accept_kemtls_async_with_peer_init(std_stream, server_cfg)` (`:1140`) → `spawn_blocking(|| SecureChannel::
from_accepted_with_peer_init(stream, cfg))` (`secure_channel.rs:1055-1062`) → `configure_socket` (10 s I/O
timeouts, `:337`) → `read_handshake_packet` (ClientInit, ≤16 KiB cap, `:343`) → `handle_handshake_frame` →
**no-cookie** `handle_client_init` incl. **ML-KEM decaps** (`:352`) → `write_handshake_packet` (ServerAccept,
`:359`) → established → `connections_current.fetch_add` (`p2p_tcp.rs:1196`) → peer registration + read/write
loop spawn.

| Stage | Resources acquired | Peer authenticated? | Applicable bound | Enabled on selected binary? | Rejection/cancel + who releases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `listener.accept()` | OS socket (fd) | No | OS accept-queue/backlog + fd ulimit | OS only (no app `max_conn`) | OS refuses on fd exhaustion; fd released on drop |
| Run-362 admit check | read-lock | No | per-source connection **rate** | **default OFF** (`abuse_dos_runtime=None`) | if over-budget: `drop(stream)`, continue (`:1008-1015`) |
| `tokio::spawn` task | one async task | No | **none** (unbounded per-socket spawn) | n/a | task ends on handshake error/drop |
| `spawn_blocking` handshake | one **blocking-pool thread** for the whole handshake | No | tokio `max_blocking_threads` (runtime, not app) | tokio **1.49.0** default (documented ~512; not vendored/verified here; deployment may override) | thread released when handshake returns; excess handshakes **queue** (unbounded) |
| `read_handshake_packet` | ≤16 KiB buffer; **per-read 10 s** timeout | No | 16 KiB payload cap (`MAX_HANDSHAKE_PAYLOAD`); **no absolute deadline** | cap yes; deadline **no** | read timeout → `Err` → thread/socket released |
| `handle_client_init` | **ML-KEM-768 decapsulation** (CPU) + transcript/KDF | No (runs before any cert/cookie gate) | **no cookie precondition** (cookie unwired) | decaps always runs | failure → `Err`; thread/socket released |
| cert/KEM verification | ML-DSA verify (if mutual-auth) | becomes known here | per handshake | mode-dependent | `Err` → release |
| peer registration | peers-map entry + read/write tasks | Yes | — | — | eviction drops handles |

**First effective protection against many simultaneous unauthenticated connections:** on the selected binary
with defaults, **none at the application admission layer** — only (a) the **optional** Run-362 **rate** limiter
if enabled, then (b) the tokio **blocking-pool** thread cap (a *runtime* limit bounding concurrent in-progress
handshake threads, **not** a bound on accepted sockets or the blocking queue), then (c) **OS** fd/backlog
limits. A runtime thread limit is **not** an occupancy bound; accepted sockets and queued handshakes grow
unbounded. No limiter on this surface runs **before** the KEM decaps except the (default-off) Run-362 check.

## A12.4 Time and framing bounds (five cases)
Socket: blocking mode (`set_nonblocking(false)`), per-I/O `SO_RCVTIMEO`/`SO_SNDTIMEO` = 10 s (`.ok()`-ignored
errors); **no whole-handshake absolute deadline**; handshake payload ≤ 16 KiB (`read_handshake_packet`).
- **(1) No bytes sent:** `read_exact` of the 3-byte header blocks; first read times out at **10 s** → `Err` →
  thread/socket released. Bounded.
- **(2) Partial length/header:** sends <3 header bytes then stalls → next `read_exact` read times out at 10 s →
  `Err`. Bounded (~10 s hold).
- **(3) Slow but progressing bounded frame:** sends 1 byte just before each 10 s window across the ≤16 KiB
  payload → **finite** hold bounded by `payload_bytes × 10 s` (≤ ~16 384 × 10 s ≈ 45 h worst case **per
  connection**), each holding **one blocking-pool thread**. **Finite** (frame-size-bounded), **not infinite** —
  but there is **no absolute-deadline parameter** to cut it short (the missing parameter). Multiplied by the
  unbounded accepted-socket count → blocking-pool saturation pressure.
- **(4) Complete malformed frame:** decode error → `Err` quickly; released.
- **(5) Complete frame to cert/KEM:** ML-KEM decaps + (mutual-auth) ML-DSA verify run; on bad cert → `Err`;
  resources released.
**Resource-occupancy scenario (source-supported, UNEXECUTED):** many case-(3) connections each occupy a
blocking-pool thread for a long finite interval with trivial traffic, and nothing at the app layer caps their
count → the blocking pool fills and further handshakes queue (growth). **Rejection counterexample:** a
no-bytes (case 1) or stalled (case 2) connection is released at the 10 s per-read timeout. Concurrency, memory,
CPU and downstream-liveness effects kept separate; **no process-crash / consensus-halt / numeric-capacity claim
is made** (no evidence; unexecuted).

## A12.5 DoS-cookie end-to-end trace
- **Configuration / secret provisioning:** the production `ServerHandshakeConfig` is built with
  **`cookie_config: None`** (`p2p_node_builder.rs:2180`) — the only production construction. No cookie secret is
  provisioned on the listener.
- **Challenge generation/verification (library, unwired):** `ServerHandshake::handle_client_init_with_cookie`
  (`qbind-net/src/handshake.rs:847-891`) validates the cookie (bound to client IP + suite ids + client_random +
  validator_id + time) **before** `handle_client_init_inner`, so the **KEM decaps occurs only after** a valid
  cookie on that path. **Production does not call it** — the accepted path uses `handle_handshake_frame` →
  no-cookie `handle_client_init` (`secure_channel.rs:352`), so **decaps runs on the first ClientInit** with no
  challenge/retry.
- **Expensive-op ordering:** cookie-path = cookie-verify → (only then) decaps; production no-cookie path =
  decaps immediately. So the cookie, *if wired*, would gate the expensive op; it is **not wired**.
- **Client retry support:** `ServerHandshakeResponse::CookieChallenge` exists, but since the server never
  issues a challenge in production, no client challenge/retry exchange is exercised on the wired path.
- **Production callers vs test-only:** `handle_client_init_with_cookie` and `CookieConfig` appear only in
  `qbind-net` + tests (`m6_dos_cookie_protection_tests.rs`); **no non-test production caller** (grep).
**Classification:** an **integration/assurance gap** (A4-F2) — the mechanism is present and unit-tested but
unwired — **not** a demonstrated exploitable cookie defect. The existence of cookie types/tests does not imply
integration.

- **A4-F2 — integration gap:** cookie unwired (`cookie_config: None`); decaps ungated by a cookie. Execution:

- **A12-F1 — NoV2 bypass, severity unresolved:** source-confirmed; reachable only with the drain file present

- **Test coverage (read, not run):** `m6_dos_cookie_protection_tests.rs` exercises the cookie library path

- **Remaining verification obligations (open static / runtime):** the exact tokio 1.49.0 `max_blocking_threads`

## A11.1.2 Correction 1 — two distinct file paths
**[SUPERSEDED-A11]** "received bytes are not persisted to disk." The dispatcher **does** materialize the
received bytes to a **validation-scratch** temp file:
- `pqc_trust_peer_candidate.rs:708` → `write_scratch(ctx.scratch_dir, &envelope.bundle_bytes)`; `write_scratch`
  (`:885-912`) `create_dir_all`s `scratch_dir` if absent, builds
  `<ctx.scratch_dir>/qbind-run076-peer-candidate-<pid>-<nanos>-<rand_suffix>.json`, and `std::fs::write`s the
  bytes.
- `:726-739` validates that file via `validate_candidate_bundle_full[_with_ratification]`
  (`ReloadCheckInputs.candidate_path = &staged_path`).
- `:743` `let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&staged_path);` — **cleanup is best-effort; its result is ignored.**
  **Deletion is not guaranteed** (a crash/early-return between the `:708` write and the `:743` remove, or a
  failing `remove_file`, leaves the `qbind-run076-*.json` file on disk).

This is a **different path** from the drain's `<temp>/qbind-run153-drain-scratch-<pid>/drain_candidate.bundle`
(`main.rs:8235-8240`, where only the directory is `create_dir_all`'d). **No executable path connects them:**
the validation file lives under the dispatcher's `ctx.scratch_dir` with a per-submission randomized name and is
(best-effort) unlinked; nothing copies/renames/writes it to the drain's fixed `drain_candidate.bundle`. So the
**corrected** statement: received bytes are transiently written to a dispatcher validation temp file (cleanup
best-effort), **but no production path writes the validated bytes to the drain file the apply builder
requires.** The A11 handoff-missing conclusion stands; only the "no disk write at all" phrasing is corrected.

## A11.1.4 Correction 3 — negative result bounded to its filesystem assumptions
"No production write found" does **not** prove the pathname cannot already exist. Separate static cases:
- **(i) Drain file ABSENT, eligible candidate selected (the production state):** `build_for` → `precheck` →
  `if !candidate_path.exists() { Err("missing candidate bundle material …") }` (`pqc_peer_candidate_drain.rs:
  898-903`). **Rejection here; no apply.** This is the state the selected binary produces.
- **(ii) Drain file PRESENT (requires an out-of-band writer):** `precheck`'s remaining checks run
  (`signature_verified`, fingerprint/prefix well-formed, freshness, env/chain, optional
  `require_v2_marker_digest`), then `build_for` passes `ReloadCheckInputs{candidate_path, local_leaf_cert_bytes:
  None}` into Run-070 apply. **`build_for` does not re-load the staged bytes nor enforce any file↔staged
  fingerprint/sequence/content equality** — whatever bundle is at the path is validated on its own. The apply
  then proceeds per §A11.1.6. **Capability/prerequisite:** some process must have written a well-formed signed
  bundle to that exact `drain_candidate.bundle` path — i.e. **local filesystem write access to the per-pid
  scratch dir**. A **network sender cannot create it**; and **not every filesystem writer is an authorized
  operator** (e.g. another local process, a shared-tmp race). This is not assumed to exist at HEAD.
- **(iii) Unresolved caller/path case:** no production component writes the file (§A11.1.3). The only residual
  is a future wiring or an out-of-band writer (§A11.1.8) — named, not assumed.

**Strongest scoped conclusion:** *On the selected binary at HEAD, with staging+apply+drain-once armed, the
`0x05` route stages validated metadata and (separately) propagates, but the drain's apply **cannot proceed**
because no production code writes `drain_candidate.bundle`; the first rejection is the `precheck` missing-file
check. Root installation via this route requires an additional, unestablished **local filesystem write** of the
drain file — outside any network or armed-operator capability traced here.*

## A11.1.5 Correction 4 — configuration and pre-staging authorization matrix
**Required flag added:** staging also requires `--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-wire-validation-enabled`;
`main.rs:3767-3776` FATAL-exits if `--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-staging-enabled` is set without it. So the
armed DevNet/TestNet config needs **four** flags: `…-wire-validation-enabled` (receipt/validation) +
`…-staging-enabled` + `…-apply-enabled` + `…-drain-once` (plus `PqcStaticRoot`, `--p2p-trust-bundle`,
`--data-dir`). **[SUPERSEDED-A11]** the three-flag list.

**Ingress order (receive side, validation/propagation only):** envelope decode + declared-length/limit checks →
`write_scratch` (temp file) → Run-069 bundle validation (signature vs configured signing keys, env/chain,
activation, sequence) **+ ratification when a ratification ctx is present** (`pqc_trust_peer_candidate.rs:736-
739`) → policy-selected ordinary/v1/v2 dispatch (`pqc_peer_candidate_wire.rs:1569-1589`) with v2/v1 **marker
checks before staging** (`:1602-1623`) → best-effort temp-file removal → staging (**only `Validated` outcomes**
enter the queue, `pqc_peer_candidate_staging.rs:613-624`) → propagation (only under its own enablement +
rate/dup eligibility).

**`signature_verified` provenance corrected.** **[SUPERSEDED-A11]** "rejected input is staged with
`signature_verified=false` and filtered." Malformed/invalidly-signed input is **Rejected** and **never
staged** (only `Validated` outcomes reach the queue, `pqc_peer_candidate_staging.rs:613-624`). The
`signature_verified` flag on a staged candidate records what the upstream validator reported for the candidate
(and the staging doc notes the queue does **not** itself verify ratification); the apply controller treats
`!signature_verified` as "impossible under Run-142 invariants, checked defensively" (`pqc_peer_candidate_apply.rs:
847-854`). An **unsigned bundle accepted under an applicable policy** is distinct from a rejected one — it would
be `Validated` under that policy and staged; a malformed/bad-signature bundle is neither.

Kept separate: **transport admission** (established KEMTLS session) · **consensus binding** (Run-418 gate —
**does not guard the `0x05` route**) · **bundle-signature validity** (vs configured signing keys, pre-stage) ·
**ratification** (receive-side marker checks `:1602-1623`; drain-side coordinator §A11.1.6) · **root-install
authority** (only via the unreachable drain apply).

## A11.1.6 Correction 5 — NoV2 fallback executable behavior; five separate mechanisms
- **Policy:** `PeerDrivenApplyPolicy::default` sets `require_v2_ratification=true` and `require_staged_candidate
  =true` (`pqc_peer_candidate_apply.rs:157-165`); `devnet_enabled()`/`testnet_enabled()` **inherit** both
  (`:175-197`). (The module-level default policy is "disabled on every environment"; the enabled constructors
  are what the armed path uses.)
- **NoV2 coordinator is a no-op bypass, not fail-closed:** `NoV2MarkerCoordinator::decide_pre_apply` and
  `persist_after_commit` both `return Ok(())` (`:267-273`). The controller gates the marker **solely through
  the coordinator**: `if policy.require_v2_ratification { if let Err(reason)=marker_coordinator.decide_pre_apply()
  {return CandidateMarkerConflict} }` (`:872-875`) and the post-commit persist likewise (`:904-910`). The
  doc-comment (`:258-263`) claims production "fails closed via `ApplyRejected`" when a NoV2 is used under
  `require_v2_ratification=true` — **but that fail-closed is for passing `None`; `main.rs:8341-8370` installs a
  concrete `NoV2MarkerCoordinator` instance** on v2-verify-failure / missing-v2-material / reload-context
  build-failure, so the controller calls its `Ok(())` no-op and the v2 marker discipline is **vacuously
  bypassed** despite the flag. **Reconciliation: executable behavior contradicts the fail-closed comment on
  this drain-once path** (gated behind the missing drain file).
- **`authority_marker_digest` provenance is weak:** the dispatcher sets it to `Some("fp={fingerprint_hex};seq=
  {sequence}")` for a `Validated` outcome, else `None` (`pqc_peer_candidate_wire.rs:1997-2002`) — a **non-
  cryptographic** fingerprint+sequence string (the comment says a future Run-147 wiring "may substitute the
  persisted authority-marker file digest"). The builder's `require_v2_marker_digest && staged.authority_marker
  _digest.is_none()` check (`pqc_peer_candidate_drain.rs:949-955`) therefore proves only that the candidate was
  `Validated` (has a `fp;seq` string), **not** that any v2 authority marker was cryptographically verified.
- **Branch coexistence:** the receive side performs v1/v2 marker checks **before** staging (`pqc_peer_candidate_
  wire.rs:1602-1623`); the drain-time NoV2 fallback is selected independently at coordinator construction
  (`main.rs:8341-8370`). A candidate can thus be staged after passing a receive-time marker check yet reach a
  drain whose coordinator is NoV2 (e.g. the v2 sidecar is absent/unverifiable **at drain time**), so the
  drain-time marker gate is bypassed. Do not combine incompatible assumptions: a candidate rejected at receive
  time is never staged, so only receive-accepted candidates reach the drain.

**Five mechanisms kept separate (no shared-root-cause claim; no grouping under one ID):**
1. **Missing received-bytes→drain-file handoff** (§A11.1.2) — the operative blocker at HEAD.
2. **Missing file→staged-candidate identity binding** — `build_for` never checks the file equals the staged
   candidate (§A11.1.4).
3. **Absent local-leaf/issuer inputs** — drain passes `local_leaf_cert_bytes: None`, so
   `validate_candidate_bundle_full`'s local self-checks are skipped (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:533`).
4. **NoV2 verification/marker bypass** — this section.
5. **A23-F1 signer K vs target T binding** — not enforced on the plain (non-ratification) apply used here.

**Bounded trace — REJECTION (production state) / CONDITIONAL ACCEPTANCE (present file):**
- *Rejection (file absent):* receive→validate→stage (metadata) → drain selects → `precheck` missing-file Err
  → **no apply.** (The only state the selected binary reaches.)
- *Conditional acceptance (file present, requires out-of-band local write):* `precheck` passes →
  `require_v2_ratification=true` but coordinator = NoV2 ⇒ `decide_pre_apply()=Ok` (marker gate vacuous) →
  Run-070 `apply_validated_candidate_with_previous` validates the **file** (signature/env/chain/activation/
  sequence; **local-leaf/issuer skipped**, **no K↔T**) → swap → evict → sequence commit →
  `persist_after_commit()=Ok` (NoV2) → **roots installed.** Furthest effect **supported only under the explicit
  local-filesystem-write assumption**; **UNEXECUTED**; not reachable by a network sender or by the armed flags
  alone.

## A11.0 Disposition (A11)
| ID | A11 disposition |
|---|---|
| **A31-F1** | Unchanged (A10.1 two-root construction retained). A11 **resolves the A10/A9.1 residual** "operator-armed `0x05` drain can install roots / K↔T unresolved": the armed drain-once path is **blocked at a missing production file handoff** (§A11.3), so `0x05` root installation is **not source-reachable in the selected binary**, even fully armed. |
| **A23-F1** | Unchanged; its signer-to-ratification-binding gap and skipped-verifier branch remain separately described. The `0x05` apply route does **not** reach root installation, so it does not add a new A23-F1 instance. |
| **(no new ID minted)** | The `0x05` staging→drain→apply route is **not reachable** for root installation (negative result). Two **latent, local-operator-gated** observations (§A11.5) are recorded without an ID because a network sender cannot reach them (blocked at the file handoff); they are not hidden under another finding. |
| **all others** | Latest accepted dispositions retained; not reopened. |

## A11.2 Carried-forward corrections / distinctions
- **A10.1.7 retry wording corrected (again, precisely):** 8 dial attempts permit **at most 7 sleeps totaling
  4.5 s** of backoff (`100+200+400+800+1000+1000+1000` ms), **excluding** per-attempt TCP-connect/KEMTLS-
  handshake duration and scheduler delay. This is **not an end-to-end deadline** and **not a bound on an
  established session's lifetime** (a succeeded dial returns from the retry loop and lives until eviction/drop).
- Retained unresolved distinctions: **operator arming is a configuration prerequisite**, which does **not**
  establish that an attacker needs local access; **A23-F1's missing signer↔ratification binding and skipped-
  verifier branch stay separately described**; **receiving, validating, staging, selecting and installing a
  candidate are distinct events** (the A11 data flow makes this concrete).

## A11.3 Candidate data-flow through the selected binary
Live inbound `0x05` path = `LivePeerCandidateWireDispatcher` (validation/propagation only), with
`local_leaf_cert_bytes: None` on the receiver (`main.rs:7783-7824`). Armed drain-once block: `main.rs:8178-8258`
(+ invocation `:8425-8434`).

| Object | Producer | Who controls contents | Validation | Consumer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Received bundle bytes** | network sender over an established KEMTLS session | the sender | Run-069 loader validates signature (vs configured signing keys), env/chain/activation/sequence **before staging** | held in memory as `bundle_bytes` (`pqc_peer_candidate_wire.rs:277,302`); **not persisted to disk** |
| **Full fingerprint / sequence** | derived from the validated bytes | — | self-consistency | recorded in staged metadata |
| **Staged metadata (`StagedPeerCandidate`)** | staging queue (`pqc_peer_candidate_staging.rs:294-323`) | derived | metadata-only: `fingerprint_prefix/hex`, `sequence`, `environment`, `chain_id_hex`, `staged_at`, `authority_marker_digest`, **`signature_verified`** | the drain selector (filters `signature_verified==false`) |
| **`signature_verified`** | recorded from upstream `ValidatedPeerCandidate` | — | staging does **not** itself verify ratification | drain precheck (defence-in-depth) |
| **File loaded by apply pipeline** | `ProductionDrainInvocationBuilder.candidate_path = <temp>/qbind-run153-drain-scratch-<pid>/drain_candidate.bundle` (`main.rs:8235-8240`); only the **directory** is `create_dir_all`'d | nobody writes the file | `precheck` requires it to **exist** (`pqc_peer_candidate_drain.rs:898-903`) | `ReloadCheckInputs.candidate_path` → Run-070 apply |
| **Candidate signing key K** | the file's bundle signature (if loaded) | — | `validate_candidate_bundle_full` vs configured signing keys | not reached (no file) |
| **Ratification target T / authority** | v2 sidecar via `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2` in the marker coordinator (`main.rs:8266-8340`) | operator sidecar | authenticity only (no K↔T, per A9/A23-F1) | marker coordinator |
| **Roots installed** | Run-070 apply → `LivePqcTrustState` swap | — | — | **not reached** |

**The decisive handoff is MISSING.** The staging queue holds **metadata only** (no bundle bytes;
`StagedPeerCandidate` has no byte field) and `try_drain_once_shared` is documented as "**no disk persistence**"
(`pqc_peer_candidate_drain.rs:988-998`). The drain-once block creates only the scratch **directory**
(`main.rs:8239`), never the `drain_candidate.bundle` **file**, and the dispatcher performs no `fs::write` of the
received bytes to that path (its own `scratch_dir` is a different field and is not written with the candidate on
this path). `ProductionDrainInvocationBuilder::build_for` → `precheck` (`:964-985`, `:896-903`) therefore hits
`if !self.candidate_path.exists() { return Err("missing candidate bundle material at …") }` **first** and the
drain stops. **`build_for` also does not re-load the staged bytes nor enforce any file↔staged
fingerprint/sequence/content equality** — it merely passes the (non-existent) path into `ReloadCheckInputs`.

## A11.4 Configuration / capability matrix
| Config | Flags / prerequisites | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Default (disabled)** | none set | no `0x05` receipt/staging/drain; route inert |
| **Armed DevNet** | `--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-staging-enabled` (Run 147) + `…-apply-enabled` (Run 149) + `…-drain-once` (Run 151/153); `PqcStaticRoot`; `--p2p-trust-bundle` baseline; `--data-dir`; `QBIND_DRAIN_ONCE_DELAY_SECS` (default 10) | one-shot delayed drain after receipt/stage; **blocked at the missing-file precheck** (§A11.3) → no apply |
| **Armed TestNet** | same flags; `testnet_enabled()` policies | same as DevNet (staging/drain policies enabled); same missing-file block |
| **MainNet** | any of the three flags | **FATAL `exit(1)` unconditionally** at staging (`main.rs:7958-7969`), apply (Run 149), and drain (Run 151/153 + defensive guard `main.rs:8388-8394`) |

The delayed **one-shot** drain (`--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-drain-once`) is distinct from **automatic
apply on receipt** (does not exist — receipt is validation/propagation only) and from any **recurring background
drain** (does not exist). **Checks on raw `0x05` ingress:** transport admission (an established KEMTLS session);
the Run-069 loader validates the candidate **signature** (vs configured signing keys) + env/chain/activation/
sequence before staging; staging and propagation are **non-mutating** (never install roots). **Ordinary
consensus-message authorization (the Run-418 binding gate) does not guard this route** — it is a separate wire
discriminator; the `0x05` route's only pre-stage gate is the bundle-signature/env/chain validation, and its
only apply gate is the (unreachable) drain pipeline.

**Capabilities:**
| Capability | Reaches root install? |
|---|---|
| Network sender, **no** valid candidate | staged `signature_verified=false` → filtered by the drain selector; never selected |
| Network sender with an **already valid signed** candidate | staged `signature_verified=true` → selected → **drain precheck fails (missing file)** → not applied. (Delivering signed bytes does **not** imply holding the signing private key.) |
| Holder of a **configured bundle-signing key** | can mint fresh valid candidates → same outcome (blocked at file handoff) |
| **Local operator** controlling files | could write `drain_candidate.bundle` out-of-band → the apply pipeline would then run (§A11.5) — this is **local filesystem access**, not a network-sender capability, and is not assumed here |

## A11.5 Authority checks at the apply boundary + the ordered REJECTION trace
Because the drain-once path never reaches the apply boundary (file missing), the following are the checks that
**would** run only if the file existed — recorded for completeness and bounded as **local-operator-gated**:
- **Ratification / marker:** the marker coordinator runs `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2` when a v2
  sidecar is present (`main.rs:8274-8340`; default governance-proof `NotRequired`); **no K↔T comparison** (as
  A9/A23-F1). With no sidecar → `NoV2MarkerCoordinator`.
- **Local-leaf / local-issuer revocation self-checks are SKIPPED:** the production drain passes
  `local_leaf_cert_bytes: None` (`main.rs:8256`), so `validate_candidate_bundle_full`'s `if let Some(local_leaf
  _bytes)` guard (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:533`) is false — the A10.1 local-issuer-root rejection does **not**
  protect this route. **(Latent observation #1 — gated behind the missing file + local FS access.)**
- **No file↔staged equality:** `build_for` enforces no content/fingerprint/sequence equality between the
  selected staged candidate and the file at `candidate_path`. **(Latent observation #2 — same gating.)**
- Candidate signature / env / chain / activation / sequence **are** re-checked by `validate_candidate_bundle_
  full` on whatever file is loaded; swap→evict→sequence→marker ordering is the Run-070/073 pipeline (A10).

**Ordered trace (REJECTION; DevNet, all three flags armed, a valid signed candidate delivered and staged):**
1. `0x05` frame received over an established session → Run-069 validation PASS → staged with
   `signature_verified=true` (metadata only; **bytes not persisted**).
2. After the delay, drain-once fires: builds `ProductionDrainInvocationBuilder{candidate_path=<scratch>/
   drain_candidate.bundle, local_leaf_cert_bytes=None}` (`main.rs:8248-8262`); only the directory exists.
3. `try_drain_once_shared` selects the staged candidate (`signature_verified` filter PASS) and calls
   `build_for` → `precheck` (`pqc_peer_candidate_drain.rs:968,896`).
4. **FIRST failed operation:** `self.candidate_path.exists()` is **false** → `Err("missing candidate bundle
   material at …/drain_candidate.bundle")` (`:898-903`). The drain returns without entering the Run-070 apply;
   **no swap, no eviction, no sequence/marker write, no root installation.**

**Furthest effect supported by source:** a received `0x05` candidate is **validated and staged as metadata**
and (separately) **propagated**; **it is never applied and no roots are installed** on the selected binary,
even with staging+apply+drain-once all armed, because the staged bytes are never materialized to the file the
apply builder requires. Completing an acceptance trace would require an **out-of-band write** of
`drain_candidate.bundle` (local filesystem access) — **not** granted by any network-sender capability and
**not** assumed here. Missing step named: the production write of the selected staged candidate's bytes to
`ProductionDrainInvocationBuilder.candidate_path`.

## A10.1.0 Disposition (A10.1)
| ID | A10.1 disposition |
|---|---|
| **A31-F1** | **OPEN — RETAINED.** The stale outbound-root mechanism (outbound dialer verifies against the startup-baked `peer_root_network_pk`, never the live snapshot) is unchanged and independently supported. **Corrections:** (a) A10's single-root witness is **rejected** by a local-issuer self-check before the swap (§A10.1.2) — **[SUPERSEDED-A10 §A10.6]**; (b) a **two-root `[R,L]`** configuration is a jointly-satisfiable replacement witness (§A10.1.3); (c) the exposed party must **possess the pinned peer KEM private key** — public cert possession is insufficient, and neither A2-F1 nor A11-F1 fills this (§A10.1.4); (d) retry window recomputed to **≤7 sleeps ≤4.5 s** (§A10.1.5). Stable ID retained; distinct from A2-F1/A11-F1/A23-F1. |
| **all others** | Unchanged; not reopened. |

## A10.1.2 Rejected original (single-root) witness — superseded
`validate_candidate_bundle_full` runs, **before** the state-changing swap (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:992-994`), a
local-leaf self-check (`:533-541`) and a **local-issuer-root** self-check (`:546-551`) →
`pqc_trust_bundle::check_local_leaf_issuer_root_not_revoked` (`pqc_trust_bundle.rs:2056-2077`): if the **local
node's own leaf cert's `root_key_id`** is in the candidate's `revoked_root_ids`, it returns `IssuerRootRevoked`
and the reload fails (`ReloadCheckError::LocalIssuerRootRevoked`). The SIGHUP path wires this: the local leaf
bytes captured at `main.rs:7598-7600` flow through the controller (`:8603`/config `:9078`) into
`ReloadCheckInputs.local_leaf_cert_bytes` (`pqc_live_trust_reload.rs:873-897`), so `inputs.local_leaf_cert_bytes
= Some`. **Therefore A10 §A10.6's single-root case** (revoke the only root R, which also issued the local cert)
**is rejected at validation — `validate PASS → swap` is WITHDRAWN for that construction.** First rejection:
`check_local_leaf_issuer_root_not_revoked` (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:546-551`). This does **not** close A31-F1; it
only invalidates that particular witness.

## A10.1.3 Replacement witness — two roots `[R, L]` (jointly satisfiable)
**Minimal configuration (DevNet, `PqcStaticRoot`, mutual-auth `Required` or `Optional`, real ML-DSA-44):**
- Trusted transport roots in order **`[R, L]`**, distinct `root_key_id`s and distinct ML-DSA-44 key bytes.
  (Order is load-bearing: the outbound baked root is `trusted_roots.first()` = **R**, `p2p_node_builder.rs:1955-1963`.)
- **Local** node's leaf cert issued by **L** (`root_key_id = L`). Startup check
  `verify_cert_with_configured_root` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:629-638`) looks the root up **by the cert's
  `root_key_id`** (`cfg.lookup_root_pk(&cert.root_key_id)`), so it verifies the local cert against **L** and
  boots regardless of which root is first.
- Configured outbound **peer**'s server cert issued by **R**; the dialer's baked `peer_root_network_pk = R`
  (first) verifies it (`handshake.rs:441-467`); the per-peer `peer_kem_pk` pin is the peer's leaf KEM pk
  (`certified_peer_kem_pk_for_validator`, baked).
- Candidate bundle **revokes R, retains L** (R ∈ `revoked_root_ids`, L ∉). The bundle must pass its own
  signature (signed by a configured signing key), env/chain, Run-062 activation (the revocation must be
  **active**, not pending), sequence monotonicity, and the ratification/marker gates (A23-F1 domain — the
  bundle-signing key remains valid). These are assumed satisfied by a legitimate operator-signed revocation.

**Why validation now passes:** the local leaf's `root_key_id = L`; `revoked_root_ids = {R}`; `L ∉ {R}` ⇒
`check_local_leaf_issuer_root_not_revoked` → `Ok` (`pqc_trust_bundle.rs:2066`), and the local leaf's fingerprint
is not in `revoked_leaf_fingerprints` ⇒ local-leaf self-check `Ok`. Validation PASS ⇒ `swap_snapshot` installs
`revoked_root_ids = {R}` / `active_roots` without R (`pqc_live_trust_apply.rs:274`) ⇒ `evict_all_sessions`.

**Relevant root-byte equality (not identifier-only):** the baked `peer_root_network_pk` is **exactly**
`R.root_pk` (a clone of `trusted_roots.first().root_pk`, `:1961`), and the peer's cert chains to R (verified
against `R.root_pk`). So the bytes the surviving outbound verifier uses equal R's configured key bytes by
construction — the same single cloned value, not merely a matching id.

**Net:** post-swap, inbound `lookup_active_root_pk(R)` → `None` (reject new inbound peers chaining to R), but
the outbound dialer still verifies the peer's server cert against baked **R** (accept). The two-root witness
**supersedes** the single-root one and realizes the A10 §A10.4 asymmetry under a configuration that actually
boots and passes live-reload validation.

## A10.1.4 Event order and attacker prerequisites (two-root witness, in-flight dial)
Source-feasible ordering (NOT an executed schedule), state C (handshake already in flight to the R-issued peer
when the operator issues the SIGHUP revocation of R):
1. **Candidate validation** — local-issuer self-check: `L ∉ {R}` ⇒ PASS (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:546-551`).
2. **Trust swap** — `swap_snapshot(new)` with `revoked_root_ids = {R}` (`pqc_live_trust_apply.rs:274`).
3. **Peer-map drain + abort requests** — `evict_all_sessions` `std::mem::take`s `peers` and calls
   `read_handle.abort()`/`write_handle.abort()` + drops `tx`/`raw_tx` (`p2p_tcp.rs:1796-1821`). This is a
   **registry removal plus cooperative abort requests**; it does **not** itself prove the sockets are closed or
   the worker tasks have terminated (abort cancels at the next await point). The in-flight handshake is **not**
   in `peers`, so it is untouched.
4. **Sequence commit** (+ post-commit marker persist) — live reload reports success.
5. **Surviving dial's server-cert check** — the in-flight `connect_kemtls_async_with_server_identity`
   (`p2p_tcp.rs:1986`) holds the already-cloned `client_cfg` with baked `peer_root_network_pk = R`; verifies the
   peer's cert against R (`handshake.rs:444`) ⇒ **PASS** (revocation not consulted).
6. **Identity mapping** — Run-418 outbound mapping: verified `(node_id, validator_id)` == configured pair ⇒
   PASS (identity check, not revocation).
7. **Peer registration** — the completed connection is inserted into `peers` (`spawn_peer_handlers`), i.e.
   **after** the step-3 drain snapshot, so the new session registers post-eviction.
8. **First successful encrypted s2c receive** — requires the server to **decrypt/produce** AEAD traffic under
   the session keys, which exist only if the server **possesses the KEM private key** matching the baked
   `peer_kem_pk` pin (the dialer encapsulated to it; key confirmation lands at the first successful s2c AEAD
   open, per A6.1).

**Three distinct milestones kept separate:** (a) **certificate acceptance** (signature vs baked R, step 5);
(b) the implementation's **"established"** state + **authenticated-origin metadata** (steps 6-7); (c)
**cryptographic key confirmation** at the first successful s2c AEAD open (step 8). Only (c) proves a live
authenticated channel.

**Attacker capability:** producing valid encrypted traffic under the pinned peer KEM key requires **possession
of that KEM private key** — **public certificate possession alone is insufficient**, and this is **not**
supplied by A2-F1 (client-side cert presentation without PoP) or A11-F1 (replay). The exposed counterparty is
therefore the **holder of the revoked-root-chained server's KEM private key** — i.e. the very peer whose
transport root was just revoked (the canonical revocation target: a compromised/rotated root whose key-holder
the dialer must stop trusting but does not, for in-flight/retry-window dials).

**Inbound bound:** the inbound rejection applies only to root lookups performed **after** the swap; an inbound
handshake that already passed its root lookup before the swap is **not** retroactively revalidated (it is
instead torn down only if it reached an established session that eviction drained).

## A10.1.5 Lifecycle tightening (no scope expansion)
- **No automatic reconnection** — retained (caller inventory: dials spawned only by `start()` over
  `config.static_peers`, `p2p_tcp.rs:949-957`; `send_to` no-ops when the peer is absent, `:2116-2123`).
- **Retry = attempt-count limit, recomputed.** `DialRetryPolicy` default: `max_attempts=8`,
  `initial_backoff=100ms`, `multiplier=2`, `max_backoff=1000ms` (`p2p_tcp.rs:286-292`). The loop
  (`:2058-2103`) sleeps **between** attempts only on a **transient** TCP-connect error and only while
  `attempt < max_attempts`, so **8 attempts ⇒ at most 7 sleeps**: `100+200+400+800+1000+1000+1000 = 4500 ms`.
  **[SUPERSEDED-A10]** "~5.5 s / 8 sleeps" → **≤7 sleeps, ≤4.5 s of backoff** (plus per-attempt connect/handshake
  time). An **attempt-count limit** (8) is distinct from a **wall-clock deadline** (~4.5 s of backoff) and from
  the **lifetime of a session that succeeds** (unbounded until eviction/drop — a succeeded dial returns from the
  loop, `:2070`, and is not retry-bounded). Retry covers only the **initial** dial; nothing retries after a
  success or a drop.
- **Eviction wording.** `evict_all_sessions` performs **registry removal + `JoinHandle::abort()` requests +
  channel drops** (`p2p_tcp.rs:1796-1821`); describe it as such, **not** as observed socket closure or
  completed worker termination. In-progress handshakes and still-retrying initial dials are **not** cancelled.

| 5 | retry "~5.5 s", eviction "aborts loops" | retry **≤7 sleeps ≤4.5 s**; eviction = **abort requests**, not proven socket close (§A10.1.5) |

## A10.1.7 Disposition, config requirements, attacker capability, unexecuted consequence
- **Static evidence:** baked outbound root (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1955-1963,2165`; per-dial clone
  `p2p_tcp.rs:1953`; verify `handshake.rs:444`); live inbound resolver + swap (`pqc_live_trust_apply.rs:274`);
  pre-swap local-issuer self-check (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:546-551`); eviction scope (`p2p_tcp.rs:1796-1821`);
  retry (`:2058-2103,286-292`).
- **Configuration requirements:** DevNet `PqcStaticRoot`, mutual-auth `Required`/`Optional`, real ML-DSA-44;
  two transport roots `[R, L]` with R first; local leaf issued by L; outbound peer issued by R; an
  operator-signed candidate bundle revoking R (active) that passes signature/env/chain/sequence/ratification/
  marker.
- **Attacker capability:** the counterparty must possess the KEM private key matching the baked peer KEM pin
  (not borrowed from A2-F1/A11-F1); the operator performs the live revocation; an outbound dial to the R-issued
  peer must be in flight or in its ≤8-attempt/≤4.5 s initial-retry window at swap time (no restart).
- **Unexecuted consequence:** continued outbound establishment of an authenticated, key-confirmed transport
  session under a revoked transport root R for that bounded set of dials; **not self-perpetuating** (no
  auto-reconnect). Scheduling of which dials are in flight at swap time → **conditional; UNEXECUTED**.

## A10.2 Carried-forward reporting qualifications (bounded; A9/A9.1 not re-analyzed)
1. **A23-F1 — two conditions kept separate, classification left open.** (A) *verified-ratification K≠T* (v2
   verifier runs and passes, no K==T check) and (B) *skipped verifier* (DevNet `--data-dir`-unset early return
   before the verifier). These are **not asserted to share a root cause**. Branch (B) is **not** dismissed as
   harmless "legacy ergonomics" merely because it is DevNet — notably it is reachable **with enforcement
   explicitly enabled** (`--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-enforcement-enabled`) yet `--data-dir` unset; whether
   (B) is benign is **left unresolved** pending an invariant/causal analysis, not closed here.
2. **Peer-candidate armed route — operator arming ≠ local-access-only attacker.** The disabled-by-default
   staging/apply/drain path (A9.1 §7) requires operator arming as a *configuration* prerequisite; this does
   **not** itself establish that the *attacker* needs local access. The armed route's attacker-capability
   profile (who supplies the applied candidate, over which channel) remains **unresolved pending its complete
   trace** and is not claimed either way.
3. **"ACTIVATED/live trust set" shorthand corrected.** At the startup root-merge step, roots are **pushed into
   a `trusted_roots` preparation vector** (`main.rs:7181-7185`); they become part of a *live* trust set only
   when that vector is used to build/start the P2P service. Per A9.1's own mutation-order table, the merge is a
   **preparation** step, not an in-place mutation of an already-running node's trust state.

## A10.3 Revocation invariant and identities
**What a live transport-root revocation is intended to achieve** (derived security invariant, distinguished
from any documented contract): after revoking transport root R, (i) existing sessions authenticated under R are
evicted, and (ii) **subsequent handshakes — inbound and outbound — reject any peer whose certificate chains to
R**. Distinct revocation/eviction concerns kept separate: **bundle-signing-key** revocation (A23-F1 domain),
**transport-root** revocation (`revoked_root_ids`, this finding), **individual leaf-cert** revocation
(`revoked_leaf_fingerprints`), **session eviction** (`evict_all_sessions`), and **subsequent-handshake
acceptance** (the resolver / baked root).

**Root/key provenance table:**
| Value | Source / lifetime | Live? |
|---|---|---|
| Configured transport roots | `pqc_root_config.trusted_roots` (PqcStaticRoot); bundle `active_roots` | startup input |
| `root_network_pk` | `trusted_roots.first().root_pk.clone()` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1955-1963`) — **first-root selection** | **startup clone** |
| Outbound `peer_root_network_pk` | `ClientHandshakeConfig` (`:2165`); re-cloned per dial (`p2p_tcp.rs:1953`); verified at `handshake.rs:444` | **baked (not live)** |
| Inbound `local_root_network_pk` | `ServerHandshakeConfig` (`:2176`) — local cert binding material | baked |
| Inbound `trusted_client_roots` resolver | `live.lookup_active_root_pk` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:2036-2044`) | **live** |
| `LivePqcTrustState` snapshot | `Arc<RwLock<Arc<LivePqcTrustSnapshot>>>`; `active_roots`/`revoked_root_ids`/`revoked_leaf_fingerprints`; swapped by Run 073 apply (`pqc_live_trust_apply.rs:274`) | **live (swappable)** |
| `leaf_cert_revocations` (both sides) | live closure `live.is_leaf_revoked` **iff** startup snapshot had ≥1 active leaf revocation, else `None` forever (`p2p_node_builder.rs:2097-2158`) | **live-but-conditional** |
| Peer KEM-key pins | `certified_peer_kem_pk_for_validator` override map | baked |

**Concrete single-root config where the static baked entry and the live entry are the SAME root bytes:** DevNet
`PqcStaticRoot` with exactly one configured transport root **R**. Then `trusted_roots.first() = R` ⇒ baked
`peer_root_network_pk = R.root_pk`; `LivePqcTrustState` is initialized from the same bundle ⇒ `active_roots =
{R}`, so the live lookup for R's id returns the same `R.root_pk` bytes. (Matching `root_key_id` returns the
same bytes here because it is a single root; `lookup_active_root_pk` returns the stored `root_pk` for a matching
id — identical ids need not imply identical bytes in a multi-root/rotated config, so this concrete case fixes
the single-root shape.)

## A10.4 Inbound vs outbound trust-decision comparison (post-revocation of R)
| Step | Inbound (listener verifies dialer's client cert) | Outbound (dialer verifies listener's server cert) |
|---|---|---|
| Trust config captured | resolver closure holds `Arc<LivePqcTrustState>` (shared handle) | `ClientHandshakeConfig.peer_root_network_pk` cloned at build, re-cloned per dial |
| Root lookup reads live snapshot? | **Yes** — `live.lookup_active_root_pk(root_key_id)`; returns `None` for a revoked/removed root (`pqc_live_trust.rs:304-312`) | **No** — compares against baked `peer_root_network_pk` (`handshake.rs:441-467`) |
| Cert signature / validity / leaf-revocation | signature vs resolved root; Run 045 validity window; leaf-revocation via live closure (if installed) | signature vs baked root (`handshake.rs:444`); validity window; leaf-revocation via live closure (if installed) |
| Peer KEM-key pin / key confirmation | n/a (listener) | baked per-peer KEM pin; key confirmation at first s2c AEAD open (A6.1) |
| Identity binding / authorization | `verified_client_node_id` → Run-418 binding gate | `server_node_id` → Run-418 outbound mapping check |
| **First boundary after revoking R** | **REJECT** — `lookup_active_root_pk(R)=None` ⇒ `untrusted root`, new inbound handshake fails | **ACCEPT** — baked `peer_root_network_pk=R` still verifies the server cert; no rejection on the revoked root |

Do not read success from a signature check alone: the inbound rejection is because the live resolver yields no
root for R (not a signature failure); the outbound acceptance is a genuine signature verification against the
stale baked R. The Run-418 outbound mapping check is an **identity** check (verified pair == configured pair),
**not** a revocation check — it does not reject the revoked-root case.

## A10.5 Lifecycle and connection-state / cancellation table
SIGHUP live-reload (`pqc_live_trust_reload.rs`, Run 073 `ProductionLiveTrustApplyContext`): `validate →
swap_trust_state` (`swap_snapshot`, `pqc_live_trust_apply.rs:269-281`) `→ evict_sessions`
(`evict_all_sessions`, `:289-310`) `→ sequence commit → post-commit marker persist`; a partial eviction or swap
failure rolls back. Process-start reload-apply uses a **temporary adapter** and exits after its result (A9.1)
— kept separate from the running-node SIGHUP handle.

| Outbound connection state | Reachable at a live swap? | Cancelled by `evict_all_sessions`? | Uses baked root? |
|---|---|---|---|
| (A) Established session | yes | **Yes** — drained from `peers`, loops aborted (`p2p_tcp.rs:1796-1821`) | was authenticated under baked R in the past; torn down |
| (B) Initial outbound dial still retrying (bounded 8 attempts, ~5.5 s backoff `p2p_tcp.rs:286-292, 2058-2103`) | yes | **No** — eviction does not touch `dial_handles` (`:1776-1778`) | **Yes** — completes handshake on the next successful TCP connect using baked R |
| (C) Handshake already in progress | yes | **No** — not yet in `peers`; in-flight `connect_kemtls_async…` holds cloned cfg (`:1986`) | **Yes** — completes trusting baked R |
| (D) Genuinely new dial after revocation | **only via process/service (re)start** — no auto-reconnect; `send_to` no-ops if peer absent (`:2116-2123`); dials spawned only by `start()` over `config.static_peers` (`:949-957`) | n/a | a same-object `start()` re-dial uses baked R; a full restart re-reads the on-disk bundle (excludes R if persisted revoked) |

An eviction **count** does not prove in-progress handshakes were cancelled or sockets fully closed: states
(B)/(C) survive eviction by construction.

## A10.6 One bounded ordered trace (outbound ACCEPT of a revoked root; state C)
Config: DevNet single transport root **R** (§A10.3); a configured peer P whose server delegation cert chains
to R, leaf **not** individually revoked, other credentials valid; an outbound handshake to P already in flight.
1. Operator issues a live transport-root revocation of R via SIGHUP → `validate` PASS →
   `swap_snapshot(new)` where `new.revoked_root_ids ∋ R`, `new.active_roots ∌ R` (`pqc_live_trust_apply.rs:274`).
2. `evict_all_sessions` drains established `peers` and aborts their loops (`p2p_tcp.rs:1796-1821`) — the
   **in-flight handshake to P is not in `peers`**, so it is **not** aborted.
3. The in-flight dial’s `connect_kemtls_async_with_server_identity` (`p2p_tcp.rs:1986`) proceeds with the
   already-cloned `client_cfg` whose `peer_root_network_pk = R.root_pk` (baked).
4. Client-side server-cert verification: `verify_delegation_cert(crypto, server_cert, peer_root_network_pk=R)`
   (`handshake.rs:441-444`) — **signature verifies against R** → PASS; validity window PASS; leaf-revocation
   closure (if installed) does not list P's leaf → PASS; `validator_id` matches → PASS.
5. `server_node_id` derived; Run-418 outbound mapping check: verified pair == configured `vid@addr` pair → PASS
   (identity check, not revocation).
6. **Session established trusting a server cert chaining to the revoked root R.** The revocation did not reach
   this decision. *(Rejection counter-case: if instead a brand-new dial were attempted only after a full
   process restart that re-read the on-disk bundle with R persisted-revoked, `trusted_roots.first()` would no
   longer be R and the baked root would exclude it — but that is restart, not live revocation.)*
**Furthest boundary established by source:** an **established secure transport** under the revoked root (and the
authenticated outbound origin that follows). Consensus effects beyond that are gated by the independent Run-418
binding + per-message signature/freshness checks (A6.x) and are **not** claimed here. Scheduling-dependent
(which dials are in flight / in the retry window at swap time) → **conditional; UNEXECUTED**.

## A10.7 Disposition, preconditions, consequence, uncertainty
- **Disposition:** A31-F1 **present at HEAD** — outbound transport-root revocation does not propagate to the
  dialer's baked `peer_root_network_pk`; the live snapshot is consulted only inbound. Stable ID retained;
  distinct from A2-F1/A11-F1 and from A23-F1 (signing-key, not transport-root).
- **Preconditions:** a running node with a configured peer whose cert chains to the to-be-revoked transport
  root; an operator performing a **live** (SIGHUP) root revocation; an outbound dial to that peer **in flight
  or in its bounded initial-retry window** at the moment of the swap (no restart). The "attacker" is a server
  presenting a cert chaining to the now-revoked root; **no A2-F1 impersonation or A11-F1 replay is assumed.**
- **Bounded consequence:** continued establishment of an authenticated outbound transport session under a
  revoked transport root, for the bounded set of in-flight/retry-window dials; **no automatic reconnection**
  re-opens evicted sessions, so the exposure is not self-perpetuating within a single live reload. Mitigations
  the source suggests (not implemented): cancel `dial_handles` on eviction, or resolve the outbound root through
  `LivePqcTrustState`.
- **Remaining uncertainty:** multi-root / rotated configurations (only `trusted_roots.first()` is baked — a
  separate "first-root-only" limitation); whether any deployment runs with the leaf-revocation closure installed
  at startup (which would let a **leaf** revocation of the peer propagate outbound as a partial workaround);
  the exact scheduler timing of in-flight dials (UNEXECUTED).

  source (confirmed present). Stable ID retained; A2-F1/A11-F1/A23-F1 kept distinct; A33-F1/timeout/execution/

## A9.1.2 Corrected configuration / dispatch matrix
**[SUPERSEDED-A9]** "v2 dispatch depends only on sidecar presence." There are **two layers**:
1. **Outer gate** `ratification_gate_decision(env, operator_opt_in)` (`pqc_ratification_policy.rs:156-175`):
   Mainnet → `Invoke(MainnetDefaultStrict)`; Testnet → `Invoke(TestnetDefaultStrict)`; **DevNet →
   `Invoke(DevnetOperatorOptIn)` iff `--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-enforcement-enabled`, else
   `Skip(DevnetNoOperatorOptIn)`**. The gate body runs only `if should_invoke()` (startup `main.rs:6695`;
   reload-apply `:4498-4502`; SIGHUP `:8938-8943`). On DevNet-no-opt-in the **whole** gate (v1 and v2) is
   skipped — legacy unsigned/legacy-bundle path.
2. **Inside an invoked gate**, v1 vs v2 dispatch is on **v2-sidecar presence** (`ctx_data.ratification_v2.is_some()`).

| Env | opt-in flag | outer gate | sidecar present | effective path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mainnet | any | **Invoke** (Strict) | v2 | v2 preflight (K≠T gap applies; `--data-dir` required or FATAL) |
| Mainnet | any | Invoke | v1/none | v1 enforce (K↔T bound) / Missing→fail-closed |
| Testnet | any | **Invoke** (Strict) | v2 / v1 | as above (`--data-dir` required) |
| DevNet | set | **Invoke** | v2 | v2 preflight; if `--data-dir` unset → **verifier no-op** (§A9.1.3) |
| DevNet | set | Invoke | v1/none | v1 enforce / legacy |
| DevNet | unset | **Skip** | any | gate skipped (no ratification enforcement at all; legacy) |

**CLI spelling corrected:** the flag is singular and repeatable `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-key`
(`clap … ArgAction::Append`, `cli.rs:401-403`); the Rust field is plural `p2p_trust_bundle_signing_keys`
(`cli.rs:405`). **[SUPERSEDED-A9]** the plural flag spelling.

**Sidecar failure classes (not "every invalid sidecar fails closed"):** a sidecar is read by the versioned
dispatcher in `build_run_105_reload_check_context` (`main.rs:498+`). Distinguish: **parser/I/O** failure
(absent/unreadable/malformed JSON) → context build errors or no v2 object; **semantic** failure (schema/
env/chain/genesis/authority-root/target-consistency/lifecycle) → typed `RatificationV2Failure`; **cryptographic**
failure (authority signature) → `SignatureInvalid`. Semantic/crypto failures in an *invoked, data-dir-set* v2
preflight do fail closed (`std::process::exit(1)`, `main.rs:6794-6808`); but the **data-dir-unset** branch
(§A9.1.3) and the **DevNet-skip** branch return without ever reaching the verifier.

## A9.1.3 Missing binding vs skipped verifier (two distinct conditions)
- **(A) Verified-ratification K≠T** — the A23-F1 gap. Requires: outer gate invoked, v2 sidecar, **`--data-dir`
  set**. The v2 verifier RUNS and PASSES on an authentic ratification for target T; **no code compares T to the
  bundle's verifying key K**; roots install. First rejecting boundary exists only on the **v1** route
  (`RatifiesDifferentKey`).
- **(B) Skipped verifier** — the **data-dir-unset** DevNet branch. `preflight_run_136`/`_134` return `Ok(None)`
  **before** the verifier (`main.rs:1203-1210`, `:860-866`; SIGHUP `pqc_live_trust_reload.rs:1357-1365`). The
  v2 ratification signature is **never checked** on this branch. **Reachable only on DevNet** (TestNet/MainNet
  FATAL-reject `--p2p-trust-bundle` without `--data-dir` earlier). It does **not** require "an authentic
  ratification" (none is verified). It is a DevNet-only configuration no-op within the legacy ergonomics, **not**
  the K≠T binding gap and **not a distinct root cause** warranting a new ID; recorded under A23-F1's reachability.
Keep (A) and (B) separate; A9's single framing conflated them.

| Authority (`bundle_signing_authority_roots`) + expected genesis hash | `build_run_105_reload_check_context` loads the **external `--genesis-path`** file (`load_external_genesis`, `main.rs:473-485`), extracts `genesis_cfg.authority` (`:486-492`), recomputes `canonical_hash = compute_canonical_genesis_hash(...)` (`:494-495`) | **[SUPERSEDED-A9]** "uses boot-accepted GenesisAuthorityConfig." It is the authority/hash from the external genesis file at gate-build time. **Equality with the boot-accepted genesis/authority is not established in this code** (no located check). |

| `pqc_transport_roots` | the **TransportRootNotAllowed** branch (`bundle_signing_ratification.rs:674-691`, `:1859-1873`) consults **`GenesisAuthorityConfig.pqc_transport_roots`** (the authority's transport roots) | **[SUPERSEDED-A9]** "transport roots carried by the candidate bundle." ## A9.1.5 Complete jointly-satisfiable acceptance trace (Ratify, K≠T, startup v2)
**Config:** DevNet with `--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-enforcement-enabled` (so the gate is invoked),
`--data-dir` **set**, `--genesis-path` present (authority A, assumed == boot-accepted), signing-key set
**`S = {K}`** (a single configured `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-key`), default governance-proof policy
(`NotRequired`) and default governance-execution policy. **Authority records:** an authentic v2 ratification
signed by A naming target **T ∉ S, T ≠ K** (attacker holds the object, not A's private key). **Candidate:** a
trust bundle signed by **K** with active roots R, plus the v2 sidecar.

| # | Gate (file:line) | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | bundle schema/signature/domain/validity/activation — `TrustBundle::load_...with_signing_keys` (`main.rs:6589`) | PASS → `signature_status = Verified{K}`; active roots R filtered to in-window/not-revoked |
| 2 | outer policy — `ratification_gate_decision(DevNet, opt_in=true)` (`main.rs:6669-6673`) | `Invoke(DevnetOperatorOptIn)` → gate body runs (`:6695`) |
| 3 | versioned sidecar parse — `build_run_105_reload_check_context` (`:473-498`) | v2 object present → `dispatch_v2` (`:6746-6751`); v1 gate SKIPPED (`:6753-6758`) |
| 4 | `--data-dir` present (`:1203-1210`) | set → verifier NOT skipped |
| 5 | authority source + v2 verify — `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2` (`:1216`; verifier `bundle_signing_ratification.rs:1808-2058`): schema=2, env/chain/genesis(A's hash), authority-root A in `bundle_signing_authority_roots`, PK binding, target T self-consistent, **authority A signs the v2 digest** | PASS → `ratified_v2{public_key=T}` — **no K comparison, no S membership check for T** |
| 6 | lifecycle action = Ratify field checks (`:1994-2000`) | PASS |
| 7 | anti-rollback marker — `preflight_v2_marker_decision_with_governance_proof_load` (`main.rs:1264-1278`): candidate marker from **T** + authority metadata vs on-disk marker | PASS (fresh/higher sequence); compares nothing to K |
| 8 | governance-proof policy — default `NotRequired` (`pqc_governance_proof_surface.rs:151-178`) | no-op → PASS |
| 9 | Run 220 governance-execution — `consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome` (`main.rs:1297-1303`) with default (Disabled/absent carrier) | no short-circuit → PASS (present carrier may differ; not required here) |
| 10 | Run 055 sequence persistence — `check_and_update_sequence` (`main.rs:6921`) | PASS (persistent) |
| 11 | v2 authority-marker persistence — `persist_accepted_v2_marker_after_commit_boundary` (`:7067-7103`) | PASS (or FATAL on persist failure — §A9.1.6) |
| 12 | **root install** — `for r in &loaded.active_roots { trusted_roots.push(r) }` (`:7181-7185`) | **ACTIVATED** — roots R from the K-signed bundle enter the live trust set |

**No gate checks K == T, and T is never required to be in S.** On the **v1** route step 5 is
`enforce_bundle_signing_key_ratification` with `candidate_bundle_signing_public_key: &signing_pk_bytes`
(`main.rs:273-279`) → `RatifiesDifferentKey` (`bundle_signing_ratification.rs:1213`) = first rejecting check.
**[SUPERSEDED-A9]** "configured set must be a proper superset of {T}": **T need not be in S at all**; `S={K}`
with `K≠T` is sufficient. The trivial safe case `S={T}` (K==T by construction) is preserved but is **not** the
only safe alternative — a v1-route or a future explicit K==T binding also closes it.

## A9.1.6 Corrected activation / mutation-order
| Surface | Order of effects | On a late failure |
|---|---|---|
| **Startup v2** | v2 preflight (verify+marker decision) → Run 055 **sequence write** → **marker persist** (`main.rs:7067-7103`) → **root merge into `trusted_roots` vector** (`:7181-7185`) → P2P startup | **marker persist fail AFTER sequence advanced** → FATAL `exit(1)`: sequence **committed**, marker **stale-by-one** (re-derived next mutation), **no root merge, no P2P** (`:7087-7101`) |
| **Process-start reload-apply v2** | preflight → `apply_validated_candidate_with_previous` (non-ratification pipeline): in-memory **swap** in the reload adapter, `NoActiveSessionsEvictor`, sequence commit → post-commit marker persist; **process exits after the adapter result** | constructs `NoActiveSessionsEvictor` and **exits** — **not** a change to a running node's sessions |
| **SIGHUP live reload v2** | re-read sidecar → verify → snapshot/**shared trust-state swap** + session **eviction** + sequence commit → post-commit marker persist (`pqc_live_trust_reload.rs`) | swap/eviction/sequence may persist before a post-commit marker failure; rollback scope is the live-reload outcome, not a full revert |
Distinct state classes kept separate: (i) startup `trusted_roots` **vector** prep; (ii) reload-adapter **in-memory** swap (process exits after); (iii) running-node **shared trust-state** swap (SIGHUP only); (iv) persistent **sequence/marker**; (v) successful **P2P startup**. The missing element remains **K↔T**, not the ordering.

## A9.1.7 Bounded peer-candidate (0x05) exclusion
**[SUPERSEDED-A9]** "0x05 paths can never install roots." Correction:
- The **immediate 0x05 receive handler** is validation/propagation-only (never applies, never installs roots).
- A **disabled-by-default** peer-candidate **staging / apply / drain** machinery exists and is **refused on
  MainNet unconditionally** (Run 147 `--p2p-trust-bundle-peer-candidate-staging-enabled` `main.rs:2078-2091`;
  Run 149 `…-apply-enabled` `:2100-2114`; Run 151 `…-drain-once` `:2127-2141`). On **DevNet/TestNet** an
  operator who **explicitly arms** these flags enables `PeerDrivenApplyDrain::try_drain_once → Run 148
  try_apply_staged_peer_candidate → Run 070 apply` (`main.rs:3992-3993`), which **can** install roots.
- **First rejecting guard for a remote actor:** the staging/apply/drain flags are off by default and
  MainNet-refused; nothing applies a peer candidate without local operator arming on a non-MainNet node. **Not
  a remote exploit.** Whether the Run 148/070 apply pipeline binds K↔T (v1 enforce) or not (v2/non-ratification)
  on this armed DevNet/TestNet path is an **open residual** I did not fully trace. A9's blanket exclusion is
  replaced by: immediate handler never installs roots; operator-armed non-MainNet drain/apply can, with its
  K↔T enforcement unresolved.
