## A9.0 Current disposition table (A9)
| ID | A9 disposition | Reachability / first missing-or-rejecting boundary |
|---|---|---|
| **A23-F1** | **OPEN — CONFIRMED PRESENT at HEAD on the v2 trust-bundle activation surfaces** (was NYR@CB "not revalidated"). The candidate-signer↔ratification-target binding (K==T) is **enforced on the v1 route** (`bundle_signing_ratification.rs:1208-1218` `RatifiesDifferentKey`, via `enforce_bundle_signing_key_ratification`), but is **absent on every v2 root-installing surface**: startup Run 136, process-start reload-apply Run 134, SIGHUP live-reload Run 138. The v2 route verifies the bundle signature under a **configured** signing key K and authenticates a v2 ratification naming target T, but **never compares K to T**, and installs the bundle's roots regardless. Same root cause as historical A23-F1; **stable ID retained.** | **Local/operator surfaces, not remote.** Prereqs: ability to supply a candidate bundle + v2 sidecar (startup `--p2p-trust-bundle`, reload-apply, or SIGHUP), a bundle signed by **any one configured** `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-keys` key K, and an **authentic** v2 ratification for some T (does **not** require the authority private key). First rejecting boundary on the **v1** route: `RatifiesDifferentKey`. Runtime UNEXECUTED. The inbound `0x05` peer-candidate paths are **validation-only** (never install roots) — not a root-installing surface. |
| **A8-F1 / QBIND-A1-F002** | Unchanged and **kept distinct**: A8-F1 = native `GovernanceProgram` authorization (library path); QBIND-A1-F002 = offline `qbind-gov` approval counting. Neither is the trust-bundle signer-binding gap. |
| **A31-F1** | Unchanged — outbound static-root revocation propagation; **queued** for the next phase (does not change this result). |
| **A7-F1, A2-F1, A11-F1, A17-F1, A21-F1, A1-F1/F2/F3, A33-F1, A11-F2, QBIND-A1-F003/F004/F006, NYR@CB** | Latest accepted dispositions retained; not reopened. |

**No new ID minted** (same A23-F1 root cause). Report-only corrections (A9.6) mint nothing.

## A9.2 Identities and data flow (kept separate)
| Identity | Source at HEAD | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Configured bundle-signing key(s)** | `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-keys` (`cli.rs:405`) → `BundleSigningKeySet` (`main.rs:6460-6473`, required non-empty off-DevNet `:6504-6515`) | the set the loader will accept a bundle signature against |
| **K — key that actually verified the candidate bundle** | `TrustBundle::load_..._with_signing_keys_chain_id_and_activation` (`main.rs:6589-6594`) → `loaded.signature_status = Verified { signing_key_id }` (`main.rs:6186-6192`) | the concrete key that signed the accepted bundle |
| **T — target key named by the verified ratification** | v1 `RatifiedBundleSigningKey.public_key` (`bundle_signing_ratification.rs:602-828`); v2 `RatifiedBundleSigningKeyV2.public_key` (`:1808-2058`, field `target_bundle_signing_public_key`) | the key the authority *authorized* to sign bundles |
| **Genesis/governance authority** | `GenesisAuthorityConfig.bundle_signing_authority_roots` (ML-DSA-44); the ratification is authenticated by this authority's signature over the canonical v1/v2 digest (`:2044-2057`) | authorizes a ratification for T |
| **Transport roots carried by the candidate bundle** | `pqc_transport_roots` — **explicitly rejected** as a bundle-signing authority (`TransportRootNotAllowed`, `:674-691`, `:1859-1873`) | must not serve as signing authority (kept separate) |

Matching identifiers ≠ matching key material: both verifiers recompute fingerprints from key bytes
(`:657-663`, `:1906-1931`, `:1977-1984`) and bind fingerprint↔pk. **Valid ratification signature ≠ authorization
to activate a bundle signed by a different key** — that step is the K==T binding, present only on v1.

## A9.3 Ordered acceptance trace — one jointly-satisfiable K≠T case (v2 startup, Run 136)
**Initial configuration:** any environment (the v2 dispatch is independent of the ratified/unratified policy
flag); `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-keys` contains a key **K**; genesis authority block carries a
`bundle_signing_authority_root` **A** (ML-DSA-44) consistent with the runtime chain/env/genesis_hash;
`--data-dir` set (or unset on DevNet → marker preflight is a no-op).
**Authority records:** an **authentic** v2 ratification signed by **A** naming target **T ≠ K** (a key A
legitimately ratified at some point; the actor holds this ratification object but **not** A's private key).
**Candidate contents:** a trust bundle signed by **K** carrying active roots **R**, plus the v2 sidecar (the
authentic ratification for T).

| # | Gate (file:line) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | bundle signature vs configured keys — `TrustBundle::load_...with_signing_keys` (`main.rs:6589`) | PASS → `signature_status = Verified{K}` |
| 2 | dispatch — `ctx_data.ratification_v2.is_some()` (`main.rs:6746-6751`) | v2 selected ⇒ **v1 gate `apply_run_105_ratification_gate_at_startup` SKIPPED** (`:6753-6758`) |
| 3 | `preflight_run_136_v2_marker_decision_for_startup(env, chain_id, ctx_data, data_dir, now)` (`main.rs:6784-6789`) — note: **receives neither `&loaded` nor `&bundle_signing_keys`** | runs `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2` (schema/env/chain/genesis/authority-root/PK-binding/target self-consistency/authority signature) → `ratified_v2{public_key=T}` PASS — **no K comparison** |
| 4 | anti-rollback marker — `decide_marker_acceptance_v2` (candidate marker from **T** + authority metadata vs on-disk marker) | PASS (fresh/higher sequence); compares nothing to K |
| 5 | Run 055 sequence write — `check_and_update_sequence` (`main.rs:6921`) | PASS |
| 6 | **root install** — `for r in &loaded.active_roots { trusted_roots.push(r) }` (`main.rs:7181-7185`) | **ACTIVATED** — roots R from the K-signed bundle enter the live trust set |

**No gate checks K == T.** On the **v1** route the same inputs reach `enforce_bundle_signing_key_ratification`
with `candidate_bundle_signing_public_key: &signing_pk_bytes` (`main.rs:273-279`) → step 4
(`bundle_signing_ratification.rs:1213`) `ratified.public_key != candidate` ⇒ **`RatifiesDifferentKey`**,
FATAL, no root merge. **Honest bound:** the gap bites only when the configured signing-key set is a proper
superset of {T} (e.g. a rotated/retired-but-still-configured key, or multiple configured keys); if the only
configured key equals the ratified T, K==T holds trivially and there is no divergence. The consequence is that
the v2 ratification does **not** constrain *which* configured key signed the activated bundle — the authority's
binding of its blessing to a specific key is not enforced on v2. Source-established; runtime UNEXECUTED.

## A9.4 Activation-surface comparison (v2 vs v1)
| Surface | Entry point | Candidate signer (K) | Ratification target (T) | K==T check? | Policy/anti-rollback gates | Persistent mutations | Active-trust effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Startup `--p2p-trust-bundle` v2 (Run 136)** | `main.rs:6784` | `loaded.signature_status` (configured keys) | `verify_...v2` → `ratified_v2` | **NO** | v2 marker anti-rollback; sequence write | marker (post-commit), sequence record | roots merged `:7181-7185` |
| **Reload-apply v2 (Run 134)** | `main.rs:4519-4554` (`preflight_run_134…` → `apply_validated_candidate_with_previous`) | `validate_candidate_bundle_full` (configured keys) | `verify_...v2` (preflight) | **NO** | v2 marker; sequence | marker, sequence | live trust swap |
| **SIGHUP live-reload v2 (Run 138)** | `pqc_live_trust_reload.rs:923-1003` → `apply_validated_candidate_with_previous` | `validate_candidate_bundle_full` | `verify_...v2` | **NO** | v2 marker; sequence | marker, sequence | live trust swap |
| **v1 (all three surfaces)** | `enforce_bundle_signing_key_ratification` via `validate_candidate_bundle_full_with_ratification` (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:614-615`) | configured keys (K passed in) | v1 `verify_...` | **YES → `RatifiesDifferentKey`** | Run 105 policy (Strict/MainNet) | — | gated on K==T |
| **Peer-candidate `0x05` (v1/v2)** | `pqc_peer_candidate_wire.rs:1657/1813` | — | — | n/a | validation/propagation only | **none** | **never installs roots** (out of scope) |

Dispatch is **purely on v2-sidecar presence** (`ctx_data.ratification_v2.is_some()`); a malformed/invalid sidecar
**fails closed** (no v1 fallback): startup/reload-apply `std::process::exit(1)` on verifier failure
(`main.rs:6794-6808`, `:4533-4544`), SIGHUP → `LiveReloadOutcome::Invalid`. The v2 preflight runs **before** the
sequence write and the root merge; the apply pipeline reached on reload-apply/SIGHUP is the **non-ratification**
`validate_candidate_bundle_full` (`pqc_trust_reload.rs:993`) — it verifies the signature under K but calls **no**
ratification enforcer. **The missing element is the K↔T binding, not the mutation ordering.**

## A9.5 Attacker-capability bounding (item 5)
- **Unauthenticated remote actor:** cannot reach a root-installing surface (startup/reload-apply/SIGHUP are
  local/operator; peer-candidate `0x05` is validation-only). **Out.**
- **Party able to supply a candidate bundle/sidecar:** this is the operative capability — a local operator or
  anyone controlling the bundle file + v2 sidecar + data dir on a reload/SIGHUP surface.
- **Holder of an already-configured signing key K:** can sign a bundle the loader accepts. The gap lets such a
  bundle activate paired with a ratification for a **different** T.
- **Holder of the genesis/authority private key:** **not required** — only an *authentic* v2 ratification for
  T is needed; a legitimate ratification for T does **not** imply possession of A's key.
- **Actor able to replace genesis/authority files:** a strictly stronger capability, **not** assumed here and
  kept separate from candidate-key substitution.
**DevNet flags/defaults:** `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-keys` (non-empty required off-DevNet, `main.rs:6504-6515`);
v2 dispatch = v2 sidecar present; `--data-dir` required off-DevNet for the marker preflight (DevNet no-op);
the `--p2p-trust-bundle-allow-unratified-testnet-devnet` policy flag governs the **v1** enforcer only
(`main.rs:262-269`) and does not alter the v2 dispatch. **Authority source:** verification uses the runtime's
boot-accepted `GenesisAuthorityConfig` (`RatificationV2VerifierInputs.authority`), not a later file reload on
these surfaces; equality with the intended authority is enforced by the authority-root lookup + ML-DSA
signature, **but equality of K with the ratified T is not.** TestNet/MainNet differ only in the v1 Strict
policy and the non-empty-key/`--data-dir` requirements; this was not expanded into a deployment audit.

## A8.1.3 EVM authentication — corrected
`qbind_tx.rs:15-19` states execution *assumes* authentication ("Signature verification is handled by the
consensus layer, not execution; the execution engine does not verify signatures"). The revm wrapper confirms
no authentication occurs there:
- `validate_tx` (`revm_engine.rs:194-224`) checks **only** sender **nonce** (`:204`) and **balance for max
  cost** (`:212-222`). No signature.
- `build_revm_tx_env` (`:247-268`) sets `caller: qbind_addr_to_revm(&tx.from)` (`:255`) — the **supplied**
  `QbindTx.from` becomes the revm `TxEnv.caller` directly, unauthenticated.
- context/exec (`:153-180`): `SpecId::CANCUN` (`:160`), `ctx.build_mainnet()` (`:177`),
  `evm.transact_commit(revm_tx_env)` (`:180`).

**Actual upstream authenticator of `from`:** **unresolved on the inspected path.** No executable code that
authenticates `QbindTx.from` was found (no `QbindTransaction`→`QbindTx` conversion that verifies the ML-DSA
signature and derives `from`); the attribution to consensus exists only in comments. Because the EVM path is
not wired into the selected binary (§A8.1.5), this is a **latent obligation**, not a demonstrated flaw.

**Precompiles / classical crypto:** the wrapper selects CANCUN + `build_mainnet`, so the active precompile set
is whatever the **pinned revm version's mainnet CANCUN precompile table** installs. **I did not vendor the revm
source**, so the active precompile inventory (including whether `ecrecover`/secp256k1 is active) is **explicitly
unreviewed**. `revm`, `k256`, `secp256k1` appear in `Cargo.lock`, but **A8's claim that classical crypto is
"confined to EVM transaction authentication" is withdrawn** (the EVM does not authenticate txs here; the most
likely consumer is a precompile such as `ecrecover`, unconfirmed). **Compiled classical-crypto dependencies do
not, by themselves, establish any consensus or transport PQ-authentication weakness** (consensus = ML-DSA-44;
transport = ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-44).

constructed only in `tests/` — **library/simulation code never reached from the selected binary.**

**Conclusion:** the corrected caller graph establishes that **no transaction-execution component (wire-program,
ledger nonce/VmV0, or EVM) and no mempool is constructed or driven by the selected binary**; committed blocks
reach only epoch-transition logic. This is established by the constructor caller-inventory (every executor/
ledger/mempool constructor resolves to `#[cfg(test)]`/`tests/`), not merely by a missing symbol in `main.rs`.
**Residual (negative scope):** a line-by-line read of the full `run_p2p_node`/`run_local_mesh_node` bodies was
not performed; the conclusion rests on the dispatch/spawn/commit-consumer inspection plus the exhaustive
constructor inventory. It is therefore **strongly supported but not certified complete**; treat as established
for the inspected path, provisional pending that full body trace.

## A8.2 Three transaction types — input/decoder/auth/consumer/state (source-backed)
| Type | External input / decoder | Authentication | Admission | Consumer | State mutation / persistence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Wire `Transaction`** (`qbind-wire/src/tx.rs`) | carried as opaque `Vec<u8>` in `BlockProposal.txs`; decoded by `Transaction::decode` **only** at `qbind-node/src/lib.rs:2615` (`apply_block`) | `verify_transaction_auth` (`auth.rs:24`) — **A7-F1** (empty→Ok; sig-only) | — | `TxExecutor`→qbind-system `KeysetProgram`/`ValidatorProgram`/`GovernanceProgram` (`qbind-runtime/src/lib.rs:127-158`) | `ExecutionContext.store.put` into `AccountStore` (in-memory/RocksDB) — **A8-F1** governance mutations |
| **Ledger/EVM `QbindTransaction`** (`qbind-runtime/src/qbind_tx.rs`) | `QbindBlock.body.transactions`; built/consumed by the EVM engine | EVM tx auth inside `execute_block` (revm; classical ECDSA) | — | `apply_qbind_block` (`block_apply.rs:153`) → `ExecutionEngine::execute_block` (`revm_engine.rs`) | `EvmLedger`/`EvmStateStorage` (`evm_commit.rs:323`) |
| **EVM transaction** (revm internal) | inside a `QbindTransaction` body | secp256k1 ECDSA (revm) | — | revm `execute_block` (`execution_engine.rs`) | EVM account/storage state |
| **Decode→execute wiring in the selected binary** | — | — | — | **NONE** — see §A8.3 | committed blocks advance **consensus metadata only** |

## A8.3 Execution reachability in the selected binary (bounded trace)
Inspected startup path: `main()` → network-mode dispatch (`main.rs:5421-5445`: `NetworkMode::LocalMesh` →
`run_local_mesh_node`; `NetworkMode::P2p` → `run_p2p_node`) → `spawn_binary_consensus_loop(_with_io)`
(`main.rs:5590/8685`) → `run_binary_consensus_loop` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2778/2805`), which drives a
**`BasicHotStuffEngine<[u8;32]>`** (its only engine parameter; `:1515/1538/2778…`). The committed-block
handling in the loop updates `committed_height`, the progress struct, and epoch transition only
(`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3159-3182`) — **no executor call**.

- `VmV0RuntimeState` (`vm_v0_runtime.rs`) — the only "runtime" the binary opens — is a **snapshot-only state
  holder**: fields `snapshot_dir`/`max_snapshots`/`snapshot_in_progress`; methods `open_from_config`,
  `open_existing_from_config`, `state_dir`, `snapshot_dir`, `create_snapshot` (`:51-205`); module doc: "runtime
  state opener and snapshot trigger." **It has no execute/apply/commit-transactions method**, and `main.rs`
  passes it only to the node runners for snapshotting (`main.rs:5428/5440/5512/5584/8485/8555`).
- **No selected-binary caller** of the execution entry points (grep over `main.rs`/`binary_consensus_loop.rs`,
  non-test): `apply_block`, `BlockExecutor`, `TxExecutor`, `execute_block`, `EvmCommitProcessor`,
  `apply_committed_block`, `ExecutionAdapter`, `Node::new` → **all absent**.
- The non-test callers of the execution chain are **library/simulation**: `ExecutionAdapter`/
  `InMemoryExecutionAdapter` (`execution_adapter.rs`, only `pub use`-exported at `lib.rs:2234-2239`);
  `LedgerBridge::step_once` → `apply_committed_block` (`ledger_bridge.rs:132`) — but `LedgerBridge` wraps the
  simulation `NodeHotstuffHarness` and has **no non-test constructor** anywhere; `hotstuff_node_sim.rs:3156`
  (simulation); and `evm_commit.rs:539-588` (tests).

**Conclusion (scoped):** within the inspected startup path, **no transaction execution of any kind — native
qbind-system programs or EVM — is wired to committed blocks.** Externally-influenced wire `Transaction`
payloads inside committed blocks remain opaque `Vec<u8>` and are never decoded or executed by the selected
binary. **First missing boundary for a network attacker targeting execution:** the startup path never drains
committed blocks into any executor (`Node`/`BlockExecutor`, `EvmCommitProcessor`/`LedgerBridge` unconstructed;
`VmV0RuntimeState` snapshots only). **[Per R7]** this is a **scoped statement about the inspected startup path**,
not a global "unreachable at HEAD": `qbind-system` native-program dispatch and the EVM engine are real
non-test library code with real callers (R7-C) — they are simply not reached from this binary's ingress. The
residual is a full function-by-function trace of `run_p2p_node`/`run_local_mesh_node` bodies (inspected at the
dispatch/spawn/commit/vm-open level and by caller inventory, not line-by-line).

## A8.4 One downstream authorization trace — native governance (library path)
Ordered source trace for a concrete privileged state change (suite-status update), separating **signature
validity** from **permission**:
1. **Input:** a wire `Transaction` with `program_id = GOVERNANCE_PROGRAM_ID`, `call_data = [OP_GOV_UPDATE_SUITE_STATUS, …]`,
   and `auths` chosen by the sender.
2. **Decode:** `Transaction::decode` (`lib.rs:2615`, library only).
3. **Auth (A7-F1):** `TxExecutor::execute_transaction` → `ctx.verify_tx_auth(tx)` → `verify_transaction_auth`
   (`auth.rs:24`): **if `auths` empty ⇒ `Ok(())`** (`:31-33`); else each auth's signature is checked against a
   key in the keyset that `auth.account_index` selects, over `tx_digest = sha3_256_tagged("QBIND:TX",
   tx_sign_body_preimage(tx))` (`qbind-hash/src/tx.rs:51-53`; preimage covers version, **chain_id**, payer,
   nonce, fee_limit, accounts, program_id, call_data — `tx.rs:8-40`). **No check binds the signer to governance
   authority, nor requires a distinct/threshold set.**
4. **Dispatch:** `program.execute` (trait object, `qbind-runtime/src/lib.rs:158`) → `GovernanceProgram::execute`
   (`governance_program.rs:78-82`) switches on `call_data[0]`.
5. **State change (A8-F1):** `handle_update_suite_status` (`:92-153`) loads `SUITE_REGISTRY_ACCOUNT_ID`, sets
   the suite's status, and `ctx.store.put(account)` — **with no authority/permission check whatsoever** (same
   pattern for `handle_update_param_registry` `:156-`, `handle_update_launch_checklist`, `handle_set_mainnet_status`).
6. **Rejection points that exist:** program-id mismatch (`:70-73`), empty/garbage call_data (`:74-85`),
   unknown opcode (`:83-85`), account-not-found/decode errors, and — if `auths` are non-empty — a failed
   signature (`auth.rs:98-100`). **None of these is an authority check.**

So a transaction with **no auths** (or auths satisfying any keyset the sender controls) that reached this chain
would mutate governance state; **signature validity (A7-F1) is independent of permission to perform the
governance operation (A8-F1).** This holds in the **callable library/simulation path**; it is **not** a
demonstrated network exploit in the selected binary (§A8.3). Offline `qbind-gov` approval counting
(QBIND-A1-F002) is a separate surface and is not conflated here.

## A8.5 EVM boundary map
- **Engine:** revm, pinned in `Cargo.lock` (`revm`, `k256`, `secp256k1`); QBIND wrappers in
  `qbind-runtime/src/revm_engine.rs`, `execution_engine.rs`, `evm_state*.rs`, `block_apply.rs`;
  `qbind-node/src/evm_commit.rs` (`EvmCommitProcessor`) and `ledger_bridge.rs` (`LedgerBridge`).
- **Untrusted-input reachability:** EVM execution consumes `QbindBlock.body.transactions` via
  `apply_qbind_block` (`block_apply.rs:153-185`) → `ExecutionEngine::execute_block`. The only drivers are
  `EvmCommitProcessor::apply_committed_block` (test callers) and `LedgerBridge::step_once` (no non-test
  constructor; simulation `NodeHotstuffHarness`). **No inspected production entry point in the selected binary
  feeds untrusted input to the EVM engine.**
- **Classical-crypto trust boundary:** compiled `secp256k1`/`k256` ECDSA is used at the **EVM transaction
  authentication** boundary inside revm (an EVM-internal, currently unwired path). It is **not** used by the
  consensus (ML-DSA-44) or KEMTLS transport (ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-44) post-quantum authentication boundaries;
  compiled classical crypto therefore does **not** by itself establish any break in consensus or transport PQ
  authentication. Full EVM internals, precompile configuration, and the governance lifecycle are **queued**,
  not audited here.

  authorization (A8-F1); the EVM driver reachability and classical-crypto boundary.
- **Bounded negative:** "no execution wired in the selected binary" is scoped to the inspected dispatch/spawn/
  commit/vm-open sites plus the caller inventory of the execution entry points — **not** a line-by-line trace
  of `run_p2p_node`/`run_local_mesh_node`.
- **Open static questions (not execution-only):** full function-body trace of the node runners for any

- **Unexecuted runtime obligations:** any observed execution/state-mutation/DoS outcome — none performed.

## R7.1 Current disposition and accepted A7.1 work

| Item | Current disposition after this review |
|---|---|
| **A21-F1 = QBIND-A1-F001** | **OPEN STATIC.** The hand-written proposal count drives a very large reservation before body validation and before sender binding. Keep the corrected handshake-only allocation prerequisites, platform-dependent outcomes, and distinction between reservation, RSS, later decode failure and process failure. Do not describe the finite u32-based request as literally unbounded, or claim uniqueness across unreviewed subsystems. |
| **A2-F1 / A11-F1 / A17-F1** | Prior **OPEN STATIC** findings retained. This review does not close them, turn them into execution-only questions, or expand transport impersonation into a universal ability to forge inner consensus signatures. |
| **A7-F1 = QBIND-A1-F005** | Prior source-level authorization-completeness finding retained, with the existing selected-binary wiring limitation. Compiled library execution and native-program dispatch exist; current external reachability must be distinguished from their existence. See R7.4 and the A8 queue. |
| **DAG batch-codec wiring** | Accept the narrow main-entry-point observation: the inspected builder defaults to `NullDagHandler`, and the inspected `main.rs` does not install `DagFetchHandler`. This does not establish that all binaries, custom embedding applications or future configurations have the same wiring. |
| **Resource coverage labels** | Framing limits and individual guards remain evidence. Broad total-heap conclusions for serde-decoded messages are **not verified aggregate bounds**. See R7.2–R7.3. |

The A21-F1 allocation boundary stays separate from the later authorization boundary. In the accepted A7.1 trace, Optional/Disabled allow certificate-less access to this allocation; Required requires an accepted valid non-revoked certificate, not binding-map membership. These are P2P configurations; LocalMesh without P2P ingress remains distinct. A2-F1 is not needed to supply a configured origin to an allocation that precedes the origin check.

## R7.2 Bincode 1.3.3 source gap resolved for the inspected decoding operations

`Cargo.lock` at the pinned commit selects bincode 1.3.3 and serde/serde_core 1.0.228. The published bincode package source was inspected on docs.rs. Its `.cargo_vcs_info.json` identifies upstream commit `c44b5e364e7084cdbabf9f94b63a3c7f32b8fb68`. This is package-source provenance; the crate archive was not downloaded and independently checked against the lockfile checksum.

**Correction R7-A — limit attribution.** Bincode's `Options::deserialize` delegates to the slice path. In `internal::deserialize_seed`, that path replaces the supplied limit with `Infinite` before constructing `SliceReader`. Therefore `.with_limit(...).deserialize(&bytes)` does not enforce the configured byte counter on this path. Reader-based deserialization follows a different path; do not generalize between the two APIs. [Options implementation](https://docs.rs/crate/bincode/1.3.3/source/src/config/mod.rs); [internal implementation](https://docs.rs/crate/bincode/1.3.3/source/src/internal.rs).

QBIND nevertheless performs explicit input-length checks before both relevant calls: `binary_consensus_loop.rs:6975-6986` for Timeout and `:7184-7195` for NewView, followed by slice deserialization at `:6988-6991` and `:7197-7200`. **Those checks preserve the stated 64 KiB input cap.** This correction does not establish a bypass of that cap. Replace the coverage-table attribution to `with_limit` with attribution to the explicit precheck. Neither mechanism establishes a total heap budget.

**Correction R7-B — sequence hints and distinct visitor paths.** Bincode reads the declared sequence length, and its sequence access reports the remaining declared count as the size hint. The hint is not reduced to bytes remaining in the slice. Owned strings and byte buffers use separate decoding methods; they do not obtain a universal 1 MiB initial-allocation ceiling from Serde's ordinary `Vec<T>` sequence visitor. [Deserializer implementation](https://docs.rs/crate/bincode/1.3.3/source/src/de/mod.rs).

For the inspected slice reader, byte-buffer copying first checks that the declared bytes remain in the input. An exaggerated string/byte-buffer length therefore does not itself make this route allocate that many absent bytes. The `IoReader` implementation has different buffering behavior and needs separate analysis wherever used. [Reader implementations](https://docs.rs/crate/bincode/1.3.3/source/src/de/read.rs).

## R7.3 Narrow the resource claims to what was actually established

Retain the previously inspected Serde 1.0.228 `Vec<T>` cautious **initial reservation** behavior for the applicable visitor. It is not a universal collection limit, total allocation budget, process-memory limit or CPU budget. Growth by `push`, other visitors, nested values and partially constructed objects require separate accounting.

The actual P2P schema contains an owned string: `ControlMsg::PeerExchangeResponse.peers` contains `PeerInfo.address: String` (`p2p.rs:310-325`). Thus the report's universal “≤1 MiB initial per collection” framing is too broad. This observation identifies a different allocation path, not a newly established giant-allocation exploit; the inspected slice-copy check still applies.

Withdraw the asserted total “O(tens of MiB)”/“small nesting factor” and unqualified “heap O(1 MiB)” estimates as verified budgets. A fixed input cap plus a single visitor's initial cap does not, by itself, supply the missing schema-specific accounting. Likewise, “each pushed element consumes ≥1 input byte” must be demonstrated for the actual types and serialization options, not assumed as a generic Serde property.

| Route or question | Evidence retained | What remains unverified |
|---|---|---|
| Outer ConsensusNetMsg / DAG / Control decode | Existing transport-frame cap; slice input; applicable Vec initial-reservation cap | Peak heap across decoded variants, strings, nested allocations, temporary copies and partial failure; processing and retention after decode |
| Timeout / NewView | Explicit 64 KiB precheck; applicable Vec initial cap | Aggregate peak over nested evidence/QCs and failure paths; any claimed numerical total |
| Restore catch-up messages | Existing frame cap and applicable Vec initial cap | Aggregate decoded footprint and subsequent storage/work; A17-F1 remains a separate state-authentication finding |
| Hand-written proposal decoder | A21-F1 reservation before body/binding checks | Actual allocator/RSS/process outcome on a specified target; later handling of fully populated large proposals |
| Concurrent traffic | One synchronous handler invocation in the inspected consensus loop | Total node buffers, queues, retained messages/blocks and simultaneous work in other tasks |

These residuals are **open static analysis tasks**, except for measurements or demonstrations requiring execution. No new resource-exhaustion vulnerability is inferred solely from the absence of a completed bound. The existing oversized-reservation finding remains open independently of this accounting work.

## R7.5 Small but consequential reporting corrections

1. **Private-key requirement:** withdraw A7.1's blanket statement that binding-map membership *and a validator private key* are prerequisites for authorized consensus effects. A mapped identity is an authorization prerequisite on the relevant routes, but A2-F1 can impersonate that transport identity without the validator's private key. Inner signature requirements depend on message type and effect; restore-catch-up remains the separately tracked A17-F1 exception. A previously signed replay also must not be described as a new signature forgery.
2. **Panic configuration:** absence of `panic = "abort"` in the inspected workspace manifest does not establish the strategy of an unobserved build. Retain the standard default only conditionally on target/build configuration and overrides. No deployed panic strategy, task survival, crash or RSS outcome was observed.
3. **Concurrency:** one synchronous proposal decode in one loop does not establish a one-allocation bound for the entire node, nor rule out retained decoded storage. Keep the precise per-handler observation and the separate queues/buffers question.
4. **Static versus runtime:** downstream handling of a fully populated large proposal and aggregate schema bounds are still source-answerable questions. Measured runtime memory/CPU/liveness outcomes remain unexecuted. Do not move unfinished source tracing into an execution-only queue.

## A7.1.1 Corrected pre-authorization reachability
Trace (all first-hand at HEAD): handshake acceptance (`handshake.rs:1079-1113` Optional accepts **cert-less**
v1; `:1137-1226` Required accepts a parse+root-signature+validity+revocation-passing cert) → origin resolution
(`p2p_tcp.rs:1191-1194`, may be `None`) → the session is **not** terminated on a `None` origin
(`:1196-1210`, `spawn_peer_handlers` runs regardless) → read loop decodes the frame and forwards it with the
(possibly `None`) origin after an **optional** per-peer rate check that only drops the frame and keeps the
connection (`:1489-1519`) → demuxer forwards `Consensus` to the handler (`p2p_inbound.rs:374-386`) → the
consensus loop calls the handler **synchronously** (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3126-3146`) → `BlockProposal::
decode` runs its `with_capacity(tx_count)` (`:6192`) **before** `bind_sender` (`:6199`). **The binding gate is
therefore downstream of the allocation and cannot gate it.**

**Allocation-reachability prerequisites vs authorized-consensus-effect prerequisites (six combinations):**

| mutual_auth × root | Reaches the A21-F1 **allocation**? (prereqs) | Reaches **authorized consensus effect**? (additional prereqs) |
|---|---|---|
| **Optional × static-root, no client cert** | **Yes** — cert-less v1 accepted (`handshake.rs:1101-1112`); origin `None`; connection kept; frame decoded+forwarded. Prereqs: listener up, server KEM pubkey known, KEMTLS completed, limits/queue passed. **No cert, no key.** | **No** — `None` origin ⇒ `bind_sender` → `MissingOrigin` fail-closed. |
| **Required × static-root, root-accepted valid non-revoked cert NOT in binding map** | **Yes** — handshake accepts the cert (`:1137-1226`); `mutual_auth_complete=true`; but `validate_pair` fails ⇒ origin `None`; connection kept; proposal decoded. **No binding-map membership, no private key (no PoP).** | **No** — origin `None`/unmapped ⇒ `bind_sender` fail-closed (`UnknownPeer`/`MissingOrigin`). |
| **Required × static-root, cert IS a binding-map member (A2-F1 impersonable)** | **Yes** | **Yes** — origin resolves and `authorize` passes (A2-F1: presentation without PoP). |
| **Disabled × static-root** | **Yes** — cert ignored (`handshake.rs:1084-1086`); self-asserted id; connection kept; proposal decoded | **No** — `hardened` false ⇒ empty binding map ⇒ `bind_sender` fail-closed. |
| **Optional/Required × test-grade** | **Yes** — `DummySig` accepts any well-formed cert; cert-less also accepted under Optional | **No** — `pqc_active` false ⇒ empty binding map ⇒ fail-closed. |
| **Disabled × test-grade (executable P2P default)** | **Yes** — any peer completing the server-auth handshake | **No** — empty binding map. |

`Disabled` is the **executable P2P-configuration default** (`main.rs:6200`), **not** an observed deployment
setting; the **LocalMesh / no-P2P** case (no listener) is separate — the route is then unreachable. Net: under
every P2P configuration, the A21-F1 allocation is reachable by a peer that merely completes the server-auth
KEMTLS handshake (cert-less under Optional/Disabled; any root-accepted cert under Required) — **binding-map
membership and a validator private key are prerequisites only for authorized consensus effects, not for the
allocation.** **[SUPERSEDED-A7]** the A7 claim that hardened-mode reach needs a binding-map-member cert.

## A7.1.2 Actual resource bounds (pinned dependency source)
**Verified from pinned serde `v1.0.228`** (`serde_core/src/private/size_hint.rs`, `de/impls.rs`; retrieved
read-only from the tagged source):
```
pub fn cautious<Element>(hint: Option<usize>) -> usize {
    const MAX_PREALLOC_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;   // 1 MiB
    if size_of::<Element>() == 0 { 0 } else { min(hint.unwrap_or(0), MAX_PREALLOC_BYTES / size_of::<Element>()) }
}
```
and the `Vec<T>` visitor: `let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(cautious::<T>(seq.size_hint())); while let
Some(v) = seq.next_element()? { values.push(v); }`. So for any serde-decoded collection the **initial
reservation ≤ 1 MiB of element storage**, independent of the declared length; the vector then **grows by
`push`**, bounded by the elements the deserializer actually yields. **This is an initial reservation, not a
total budget** (per the prompt and the source).

Applying this to each serde/bincode route (`bincode 1.3.3`; `decode_frame` hands `bincode::deserialize` a
**fixed `&frame[5..5+len]` slice** — first-hand `p2p_tcp.rs:189` — so the reader cannot over-read beyond the
frame):

| Route | Encoded-byte limit | Initial reservation | Subsequent growth | Nested / live copies | Work before decode failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outer P2P (`decode_frame`) ConsensusNetMsg / DAG / Control | **16 MiB frame** (`framed_io.rs:117`) | ≤1 MiB per collection (serde cautious) | bounded by the 16 MiB slice (each pushed element consumes ≥1 input byte) | nested `Vec<Vec<…>>` adds a header-expansion factor (e.g. `Vec<Vec<u8>>` of empty inners ≈ 24 B out per ~8 B in ⇒ ≈3× ⇒ ≲ ~48 MiB) | reads elements until slice EOF |
| Timeout / NewView | **64 KiB** (`with_limit`, `binary_consensus_loop.rs:6988/7197`) | ≤1 MiB per collection (cautious) | bounded by ≤64 KiB input | small | ≤64 KiB read |
| RestoreCatchup Request/Response (`blocks: Vec<RestoreCatchupBlock>`, `qc_signer_indices: Vec<u16>`) | 16 MiB frame | ≤1 MiB per collection | bounded by 16 MiB slice | 2-level nesting, O(frame) total | reads until slice EOF |

**[SUPERSEDED-A7]** "heap amplification ≤ 64 KiB" for Timeout/NewView: the 64 KiB `with_limit` bounds the
**encoded bytes read**, not the heap; the decoded heap is bounded by **≤ ~1 MiB per serde collection initial
reservation plus the elements representable in ≤64 KiB of input**, i.e. O(1 MiB), not ≤64 KiB.
**[SUPERSEDED-A7]** bare "frame+serde bounded": the actual bound is **≤1 MiB initial reservation per collection
(serde v1.0.228 cautious) + total growth bounded by the ≤16 MiB frame slice (bincode reads a fixed slice) + a
small per-nesting header-expansion factor**, i.e. O(tens of MiB) per in-flight message. Assumptions: the serde
cautious cap (verified) and the fixed-slice reader bound (first-hand `decode_frame`). **I did not vendor
bincode 1.3.3 source**, so bincode's exact `SeqAccess::size_hint` value is unverified — but it is immaterial to
the upper bound because `cautious` caps at 1 MiB regardless of the hint, and the reader is slice-bounded.
**The hand-rolled `BlockProposal::decode` (A21-F1) does NOT use serde and is NOT subject to the 1 MiB cautious
cap** — this is exactly why it, uniquely, can request up to a multi-GiB initial reservation.

A byte cap is a useful guard but is **not** by itself sufficient to dismiss a resource candidate — the serde
cautious cap (not the byte cap alone) is what bounds the serde-route reservations.

## A7.1.3 Platform and concurrency classification
- **Element size by target.** `Vec<Vec<u8>>` element = `Vec<u8>` = `3·size_of::<usize>()`: **24 B on a 64-bit
  target, 12 B on 32-bit.** QBIND DevNet nodes build for 64-bit (no `target_pointer_width` gating in the
  decoders; no 32-bit target pinned) ⇒ reservation ≈ `24·tx_count`, up to `24·(2³²−1) ≈ 96 GiB`. The A7
  figure is retained **only under the stated 64-bit assumption**; it is not carried onto 32-bit.
- **Failure taxonomy (separated; none asserted to occur):**
  - *Capacity-overflow panic*: only if `tx_count·elem > isize::MAX`. On 64-bit (`isize::MAX ≈ 9.2e18`),
    `24·(2³²−1)` does **not** overflow ⇒ **no** capacity-overflow panic; a real ~96 GiB request is made. On
    **32-bit** (`isize::MAX ≈ 2.1e9`), `12·tx_count` exceeds `isize::MAX` for `tx_count ≳ 1.8e8` ⇒
    `capacity_overflow()` **panic** instead of a huge request.
  - *Allocator refusal* → `handle_alloc_error` → **process abort** (this path aborts regardless of panic
    strategy).
  - *Panic strategy*: the workspace `Cargo.toml` defines only `[profile.dev]`/`[profile.test]` and sets **no
    `panic = "abort"`** ⇒ default **unwind**. A capacity-overflow panic would unwind on the consensus-loop
    thread; whether that terminates the task, the runtime, or the process depends on the tokio/runtime wiring,
    which **I do not assert**.
  - So: on 64-bit the realistic outcome is a large allocation request → lazy mmap success (transient virtual
    mapping, dropped on decode failure) **or** allocator refusal → abort; on 32-bit, a capacity-overflow
    panic. **Conditional on allocator/overcommit/ulimit/target; no observed RSS or crash claimed.**
- **Fully-decoded vs truncated.** For a **fully populated** `txs`, each entry costs ≥4 bytes (`u32` `tx_len`),
  so a 16 MiB frame admits ≤ ~4.19M txs ⇒ a populated `txs` vector is ≲ ~100 MiB (4.19M·24 B). The ~96 GiB
  figure is the **truncated** case: `tx_count = u32::MAX` with the body absent — the reservation is attempted,
  then the per-tx loop fails at the first `get_u32`/`get_bytes` and the `Vec` is dropped. **These are distinct
  cases** and must not be conflated.
- **Concurrency ownership.** The consensus loop consumes inbound envelopes and calls the proposal handler
  **synchronously** (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:3126-3146`), so **at most one** `BlockProposal::decode`
  reservation is live at a time — **do not multiply it by connection count.** Separately: each accepted
  connection runs a `reader_worker` holding one ≤16 MiB `read_transport_frame` buffer (`framed_io.rs:125-128`),
  and the inbound channel retains forwarded envelopes (each `Proposal(Vec<u8>)` ≤16 MiB) until the single
  consensus loop drains them — these **per-connection** buffers scale with connection count and queue depth,
  independently of the single-instance proposal-decode reservation. **No hard max-connection cap is enforced by
  default**; the Run-362 connection-rate limiter and Run-369 per-peer message-rate limiter are **opt-in** (the
  message-rate limiter runs *after* `decode_frame` and, if enabled, throttles how many proposals reach
  `BlockProposal::decode`, but is off by default).

## A7.1.4 Completed coverage gaps
- **DAG `decode_batch` / `decode_batch_ref`.** Sole callers are in **`DagFetchHandler`** (`dag_fetch_handler.rs:
  211` `decode_batch_ref` on `BatchRequest`, `:245` `decode_batch` on `BatchResponse`; `impl DagInboundHandler`
  at `:264-295`). The production builder defaults the DAG handler to **`NullDagHandler`** unless
  `with_dag_handler(...)` is called (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1803-1804`); **`main.rs` does not call
  `with_dag_handler` and does not construct `DagFetchHandler`** (grep: only the `pub use`/module declaration in
  `lib.rs:2113,2269`). So on the **deployed binary** DAG messages are delivered to `NullDagHandler` and
  **`decode_batch*` are not reached from the network**; they become reachable only if an operator installs
  `DagFetchHandler`. Even then, `data` is bounded by the ≤16 MiB frame and (bincode/serde) by §A7.1.2.
  `decode_frame` still bincode-decodes the `DagNetMsg` envelope (frame+serde bounded) before `NullDagHandler`
  drops it. **Resolved: not a deployed-path finding; operator-wired reachability noted.**
- **Transaction / keyset / governance / validator body decoders — caller inventory.** `Transaction::decode`
  has exactly one caller at HEAD: `apply_block` (`lib.rs:2615`), with `Vec::with_capacity(proposal.txs.len())`
  (`:2612`, bounded by the already-decoded count). Per A7-F1, `apply_block`/`Node` is **unwired in `main.rs`**.
  The program-call decoders (`CreateKeysetCall`, `RegisterValidatorCall`, `UpdateConsensusKeyCall`,
  `GovUpdate*`) have **no non-test caller in `qbind-node`/`qbind-runtime`/`qbind-ledger`** (grep). So at HEAD no
  **wired** network route decodes `Transaction` or these call bodies. **[Narrowed per the prompt]**: the
  exclusion now rests on this caller inventory (single unwired caller), not merely on "proposal txs are
  opaque." Residual: the offline `qbind-gov`/`qbind-system` tooling decodes governance envelopes (QBIND-A1-F002,
  offline — not a network route); any future wiring of `apply_block` or a tx-submission endpoint would move
  these u16-count decoders (`tx.rs:169/182`, `keyset.rs:89`) onto a network route.

## A7.2 A21-F1 / QBIND-A1-F001 — revalidation at HEAD
- **Exact bytes before the allocation.** `BlockProposal::decode` sequentially reads msg_type(1)+version(1)+
  chain_id(4)+epoch(8)+height(8)+round(8)+parent_block_id(32)+payload_hash(32)+proposer_index(2)+suite_id(2)+
  **tx_count(4)**+timestamp(8)+payload_kind(1)+next_epoch(8)+batch_commitment(32)+qc_len(4) = **155 bytes**, then
  (if `qc_len>0`) a `get_bytes(qc_len)` (input-bounded), then `Vec::with_capacity(tx_count)` at `:766`. So a
  **~155-byte** proposal prefix (qc_len=0) suffices to reach the reservation.
- **Count encoding / conversions / element size.** `tx_count = get_u32` little-endian (`io.rs:48-55`), used as
  `tx_count as usize` (`:766`). On 64-bit `u32→usize` is lossless; the reserved bytes are
  `tx_count · size_of::<Vec<u8>>()` = `tx_count · 24`. Max `24·4 294 967 295 ≈ 96 GiB`. On a 32-bit target the
  `24·count` size computation triggers Rust's capacity-overflow check → panic/abort instead (platform note).
- **Remaining-input does NOT constrain capacity.** `get_bytes` (`io.rs:72-79`) checks `input.len() < len`
  **inside** the per-tx loop (`:768-769`), i.e. **after** `with_capacity`. Nothing compares `tx_count` to the
  remaining byte count before the reservation. (Contrast `PeerList`, §A7.3, which checks the count first.)
- **Every production caller / preceding limit.** Inbound: `handle_inbound_consensus_msg`
  (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6190-6192`) decodes `ConsensusNetMsg::Proposal(bytes)` where `bytes` came from
  `decode_frame` (≤16 MiB). **No byte-length cap smaller than 16 MiB precedes the proposal decode** (unlike
  Timeout/NewView). The decode runs **before** `bind_sender` (`:6199`). (Encode-side callers build proposals
  locally and are not attacker-controlled.)
- **Authentication/authorization reached first.** A completed KEMTLS session is required (transport). Consensus
  authorization (`bind_sender`→`authorize`) is **not** reached until after the decode — so the binding gate
  cannot protect this allocation. Handshake prerequisites still apply (deployed `Disabled` default: server-auth
  only, no client cert; `Required/Optional`+`pqc_active`: a configured validator's cert, A2-F1 impersonable).
- **Consequence, separated (no guaranteed RSS, no guaranteed crash):**
  - *Requested capacity:* a single contiguous allocation of up to ~96 GiB.
  - *Virtual reservation vs touched RSS:* `Vec::with_capacity` does **not** initialize the buffer; under Linux
    default overcommit the large request is typically an `mmap` reservation with **no immediate RSS**. On a
    truncated proposal the body loop fails at the first `get_u32`/`get_bytes` and the `Vec` is dropped, so
    touched resident memory stays minimal.
  - *Allocation failure / abort:* if the allocator rejects the request (overcommit disabled / `vm.overcommit=2`,
    address-space or `ulimit` exceeded, 32-bit capacity overflow), `Vec::with_capacity` calls
    `handle_alloc_error` ⇒ **process abort** (availability DoS). Whether this occurs is platform/allocator-
    dependent.
  - *Later decode failure:* independent of the above, the truncated body yields a decode `Err` ⇒ proposal
    rejected — **after** the allocation attempt.
  - *Process impact:* **conditional** — either a transient large virtual mapping then drop (no crash), or an
    allocation-failure abort. Repeated frames and concurrent connections multiply the transient requests
    (each completed session can stream many proposal frames); this repeated/concurrent pressure is **separate**
    from one-message amplification and is not quantified here.

## A7.4 Serialization-library behavior and the `decode_frame` budget gap
- **Pinned version:** `bincode 1.3.3` (`Cargo.lock`). **The bincode/serde crate source is NOT vendored in this
  checkout** (no `vendor/` or local registry cache), so the following is asserted from authoritative upstream
  documentation, **not** from pinned local source — named here as a **dependency-source gap**: serde's derived
  `Vec<T>` visitor uses a *cautious* capacity (`size_hint`-bounded, not the raw length prefix), so a bincode
  length prefix does **not** by itself drive an arbitrary preallocation. Under that behavior the serde/bincode
  routes (`ConsensusNetMsg` outer, `RestoreCatchup*`, DAG, Control) are bounded by the **16 MiB frame** plus
  serde's cautious cap, not GB-scale.
- **`decode_frame` lacks an explicit `.with_limit`** (`p2p_tcp.rs:191`), unlike the Timeout/NewView path which
  sets `bincode…with_limit(64 KiB)` (`:6988/7197`). This is a **defense-in-depth gap**, not a confirmed
  unbounded allocation: in practice it is bounded by the 16 MiB frame + serde cautious capacity. If the cautious
  behavior were absent in the pinned versions (unverifiable from local source), a 16 MiB frame could drive a
  larger transient preallocation. Recorded under A21-F1's umbrella.
- **A21-F1 itself is independent of this gap:** `BlockProposal::decode` is QBIND's **own hand-rolled**
  `WireDecode` (`Vec::with_capacity(tx_count)` directly), which does **not** pass through serde's cautious cap.
  So A21-F1 stands on first-hand pinned source regardless of bincode/serde behavior.
- **`dag_mempool.rs:1183/1201`** (`decode_batch_ref`/`decode_batch`) use `bincode::deserialize` with **no
  `.with_limit`**; their `data` provenance is storage/mempool. **Unresolved:** whether peer-originated DAG batch
  bytes reach these codecs without a budget (a static reachability question for a later pass, named not deferred).

## A7.6 Findings and rejected candidates (summary)
- **Finding (A21-F1, extended):** `consensus.rs:766` (u32, primary) + `consensus.rs:351` (u16 sibling) —
  unguarded `with_capacity` from a decoded count, before element reads, **before authorization**.
- **Rejected (guarded) candidates and their guards:** `net.rs:521` PeerList (`count>MAX_PEER_LIST_SIZE`);
  `framed_io.rs:58/117` (16 KiB / 16 MiB caps before alloc); `transport.rs:58` (buffer bound);
  `pqc_peer_candidate_wire.rs:499` (declared-len cap); `binary_consensus_loop.rs:6975/6988/7184/7197`
  (byte cap + `bincode with_limit`). All `get_bytes`-based variable fields are input-bounded.
- **Class-members not on the pre-auth network route:** `tx.rs:169/182`, `keyset.rs:89` (and the gov/validator
  call decoders) — transaction/program-call bodies decoded in execution, not at proposal ingestion (A7-F1:
  proposal `txs` are opaque bytes). u16-bounded.

- **Static (source-answerable, not yet closed):** (1) whether peer DAG batch bytes reach
  `dag_mempool::decode_batch*` without a decode budget; (2) the exact serde/bincode cautious-capacity behavior

The correctly bounded catch-up witness requires an admitted replay connection, retained exportable blocks, different response plaintext, successful queueing/writing, and matching outbound counter positions. Competing writes and connection replacement matter. These are explicit conditions, not guarantees about a running network.

## R2. Correct the receiving-session exclusion

**SUPERSEDES A6.2 §A6.2.4 and §A6.2.6 where they conclude that per-connection keys exclude transfer to another connection or leave only execution questions.**

A connection has its own counter state, but that does not imply its keys are unique. The entire A11-F1 mechanism is that multiple connections can receive identical key material. Separate these cases:

| Receiver or connection | Key relationship | Correct conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh honest connection using a different encapsulation and otherwise normal cryptographic operation | Expected to derive different keys | Traffic from the recorded session is not thereby a valid forgery for this unrelated connection. |
| Additional server connection initialized by the exact recorded ClientInit | Same directional key inputs under the finding's prerequisites; counters restart | Reinstalled key/nonce state remains source-supported. |
| Original honest dialer whose ClientInit was recorded | Holds the original session keys, which are also reconstructed in the replayed server session | A key mismatch cannot exclude this target. Acceptance depends on its expected receive counter, framing/AAD, delivery opportunity, connection lifetime, and handler checks. |

The missing attack step is not solved here: the reviewer has not established a full schedule that obtains useful ciphertext/tag pairs and delivers a successful forgery to the original dialer while it expects the relevant counter. Blocking or delaying traffic, peer replacement, read timeouts, and reader-worker progress require an explicit trace. Counter alignment is necessary but is not, alone, a demonstrated forgery.

Server-to-client forgery is still not client-to-server injection. Nor does successful transport decryption alone prove a consensus effect. Retain both separations.

Evidence: [deterministic key derivation](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/keys.rs#L279); [per-direction counters](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/session.rs#L58); [client/server receive-direction selection](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/connection.rs#L407); [server decapsulation and key construction](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/handshake.rs#L988).

## R3. Correct the active-actor exclusion

**SUPERSEDES A6.2's blanket conclusion that active encapsulation necessarily gives fresh ciphertext and therefore cannot participate in nonce reuse.**

The normal client start routine invokes encapsulation and retains both the ciphertext and shared secret. A malicious client is not required to call that routine afresh for every connection: it can retain and resend its own ClientInit. Under the same server key, transcript inputs, accepted certificate, and suite configuration, replay of that retained message reproduces the same key inputs and resets connection counters.

Thus:
- An actor replaying another client's captured handshake generally does not know that client's shared secret.
- An actor performing its own encapsulation knows its own shared secret; fresh encapsulation normally separates it from an unrelated victim session.
- An actor replaying its own retained handshake can cause reuse of key/nonce state that it already knows.

The last case is not automatically a new confidentiality break against somebody else's session, and knowing one's own keys does not prove compromise of the original victim connection. It is nevertheless incorrect to rule out reuse categorically. Attribute configured-identity impersonation to A2-F1 and repeated key/nonce installation to A11-F1 without counting the same security effect twice.

Evidence: [client start and retained encapsulation output](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/handshake.rs#L355); [server decapsulation](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/handshake.rs#L988); [key derivation](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/keys.rs#L279).

## R4. Correct the known-plaintext classification

**SUPERSEDES A6.2's description of the relevant 32-byte block IDs as cryptographic hashes and its implication that fixed-width fields are necessarily known.**

On the inspected engine route, derive_block_id_from_header constructs:

`LE64(proposer) || LE64(view) || parent_block_id[0..16]`

It does not hash. This is the already-established A5.1 correction, not a reopening of A33-F1. A parent derived by the same route also has structured content; a snapshot anchor may instead contain operator-supplied opaque bytes. Neither every ID being unknown nor every ID being recoverable is established.

The length/type of a height, view, validator index, or ID does not reveal its value. Echoed request fields are known to an attacker only if the attacker actually knows their values; capture of an encrypted request alone does not establish that knowledge.

For repeated ChaCha20 key/nonce use, the XOR relation applies to aligned encrypted message-body bytes over their common length; do not apply it indiscriminately to appended authentication tags. Plaintext recovery requires known aligned bytes or an explicitly justified inference. No complete or precisely quantified partial recovery is demonstrated by this review.

Framing distinction, retained for clarity: the outer TransportFrame type/length is outside the AEAD ciphertext. The inner P2P discriminator/length produced by encode_frame is included in the plaintext sent for encryption. Do not combine the two layers when counting known bytes.

Evidence: [block-ID construction](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs#L3865); [inner frame encoding](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-node/src/p2p_tcp.rs#L146); [encoded frame handed to the secure channel](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-node/src/p2p_tcp.rs#L1568); [outer frame format](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/transport.rs#L14); [application encryption and AAD](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-net/src/transport.rs#L74).

## R5. Correct the per-message table's attribution and scope

**NewView.** A6.2 lists bind_sender for NewView. The production handler actually calls authorize_origin because this TC message has no single immediate claimed sender. It then applies its decoding and independent TC-verification gates. This is an attribution correction, not a new authentication bypass.

Evidence: [NewView origin-only admission](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs#L7142).

**Vote.** The cited qc.rs validation rejects duplicate signer entries within a QC; that alone does not establish idempotent handling of replayed vote messages. The accumulator's insertion classification checks membership in the retained signer set indexed by (view, block_id). Its narrow established property is no additional insertion of the same voter into that retained set. This is not a proof of lifetime replay exclusion, of deduplication across different block IDs, or of absence of every earlier/later effect. Complete production-route replay effects remain a static-analysis obligation; do not label them execution-only.

Evidence: [QC object validation](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-consensus/src/qc.rs#L83); [retained accumulator key and insertion](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-consensus/src/vote_accumulator.rs#L379); [duplicate classification](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-consensus/src/vote_accumulator.rs#L422).

**RestoreCatchupRequest.** Absence of a body signature or generic duplicate gate is retained. Replace “every replay emits a response” with: a bound request may cause a new export and response attempt if requester is not self, an outbound facade exists, and export is non-empty. Successful delivery also requires registration, queue acceptance, and writing. The response uses current engine state. The source witness is conditional on those conditions, not universal.

Evidence: [request servicing](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs#L8381).

**RestoreCatchupResponse.** Anchor equality gates the non-empty block-application route. It is not an all-effects gate: the empty-block branch and stale/mismatched-anchor branch call evaluate_restore_mode_transition. This in turn invokes the restore-mode state transition logic and updates metrics. Preserve the earlier active/progress/monotonicity qualifications; this review does not assert an unconditional restore exit or finality violation.

Evidence: [empty and mismatched response branches](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs#L8433); [transition evaluation](https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs#L8536).

Proposal, Timeout, and remaining Vote/NewView engine-level replay consequences not actually traced must remain NOT COMPLETED AT SOURCE. Existing timeout verification and TC/F7 findings retain their accepted scopes. A table entry saying “not re-audited” cannot also support a claim that all per-message replay questions have been resolved.

**Net correction:** the only routes with no freshness/duplicate gate beyond the (passable) `bind_sender` are the
**RestoreCatchupRequest** (re-emits current-state response) and, while the anchor is unchanged, the
**RestoreCatchupResponse** apply. Proposal/Vote/Timeout/NewView enforce epoch/context + signature + (type-
specific) accumulation/dedup, but **none of those is a per-message nonce/anti-replay**, and a current-epoch
replay is admitted to the engine; engine-internal view/duplicate handling was **not** re-audited here and is
**not** asserted as a universal rejecter. Do **not** claim replay causes finality failure — that chain is not
established.

## A6.2.3 Correction 2 — one conditional source witness for differing s2c plaintext
**Claim (conditional, source-reachable, UNEXECUTED):** a recorded, authorized `RestoreCatchupRequest` replayed
into a reinstated session can cause a `RestoreCatchupResponse` whose plaintext **differs** from the original
session's at the **same** outbound s2c counter.

Traced path: replayed `ClientInit` reinstalls `k_s2c`+`session_id`+counter 0 (A11-F1) → attacker replays the
recorded request over this session → `bind_sender` **passes** iff the session's authenticated origin is a
configured validator (A2-F1 spoof, or the genuine holder) → `handle_restore_catchup_request`
(`binary_consensus_loop.rs:8394-8419`) calls `engine.export_restore_catchup_blocks(req.from_height, …)` and
builds a response with `responder_committed_height = engine.committed_height()` (**current**) →
`facade.broadcast_consensus_msg` (`consensus_net_p2p.rs:362-364`) → `P2pService::broadcast` fans out to every
registered peer via `conn.tx.try_send` (`p2p_tcp.rs:2107-2113`) → per-peer bounded channel (cap 64,
`:1382`) → `write_loop` `encode_frame` → `SecureChannel` AEAD `seal` on the per-connection s2c counter
(`session.rs:77-82`).

**Explicit preconditions (a possible, not guaranteed, schedule):**
1. The attacker's replayed connection is **registered in `self.peers` under the impersonated NodeId**
   (`p2p_tcp.rs:1417-1426`); registration/replacement means a new connection for an existing NodeId replaces
   the prior entry, so the broadcast reaches the attacker's connection.
2. **Retained blocks still satisfy export** at `req.from_height` (non-empty, else `:8399` returns — no response).
3. **State changed between recordings:** `committed_height` advanced (or the exported block set, or the
   `responder_committed_height` field) so the response plaintext genuinely differs.
4. **Counter alignment:** the response occupies the **same** s2c counter index in both sessions. Because
   `broadcast` interleaves other consensus traffic and the `write_loop` multiplexes raw peer-candidate frames
   onto the same direction, this is only realizable under a matching pre-response frame count — cleanest when
   the response is the **first** s2c app frame on each connection (counter 0). **Competing writers make this a
   schedule, not a guarantee.**

If (1)–(4) hold, two different plaintexts are sealed under one `(k_s2c, nonce)` → keystream reuse at that
counter. **This is a source-established possible schedule with named preconditions; it is NOT executed and
NOT asserted to occur in any particular deployment run.**

## A6.2.4 Correction 3 — receiver-side boundary, actor scoping, and known-plaintext bound
**Receiver-side acceptance of a replay-session ciphertext (s2c forgery).** A ciphertext sealed in the
attacker's replay session is bound to **that session's** `k_s2c` and **per-connection** counter
(`session.rs:58-66,84-89`; keys per-session from `kem_ct`+randoms). For an **honest dialer on an independent
connection** to accept it, that connection would need the **same** `k_s2c` **and** to be expecting the **same**
counter — which it is not (independent `kem_ct` ⇒ independent key; independent counter state). So a
replay-session ciphertext is **not automatically acceptable to another connection**; `decrypt_app`/`open`
fails (Poly1305) on key or counter mismatch. A Poly1305 one-time-key-reuse **forgery** (from link D) is
likewise only valid **within a session sharing that `k_s2c` and at that nonce** — i.e., the reinstated-key
session itself, never transferred to an independent honest session. **Therefore s2c transport forgery is NOT
client→server consensus injection**, and any consensus effect still requires the inner ML-DSA signature,
except the signature-free A17-F1 catch-up payload.

**Passive replay vs active encapsulation (do not double-count A2-F1).**
- **Passive replay** (replaying *someone else's* captured `ClientInit`, the A11-F1 scenario): the actor does
  **not** know the session shared secret (ML-KEM `ss` is never on the wire and is not recoverable from `kem_ct`
  without the server KEM sk). It holds only ciphertext; it can compute the two-time-pad XOR but cannot directly
  decrypt. **[This is the correct scope for A6's "replayer lacks the shared secret."]**
- **Active encapsulation** (A2-F1 cert-presentation spoof with the actor performing its **own** encaps): the
  actor **does** know **its** session's shared secret and keys — but that session has a **fresh randomized
  `kem_ct`** ⇒ **different keys**, so it yields **no nonce reuse** with recorded traffic. Its value is
  transport-identity impersonation reaching gated ingress (the **A2-F1** consequence), **not** an A11-F1
  key/nonce-reuse consequence. These are analyzed separately and not double-counted.

**[SUPERSEDED-A6.1]** "full recovery given known/structured plaintext." Corrected: the two-time pad yields
`C₁⊕C₂ = P₁⊕P₂`, so a byte of one plaintext is recovered **only where the aligned byte of the other is
known/predictable**. For a catch-up response the predictable bytes are the sealed payload's **message
discriminant, echoed `request_from_height`/`request_from_block_id`, and fixed-width counters/indices
(`height`, `view`, `*_validator_index`)**; genuinely unpredictable bytes (e.g. `block_id`/`parent_block_id`
32-byte hashes the attacker does not already hold) are **not** recovered from structure alone. (Transport
framing `msg_type`+`len` are outside the AEAD ciphertext and are already cleartext.) So the supported
consequence is **partial, field-scoped recovery**, not complete plaintext recovery.

| mutual_auth × root | Startup prereq | Handshake acceptance | Verified identity | Authenticated consensus origin |

| **Required × test-grade** | DummyKem/Aead/Sig | v2+cert required; DummySig accepts any well-formed cert | cert-derived (vacuous sig) | **No** — `pqc_active` false ⇒ empty map ⇒ fail-closed |
| **Optional × static-root** | **static-root leaf creds still required to run pqc_active** | v1 (cert-less) **or** v2 (cert-bearing) accepted; cert verified **iff present** | cert-bearing → cert-derived; cert-less → none | cert-bearing → **Yes iff** pair ∈ map; cert-less → **No** |
| **Optional × test-grade** | DummyKem/Aead/Sig | v1 or v2 accepted | cert-derived iff present (vacuous) | **No** — empty map ⇒ fail-closed |
| **Disabled × static-root** | **static-root leaf creds still required to run pqc_active** | v1 & v2 accepted, **cert ignored** | `init.validator_id` self-asserted; no node_id | **No** — `hardened` false ⇒ empty map |
| **Disabled × test-grade** | DummyKem/Aead/Sig | v1 & v2 accepted, cert ignored | self-asserted; no node_id | **No** — empty map |

## A6.1.2 Correction 1 — configuration and authorization matrix (executable wiring)
**Deployed default is `Disabled`, not `Required`.** `main.rs:6187-6207`: `--p2p-mutual-auth` wins, else
`QBIND_MUTUAL_AUTH`, else **absent/unparseable ⇒ `Disabled`** (`:6200` `unwrap_or(NodeMam::Disabled)`). The
`#[default]` on the *enum* is `Required`, but the binary never relies on it. **[SUPERSEDED-A6]** "Required
(default)".

**Binding gate / inbound resolver** (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1583-1686`): entries are built **only** when
`hardened (Required\|Optional) && pqc_active` (`:1587-1591`), from the local + every configured peer leaf cert,
each fully validated before admission (`validated_cert_bound_node_id`, `:1602-1628`). In **any other mode the
map is empty** and the transport surfaces no origin ⇒ the gate **fails closed** (`:1580-1582`). The inbound
resolver (`:1661-1680`) yields an origin **only** when `mutual_auth_complete` **and** `verified_client_node_id`
**and** `verified_peer_validator_id` are present **and** `validate_pair` recognizes the exact one-to-one pair.

**Trusted-root resolver** (`:2025-2058`): `Required\|Optional` **always** receive a resolver through this
builder — static-root reads configured operator roots (`:2036-2050`), test-grade installs the dummy resolver
`Some([0x01;32])` (`:2052-2056`); **`Disabled` ⇒ `None`** (`:2057`). The low-level `trusted_client_roots=None`
"signature-skipped" branch (`handshake.rs:1167-1176`) is therefore **not produced by any production
constructor for `Required\|Optional`**; it is a raw-config possibility only. **[SUPERSEDED-A6]** the matrix row
implying production `Required` with `roots=None` skips signature verification.

**Six explicit rows** (startup prereq → handshake acceptance → verified identity → authenticated consensus
origin → handler authorization):

| mutual_auth × root | Startup prereq | Handshake acceptance | Verified identity | Authenticated consensus origin | Handler authorization (incl. restore-catchup) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Required × static-root** | ML-KEM-768 leaf creds required else `Config` error | v2 **with** cert required; cert sig vs **operator roots** + validity + revocation; malformed/expired rejected **separately** from bad-signature | `client_node_id=derive_node_id_from_cert`, `peer_validator_id=cert.validator_id` | **Yes, iff** verified pair ∈ authoritative map (`validate_pair`) | `authorize` passes only for the mapped pair; all else fail-closed |
| **Required × test-grade** | none special (DummyKem/Aead/Sig) | v2+cert required; **DummySig accepts any** well-formed cert (dummy resolver) | node_id/vid derived from cert | **No** — `pqc_active` false ⇒ **binding map empty** ⇒ gate fails closed | **rejected** (`MissingOrigin`/`UnknownPeer`); no consensus effect **[SUPERSEDED-A6: "mapped id → dispatch"]** |
| **Optional × static-root, cert-bearing** | as Required-static | cert verified if present | as Required-static | **Yes, iff** pair ∈ map | mapped pair only |
| **Optional × static-root, cert-less (v1)** | — | v1 accepted server-auth-only | **none** (`client_node_id=None`, `mutual_auth_complete=false`) | **No** (resolver returns `None`) | **rejected** fail-closed — cert-less acceptance grants **no** consensus access **[SUPERSEDED-A6]** |
| **Optional × test-grade** | — | v1 or v2 accepted | cert-derived if present (vacuous sig) | **No** (`pqc_active` false ⇒ empty map) | rejected fail-closed |
| **Disabled × (either)** | — | v1 & v2 accepted, **cert ignored** (`handshake.rs:1084-1086`) | `peer_validator_id=init.validator_id` (self-asserted), no node_id | **No** (`hardened` false ⇒ empty map; resolver `None`) | rejected fail-closed |

**Resource-consumption vs authorization kept separate.** The gate authorizes **consensus state changes**; it
does not sit before earlier decode/allocation work. The wired inbound Proposal arm decodes (and the A21-F1
`u32`-count pre-size executes) **before** `bind_sender` (decode precedes sender-binding, register §A3), so the
binding gate does **not** prevent that earlier resource-consumption effect. **[Do not infer the gate blocks

## A6.1.3 Correction 2 — bound the server-authentication conclusion
**[SUPERSEDED-A6]** the blanket "dialer→listener (server-auth) is KEM-backed and sound." Precisely supported
properties, in order along the dial path:
1. **Peer-key pinning (caller level).** The dialer encapsulates to a **pinned** peer KEM key, not a
   self-asserted one: `certified_peer_kem_pk_for_validator` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:641`) builds
   `peer_kem_pk_overrides` (`:1367-1462`, installed `:1461-1462`). This **closes the A6 "caller-binding
   note"** — the `leaf_kem_pk`↔`peer_kem_pk` link is enforced by the caller's pin, not inside
   `handle_server_accept`.
2. **Certificate validation.** `handle_server_accept` verifies the returned server cert vs the configured
   root, matches `validator_id`, checks validity window and leaf revocation, and derives `server_node_id`
   (`handshake.rs:441-556`). Validity/revocation failures are distinct from signature failure.
3. **Outbound mapping check (Run 418).** `p2p_tcp.rs:1301-1340`: when an `outbound_consensus_origins`
   expectation exists for the dial address, the **verified** server identity must match it **exactly**
   (`authenticated && node_match && vid_match`) or the **session is rejected**; with **no** expectation the
   origin is `None` and the consensus ingress gate fails closed. The dial address never mints an origin.
4. **Possession / key confirmation.** Only a holder of the KEM private key matching the **pinned**
   `peer_kem_pk` can decapsulate the dialer's `kem_ct` and derive matching keys. **Key confirmation is
   obtained only at the first successful `s2c` AEAD open** — the unauthenticated `ServerAccept` packet alone
   is **not** evidence the peer decapsulated. **[SUPERSEDED-A6: implicit "sound" without this qualifier.]**

**Assumptions** this soundness rests on: `pqc_active` + a configured `vid@addr`/override map; cert still within
its validity window at dial; operator root distribution correct. **Suite/version/transcript checks retained:**
suite ids must match exactly or `UnsupportedSuite` (`handshake.rs:855-860,1241-1246`) and are bound into the
KDF `info` (`keys.rs:292`); the client `ServerAccept.version` is echoed; the transcript binds
`client_random‖server_random‖kem_ct‖client_cert?`. The "no executable crypto-suite downgrade" conclusion is
retained on that basis; the only executable downgrade remains mutual-auth **presence** under Optional/Disabled.
**A2-F1's client-PoP defect is retained** with its exact prerequisites (validity, revocation, config,
binding-map membership) in §A6.1.0.

## A6.1.4 Correction 3 — replay consequences, per direction
Direction keys are distinct (`keys.rs:300-301`: `k_c2s`="QBIND:k_c2s", `k_s2c`="QBIND:k_s2c") and each
direction has an independent counter + flag (`session.rs:64,145-146`). Reinstallation of **both** directions'
(key,nonce) state holds on exact ClientInit replay (§A6 §A6.4-A), but the **consequences differ by direction**.

**Possible first encrypted application writes.** The outbound `write_loop` (`p2p_tcp.rs:1558-1620`) multiplexes
**two** producers onto one AEAD direction: the structured `P2pMessage` channel (`encode_frame`) **and** a raw
already-framed channel whose only production writer is the Run-080 `LivePeerCandidateWirePublisher`
(length-prefixed, `MAX_PEER_CANDIDATE_WIRE_FRAME_BYTES`-capped). So the counter-0 slot's plaintext is **not a
single fixed message**; source establishes a **set of possible schedules** (first structured consensus frame,
or first raw peer-candidate frame, per connection ordering), not one universal first packet.

| Direction | Repeated key/nonce install | Recorded-ciphertext acceptance | Differing plaintext at reused counter? | Confidentiality/authentication consequence | Application acceptance after binding/sig/freshness/dup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **c2s** (replayer→server) | Yes (replay) | Yes — server `c2s.open` re-accepts in-order from 0 (`session.rs:84-89`; const AAD) | Only if the replayer sends *new* c2s plaintext under the reinstalled key — but it **cannot** (it lacks the KEM shared secret; it holds only recorded ciphertext) | So c2s stays **pure replay** of the victim's prior frames; **no new-plaintext keystream reuse** in this direction | **First rejecting guard:** `bind_sender`→`authorize` (origin must be a configured validator — reachable only via A2-F1 impersonation) **then** inner ML-DSA signature + view-freshness + duplicate checks. Replayed **old** messages carry stale views/valid-but-old signatures → rejected/no-op. **Decryption ≠ consensus effect.** |
| **s2c** (server→replayer) | Yes (replay) | Attacker **records** s2c ciphertext; cannot decrypt (no key) | **Yes, conditionally** — if the server, in the replayed session, emits s2c plaintext differing from the recorded session at the same counter (consensus state advanced, or a different multiplexed producer fires) | **Two-time pad:** `C₁⊕C₂ = P₁⊕P₂` computable **without** the key ⇒ confidentiality loss of s2c (full recovery given known/structured consensus plaintext); Poly1305 one-time-key reuse ⇒ a **bounded** s2c-frame forgery surface **toward a dialer** | A forged s2c frame targets a **dialer's** receive path, **not** the server's consensus ingress — **server→client forgery is not client→server injection.** Any consensus effect still needs the inner ML-DSA signature, except the A17-F1 catch-up payload. |

**Unresolved steps (named, not deferred):** (c-schedule) the actual first multiplexed plaintext per
connection; (s2c-D trigger) an executed witness that the reinstalled s2c direction emits ≥1 differing plaintext
at a reused counter; (E) a dialer-side receive-path trace showing whether a forged s2c frame survives framing +
signature + freshness + duplicate checks. **Cross-restart replay** is qualified by: unchanged
`validator_id`/leaf key/suite config (keys reproduce), the leaf cert **still within its validity window** at
replay (else handshake fails Run-045), and unchanged trusted-root config (cert still accepted). All downstream
runtime consequences remain **explicitly UNEXECUTED**.
