## A6.2 Configuration and trust-boundary matrix (executable behavior, not R3/R4 shorthand)
Two **independent** axes, traced CLI/env → `with_pqc_root_config` → `P2pNodeBuilder::build` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1233`)
→ `create_connection_configs` (`:1853`) → `Connection`/`SecureChannel` → consensus dispatch.
`pqc_active = (pqc_root_config.mode == PqcStaticRoot)` (`:1248-1251`).

| mutual_auth_mode | pqc_root_mode | Startup | Crypto backend | Cert trust + revocation | Identity to origin resolver | Binding-map / reachable ingress |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Required** (default) | **PqcStaticRoot** (`pqc_active`) | OK, but **requires local ML-KEM-768 leaf creds** else `Config` error (fail-closed `:1252-1261,:1930-1934`) | Real ML-KEM-768 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 + ML-DSA-44 (`:1284-1310`) | Client cert sig verified vs **operator roots** (live/`cfg` resolver `:2025-2050`); validity window (Run045) + leaf revocation (Run052) enforced | `client_node_id = derive_node_id_from_cert(verified client cert)`; `peer_validator_id = cert.validator_id` (`:1034-1037,:1098`) | mapped id → consensus sender-binding; **impersonable (A2-F1)**; ingress incl. A17-F1 catch-up |
| **Required** | test-grade default | OK | **DummyKem (deterministic) + DummyAead (XOR, nonce-ignored) + DummySig (verify→Ok)** | Dummy resolver returns `Some([0x01;32])` so **DummySig passes any cert** (`:2052-2056`) | same mapping, but signature is vacuous | mapped id → dispatch; no real confidentiality (DummyAead) |
| **Required** | (roots = `None`) | OK | either | **signature check SKIPPED** — empty `root_pk` ⇒ `if !root_pk.is_empty()` false (`handshake.rs:1167-1173,:1176`): any *parseable* cert accepted | node_id from unverified cert | weakest accept; still no PoP |
| **Optional** | any | OK; accepts **v1** (no cert) server-auth-only (`:1101-1112`) | as above | cert verified **iff present**; absent ⇒ no client identity | `client_node_id=None` when no cert | **mutual-auth downgrade**: a would-be-authenticated peer may present v1 and be accepted id-less |
| **Disabled** | any | OK; accepts v1 & v2 | as above | **client cert ignored** (`:1084-1086`) | `peer_validator_id = init.validator_id` (**fully self-asserted**), `client_node_id=None` | identity is pure self-assertion; no cert needed to claim any id |

**Transport establishment ≠ consensus authorization.** Completing a handshake and being mapped to validator
V at the transport layer does **not** confer authority to author consensus messages (proposals/votes/timeouts
require the ML-DSA consensus key, verified independently inside the engine). The one ingress that accepts
**no inner consensus signature** is restore-catchup (A17-F1) — which is precisely why transport impersonation
(A2-F1) is most consequential there. **Suite negotiation is fail-closed**, not downgradable: `init.kem_suite_id`
/`aead_suite_id` must equal the server's configured ids or `UnsupportedSuite` (`handshake.rs:855-860,1241-1246`);
the suite ids are also mixed into the KDF `info` (`keys.rs:292`), so a mismatch fails key agreement.

## A6.3 A2-F1 — identity and possession proof (both roles)
**Dialer authenticates listener (server-auth) — KEM-backed, sound.** The client verifies the server's
`NetworkDelegationCert` against `peer_root_network_pk` (`handshake.rs:441-467`), matches `validator_id`
(`:470-475`), checks validity window + leaf revocation (`:482-490`), and binds the full cert-derived
`server_node_id` (`:548-556`). Possession is proven implicitly: only a holder of the KEM private key
matching the cert's `leaf_kem_pk` can decapsulate the client's `kem_ct` and derive the matching session
keys; the first successful AEAD exchange is the (implicit) key confirmation — **there is no explicit
Finished/MAC message** (handshake is ClientInit → ServerAccept → Established; ServerAccept carries no
transcript MAC, `:1040-1049`). *Caller-binding note:* `handle_server_accept` does not itself re-assert
`delegation_cert.leaf_kem_pk == peer_kem_pk` (the key the client encapsulated to, supplied via
`ClientConnectionConfig.peer_kem_pk`); server-auth soundness therefore assumes the dialer sources
`peer_kem_pk` from the same verified cert identity. Recorded as a checked boundary, **not** a new finding.

**Listener authenticates dialer — cert presentation WITHOUT possession proof (the A2-F1 gap).** Map of each
claimed identity → its verification:

| Claimed value | What the server checks | Possession proven? |
|---|---|---|
| `init.validator_id` | (Disabled) taken verbatim as `peer_validator_id` (`:1037`) | No — self-asserted |
| client `NetworkDelegationCert` chain | parse + signature vs trusted root *if configured* (`:1156-1196`); else skipped (`:1167-1173`) | No — the root's signature over the cert is **public** |
| cert validity window / revocation | Run045 window, Run052 leaf fingerprint (`:1206-1214`) | No |
| cert `leaf_kem_pk` (the dialer's key) | **never used** — server decapsulates with **its own** `local_kem_sk` (`:988`); dialer performs the only KEM op (encaps to server) | **No — this is the gap** |
| binding to transcript | `client_cert` hashed into transcript (`:1006-1008`) | Binds the *claim* to the session, but the attacker also derives the same key (it performed the encaps), so the claim is unauthenticated |

**Impersonation trace (end to end).** (1) An attacker obtains a target validator's client delegation cert
bytes — transmitted **in cleartext** inside ClientInit v2 (the handshake precedes the AEAD session) and/or
published in trust material. (2) It opens a connection, performs its **own** ML-KEM encapsulation to the
listener's KEM public key, and sends a v2 ClientInit carrying the target's cert. (3) Rejection points it
must clear: unknown `root_key_id` → `ClientCertInvalid("untrusted root")`; bad signature under the real
suite → `KeySchedule`; expired/not-yet-valid → Run045; revoked leaf → Run052. **A genuine validator's cert
clears all of these** (that is the target of impersonation). (4) No possession check exists, so the server
completes the handshake and binds `peer_validator_id`/`client_node_id` to the target → the consensus
origin resolver sees the target's identity. **Authenticated identity becomes available** on the server at
the end of `verify_client_cert_if_required` — as an *asserted* (root-signed) identity, never a *possessed*
one. Transport impersonation is kept strictly separate from consensus-signature forgery (needs ML-DSA key)
and from the A17-F1 catch-up endorsement gap (no inner signature).

## A6.4 A11-F1 — replay and key/nonce reuse (state transitions at the mutation points)
**Session-key derivation inputs and their variability** (`keys.rs:279-316`; `AeadSession::new` `session.rs:130-149`):

| Input | Source | Changes per connection? | per restart? | only on rotation? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client_random` | `"qbind-client-<localValId>"` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1966-1968`) | **No (constant)** | No (pure fn of validator_id) | only if validator_id changes |
| `server_random` | `"qbind-server-<localValId>"` (`:1970-1972`) | **No (constant; independent of peer)** | No | only if validator_id changes |
| `kem_ct` → `shared_secret` | client ML-KEM encaps → server `decaps(local_kem_sk,·)` (`handshake.rs:375-377,988`) | **Yes under real ML-KEM** (randomized, `ml_kem768.rs` test `encapsulation_is_randomized`); **No under DummyKem** (deterministic) | n/a | n/a |
| `client_cert` | fixed self-issued cert | No | No | on cert rotation |
| `kem_suite_id`,`aead_suite_id` | config | No | No | on reconfig |
| `transcript_hash` | `SHA3("QBIND:KEMTLS"‖c_rand‖s_rand‖kem_ct‖client_cert?)` | tracks `kem_ct` only | — | — |
| `session_id`,`k_c2s`,`k_s2c` | deterministic HKDF (no fresh entropy) | tracks inputs only | — | — |

→ On the **PQC-active (real AEAD)** path the **only** per-connection-varying key input is `kem_ct`.

**Replayed-ClientInit state transitions (production listener, no cookie):**

| Mutation point | Code | State on an exact ClientInit replay |
|---|---|---|
| server key selection | `local_kem_sk` (fixed) | identical |
| decapsulation | `kem.decaps(sk, init.kem_ct)` (`handshake.rs:988`) | identical `shared_secret` (same ct ⇒ same ss) |
| transcript | `:1000-1009` | identical (all inputs constant/replayed) |
| key derivation | `SessionKeys::derive` (`keys.rs:279-316`) | identical `k_c2s`,`k_s2c`,`session_id` |
| session creation / counters | `AeadSession::new`; `counter:0` (`session.rs:64`) | **counters reset to 0 both directions** |
| replay cache / cookie / dup-session rule | `cookie_config:None` (`:2180`); none in `connection.rs`/`secure_channel.rs` | **none — replay not rejected** |
| app delivery | `recv_app → decrypt_app → c2s.open` (`secure_channel.rs:415-419`), AAD const (`transport.rs:10`) | nonce = `0x01‖session_id‖counter`; identical sequence |

**Precise conditions that REINSTALL the same key + nonce:** an exact replay of a recorded ClientInit (fixing
`kem_ct`) to the same listener (whose `server_random` is a fixed constant); holds **across process restarts**
(randoms, decaps, and `local_kem_sk` are all stable). On the DummyKem path `kem_ct` is also constant, so keys
repeat for *any* two connections — but DummyAead provides no confidentiality, so that case is moot.
**Conditions that PREVENT it (none present on the wired path):** a freshly-random `server_random` per
connection; a single-use `kem_ct`/`client_random` replay cache; or cookie enforcement with a fresh server
nonce (disabled). Nothing in the production listener supplies any of these.

**Downstream evidence chain (kept separate):**
- **A. Reinstallation of key/nonce state — SOURCE-ESTABLISHED.** Identical `k_c2s`/`k_s2c`/`session_id`;
  counters→0. (Corroborated by the existing unit test `session_keys_derive_is_deterministic`, `net_session_tests.rs:94`.)
- **B. Acceptance/decryption of previously recorded application ciphertext — SOURCE-SUPPORTED.** On the
  reinstalled session the server's `c2s` direction re-opens the recorded frames in order from counter 0 with
  the identical key+nonce and constant AAD → Poly1305 verifies → plaintext delivered. No anti-replay beyond
  the in-session monotone counter (`AeadDirection::open` `session.rs:84-89`). The server thus re-ingests the
  victim's earlier c2s messages. (This is pure ciphertext replay; the attacker needs no secret.)
- **C. First application plaintexts and counters — counters source-fixed, content UNEXECUTED.** Both directions
  start at counter 0; the first post-handshake plaintext **content** (the "content schedule") is produced by
  the consensus loop and is **not pinned without execution** — this is the exact residual boundary, not a
  generic "needs testing."
- **D. Different plaintexts under the same key/nonce — CRYPTOGRAPHIC CONSEQUENCE ESTABLISHED, CONDITIONAL.**
  If the reinstalled direction (notably `s2c`, driven by advanced consensus state) emits any plaintext that
  differs at a counter value already used in the recorded session, then real ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypts two
  different plaintexts under one (key, nonce): keystream reuse ⇒ `C₁⊕C₂ = P₁⊕P₂` (a two-time pad the attacker
  computes from ciphertext **without** the key; full recovery given known/structured consensus plaintext),
  **and** the Poly1305 one-time key is reused. The *triggering condition* (a differing plaintext at a reused
  nonce slot) is content/runtime-dependent ⇒ **UNEXECUTED**. Moot on the DummyAead path.
- **E. Application-level forgery / unauthorized effects — NOT ESTABLISHED; bounded.** (i) Replayed decrypted
  consensus messages (link B) carry the **original valid ML-DSA signatures** and stale views; the engine's
  staleness/monotonicity bounds their effect — a complete consensus-ingress dedup trace is a separate
  obligation. (ii) A transport-frame **forgery** via Poly1305 one-time-key reuse (link D) is cryptographically
  conceivable for the specific reused nonce slot given known plaintext, but any forged frame's **inner**
  payload must still be independently authenticated by the consensus layer (ML-DSA) to have consensus effect
  — **except** restore-catchup (A17-F1), which requires no inner signature. So the first-order unauthorized-
  effect surface of a transport forgery **coincides with the already-recorded A17-F1 gap**, not a new
  mechanism. **Missing evidence to close E (named):** (1) an executed demonstration that the reinstalled `s2c`
  direction emits ≥1 differing plaintext at a reused counter (link D trigger); (2) the actual first-message
  content schedule (link C); (3) a consensus-ingress dedup/staleness trace for replayed c2s messages.

**ServerAccept is a handshake packet, not AEAD application data** (E2 retained): it is sent before the AEAD
session is used for app traffic and must **not** be counted as new `s2c` encryption under the derived key.

## A6.5 Version negotiation / downgrade (executable only)
`ServerAccept.version = init.version` (echo, `:1041`); `MutualAuthMode` governs v1 acceptance. The only
executable downgrade is **mutual-auth presence**: under `Optional`/`Disabled` a peer capable of presenting a
cert may send v1 (or a certless v2) and be accepted with no client identity (`:1090-1092,:1101-1112`). This
strips identity; it does **not** by itself reinstall keys. There is **no** executable crypto-suite downgrade
(suite ids are matched exactly and bound into the KDF).

## A6.6 Test coverage read (not executed) — covers / omits
- `net_session_tests.rs`: `session_keys_derive_is_deterministic` (`:94`) and `…_different_for_different_inputs`
  (`:128`) — **confirm** the KDF determinism that underpins A11-F1; `aead_session_counters_advance_independently`
  (`:240`) — per-direction counters. **Omits** any cross-session nonce-uniqueness or replay-rejection assertion.
- `m8_mutual_auth_tests.rs`: cert-required/empty/parse-error/**signature-fail** (`:227-576`),
  successful-returns-node-id (`:677`), optional-v1 (`:798`), disabled-ignores-cert (`:889`),
  transcript-binding-includes-cert (`:985`). **Omits** any proof-of-possession test (none can exist without a
  PoP mechanism) — `test_successful_mutual_auth_returns_client_node_id` in fact exercises the A2-F1 model
  (identity accepted on presentation).
- `t141_aead_key_hygiene_tests.rs`: only **zeroization/Debug-no-leak/not-Clone** (`:153-233`) — memory hygiene,
  **not** (key,nonce) uniqueness. `run_045`/`run_052`: validity-window and leaf-revocation only.
- No test anywhere targets replay, key/nonce reuse, impersonation, keystream reuse, or forgery.

## A6.7 Disposition
- **A2-F1 — OPEN (source-confirmed, deepened).** Listener-side client authentication is cert-presentation
  without possession proof in every mode that accepts a cert; impersonable by any holder of a target's public
  client cert. Severity: identity-spoofing at the transport layer. Reachability: DevNet P2P listener in
  Required/Optional; trivial/irrelevant under Disabled (pure self-assertion). Confidence: high (source).
  Execution evidence: none. **Not** consensus forgery; its sharpest downstream use is A17-F1 catch-up.
- **A11-F1 — OPEN (source-confirmed, deepened).** Deterministic handshake randoms + deterministic KDF +
  counter-reset + no replay guard ⇒ exact-ClientInit-replay reinstalls identical (key, nonce) on the
  real-AEAD path. Links A/B source-established; D cryptographically-established-but-conditional; C/E unexecuted
  with the three named boundaries above. Severity: potential confidentiality loss (two-time pad) and a bounded
  transport-forgery surface on the PQC-active path. Confidence: high for A/B, medium-conditional for D, open
  for E. Execution evidence: none.
- **No new finding IDs minted.** The replay/keystream/forgery items are consequences of A11-F1 (and, for
  forgery effect, overlap A17-F1); the DummyAead observation corroborates QBIND-A1-F004. A6 counts none of
  these as separate defects.

- A2-F1 and A11-F1 re-traced first-hand at HEAD from CLI/builder config through handshake, KDF, session and
  inbound dispatch; dispositions follow the source trace. A5.3's A33-F1 conclusion and all completed timeout/
  ancestry analyses are retained, not reopened (no new contradictory evidence surfaced).
- Each obligation A6 could resolve from readable source is resolved; the three that remain (C content schedule,
  D differing-plaintext trigger, E ingress dedup) are named as exact boundaries, not deferred generically.

| **A33-F1** | **ENGINE-LEVEL NON-TERMINATION SOURCE-ESTABLISHED under the stated construction — A5.2's "NOT ESTABLISHED / needs an orphan" is WITHDRAWN (it was wrong).** Re-tracing the **exact registration-time state** (register_block inserts+queues+evicts **before** `on_vote`, `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1478-1486`; `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4008-4018`) shows the just-inserted candidate `B4096` is the **lock's child** (not an ancestor) and has **no own-QC yet**; the lock is still `B4095`. `is_block_safe_to_evict(B4096)` clause #2 walks **from the lock B4095 toward its parents** (`B4094→…→B1→A→A→…`) and **never encounters B4096**, reaching the self-loop `A` (`A.parent=A`) → **infinite walk** (`hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1105-1161`; unbounded, unlike `bounded_safety_decision:2198-2247`). ## A5.3.2 Three direct contradictions resolved
- **(A) Registration precedes votes.** `register_block` (`hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1478-1486`) inserts the
  node, pushes it to `pending_block_order`, and runs `evict_blocks_if_needed` — **all before**
  `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` calls `on_vote` for that block (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4008-4018`). So
  when eviction examines the newest candidate, it has **no own-QC** and the lock is **still the previous
  block**. A5.2 wrongly reasoned from the **post-vote** state (where the newest block would be the lock and
  carry own_qc), which hid the hang. **Corrected.**
- **(B) No re-commit of an already-committed G.** `try_commit_with_qc` sets `should_commit=false` when
  `committed_id == g_id` (`:1897-1902`). The snapshot sets `committed_block=A` (`initialize_from_snapshot_baseline`),
  so the first 3-chain `B2→B1→A` with `G=A` is **rejected** (already committed) — A5.2's "recommit A at
  height h+1" was wrong. The first **successful** commit is `G=B1@height 3` when **B3**'s QC forms
  (`committed_id=A ≠ B1`, `g_view 3 > A.view 2`, `g_height 3 > committed_height 1`). Thereafter `B_k`'s QC
  commits `B_{k-2}`; after **B4095** the committed block is **B4093 @ height 4095** (matches the recomputed
  table). **Corrected.**
- **(C) Eviction break is not a refusal.** `evict_blocks_if_needed` (`:1168-1187`) breaks via `if !evicted`
  **without** undoing the insertion or returning any capacity error; `blocks.len()` simply stays over the
  limit. A5.2's "bounded-growth refusal" framing is **withdrawn**. (Moreover, in this construction the loop
  does **not** reach that break — it **hangs** inside `is_block_safe_to_evict(B4096)` first.)

## A5.3.3 Concrete candidate — recomputed intermediate state (h=1; A = P16‖P16, P16 = LE64(leader_for_view(2))‖LE64(2))
`leader_for_view(v)=leaders[v % 4]` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2395-2399`); `two_thirds_vp = ceil(2·4/3)=3`,
so 3 distinct signers per block satisfy the logical `qc.validate` (`qc.rs:83-114`). Views/heights:
`A`: view 2, height **2** (after block0 overwrite; parent=A); `B_k`: view = height = `k+2`.

| Moment | blocks | lock (view) | committed (blk@h) | new candidate |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| after block0 (self-loop A) | 1 (A) | A (2) | A@1 | — |
| after B4095 + its votes | 4096 (A,B1..B4095) | **B4095 (4097)** | **B4093 @ 4095** | — |
| inserting **B4096**, inside eviction, **before** its votes | 4097 | **still B4095** | **B4093 @ 4095** | **B4096 @ 4098, no own-QC** |

**Eviction scan at B4096 (queue `[A,B1,…,B4096]`, popped front-first):**
- `A` → clause #1 `A.height 2 ≤ committed 4095` ⇒ `false` (no walk).
- `B1…B4093` (`height=j+2 ≤ 4095`) → clause #1 `false`.
- `B4094` (height 4096) → clause #2 walk from lock B4095: first step `parent(B4095)=B4094 == candidate` ⇒ `false`.
- `B4095` → clause #2 line-1 `candidate == locked` ⇒ `false`.
- `B4096` (height 4098, lock's **child**) → clause #1 no; clause #2 walk `B4095→B4094→…→B1→A→A→…`:
  B4096 is never a parent on this chain, and `A.parent=A` ⇒ **non-terminating walk (HANG)**.

The walk from the lock follows **older** parents toward A; B4096 (a descendant) is never reached, so the
`parent_id == candidate` early-return never fires for it, and the self-loop makes the `while let Some(..)`
never hit a `None`-parent break. **Verified against every clause and the committed/locked/ancestor early
returns; no separately-admitted orphan is required.** Accounted for: vote-accumulator/vote-history/commit-log
evictions prune their own maps (not the block tree) and do not remove `A` or the `B4095→…→A` chain;
`A` is never evicted (clause #1, stored height 2 ≤ committed 4095); all arithmetic is within `u64`.

## A5.3.4 Admission and size (production prerequisites, kept separate)
- **Snapshot (metadata vs bootable validator):** `validate_snapshot_dir` accepts an operator-chosen opaque
  `block_hash` (A5.2) — but the operator must additionally **successfully start a configured P2P
  validator**: a valid non-empty `state/` the node can materialize, and an authority/epoch/genesis marker
  matching the node (`enforce_authority_marker_check`). This is a **local/operator** capability over the
  node's own data dir, not a remote one.
- **Inbound response size — admissible.** The exporter cap `RESTORE_CATCHUP_MAX_BLOCKS_PER_RESPONSE = 128`
  is applied **only** by the honest responder `handle_restore_catchup_request` (`:8394-8398`); the **inbound**
  `handle_restore_catchup_response`/`apply_restore_catchup_blocks` impose **no** `blocks.len()` cap. A
  malicious responder crafts the frame directly. Size (bincode 1.3.3; `p2p_tcp.rs:146-191`): per
  `RestoreCatchupBlock` = 8+8+32+32+2 + (8 Vec-len + 3·2) = **96 B**; 4097 blocks = 393,312; response
  (incl. `responder_committed_height=Some`, +Vec len) = **393,371**; enum tags → **393,379**; discriminator
  + u32 length prefix → application frame **393,384 B**. This is **far below** the ~16 MiB transport
  ciphertext cap (`MAX_TRANSPORT_CIPHERTEXT`), so AEAD framing overhead is immaterial and the frame is
  accepted by `decode_frame`. (Source/arithmetic only; no serialization executed.)

1. **Algebraic self-loop** — ESTABLISHED (A5.1).
2. **Engine-level non-terminating walk** — **ESTABLISHED (source trace, §A5.3.3)**; reached by the newest

| **A33-F1** | **CONDITIONAL — production non-termination NOT established; A5.1's "finite non-returning-walk construction" is WITHDRAWN/CORRECTED.** The latent defect is real and unchanged: `is_block_safe_to_evict` (`hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1105-1161`) has **no cycle/visited/depth guard** (vs the engine's bounded `bounded_safety_decision` `:2198-2247`), and a self-loop `A=P16‖P16` is algebraically derivable (concatenating `derive_block_id_from_header`, A5.1). **But** the walk returns `false` via the per-step `parent_id == candidate` check (clauses #2 `:1123-1132`, #4 `:1146-1156`) **before** ever revisiting the self-loop, for **every** candidate the inspected admission paths can co-resident (the committed anchor → clause #1 `:1107-1112`; any lock-ancestor → clause #2/#4 early match). A genuine non-returning walk needs a **co-resident candidate C ∉ {A, committed, lock-ancestry}** — an **orphan/fork** node — which linear catch-up cannot create (contiguous `parent==expected_parent`) and the production proposal path does not admit (fail-closed `pv_authority=None`; `plan_leader_registration` rejects same-id `CandidateCollision` `:1234-1235`). | **Layered (see §A5.2.4):** self-loop algebra ✓; snapshot-loader accepts an operator-chosen opaque anchor ✓ (local/operator capability; `validate_snapshot_dir` does **not** content-verify `block_hash`); admitted catch-up can install the self-loop ✓ (conditional); **capacity-triggered non-returning walk ✗ — first unresolved step: admitting a co-resident non-ancestry orphan block via a production path.** Remote actor is blocked earlier (cannot author the snapshot/anchor). set) are **unchanged** by A5.2; A5.1's completed corrections stand.

## A5.2.2 Item 1 — snapshot-admission boundary (resolved at source)
Executable chain: production restore → `validate_and_authorize_for_restore` (`snapshot_restore.rs:537-568`)
→ `validate_snapshot_for_restore` (`:720`) → `qbind_ledger::validate_snapshot_dir`
(`state_snapshot.rs:1189-1252`), plus `enforce_authority_marker_check` (`:741+`).
- **`block_hash` is operator-supplied and NOT content-verified.** `StateSnapshotMeta::from_json`
  (`state_snapshot.rs:503-544`) parses `block_hash` as 64 hex chars verbatim. `validate_snapshot_dir`
  checks only: `meta.json` parses, `chain_id == expected`, `height != 0`, `state/` exists and is
  non-empty (`:1213-1251`). **No check ties `block_hash` to state/checkpoint content.**
- **The authority marker binds identity, not the anchor.** `enforce_authority_marker_check` routes to
  `verify_snapshot_authority_state_for_restore[_v2]`, comparing the snapshot's authority block to the
  runtime **env / chain_id / genesis_hash** (`RestoreAuthorityContext`, `:589-599`); the legacy no-context
  path fails closed if a local marker exists (`:553-560`). None of this constrains `block_hash`.
- **Conclusion (bounded to the inspected route):** an actor who can **author the snapshot directory**
  (write `meta.json` with `block_hash = A = P16‖P16`, matching `chain_id`, `height = h`, a non-empty
  `state/`, and an authority block matching the node's accepted env/chain/genesis) obtains an accepted
  restore with the opaque anchor `A`. This is a **local/operator** capability. **First rejecting guard for
  a remote-anonymous attacker:** it cannot write the snapshot dir / set `block_hash` — blocked before any
  consensus effect. A local prerequisite here does **not** prove every remote construction impossible; it
  bounds *this* route.

## A5.2.3 Item 2 — evolving-state recomputation (corrects A5.1 T2)
Catch-up loop order (per block): `register_block` (→ `evict_blocks_if_needed`) **then** `on_vote`→`on_qc`
(`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4008-4018`). `leader_for_view(v) = leaders[v % n]` round-robin (`:2395-2399`).
State after each transition (anchor `A` at height `h`; `Lk = leader_for_view`):

| Step | Register | blocks (id→parent@height) | own_qc | locked_qc (view) | committed (blk@h) | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| snapshot | insert A | A→∅@h | — | None | A@h | anchor, parent None |
| block0 | A, parent=A (same-id overwrite, `:1471-1478`) | A→A@h+1 (self-loop) | A | **A (h+1)** | A@h | `on_qc` sets lock=A, A.own_qc |
| block1 | B1=derive(L_{h+2},h+2,A), parent=A | A→A@h+1, B1→A@h+2 | A,B1 | **B1 (h+2)** | A@h | lock **advances off A**; commit: G=parent(P=A)=A ⇒ G=P=A, `g_view<p_view` fails `:1886` → no commit |
| block2 | B2=derive(L_{h+3},h+3,B1), parent=B1 | …,B2→B1@h+3 | A,B1,B2 | **B2 (h+3)** | **A@h+1** | 3-chain B2→B1→A with h+1<h+2<h+3 ✓ ⇒ commit G=A@h+1 (`:1918-1920`) |
| block k≥2 | Bk→B(k-1)@h+k+1 | linear chain A←B1←…←Bk | all | **Bk** | advancing along the chain | lock = newest Bk; committed trails by 2 |

**Key corrections:** (a) the lock does **not** remain `A` — `on_qc` advances it to each higher-view QC
(`:1787-1793`); (b) the self-loop makes `G == P == A` in the first commit attempt so the strictly-increasing
-view guard (`:1886`) **fails**, and commit only proceeds once a genuine linear suffix exists, then commits
`A` (which clause #1 thereafter protects). Evaluating the **newest** block `Bk` at the first overflow as a
candidate: `Bk` is the lock → clause #2 line-1 `false`. Every other queued candidate is either `A`
(committed → clause #1 `false`) or an ancestor `Bj` of the lock (clause #2 descent matches
`parent_id==Bj` and returns `false`) — **all before** the walk reaches the `A→A` step. So
`evict_blocks_if_needed` finds nothing safe and `break`s (`:1182-1185`): bounded-growth **refusal**, not a
hang.

## A5.2.4 Item 3 — capacity/transport, and item 4 — layered disposition
- **Capacity:** `max_pending_blocks` default **4096** (`vote_accumulator.rs:123`). Admission check is
  `>= max` (`:1237`, leader path) / `can_admit_block_slot` (`:910-923`); legacy eviction is `> max`
  (`:1170`). The anchor overwrite (block0) is a **replacement** (`is_new == false`, not re-queued); only
  **distinct** blocks (B1…) grow the count. Reaching `> 4096` therefore needs ~4096 distinct contiguous
  catch-up blocks in one response; `leader_for_view` forces each `proposer = leaders[view % n]`, so the
  operator/peer must emit the round-robin-correct proposer per view. **But per §A5.2.3 this does not
  produce a hang** (no non-ancestry candidate), so the exact byte-size/leader schedule is moot for
  non-termination and is **not** asserted.
- **Transport:** inbound `RestoreCatchupResponse` is bincode-decoded; the only size bound found is the
  transport frame cap (~16 MiB). No dedicated inbound per-message block-count cap surfaced in the inspected
  decode path (residual if pursued). The A5.1 "thousands of ~90-byte blocks fit" inference is **not** used
  as support for any effect.
- **Layered disposition:**
  1. Algebraic self-loop possibility — **ESTABLISHED** (A5.1).
  2. Snapshot-loader acceptance of an operator-chosen opaque anchor — **ESTABLISHED, local/operator**
     capability, inspected route (§A5.2.2).
  3. Admitted catch-up installing the self-loop into live `blocks` — **CONDITIONAL-ESTABLISHED** (requires
     transport admission + anchor-equality; identity impersonable via A2-F1, no consensus key).
  4. Capacity-triggered non-returning eviction walk — **NOT ESTABLISHED.** First unresolved/rejecting step:
     a co-resident candidate `C ∉ {A, committed, lock-ancestry}`; linear catch-up and the fail-closed
     proposal path do not produce one.
  5. Runtime observation — **NONE (UNEXECUTED).**
  **Overall:** A33-F1 is a **real latent unguarded-walk defect** with an **operator-admittable self-loop**,
  but a **reachable non-termination is not proven**; it is **CONDITIONAL**, blocked at layer 4 (and, for a
  remote actor, already at layer 2). The production construction is **not** called proved.

## A5.1.2 Correction 1 — withdraw the false block-ID (SHA3/collision) assumption
A5 (§A5.0/§A5.4 of the layer below) stated the catch-up path's `block_id` derivation is SHA3 and used
**collision resistance** to argue a remote attacker cannot forge a same-id/forward-parent block. **This is
false and is withdrawn.** First-hand at HEAD, `derive_block_id_from_header`
(`crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3865-3879`):
```
id[0..8]  = LE64(proposer);  id[8..16] = LE64(view);  id[16..32] = parent_block_id[0..16]
```
No hash. Let `P16 = LE64(proposer)‖LE64(view)` (16 bytes). If a parent `A = P16‖P16`, then
`derive(proposer,view,A) = P16‖A[0..16] = P16‖P16 = A` — a **self-parent**, reachable by **plain
algebra**, no collision. The identity alone proves **neither** production admission **nor** an executed
attack (that is §A5.1.3–§A5.1.4). The A5 wording is retained below as superseded evidence.

## A5.1.3 Correction 2 — A33-F1 admission, re-traced at HEAD (ordered state transitions)

Actor classes kept separate: **remote-anonymous**, **admitted-peer** (transport-bound, impersonable per
A2-F1 — no consensus key), **local/operator** (restore input), **artificial** (direct state edits — not
counted). A proposed cycle is accepted only if **all** prerequisites coexist; else the first rejecting
guard is named.

**T1 — install a self-loop by overwriting the restore anchor via catch-up**
| # | State before | Actor/input | Guard (source) | Mutation / result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | engine fresh | **local/operator** restore: `snapshot_block_id = A = P16‖P16`, `snapshot_height = h`, with `P16 = LE64(leader_for_view(h+1))‖LE64(h+1)` | restore is locally-trusted (chain-id/anti-rollback/epoch; **not** signature-authenticated; anchor id is an **opaque** `block_hash`, `:2029-2033`) | `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` inserts node `A` {parent=None, height=h, own_qc=None}; `committed_block=A`, `committed_height=h` (`:2053-2082`) |
| 2 | `blocks={A@h}` | **admitted-peer** `RestoreCatchupResponse` | dispatch sender-binding `binary_consensus_loop.rs:7392-7409` (impersonable id, A2-F1); handler anchor-equality `committed==request_from_*` (`:8454-8456`) | enters `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` |
| 3 | — | block0: height=h+1, view=h+1, parent=A, proposer=`leader_for_view(h+1)`, `qc_signer_indices`=any ≥⅔ voting-power set | structural: height==expected ✓, parent==expected_parent(A) ✓, height==view ✓, proposer==leader ✓, `block_id==derive(proposer,view,A)=A` ✓ (algebra), `qc.validate` logical ✓ (no signatures, `qc.rs:83-114`) | `register_block(A, view=h+1, parent=Some(A), …)` — legacy path **replaces** anchor node (`:1455-1487`, same-id overwrite `:1471-1478`) ⇒ **`A.parent = A` (self-loop)**, height=h+1 |
| 4 | self-loop `A` | block0 signers → `on_vote` → `on_qc` | `on_qc` (`:1782-1804`) | `A.own_qc = Some` (`:1797-1799`); `locked_qc = A` (view h+1 > prior) (`:1793`) |

*First rejecting guard for a pure **remote** attacker:* step 1 — a remote actor cannot set the opaque
`snapshot_block_id`. The **leader/proposal** path is also **not** a vector: `plan_leader_registration`
rejects `CandidateCollision` on an existing id (`:1234-1235`), so same-id overwrite is unavailable there.
The catch-up **legacy** `register_block` is the only inspected path admitting the overwrite.

## A5.1.4 Correction 3 — non-termination proved precisely (which walk reaches the cycle)

A cycle in `blocks` does **not** make every eviction check hang. `is_block_safe_to_evict(C)`
(`:1105-1161`) has ordered early returns: clause #1 committed-height; clause #2 locked-ancestor walk;
clause #3 candidate `own_qc`; clause #4 own_qc-ancestor walks. The hang occurs **inside** a walk, before
any return; the outer `evict_blocks_if_needed` `if !evicted break` (`:1182-1185`) is never reached.

**T2 — non-returning walk (continues from T1; `A` is a self-loop with `own_qc` and is `locked`)**
| # | Condition | Guard reached | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | catch-up supplies further contiguous blocks until `blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks` (default 4096) | `register_block` → `evict_blocks_if_needed` (`:1486,1168-1170`) | eviction loop pops candidate `C` from `pending_block_order` |
| 2 | candidate `C ≠ A` | `is_block_safe_to_evict(C)` clause #2: `locked_block_id = A`; `C != A` so no early `false`; walk `current_id=A` → `blocks[A].parent=Some(A)` → `parent_id(A) == C`? **no** → `current_id=A` … | **infinite loop** (also independently via clause #4: `A` has `own_qc`, walk from `A` self-loops) |

**Finite source-level construction reached** (consensus-task non-termination). **Prerequisites that must
coexist:** (local) operator-crafted opaque anchor `A=P16‖P16` + `committed_height` aligned to
`leader_for_view(h+1)`; (admitted-peer) one catch-up responder passing transport-binding + anchor-equality,
supplying a ≥⅔ voting-power logical signer set **and** enough blocks to exceed `max_pending_blocks` in one
bounded response (≤16 MiB frame admits thousands of ~90-byte `RestoreCatchupBlock`s). **Not** remote-anonymous;
**no** hash collision. **Unresolved / unexecuted (do not overclaim):** (a) whether the real snapshot loader
(`snapshot_restore.rs`) imposes any integrity/manifest constraint on the opaque `block_hash`/anchor id
beyond chain-id/epoch (not deep-read this pass); (b) the exact `leader_for_view` schedule making proposer
match at `h+1`; (c) that `max_pending_blocks` saturation is reached before the response ends; (d) runtime
CPU/liveness impact — **E27, NOT EXECUTED**. This is a source-derived construction, not a runtime
reproduction.

## A5.1.5 Correction 4 — lock-mutation inventory and attribution
- **Three distinct `locked_qc` mutation routes** (keep separate; do not collapse into "all verified"):
  1. **`on_qc:1793`** — `self.locked_qc = Some(qc)` for a higher-view formed QC; reached by **ordinary
     and restore-catchup** vote processing (`on_vote → on_vote_detailed → on_qc`). **Not** F7/signature-verified
     — this is the **A17-F1** catch-up lock path and the T1-step-4 enabler.
  2. **`set_locked_qc:1943`** — direct setter; the **only** production caller is `on_timeout_certificate`
     (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5177`), i.e. the **TC** path, which the node handler **F7-gates** before
     calling (A1-F3, both production callers `binary_consensus_loop.rs:7329,:7938`). A1-F3's conclusion is
     scoped to **this** route.
  3. **restart-init `:2002`** (`initialize_from_restart`, sim/test per A4) — sets `locked_qc` from a
     supplied Option; the **production** `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` (`:2053-2082`) sets **no**
     `locked_qc`.
  So A5's "only production lock-install is 5177" is narrowed: it is the only **`set_locked_qc`** site; the
  `on_qc` route (1793) also installs locks, unverified, via the catch-up path (A17-F1).
- **Attribution fix:** A5's §A5.5 attributed the "any ≥⌈2/3⌉ indices" shorthand to "A4/v1.52." **v1.52 did
  not introduce it — v1.52 already corrected it** to the voting-power-weighted `two_thirds_vp` threshold

## A5.3 Restore-catchup state effects (A17-F1) — three submechanisms

Admission chain (source): dispatch `binary_consensus_loop.rs:7392-7409` binds `responder_validator_index`
to the authenticated transport origin (Run 418; **impersonable** per A2-F1, no consensus key); binding gate
is populated only for Required/Optional mutual-auth + static-root PQ (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1583-1687`, else
empty→refuse). Handler `:8426-8520`: rejects self-addressed (`:8433`); applies blocks only if
`committed_height==request_from_height` **and** `committed_block==request_from_block_id` (`:8454-8456`);
**no outstanding-request or restore-mode-active gate on application.**

**(1) Missing quorum-endorsement verification** (source-confirmed)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Victim committed at anchor (H,B); P2P wired | Transport identity of a mapped validator (A2-F1 cert, **no** consensus key) | Contiguous blocks from B; `qc_signer_indices` = any configured set meeting voting-power `two_thirds_vp` | PASS: transport-bind, anchor-equality, structural (`:3963-4002`), **logical** `qc.validate` (`qc.rs:83-114`, **no signatures**). FAIL: none crypto | `register_block`+`on_vote` per block → logical QC via `on_qc` | consensus-metadata advancement along an **unendorsed** chain (no tx/state payload). Finality/divergence harm **UNEXECUTED** |

**(2) Accepted-prefix survives a later-block error** (source-confirmed; not atomic)
| Initial | Capability | Input | Guards | Mutation | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| As above | As above | Valid prefix [0..k) then an invalid block k | prefix PASSes per-block; block k fails a structural/`qc.validate` check → `Err` | prefix `register_block`/`on_vote`/any `on_qc` commit **persist** (no rollback); final `set_view` **skipped** on `Err` (`:4029-4031`) | handler's "did NOT mutate" log (`:8520`) is **inaccurate** for partial prefixes; a short prefix mutates block/vote state without necessarily committing (3-chain prerequisites, `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1782-1918`) |

**(3) Peer-asserted restore target / exit** (guarded; liveness scope)
| Initial | Capability | Input | Guards (`maybe_exit_after_response` `:2386-2424`) | Mutation | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Restore mode **active** | Transport identity | `responder_committed_height` (self-reported) | active-only; stores **monotonic max**; requires local height ≥ that max **and** strict progress above the snapshot baseline before exit; empty/stale cannot exit at baseline; a smaller later report cannot lower the max; inactive ⇒ no reactivation | restore-mode flag / target | a high **unsupported** report can raise the target while active (availability, conditional, **UNEXECUTED**); cannot force a premature exit at baseline |

**not** cover valid-prefix/invalid-suffix atomicity (submechanism 2); restore-mode tests
`binary_consensus_loop.rs:~9957-10101` (names ≠ assertion coverage).

## A5.4 A33-F1 revalidation (cyclic ancestry walk)

- **Non-termination mechanism — CONFIRMED present at HEAD.** `is_block_safe_to_evict`
  (`hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1105-1161`) clauses #2 (`:1121-1133`) and #4 (`:1143-1158`) follow
  `parent_id` via `while let Some(current)=self.blocks.get(current_id)` with **no visited set, depth
  bound, or cycle detection**; callers are the eviction paths (`:899,:953,:969,:1174`) under capacity
  pressure (`blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks`). A `blocks` parent cycle ⇒ infinite loop (consensus-task
  hang).
- **Cycle admission — UNRESOLVED / BLOCKED for remote input.** A cycle needs a block whose `id` already
  exists but whose `parent_id` is reset to point forward. `register_block` (`:1455-1487`) **does** replace
  a prior node for the same id including its `parent_id` (`:1473-1478`, `insert_block_node`). But the
  production write paths constrain the id: the restore-catchup path requires `block.block_id ==
  derive_block_id_from_header(proposer,view,parent)` and `parent == expected_parent` (contiguous), so a
  **remote** input cannot produce a same-id/forward-parent node **without a block-id (SHA3) hash
  collision** — not admitted. The only identified admission is an **operator-crafted restore
  `snapshot_block_id`** that later coincides with a catch-up block's derived id (the v1.48 §26.2N /
  **E22** `D(P,A)=A` fixed-point premise) — a **local/operator** capability, not anonymous-remote.
- **Disposition:** mechanism source-confirmed; **remote reachability not established** (precise missing
  step: a production input that writes a same-id/forward-parent node without a hash collision). The
  local-operator-crafted-anchor route remains a premise; runtime CPU/liveness impact **UNEXECUTED (E27)**.
  Per instruction: a loop that would hang on an artificially corrupted in-memory graph does **not** by
  itself establish remote reachability.

## 3. Independent A4 review — corrections and bounded evidence

This section records ChatGPT's read-only source cross-check at the pinned commit. A4 remains useful evidence but its delivered master was incomplete, and several requested static-source questions were deferred despite adjacent source resolving them. A4 is not accepted as complete on those grounds. This review supplies the bounded resolutions below; it does not claim a complete security review of the files or callers.

### 3.1 A1-F1: handler refusal is a source control

`crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs:7019–7030` and `:7208–7220` explicitly reject absent verification context before inbound Timeout/NewView verification and effects. The local TC helper takes `&TimeoutVerificationContext` rather than an optional context (`:7863`, `:7880`). This supports A4's correction of A3; it is more than startup containment. Do not assert that all other production callers have been inventoried, or merge the distinct catch-up endorsement mechanism into this historical timeout-context finding.

### 3.2 A1-F2: signed timed-out view binding is present

`crates/qbind-consensus/src/timeout.rs:157–187` serializes the timeout view into the signing preimage (`:170`). `timeout_verify.rs:292–304` supplies that view to the verified preimage. In `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`, target validation occurs at `:376`; each evidence view must equal `tc.timeout_view` at `:409–416`, followed by `verify_timeout_msg`. The target rule uses `checked_add(1)` at `timeout.rs:294–311`. This closes A4's *static-source uncertainty* about cross-binding; it does not constitute executed validation or full finding closure.

`TimeoutCertificate::new` and `new_with_evidence` use `saturating_add(1)` (`timeout.rs:383–410`), so construction at MAX can produce an object that validation must reject. Do not describe the constructors themselves as checked. The accumulator's inspected construction path groups evidence by view (`:674–712`). Tests present in inline `timeout_verify.rs` include `run422_tc_target_view_valid_successor_is_accepted` (:709), `run422_tc_target_view_rejects_signed_evidence_with_substituted_target` (:731), `run422_tc_target_view_rejects_before_signature_backend_calls` (:765), `run422_tc_target_view_accepts_largest_representable_successor` (:855), and `verify_mixed_view_tc_is_rejected` (:971). Presence and inspected assertions are not test results.

### 3.3 A1-F3: local TC applies F7 before the effect

`apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view_with_auth` in `binary_consensus_loop.rs:7875–7967` verifies signed TC evidence (:7886–7907), calls `admit_f7_retained_high_qc` (:7908–7919), confirms the admitted claim before effect (:7920–7936), and only then invokes `engine.on_timeout_certificate` (:7938). Errors return before application/broadcast. The wrapper passes no current-auth snapshot, so a high-QC-bearing claim cannot bypass that F7 refusal through this wrapper. The engine's lock installation (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5169–5178`) is not self-guarding. The local TC question is resolved for this inspected helper; completeness across the repository is a separate remaining obligation.

### 3.4 A17-F1: logical votes can reach QC/commit processing

The inspected catch-up loop (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3944–4034`) validates structure and a logical QC, registers each accepted block, and feeds supplied signer IDs through `state.on_vote`. `qc.rs:83–114` checks membership, distinctness and accumulated **voting power**, not signature endorsements. The threshold is `ceil(2 * total_voting_power / 3)` (`validator_set.rs:488–494`). A4's shorthand “any ≥⌈2/3⌉ indices” is inadequate: actual configured voting weights and the distinct-validator threshold matter.

In `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1692–1714`, ordinary `on_vote` reaches `on_vote_detailed`, forms a logical QC and calls `on_qc`; it does not use the separate effect-gated method beginning at :1717. The inspected `on_qc` updates lock/own-QC state and attempts commit (:1782–1802). Commit logic still requires the resident B/P/G chain, the required QCs, increasing views, and height/commit-view progression (:1828–1918). Equivocation history can suppress votes (:1737 onward). Thus fabricated signer indices are not equivalent to valid signatures, but neither does every arbitrary response necessarily commit. End-to-end divergence, persistence, finality, and downstream execution harm remain unexecuted and require their own evidence.

Accepted-prefix mutation is source-supported: earlier loop iterations register blocks and process votes before a later structural/QC error returns. No rollback appears in this function; final `set_view` is skipped on error. A sufficiently prepared prefix may reach QC/commit effects subject to the preceding prerequisites, but a short prefix can mutate block/vote state without a commit. The handler's unconditional no-mutation log at `binary_consensus_loop.rs:8520` is inaccurate for this partially-valid case. Treat endorsement verification and atomicity as separate proof/closure obligations under A17-F1, not automatically as two independently proven runtime attacks.

### 3.5 Transport admission constrains catch-up reachability

`p2p_node_builder.rs:1583–1687` constructs a binding gate and returns `Some(gate)` in the inspected builder. It populates the authoritative identity map for Required **or Optional** mutual-auth plus active static-root PQ mode. Other combinations leave an empty map; an absent/unknown authenticated origin is refused by the installed gate. The inbound resolver requires `mutual_auth_complete`, certificate-derived fields and an approved NodeId/ValidatorId pair. Catch-up dispatch also applies sender binding (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:7392–7409`).

Therefore an open listener or dummy transport does not by itself prove catch-up application ingress. A2-F1 concerns possession proof for an otherwise accepted public certificate; to chain it into A17-F1, trace that certificate through the actual configured trust checks, map, origin resolver, sender binding and committed anchor. Certificate possession is not consensus signing-key possession. R3/R4 shorthand must not replace the full configuration matrix. This cross-check does not test a handshake or any deployed configuration.

### 3.6 Restore-mode target is peer asserted, but exit has guards

The response height is transport-delivered and peer asserted; it lacks an independently checked quorum endorsement on the inspected path. “Unauthenticated” must not imply the absence of every transport admission check. `maybe_exit_after_response` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:2386–2424`) only operates while active, stores the **maximum** reported height, requires a local committed height at least that maximum, and requires strict local progress above the snapshot baseline before exit. An empty/stale response alone cannot exit while local height remains at the baseline; a smaller later report cannot lower a previous maximum. A high unsupported report can raise the target while active; resulting availability harm remains conditional and unexecuted. Once inactive, this method does not reactivate restore mode. Assess this policy separately from a cryptographic commit-safety claim.

### 3.7 Test-source inventory correction

A4's search under `crates/*/tests` was not a complete test inventory. Inline tests exist in `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs`: `restore_catchup_applies_valid_peer_learned_suffix_above_snapshot` (:10320) constructs a four-block suffix and asserts committed progress; `restore_catchup_rejects_malformed_parent_fail_closed` (:10345) rejects a malformed **first and only** block and checks unchanged height/log. The latter does not cover valid-prefix/invalid-suffix atomicity. Inline restore-mode tests also exist in `binary_consensus_loop.rs` around :9957–10101; names alone are not complete assertion coverage. No tests were executed by this review. These observations correct inventory gaps, not project code.

### 3.8 A3 corrections retained from A4

A4 corrects `ServerAccept.delegation_cert` to the server's own certificate, distinguishes that handshake packet from AEAD application data, narrows consensus-authorship protection to signature-checked paths (excluding this catch-up gap), and corrects A1-F1's earlier containment-only description. Preserve these corrections as attributed A4 evidence. The original A3 text below remains unchanged for traceability.

**A17-F1 refinements surfaced by A4 (same ID, not new findings):**
- **(e) Failure atomicity — handler comment inaccurate.** `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` mutates **per
  iteration** (`register_block` + `on_vote`, and any resulting QC/commit) and advances `set_view` **only
  after** the loop; on a later-block error it returns `Err` with the **accepted prefix already mutated**
  (no rollback). The handler's "a rejected response did NOT mutate engine" log (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:8520`)
  is therefore **inaccurate for partially-valid responses** — only the final `set_view` is skipped.
- **(f) Restore-mode exit on unauthenticated self-report.** `evaluate_restore_mode_transition`
  (`:8536-8544`) feeds the **sender-controlled** `responder_committed_height` into
  `restore_mode.maybe_exit_after_response(...)` even on empty/stale/anchor-mismatch responses
  (`:8441-8475`); the only authentication is the (impersonable) transport identity. Scope: restore-mode
  **liveness/availability** (premature or withheld catch-up exit), not a safety-commit by itself.

All other findings (A2-F1, A7-F1, A11-F1, A21-F1, QBIND-A1-F002/F003/F004/F006, and the §1C NYR@CB set
including **A33-F1**) are **unchanged from the §S snapshot**; A4 did not revalidate them.

## A4. Detailed revalidation (timeout / NewView / restore-catchup)

### A4.1 A1-F1 — missing verification context
- **Historical claim:** a context-absent path permits consensus processing of Timeout/TC without
  signature verification.
- **Current evidence:** both inbound handlers **fail-closed at the handler** on `verification_ctx ==
  None` (`let Some(ctx) = verification_ctx else { …reject; return }`, Timeout `:7019-7030`, NewView
  `:7208-7220`) — **before** `verify_timeout_msg` / `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`, the F7
  admission, and any accumulator/lock/view effect. This is in addition to the mandatory startup preflight
  (`RequireOrFail`, `main.rs:5695`,`:6078-6134`) and is a **source-level control the handler enforces
  independently of startup**. LocalMesh (`main.rs:5485+`) constructs no context but exposes no external
  consensus ingress.
- **Disposition:** **SOURCE-ADDRESSED on inspected inbound production paths, execution-verification
  pending.** This **corrects A3 §6** ("underlying code unchanged; containment only"): the current source
  contains explicit refusal branches. Not closed: a lower-level engine API still assumes validated input,
  so the remaining obligation is to prove **no** context-absent production caller (notably local TC
  processing `~:7908`, and the restore-catchup path, which is a **different** mechanism — A17-F1) reaches
  a consensus effect, plus behavioral evidence.

### A4.2 A1-F2 — timeout-certificate target-view binding
- **Historical claim:** `target_view` is not constrained to the authenticated timed-out view.
- **Current evidence:** `validate_timeout_target_view` (`timeout.rs:294-311`) requires `target_view ==
  timeout_view.checked_add(1)`, returning `NotImmediateSuccessor` otherwise and `SuccessorOverflow` at
  `u64::MAX`. It is reached on **both** TC paths: the engine application path `on_timeout_certificate`
  (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5159`) via `TimeoutCertificate::validate` → `validate_target_view`
  (`timeout.rs:424,430,467`), and the evidence-verification path
  `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (`timeout_verify.rs:376`, before signer-set allocation).
- **Disposition:** **SOURCE-FIX-IDENTIFIED, execution-verification pending.** Repair scope = immediate-
  successor binding + overflow handling on both inspected paths. **Remaining:** confirm `tc.timeout_view`
  is itself cross-bound to the signed evidence (so target binding can't be satisfied with a mismatched
  signed view), that local TC construction preserves the invariant, and execute the boundary matrix
  (correct successor; same/backward/skipped; `MAX-1`→`MAX`; overflow at `MAX`; target substitution with
  otherwise-valid evidence). Test-source exists (≥5 refs in `crates/qbind-consensus/tests`) but was
  **not executed** and the exact cases were not enumerated this pass.

### A4.3 A1-F3 — reported high-QC vs verified endorsement
- **Historical claim:** a timeout signer's **reported** high-QC is installed as a lock without evidence
  the referenced block received a quorum of votes.
- **Current evidence:** the node gates high-QC through F7 before any effect — `admit_f7_retained_high_qc`
  (`:1537-1622`): `None` logical-QC ⇒ `NoQc`; `None` snapshot/`current_auth` ⇒ **`AuthorityUnavailable`
  refusal**; otherwise requires engine-epoch/membership/chain agreement, a **retained on-tree evidence
  lookup** (`retained_qc_for_timeout_projection`; `MissingRetainedProof` if absent), a working-set bound,
  and **`reverify_quorum_certificate_with_domain`** (real signature/domain/membership re-verification).
  `confirm_f7_high_qc_before_effect` (`:1490-1504`) re-confirms the **same** admitted claim immediately
  before effect (else `OperationSubstituted`). Applied on inbound Timeout (`:7065-7094`) and NewView
  (`~:7294`). In production `current_auth` is `None`, so any high-QC-bearing timeout/TC is refused.
- **Caveat (engine lock-install is not self-guarding):** `on_timeout_certificate` installs `locked_qc`
  from `tc.high_qc` whenever `tc.high_qc.view > locked.view` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:5169-5178`) with
  **no F7 check inside the engine** — protection depends on the node handler running F7 first.
- **Disposition:** **SOURCE-GATED on inspected inbound paths + production fail-closed (snapshot `None`),
  execution-verification pending.** The old unverified-lock-install scenario is not reachable on the
  inspected inbound paths with `current_auth=None`. **Remaining:** confirm **every** `on_timeout_certificate`
  caller (local TC processing `~:7908` and any other) applies F7 or supplies only re-verified high-QC;
  execution proof. Not closed.

### A4.4 A17-F1 — restore-catchup endorsement (priority deep trace)
Bounded static trace (source-derived, **not** a runtime reproduction):
- **Initial state:** honest victim with `committed_height = H`, `committed_block = B` (anchor), P2P wired
  (R3/R4), capable of processing `RestoreCatchupResponse`.
- **(a) Admission prerequisites:** dispatch binds `resp.responder_validator_index` to the authenticated
  transport origin (`:7392-7406`, Run 418). Per **A2-F1**, that transport identity is **impersonable**
  with a public delegation cert and **no consensus signing key**. `handle_restore_catchup_response`
  (`:8426-8520`) rejects self-addressed responses (`:8433`), then applies only if
  `committed_height==resp.request_from_height` **and** `committed_block==resp.request_from_block_id`
  (`:8454-8456`) — an **anchor-equality** check. There is **no** outstanding-request requirement and
  **no** restore-mode-active gate on *application*; unsolicited anchor-matching responses are applied.
- **Attacker-controlled fields:** `blocks[].{height,view,parent_block_id,block_id,proposer_index,
  qc_signer_indices}` and `responder_committed_height` (`p2p.rs:200-218`).
- **(b) Endorsement evidence:** **none verified.** `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` builds
  `QuorumCertificate::new(block_id,view,qc_signers)` and calls `qc.validate(validators())` =
  **logical-only** (membership + dedup + ≥2/3 unit-weight power, **no signatures**, `:4004-4006`). The
  wire carries only `qc_signer_indices` (no signatures, no tx/state payload). No field is cryptographically
  authenticated as an endorsement; signer identities are **derived from sender-controlled indices**.
- **(c) State effects / first security-relevant effect:** for each contiguous valid-structured block,
  `register_block(...)` + `on_vote(signer,view,block_id)` for every listed signer (`:4008-4018`) → forms
  the logical QC, can advance lock/high-QC/committed height per the 3-chain rule, and `set_view` advances
  (`:4029-4031`). **Consensus-state advancement only** (no transaction execution / ledger-state change on
  this path).
- **(d) Interaction with newer guards:** the F7 high-QC admission (A1-F3) and Proposal/Vote `Required`
  rejection are **not** on this call chain — `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` neither calls
  `admit_f7_retained_high_qc` nor `reverify_quorum_certificate_with_domain`. No protection is inherited
  from the similarly-named Proposal/Vote checks.
- **(e) Failure atomicity:** **not atomic** — accepted-prefix `register_block`/`on_vote`/commit persist;
  only the post-loop `set_view` is skipped on a later-block `Err`. The handler's "did NOT mutate" comment
  (`:8520`) is inaccurate for partial prefixes.
- **(f) Empty/stale responses:** `responder_committed_height` (sender-controlled) drives
  `maybe_exit_after_response` even on empty/stale/mismatch (`:8441-8475`, `:8536-8544`) — restore-mode
  exit influenced by an unauthenticated self-report (liveness scope).
- **(g) Transport interaction:** A2-F1 supplies the **transport identity** (public cert, no consensus
  key); the catch-up path requires **no** consensus signature, so transport impersonation is sufficient
  to be admitted as a "validator" responder. **Transport impersonation ≠ consensus-signature forgery** —
  but here the catch-up path never asks for a consensus signature, so the distinction does not protect it.
- **Checks passed → first effect:** transport-bound (impersonated) responder id ✓ → anchor-equality ✓ →
  structural/deterministic block checks ✓ → logical `qc.validate` ✓ → `register_block`/`on_vote` mutate
  committed consensus metadata along an **unendorsed** chain.
- **Unresolved prerequisites / obligations:** whether a deployment enters restore mode only under operator
  config; honest-node divergence / finality-safety harm (E20, **unexecuted**); any downstream consumer of
  the advanced metadata.
- **Disposition:** **OPEN at current baseline** (source-confirmed). No new ID; refinements (e)/(f) folded
  into A17-F1.

### A4.5 Distinct-mechanism check (no new IDs introduced)
A1-F1 (missing-context Timeout/TC verification), A1-F3 (TC high-QC lock-install), and A17-F1 (catch-up
logical-QC) are **distinct call chains**; A17-F1 is **not** protected by the A1-F1 rejection branches or
the A1-F3 F7 gate. A2-F1 (transport possession) is a **prerequisite enabler** for A17-F1 reachability, not
the same defect. No finding was merged or duplicated.

### A4.6 A3 correction table (narrow; A3 preserved verbatim as historical evidence)
| # | A3 statement | Correction (A4), with source |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | A3 §3.2: client cert "echoed in `ServerAccept.delegation_cert`" | **Wrong.** `ServerAccept.delegation_cert = self.cfg.local_delegation_cert.clone()` (`handshake.rs:1047`) — it is the **server's own** local certificate, **not** an echo of the client cert. |
| E2 | A3 §4: A11-F1 link (c) "first s2c message (e.g. ServerAccept)" counted as reused-key AEAD app-data | **Corrected.** `ServerAccept` is a **handshake packet**, not application data under the derived AEAD session; it must **not** be counted as new s2c encryption when assessing A11-F1 nonce reuse. Link (c) still concerns post-handshake app-data s2c traffic, which remains UNPROVEN. |
| E3 | A3 §3.3(c): "consensus authorship remains protected by a key the attacker does not hold" | **Narrowed.** True only for the signature-checked **Proposal/Vote/Timeout/NewView** paths. It does **not** hold for the **restore-catchup** path (A17-F1), which performs **no** endorsement-signature verification. |
| E4 | A3 §6 / v1.49.1 §1C A1-F1: "underlying code unchanged; containment only" | **Corrected.** Current source has explicit handler-level rejection branches (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:7019-7030` Timeout, `:7208-7220` NewView) when `verification_ctx == None`; A1-F1 is **SOURCE-ADDRESSED on the inspected inbound paths** (verification pending), not containment-only. |

| **QBIND-A1-F006** (documentation overstates deployed posture) | *(no historical alias; v1.48 is itself the living reconciliation register)* | Repository-documentation defect. **Separated** in A3 from *audit-report* errors (A1/A2 self-corrections), which are a different category. | OPEN (repo-doc accuracy) + audit-report corrections tracked in §5. |
| **A2-F1** (client cert accepted without session-bound possession proof) | **A2-F1** (register) | **REVALIDATED at HEAD in A3** (§3). Not a QBIND-A1 ID. | OPEN; confirmed at pinned source; **corrects A2's R4 assumption**. |
| **A11-F1** (replayed ClientInit → key/nonce reuse) | **A11-F1** (register) | **REVALIDATED at HEAD in A3** (§4). Not a QBIND-A1 ID. | OPEN; deterministic randoms confirmed at pinned source. |

No historical finding is presented as newly discovered; no QBIND-A1 finding is silently merged into a
historical one. Evidence gaps and hypotheses from v1.48 are carried, not re-opened as new.

## 3. Corrected R4 authentication analysis (revalidate A2-F1 at the pinned source)

### 3.1 Confirmed source facts (first-hand, HEAD)

Client side `ClientHandshake::start` (`handshake.rs:362-407`): the client **encapsulates to the
server's public KEM key** (`kem.encaps(peer_kem_pk)`, `:375-376`), stores `(kem_ct, shared_secret)`,
and **attaches its delegation cert** (`client_cert`) if configured (`:390-405`). `client_random` is
caller-supplied (`:346,401`).

Server side `handle_client_init_inner` (`handshake.rs:966-1064`):
1. `verify_client_cert_if_required` (`:974-1099`): in `Required` mode, parses+verifies the client cert
   and derives `node_id = derive_node_id_from_cert(cert)`, returns `mutual_auth_complete = true`
   (`:1088-1099`). `parse_and_verify_client_cert` (`:1137-1206`) checks only: cert **parses**; its
   `root_key_id` resolves to a configured trusted root; the cert **signature verifies** against that
   root; validity window; configured leaf-revocation. **If `trusted_client_roots` is `None`, signature
   verification is skipped entirely** ("for testing, we accept any cert", `:1167-1173`, `if !root_pk.is_empty()` false).
2. **Shared secret** = `kem.decaps(self.cfg.local_kem_sk, init.kem_ct)` (`:988`) — the **server's** KEM
   private key decapsulating a ciphertext the **client chose**. This proves the **server** holds its KEM
   key (to the client); it proves **nothing** about the client.
3. Transcript = `SHA3("QBIND:KEMTLS" ‖ client_random ‖ server_random ‖ kem_ct ‖ client_cert)`
   (`:1000-1009`); session keys = `HKDF(salt="QBIND:KDF"‖transcript, ikm=shared_secret)` (`keys.rs:286-316`).
4. `peer_validator_id = verified_client_cert.validator_id` (`:1034-1037`); the server records
   `peer_validator_id`/`client_node_id`/`mutual_auth_complete` and goes **Established** with **no further
   step** (`connection.rs:286-310`). `p2p_node_builder.rs:1661-1678` maps that cert-derived identity to a
   consensus origin.

**There is no point at which the client proves possession of the private key corresponding to the cert.**
Real KEMTLS client authentication would require the server to encapsulate to the **client's** cert key and
require the client to decapsulate (implicit proof), or require a client signature over the transcript.
Neither occurs. This **confirms historical A2-F1 at the pinned source.** (v1.48 reached the same
conclusion — "the handshake does not prove client private-key possession", register line 96.)

### 3.2 Separated possessions / prerequisites

| Thing the attacker needs | How obtained | Proven by the handshake? |
|---|---|---|
| An **acceptable public client cert** | It is a **public wire object**: sent in every `ClientInit` (`:405`) and echoed in `ServerAccept.delegation_cert`; any server the victim dials, any on-path observer, or any published cert yields it. **Acquisition prerequisite: observe one ClientInit/ServerAccept from (or to) the victim, or obtain a published delegation cert.** | n/a (public) |
| The **server's public KEM key** | Public (needed to dial; distributed as the server identity) | n/a (public) |
| A **client private key** (cert's leaf KEM key) | **NOT required** to be presented or exercised | **No** — this is the A2-F1 gap |
| A **consensus signing key** (ML-DSA-44) | A **separate** key; required to produce valid Proposal/Vote/Timeout **consensus** signatures | **No** — and transport admission does not grant it |

### 3.3 The three boundaries (kept separate)

- **(a) Established transport:** under `Required` mutual-auth, reached by any peer that presents **a**
  valid (root-signed, in-window, unrevoked) client cert and encapsulates to the server's public KEM key.
  Because of A2-F1 this peer **need not hold** the cert's private key — transport identity is
  **impersonable** by cert replay/copy.
- **(b) `BlockProposal::decode` (A21-F1/F001):** reached **after** an established session delivers a
  `ConsensusNetMsg::Proposal` frame; the decoder runs **before** the Run 418 sender-binding and the
  `Required` Proposal/Vote rejection (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6192-6199`). **Earlier transport dispatch
  imposes only the handshake/established-session requirement** (and the default-off rate limiters); it
  does **not** add a possession check. (Contrast: the **NewView** arm performs origin authorization
  **before** TC decode, `binary_consensus_loop.rs:6799-6841` per v1.48 §6A — an asymmetry; the Proposal
  arm does not.)
- **(c) Admitted consensus processing:** even with an impersonated transport identity, a proposal/vote
  must carry a valid **ML-DSA-44 consensus signature** over the domain-bound preimage to be engine-admitted
  — and in current production Proposal/Vote are fail-closed anyway (`pv_authority=None`). **So consensus
  *authorship* remains protected by a key the attacker does not hold.** Transport impersonation does
  **not** by itself yield consensus forgery.

### 3.4 Reassessment of A2's R4 restriction

A2 (§3, R4 row) said F001 under static-root+mutual-auth is reachable "only for peers that pass KEMTLS
mutual-auth with a trusted-root-chained cert … effectively a provisioned validator/seed." **Corrected:**
because client authentication is **cert presentation without possession proof** (A2-F1), an attacker who
merely **obtains a valid client cert** (a public object) can pass `Required` mutual-auth and impersonate
that validator's **transport identity** — **without holding any private key**. Therefore **R4 does not
restrict (a)/(b) to key-holding validators**; it restricts them to parties able to present *some* valid
cert (far weaker). What R4 *does* still provide: real ML-KEM-768 confidentiality and ML-DSA-44
**cert-chain** validation (so a cert must be genuinely root-issued and unrevoked). What remains effective
regardless of transport impersonation: the **consensus-signature** check on message content (c).

- **Static support:** high — the possession gap and the decode-before-bind ordering are read first-hand
  at the pinned blobs.
- **Runtime uncertainty (separate):** whether a specific deployment configures `trusted_client_roots`
  (so cert-chain validation is actually enforced vs the `None`→accept-any path), the real distribution/
  secrecy of delegation certs, and whether the identity-map lookup at origin resolution rejects an
  impersonated-but-unmapped id — **not observed**; no runtime reproduction performed.

---

## 4. Session-freshness revalidation (A11-F1)

### 4.1 Confirmed source facts (first-hand, HEAD)

- **Deterministic randoms (the root cause):** the wired path sets
  `client_random = "qbind-client-<validator_id>"` and `server_random = "qbind-server-<validator_id>"`,
  zero-padded to 32 bytes (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1965-1972`) — **fixed per-validator constants, not
  per-connection random.** `qbind-net` itself does **not** generate randomness (`handshake.rs:319-320`
  "randomness not modeled; caller passes"; no `OsRng`/`getrandom`/`rand` in `qbind-net`).
- **Deterministic key schedule:** session keys + 3-byte `session_id` derive from
  `HKDF(shared_secret, transcript)` with `transcript = SHA3(tag ‖ client_random ‖ server_random ‖ kem_ct
  ‖ client_cert)` (`handshake.rs:1000-1024`, `keys.rs:286-316`).
- **Counters start at 0:** each `AeadDirection` starts `counter: 0` (`session.rs:58-65,68-75`); nonce =
  `flag(1) ‖ session_id(3) ‖ counter(8)` (`session.rs:6-13`). The code comment itself states AEAD safety
  "relies on each session using independent keys" (`session.rs:16-21`).
- **Server contributes no freshness:** because `server_random` is a fixed constant, the **only**
  per-connection variability is the client's `kem_ct` (and thus `shared_secret`). A **replayed**
  `ClientInit` reuses the same `kem_ct` byte-for-byte, so the server (fixed `server_random`, deterministic
  decaps) derives **identical keys + session_id**, and both directions restart at counter 0.
- **No ClientInit replay rejection found on the wired server path:** `connection.rs:286-288` calls
  `handle_client_init` (not the cookie-aware API); I found no per-ClientInit nonce cache / replay guard on
  this path (static inspection; not exhaustive).

This **confirms historical A11-F1 at the pinned source.** Note the defect is in the **caller's random
handling**, so it applies to **both** the test-grade (R3) and PqcStaticRoot (R4) transports — ML-KEM
decapsulation is deterministic, so a replayed `kem_ct` yields the same shared secret under real crypto too.

### 4.2 Separated links (as required; no over-promotion)

| Link | Status (A3, static) |
|---|---|
| (a) repeated key/nonce **installation** on a replayed ClientInit | **SOURCE-SUPPORTED** — deterministic randoms + deterministic HKDF + counter 0 ⇒ identical `(key, session_id, starting nonce)`. |
| (b) a **recorded c2s ciphertext re-decrypting** at the reset receive counter | **SOURCE-SUPPORTED** (same key+nonce reinstalled) — transport-layer replay acceptance. |
| (c) **new s2c encryption** under the reused key/nonce | **REACHABLE but content-UNPROVEN** — requires the server to emit s2c traffic (e.g., ServerAccept / a timeout/NewView broadcast) on the replayed connection; which message is first and its content are not pinned. |
| (d) two ciphertexts for **different plaintexts** / (e) keystream recovery / Poly1305 forgery | **UNPROVEN** — RFC 8439 §4 is the general one-time-key-reuse mechanism; a concrete differing-plaintext schedule and practical recovery/forgery are **not** demonstrated. |
| application delivery / consensus effects | **NOT ESTABLISHED** — consensus authorship still needs ML-DSA signatures; nonce reuse breaks **transport** confidentiality/integrity, not consensus authorization. Kept separate. |

No runtime reproduction performed (none authorized). The catastrophic-AEAD-misuse condition is strongly
supported at the source level for links (a)/(b); downstream (c)-(e) remain explicitly unproven.

---

## 5. A2 correction table (narrow corrections; completed reviews not restarted)

| # | A2 statement | Correction (A3) |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | F003: "whenever the P2P path runs, timeouts **are** signed" | **Overstated.** The timeout **signer is mandatorily constructed** on the P2P path (RequireOrFail), but **actual signing is conditional** on the timeout/restore/outbound/identity/high-QC admission gates. A3 states **source reachability**, not observed execution. |
| D2 | F003: "emitted timeouts **carry `high_qc=None`**" (implying rewrite) | **Corrected.** A high-QC **admission failure suppresses emission**; it does **not** necessarily rewrite an existing message's `high_qc` to `None`. The correct statement is: a `high_qc`-bearing timeout is **not emitted** under the refusing gate (suppression), not that its field is rewritten. |
| D3 | F003: "two timeouts at the same view are **byte-identical**" | **Corrected.** ML-DSA-44 `try_sign` is **randomized**, so identical signing **preimages do not** yield identical signature **bytes**. The relevant notion is identical **signed content/preimage**, not identical bytes. Whether that constitutes a protocol-defined **conflicting** message and a **slashable** event requires separate evidence (the slashing taxonomy targets conflicting content, not re-signs) — **not** established here. |
| D4 | §3 R3/R4 presented as the matrix | **Corrected.** `mutual_auth_mode` (Disabled/Optional/Required) and `pqc_root_mode` (TestGradeDummySig/PqcStaticRoot) are **independent configuration axes**; R3/R4 are two points, **not exhaustive** (e.g. Required+TestGradeDummySig, or Disabled+PqcStaticRoot, are distinct combinations with different properties). A3 inspects the relevant combinations rather than treating R3/R4 as a closed matrix. |
| D5 | "flag set ⇒ node starts P2P" phrasing | **Clarified.** Flag presence alone does **not** establish successful startup; the P2P path additionally requires a **valid loaded signer**, a **peer key provider** (`--validator-consensus-key`) or genesis authority, and (for R4) real trusted-root credentials — else the preflight fatal-exits. |
| D6 | F001 §4.2/§4.3: "no pages faulted / no RSS growth" (universal); "glibc routes >128 KiB to mmap"; "cgroup limit ⇒ abort" | **Withdrawn as universal.** Retain only: the **155-byte** minimum inner prefix and the **count-driven `u32` allocation request** (up to `tx_count × size_of::<Vec<u8>>()` = up to `103,079,215,080` B). The **outcome is one of several, host/allocator/runtime-dependent**: (i) allocation **failure → `handle_alloc_error` abort**; (ii) **capacity-overflow panic** if the requested byte size exceeds `isize::MAX` (not the case for ~103 GB on 64-bit, but relevant for larger element types/counts); (iii) successful reservation then **later OOM-kill** if pages are faulted; (iv) **successful reservation followed by `UnexpectedEof`** (freed). No claim is made that a cgroup limit **deterministically** forces rejection. No execution evidence. |
| D7 | F001: "tx_count is the **sole** unbounded pre-size"; QC u16 "bounded/acceptable" | **Corrected.** Within the **inspected `qbind-wire` decoders**, `tx_count` (u32) is the only pre-size not bounded below `u32`. A **complete workspace sweep of all `with_capacity`/pre-size-from-untrusted-count sites was NOT performed**, so "sole problematic allocation" is withdrawn. A finite **u16** count (≤65,535) is a finite cap but is **not** automatically an acceptable resource budget — it is recorded as finite, not validated. |
| D8 | §7: EVM/classical-crypto "not used for native trust" | **Marked unresolved by stage.** Keep distinct: (manifest feature selected) vs (dependency compiled into the binary) vs (code retained in the release executable) vs (**which EVM precompiles are active**) vs (**reachable to authorize** anything). A2 established the first two; the **active precompile set** and any **native→EVM crypto bridge** are **UNRESOLVED**. A3 does **not** claim complete isolation of native trust from the EVM classical surface based only on selected-wrapper inspection. |
| D9 | F002 CLI citation `qbind_envelope.rs:290-353 / :304-352 / :42-46` | **Corrected per source:** signature-verification invocation at **`qbind_envelope.rs:224`**; exit-status selection at **`:247-254`**. The core defect (no approval-dedup in `verify.rs:95-124`; `is_valid()` at `:56-58`) is unchanged. |
| D10 | F005: "apply_block only via sim/tests" | **Refined (3 representations).** Keep distinct: **wire `tx::Transaction`** (A7-F1, consumed by `Node::apply_block`, `lib.rs:2538/2590-2623`), **ledger `QbindTransaction`** (DAG `QbindBatch`), and **EVM `QbindTx`** (revm). The binary instantiates **no `Node`/`TxExecutor`**; do **not** infer one path's reachability from another's similarly named `apply_block`. F005/A7-F1 is LATENT because the **wire-`Transaction`** consumer is unwired — a separate fact from EVM/ledger reachability. |
| D11 | F006 conflated repo docs with report errors | **Separated.** F006 = **repository-documentation** overstatement (a repo defect: e.g. the M-series "residual risk Low" vs RS1 OPEN). The A1/A2 **audit-report** overstatements (e.g. "timeout verification off by default"; "no classical crypto anywhere"; F001 "guaranteed crash"; R4 restriction) are **audit-report errors**, corrected in A2/A3 — a **different category**, not a repository finding. |
