### A7-F1 — `wire::tx::Transaction` authorization-completeness defect (source-level; LATENT on DevNet)

**Evidence:** STATIC-SUPPORTED (source-level, callable library path) · **OPEN** · **DevNet applicability:** **LATENT** (consumer `Node::apply_block` is a library pipeline struct, not instantiated in the binary) · **Reviewer attribution:** A7/A7.1/A8 (local, static); ChatGPT supplied/concurred the mechanisms; independently verified. = project **F1/F2**. Not executed; not newly reproduced.

**Violated invariant.** A transaction that mutates privileged/owned state must carry sufficient authorization from the accounts whose authority it exercises. `verify_transaction_auth` does not enforce this: empty `auths` pass trivially (auth.rs:31–33); there is **no threshold/weight**; and a supplied auth selects the **first** keyset entry matching its `suite_id` via `.find(...)` (auth.rs:78) — it does **not** iterate every matching key — then verifies that one. So required authorizations can be omitted while an unrelated supplied signature passes.

**Four distinct layers (keep separate; A7.1).** (1) *a supplied signature verifies* — checked; (2) *all required authorities are represented* — **not** checked (no is_signer-coverage obligation); (3) *required distinct-key weights reach a threshold* — **not** checked; (4) *the authorized operation may mutate the selected account* — a **downstream program** concern, **uninspected here** (E15). `is_writable` (write permission) and `is_signer` (signing authority) are **separate**; the register does **not** assert a requirement that every writable account independently sign. The signed body (qbind-hash/src/tx.rs) covers metas/flags but **does not itself establish** chain-selection, nonce-freshness/replay, or payer-authorization enforcement — those are **not located** on this path here and are recorded as **unresolved (E15)**.

**Reachability (bounded; corrected A8).** The wire-tx consumer `Node::apply_block` is a method on the `Node<S>` **library pipeline struct** (qbind-node/src/lib.rs:2538/2590–2623); `main.rs` instantiates **no `Node`** and calls **no `.apply_block(`** (and no `TxExecutor`/`GovernanceProgram`); the `NodeHotstuffHarness` mentions in `main.rs` comments are a different harness and do not establish `Node::apply_block` callers; `binary_consensus_loop`/`vm_v0_runtime` invoke none of `verify_transaction_auth`/`BlockExecutor`/`execute_block`. The transaction-bearing P2P surface (DAG `QbindBatch`) is **decoded at the outer `P2pMessage` level then discarded** by the default `NullDagHandler` (binary installs only a consensus handler). So the defect is **not anonymously reachable** on the pinned binary; the project itself gates F1/F2 "before transaction ingress is enabled" (public DevNet NO-GO).

**Consumer/configuration prerequisites to expose it (latent-finding requirement; corrected A8).** Exposure requires a wired path that **drives wire-`Transaction` blobs into `Node::apply_block`/`BlockExecutor` on committed blocks** (and admits externally-influenced blobs). **A non-null DAG handler alone does NOT expose A7-F1:** DAG batches carry ledger `QbindTransaction` values, not wire `Transaction`, so exposure would additionally require an explicit consumer/conversion reaching the wire execution path. None is present in the selected binary.

**Disposition.** Preserved source-level defect (= project F1/F2), contained on DevNet by inactive wiring (not a fix). Run 417 F1/F2 independently re-verified at this revision — not newly reproduced.

**Remaining uncertainty (E15).** The omitted-authority / threshold consequence on at least one bounded **downstream system program** (uninspected here — do not describe its protection or bypass as established; broader governance = **H03**); chain/nonce/replay/payer enforcement location; the ledger `QbindTransaction` boundary (optional/caller-dependent verification above) and EVM `QbindTx` upstream contract; real-crypto (non-stub) behavior.

## 6H. A8 — Governance authorization (H03) → A8-F1

Bounded audit of the wire `GovernanceProgram` and its **four** mutation operations. **Result: A8-F1 — the governance program enforces NO authorization (no Safety-Council membership, threshold, signer-authority, proposal/approval/timing, or replay check) against the intended 5-of-7 Safety Council policy; the only upstream gate is `verify_transaction_auth` (A7-F1), which does not check governance authority.** This is a **distinct root cause** from A7-F1 (authorization *absence in the program* vs authentication *completeness* in the verifier); the two compound but are not double-counted. Like A7-F1 it is **LATENT** — the `TxExecutor`/`GovernanceProgram` path is unwired in the pinned binary.

### Required authority (normative basis)
`qbind-types/src/state_governance.rs:152–165` defines the canonical genesis `SafetyCouncilKeyset` as a **5-of-7 council** (`threshold: 5`, `member_count: 7`, ML-DSA-87 Cat-5); `genesis_safety_council_accounts` (172–186) ships **placeholder** 32-byte keys ("operators should replace these with real keys" — and 32 bytes is not a valid ML-DSA-87 public key). `governance_program.rs:30–34` fixes the council keyset/member AccountIds. This is the state-level **membership** invariant for *who may* perform governance mutations. **It is never consulted by the program.**

**Supported defect vs exact policy (A8.1 obs 1 — kept separate).** The **supported, source-level** claim is narrow and robust: `GovernanceProgram` consults **no** governance authority at all (not membership, not threshold, not per-operation rules). The **exact intended governance policy** is a **separate, only partly-located** question and is **not** asserted here beyond what source shows: (a) the genesis 5-of-7 `SafetyCouncilKeyset` is the **membership/threshold config**, which is **not** the same as **op-specific** approval/timelock/ETA-height/replay/emergency rules — those would govern *how* an op is authorized and are **not located** as enforced anywhere on this path (the `proposal_id`/`eta_height` fields exist but are unread); (b) the register does **not** assume "5 signatures suffice for every operation" — some operations could, by an undocumented policy, require a higher bar, and that per-op policy is unestablished; (c) the **`qbind-gov` crate's Protocol-Council / upgrade-envelope** policy (the off-chain `qbind-envelope` CLI path) is a **different authority surface** and is **not** imported into — nor a substitute for — this on-chain wire `GovernanceProgram` / Safety-Council path. So the finding is "**no** op-specific authority is enforced," with the precise normative target recorded as a **policy gap** to be pinned by a future governance-policy trace, not over-specified now.

### Actual entry path (one full authorization-to-state-write trace: `OP_GOV_SET_MAINNET_STATUS`)
`wire::tx::Transaction{program_id = GOVERNANCE_PROGRAM_ID (0x47…), call_data[0]=0x23}` → `TxExecutor::execute_transaction` (runtime/lib.rs:139–159): `ctx.verify_tx_auth(tx)` (the A7-F1 gate — empty `auths` pass; else first-`.find` suite-match verify; **no council/threshold**) → dispatch by `tx.program_id` → `GovernanceProgram::execute` (governance_program.rs:64–88): checks only `program_id` match + non-empty `call_data`, then opcode-dispatches → `handle_set_mainnet_status` (252–288): decodes `GovSetMainnetStatusCall`, loads `PARAM_REGISTRY_ACCOUNT_ID`, decodes `ParamRegistry`, sets `params.mainnet_status = call.new_status`, re-encodes, `ctx.store.put(account)` (280–285). **No authorization check at any step after authentication.** `GovSetMainnetStatusCall` carries `proposal_id`/`eta_height` (declared gov.rs:245–250; decoded gov.rs:263–289, `proposal_id` at 280 and `eta_height` at 281) that are **decoded but never read**; the distinct `GovUpdateSuiteStatusCall` has its own `proposal_id`/`eta_height` fields at gov.rs:24–25 (likewise decoded-not-read). *(v0.15 correction, A8.1 obs 1: v0.14 cited "gov.rs:24–25" for this `OP_GOV_SET_MAINNET_STATUS` trace — those are the **other** call type's field lines; the correct `GovSetMainnetStatusCall` locations are 245–250/263–289.)* No proposal identity, approval, ETA-height gate, or replay protection on either op.

### Four-operation comparison

| Op (call_data[0]) | Handler | Account mutated | Fields changed | AuthZ / council / threshold | Proposal/timing/replay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x23` SET_MAINNET_STATUS | `handle_set_mainnet_status` (252–288) | `PARAM_REGISTRY` (0xA2…) | `mainnet_status` | **none** | `proposal_id`/`eta_height` decoded, **not enforced** |
| `0x20` UPDATE_SUITE_STATUS | `handle_update_suite_status` (92–153) | `SUITE_REGISTRY` (0xA1…) | one suite entry `status` (Active/Legacy/Disabled) | **none** | decoded, not enforced |
| `0x21` UPDATE_PARAM_REGISTRY | `handle_update_param_registry` (156–194) | `PARAM_REGISTRY` (0xA2…) | `slash_bps_prevote/precommit`, `reporter_reward_bps` | **none** | decoded, not enforced |
| `0x22` UPDATE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST | `handle_update_launch_checklist` (197–249) | `LAUNCH_CHECKLIST` (0xA3…) | 7 `*_ok` flags + 7 report hashes | **none** | decoded, not enforced |

### A8-F1 — GovernanceProgram enforces no authorization (source-level; LATENT on DevNet)

**Evidence:** STATIC-SUPPORTED (source-level, callable path) · **OPEN** · **DevNet applicability:** **LATENT** (`TxExecutor`/`GovernanceProgram` unwired in the binary) · **Reviewer attribution:** A8 (local, static); ChatGPT supplied H03 starting points; independently verified. Distinct root cause from A7-F1; compounds with it.

- **Violated invariant.** Privileged governance-state mutations must require the intended 5-of-7 Safety Council authorization (state_governance.rs:152–165). The program performs **zero** authorization: `execute` (64–88) and all four handlers (92–288) never read the `SafetyCouncilKeyset`, never check membership/threshold/signer-uniqueness/account-ownership, and never enforce `proposal_id`/`eta_height`/replay (module doc line 4: "No timelock/TA/SC enforcement yet").
- **Distinction the task required.** (i) *A7-F1 empty-auth* → a tx with **no** signature reaches the handler; (ii) *valid signature from a non-council account* → still authorized (the program never checks council), so **one valid signature does not establish council authorization**; (iii) *genuinely council-authorized* → the program cannot distinguish it from (ii). So H03 is a **distinct authorization-absence root cause**, not merely a consequence of A7-F1; they compound.
- **Bounded consequence.** A successful write to the **stored data of the well-known system account** (`SuiteRegistry`/`ParamRegistry`(incl. `mainnet_status`)/`LaunchChecklist`) held in whatever `AccountStore` the (hypothetical) wired executor uses. The supported in-memory write is specifically `InMemoryAccountStore::put` (store.rs:43–45: `self.inner.insert(account.id, account); Ok(())`) — a property of **that** store impl, **not** transferred to every `AccountStore` (durable/remote stores are untraced). **Not established:** durable persistence beyond the store, runtime activation, or network-wide effect. Changing `mainnet_status`/`LaunchChecklist` does **not** prove MainNet activation/launch approval; changing `SuiteRegistry` does **not** prove runtime cryptographic-provider or transport-root replacement.
- **E16 `mainnet_status` consumer trace (A8.1 obs 7; bounded, narrowed A9 obs A).** A read-only trace of the **stored `ParamRegistry.mainnet_status` field** found **no activation/gate reader in the inspected paths** at this revision. `crates/qbind-node/src` (193 files) contains **zero** occurrences of `mainnet_status`/`MainnetStatus`/`ParamRegistry`. The field's only non-test reads located are **serialization** (qbind-serde/src/governance.rs:213 `encode_state`) and **decode-into-a-fresh-struct** (qbind-serde/src/governance.rs:238–242/270); the sole writer is `handle_set_mainnet_status` (governance_program.rs:280), which **overwrites unconditionally** without comparing the prior value; genesis initializes it to `PreGenesis` (qbind-genesis/src/lib.rs:41). No `if`/`match` in the inspected paths branches on the stored value to select a binary/path or gate activation. **Distinguish** this stored field from: (a) the `MainnetStatus` enum type and its `PreGenesis/Ready/Activated` variants (qbind-types/src/primitives.rs:190–196); (b) the wire `GovSetMainnetStatusCall.new_status` carrier (gov.rs:8/245–289) — the transport for the write, not a read of state; (c) the unrelated `MainNet…` strings in `qbind-node/src/pqc_*` (e.g. `MainNetPeerDrivenApplyRefused`) — a PQC peer-driven-apply refusal concept, not this field; (d) readiness/launch documentation; (e) test/fixture state. **Search scope:** `mainnet_status|MainnetStatus|ParamRegistry` over `qbind-node/src` (no matches) and `\.mainnet_status`/`MainnetStatus`/`ParamRegistry` workspace-wide over `**/src/**`. **Scope limit of the negative (A9 obs A):** this supports "**no activation reader was found in the inspected paths**," which is **narrower** than "no callable reader exists" or "the field is globally inert." Runtime **loaders of `PARAM_REGISTRY_ACCOUNT_ID`** (raw account bytes, not the type name) outside the gov handler were **not exhaustively traced**, and absence of the field/type name in `qbind-node/src` does **not** by itself exclude a **dependency-mediated or raw-account** consumer elsewhere. **Corrected edge (A9 obs A):** the earlier claim that `qbind-consensus/src/slashing/mod.rs` "decodes `ParamRegistry`" is **wrong** — `from_governance_schedule` (slashing/mod.rs:2285) takes a **`GovernanceSlashingSchedule`** (a consensus-local struct, 2340–2351) and copies penalty fields (2286–2303); the `ParamRegistry` mentions in its doc comment (2330–2338) are **documentation**, not a decode. No actual `ParamRegistry`-decode conversion/loader is claimed here; whether one exists is left **unresolved**, not asserted. **Conclusion (bounded, narrowed):** at `ef99e29`, **no `mainnet_status` activation reader was found in the inspected paths**, and the **independent containment** is that the affected transaction-execution path is **unwired** in the selected binary — not a claim that the field is globally inert. `SuiteRegistry`/`LaunchChecklist` consumers remain E16.
- **Exposure.** LATENT — `main.rs` instantiates no `TxExecutor`/`GovernanceProgram`/`Node`; the tx-execution path is unwired (same containment as A7-F1). Library-callable; existing `governance_program_tests.rs` call `GovernanceProgram::execute` **directly** (94/109, 150/165, 212/239, 288/301, `.expect("execute ok")`) — **not** through `TxExecutor`, so they do not exercise the authentication→authorization composition and are **control-flow evidence only**, not a newly observed end-to-end result.
- **Counterevidence / limits.** The gov system accounts *are* written at genesis (qbind-genesis/src/lib.rs) — which shows the accounts **can** be initialized, **not** that a wired handler automatically reaches `store.put` (corrected A9 obs D): a successful mutation still requires **initialized, valid** accounts (decodable registry data), **valid input** (opcode/call parse + empty-remainder checks), and a **store that accepts the write** (`InMemoryAccountStore::put` returns `Ok`, but another `AccountStore` impl need not) — otherwise the handler returns `AccountNotFound`/`SerializationError`/`InvalidCallData` before any write. The PQC governance runtime is a **separate authority domain** (below) and does not supply this program's authorization. The placeholder-key observation is **one** limitation, not the whole story — see the legitimate-authority analysis next.

### Legitimate-authority control — why no authorization-positive control exists today (A8.1 obs 3)
The supported defect is **authorization absence in `GovernanceProgram`**; separately, there is currently **no way to express an authorization-positive control** (an operation accepted *because* council policy was enforced). Three claims must be kept distinct:
1. **A signature passes ordinary transaction auth.** `verify_transaction_auth` selects the account meta at `TxAuth.account_index`, loads that account, decodes a **`KeysetAccount`** (auth.rs:62–74), `.find`s the first `KeysetEntry` whose `suite_id` matches (auth.rs:76–86), resolves the suite from the `CryptoProvider`, and verifies that one signature (auth.rs:88–100). This is **authentication of an ordinary keyset account**, nothing more.
2. **The signatures come from proposed council members.** The council is modeled by **different** state types — `SafetyCouncilKeyset{threshold, member_count, members}` and `SafetyCouncilKeyAccount{suite_id, pk_bytes}` (state_governance.rs:7–21), a **distinct struct and encoding** from `KeysetAccount`. `genesis_safety_council_keyset` fixes a 5-of-7 ML-DSA-87 council (state_governance.rs:152–165) and `governance_program.rs:30–34` fixes the member AccountIds. Even a transaction signed by council-member keys is only claim (1) unless something resolves and checks these council structures.
3. **The operation is accepted because council policy was enforced.** Only this is an **authorization-positive** control. **No such control is enforced today**, for reasons broader than placeholder keys. **Two independent axes (corrected A9 obs C):** the **policy-enforcement** axis (below) is the substantive one — it is what a future **library-level** authorization-positive control would need, and such a control could be exercised through a harness (e.g. `TxExecutor::execute_transaction`) **even without** binary wiring; the **binary-wiring** axis is **separate** and explains only the absence of *deployment exposure*, not whether a library-level control can exist. Keep **fixture success**, **production authority**, and **runtime exposure** distinct.
   - **Membership / key resolution is absent (policy axis):** `GovernanceProgram` loads only `SUITE_REGISTRY`/`PARAM_REGISTRY`/`LAUNCH_CHECKLIST` and **never reads** the `SafetyCouncilKeyset`/`SafetyCouncilKeyAccount` accounts — it consumes **neither** the ordinary `KeysetAccount` path nor the council types.
   - **Signature *representation* exists; the *binding and enforcement* do not (corrected A9 obs B).** A wire `Transaction` carries `auths: Vec<TxAuth>` (qbind-wire/src/tx.rs:107–118, `auths` at 117), a **generic representation for multiple signatures over the same transaction body** — each `TxAuth` selects an `account_index` into `accounts[]` and supplies a signature over `tx_digest`, which covers `program_id`/account metas/`call_data` (qbind-hash/src/tx.rs:8–53). So it is **wrong** to say "the wire format cannot represent multiple members' signatures" (v0.15 statement **withdrawn**); a new wire format or cryptographic construction is **not** shown necessary. What is absent is the **connection and enforcement**: no resolution of `auths[]` signers against the **distinct council account encodings** (`SafetyCouncilKeyset`/`SafetyCouncilKeyAccount`), no **threshold** count, no signer-uniqueness, and no **operation-specific approval** — none of which `GovernanceProgram` performs.
   - **Policy enforcement is absent:** no threshold/`member_count`/signer-uniqueness/`proposal_id`/`eta_height`/replay check exists in `execute` or the handlers.
   - **Policy enforcement is absent (policy axis):** no threshold/`member_count`/signer-uniqueness/`proposal_id`/`eta_height`/replay check, and no operation-specific approval, exists in `execute` or the handlers.
   - **Binary wiring is absent (separate axis):** the `TxExecutor`/`GovernanceProgram` path is unwired on the pinned binary (LATENT) — this is why there is **no deployment exposure**, but it does **not** bear on whether a library-level control could be implemented and exercised in a harness.
   - **Placeholder keys (real-crypto axis):** `genesis_safety_council_accounts` ships 32-byte placeholder `pk_bytes` (state_governance.rs:172–186) that are **not** valid ML-DSA-87 public keys, so a *real-crypto* council verification could not succeed against genesis state even if policy enforcement were implemented.
   **Fixture note:** a future reproduction may mint **disposable real keys** to exercise a council check — that is legitimate harness practice and is **not** a "fake control"; but **invented fixture-only council authority must not be presented as current behavior**, and fixture success is not production authority. At this revision, claims (1) and (2) are expressible; claim (3)'s policy enforcement is unimplemented (so no authorization-positive control exists yet, in library or binary).

### Separate PQC governance runtime boundary (precise; not conflated) — corrected A8.1 obs 2
The startup `--p2p-trust-bundle` mutating-preflight calls `consume_run_220_governance_execution_runtime_outcome(&decision, …governance_execution_policy_selector…, …governance_execution_load, GovernanceExecutionRuntimeSurface::StartupP2pTrustBundle)` with `.map_err(run_220_…marker_error)?` (main.rs:1297–1303); per its own comment, "a fail-closed decision short-circuits BEFORE any mutation" (1295–1296), and on the non-fail-closed path the preflight returns `Ok(Some(decision))` (1305) — i.e. **the call site continues**. The underlying pure helper `wire_governance_evaluator_runtime_callsite` (pqc_governance_execution_evaluator_runtime_integration.rs:547–562; doc 530–546: "Pure — performs no I/O and no mutation") returns `Ok(outcome)` when `outcome.is_proceed()` else `Err(GovernanceEvaluatorRuntimeCallsiteFailClosed)`. Its three documented outcomes: `Ok(ProceedLegacyBypass)` — "default Disabled + absent carrier legacy bypass (Run 214 compatibility); **the call site continues unchanged**"; `Ok(ProceedMutate{..})` — "**the only** outcome that authorizes a mutation"; `Err(…FailClosed)` — "the call site MUST fail closed BEFORE any mutation" for every non-proceed outcome (`RuntimeConsumptionFailClosed`/`EvaluatorRejected`/`MainNetPeerDrivenApplyRefused`). `ProductionDecisionSourceEvaluatorInterface` (pqc_governance_execution_evaluator.rs:915–944) **fails closed** (`ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`).

**Type correction (A8.1 obs 2 — v0.14 WITHDRAWN).** v0.14 asserted that the production `ProceedLegacyBypass` "is the pipeline's `ProceedLegacyBypassNoMutation` variant." That is **withdrawn**: they are **different types on different paths**. The production value is `GovernanceEvaluatorRuntimeIntegrationOutcome::ProceedLegacyBypass` (integration.rs:171/175; `is_legacy_bypass` 227–228, `is_proceed` 213–214). `GovernanceModeledEndToEndPipelineOutcome::ProceedLegacyBypassNoMutation` is a **separate** enum variant in a **separate** file (pqc_governance_modeled_end_to_end_pipeline.rs:445/448/525/536); the integration outcome maps into the modeled enum via a conversion to an intermediate `LegacyBypass` (pipeline.rs:170), not an identity with `…NoMutation`.

**What is and is not supported.** The helper being pure/no-mutation is a property of **that helper**, not of the caller: on legacy bypass the caller **continues under other controls**, it does not itself perform a trust mutation here. The documented "fail closed BEFORE any mutation" is scoped to the **non-proceed / present-carrier** outcomes at the **inspected startup call sites**; `ProceedMutate` is documented as the only mutation-authorizing outcome. **Do not equate:** (a) wire-program council authz with PQC trust-update authz (different authority domains); (b) `ProceedLegacyBypass` with unauthorized access, nor with proof that *no* mutation occurs anywhere — it is the PQC runtime's own legacy-continue path and neither authorizes nor blocks the wire `GovernanceProgram`; (c) a fixture evaluator with production authority (production is `ProductionDecisionSourceUnavailable`/fail-closed); (d) a disabled PQC layer with every governance operation being disabled (the wire `GovernanceProgram` is a separate layer). This PQC runtime is **not** an upstream control for A8-F1, and the legacy-bypass path is **not** evidence of an unauthorized trust update. Deeper PQC-runtime branches (arming variants, carrier-present fail-closed reasons, modeled-pipeline outcomes) are **queued** (E16), not resolved here.

## 6I. A9 — Remote-signer reachability and signing authority (H04) → H04-F1

Bounded first pass on H04 (remote-signer daemon + node signer wiring). **Result: the entire remote-signer stack is uncalled library/stub code; only the local-keystore signer is ever constructed, and it feeds solely the timeout-verification context.** This is resolved as **H04-F1 — an implementation gap + documentation mismatch (custody/remote-signing path non-functional/unwired), NOT a reachable network signing oracle and NOT (by itself) a public-DevNet launch blocker.** It supports keeping **C5 OPEN** (production custody/remote-signing is not realized). Do not read this as "all signing is non-functional": the **local-signer source path is implemented** (it is **wired** into the Timeout/NewView context; its real-signature behavior and the end-to-end timeout sign/verify flow are **not executed** here — implemented-source vs runtime-wiring vs unexecuted-verification kept distinct). The loaded local signer feeds **only** the Timeout/NewView context; **Proposal/Vote authority is a separate capability, set to `None` in production** (so loading a signer does **not** establish Proposal/Vote signing).

| Error propagation / fallback / verification-state | `main.rs:5707–5781`; non-genesis bridge arm (main.rs:6038–6067); bridge `enforce_policy` (timeout_verification_bridge.rs:505–527; main.rs:6090–6109) | `--require-timeout-verification` ⇒ `RequireOrFail`, else `OptionalActivate` | **Three distinct states (corrected A9.1):** (i) **no loaded signer** `signer_for_bridge=None` (loader error incl. `SignerModeNotWiredYet`→None 5749–5756; `KeystorePathNotConfigured`→None 5736–5748); (ii) **no verification context** `verification_ctx=None` — on the reachable non-genesis arm a missing signer **or** missing key-provider takes the `_`→`run_032_probe_with_signer` disabled branch (6062–6065) → `enforce_policy(OptionalActivate, Disabled)`→`Ok(None)` (DISABLED, logged "Run 030 bit-equivalent path" 6150–6157); under `RequireOrFail` any load `Err`→FATAL `exit(1)` **before** the bridge (5767–5781), and a `Disabled` outcome→`enforce_policy` `Err`→`exit(1)` (6093–6108); (iii) **verify-only active** `Some(ctx)` with `ctx.signer=None` — permitted by the library constructor (bridge 415–453) but **NOT reached by this binary** (the non-genesis arm calls the constructor only with `Some(signer)`; the genesis arm is refused at 5405–5417) | **no silent fallback to a different backend**; "no backend substitution" does **not** mean verification stays active — missing signer yields `verification_ctx=None` (verification DISABLED), not a signer-less active context | STATIC-SUPPORTED | overlaps A1-F1/E09 (does a bridge activate), not a new consensus-verification finding |

### Configuration / authority table (A9.1 — reachable binary configs vs callable-library possibilities)
Non-genesis P2P preflight (`--consensus-authority-from-genesis` is refused at main.rs:5405–5417). **These rows are representative control-flow cases, not an exhaustive enumeration of every configuration (A10 obs 1).** Read "Loader result" as a **successfully loaded signer/provider object**, not mere configuration presence. The **key-provider** side has three distinct outcomes (main.rs:5958–6002): `Ok(loaded)` (built honestly); `Err(NoConfiguredKeys)` → `None` kp, **no exit even under RequireOrFail** (preserves Run-032 disabled behavior) → reaches the later disabled-outcome **policy** failure; `Err(other provider error)` → under RequireOrFail **FATAL before the bridge** (5990–6000), else `None`. So distinguish **loader failure** (signer), **provider-construction failure** (kp), and **bridge-policy failure** (`enforce_policy`), and **no configured peer keys** from **invalid** configured keys — upstream validation at peer_key_provider.rs:329–442 validates configured keys, checks any explicit local key against the signer-derived public key, and inserts the signer-derived key when the local entry is absent, so some "invalid key" shapes are rejected there rather than reaching the bridge. Successful activation additionally requires the constructor checks at timeout_verification_bridge.rs:361–453. "Startup outcome" = whether the policy **permits continuation** at this preflight, not that the whole node necessarily finishes starting (other startup checks apply).
| # | Loader result | Timeout policy | Bridge outcome | Effective `verification_ctx` | Local timeout signing | Proposal/Vote authority | Startup (preflight) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Local signer loaded (`EncryptedFsV1`/`LoopbackTesting`) **+ key-provider present** | OptionalActivate | `try_build`→`Active` (6039–6060) | `Some(ctx)`, `ctx.signer=Some` | ON (sign_timeout) | **None** (suppressed) | continues |
| 2 | Local signer loaded **+ kp present** | RequireOrFail | `Active` | `Some(ctx)` | ON | **None** | continues |
| 3 | Local signer loaded **but no kp** | OptionalActivate | `_`→`run_032_probe` Disabled (6062–6065) | **`None`** (DISABLED) | OFF | **None** | continues (verify/sign OFF) |
| 4 | Local signer loaded **but no kp** | RequireOrFail | Disabled → `enforce_policy` `Err` | — | — | — | **FATAL exit(1)** (6093–6108) |
| 5 | No signer (`KeystorePathNotConfigured`) | OptionalActivate | `_`→Disabled | **`None`** | OFF | **None** | continues |
| 6 | No signer (any loader `Err`) | RequireOrFail | — (fails before bridge) | — | — | — | **FATAL exit(1)** (5767–5781) |
| 7 | **`RemoteSigner` mode** → `SignerModeNotWiredYet` (signer `None`) | OptionalActivate | `_`→Disabled | **`None`** | OFF | **None** | continues, but the **operator's intended remote mode is NOT active** (misconfiguration, not a working remote signer) |
| 8 | **`RemoteSigner` mode** → `SignerModeNotWiredYet` | RequireOrFail | — | — | — | — | **FATAL exit(1)** (5767–5781) |
| L | (callable-library only) signer supplied `None` to `try_build` with other checks passing | n/a | `Active` with `ctx.signer=None` (bridge 415–453) | `Some(ctx)`, `signer=None` ("verify-only") | OFF | n/a | **not a reachable binary route** — the non-genesis arm only calls `try_build` with `Some(signer)`; genesis arm refused |

**Reading:** the "verify-only active" state (row L) is a **library** possibility, **not** a reachable node configuration; every reachable missing-signer config yields `verification_ctx=None` (DISABLED) or a FATAL exit, and **Proposal/Vote authority is `None` across all rows**. *(Distinction, A10 obs 4: an **active verify-only** context (row L) would still perform **inbound** Timeout/TC verification — it only suppresses **local timeout production**; "verification DISABLED" (`ctx=None`) performs neither. Neither an active verify-only context nor local-signer availability alone establishes satisfaction of the full **RS1** gate; "no backend fallback" is a single property, not a blanket claim that every startup/client path is fail-closed in all respects.)*

### Bounded answers (A9 §4)
- **Can the supplied daemon serve a signing request through its actual executable path?** **No.** `fn main()` is synchronous; the accept loop (673–691) accepts a `TcpStream`, binds it + signer/config to `_`-discarded locals, increments a counter, logs "KEMTLS handshake not yet implemented," and drops the stream. No handshake, no read, no `handle_connection`, no signature. The backend signer is really initialized (651) but never used to serve a connection.
- **Can the selected node construct and use the remote transport?** **No** (in the node binary). `SignerMode::RemoteSigner` returns `SignerModeNotWiredYet` (signer_loader.rs:323–325); `TcpKemTlsSignerTransport` is never constructed in the node binary. *(Scope, A9.1:* `RemoteSignerClient` **is** constructed in `src` at hotstuff_node_sim.rs:2335–2355, but over a `LoopbackSignerTransport` in the simulation — not the TCP/KEMTLS transport, and not in the node binary.*)*
- **Does failure stop startup / disable verification / select another backend?** (corrected A9.1) Under **`RequireOrFail`** a signer-load error (including the RemoteSigner "not wired" error) is **FATAL** (`exit(1)`, 5767–5781). Under default **`OptionalActivate`** the preflight **permits continuation** with `signer_for_bridge=None`; on the reachable non-genesis arm that takes the `_`→`run_032_probe` **disabled** branch, so **`verification_ctx=None` (verification DISABLED)** — **not** a signer-less *active* ("verify-only") context, which is a library-only state (row L). "Policy permits continuation" is distinct from "the whole node successfully starts" (other startup checks apply). **No silent fallback** to another backend occurs; and **no backend substitution does not mean timeout verification remains active** — it is disabled.
- **Is any fallback explicit/documented?** There is **no** remote→local (or local→remote) fallback. Local is the only backend ever constructed; its absence yields a `None` signer, not a substitution.
- **Overlap with A1-F1 / evidence gaps:** signer availability determines whether the timeout-verification *context* carries a signer — this is the **E09/A1-F1 "successful bridge activation"** surface, not a new consensus-verification defect. Recorded as overlap, not a duplicate finding.
- **Authentication/authorization (design, in uncalled code):** the daemon would authenticate the peer via KEMTLS (not run) and checks `validator_id`/`suite_id` in `validate_and_sign`; these are **request-to-key *metadata* checks** — they establish that the request names this validator/suite, **not** that the *connecting peer* is an **authenticated, authorized** requester for that validator's key (that would require the un-run transport identity + an authorization binding). The remote **cert-path config fields are read** (corrected A9.1) — but **only** by MainNet config-validation **presence checks** (`is_none()` → error, node_config.rs:5747–5762); that is **not** file loading, certificate verification, or use in an active handshake (no transport consumes them). **Trusted party (unresolved trust-model question, A9.1):** if the design intends to **trust the caller** to supply correct canonical signing bytes, no contract establishing that was located; so record it as **unresolved**, not as an accepted risk — the absence of signer-side policy enforcement does **not** by itself prove that a compromised caller is an accepted risk.
- **Signing semantics (design, in uncalled code):** canonical proposal/vote/timeout bytes are built by the **consensus caller** (`binary_consensus_loop.rs` preimage helpers), not the daemon; `validate_and_sign` signs the **raw `preimage`** it is handed (dispatching Proposal→`sign_proposal`, Vote|Timeout→`sign_vote`, 571–576) and does **not** re-derive or check that the preimage matches the claimed `view`/`kind`/chain/domain — so **metadata does not bind the bytes actually signed**. **Response checks by layer (corrected A9.1):** the generic `RemoteSignerClient::sign_common` (remote_signer.rs:346–381) maps transport errors and accepts `(Some(sig), None) => Ok(sig)` — it does **not** compare `response.request_id` nor cryptographically verify the returned signature; the **`request_id` echo check lives in `TcpKemTlsSignerTransport::decode_response`** (918–921), and `LoopbackSignerTransport` (455–540) does its own request-metadata + request-ID checks and does **not** exercise the TCP decoder. So request-ID correlation is a **transport-layer** property, not a generic-client guarantee. **Keep distinct:** key isolation (a real out-of-process signer — not realized), request-replay handling (client generates a monotonic `request_id`; the daemon keeps no replay state), signature validity (an external oracle, not client-performed), peer authentication, caller authorization, and durable anti-equivocation. None is established for the running system.
- **Resource/lifecycle:** the accept loop has no per-connection handshake/signing lifetime, no size/timeout checks on the (never-read) stream, and no retry; request-ID state does **not** persist across connections/restarts in the daemon (it has none). Do **not** credit the accept loop with the uncalled handler's checks.

### H04-F1 — Remote-signer custody/signing path is non-functional and unwired (implementation gap + documentation mismatch)
**Evidence:** STATIC-SUPPORTED (source + executable-stub inspection) · **OPEN** · **Classification:** implementation/assurance gap + documentation mismatch — **NOT a reachable vulnerability** and **NOT a standalone DevNet launch blocker** · **DevNet applicability (conditional, A9.1):** the remote path is absent from the running system; the intended DevNet posture uses the **local** signer, and when the signer half is absent the reachable state is **verification DISABLED** (`verification_ctx=None`), not an active verify-only context. Remote signing is **not** automatically a DevNet must-have, **but** selecting an unavailable remote mode (`SignerMode::RemoteSigner`) can **prevent** the operator's required configuration from working (→ `None` signer under Optional, or FATAL under Required). `verify-only`/`off` does **not** satisfy RS1, and no observed deployment is asserted to use local signing. · **Reviewer attribution:** A9 (local, static); ChatGPT supplied the five leads; A9.1 corrections independently verified.
- **Violated property / contract.** Documentation/config comments describe remote signing as production-capable/preferred and the C5 narrative anticipates production custody; the implementation provides **no** working remote signing service, **no** node-side remote transport wiring, and **no active consumption** (file loading / certificate verification / handshake use) of the remote cert/key config — those fields **are** read by MainNet config-validation **presence checks** (node_config.rs:5747–5762), corrected A10.1; the active integration is what is absent. The contract (operable, authenticated, key-isolating remote signer) is unmet.
- **Callable/executable path.** Daemon accept loop drops streams (main.rs:673–691); node loader errors `SignerModeNotWiredYet` (signer_loader.rs:323–325); `TcpKemTlsSignerTransport` is **never constructed in `src` at all** (corrected A10: the sim at hotstuff_node_sim.rs:2335–2355 constructs **`RemoteSignerClient` with a `LoopbackSignerTransport`**, not the TCP/KEMTLS transport); cert-path fields **are read** — but only by MainNet config-validation **presence checks** (node_config.rs:5747–5762), not loaded/verified/used in a handshake (active certificate loading/handshake integration is absent); `.ping()` has no caller.
- **Prerequisites.** None for an attacker (there is no running oracle). For an *operator* intending remote signing: there is no supported path at this revision.
- **Bounded consequence.** Any assurance claim crediting the running system with remote **key isolation**, **authenticated remote signing**, or **fail-closed remote verification** is **unsupported** — C5 stays OPEN. There is **no network signing oracle** (the handler is uncalled), so this is not an exposure. Local signing is unaffected and functional.
- **Counterevidence / limits.** The local-signer source path is implemented (`LocalKeySigner` via `EncryptedFsV1`/`LoopbackTesting`) and is wired into the Timeout/NewView context fail-closed; `RemoteSignerClient` **does not substitute a local backend on transport error** (restricted sense of "fail-closed" — a single property on the error path, **not** a blanket claim that the client is fail-closed in every respect, corrected A10.1); the uncalled handler *does* contain request-to-key **metadata** checks (so the design intent exists, though not peer-authorization). The daemon being a stub means it cannot be a signing oracle — the absence is the point, not an exploit.
- **Falsifier (refined A9.1 — two independent sides).** (a) A **daemon** handshake/handler integration (accept loop performing the KEMTLS handshake and invoking `handle_connection`) challenges the **daemon-side** claim; (b) a **node** TCP remote-signer construction (`TcpKemTlsSignerTransport`/a remote `SignerBackend` selected in the node binary) challenges the **node-side** claim. **Either alone does NOT** establish a working, authenticated **end-to-end** service. *(Scope, A10.1: authenticated transport, caller-authorization, and signing-policy/anti-equivocation are **separate properties** a complete solution would need, each requiring its **own established policy and responsible component** — they are listed as what a full service entails, **not** added as closure criteria for H04-F1, which is scoped to the **integration gap**. No specific signing-policy/anti-equivocation contract has been identified in source.)* Finding either narrows the corresponding half of the disposition.
- **Overlaps.** Shares the timeout-verification-context surface with **A1-F1/E09** (signer presence ↔ bridge activation); relates to **C5** custody (kept OPEN). Distinct root cause (signer wiring/custody) — not double-counted with A1-F1.

## 6J. A10 — Local validator keystore loading and secret handling → A10-F1

Bounded audit of the **local** validator key-loading path the selected binary uses: configuration → backend selection → file read → parse/decrypt → signing-key construction/validation → local identity comparison → timeout-context handoff. **Result:** the local key-loading **source path is implemented** and **wired** into the Timeout/NewView signer; the surfaced items are source-supported **assurance/hardening gaps** against the **local** capabilities in the table below, **not** reachable network vulnerabilities and **not** a demonstrated decryption downgrade or key recovery. Bundled as **A10-F1**. Distinguish throughout (A10.1): **implemented source behavior** vs **binary wiring** vs **existing test source** (e.g. `t153_encrypted_keystore_integration_tests.rs:122–169` loads a disposable encrypted key and signs/verifies — present, **not** executed here, and **not** evidence of selected-binary activation) vs **unexecuted behavioral verification** (nothing here is executed). HSM internals, the remote service, full signing-journal, and key-rotation design are out of scope (handoffs recorded).

### Threat model (A10 §A, corrected A10.1) — distinct local capabilities
The path is **not anonymously network-reachable** (a scope condition, not a dismissal). The relevant attacker/operator capabilities are **distinct** and must not be conflated:
| Capability | What it enables | Established here? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Encrypted-file read, no passphrase** | **Offline passphrase guessing** against the stored ciphertext+tag; this is precisely the risk PBKDF2 is meant to raise the cost of | Success depends on passphrase strength + resources — **not established**; the KDF-cost-floor gap (obs 1) bears directly on this |
| **Honest provisioning with an inadequately costly KDF** | Leaves a file **cheaper to attack later**; the attacker need not have provisioned it or know its passphrase | Source-supported gap (no application iteration floor); downstream offline-guessing cost **unmeasured** |
| **File modification, no passphrase** | Corrupt inputs / influence **work performed before authentication** (e.g. KDF work factor); cannot obtain valid plaintext | Source-supported (file-supplied params consumed pre-auth); no attacker-chosen plaintext |
| **Plaintext-keystore read** (`LoopbackTesting`→plaintext FS) | Discloses the key **without any passphrase** | Source-supported (plaintext backend exists); DevNet-allowed, forbidden Test/MainNet (node_config.rs:647/696/731) |
| **Process-memory / environment access** | Observe **live secrets and residual copies** (transient unzeroized values) | Source-supported absence of erasure; **demonstrated extraction not attempted** |
| **Trusted operator configuration** | Sets backend/path/passphrase as designed — **distinct** from an attacker who can modify only one selected file | Operator capability, not an attacker escalation |
Do **not** grant one actor another's capability. Retain the **narrow** conclusion that changing an *adequately-provisioned* file's iteration count does **not** establish a successful **decryption downgrade** (the tag breaks) — but do **not** use that to dismiss **weak initial provisioning** or **offline guessing**, which are separate. "Not anonymously network-reachable" does **not** mean "not a reachable vulnerability"; each A10-F1 component is assessed on its own invariant/consequence/counterevidence below. `LoopbackTesting`→**plaintext** FS keystore when a path is set (signer_loader.rs:322); `EncryptedFsV1`→encrypted.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Header field-behavior table (A10.1 obs 3 — field-specific, not blanket)
| Field | How the loader treats it | Effect of changing it | "Authenticated"? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | **equality `==1` before decrypt** (377) | mismatch → `Parse` reject (fail-closed) | checked by application equality, not by AEAD |
| `suite_id` | **equality `==100` before decrypt** (385) | mismatch → `InvalidKey` reject (fail-closed) | checked by application equality, not by AEAD |
| `kdf_iterations` | PBKDF2 iteration count (416) | **generally alters the derived key** → tag fails (subject to the pbkdf2 0↔1 qualification below) | affects derivation; **not** in AAD |
| `salt` | PBKDF2 salt (416) | alters the derived key → tag fails | affects derivation; **not** in AAD |
| `nonce` | AEAD nonce (12 bytes) (421) | changes AEAD input → authentication fails | **supplied to AEAD** (affects auth); **not** in AAD — absence from AAD ≠ cryptographically irrelevant |
| `ciphertext` + tag | AEAD `open` input (421) | tamper → tag fails | **authenticated by AEAD** |
| `aead` / `kdf` labels | parsed as strings then **discarded** (756); optional | a well-formed changed/removed label **can leave loading unchanged** (algorithms are hardcoded) | informational; **not** checked, **not** in AAD |
| textual representation | hand parser | changing **decoded bytes** vs equivalent **encodings/whitespace** differ — only decoded-byte changes reach the crypto | n/a |

### Observations (A10 §B/§C — source-supported; local capabilities per the threat table; measurement withheld)
1. **`kdf_iterations` consumed from the file with no application floor/ceiling** (keystore.rs:416; parsed `u32` 608/642; kdf.rs:63–70 passes it straight to `pbkdf2_hmac::<Sha256>`). "Unbounded" is imprecise — the field is a `u32` (so representation-bounded), but **no operational cost floor/ceiling is enforced** in the inspected adapter; the config `100_000` (signer_loader.rs:396) is **dead on the read path**. **Ordering consequence:** a syntactically-accepted file causes **KDF work before ciphertext authentication rejects it**, and a **file modifier selects that work factor without the passphrase**. Keep timing / startup impact / severity **unmeasured**; a file modifier disrupting startup is **not** privilege escalation. **Narrow retained conclusion:** changing an *adequately-provisioned* file's iteration count is **not** a successful **decryption downgrade** (the tag breaks); this does **not** dismiss weak initial provisioning or offline guessing. **Disposition:** hardening gap (no policy floor).
   - **Supplied upstream source-review input (not locally verified).** ChatGPT inspected RustCrypto `pbkdf2-v0.12.2` (tag → commit `165f4a8907354e89dbdc0cab0545f4d7fe8a89bd`, `pbkdf2/src/lib.rs`): `pbkdf2_body` (123–148) computes the first PRF result **unconditionally** and runs extra rounds over `1..rounds`, and the wrapper (234–248) adds **no positive-round check** — so **iteration values 0 and 1 produce the same derived output** for otherwise identical inputs. This **narrows** the blanket "every iteration-field change breaks authentication" (a 0↔1 change would not). It does **not** demonstrate lowering a properly-provisioned high count while retaining successful decryption. **Provenance/limits:** this is **supplied upstream-source-review input**; the dependency source is **not vendored locally** (confirmed) so it is **not** locally verified — no checksum verification of the published crate archive, no local dependency-cache inspection, no build linkage, no constant-time assurance, no execution. Pinned resolved version from `Cargo.lock`: **pbkdf2 0.12.2**. Remaining dependency questions stay open (E18).
2. **Header fields not included as AEAD associated data (empty AAD, keystore.rs:421).** See the field table: `version`/`suite_id` are equality-checked pre-decrypt; `kdf_iterations`/`salt`/`nonce` affect derivation/authentication (changes generally break the tag, subject to the 0↔1 qualification); `aead`/`kdf` labels are ignored. **Withdrawn:** "unauthenticated fields admit only fail-closed tampering" — a well-formed **ignored label** change need not cause rejection (it is simply ignored). **Preserved bounded conclusion:** no **attacker-chosen-plaintext** and no **algorithm-switching** exploit has been established through the ignored labels. **Header binding into AAD is a *proposed control*** — no specific required-binding contract is identified in source; the proposal is separate from current algorithm selection/validation. **Disposition:** defense-in-depth gap.
3. **Transient secrets not explicitly zeroized** — see the secret-ownership inventory below. Only the final `ValidatorSigningKey` is `ZeroizeOnDrop` (a **drop-path** guarantee; **not** transferred to earlier copies, and **not** guaranteed on every early-exit/abort). **Only the absence of source-level erasure is established**; potential residual-secret lifetime and any actual memory extraction are **separate** and **not demonstrated** (no extraction experiment). **Disposition:** hardening gap (prerequisite: process-memory inspection).
4. **No loader-level file hardening** (keystore.rs:259–261/348–350/365): join-based path, **no size cap** (full-file `read_to_string`), **no symlink/canonicalization guard**, **no ownership/permission check** — relies on "OS-level disk protections" (module docs 37–38). Operator-side permission requirements exist in **documentation** (KEY_MANAGEMENT.md: private files 0600, keystore dir 0700) but are **not loader-enforced**. **Prerequisite:** control of the selected file/dir. **Disposition:** hardening gap (loader does not enforce the documented operator requirements).
5. **Hand-rolled parser — exact behavior (qualified A11 obs 1; keep each case separate — leniency alone is not a vulnerability).** (i) **Unknown fields ignored** (760–781). (ii) **Duplicate recognized fields: last-wins *when each occurrence parses successfully*** (unconditional `Some(value)` assignment, e.g. 753) — but an **earlier malformed** occurrence can reject (its own parse error) **before** a later value is reached, so "last-wins" is not unconditional. (iii) **Trailing commas accepted** (leading loop skips whitespace+commas, 651–657). (iv) **Ordinary non-`}`-terminated suffixes are *explicitly rejected*** by `trim()` + `starts_with('{')`/`ends_with('}')` (634) → "expected JSON object" (**not** merely incidental, corrected A11 obs 1); only the narrower case of extra bytes that still leave the string ending in `}` falls through the first/last-char strip (`&json[1..len-1]`, 638) into the state machine and errors there — there is still **no positive matched-object / no-trailing-data validation**. (v) `\u`/nested unsupported. **Allocation:** `decode_hex` calls `Vec::with_capacity(hex.len()/2)` (948) **before** per-char validation — that **requests** capacity; it is **not** an allocator-independent upper bound of `len/2` on memory actually committed, and there is **no max-length cap** on `salt_hex`/`ciphertext_hex` (large local field → proportional request; local/trusted input). **Disposition:** robustness note; **input owner is the local file**, not a network-reachable parser; **no vulnerability is inferred from parser leniency alone.**
6. **Provisioning — scoped negative.** There is **no encrypted-keystore production writer** in the inspected paths; the encrypted salt/nonce helpers are **test-only & deterministic** (`#[cfg(test)]`; test salt=entry_id bytes, nonce=reversed entry_id+1, 1020–1040) — **do not infer production salt/nonce quality** from them. **But** the repo **does** contain a non-test writer: `crates/qbind-node/examples/devnet_consensus_signer_keystore_helper.rs` generates real ML-DSA-44 keys and writes a **plaintext** JSON keystore (`fs::write`, 82–86; `set_mode_0600` 87), documented as a **DevNet evidence/test helper** (header 1/10–13), **not** an encrypted production provisioner. So the **blanket "all repository keystore writers are `#[cfg(test)]`" is withdrawn** (A10.1): a plaintext example writer exists. Do **not** assert operational `.enc` files must have come from an out-of-tree tool **without observing their provenance** — the encrypted-format production provisioner is simply **unlocated within scope** (E18).
7. **Operating-policy documentation vs loader (bounded; not deployment evidence).** `docs/release/public-devnet/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md` recommends **encrypted-fs** for DevNet at-rest protection (50; 69–71) and specifies **0600** private files / **0700** keystore dir (93–94/103–105) — these are **operator requirements**, distinct from loader-enforced checks (obs 4: the loader enforces none). The doc describes **`loopback-testing` as in-memory** (49), while the selected loader uses a **configured plaintext filesystem keystore** for that mode (signer_loader.rs:322) — a **bounded documentation/runtime mismatch**, recorded as such; the document is **guidance of intent, not observed deployment**.

**Separate three things (A10.1):** (i) **absence of explicit source-level erasure** — the only thing established here; (ii) **potential residual-secret lifetime** — plausible but unquantified; (iii) **demonstrated memory extraction** — **not attempted**. No key-byte leakage via Debug/errors/logs (redacted; `errors_never_carry_key_material`). **Malformed-key assurance is narrow:** the repo checks `len==ML_DSA_44_SECRET_KEY_SIZE` and invokes `PrivateKey::try_from_bytes` (ml_dsa44.rs:222–231/280–289); **without inspecting the pinned `fips204 0.4.6` criteria, do not assert every malformed or internally-inconsistent key is rejected.**

### Identity-binding note (A10 §C; refined A10.1 — not a new finding; ties to the disabled P/V boundary)
`peer_key_provider.rs:334–336` **rejects an entirely empty configured-key set** (`NoConfiguredKeys`) **before** the insertion branch — so insertion is **not unconditional**. Within a **non-empty** configured set, `peer_key_provider.rs:384–387` **inserts the signer-derived public key** as the local validator's consensus key when no explicit **local** entry is present; an explicit local entry is byte-compared against the signer-derived pk (`LocalKeyMismatchesSigner`, 371–373). Distinguish: **explicit configured-key equality** / **signer-derived insertion when the local entry is absent** / binding to an **external canonical authority** (absent). A **matching key is not proof the authority source is correct** — the authority is **self-asserted** (derived from the loaded local key), consistent with the already-**disabled** genesis / Proposal-Vote boundaries (main.rs:5405–5417/5811–5823; `proposal_vote_authority=None`). Recorded as a scoped observation, not a separate finding.

### A10-F1 — Local keystore secret-handling hardening gaps (assurance/hardening gap; local capabilities)
**Evidence:** STATIC-SUPPORTED (source) · **OPEN** · **Classification:** assurance/hardening gap — **NOT a demonstrated network vulnerability, key recovery, or decryption downgrade; NOT a standalone DevNet blocker** · **Runtime applicability:** conditional on the **local** capabilities in the threat table; **not anonymously network-reachable** (a scope condition, not a dismissal) · **Reviewer attribution:** A10/A10.1 (local, static); ChatGPT supplied the KDF/AEAD anchors (pinned repo) and the pbkdf2 upstream source-review (dependency, not locally verified); independently verified against pinned repo source. **A proposed fix is a remediation criterion, not proof the original observation was false.**

Per-component records (each a distinct shortfall, not double-counted):

**(a) No application KDF-iteration floor/ceiling.** *Source fact/scope:* `kdf_iterations` (`u32`) consumed verbatim from the file (keystore.rs:416; 608/642), passed straight to `pbkdf2_hmac::<Sha256>` (kdf.rs:63–70); config `100_000` dead on read. *Capability:* encrypted-file read for offline guessing; honest-but-weak provisioning; file-write to set the pre-auth work factor. *Existing requirement vs proposed control:* **proposed** hardening (an application floor) — no documented minimum located. *Bounded consequence + counterevidence:* a weakly-provisioned file is cheaper to attack offline (cost **unmeasured**); altering an adequately-provisioned file's count breaks the tag (**not** a downgrade) — except the supplied upstream 0↔1 equivalence (not locally verified). *Disposition / conditional DevNet relevance:* hardening gap; relevant only under the file-read/file-write capabilities, not a DevNet blocker. *Falsifier (of the source fact):* locating an application iteration floor/ceiling that this adapter actually enforces would refute the "no floor" observation (a *future* enforced floor is a **remediation criterion**, not a falsifier). *Remaining evidence:* offline-guessing cost; dependency iteration semantics (E18).

**(b) Header fields not in AEAD associated data.** *Source fact/scope:* empty AAD `b""` (keystore.rs:421); `version`/`suite_id` equality-checked pre-decrypt; `aead`/`kdf` labels ignored (756). *Capability:* file-write without passphrase. *Existing requirement vs proposed control:* **proposed** AAD binding — **no required-binding contract identified** in source. *Bounded consequence + counterevidence:* no attacker-chosen plaintext, no algorithm switch via ignored labels; equality-checked and KDF-feeding fields fail closed. *Disposition / DevNet relevance:* defense-in-depth gap. *Falsifier (of the source fact):* evidence that the header fields **are** bound as AEAD associated data would refute the "not in AAD" observation. (A header-tamper yielding a valid alternate plaintext, or an algorithm switch via a label, would be an **escalation** of consequence, not a falsifier.) *Remaining evidence:* whether a required binding contract is intended (policy question).

**(c) Transient secrets not explicitly zeroized.** *Source fact/scope:* the inventory above (passphrase ×2, derived key, plaintext Vec/String, hex buffers, fixed-size sk arrays); only the final `ValidatorSigningKey` is `ZeroizeOnDrop` (drop-path only). *Capability:* process-memory/environment inspection. *Existing requirement vs proposed control:* kdf.rs:49 **recommends** zeroizing the derived key (not done); otherwise **proposed** hardening. *Bounded consequence + counterevidence:* residual secret copies observable to an actor who can already read process memory; **only absence-of-erasure is established** — residual lifetime unquantified, extraction **not attempted**; no log/Debug leakage. *Disposition / DevNet relevance:* hardening gap behind a strong local capability. *Falsifier (of the source fact):* locating explicit `zeroize`/erasure on these specific values in source would refute the "no explicit erasure" observation. Evidence that a compiler/allocator incidentally clears the memory would **narrow the residual-memory claim** but does **not** refute the source fact that explicit erasure is absent. *Remaining evidence:* residual-lifetime/extraction (unmeasured; E18).

**(d) No loader-level file hardening.** *Source fact/scope:* join-based path, no size cap (`read_to_string`), no symlink/canonicalization guard, no ownership/permission check (keystore.rs:259–261/348–350/365); `decode_hex` allocates `len/2` before validation with no max cap (948). *Capability:* control of the selected file/dir. *Existing requirement vs proposed control:* KEY_MANAGEMENT.md **documents** operator 0600/0700 requirements — **not loader-enforced**; loader checks are **proposed**. *Bounded consequence + counterevidence:* a large/symlinked/wrong-perm local file; local-file prerequisite is a scope condition; no network exposure. *Disposition / DevNet relevance:* hardening gap (loader does not enforce the documented operator requirements). *Falsifier:* loader size/symlink/permission checks remediate it. *Remaining evidence:* none beyond the proposal.

**(e) Provisioning / policy observations.** *Source fact/scope:* no encrypted-format production writer in scope (test-only deterministic salt/nonce); a **plaintext** DevNet evidence/test helper writer exists (`examples/devnet_consensus_signer_keystore_helper.rs`); a documentation/runtime mismatch (loopback-testing "in-memory" in docs vs plaintext FS keystore in the loader). *Capability:* n/a (provenance/coverage). *Disposition:* scoped observations — do not infer production nonce quality or operational-file provenance; do not treat docs as deployment evidence. *Remaining evidence:* the out-of-scope encrypted provisioner (E18).

- **Overlaps.** Relates to **C5** custody (kept OPEN); shares the local-signer surface with **H04-F1** (H04-F1 = remote path absent; A10-F1 = local path hardening). Distinct; not double-counted. Local findings are **not** classified harmless merely because they require local access, and no key recovery / network exploit / practical exhaustion / DevNet blocker is claimed without evidence.

## 6K. A11 — Transport session freshness, AEAD counters, and replay boundaries → A11-F1

Bounded audit of the KEMTLS transport session lifecycle (configuration → handshake freshness/transcript → session-key derivation → directional AEAD → app-frame send/receive → retry/error → reconnect/disposal). **Result: A11-F1 — the transport provides no independent session freshness; combined with no ClientInit replay rejection, a *replayed* ClientInit reinstalls identical directional keys + `session_id` with per-direction counters from 0, so the first frames reuse the same (key, nonce). STATIC-SUPPORTED and DevNet-reachable (this is the one wired, externally-facing surface).** The consequence is expressed as **five distinct links** (A11.1), each dispositioned separately: **(a) reinstallation of identical directional key/nonce state** — source-supported (deterministic derive + counters-from-0); **(b) acceptance of a *recorded c2s ciphertext* at the reset receive counter** — **source-supported** (the server's wired inbound reader opens c2s frames at counter 0 with the reinstalled `k_c2s`; the recorded first c2s frame carries the exact `(k_c2s, nonce)` so its Poly1305 tag re-verifies → the server decrypts and delivers a replayed application frame in a fresh session; this does **not** require the server to emit any outbound traffic — but transport delivery is kept **separate** from P2P decoding, authenticated-origin binding, consensus-freshness checks, and application-layer acceptance, none of which is claimed here); **(c) a new s2c encryption at a reused counter** — **UNPROVEN as to attacker-relevant plaintext** (the outbound s2c route is now traced to the wired binary caller, below, so s2c encryption at counter 0 on a replayed server-side connection is *reachable*, but the content/eligibility conditions are not established); **(d) observing two ciphertexts for different plaintexts under the same (key, nonce)** — UNPROVEN (requires (c) in both the original and replayed sessions with *different* first-s2c plaintexts); **(e) plaintext recovery / Poly1305 forgery / application effect** — UNPROVEN here (a *general* consequence of one-time-key reuse per **RFC 8439 §4** — the ChaCha20 keystream and the Poly1305 one-time key are fixed by `(key, nonce)`, so two ciphertexts under a repeated pair expose the plaintext XOR and void Poly1305's one-time-MAC guarantee — but **not** demonstrated as practical recovery or forgery against this code). **Invariant (precise):** nonce uniqueness for encryption under a fixed key (per-connection *independent keys* are one satisfying design — session.rs:17–21 — not the only one; a fresh per-connection nonce/salt in the key schedule would equally satisfy it). CA lifecycle, full crypto-dependency internals, consensus replay, broad DoS, and storage/recovery are out of scope (boundaries only).

### Transport session lifecycle table
| Stage | Input owner | Enforced checks | State transition | Binary applicability | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Configuration | node builder (config) | — | `client_random`="qbind-client-{id}", `server_random`="qbind-server-{id}" — **deterministic per-validator constants** (no RNG) | DevNet (real posture) | p2p_node_builder.rs:1965–1972 |
| Handshake admission | remote peer (ClientInit) | client-cert verify (if Required); suite-id match. **Cookie enforcement is bypassed twice over (A11.1):** (i) the wired `Connection` server path calls `hs.handle_client_init` (connection.rs:286–288), **not** `handle_client_init_with_cookie` — the cookie-aware API is a *separate callable path* the wired surface does not invoke; and (ii) the builder supplies `cookie_config=None`. The DoS cookie, when used, binds ip+client_random+time, **not** `kem_ct` (cross-ref A4-F2) | server decapsulates `kem_ct` → shared secret; **no replay/dedup/freshness check** | DevNet | handshake.rs:847–891/966–1064/1229–1250; connection.rs:286–288 |
| Key derivation | transcript + shared secret | HKDF-SHA3 (`hkdf_extract`/`hkdf_expand_label`) | `session_id`, `k_c2s`, `k_s2c` = **pure deterministic fn** of (shared_secret, transcript=`"QBIND:KEMTLS"‖client_random‖server_random‖kem_ct‖client_cert`, suite ids); **no random input**; shared secret + PRK zeroized | DevNet | keys.rs:279–316; handshake.rs:998–1030; hkdf.rs:10–60 |

| Send-error | writer worker | — | a **10 s write timeout is REQUESTED** on the wired path (`configure_socket` 195–204 via `from_accepted_with_peer_init` 337, with `.ok()` — successful install per-socket not verified; `try_new` changes only the read timeout to 100 ms, 618–621, leaving write intact; the async `set_write_timeout` 914–920 is a no-op) → **if installed**, a stalled write returns **`WouldBlock`** (Unix) / **`TimedOut`** (Windows, external docs); it is not a guaranteed 10 s deadline for a whole `write_all`. **`WouldBlock` → retry** re-invokes `send_app` → **re-encrypts** (sender counter advances again), holding only plaintext (no prior ciphertext / write offset); **`TimedOut` + other errors → fatal** (no retry). **Zero-progress** (no bytes transferred) leaves the counter advanced with no frame on the wire → next frame uses a later counter than the receiver expects; **partial aggregate progress** inside `write_all` can leave a truncated prefix then restart a new frame → framing disruption. **No counter rollback.** → **A11-F2** | DevNet | secure_channel.rs:195–204/337/608–621/401–406/707–736; framed_io.rs:88–97; session.rs:68–89 |
