### 21.4 Invariant assessment

1. **Monotonic view advance — HOLDS on the guarded paths; one unguarded setter recorded (A14.1).** The advance paths on the **timeout/TC** surface are fail-closed: `try_advance_to_view` returns `false` without mutating when `target_view ≤ current_view` (3106), and `on_timeout_certificate` returns the current view (no-op) when `tc.view ≤ current_view` (3264), otherwise assigning `tc.view` **directly** (3292) — no arithmetic, strictly greater than the prior view. **Correction:** the earlier blanket "`current_view` never decreases on *any* inspected path" is **withdrawn** — `advance_view` (1796) does `current_view = current_view + 1` **with no monotonicity guard**, so at `current_view = u64::MAX` a release-profile wrap would set `current_view = 0` (a regression) and a debug/test build would panic. `advance_view` is **not** on the timeout path: its only `self.` callers are the leader single-node QC branch (2371) and `on_vote`'s QC-formed branch (3024) — the **Proposal/Vote** surface, which production rejects fail-closed before engine dispatch (§6L.1), so this unguarded setter is **not production-inbound-reachable**. The monotonicity claim is now scoped to the guarded paths, not asserted globally.
2. **Stale / duplicate handling — HOLDS.** `on_timeout_msg` drops `timeout.view < current_view` as `Ok(None)` (3207). The accumulator stores **one slot per `validator_id` per view** (timeout.rs:567/581) with a per-view cap (463/487), so a second timeout from the same validator for the same view returns `Ok(false)` (not inserted) — an equivocator cannot inflate the count — and `TimeoutCertificate::validate` **independently** rejects duplicate signers via a HashSet (timeout.rs:359/369) before the `two_thirds_vp` power check (380). *(This is the logical power/dedup check; the crypto signature verification is the separate ctx-gated layer, A1-F1.)*
3. **Arithmetic (overflow / wrap / caps) — reachability reconciled with A1-F2; a consequence of the existing mechanism, not a separate finding (A14.1).** On the **timeout/TC successor computation** every view increment is **saturating**: TC target `timeout_view.saturating_add(1)` (timeout.rs:318/334), restore `committed_height.saturating_add(1)`/`snapshot_height.saturating_add(1)` (1940/2013); the tick counter is `saturating_add` (2900/3054); `timeout_window_elapsed` uses `saturating_sub` (2192); backoff is `saturating_mul` → `.min(max_ticks)` (cap after multiply, 2416–2417). The **two ordinary (unchecked) `+` on a view** are (i) the `on_timeout_msg` TC-scan upper bound `self.current_view + 10` (3222 baseline / 3239 working tree) and (ii) `advance_view`'s `current_view + 1` (1796). **Exact boundaries (M = `u64::MAX`):** `v + 10` overflows **iff `v ≥ M − 9`**; `v + 1` overflows **iff `v = M`**.

   **Build / overflow profile — committed defaults vs effective flags (A14.2).** The workspace `Cargo.toml` (baseline) defines `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.test]` overriding only `debug`/`strip`/`incremental` — **no `overflow-checks` override** — and **no `[profile.release]` stanza at all**, so the Rust **defaults** stand: **dev/test → overflow-checks on → the `+10`/`+1` panics**; **release → overflow-checks off → two's-complement wrap**. These are the committed-profile **default implications only**; the **effective flags of any actually-shipped binary are unobserved** — RUSTFLAGS, a CI profile, or `cargo build --config` could force `overflow-checks` on in release (or set `panic = "abort"`), none of which this read-only slice inspects (no build, no secret-bearing environment). **On an overflow-checked panic:** the expression panics; under the default **unwind** strategy (no committed `panic = "abort"`) the panic **unwinds the spawned consensus-loop task** (`tokio::spawn` returning a `JoinHandle`, binary_consensus_loop.rs:8854), stopping that task and resolving its handle to a panic error. **The process/node consequence** (exit, restart, or continue with consensus-loop participation halted) depends on how `main.rs` supervises that handle and is **not** established here — **whole-node termination is NOT inferred from the expression alone**. The task-level consequence (that node's consensus-loop stops) is itself a progress loss.

   **Reachability — cadence argument withdrawn.** The earlier "practically unreachable at any realistic view cadence" justification is **withdrawn**: reaching a high `current_view` does **not** require incrementing views sequentially. `on_timeout_certificate` assigns `current_view = tc.view` **directly**, and `tc.view` is **unbound** (A1-F2) — `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` binds the signed evidence to `tc.timeout_view` (the `MixedView` check) but **never checks `tc.view`** — so a single **admitted inbound NewView** can set `current_view` to any value `> current`, including `M − 9 … M`, in one step. **Evidence prerequisite corrected (A14.2):** the accepted transition needs **admissible 2/3 signed-timeout evidence for some view `T`** — NOT quorum signatures at the elevated target `V`. `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` enforces `ev.view == tc.timeout_view == T` (`MixedView`), per-signer membership + suite + signature over the preimage `(chain_id, T, high_qc, validator_id)` (timeout_verify.rs:238–320), and 2/3 VP — and `verify_timeout_msg` binds the signature to a **`chain_id` domain** (deployment/chain separation — a **domain binding**, not freshness enforcement) and otherwise checks only membership + governance key/suite + signature over `(chain_id, T, high_qc, validator_id)`; **on this reviewed TC-admission path nothing constrains `T` to the receiver's current view or epoch** (A15 — the absence-of-freshness claim is scoped to this admission path and its actual membership/key checks, not asserted of other layers), so within that path `T` may be **any** view (ordinary current-round timeouts, or captured/stale ones) and `tc.view = V` is free. Preconditions carried intact: authorized transport **origin admission** (bound peer; Run 418 `authorize_origin` when a gate is installed), applicable **membership/suite/`chain_id`** checks, and **evidence validity at `T`**; then either (b-absent) **`verification_ctx == None`** — no signature check at all (**A1-F1**), the forged TC needing only a `signers` list naming ≥ 2/3 of the (public) validator set to pass the logical `validate`; or (b-present) the admissible 2/3 evidence at `T` **repackaged** with an attacker-chosen `V`. So the ctx-present path requires only **ordinary single-view timeout evidence**, not "high-view" signatures — reachable with routine or colluded/captured evidence. The overflow prerequisite is therefore **reachable**, the **downstream manifestation of A1-F2** (absent path: A1-F1) — **not** a cadence question.

   **Consumption / consequence (traced, not assumed; A14.2 — "benign" withdrawn).**
   - `current_view + 10` is only the **upper bound of a `RangeInclusive`** `self.current_view..=self.current_view + 10` — **no wrapped value is assigned to `current_view`**, so the view value itself is not corrupted by the bound. **Release (overflow-checks off):** the bound wraps below `current_view`, the range is **empty** (`start > end`), the loop body never runs, `maybe_tc_for(current_view)` is **never evaluated**, and `on_timeout_msg` returns `Ok(None)`. **This is NOT asserted "benign":** the `on_timeout_msg` scan is the **sole** production path that forms a TC from accumulated timeouts (its only non-test caller is `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3225` → `maybe_tc_for`, verified), so while `current_view ∈ [M−9, M]` a **locally-formable TC for the current view is never formed** and **timeout-driven self-advance halts for that view band** — even though the local timeout was still ingested into the accumulator (`on_timeout`) and still broadcast (7301/7321). What is lost is local TC **formation** at the elevated view, not accumulator or broadcast state. **What can still advance progress:** only an **externally admitted inbound NewView TC** with `view ∈ (current, M]` (the same A1-F2 injection; nothing exists above `M`), or a commit-driven `advance_view` on the **Proposal/Vote** QC path (**not production-inbound-reachable**). **Unresolved (runtime, E02):** whether the stall is persistent, and whether it reaches the whole validator set, depends on delivery of the triggering TC and multi-node behaviour — source establishes the **local formation gap**, not permanent or network-wide loss. **Debug/test (overflow-checks on):** the `+10` **panics** → unwinds the spawned consensus-loop task (build bullet above); node/process effect not inferred.
   - `advance_view`'s `current_view + 1` is assigned **directly** to `current_view` with no guard (21.4 #1): a release wrap at `v = M` would **regress `current_view` to 0**, a debug/test build would panic — **but** `advance_view` is on the **Proposal/Vote** QC path, which production rejects fail-closed before engine dispatch, so it is **not production-inbound-reachable** (library/sim/test only).

   **Terminal-view distinction (A15; M = `u64::MAX`).** The `[M−9, M]` band is not uniform — two sub-cases:
   - **`v ∈ [M−9, M−1]`:** the wrapped `+10` scan is empty, so it **skips TC-formation candidates** that the scan would otherwise evaluate — including an **otherwise-eligible current-view candidate** (`maybe_tc_for(v)` with ≥ 2/3 accumulated timeouts present). Here the **scan** is the proximate cause of the missed local advance (strictly-greater views `v+1 … M` still exist, so a forward transition is not arithmetically precluded — it is the empty scan that prevents forming the TC). Quorum availability is still a precondition: if < 2/3 timeouts are accumulated for `v`, no TC would form regardless of the scan.
   - **`v = M`:** the scan is **also** empty, **but** no strictly-greater `u64` view exists, so even the saturating successor `timeout_view.saturating_add(1)` yields `M → M`, which **cannot satisfy the strictly-forward transition guard** (`try_advance_to_view` `target ≤ current → false` 3106; `on_timeout_certificate` `tc.view ≤ current → return` 3264; `maybe_tc_for`-formed TC has `view = v.saturating_add(1) = M ≤ current`). So at the terminal view the progress limitation is **not attributable to the scan alone** — the view space is exhausted and the forward-only guards reject `M → M` independently. (Reaching `v = M` still requires the A1-F2 admission preconditions — origin admission + evidence at some `T` or ctx-absent — and sufficient quorum for whatever would advance it.)

   **Disposition (A14.2; A15-refined).** Not a separate finding and not an unchanged "practically unreachable" observation. **Supported arithmetic result:** the wrapped bound is never assigned to `current_view`; in release the scan is empty, in dev/test the expression panics. **Source-established progress consequence:** for `v ∈ [M−9, M−1]` the empty scan **skips an otherwise-eligible current-view TC candidate** (local self-advance blocked by the scan, strictly-greater views still existing); for `v = M` the view space is exhausted and the forward-only guards reject the saturating `M → M` successor independently of the scan; in dev/test the expression panics-and-unwinds the consensus-loop task (default-unwind). The earlier "benign / no state corruption / **contained in the production release profile**" characterisation is **withdrawn** — the release outcome is a **local liveness gap**, not a non-consequence. The earlier "benign / no state corruption / **contained in the production release profile**" characterisation is **withdrawn** — the release outcome is a **local liveness gap**, not a non-consequence. **Remaining uncertainties:** persistence, multi-node/system-wide reach, and the actually-deployed build flags — **runtime (E02)**. (**A15 update, A15.1-reconciled:** the **owner's** supervision of the consensus task is **source-traced** (§22/A15-F1) — the consensus panic is **unsupervised by the owner** (no detection/recovery), so under the default-unwind inspected path it does **not** terminate the process (stderr diagnostics are still emitted; "silently/unobserved" withdrawn). The termination-**propagation** trace (P2P listener/acceptance lifecycle, facade/engine `Drop`) is **incomplete** (§22.5 source-review gap); the deployed `panic`/overflow flags + external recovery remain **E21**.) Folded into **A1-F2 / E02** (target-binding + overflow/permanence); totals unchanged (A15-F1 is a separate assurance-gap entry, §22).
4. **Backoff grow/reset events — HOLD as documented; "fail-closed" scoped (A14.1).** Backoff grows **only** after reaching the post-encode emission decision without committed progress (7292) and resets **only** on committed-height progress (`reset_on_progress`, 7142); **view-only / TC-driven advances reset the timeout *window* (`last_progress_tick`) but NOT the backoff level** (reset is gated on committed height, not on `current_view` change). On **invalid config** (`multiplier == 0`, `base == Some(0)`, or `max < base`) `ViewTimeoutBackoffState::new` returns `Err`; the loop (2767–2793) logs a warning and **constructs a disabled pacer (`base_ticks = None`) and continues** — startup is **not** aborted. The disabled pacer reports `threshold() == None`, so Gate 1 returns every tick: **no timeout is ever emitted, backoff never grows, and all backoff counters stay zero** for that run. "Fail-closed" here is scoped precisely to **not emitting under a rejected config** (no silent fallback to the fixed cadence); it is **not** a process halt and **not** a system-wide liveness guarantee — on the contrary, timeout-driven view change is **disabled** for that run, so liveness recovery via this primitive is lost (other liveness assumptions are 21.6).
5. **Signer absence / failure — fail-closed, five states made executable (A14.1).** Gate 3 (7161) requires an **outbound facade**; with none, the function returns before signing (no emission in any ctx). With a facade present:
   - **ctx absent (`None`):** `sign_required=false` → **skip signing** → encode → `mark_timeout_emitted` → `view_timeouts_emitted++` → **backoff grow** → local ingest → **broadcast (unsigned)** → apply TC if formed. (Unsigned emission is gated on `verification_ctx.is_none()` + facade, **not** on a literal "LocalMesh" config — the comment's label is intent, not an enforced guard.)
   - **ctx present + signer `None`:** `outbound_timeout_signing_failure++`, `mark_timeout_emitted`, `view_timeouts_emitted++`, **return** — **no encode/ingest/broadcast/backoff growth/view mutation**.
   - **ctx present + sign `Err`:** identical effect to signer-`None` (counter + mark + return; nothing emitted).
   - **ctx present + sign `Ok`:** signed msg → encode → mark → count → backoff grow → ingest → **broadcast (signed)** → apply TC if formed.

   `mark_timeout_emitted` + `view_timeouts_emitted++` fire **together at the mark point**, reached in exactly three places: signer-`None` early-return (7223/7224), sign-`Err` early-return (7259/7260), and after a **successful encode** (7281/7282). **A14.2 — one pre-mark return exists:** between signing and the mark, `bincode::serialize(&timeout_msg)` failure **returns at 7276 WITHOUT marking or counting** (and without ingest/broadcast/backoff). So the counter counts **mark-point arrivals** (fail-closed sign-aborts + successful-encode emission decisions) — **not** signing invocations, **not** broadcast enqueues, **not** deliveries — and **backoff growth and any broadcast/ingest occur only on the None-ctx and sign-Ok sub-states**. No silent downgrade to an unsigned broadcast on the signed path.
6. **Single-shot marker — ownership corrected; precise invariant (A14.1).** The marker Gate 4 reads (7165) is the **engine's single boolean `timeout_emitted_in_view`** (`BasicHotStuffEngine`), set by `mark_timeout_emitted()` and cleared on **every** path that mutates `current_view` — `try_advance_to_view` (3126), `advance_view` (1804), and `on_timeout_certificate` (3295). It is a **single bool, not a per-view-number keyed set**, and it is **not** a `ViewTimeoutState` field (`ViewTimeoutState` holds only `last_observed_view`/`last_observed_commits`/`last_progress_tick`; clearing the engine flag does **not** touch those). **Correction:** "exactly one timeout *emission* per view" is **withdrawn** — in the signer-`None`/`Err` sub-states (21.4 #5) `mark_timeout_emitted` is set with **zero** emissions. **Exact event guarded (A14.2):** the flag guards **re-entry past the mark point** (7223/7259/7281), **not** signing invocation — a **pre-mark return** (the encode-failure branch, 7276) leaves the flag **unset**, so on a later tick with the window still elapsed the loop **re-enters and re-invokes signing** within the same `current_view` occupancy. Hence signing invocation, marker consumption, counter increment, broadcast enqueue, and delivery are **distinct** and must not be equated: the supported invariant is **at most one mark-point arrival per contiguous `current_view` occupancy** (not "one signing invocation" and not "one emission"). **Preconditions for ANY mark to occur (A15):** a mark-point arrival requires, in order, all five emission gates to pass — `backoff.threshold()` is `Some` (primitive enabled, Gate 1), `restore_mode` inactive (Gate 2), an outbound facade present (Gate 3), the engine flag `timeout_emitted_in_view` currently `false` (Gate 4), and the tick window elapsed (`current_tick − last_progress_tick ≥ threshold`, Gate 5) — **then** either the ctx-present signer-`None`/sign-`Err` early-return (marks) or a successful `bincode::serialize` (marks). The encode-failure branch is a **conditional pre-mark return** (7276) that leaves the flag unset. **A15 correction:** the earlier "so in practice the mark is reached exactly once per occupancy" is **removed** — dependency semantics of `bincode::serialize` for this concrete type have **not** been verified here (bincode not vendored, E12), so **no failing input is established by this source review**, and no claim of practical unreachability (or of exactly-once) is assigned from an incomplete dependency review. The **supported** invariant stands: **at most one mark-point arrival per contiguous `current_view` occupancy** (the flag blocks re-entry past a mark), while a pre-mark serialization-error return would permit another signing invocation in the same occupancy. Re-arming additionally requires the **independent** `ViewTimeoutState` window (`current_tick − last_progress_tick ≥ threshold`), whose `last_progress_tick` is reset by `observe()` on view-or-commit progress — a separate mechanism from the engine flag — and restore-catchup (`restore_mode` active, Gate 2 at 7157) suppresses emission entirely while catching up.
7. **Channel / lock / event-loop dependencies — source-visible, runtime-unresolved.** The pacer is **tick-based** inside a single `tokio::select!` loop sharing the 100 ms interval with inbound-message handling; `apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view` depends on the outbound facade channel and the engine lock. Progress of the timer therefore has **source-visible dependencies on event-loop scheduling** that source inspection cannot quantify (see 21.6).

A14 extends A1-F1's evidence with the emission-side signer fail-closed behaviour (21.4 #5); it does **not** add a finding.

This is a **consequence of the existing A1-F2 mechanism** — extended, **not** re-counted and **not** a separate finding; persistence/system-wide reach/build-flags are runtime-unresolved (E02).

### 21.6 DevNet applicability and liveness caveat

- **Wired and DevNet-reachable** when an outbound facade is present (multi-validator public DevNet): the emission → ingest → TC → `NewView` broadcast → view advance path runs. A **single-validator / LocalMesh** configuration has no outbound broadcast target, so `outbound_new_views_sent` stays zero and the view-transition remains local.
- **Liveness is out of source scope.** Any claim that the pacemaker *guarantees* view progress under faults requires **fairness** (the `select!` loop services the tick arm), **clock** (interval accuracy under load), **delivery** (TC/NewView reach a quorum), and **scheduling** (blocking work does not starve the tick) assumptions that **source inspection cannot establish**. This slice establishes the **structure and invariants** of the transition machinery, not its runtime liveness.

### 21.7 What source alone cannot establish here

Multi-node / partition / starvation behaviour; real timer accuracy under load; whether a live deployment's `verification_ctx` is active (E09 bridge activation); the quorum-formation **crypto** verification of accumulated timeouts (A1-F1, verification-gated); the **actual CI/release build flags and `panic` strategy** of a deployed binary (only committed profile settings were inspected — external overrides unknown, 21.4 #3); the **task-supervision** consequence of an overflow panic (unwinds the spawned loop task; whether `main.rs` exits/restarts/continues is not traced here); and, for the context-present path, the runtime **availability of admissible 2/3 single-view timeout evidence for some view `T`** (the evidence need **not** be high-view and is not freshness-bound — A14.2 — so it is ordinary round or captured/colluded evidence; its runtime availability under a 2/3-honest model, and the delivery/multi-node reach that would make any resulting stall persistent or system-wide, are **runtime-evidence** questions, E02). The **source reachability** of the view-arithmetic edge and the **local** timeout-formation stall it causes are now established (21.4 #3); their **runtime manifestation, persistence, network-wide reach, and per-build consequence** remain unmeasured (E02).

### 21.10 A14.2 — empty-scan consequence and E02 prerequisite reconciliation (v0.32)

One bounded, read-only reconciliation of the remaining A14.1 conclusions against pinned source `ef99e29`. No execution/implementation/re-pin/new-subsystem review; external register the only write. **No new finding, no count change, A1-F1/A1-F2 dispositions unchanged.**

**1 — Arithmetic behaviour vs progress consequence ("benign/contained" withdrawn).** Traced the empty-scan result through `on_timeout_msg` and its sole formation caller. Established, distinctly: **(a)** no wrapped scan-bound value is assigned to `current_view` (the view value is not corrupted by the bound); **(b)** on a release wrap the `RangeInclusive` is empty so the loop performs **no candidate evaluation** and returns `Ok(None)`; **(c)** `maybe_tc_for` has exactly **one** non-test caller — the `+10` scan at `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3225` (verified) — so this scan is the **sole** production TC-formation path, and skipping it means a **locally-formable TC for the current view is never formed → local timeout-driven self-advance halts** while `current_view ∈ [M−9, M]` (the local timeout is still ingested into the accumulator and still broadcast; only local formation is lost); **(d)** the only source-visible transitions that could still advance are an **externally admitted inbound NewView TC** with `view ∈ (current, M]` (same A1-F2 injection) or the commit-driven `advance_view` on the **not-production-inbound-reachable** Proposal/Vote path. Therefore "benign," "no state corruption," and "CONTAINED (production release)" are **withdrawn** and replaced by **"local timeout-driven self-advance halts for `current_view ∈ [M−9,M]` (release); task panic (dev/test)"**. Whether the stall is **persistent** or **system-wide** is **not** inferred from source — it depends on delivery of the triggering TC and multi-node behaviour (runtime, E02). Kept under A1-F2/E02; no separate finding.

**2 — Signed-evidence prerequisite corrected.** The accepted transition's evidence prerequisite is **admissible 2/3 signed-timeout evidence for some view `T`** (with `tc.timeout_view == T`), **not** quorum signatures at the elevated target `V = tc.view`. Source: `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` enforces `ev.view == tc.timeout_view` (`MixedView`), per-signer membership+suite+signature, and 2/3 VP (timeout_verify.rs:350–427); `verify_timeout_msg` signs over `(chain_id, view=T, high_qc, validator_id)` binds the signature to a **`chain_id` domain** (domain binding, not freshness) and on this admission path imposes **no freshness/epoch binding** tying `T` to the receiver's current view (scoped to this path's membership/key checks; timeout_verify.rs:238–320). So `T` may be any view (ordinary round evidence, or captured/colluded) and `V` is free. **Corrected** the v0.31 "honest-majority availability of 2/3 **high-view** signed evidence" wording in §21.9/E02/header/§5. **Preserved genuine prerequisites:** origin admission (Run 418 `authorize_origin`), membership/suite/`chain_id`, evidence validity at `T`, `V > current_view`; ctx-absent needs no signatures at all (A1-F1). No freshness constraint is enforced on the TC path beyond `chain_id` (recorded as a source condition, distinct from unobserved deployment evidence).

**3 — Single-shot / counter semantics refined.** Inspected every return between signing, encoding, marking, and the counter increment. The engine flag `timeout_emitted_in_view` is consumed at the **mark point** — reached at the signer-`None` early-return (7223/7224), the sign-`Err` early-return (7259/7260), or after a **successful encode** (7281/7282). A **pre-mark return exists**: `bincode::serialize` failure returns at **7276 without marking or counting**, so it does **not** consume the single-shot and **permits another signing invocation** on a later tick within the same `current_view` occupancy. Hence **signing invocation, marker consumption, counter increment, broadcast enqueue, and delivery are distinct**; the supported invariant is **at most one mark-point arrival per contiguous `current_view` occupancy** (not "one emission," not "one signing invocation"), and `view_timeouts_emitted` counts mark-point arrivals (fail-closed sign-aborts + successful-encode decisions), not transmissions. The encode-failure branch is **defensive**: the outbound emit uses the **unbounded** `bincode::serialize(&timeout_msg)` (7268) and `TimeoutMsg<[u8;32]>` is a plain serde struct (`u64`/`[u8;32]`/`Option`/`Vec<u8>`) serialized to a `Vec` writer, for which no failing input is apparent under the default serializer — stated as **practically-unreachable-from-source** (bincode internals not vendored, E12), not proven-impossible.

## 22. A15 — Consensus-loop task supervision (read-only source slice; v0.33)

**Scope.** One bounded, read-only source slice tracing the production consensus-loop `JoinHandle` from `spawn_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` through its owner in `main.rs`. Baseline `ef99e29`; all citations baseline line numbers. This resolves — at the source level, for the unwind case — the "task/process consequence" question left open in §21.4 #3 / §21.10 (A14.2). Not a persistence/recovery audit.

### 22.1 Production call chain and handle ownership

- **Spawn.** `spawn_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:8854) and `spawn_binary_consensus_loop` both `tokio::spawn` the loop and return `(JoinHandle<BinaryConsensusLoopProgress>, Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<BinaryConsensusLoopProgress>>)` (8863–8876).
- **Two production call sites, both async fns in `main.rs`:** the wired **P2P** path `run_p2p_node` (main.rs:6176) at **8708–8709** (`spawn_binary_consensus_loop_with_io(consensus_cfg, shutdown_rx, node_metrics, io)`); the **LocalMesh** path `run_local_mesh_node` (main.rs:5485) at **5590** (`spawn_binary_consensus_loop(cfg, shutdown_rx, node_metrics)`). `async fn main()` (2009) dispatches to these.
- **Owner.** Each enclosing async fn owns the returned `JoinHandle` as a local binding `consensus_handle`; the `Arc<Mutex<…Progress>>` is bound as **`_progress` and left unused** in both sites (main.rs:5590/8708) — no in-process watchdog reads the progress object.
- **Handle handling — complete inventory (grep over `consensus_handle`, main.rs):** bound at 5590/8708; awaited at 5596/8730; **nowhere else** — no `.abort()`, no `JoinSet`, no `.is_finished()`, not placed in any `tokio::select!`. During the run each fn **parks on `tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await`** (5593/8726). On the signal it `drop(shutdown_tx)` (5595/8729) then `let _ = consensus_handle.await` (5596/8730) — the result is **discarded**.

### 22.2 Task-lifecycle table (production, baseline `ef99e29`)

| Lifecycle aspect | Source behavior | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spawn | `tokio::spawn` → `JoinHandle<…Progress>` + unused `Arc<Mutex<…Progress>>` | binary_consensus_loop.rs:8854–8876 |
| Owner | enclosing async fn; local `consensus_handle`; `_progress` **unused** | main.rs:8708 (`run_p2p_node` 6176) / 5590 (`run_local_mesh_node` 5485) |
| Poll during run | **NONE** — fn parks on `ctrl_c().await`; handle in no `select!` | main.rs:8726 / 5593 |
| Await | **once, at shutdown only**, after `drop(shutdown_tx)`; result **discarded** (`let _ =`) | main.rs:8729–8730 / 5595–5596 |
| Normal completion mid-run | **unobserved** (handle ready; nothing awaits until Ctrl+C) | — |
| Normal task output (A15.1) | `BinaryConsensusLoopProgress` — the loop fns return this value, **not** a `Result` | binary_consensus_loop.rs:2462 / 2490 |
| Join completion type (A15.1) | `Result<BinaryConsensusLoopProgress, JoinError>` (the `.await` result): `Ok(progress)` on normal completion, `Err(JoinError)` on panic. **No application-level `Err` outcome exists** (the loop returns a bare `Progress`) — the A15 "returned error" outcome is **withdrawn** | main.rs:8730 / 5596 |
| Internal errors (A15.1) | handled **inside** the loop; none escape as a fn `Err` (e.g. the Run 096 reconfig-intent `Err` arm logs `FATAL …` then `return BinaryConsensusLoopProgress::default()`, 2580; engine-reject / broadcast-fail paths bump stats + `eprintln`) | binary_consensus_loop.rs:2580 |
| Exit points + diagnostics (A15.1) | (a) **intended shutdown** — the `shutdown_rx.changed()` arm logs `"[binary-consensus] Shutdown signal received after N ticks."` then `break`; (b) **unexpected completion** — the Run 096 FATAL early return (2580) logs `FATAL …`. **Both are logged** and both yield `Ok(progress)` at join | binary_consensus_loop.rs:2580 + shutdown arm |
| Cancellation (owner) | a **real cooperative-cancellation mechanism IS implemented**: `drop(shutdown_tx)` closes the `watch` → the loop's `select!{ shutdown_rx.changed() => … }` arm exits. Absence of `handle.abort()` is **not** absence of cancellation (A15.1) — the owner cancels **cooperatively**, not abortively | main.rs:8729; loop 2484+ |
| Panic (unwind strategy) | caught at the task boundary → handle resolves to `Err(JoinError)` (discarded at shutdown; unobserved by the **owner** mid-run) — **but** Rust's **default panic hook emits a stderr panic diagnostic** independently of the await (no `panic::set_hook` anywhere in the tree; tokio **1.49.0**, default unwind), and the worker thread + process continue | no committed `panic = "abort"`; std default hook |
| Propagation to `main` | **NONE** (no owner-side detection); the panic/exit diagnostics still reach stderr | main.rs:8730 |
| Triggers node shutdown | **NO** — node shutdown is driven only by Ctrl+C / signal | main.rs:8726 / 5593 |
| Owner-side detection / in-process collection / alerting | **NONE** (the owner discards the handle result; no in-process aggregator/alerter) — **distinct from diagnostic emission**, which does occur (loop-exit logs; default panic hook; post-closure forward-failure logs below) | main.rs:8730 / 5596 |
| Other tasks on consensus death | the **inbound consensus handler** keeps running and **logs each dropped forward** after the receiver is gone (`try_send` → `Closed` → `"[P2P Inbound] Failed to forward consensus message (channel full or closed)"`, p2p_inbound.rs:549–553); SIGHUP (9174) / SIGUSR1 (9289) / run035 tasks are independently spawned. **A15.2/A15.3: the P2P listener/acceptance task lifecycle IS now traced (§22.8) — service-owned, driven only by the service's own `broadcast shutdown_tx` or socket EOF, unreached by consensus-task death** (one narrow outbound-dial caveat) | p2p_inbound.rs:549–553; main.rs:9174 / 9289; §22.8 |
| Restart | **NONE in source** (no respawn / supervision loop) | — |
| Shutdown propagation INTO loop | `drop(shutdown_tx)` → `shutdown_rx.changed()` select arm | main.rs:8729 |
| Loop-death signal OUT to main | **NONE** | — |

### 22.3 Supported conclusions → A15-F1 (availability/observability assurance gap)

**A15-F1 — consensus-loop task failure is unsupervised by its owner in-process (A15.1-reconciled; A15.2-completed).** The production consensus-loop `JoinHandle` is awaited only at shutdown with its result **discarded** (main.rs:8730/5596) and is **never polled during the run** (the owner parks on `ctrl_c().await`); in the **inspected owner call chain** (`run_p2p_node` 6176 / `run_local_mesh_node` 5485) there is **no owner-side failure detection, `.abort()`, restart, or failure-triggered node shutdown**, and the returned progress `Arc` is bound `_progress` and read by nothing in that chain. *(Scoping, A15.2: the unused `_progress` binding establishes absence of a health observer **in the inspected owner/call chain only** — it does not by itself rule out every conceivable observer elsewhere; none was found, but that is a scoped negative.)*

**Exit cases by phase (A15.2 — do not conflate):**
- **(P1) Task-startup refusal / early return (initialization phase):** the Run 096 reconfig-intent `Err` arm logs `FATAL …` and `return BinaryConsensusLoopProgress::default()` at **2580**, which is **before** the tick `loop` (the loop begins after pacer construction, ~2793). This is an **initialization-only** early return (`Ok(default)` at join), **not** an established mid-operation exit.
- **(P2) Orderly shutdown:** the `shutdown_rx.changed()` select arm logs `"[binary-consensus] Shutdown signal received after N ticks."` then `break` → returns progress (intended; driven by the owner's `drop(shutdown_tx)` at Ctrl+C).
- **(P3) Unexpected termination during operation:** an **unwind-strategy panic** mid-loop (e.g. the dev/test overflow-checked `+10` of §21.4 #3). A plain mid-loop `Ok` return is **not** a source-established case (once running, the loop exits only via P2 or a panic).

**A15.3 scoping:** the supervision gap applies to **P1 and P3** — premature/unexpected exits that occur while the owner is parked on `ctrl_c().await`, so they are **not detected, acted on, or restarted**, and the process continues (P3 on the default-unwind path). It does **NOT** apply to **P2** (orderly shutdown): there the owner itself initiates cancellation and **awaits** the handle (discarding only the result), then runs the **source-defined shutdown sequence** (await run035/snapshot handles → `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown`), and **process exit follows if those awaited operations complete** — this slice does **not** establish bounded completion of those awaits (A16-A2), so "the process exits" is the source-defined *sequence*, not a proven termination. The earlier "in every phase the exit is not detected … the process continues" is withdrawn; not restarting after an intended P2 shutdown is correct behaviour, not the gap. **Shutdown-completion (whether the awaited operations are bounded) is a separate question from A15-F1's premature-exit (P1/P3) supervision gap.**

**Diagnostics vs supervision — four separable layers (A15.1; "silently / not logged / undetected" withdrawn).** The A15 blanket "silently stopped / not logged / undetected" is **over-stated** and is corrected to:
- **Diagnostic emission — PRESENT.** The loop logs its own exits (intended-shutdown line; Run 096 `FATAL …`, 2580); a panic emits Rust's **default-panic-hook** stderr diagnostic (no `panic::set_hook` anywhere in the tree; tokio 1.49.0, default unwind); and after the consensus receiver is dropped the inbound handler logs **each** dropped forward (p2p_inbound.rs:549–553). So the failure is **not silent at stderr**.
- **Diagnostic collection / alerting — NOT ESTABLISHED.** No in-process aggregator/alerter reads those diagnostics or `_progress`.
- **Owner-side failure detection — ABSENT.** The owner discards the handle result and never polls it.
- **Automatic shutdown / recovery — ABSENT.** No source-defined restart or failure-triggered node shutdown.

**Immediate termination propagation (A15.1 item 3 — now COMPLETED for the inbound path in A15.2, §22.8).** The A15.1 "partial / source-review gap" is **closed** for the inbound path: the full ownership and propagation trace (tables in §22.8) establishes that **consensus-task death reaches no shutdown mechanism of the P2P service**. On exit the consensus task drops its owned values (`inbound_rx`, `engine`, `shutdown_rx`, pacer state) and the facade/`Arc` members (`outbound`, `peer_connectivity`, `verification_ctx` if Some, `binding_gate`, `progress`, `metrics`). **A15.3 — corrected destruction semantics:** these drops do real field-level work (the outbound/peer-connectivity **facade wrappers are destroyed** — the task is their last owner — and the inbound channel receive-half closes), but the **inner `TcpKemTlsP2pService` is not destroyed** because a concrete surviving strong owner of that exact allocation remains: `node_context.p2p_service` (`Arc<TcpKemTlsP2pService>`, p2p_node_builder.rs:147). *(The reason the service survives is the retained owner, **not** the absence of a custom `Drop`; separately there is no `impl Drop` on `TcpKemTlsP2pService`/`P2pConsensusNetwork`, so even a final-owner drop would run only recursive field-drop, not a custom shutdown — §22.8.)* The listener/accept loop and per-connection read loops run under the **service's own `broadcast shutdown_tx`** (p2p_tcp.rs:432/966/983) or socket EOF — **never** the consensus `watch` channel — so they are **not signalled** by consensus-task death. Established properties on consensus-task death: **process alive**, **listener remains bound**, **connection acceptance continues**, **consensus-message forwarding keeps being attempted and fails+logs** per frame (demuxer → `handle_consensus_msg_from` → `try_send`→`Closed`→`eprintln`→return, p2p_inbound.rs:360/386/506–554), **consensus processing stopped**. So "the node keeps serving transport" is now **source-established** (inbound), not inferred from `ctrl_c().await`. ~~Remaining caveat: the outbound-dial read-loop call site into `spawn_peer_handlers` was not re-traced line-by-line (same mechanism as inbound; §22.8).~~ **RESOLVED (A26 §31):** the production outbound path (`dial_once`:2038, not the dead `dial_peer`:1345) calls the **identical** `spawn_peer_handlers`/`read_loop`/`inbound_tx`→demuxer as the inbound path — a **supported negative**: it does not alter this conclusion, and A15-F1 is unchanged. The transport-established result now covers **both** inbound and outbound connections.

**Process / recovery, scoped to the inspected path (A15.1 — replaces "whole-node termination only under `panic=abort`").** The binary runs under `#[tokio::main]` (default **multi-thread** runtime, main.rs:2008). On the **inspected path** — committed profiles leaving the **default unwind** strategy (no `panic = "abort"`; §21.4 #3) — a consensus-task panic is caught at the task boundary, the worker thread and **process continue**, and the default hook prints the panic to stderr; the node becomes **consensus-processing-stopped, not dead**. A `panic = "abort"` build would abort the process instead, **but the effective `panic` strategy of any shipped binary is unobserved** (deployment-evidence gap, E21). These rest on **documented Rust/tokio unwind + `JoinError` semantics** (external evidence; tokio **1.49.0** recorded; **not re-verified** against the pinned toolchain/impl). **Recovery:** there is **no source-defined automatic restart**; external recovery is **unobserved and not assumed**; and an **exit-triggered** external restart policy (e.g. systemd `Restart=on-failure`) would **not** address the alive-but-consensus-stopped case (no process exit to trigger it) — detecting that case would require a **health/liveness watchdog**, which is **not established** in source (and is not assumed to exist, nor assumed to be the only possible mechanism).

**Disposition.** STATIC-SUPPORTED (source-level) **owner-supervision + in-process-detection/recovery assurance gap** (not an observability-of-emission gap — stderr diagnostics are emitted). **Not** a demonstrated exploit and **not** a static-supported security-weakness finding; it remains in the **assurance-gap disposition class** (with A4-F2 / H04-F1 / A10-F1), so the **11 static-supported** count is unchanged and the assurance-gap class is **4**. **This refines (does not withdraw) the A14.2 open question:** a consensus panic does **not** terminate the process on the inspected (unwind) path — resolving "whole-node termination not inferred" for that path — while the owner-supervision gap stands.

### 22.4 Negative-claim verification (nonempty scope + positive controls)

The "no supervision" claims were checked against a **live** search scope (`git grep` over `crates/qbind-node/src/main.rs` at `ef99e29`). **Positive controls** confirm the scope is non-empty and the patterns are searchable: `tokio::select!` **is** present (2 matches — the SIGHUP task 9174 and the SIGUSR1 snapshot task 9289, **neither on `consensus_handle`**), and `ctrl_c().await` **is** present (5593/8726, the actual park points). Against that live scope, `consensus_handle` matches **only** the bind (5590/8708) and the discarded await (5596/8730); `.abort()`, `JoinSet`, and `.is_finished()` on the handle return **no matches**. Process termination / continued service is **not** inferred from the mere presence of `tokio::spawn` — it is read from the owner's actual await/park structure. **A15.1 additions:** (i) `panic::set_hook` / `set_hook(` returns **no matches across the entire tracked tree** at `ef99e29` (positive control: `tokio::spawn` matches many files in the same scope), so **no custom panic hook** suppresses the std default hook — the default stderr panic diagnostic applies. (ii) the inbound closed-channel behavior is a **positive** trace, not an inference: `ChannelConsensusHandler::handle_consensus_msg_from` calls `self.sender.try_send(...)` and, on `Err`, executes the `eprintln!("[P2P Inbound] Failed to forward consensus message (channel full or closed): …")` branch and returns — it does **not** exit or propagate (p2p_inbound.rs:506–554).

### 22.5 Uncertainty classification

- **Source review — the A15.1 gaps are now CLOSED (A15.2, §22.8):** (a) the **P2P listener / transport-acceptance task lifecycle** on consensus-task death is traced — those tasks are owned by the service (accept loop `listener_handle`, p2p_tcp.rs:938; read/write loops in the `peers` map) and are driven only by the service's own `broadcast shutdown_tx` or socket EOF, never by consensus-task death; and (b) the field-level cleanup is inspected (A15.3): the facade wrappers are destroyed but the inner service survives via the concrete owner `node_context.p2p_service` (147); the `engine` is destroyed with recursive field-drop (consensus state + recorder `Arc` refcount−1) and holds **no channel/handle/service field** (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:1082–1173), so no shutdown propagates; there is no custom `impl Drop` on the transport types (so no custom-shutdown would run even on a final drop). ~~**One narrow source caveat remains:** the outbound-dial read-loop call site into `spawn_peer_handlers` was not re-traced line-by-line (same mechanism as the inbound path).~~ **RESOLVED (A26 §31):** the outbound-dial read-loop was re-traced firsthand — production site `dial_once`:2038 → identical `spawn_peer_handlers`:1362 → `read_loop`:1448 with the same `inbound_tx`→demuxer; supported negative, A15-F1 unchanged. The "node keeps serving transport" consequence is now **source-established for both inbound and outbound** connections.
- **Dependency-evidence gap:** the exact panic-catch / `JoinError` semantics of `tokio::spawn`/`JoinHandle` and the std **default panic hook** are tokio/std-defined and documented, but tokio (**locked 1.49.0**, Cargo.lock) is not vendored here (E12 class) — treated as **external semantic evidence** (supplied general Rust/tokio documentation), **not** re-verified against the pinned dependency implementation, and the **current online docs are not claimed to verify the locked `1.49.0` build**.
- **Deployment/runtime-evidence gaps (E21):** the **effective `panic` strategy and overflow flags** of a shipped binary; whether (and how) any **external recovery** acts; and the **observed runtime behavior** of a node whose consensus task has stopped — all unobserved. Note an **exit-triggered** external restart does not cover the alive-but-consensus-stopped case.

### 22.6 Public DevNet applicability (conditional)

On the intended multi-validator **P2P DevNet** profile (`run_p2p_node`), A15-F1 means a consensus-task failure yields a node whose **consensus processing has stopped with no owner-side detection or automatic recovery**, while (A15.2, §22.8) the **P2P transport keeps running** — listener bound, connections accepted, inbound read/demuxer draining — and each consensus frame's final forward **fails and is logged** (`"[P2P Inbound] Failed to forward consensus message (channel full or closed)"`). Stderr diagnostics are emitted (loop-exit log and/or default panic hook, plus the per-frame forward-failure logs). This "alive node, live transport, dead consensus, logged-but-unacted-on" state is now **source-established** on the inspected (default-unwind) path, **conditional on** the deployed `panic` strategy (a `panic="abort"` build would instead abort the process — unobserved) and on whatever external recovery exists (E21; an exit-triggered restart would not cover the alive-but-stopped case). Applicability remains **conditional on the intended configuration and available evidence**; no live runtime behavior is asserted.

### 22.8 A15.2 — immediate ownership and termination-propagation trace (v0.35)

Completes the outstanding A15.1 source portion (the termination-propagation / cleanup trace) **before** opening any new subsystem. Baseline `ef99e29`; citations are baseline line numbers. A corroborating subagent independently re-traced the P2P-service task lifecycle; the three load-bearing facts (the `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown` body, that `TcpKemTlsP2pService::shutdown` has no node-path caller, and the accept-loop's own-broadcast select) were **independently re-verified here** against pinned source. **No new finding, no count change; A15-F1 retained and its propagation portion completed.**

**Table 1 — Ownership / cleanup at consensus-task termination.** The loop task owns `io: BinaryConsensusLoopIo` (moved in), the `engine` local, `shutdown_rx`, and local pacer state.

*(A15.3 note: Rust **recursively drops every field** when a value is dropped, with or without a custom `Drop` impl, and dropping an `Arc` **does** run the inner value's destructor **iff it was the last strong owner**. The table below therefore records the actual field-level cleanup each drop performs and names, for each shared allocation, a **concrete surviving strong owner of the same allocation**.)*

| Object (held by the consensus task) | Kind | What its drop actually does at task end | Concrete surviving owner of the same allocation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `io.inbound_rx` (`mpsc::Receiver<InboundConsensusEnvelope>`) | **owned value** | **destroyed** → closes the channel's receive half (a real cleanup effect) → the demuxer's `Sender::try_send` now returns `Closed` (p2p_inbound.rs:467/511) | — (the `Sender` is the surviving half, in the demuxer) |
| `io.outbound` (`Arc<P2pConsensusNetwork>` facade wrapper, **moved** in — built `Arc::new(P2pConsensusNetwork::new(node_context.p2p_service.clone(), …))` main.rs:8495) | **sole owner of the outer facade wrapper** | the task is the last owner of **this facade wrapper**, so the wrapper **is destroyed**; its recursive field-drop drops the **inner `Arc<TcpKemTlsP2pService>` clone** (refcount−1) and an `Arc<NodeMetrics>` clone (refcount−1). **Facade-wrapper destruction ≠ inner-service destruction.** | **inner service:** `node_context.p2p_service` (`Arc<TcpKemTlsP2pService>`, p2p_node_builder.rs:147) — the exact allocation the facade cloned |
| `io.peer_connectivity` (`Some(Arc<P2pServicePeerConnectivity>)`, **moved** in — `Arc::new(P2pServicePeerConnectivity::new(node_context.p2p_service.clone()))` main.rs:8655–8661) | **sole owner of this wrapper** | wrapper **destroyed**; recursive field-drop drops its inner `Arc<TcpKemTlsP2pService>` clone (refcount−1) | **inner service:** `node_context.p2p_service` (147) |
| `io.verification_ctx` (`Option<Arc<TimeoutVerificationContext>>`, from the consumed `ConsensusSecurityPreflight`) | **Some or None** (Timeout/NewView config; see note below) — when `Some`, the task is the owner | if `Some`: `TimeoutVerificationContext` **destroyed** → recursive field-drop drops its `validators`/`key_provider`/`backend_registry` `Arc` clones (refcount−1 each) | the key-provider / backend-registry / validator-set allocations have their own owners in the preflight-built graph; none is a transport channel |
| `io.binding_gate` (`Option<Arc<PeerConsensusBindingGate>>`, a clone) | shared `Arc` clone | refcount−1 (not last owner) → inner **not** destroyed | `node_context.binding_gate` (p2p_node_builder.rs:200) |
| `engine` (`BasicHotStuffEngine<[u8;32]>`) | **owned local** (2492) | **destroyed** → recursive field-drop releases consensus state (`state`, `timeout_accumulator`, `leaders`: ordinary memory) and drops four optional **recorder `Arc` clones** (`view_duration`/`progress`/`validator_vote`/`equivocation`, refcount−1). **Inspected: the engine holds no `Sender`/`Receiver`/`JoinHandle`/service/facade field** (struct basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:1082–1173), so its drop performs **no channel closure, task abort, or shutdown signal** | recorder allocations: `node_metrics` recorders (other owners) |
| `shutdown_rx` (`watch::Receiver<()>`) | owned value | **destroyed** → one fewer `watch` receiver; **no effect** on the sender or other receivers | `shutdown_tx` retained by the owner fn (dropped only at Ctrl+C) |
| `progress` (`Arc<Mutex<BinaryConsensusLoopProgress>>`) | shared `Arc` clone | refcount−1 → inner not destroyed | the owner's `_progress` clone (unused) |
| `metrics` (`Arc<NodeMetrics>`) | shared `Arc` clone | refcount−1 → inner not destroyed | the node's other `node_metrics` owners |

**Cleanup-proof correction (A15.3).** The v0.35 claims "no `Drop` impl → no cleanup side effect" and "dropping an `Arc` clone cannot destroy its contents" are **withdrawn** — both are wrong in general: Rust recursively drops fields regardless of a custom `Drop`, and an `Arc`-clone drop *does* destroy the inner value when it is the last strong owner. The corrected position: the facade wrappers `io.outbound` / `io.peer_connectivity` **are** destroyed at task end (the task is their last owner) and their field-drops do real work (dropping inner `Arc` clones); the **inner `TcpKemTlsP2pService` is not destroyed** because `node_context.p2p_service` (p2p_node_builder.rs:147) is a concrete surviving strong owner of that exact allocation. (There is separately **no `impl Drop`** on `TcpKemTlsP2pService`/`P2pConsensusNetwork` — the only `impl Drop`s under `crates/qbind-node/src` are `GateReleaseGuard`, `SingleThreadExecutionService`, `Reservation`, `DupBackingLiveProbe`, `PreparedPin`, `SnapshotProgressGuard` — so even a hypothetical final-owner drop would run only the compiler-generated recursive field-drop, not a custom shutdown; but that fact is now used only to describe *what a final drop would do*, not to claim Arc-clone drops are inert.) The conclusion that follows is scoped as: **ordinary memory/resource release and `Arc` refcount decrements occur, but none of the inspected field-drops reaches the P2P service's own shutdown mechanism** (its `broadcast shutdown_tx`, accept loop, or read loops) — see Table 2 and the exit-phase conclusion.

**Configuration note (A15.3 — corrects "`verification_ctx=None` in production").** Three authority axes are **separate** and must not be collapsed: (a) **TimeoutVerificationContext activation** — `io.verification_ctx` is `Some` when `run_p2p_consensus_security_preflight` builds a Timeout/NewView context (a local consensus signer + peer keys are configured) and `None` otherwise (e.g. single-validator LocalMesh with no signer); (b) **Proposal/Vote authority** — `io.proposal_vote_authority`, a *distinct* message-family capability, which the header records as `None` on the production `Required`-policy path; (c) the **current-authorization snapshot** (`current_auth`), also `None` in production. The v0.35 ownership row's flat "`None` in production" conflated (a) with (b)/(c); corrected to "`Some` or `None` per the Timeout/NewView signer+peer-key configuration." The **actual deployed configuration remains unobserved**; this note only restores the source-level distinction and does **not** reopen the §3/§6L configuration analysis.

**Table 2 — Immediate termination propagation (consensus-task death; inbound path).**

| Property | On consensus-task death | Established from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Process remains alive | **YES** — owner is parked on `ctrl_c().await`; task end does not exit `main` | main.rs:8726 / 5593 |
| Listener remains bound | **YES** — accept loop stops only on the service's own `broadcast shutdown_tx` or the listener's final drop; consensus death fires neither | p2p_tcp.rs:432 / 966 / 983 |
| Connection acceptance continues | **YES** — accept loop (`listener.accept()` arm) is unaffected | p2p_tcp.rs:978 / 986 |
| Consensus-message forwarding | **attempted and FAILS+LOGS per frame** — demuxer (`demuxer_handle`, node_context) keeps draining and invoking the handler; `try_send`→`Closed`→`eprintln`→return | p2p_inbound.rs:360 / 386 / 506–554 |
| Consensus processing | **STOPPED** (task gone) | — |
| Reaches any P2P shutdown mechanism? | **NO** — transport uses its own `broadcast`, never the consensus `watch`; `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown` aborts **only** `demuxer_handle` (p2p_node_builder.rs:2255); `TcpKemTlsP2pService::shutdown` (p2p_tcp.rs:1670) has **no node-path caller**; no `Drop` impl | p2p_node_builder.rs:2247–2263; p2p_tcp.rs:1670 |

**Process / exit-phase conclusion (completed trace; A15.3-scoped).** The supported conclusion is: **No shutdown propagation is identified through the inspected ownership and cleanup paths.** Explicit assumptions: field-level cleanup *does* occur (facade wrappers destroyed, the inbound channel's receive-half closed, `Arc` refcounts decremented — Table 1), but **none of the inspected field-drops signals another task, closes a channel the P2P service depends on, or triggers a custom `Drop`**; the service's accept loop / read loops stop only on the service's own `broadcast shutdown_tx` or socket EOF (Table 2). This is a **project-source** conclusion, separate from (i) documented Rust/tokio recursive-drop + unwind/task-boundary + `JoinError`/default-hook semantics (external evidence, tokio **1.49.0**, not re-verified against the pinned build) and (ii) **unobserved** deployed `panic`/overflow flags and external recovery (E21). **Exit phases differ and are NOT uniform (A15.3):**
- **P1 — task-startup refusal / early return** (Run 096 FATAL at 2580; initialization-only, *not* a mid-operation exit): the task returns `Ok(default)` **before** the owner reaches its await; the owner is parked on `ctrl_c().await` and does **not** observe it → premature, **unmonitored** exit; process continues.
- **P2 — orderly shutdown** (operator Ctrl+C): the **source-defined shutdown sequence** — the owner **initiates cancellation** (`drop(shutdown_tx)`, main.rs:8729), **awaits** the handle (`let _ = consensus_handle.await`, 8730; *discards the result* but is **not** unmonitored here), then awaits the run035/snapshot handles and calls `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown(node_context)` (8738); `main` then returns → **process exit follows IF those awaited operations complete**. This slice does **not** establish that each await is bounded (the `consensus_handle.await` and the handle-awaits have no timeout; `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown` times out only the demuxer, §22.8), so P2 is the ordered *sequence*, not a proven termination — **shutdown-completion is a separate question** from A15-F1's premature-exit gap, and is not asserted here. Not restarting after an intended shutdown is correct behaviour, **not** evidence of the supervision gap.
- **P3 — unexpected termination during operation** (unwind panic, e.g. §21.4 #3): occurs while the owner is parked on `ctrl_c().await` → premature, **unmonitored** exit; on the default-unwind path the process continues (consensus stopped, transport live).

So the earlier blanket "in every phase the exit is not detected … the process continues" is **withdrawn**: it holds for **P1/P3** (premature/unexpected exits that the owner, waiting on Ctrl+C, does not observe) but **not** for **P2**, where the owner awaits completion and the process then exits. The **supervision gap (A15-F1) is scoped to P1/P3**.

**Incidental observation (NOT a new finding; out of A15.2 scope).** On the node path `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown` aborts only the demuxer and relies on the service's `broadcast` closing "when it's dropped" (comment p2p_node_builder.rs:2261); the service's own `shutdown()` (which would drain `peers` and await the accept/read/write handles) is never invoked, so the per-connection read/write loops are not actively drained on the node path. This is a transport **shutdown-completeness** observation adjacent to A6-F1 (§6F) and is **recorded, not expanded** here (no persistence/recovery audit).

**Remaining gaps (classified).** **Source:** ~~one narrow caveat — the outbound-dial read-loop call site into `spawn_peer_handlers` (p2p_tcp.rs:1360) was not re-traced line-by-line (same mechanism as the inbound path).~~ **RESOLVED (A26 §31):** the outbound call site was corrected (production `dial_once`:2038; the cited :1360/:1345 belongs to the dead `dial_peer`) and re-traced — identical `spawn_peer_handlers`/`read_loop`/`inbound_tx`→demuxer; supported negative, A15-F1 unchanged (no source caveat remains here). **Dependency-evidence:** tokio **1.49.0** `JoinHandle`/`mpsc`/`broadcast`/`watch` + std default-hook semantics treated as external documented evidence, not re-verified against the pinned build. **Deployment/runtime (E21):** effective `panic`/overflow flags; external recovery (exit-triggered restart does not cover the alive-but-consensus-stopped case); observed runtime behavior.

### 22.9 A15.3 — destruction-semantics correction and lifecycle scoping (v0.36)

One bounded reconciliation of §22.8 and affected summaries at `ef99e29`; external register only. **No new finding, no count change; A15-F1 retained (owner-supervision gap, scoped to P1/P3).**

1. **Cleanup proof repaired.** Withdrew "no `Drop` impl → no cleanup side effect" and "dropping an `Arc` clone cannot destroy its contents" — both wrong in general (Rust recursively drops fields with or without a custom `Drop`; an `Arc`-clone drop destroys the inner value iff it is the last strong owner). Corrected Table 1: the `io.outbound` (`Arc<P2pConsensusNetwork>`, built main.rs:8495) and `io.peer_connectivity` (`Arc<P2pServicePeerConnectivity>`, main.rs:8655–8661) **facade wrappers are both moved into the task and destroyed at task end** (the task is their last owner), their field-drops dropping inner `Arc<TcpKemTlsP2pService>` clones; the inbound channel receive-half closes. The **inner `TcpKemTlsP2pService` survives via the concrete surviving owner `node_context.p2p_service`** (p2p_node_builder.rs:147 — the same allocation the facades cloned) — **not** because a custom `Drop` is absent. The owned `engine` (2492) is destroyed with recursive field-drop (consensus `state`/`timeout_accumulator`/`leaders` memory + four recorder `Arc` refcount−1) and was inspected to hold **no `Sender`/`Receiver`/`JoinHandle`/service/facade field** (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:1082–1173). Facade-wrapper destruction ≠ inner-service destruction. The inbound conclusion (service survives, transport continues) is **preserved on this corrected basis**; no new defect inferred from the earlier proof being incomplete.

2. **Configuration distinctions restored.** `io.verification_ctx` is `Some`/`None` per the **TimeoutVerificationContext** activation (local Timeout/NewView signer + peer keys, via `run_p2p_consensus_security_preflight`), kept **separate** from **Proposal/Vote authority** (`proposal_vote_authority`, production `None`) and the **current-authorization snapshot** (`current_auth`, production `None`); the flat "`verification_ctx=None` in production" is corrected; actual deployed config unobserved (no unrelated config work reopened).

3. **Premature exit vs orderly shutdown separated.** **P1** (startup refusal, Run 096 FATAL 2580 — initialization-only) and **P3** (unexpected unwind panic mid-operation) occur while the owner is parked on `ctrl_c().await` → unmonitored; process continues (default-unwind). **P2** (orderly shutdown) is different: the owner initiates cancellation (`drop(shutdown_tx)` 8729) and **awaits** the handle (8730, discarding only the result), then awaits the run035/snapshot handles and calls `P2pNodeBuilder::shutdown(node_context)` (8738) — the **source-defined shutdown sequence**; `main` then returns → **process exit follows if those awaited operations complete** (bounded completion of the awaits is **not** established in this slice; the shutdown-completion question is separate from the supervision gap). The blanket "in every phase the exit is not detected … the process continues" is **withdrawn**; A15-F1's supervision gap is **scoped to P1/P3**, and not restarting after an intended P2 shutdown is **not** the gap.

4. **Scoped conclusion.** Replaced "zero source-defined shutdown propagation / no `Drop` runs with a cleanup side effect" with: **"No shutdown propagation is identified through the inspected ownership and cleanup paths."** Assumptions: field-level cleanup occurs (facade wrappers destroyed, receive-half closed, `Arc` refcounts decremented), but none of the inspected drops signals another task, closes a service-depended-on channel, or triggers a custom `Drop`; accept/read loops stop only on the service's own `broadcast shutdown_tx` or socket EOF. **Remaining edges:** ~~the outbound-dial read-loop call site (same mechanism, not re-traced line-by-line);~~ **[outbound-dial read-loop RESOLVED in A26 §31 — re-traced, supported negative]**; tokio **1.49.0** recursive-drop/`JoinError`/channel semantics as external evidence, not re-verified against the pinned build; deployment/runtime (E21). Reconciled §22.2's stale "listener NOT traced" row with the established result. *(A26 §31 precision refinement: the per-connection **read** loop is **not** subscribed to the `broadcast shutdown_tx` — only the **accept** loop is; the read loop stops on socket recv-`Err`/decode-error/`inbound_tx`-receiver-closed and is reaped at teardown by `PeerConnection::shutdown`. This refines the "accept/read loops stop only on `broadcast shutdown_tx` or socket EOF" wording without changing the conclusion.)*

## 23. A16 — Production startup restoration (read-only source slice; v0.37)

**Scope.** One bounded, read-only slice: the **production** startup path that loads persisted state at boot and installs a consensus baseline into the engine, for the public-DevNet binary. Baseline `ef99e29`; citations are baseline line numbers; a corroborating subagent re-traced the `snapshot_restore`/storage/engine-install chain and the **load-bearing facts were re-verified firsthand** (engine install, caller inventory, failure branch, install-before-loop ordering, trust-assumption comment). Not a full crash-recovery audit.

**Headline (reframes the question).** The production restore path does **NOT** load a persisted *consensus* record (no QC, no `locked_qc`, no view, no validator set, no committed-block log) from storage into HotStuff. It (1) materializes **VM-v0 account state** from an on-disk snapshot directory into `<data_dir>/state_vm_v0`; (2) the restore **consumes** one consensus-storage key, `meta:current_epoch` (read for an epoch-conflict guard, written for parity) — **A16.1: the backend open additionally reads two more meta keys** (`meta:schema_version`, `meta:epoch_transition_marker`), so "only one consensus-storage record read" is **withdrawn**; and the open is **not** a pure read (it `create_dir_all`s the parent and opens RocksDB with `create_if_missing(true)`, creating the DB directory/files) — "non-mutating open" is **narrowed** to "performs no consensus-record *keyspace* writes"; (3) seeds the engine from a **2-field `RestoreBaseline { snapshot_height, snapshot_block_id }`** (built from the snapshot `meta.json`). The snapshot is **trusted local storage**: checks are decode + chain-label (chain_id) + authority-state anti-rollback + epoch-compatibility — **no cryptographic authentication / signature verification** of the snapshot record, its `block_hash`, or its height (documented "operator-honest" assumption). Restore errors **that are detected** fail closed via `std::process::exit(1)`; this is **not** a claim that every semantically-invalid snapshot is detected (a forged-but-consistent snapshot under local write access is the E22 boundary).

### 23.1 Wiring (production entry → install → consensus-enable)

Entry `async fn main()` (main.rs:2008) → network-mode dispatch (5421) → `run_local_mesh_node` (5485) / `run_p2p_node` (6176). Restore is gated on `--restore-from-snapshot` (absent ⇒ `Ok(None)` ⇒ normal genesis start, main.rs:2838). Chain:
- **Storage backend:** RocksDB — `open_production_consensus_storage(&config)` (main.rs:2605 pre-restore epoch probe; 5157 normal open) → `RocksDbConsensusStorage::open` (production_consensus_storage.rs:416; storage.rs:719). **A16.1 — open/recovery is not a pure read and touches three meta keys:** it `std::fs::create_dir_all`s the parent (prod_cons_storage.rs:405) and opens RocksDB `create_if_missing(true)` (storage.rs:755) — filesystem writes creating the DB dir/files — then **reads** `meta:schema_version` (`ensure_compatible_schema`, storage.rs:372/1886), `meta:epoch_transition_marker` (`verify_epoch_consistency_on_startup`, :381/1230 — **read-only detect-and-refuse: returns `Err` on a present marker, does NOT clear/reconcile** — the clearer is `#[cfg(test/test-utils)]`), and `meta:current_epoch` (:365, BE u64 + checksum; the key the restore actually **consumes**, read twice). **No** consensus-record *keyspace* `put`/`delete` occurs at open; **no** block (`b:`) / QC (`q:`) record and **not** `meta:last_committed` (:358) are read. So the earlier "only one consensus-storage record read" is **withdrawn** (three meta records) and "non-mutating" is **narrowed** to "no consensus-record keyspace writes" (the filesystem is written).
- **Restore fn / record type:** `apply_guarded_snapshot_restore(&config, authority_ctx, epoch_precheck, &hooks)` (main.rs:2829; snapshot_restore.rs) decodes `StateSnapshotMeta` from `<snap>/meta.json` (fields: `height:u64`, `block_hash:[u8;32]`, `created_at_unix_ms`, `chain_id:u64`, `epoch:Option<u64>`; state_snapshot.rs:91–137) + optional embedded `authority_state`/`_v2` blocks.
- **Baseline + install:** `RestoreBaseline { snapshot_height, snapshot_block_id }` (main.rs:2866; struct binary_consensus_loop.rs:529–537) → `with_restore_baseline` (5507 LocalMesh / 8504 P2P) → installed at **binary_consensus_loop.rs:2517** via `engine.initialize_from_snapshot_baseline(block_id, snapshot_height)` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:1995 → hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1254).
- **Consensus-enable point:** the tick/ingest `loop { tokio::select! … }` begins at **binary_consensus_loop.rs:2790**, strictly **after** the baseline install (2517); all `main`-side checks + VM-state materialization + epoch-persist + restore-transaction COMPLETE happen earlier still.
