| **Engine install** (binary_consensus_loop.rs:2517 → basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:1995 → hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1254) | `RestoreBaseline` | **none at install** (no QC, no validator check, no crypto) | `committed_block/height=Some`; anchor `BlockNode(parent=None, justify_qc=None, own_qc=None)`; `current_view = snapshot_height.saturating_add(1)`; flags reset; `locked_qc` stays None **at install** (A16.1 — `own_qc`/`locked_qc` are library-mutable over the anchor via `on_qc` 1004/1009, but **A16.2: not reached on the wired production inbound-Vote path**, which rejects fail-closed before `on_vote_event`; the no-re-commit guard is the strict height floor `g_height > committed_height` 1114–1121 + committed-height monotonicity + eviction floor — **A16.3: conditional** on the anchor entry retaining `height = snapshot_height` (entry-preservation premise OPEN, E22), **not** own_qc immutability, §23.6) | **no error return (`-> ()`)**: a sequence of in-memory field assignments + one map insert, with **no fallible operation on the inspected path** — an **in-memory** completion statement, **not** an atomicity / crash-consistency / failure-free guarantee (A16.3). Supported ordering: consensus processing begins only **after** this initializer returns normally (loop :2790 after install :2517); detected pre-install refusals exit first |

All missing/malformed/inconsistent/unsupported/epoch-incompatible records **that are detected** **refuse startup via `std::process::exit(1)`** before or during materialization — on a detected error there is **no genesis-fallback and no uninitialized-and-running engine**. Top-level branch: `Err(e) => { eprintln!("[restore] ERROR: …"); … std::process::exit(1); }` (main.rs:2847–2857). **A16.2/A16.3 scoping:** "never partial install" is **not blanket** — what the inspected ordering supports at the **engine level** is that consensus processing begins only **after** `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` returns normally and that detected pre-install refusals exit first (install reached only after COMPLETE); the initializer's `-> ()` means only "no application error," **not** failure-free execution / atomicity / rollback, so the earlier "single infallible in-memory op … no half-installed engine" structural guarantee is **superseded** (proof-scope only — **no** new implementation defect asserted, §23.6). It is **not** a complete crash-consistency claim for the **storage/filesystem** layer (mid-sequence IO/publish failures can leave INTENT RTR + partial/full `state_vm_v0` residues, §23.6), which are handled fail-closed on the **next startup** only through the **recorded `RtrState::Intent → RefuseIntent` / `RefuseOccupied` / non-empty-`state_vm_v0` occupancy** branches (restore_completion.rs:988–1021; snapshot_restore.rs:815) — **not** a general journal/replay crash-recovery guarantee (that remains the separate Run 422 thread, unaudited).

### 23.4 Representation and trust boundary

Persisted fields (snapshot `StateSnapshotMeta`): height, block_hash (opaque anchor), chain_id, `epoch:Option<u64>` (additive versioning — `None` for pre-Run-097 snapshots), created-at. **Distinct obligations, separated (A16.1 — do not lump as one "anti-rollback"):**
- **chain_id match** (`meta.chain_id == config.chain_id`, state_snapshot.rs:1214) — a **label-consistency** check (are these the same chain's artifacts?), **not** authenticity of the snapshot.
- **authority-marker rollback protection** (snapshot_restore.rs:741 → pqc_authority_state.rs:2631) — protects **only the marker's protected fields** (the authority-state digest/fingerprint/sequence): rejects downgrade/rollback/wrong-domain **of the authority state**. It does **not** authenticate the snapshot height, `block_hash`, or VM-state payload.
- **epoch compatibility** (`meta.epoch` vs live `get_current_epoch()`) — an **integrity matrix**; preserves the `epoch=None` (pre-Run-097) case as compatible.
- **snapshot-height rollback** — a **separate obligation that is NOT checked here**: `height>0` is the only height check; there is **no** verification that `snapshot_height` is not older than a previously-committed height (the consensus-storage `meta:last_committed` key is not consulted by restore; the empty-`state_vm_v0` occupancy guard prevents overwriting a populated local state dir but is **not** a height-rollback check).
- **state-to-block binding** (`block_hash` ↔ the materialized VM state) — **not verified**: `block_hash` is used only as an opaque parent id and is never recomputed/checked against the state.
- **restored voting / locking history** — **not an obligation this path discharges at all**: the engine installs **no QC, no lock, no vote history** (see §23.6/§23.7).
- **cryptographic authentication / signature** of the snapshot — **absent**.

Documented trust assumption (snapshot_restore.rs module header): "operator-honest: refuse rather than corrupt local state." So this is **trusted local storage, consistency- and chain-label-checked, with authority-state rollback protection, but neither authenticated nor height-rollback/state-binding-checked** — recorded as the restore's trust boundary (which checks are *enforced* vs *assumed* vs *outside this slice* is made explicit above), **not** framed as a defect (the register does **not** assert that every persisted record must be independently signed).

### 23.5 Preconditions before state installation

Chain identity (`meta.chain_id == config.chain_id`, state_snapshot.rs:1214) and epoch compatibility (`meta.epoch` vs fresh live `get_current_epoch()`, prod_cons_storage.rs:562–574) are enforced **before** materialization and thus before the baseline is built. **No** validator-membership / QC / lock / committed-vs-snapshot-height relationship is checked at the engine install — the snapshot carries none of those; `height>0` (state_snapshot.rs:1222) is the **only** height check and there is **no upper bound and no anti-rollback** on `snapshot_height`. The restored view is `current_view = snapshot_height.saturating_add(1)` — the `+1` itself is saturating (no overflow). **View-bound → E02 (A16.1):** because `h.saturating_add(1) ≥ M−9` for `h ≥ M−10` (M = `u64::MAX`), a crafted snapshot with `snapshot_height ≥ M−10` lands `current_view` in the `[M−9, M]` band where `on_timeout_msg`'s ordinary `current_view + 10` scan overflows (A14.1/A14.2/§21.4 #3) **if that timeout path later executes**. This is a **distinct, local restore entry** into that band — reached via a crafted `snapshot_height` under the **E22 local-write prerequisite** — separate from **A1-F2's admitted-TC entry** (`current_view = tc.view` over the network); the terminal view `v=M` differs from lower values exactly as in §21.4 #3 (no strictly-greater view exists at `M`). Cross-referenced to **E02**; **no new finding** (the arithmetic consequence, admission, and scheduling preconditions are as already recorded under E02). **Constructor vs caller:** `evaluate_restore_epoch_compatibility` is a non-writing decision fn that reads the **live** epoch itself; the **caller** (main.rs:2691 closure / `persist_restored_snapshot_epoch_durable`) decides to refuse or write. `OpenedProductionConsensusStorage` guarantees only an opened+schema-checked handle and a startup-observation `state` (explicitly stale-able; the compatibility decision reads live, not the cached observation).

### 23.6 Validation / mutation ordering and failure semantics

Order (all before any consensus message processing): storage-open (filesystem-creating; see §23.1) → RTR precondition → snapshot decode+structural → authority anti-rollback → epoch precheck → occupancy → **INTENT published** (snapshot_restore.rs:504, *before* any copy) → **materialize VM state** (copy `state/` → `state_vm_v0` + audit marker) → build `RestoreBaseline` → epoch-persist → COMPLETE → (dispatch to loop) → **engine baseline install (binary_consensus_loop.rs:2517)** → **loop select begins (2790)**. Rejection at a **detected** error is an explicit **startup refusal (`exit(1)`)** (not inferred from a bare `Err`).

**"Never partial install" — narrowed by storage layer (A16.1) and proof-scoped (A16.3):**
- **Engine level — what the inspected ordering supports:** every **detected** pre-COMPLETE failure branch `std::process::exit(1)`s **before** the consensus loop constructs/installs the engine (install site binary_consensus_loop.rs:2516–2520 runs only after `main` passes COMPLETE). In the inspected startup control flow, **consensus processing begins only after the initializer (`initialize_from_snapshot_baseline`) returns normally; detected pre-install refusals exit before that point** (loop select :2790 is strictly after install :2517). **A16.3 — do not over-read this:** the initializer's `-> ()` signature means only that it returns **no application error**; that is **not** a guarantee of failure-free execution, atomicity, or rollback. It performs a sequence of in-memory field assignments + one `HashMap` insert with no fallible operation **on the inspected path**, but the register does **not** assert the step is panic-proof or transactional. The supported conclusion is the **ordering** one above (processing follows a normal return; detected refusals exit first), **not** "no half-installed engine" as an independent structural guarantee — the former phrasing ("single infallible in-memory op … no partial/half-installed engine") is **superseded**. This is a **proof-scope** correction only; it does **not** assert or imply a new implementation defect.
- **Storage/filesystem level — residues ARE possible:** INTENT is written **before** the copy (snapshot_restore.rs:504), so a mid-copy IO failure leaves the **INTENT RTR + a partial `state_vm_v0`** (no audit marker, no COMPLETE); an epoch-persist failure (main.rs:5234) leaves **INTENT + full `state_vm_v0` + marker + possibly the persisted `meta:current_epoch`**, no COMPLETE; a COMPLETE-publish failure leaves the RTR in an observed-but-unacked state. **Next-startup handling is fail-closed:** ordinary startup maps `RtrState::Intent → RefuseIntent` → FATAL `exit(1)` (restore_completion.rs:988–1021, main.rs:5042+); a requested restore's pre-INTENT precondition refuses any existing INTENT/COMPLETE (`RefuseOccupied`); and the occupancy guard refuses a non-empty `state_vm_v0` (snapshot_restore.rs:815) — residues are **detected and refused**, not auto-reconciled.

**Anchor commit-safety — mechanism corrected (A16.1), admission-scoped (A16.2), ordering-grounded (A16.3/A17-A).** The engine install **performs no validation and returns no application error (`-> ()`)** — which is **not** a failure-free/atomic/rollback guarantee (A16.3); what the inspected ordering supports is that consensus processing begins only after the initializer returns normally and detected pre-install refusals exit first. It installs a height anchor with `own_qc=None` **immediately after installation** and `parent_id=None`/`justify_qc=None`, with `locked_qc` staying None. **Withdrawn:** the claim that "`own_qc=None` ⇒ the anchor can **never** be the G of a 3-chain" — `own_qc` is **not immutable** at the library level: `on_qc` writes `node.own_qc = Some(..)` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1009) and may replace `locked_qc` (:1004, when `qc.view` exceeds the current lock) for the QC's `block_id`.

**A16.2 — "production-reachable from `on_vote_event → on_vote → on_qc`" QUALIFIED/WITHDRAWN as stated.** The epoch-only gate at the engine entry (`on_vote_event`, basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2960–2973: rejects only `vote.epoch != current_epoch`, no height/view guard) is a **library fact**, **not** a complete production-admission predicate. On the **wired production inbound-Vote path** the engine entry is **not reached**: the binary selects `ConsensusVerificationPolicy::Required` with `proposal_vote_authority=None` and `current_auth=None` (§6L.1), so `effective_pv` resolves to `None` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:6407–6410: `current_auth None → pv_authority`, itself `None`), and the `None =>` arm under `requires_context()` **rejects the vote fail-closed** (`inbound_vote_verification_context_unavailable_total`, `eprintln!("… REJECTED (verification context unavailable) … policy=Required — fail-closed, not delivered")`, `return;` at ~6544–6563) **before** the sole production call site `engine.on_vote_event(from, &vote)` at binary_consensus_loop.rs:6584. So a **production inbound vote never reaches `on_qc`** to set the anchor's `own_qc`/`locked_qc`. **Scoped, nonempty caller inventory** of the mutator (search scope: 316 `crates/*/src` `.rs` files at `ef99e29`, positive-controlled): `on_qc` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:995) ← `HotStuffStateEngine::on_vote` (:983) ← engine callers of `self.state.on_vote`: **(a)** `on_vote_event`:2983 (inbound; production rejects **before** this per above — reachable only under the test-only `LocalFixtureUnsigned` passthrough or a wired verification context, neither in the production binary); **(b)** `on_leader_step`:2332 and `ingest_proposal`:2911 — the node's **own local self-vote** (`self.local_id`), on the proposal/leader path (whose production inbound reachability is itself gated — inbound Proposal rejects fail-closed under `Required`, §6L.1); **(c)** `apply_restore_catchup_blocks`:2194 — the **live P2P catch-up** replay (E20/E22, runtime, unaudited). **No complete admissible production path to set the anchor's `own_qc` was established in this review;** the remaining library/sim/direct-call sites (`hotstuff_node_sim.rs:2834/2997`; the restart API `binary_consensus_loop.rs:9550`; `driver.rs`) are test/simulation/direct-library, not the wired production inbound path.

**Non-recommit invariant — scoped to the inspected commit predicate and its preconditions (A16.2).** Independently of `own_qc`, the "anchor is never re-committed" conclusion rests on the following, each verified **within the inspected transitions** (not a full HotStuff safety proof): (a) **at install** `committed_height = snapshot_height` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1262) **and** the anchor `BlockNode` is created with `height = committed_height` (the same value, :1259–1266) — so `anchor.height == committed_height` immediately after install; (b) **committed-height monotonicity on the inspected path** — the only writer that advances it is the commit step `self.committed_height = Some(g_height)` (:1121), reached **only** when `height_ok` holds, i.e. `committed_height is None` or `g_height > h` (strict `>`, :1114–1119); the two other writers are install (:1262) and the restart constructor `initialize_from_restart` (:1198, sim/restart path), so on this path `committed_height` is **non-decreasing** and stays `≥ snapshot_height`; (c) **anchor-entry preservation — PARTIALLY established, one premise OPEN (A16.3).** Removal via eviction is ruled out: the anchor is **never evictable** while `anchor.height (= snapshot_height) ≤ committed_height` (eviction floor `block.height ≤ committed_height → not safe to evict`, :598–603), and no inspected transition contains a **direct field assignment** to an existing node's `height`. **But absence of a direct field write does not address replacement under the same map key.** The single block-map writer is `insert_block_node` (:568), which unconditionally `self.blocks.insert(id, node)` (:576) — it reconciles retained-evidence byte accounting but carries **no guard preserving an existing entry**; its callers `register_block` (:729, documented "adds or **updates** … replaces any prior node for this id") and `register_block_with_verified_justification` (:810) **recompute `height` from the parent** at insert (`parent_id=None ⇒ height 0`; `Some(pid) ⇒ parent.height+1`). So a replacement of the anchor's entry under its own `block_id` key, with a **different** height, is **not ruled out by any guard inside this slice** — the premise "the anchor entry retains `height = snapshot_height`" is therefore **OPEN** here (closing it would require establishing that no `register_block*`/insert path is ever invoked with `id == anchor.block_id` — a reachability question that expands the slice; note inbound Proposal, the production trigger for such registrations, is itself rejected under `Required`, §6L.1). **Conditional conclusion (replacing the earlier unconditional "never"):** *while the anchor entry retains its installed `height = snapshot_height` and `committed_height` remains non-decreasing (established in (b)), the strict height predicate `g_height > committed_height` prevents committing that entry again* — because `anchor.g_height = snapshot_height ≤ committed_height`, independent of whether `own_qc` later becomes `Some`. The anchor's `parent_id=None` is an **additional** structural barrier to the anchor being the `B` of a 3-chain (try_commit returns at the parent step). The unresolved **entry-preservation premise** is recorded at the E22 boundary. **These are the only conclusions this slice supports; the result is stated conditionally, not as an unconditional "never."** **Kept separate (not merged into one claim):** (i) **non-recommit** (**conditionally** established as above — holds while the anchor entry retains its installed height and `committed_height` stays non-decreasing; the entry-preservation premise is OPEN, E22); (ii) **later QC attachment** to the anchor's `block_id` (library-possible via `on_qc`, but no complete production admission established — above); (iii) **lock updates** — if `on_qc` ever ran over the anchor it could also update `locked_qc` (:1004); the earlier "**benign** `locked_qc`" characterization is **WITHDRAWN** (no invariant establishing that such a lock is harmless was verified in this slice); (iv) **broader restart/catch-up consistency** — out of this slice (E20/E22). So **"no QC installed at boot" does not by itself establish the commit-safety / lock properties**, and the non-recommit conclusion is scoped to the inspected commit predicate and its explicit preconditions.

### 23.7 Applicability, cross-references, and disposition

**Public-DevNet applicability:** startup restoration is wired and reachable when `--restore-from-snapshot` is supplied; otherwise the node starts at genesis. **Cross-references (no double-count):**
- **A1-F3 / E03** (unverified high-QC → lock): the startup restore **does not** extend this surface — it installs **no QC** and leaves `locked_qc = None` (anchor `justify_qc=None`/`own_qc=None`). The unverified-QC-adoption concern lives on the **TC path** (`on_timeout_certificate`, A1-F3) and, separately, the **live catch-up** path (`apply_restore_catchup_blocks` → `qc.validate` at basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2183) — **not** this slice.
- **E20** (QC-validation / recovery input-trust): the **live catch-up** `qc.validate` and its proposer/height/parent checks remain **queued, not audited** (E20); startup restoration is distinct and is **not** folded into E20.
- **E02** (pacemaker/restart view arithmetic): the restored `current_view = snapshot_height.saturating_add(1)` gives a **distinct, local entry** into the `[M−9, M]` high-view band (via a crafted `snapshot_height ≥ M−10` under the E22 local-write prerequisite), separate from A1-F2's network TC-target entry; the `+1` is saturating (no overflow itself), the overflow is the downstream `on_timeout_msg` `+10` scan if that path executes (§21.4 #3 / A14.1/A14.2). Cross-referenced to **E02**; same containment/terminal-view distinctions apply; **no new finding** and no double-count with A1-F2.

**Disposition — scoped negative for the startup-restoration slice; no new finding (A16.1-reconciled).** The scoped negative is retained, now reasoned on the **actual established controls** + **explicit trust assumptions** (not the mechanism the v0.37 comment named): (i) **fail-closed on the detected error classes** — decode / chain-id mismatch / height==0 / authority-state rollback / epoch-incompat / IO / RTR-occupancy each `exit(1)` (this is *not* a claim that every semantically-invalid snapshot is detected — a forged-but-consistent snapshot is the E22 boundary); (ii) **no QC/lock installed at boot** (`locked_qc` starts None; anchor `justify_qc=None`); (iii) the anchor **cannot be re-committed as long as its block-map entry retains its installed `height = snapshot_height` and `committed_height` remains non-decreasing** — a **conditional** invariant (A16.3), scoped to the inspected commit predicate and its preconditions: given those two premises, the strict height floor `g_height > committed_height` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1114–1121) can never hold for the anchor-as-`G` (because `anchor.g_height = snapshot_height ≤ committed_height`), with anchor `parent=None` an additional structural barrier to being `B`. **`committed_height` non-decrease IS established** within the slice (sole advancing writer :1121 is strict-`>`-guarded; other writers are install :1262 and the restart constructor :1198, held outside the invariant's lifetime). **Anchor-entry preservation is NOT established** within this slice (A16.3): `insert_block_node` (:568) unconditionally `self.blocks.insert(id, node)` (:576) — it reconciles evidence-byte accounting but carries **no entry-preservation guard**, and its callers `register_block` (:729, documented "adds or **updates** … replaces any prior node for this id") and `register_block_with_verified_justification` (:810) **recompute `height` from the parent** (`parent_id=None ⇒ height 0`), so a replacement under the anchor's map key with a different height is **not ruled out by any guard in this slice** (its production reachability over the anchor's id is a separate, ungated-here question — inbound Proposal is itself rejected under `Required`, §6L.1 — and resolving it would expand the slice). This unresolved **entry-preservation premise** is recorded at the E22 boundary. The conclusion is **not** retained as an unconditional "never." The invariant is **not** grounded in `own_qc` immutability (`own_qc` is library-mutable via `on_qc`, but **A16.2: not reached on the wired production inbound-Vote path**, which rejects fail-closed before `on_vote_event`; no complete admissible production path to set the anchor's `own_qc` was established — §23.6); the earlier "benign `locked_qc`" is **withdrawn** (its harmlessness invariant was not verified); (iv) **A16.3 (ordering, not structure):** in the inspected startup control flow consensus processing begins only **after** the initializer returns normally, and detected pre-install refusals exit before that point — the `-> ()` return means "no application error," **not** failure-free execution / atomicity / rollback, so the earlier "single/infallible/in-memory ⇒ no partial engine install" structural guarantee is **superseded** (proof-scope only; no new defect asserted); storage residues are handled fail-closed on next boot (§23.6); (v) consensus processing begins only post-install (loop :2790 after install :2517). **Explicit trust assumptions / unenforced obligations (E22):** the snapshot is **trusted local storage** — chain_id is a label check, authority-marker protects only the authority-state fields, and **snapshot-height anti-rollback, state-to-block binding, and snapshot authenticity are assumed, not enforced**; an actor with **local write access** could supply a crafted-but-consistent snapshot (arbitrary height — hence an E02 high-view entry, §23.5 — block_id, VM state) — a **local-capability** boundary (cf. A10-F1), reachable **only** under local filesystem write, **not** anonymously network-reachable, matching the documented operator-honest model. Recorded as **evidence gap E22**, **not** a finding (no per-record signing requirement invented). **Totals unchanged** (11 static-supported; 4 assurance/hardening/observability gaps; **22 evidence gaps E01–E22**); no disposition recompute warranted.

## 24. A17 — Production live catch-up: response admission, validation ordering, state invariants (read-only source slice; v0.41)

Bounded read-only slice at baseline `ef99e29`. Traces the production path for `ConsensusNetMsg::RestoreCatchupResponse` from inbound dispatch through `handle_restore_catchup_response` into `BasicHotStuffEngine::apply_restore_catchup_blocks` and its immediate engine-state effects. Search scope: 316 `crates/*/src` `.rs` files (positive-controlled). All load-bearing facts verified firsthand and independently corroborated by a second read-only trace.

**Result headline — NEW static-supported finding A17-F1 (live catch-up advances committed state without verifying quorum endorsement).** **Central obligation (A17.1):** before advancing committed consensus state, a HotStuff node must verify that a quorum of validators actually **endorsed** the block. The live catch-up path does **not**: `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` reconstructs each block's "quorum certificate" from the response's `qc_signer_indices` list and checks it only with `QuorumCertificate::validate` (qc.rs:83–115), which performs **membership + dedup + 2/3 voting-power arithmetic ONLY — no cryptographic signature verification** (its own doc comment: "performs logical validation only (no cryptographic checks)"). **The inspected path neither receives nor verifies evidence establishing that the listed validators endorsed the block** — the wire block `RestoreCatchupBlock` (p2p.rs:200–209) carries **only `qc_signer_indices: Vec<u16>`, no signatures and no tx/state payload**, so an endorsement check is impossible by construction. Transport protection (KEMTLS) and responder binding (the `PeerConsensusBindingGate` binds the responder to **its own** validator identity) are **separate properties** that do **not** authenticate the `qc_signer_indices`. The path is **not** gated by the production `Required` Proposal/Vote rejection (§6L.1) — a distinct property — and has no `restore_mode.is_active()` gate; its gates are responder-binding + anchor-equality to the victim's committed tip + deterministic chain-structure.

**Consequence (scoped; A17.1).** Under the standard BFT fault budget (`N = 3f+1`, up to `f` Byzantine tolerated, quorum `2f+1 = ⌈2N/3⌉`), a **single** responder can list ≥`⌈2N/3⌉` validator indices as `qc_signers` **without any of them having endorsed** — so committed state is **advanced upon without the precondition (verified quorum endorsement) ever being established** — a single party's unendorsed index list suffices, where a genuine verified quorum is required. The engine then registers the blocks, replays the reconstructed votes, forms per-block QCs, updates `locked_qc`, and — **for an accepted suffix of length ≥ 3** satisfying the 3-chain commit predicate — advances `committed_height`/`committed_block` (first commit fires when the **3rd** block is processed; a length-1 or length-2 accepted suffix advances registration/lock only, **not** committed height; `current_view` advances only on normal loop completion, §24.4/§24.4b). This is the supported **missing-endorsement-verification** weakness. **Explicitly NOT established here:** a demonstrated disagreement between honest nodes, downstream execution/finality inconsistency, or a runtime exploit — the message carries no tx/state payload, so this is advancement of **consensus metadata** whose downstream effect is a **source-review / runtime gap** (E20). The "single-Byzantine-validator" framing is a BFT-threshold observation **about the missing control**, not a demonstrated safety break.

**Distinct mechanisms, kept separate (A17.1):** **A1-F1** = missing-context **Timeout/TC** verification (verification conditional on the verification context), **not** Proposal/Vote; the production **Proposal/Vote rejection under `Required` with absent authority** (§6L.1) is a separate property (the `Required` policy does **not** contain A1-F1); **A1-F3** = TC high-QC adoption as lock on `on_timeout_certificate`; **A17-F1** = catch-up response admission + reconstructed quorum evidence. A17-F1 shares the "logical `validate`, no crypto" theme with A1-F1/A1-F3 but is a different entrypoint/mechanism. **E20 — narrowed (A17.1):** A17 source-resolves only the specific question *"does the catch-up `qc.validate` perform cryptographic endorsement verification?"* (no), and characterizes the input-trust boundary; the **downstream control-flow** (what a forged committed tip does to proposal admission / finality / VM) remains a **source-review gap**, and DevNet config + end-to-end exploit remain **execution/deployment evidence gaps** — all still under E20.

### 24.1 Caller inventory (production vs test/sim; positive-controlled)

- **Inbound dispatch:** `handle_inbound_consensus_msg` arm `ConsensusNetMsg::RestoreCatchupResponse(resp)` at binary_consensus_loop.rs:7000 → `bind_sender(claimed)` (Run 418 transport-origin binding, :7004) → `handle_restore_catchup_response(engine, resp, stats, local_validator_id, restore_mode)` (:7018). The arm at :5851 is a **metric-classification** block (`inc_inbound_other()`), **not** an accept/reject gate; the text at :922 is the `binding_gate` field doc, describing transport-identity binding only.
- **Handler:** `handle_restore_catchup_response` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:7865–7975) → builds `blocks: Vec<EngineRestoreCatchupBlock>` from `resp.blocks` (:7914–7929) → `engine.apply_restore_catchup_blocks(&blocks)` (:7934).
- **Engine:** `BasicHotStuffEngine::apply_restore_catchup_blocks` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2122–2211) — the **sole production call site** is binary_consensus_loop.rs:7934. The other references are tests (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3699/3722) and the restart API / its tests (binary_consensus_loop.rs:9585 and the `#[cfg(test)]` constructions at 9484/9543/9681/9797/9134/…). `deliver_inbound_for_run035` (:7030+) is a `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` test harness wrapper.
- **Response production (traced only for admission preconditions):** `handle_restore_catchup_request` builds and broadcasts a `RestoreCatchupResponse` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:7841/7858) in reply to a request; the struct is p2p.rs:213–219. The node emits catch-up **requests** while in restore-catchup mode, but the **response handler does not require the victim to be in that mode** (no `restore_mode.is_active()` gate — below).

### 24.2 Admission preconditions (transport identity vs consensus authorization vs catch-up admission — kept distinct)

1. **Transport-origin binding (Run 418), production-wired.** `bind_sender` → `PeerConsensusBindingGate::authorize(origin, claimed)` (peer_consensus_binding.rs:388–439; production installs `Some`, main.rs:8698). Fail-closed rules: absent origin → `MissingOrigin`; authenticated 32-byte NodeId not in the one-to-one map → `UnknownPeer`; `mapped_validator != origin.validator_id()` → `AmbiguousMapping`; claimed index not a known validator → `UnknownValidator`; **`claimed_validator != origin.validator_id()` → `ClaimedSenderMismatch`**. So the responder can only claim **its own** validator index — a peer cannot impersonate another validator as responder. **This binds the responder's identity; it does NOT bind or authenticate the `qc_signer_indices` carried inside each block.**
2. **No consensus-authorization / policy gate.** Unlike inbound Proposal/Vote (which under production `Required` + `effective_pv=None` reject fail-closed before engine dispatch, §6L.1/A16.2), the catch-up response path has **no `verification_policy`/`effective_pv`/`requires_context()` gate**. The `Required` rejection does **not** cover catch-up messages.
3. **Catch-up admission = anchor-equality correlation (not pending-request-id, not range).** `handle_restore_catchup_response` applies blocks only if `engine.committed_height() == Some(resp.request_from_height)` AND `engine.committed_block() == Some(resp.request_from_block_id)` (:7892–7894); otherwise stale-reject (no mutation). There is **no pending-request table, no requested-range check, and no `restore_mode.is_active()` gate** — any node whose current committed tip equals the response's declared anchor processes it (committed height/block are observable to fellow validators). Self-responses are dropped (:7872); empty-block responses only drive transition evaluation (:7882).

### 24.3 Data carried and its checks (separated by class)

Per-block wire fields (`RestoreCatchupBlock`, p2p.rs:200): `height`, `view`, `parent_block_id`, `block_id`, `proposer_index`, `qc_signer_indices` — **no signatures, no tx/state payload**. Checks in `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2141–2195):
- **Structural / chaining:** `block.height == expected_height` (contiguous from `committed_height+1`); `block.parent_block_id == expected_parent` (chains to the prior block / committed tip); `block.height == block.view`; `block.proposer == leader_for_view(block.view)` (deterministic round-robin `view % n`, :1739–1744); `block.block_id == derive_block_id_from_header(proposer, view, parent)` (deterministic: proposer→id[0..8], view→id[8..16], parent[..16]→id[16..32], :2043–2058). **All deterministic and attacker-computable** — they force the forged chain to follow the canonical leader schedule but impose no secret.
- **Membership / dedup / quorum arithmetic:** `qc.validate(self.validators())` — membership (`contains`), dedup (`HashSet`), `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp()` (`(2·total).div_ceil(3)`, validator_set.rs). Validator set = **uniform unit-weight** `build_uniform_validator_set(cfg.num_validators)` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:711–719 → engine 2491), so quorum = ⌈2N/3⌉ distinct valid indices.
- **Cryptographic verification:** **NONE.** `qc.validate` performs no signature/key/suite check; the wire carries no signatures. (Do not infer endorsement from the name `validate`.)
- **Protocol-semantic:** the reconstructed votes drive the engine's own 3-chain commit logic (below). No independent check that the listed signers actually endorsed the block.

### 24.4 Ordered input → precondition → validation → mutation → emitted action → failure outcome

Validation/mutation is **incremental, block-by-block (not batch-atomic); each block is fully validated AND mutated before the next**; a mid-batch rejection returns `Err` with **no rollback** of earlier blocks.

| # | Input | Precondition | Validation (class) | Mutation | Emitted action | Failure outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | `RestoreCatchupResponse` frame | authenticated transport origin | **transport binding** — responder index == own validator id (peer_consensus_binding.rs:388) | none | none | `bind_sender` Err → reject + `return` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:7004) |
| D2 | `resp` | — | self-response / empty-blocks (structural) | none | transition eval only | self → `return` (:7872); empty → eval + `return` (:7882) |
| D3 | `resp` anchor | — | **anchor-equality** `committed_height==request_from_height` & `committed_block==request_from_block_id` (:7892) | none | transition eval (peer anchor only) | mismatch → stale-reject, **no mutation**, `return` (:7895) |
| P0 | pre-loop | — | `committed_height`/`committed_block` present (`ok_or(MissingLocalAnchor)`, :2130–2137); `previous_qc = locked_qc().cloned()` | none | — | `MissingLocalAnchor` → `Err` **before any registration** → engine unmutated |
| B1 | block[k].height | prior accepted tip | `height == expected_height` (structural) | none yet | — | `NonContiguousHeight` → `Err` **before block[k] registration** (blocks[1..k−1] prefix already mutated; for k=1 nothing mutated) |
| B2 | block[k].parent | — | `parent == expected_parent` (structural) | none yet | — | `AnchorMismatch` → `Err` (as B1) |
| B3 | block[k].view | — | `height == view` (structural) | none yet | — | `HeightViewMismatch` → `Err` (as B1) |
| B4 | block[k].proposer | validator set | `proposer == leader_for_view(view)` (structural/deterministic) | none yet | — | `WrongProposer` → `Err` (as B1) |
| B5 | block[k].block_id | — | `block_id == derive_block_id_from_header(...)` (structural/deterministic) | none yet | — | `BlockIdMismatch` → `Err` (as B1) |
| B6 | block[k].qc_signers | validator set | `qc.validate` — **membership + dedup + 2/3 VP ONLY; NO signatures / NO endorsement** (qc.rs:83) | none yet | — | `InvalidQc` → `Err` **before block[k] registration** (as B1) |
| B7 | block[k] | B1–B6 passed | — | `state.register_block(block_id, view, Some(parent), previous_qc)` (:2186) — registers/**overwrites** key `block_id` with the **prior** block's QC as justify (height recomputed from parent) | — | infallible (`-> ()`) — **always mutates once reached** |
| B8 | each signer in qc_signers | B7 done | — | `state.on_vote(signer, view, block_id)` (:2192) → accumulates; at quorum forms this block's own_qc via `on_qc` → sets `node.own_qc` + **`locked_qc` if `qc.view` > current lock** + `try_commit_with_qc` | — | **`on_vote` Err is NOT reachable for a validated signer** — the accumulator errors only on non-members (vote_accumulator.rs:309; vote-limit → `Ok(false)`, equivocation → `Ok(None)`), and B6 already enforced membership+dedup+quorum; `maybe_qc_for`/`on_qc` do not error for members → the `.map_err(InvalidQc)?` here is effectively dead for inputs that reached B8 |
| B8c | (within B8) | B=block[k], P=parent, G=grandparent all have `own_qc`; `G.view<P.view<B.view`; `g_height > committed_height`; `g_view > committed.view` | 3-chain commit predicate (:1090–1121) | **`committed_height`/`committed_block` ← G** (+ commit_log) **only when the predicate fires** | — | fires first at **k=3** (commits block[1]); not before |
| B9 | post-loop | reached **only if the loop returned no `Err`** (Ok path) | `if current_view < expected_height` | **`set_view(expected_height)` (:2205) — the ONLY `current_view` writer in this path** | — | **skipped on any `Err`** → on `Err`, `current_view` is **NOT** advanced |
| R | `Ok(applied)` | — | — | — | `restore_catchup_blocks_applied += applied`; `evaluate_restore_mode_transition` (may flip restore mode off, update peer-tip) | `Err(e)` → `restore_catchup_responses_rejected += 1`, log; **peer-tip tracker NOT updated** (caller 7962–7972). The caller comment "did NOT mutate engine state" is accurate for a **first-block / pre-loop** rejection (reachable first-block errors are all B1–B6/P0, i.e. pre-registration; B8 is non-erroring), but **FALSE for a later-block rejection after an accepted prefix** (the prefix's registration/lock/commit persist) |

**Per-field survival on `Err` (source-established, A17.1 — not grouped):** on a mid-batch `Err` at block k (>1), the following of blocks[1..k−1] **persist** (no rollback): **registration** (B7, per block), **`locked_qc`** (last per-block update), **`committed_height`/`committed_block`** (any 3-chain that fired, i.e. if k−1 ≥ 3). The following are **skipped/unchanged**: **`current_view`** (post-loop `set_view` not reached → **not advanced**, correcting the earlier prose), **`applied`** return (discarded by the caller on `Err`), **peer-tip tracker** and **restore-mode transition** (caller skips on `Err`). **Reachable `Err` branches are exactly P0 (MissingLocalAnchor) and B1–B6**, all of which occur **before that block's registration**; **B8 does not produce a reachable `Err`** for inputs that passed B6. So a first-block rejection is genuinely non-mutating — but this rests on B8's non-erroring (established from the accumulator source), **not** on "first block" alone. There is no transactional wrapper; this is folded into A17-F1's "incremental admission" characterization, **not** a separate forced finding.

### 24.4b Symbolic commit-transition (source-only; no harness run)

**One explicit SUFFICIENT case — a freshly-restored node (A17.2).** This is **one** sufficient schedule, not a proof over all schedules; other starting states are out of scope. Its initial state is exactly what the production restore initializer produces (so it is compatible with production initialization, though whether a given DevNet runs restore + catch-up is **unobserved deployment**, §3B):
- **Restore install values (source-exact).** `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:1995–2018) calls `state.initialize_from_snapshot_baseline(C, snapshot_height, snapshot_height)` — passing `committed_view = committed_height = h` (source comment: "the binary engine conflates view and height"). So the state has `committed_height = Some(h)`, `committed_block = Some(C)`, the anchor node `C = BlockNode(view = h, parent_id = None, justify_qc = None, own_qc = None, height = h)` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1254–1283), and the initializer **does not touch `locked_qc` → `locked_qc = None` (= `L₀`)**; the engine's `current_view = h+1`.
- **Membership / quorum.** Uniform unit-weight set of size `N` with `N = 3f+1` and **`f ≥ 1`** (so ≥1 fault is within budget and `q = ⌈2N/3⌉ = 2f+1 ≤ N`); `q ≤ N ≤ 256`.
- **Accumulator.** Empty relevant state at views `h+1 … h+m` and **sufficient configured capacity** — defaults `max_tracked_views = 128`, `max_votes_per_view = 256` (vote_accumulator.rs:111–112), so `m ≤ 128` and `q ≤ 256` incur no view-eviction or per-view drop.
- **Admission.** Responder `r ≠ local_validator_id` (self-responses dropped, :7872); admitted authenticated origin bound to `r`'s own validator id (§24.2); response anchor **exactly** `(h, C)` (else stale-reject, no mutation, :7892).
- **Suffix.** Each `Bᵢ` (i = 1..m, `m ≥ 3`) has `height = view = h+i`, `parent = block_id(Bᵢ₋₁)` (`B₀ ≡ C`), `proposer = leader_for_view(h+i)`, `block_id = D(proposer, view, parent)`, with `block_id(Bᵢ)` **distinct from `C` and from each other** (the ordinary distinct-ID example — the same-key `A = P‖P` degenerate case is handled separately in §24.5/E22 and is **excluded here**), and `qc_signers` = a fixed set of exactly `q` valid member indices.
- **Arithmetic representability (A18 Part A).** `h + m + 1 ≤ u64::MAX`. The inspected path advances the height cursor with `expected_height = committed_height.saturating_add(1)` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2130–2133) and, per accepted block, `expected_height = expected_height.saturating_add(1)` (:2199), then post-loop `set_view(expected_height)` with `expected_height = h+m+1` (:2205–2207). The per-block check `block.height == expected_height` compares against these cursor values. With `h + m + 1 ≤ u64::MAX`, **no `saturating_add` saturates**, so the cursor takes the distinct strictly-increasing values `h+1, h+2, …, h+m+1` that the symbolic table and the strict floor `g_height > committed_height` rely on. (If instead `h` were within `m+1` of `u64::MAX`, a `saturating_add` would pin the cursor at `u64::MAX`, collapsing distinctness and the contiguous-height admission — a **different** regime that overlaps the restored-view `[M−9, M]` band of E02/§23.5 and the A1-F2 TC-view overflow; **out of this sufficient case** and left to those entries, not re-proved here.) This bounds the sufficient case to the ordinary non-saturating regime.

Symbolic per-step transition (separates the five effect classes), for this freshly-restored case:

| step | registration | QC formation (`own_qc`) | `locked_qc` (prev → new) | `committed_height`/`block` | engine `current_view` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B₁ (view h+1) | `B₁` inserted (justify = `L₀ = None`) | `own_qc(B₁)=qc₁` once the `q` replayed votes reach quorum | `None → qc₁` (replace: `qc₁.view = h+1 >` no lock) | **unchanged** — `try_commit(qc₁)`: B=B₁, P=parent(B₁)=C, G=parent(C)=**None** ⇒ no 3-chain ⇒ **return, no commit** | unchanged (`set_view` is post-loop) |
| B₂ (view h+2) | `B₂` (justify = `qc₁`) | `own_qc(B₂)=qc₂` | `qc₁ → qc₂` (`h+2 > h+1`) | **unchanged** — `try_commit(qc₂)`: B=B₂, P=B₁, G=C. **Primary reason it does NOT commit: the strict height floor — `g_height = C.height = h` is NOT `> committed_height = h`** (independent of `own_qc`). *Additional* independent check: `C.own_qc = None` ⇒ the predicate also returns at the G-own_qc test | unchanged |
| B₃ (view h+3) | `B₃` (justify = `qc₂`) | `own_qc(B₃)=qc₃` | `qc₂ → qc₃` (`h+3 > h+2`) | **COMMIT `B₁`**: B=B₃, P=B₂, G=B₁; all three have `own_qc` ✓; `B₁.view < B₂.view < B₃.view` ✓; **`g_height = h+1 > h` ✓** (B₁ is the first block strictly above the committed height); `g_view = h+1 > committed.view = C.view = h` ✓ (holds **exactly** because the initializer set `C.view = h`) ⇒ `committed_height ← h+1`, `committed_block ← B₁` | unchanged (post-loop) |
| B₄…B_m | `Bᵢ` | `qcᵢ` | `← qcᵢ` (each `h+i >` prior) | commits `Bᵢ₋₂` under the same predicate (sliding 3-chain) | — |
| post-loop | — | — | — | — | `set_view(h+m+1)` — **only if** the loop returned `Ok` **and** `current_view (= h+1) < h+m+1` (true for `m ≥ 1`) |

**Sufficient suffix length (this case):** the **first** committed-height advance occurs at **B₃** and requires an accepted suffix of **length ≥ 3**; each further block commits one more. A length-1 or length-2 accepted suffix produces registration + `locked_qc` updates + per-block `own_qc` but **no committed-height change** — so "every accepted suffix produces a commit" is **false** and is not claimed.

**Why B₃, not B₂ (A17.2-corrected):** the binding reason is the **strict advancing floor** `g_height > committed_height` — for `B₂` the grandparent `G` is the committed anchor `C` itself (height `h`), which fails `h > h`; the first grandparent strictly above `committed_height` is `B₁` (height `h+1`), reached when `B₃` is processed. The restored anchor's `own_qc = None` is an **additional** independent check that also blocks committing `C`, **not** the sole reason.

**Accumulator restrictions (A17.2 — stated accurately):** the clean empty-accumulator state is a **sufficient** condition for the `q` replayed votes to all count toward each `qcᵢ`; it is **not** described as necessary. Precisely: a replayed vote from a signer who already voted at that view for a *different* block_id is **suppressed as equivocation — a non-error `Ok(None)`** (on_vote step 1, hotstuff_state_engine.rs:959); a per-view capacity drop is also a **non-error `Ok(false)`** (vote_accumulator.rs:331–337); a **returned `Err`** arises only for a non-member voter (:309), which cannot occur here since B6's `qc.validate` already enforced membership. `qcᵢ` forms **iff the count of effective (non-suppressed) contributions reaches `q`**; with ≥`q` listed members and an empty accumulator at those views, it does. Thus the five outcomes are kept distinct: **returned `Err`** (non-member only; not reachable post-B6) / **non-error suppression** (`Ok(None)` equivocation, `Ok(false)` capacity) / **normal batch completion** (`Ok(applied)`) / **actual QC formation** (per block, when effective ≥ `q`) / **actual commit** (per 3-chain, suffix ≥ 3). A node with a non-empty accumulator at those views is **not** a blanket containment — the forged `qcᵢ` still forms if enough non-suppressed members remain; it is only this *sufficient case* that assumes the clean state.

**Fault-budget assumption (stated before the one-validator characterization):** HotStuff safety assumes `N = 3f+1` with ≤ `f` Byzantine and quorum `2f+1`; with `f ≥ 1`, the concern is that **one** responder supplies the full `2f+1`-index list **without any of them having endorsed**, so the committed-advancement precondition — *verified quorum endorsement* — is **advanced-upon without being established**. **This is the missing-control / BFT-threshold observation; it is NOT a demonstrated honest-node disagreement or downstream execution inconsistency** (neither traced — E20).

### 24.5 Anchor-preservation determination (relates to A16.3 / E22 — does this path resolve the open premise?)

**WITHDRAWN (A17.1): "catch-up is not a same-key replacement path."** The v0.41 exclusion rested on a collision assumption, which is wrong for this layout. The same-key case is now stated at **separated evidence levels (A17.2)** so no link is described as both established and unresolved:

- **(L1) Algebraic fixed point — ESTABLISHED (pure arithmetic).** The derivation is field concatenation `D(P, A) = P ‖ A[0:16]`, `P = proposer(8) ‖ view(8)` (16 bytes), `A` the 32-byte parent id (derive_block_id_from_header, :2043–2058). `A = P ‖ P ⟹ D(P, A) = P ‖ (P‖P)[0:16] = P ‖ P = A`. No collision assumption.
- **(L2) Field-check satisfaction UNDER the opaque-anchor precondition — ESTABLISHED GIVEN that precondition.** If the restored anchor id `C = P ‖ P` with `P = leader_for_view(h+1) ‖ (h+1)`, then the first catch-up block with `parent = C`, `block_id = D(P, C) = C`, `height = view = h+1` satisfies the inspected per-block checks B1–B5, and B6 (`qc.validate`) if ≥`q` member indices are listed. The admission checks do **not** exclude the degenerate `block_id == C` — they are exactly what the fixed point satisfies.
- **(L3) The upstream precondition — UNTRACED, named explicitly.** L2 requires the victim's committed anchor id to **be** `P ‖ P`. That id is the opaque `snapshot_block_id` installed by startup restore (§23), so the victim must have **restored from a snapshot whose `block_id = P ‖ P`** — i.e. a local-write actor supplied that crafted snapshot at the victim's data directory (the **E22 local-write boundary**). The restore validation (§23) treats `block_id` as **opaque** (checks `height > 0`, chain-id, authority-marker, epoch — not the block_id's form), so it *appears* not to constrain a `P‖P` id, **but the end-to-end restore-acceptance of such an id is NOT separately traced here** and is named as the untraced upstream premise.
- **(L4) Map replacement — CONDITIONALLY reachable (given L2 ∧ L3).** Given a crafted `C = P‖P` anchor (L3) and ≥`q` forged `qc_signers`, `register_block` is invoked with `id == C` → a same-key overwrite of the anchor entry (its height recomputed from the parent — itself — to `h+1`). This is **conditional** reachability, not an unconditional established link and not an excluded one.
- **(L5) Downstream commit consequence — UNTRACED; (L6) runtime — UNEXECUTED.** What a same-key anchor overwrite then does to `try_commit`/the chain, and whether it yields any harmful outcome, is **not traced**; no runtime behavior is executed.

**Disposition:** the v0.41 "not a same-key replacement path" claim is **withdrawn** (L1/L2 refute it under L3); the case is an **algebraic possibility gated by a crafted-snapshot (E22 local-write) upstream precondition that is itself untraced (L3)** with an **untraced downstream consequence (L5)** — **not** promoted to a finding. The precise unresolved premise (L3→L4→L5 chain) is **preserved at E22**, kept **separate** from §24.4b's ordinary distinct-ID sufficient case and from the general `register_block`/`register_block_with_verified_justification` same-key question already at E22.

**Qualified (A17.1): "successful catch-up raises `committed_height`."** It does so **only when the 3-chain commit predicate actually fires** — i.e. an accepted suffix of **length ≥ 3** with the guards of §24.4b; a length-1/2 accepted suffix raises registration/`locked_qc` only. Where a commit does fire, `committed_height` moves above `h` and the anchor at `height = snapshot_height ≤ committed_height` stays non-evictable (:598–603) — but this is conditional on the suffix length and the commit guards, not automatic from "accepted response."

### 24.6 Finding A17-F1, reachability threat model, and public-DevNet applicability

**A17-F1 (STATIC-SUPPORTED, OPEN) — live catch-up advances committed state without verifying quorum endorsement.** See §2 for the finding record. **Concrete production preconditions (all required):**
1. **Attacker is a configured validator peer** — holds valid KEMTLS credentials whose NodeId↔ValidatorId is in the node's one-to-one binding map (else `bind_sender` rejects). This is an **insider / compromised-validator** threat, **not** anonymous network-reachable. A single such validator suffices (it forges the `qc_signers` list; no other validator need cooperate and no signatures are checked).
2. **Catch-up response processing reachable** — the victim runs the binary consensus loop with the inbound path active (no feature flag gates the response arm; no restore-mode requirement on the victim).
3. **Anchor known** — the attacker sets `request_from_height`/`request_from_block_id` to the victim's current committed tip (observable to fellow validators).
4. **Deterministic chain constructable** — the attacker computes a contiguous `height==view` chain from `committed+1`, each `proposer = leader_for_view(view)`, each `block_id = derive_block_id_from_header(...)`, listing ≥⌈2N/3⌉ validator indices as `qc_signers`.

**Impact (scoped; A17.1-corrected):** the victim registers + reconstructs votes → forms per-block QCs → updates `locked_qc`; and **for an accepted suffix of length ≥ 3 satisfying the 3-chain predicate** (§24.4b) advances `committed_height`/`committed_block`. `current_view` advances **only on normal loop completion** (post-loop `set_view`), not on a mid-batch `Err`. The wire block carries **no tx/state payload**, so this is **advancement of consensus metadata**, not direct state/transaction forgery via this message. **Supported core = the missing endorsement-verification control** (committed-state advancement without verified quorum endorsement). **NOT established (A17.1):** a demonstrated disagreement between honest nodes, downstream execution/finality inconsistency, and whether/how the forged tip feeds later proposal admission or VM execution — these are a **source-review gap** (downstream control flow) plus **execution/deployment evidence gaps**, all under **E20**.

**Public-DevNet applicability (concrete prerequisites; intended config ≠ observed deployment):** reachable on a DevNet that (i) runs the binary consensus loop with the catch-up handlers wired (present in source, not feature-gated), (ii) has a multi-validator binding map so an attacker-validator is authorized, and (iii) where the attacker is or controls ≥1 validator's transport identity. Whether a given DevNet deployment enables catch-up, its validator count/threshold, and its binding-map population are **observed-deployment questions not established here**. Not anonymously reachable. **Priority note (A17.1):** A17-F1's P1 review priority reflects that it sits on a state-advancing consensus path; **priority does not itself establish a release blocker or authorize validation/reproduction** — those are separate decisions requiring the deployment evidence above, and this register records the finding without declaring a blocker.

### 24.7 Disposition, E20/E22 relation, counts

- **A17-F1** is a **STATIC-SUPPORTED security-weakness finding**, OPEN — distinct from the A4-F2/H04-F1/A10-F1/A15-F1 assurance-gap class (it is a source-established **missing-endorsement-verification** gap on a state-advancing path, not an observability/supervision gap). **Distinct mechanisms (A17.1), not merged:** **A1-F1** = missing-context **Timeout/TC** verification (NOT Proposal/Vote); the production **Proposal/Vote rejection under `Required`** (§6L.1) is a separate property — the `Required` policy does **not** contain A1-F1, and A17's being outside `Required` says nothing about A1-F1; **A1-F3** = TC high-QC adoption; **A17-F1** = catch-up reconstructed-quorum admission. Same "logical `validate`, no crypto" theme, different entrypoint/mechanism/reachability.
- **E20** — **narrowed (A17.1):** A17 source-resolves **only** the specific question *"does the catch-up `qc.validate` perform cryptographic endorsement verification?"* → **no** (logical-only; wire carries no signatures), and characterizes the input-trust boundary. Still OPEN under E20: the **downstream control-flow** of a forged committed tip (proposal-admission / finality / VM) = a **source-review gap**; and **DevNet config + end-to-end exploit + any honest-node-disagreement demonstration** = **execution/deployment evidence gaps**. Not re-counted; scope refined, not "resolved."
- **E22** — **updated (A17.1):** the v0.41 claim that "catch-up is not a same-key anchor replacement path" is **WITHDRAWN** (the `D(P,A)=A` fixed point `A = P‖P` is reachable given the opaque attacker-settable startup `snapshot_block_id`, §24.5); E22 now **also** carries the precise unresolved premise *whether catch-up + a crafted anchor id reaches a same-key anchor replacement and any commit consequence* — distinct from the general `register_block*` same-key question. Not promoted to a finding (compounds local/insider preconditions; consequence untraced).
- **Counts:** **static-supported stays 12** (A17-F1 retained — its supported endorsement-verification core is unchanged; A17.1 narrows unsupported consequences but warrants **no** count change); assurance/hardening/observability gaps **4** (unchanged); evidence gaps **22 (E01–E22)** (unchanged — E20/E22 scope refined, not re-numbered). No closure, no re-pin, no execution.

### 25.1 How to read this plan (obligation-based, not a percentage)

Progress is reported as **obligations and their statuses**, not a single percentage or calendar estimate (the inventory does not support one, and obligations differ greatly in size — raw task counts are an imperfect effort measure). Mixed "incomplete" entries are **split** into distinct obligations so that a completed caller trace, an untraced downstream consumer, unavailable dependency source, and an unexecuted runtime check never share one status. **Status legend:** **SR-DONE** (source review completed within its stated boundary) · **SR-PARTIAL** (source review partial) · **SR-NONE** (source review not started) · **SR-BLOCKED** (blocked by unavailable material) · **DEP** (dependency-evidence work) · **EXEC** (deferred execution/deployment evidence) · **IMPL** (implementation/remediation outside this audit's authorization). An obligation can carry one *source* status plus separate **DEP/EXEC/IMPL** tails (tracked in its own row, not merged). "DevNet" = supported public-DevNet applicability on the intended P2P surface; **later-stage / shared-code** relevance is marked separately and does **not** by itself make an item a DevNet blocker.

The exclusion boundary is the RUN 422 implementation work, not the baseline storage source.
- **SR-BLOCKED (genuinely unavailable material):** OBL-PROV-1's remaining fact = the **pre-graft upstream history/provenance** before the shallow graft (ancestry + content already done in §17; no fetch).
- **Conditional-future-trigger (re-open only on a change; NOT completed review evidence):** OBL-CONS-5 (verified-QC wiring) and OBL-CONS-11b (Proposal/Vote **enablement** re-review) — each a future trigger, not review already done. *(Distinct from OBL-CONS-11a, the **existing** latent Proposal/Vote signing/verification code, which is an **available** source task, SR-NONE, owned by T-A18-7.)*

### 25.4 Source-audit completion definition

**Five distinct end-states for an obligation (A18.1 — operational).** Each in-scope obligation must end in exactly one of:
1. **Completed review with explicit limits** — the available source was read to the stated depth and dispositioned; a **genuinely unprovable-from-source property** (a runtime behavior, a dependency internal) or an assumption may remain, recorded as an explicit limit. *This is the only state in which a recorded limit is acceptable.*
2. **Unfinished required source work** — an **available** required source trace (a reachable caller/consumer trace, an in-tree path) that has **not** been performed. **This cannot be converted to "complete" by recording an unresolved premise** — the trace is available and must be done. (These are the SR-PARTIAL/SR-NONE rows owned by T-A18-* tasks.)
3. **Genuinely unavailable evidence** — material not present to review (un-vendored dependency sources, pre-graft history) = **SR-BLOCKED/DEP**; recorded as blocked, not complete.
4. **Explicitly excluded scope** — e.g. the **RUN 422 implementation thread** (OBL-STO-2b); recorded with its exact boundary, not silently dropped.
5. **Deferred execution / implementation** — **EXEC** (reproductions, live deployment) and **IMPL** (fixes); separate authorization.

This read-only **source audit is complete** when: (a) **every obligation in end-states (2)'s task set has moved to (1)** — i.e. every **available required source trace** is performed to depth, with only genuinely-unprovable-from-source properties left as recorded limits; (b) items in (3)/(4)/(5) are **explicitly recorded** with their boundary, not counted as complete; (c) **supported findings and scoped negatives** carry **revision-bound evidence** (`ef99e29` citations); and (d) **applicability, counts, summaries, and the coverage ledger** are reconciled with the finding set.

**Not completion-eligible:** marking an **available required source trace** (end-state 2) "complete" merely by recording a premise; marking **unavailable** (3) or **excluded** (4) work "complete"; **silently excluding** work to inflate a fraction; or adopting a **scope change** without recording it as explicit and unapproved. **Open findings may remain at source-audit completion** — fixing (IMPL) and validation (EXEC) are separate activities. Task exit criteria are **concrete review deliverables** (§25.3), never "reviewed or deferred." **Progress is reported by obligation end-states**, not a percentage or calendar date — obligations differ greatly in size, so raw task counts are an imperfect effort measure; any remaining coverage limitation is reported plainly.

### 26.1 State & consumer inventory (revision-bound; production vs library/sim/test separated)

Engine fields live in **`HotStuffStateEngine`** (hotstuff_state_engine.rs) and are reached through the **`BasicHotStuffEngine`** wrapper (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs); the binary loop (binary_consensus_loop.rs) holds the engine. Similarly-named out-of-engine fields (`peer_max_observed_committed_height` 2074, `BinaryConsensusLoopProgress.committed_height`, `view_lag` metric) are **transfer/record points**, not the engine fields — kept separate below.

| Field (owner) | Writers (prod unless noted) | Readers (prod) | Readers (library/sim/test only) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locked_qc` (HotStuffStateEngine:173) | `on_qc` replace-if-higher-view (:1004); `set_locked_qc` (:1145) via **`on_timeout_certificate`** (basic:3279, **A1-F3**) and `initialize_from_restart` (:1203, restart ctor) | eviction floor `is_block_safe_to_evict` (:607); **timeout/NewView `high_qc`** (basic:3081 → `maybe_emit_view_timeout`); **leader self-proposal parent + `justify_qc` (basic:2244–2255, `on_leader_step` — production when leader, A19.3)**; `locked_qc_view` accessor (basic:3141); progress recorder (basic:2859/2881); catch-up `previous_qc` seed (basic:2137) | **safe-voting rule `safety_decision`/`is_safe_to_vote_on_block` (:1331/:1313)** — reached only via `ingest_proposal` (basic:2816) ← `on_proposal_event` (**inbound** proposal, Required-rejected ⇒ **latent**, §26.2/.2a); *(the leader self-vote path does NOT consult `safety_decision` — it is `state.on_vote`, moved to prod readers above)*; `set_locked_qc` test sites (basic:4025/4052/4090) |
