**Commit emits nothing downstream (source-established).** `try_commit_with_qc` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1029–1137) sets `committed_block`/`committed_height` and pushes an in-memory `CommittedEntry` to `commit_log` (evicted over a cap). It makes **no callback, channel send, `ConsensusEngineAction`, event, or ledger/execution/VM apply.** Commit is **purely in-memory consensus metadata**; everything downstream is a *reader* of `committed_*`/`commit_log` (above), never a commit-triggered push.

### 26.2 A1-F3 downstream — the TC-installed lock

**Writer (production-reachable):** `on_timeout_certificate` (basic:3256; production callers binary:6931 inbound TC/NewView, 7373 local-apply) runs `tc.validate(validators)` (logical only — no independent quorum-endorsement of `tc.high_qc`), then if `tc.high_qc.view > locked.view` calls `set_locked_qc(tc.high_qc)` (:3279) and advances `current_view = tc.view` (:3285). So an admitted TC installs an attacker-chosen `high_qc` as the lock (gated by the ctx-based TC verify / A1-F1 ctx-absent path — unchanged here).

Per-consumer transition (entry preconditions → validation → state read → branch → mutation/action → failure):

| Consumer | Entry / precondition | Reads lock | Branch / effect | Production-reachable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **safe-voting rule** `safety_decision` (:1331) | a block to vote on; reached via `ingest_proposal` (basic:2816) | `locked_qc.view` + block `justify_qc.view` / ancestry | Safe iff `justify_qc.view ≥ locked.view` (short-circuit) OR block extends locked block; else **Unsafe** (refuse vote) | **NO (latent) — corrected reasoning (A19.3).** `ingest_proposal` callers: `on_proposal_event` (inbound proposal — **rejected fail-closed under `Required`+absent authority before dispatch**, §6L.1) and the latent verified path. **`on_leader_step` does NOT call `ingest_proposal`/`safety_decision`** — it votes for its own block directly via `state.on_vote` (basic:2332). So although **`on_leader_step` IS production-reached** (via `try_propose` basic:3040 ← `do_leader_tick` binary:3360 — the v0.48/earlier "no production caller (all in mod tests)" counted only the four *direct* callers and missed the indirect `try_propose` one; see §26.2a), the **safe-voting rule itself** is reached only on the **inbound** proposal path, which is Required-rejected — so `safety_decision` remains **latent on its own merits** |
| **leader proposal parent + `justify_qc`** (basic:2244–2255) | node is **leader for `current_view`** and has not yet proposed (`on_leader_step` guards :2229 `is_leader_for_current_view`, :2233 `!proposed_in_view`) | `locked_qc().block_id` as **parent** (:2244–2250), `locked_qc().cloned()` as **justify_qc** (:2255) | the leader builds its self-proposal **on the lock**: `register_block(block_id, view, parent, justify=lock)` (:2258–2259), then self-votes via `state.on_vote` (:2332) | **YES (production-reachable when leader) — corrected (A19.3).** `on_leader_step` runs on every tick when `is_leader_for_current_view()`; it reads the lock for the proposal's parent/justify and **registers the block locally**. **No production COMMIT consequence** (but see the view caveat): on a **fresh** key a single self-vote forms a QC only at `two_thirds_vp` quorum (`on_vote`→`maybe_qc_for`, hotstuff_state_engine:979) — met only under **N=1**; under `N=3f+1, f≥1` the *fresh-key* self-vote gives `Ok(None)` (other votes are **inbound**, Required-rejected) ⇒ no `own_qc`, no 3-chain, no commit. **A19.7 caveat — the QC-result branch is NOT N=1-only:** if the leader key **collides** with a catch-up block that already holds the forged `2f+1` (the D-eq / `C[0:16]=P_{h+k}` cases, §26.2b/.2c), `maybe_qc_for` returns `Some(qc)` at `N=3f+1` and `on_leader_step` fires `advance_view()` — a **view transition** (still **no commit**: lock not replaced, self-chain fails strict-increase). Either way the outbound Proposal/Vote **emission is Required-gated** (`signer_ctx`/`journal` None → fail-closed). So the lock shapes the leader's local self-proposal and, in the collision cases, drives a conditional **view advance** — but no production commit |
| **timeout/NewView `high_qc`** (basic:3081) | `maybe_emit_view_timeout` emits a Timeout/NewView | `locked_qc.clone()` → `high_qc` | the node **propagates its current lock as its own high_qc** in its Timeout/TC | **YES** — timeout emission is wired (the node echoes the attacker-chosen high_qc outward; it does not change the node's own commit/vote) |
| **eviction floor** `is_block_safe_to_evict` (:607) | pending-block eviction | locked block id + ancestors | locked block + ancestors **not evictable** (memory retained) | **YES** (bounded memory retention) |
| **`on_qc` lock replacement** (:998–1004) | a QC forms for some block | `locked_qc.view` vs `qc.view` | `replace_lock = (no lock) ∨ qc.view > locked.view`; if so `locked_qc ← qc` | **YES** — reads the lock to decide replacement. Effect = **lock-self-update only** (not a commit/view/vote transition); a **high** attacker-installed lock would make catch-up's per-block `qc.view (= h+i)` fail `> locked.view`, so the lock **stays** at the attacker value, but `node.own_qc` is still set and `try_commit` still runs (commit independent of the lock) |
| **catch-up `previous_qc` seed → `justify_qc`** (basic:2137 → register_block 2186) **[A19.1 — was omitted in A19]** | `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` runs | `previous_qc = locked_qc().cloned()` seeds the **first** catch-up block's `justify_qc` (subsequent blocks use the prior block's qc) | B₁ is registered with `justify_qc = locked_qc` (i.e. the A1-F3 lock for B₁) | **YES (edge exists); NO production consequence.** The stored `justify_qc` is read **only** by `safety_decision` (latent, §26.2) — `try_commit_with_qc` reads `own_qc`/parent/heights, **not** `justify_qc` — so the seeded lock does not feed commit/view/vote on the catch-up path; it is stored metadata on B₁ |
| **commit predicate** `try_commit_with_qc` | a 3-chain forms | **does NOT read `locked_qc`** (nor `justify_qc`) | commit uses per-block `own_qc` + parent/heights + strict floors only | n/a — **commit independent of the lock** (see three-level independence below) |

**Three-level lock-independence of the commit path (A19.1, narrowed A19.2 — the first does NOT prove the others; (b)/(c) are PREMISED negatives, not universal):**
- **(a) No direct `locked_qc` read in `try_commit_with_qc`** — ESTABLISHED: the predicate reads each block node's `own_qc`, `parent_id`, heights/views, and `committed_height`/`committed_block`; it never reads `self.locked_qc`.
- **(b) Lock-derived inputs to the predicate — re-grounded via the own_qc gate (A19.4-corrected; A19.2's "no lock-derived value reaches the predicate" was too strong).** The predicate reads each block node's `own_qc`, `parent_id`, heights/views, `committed_*`. Enumerating their provenance: `own_qc` is set by `on_qc` from the **formed** qc (not the lock); `committed_*` is prior-commit state; heights are computed at `register_block` from the parent. **Two `parent_id`/`justify_qc` inputs ARE lock-derived, which the catch-up-only field inventory missed:** (1) catch-up B₁'s `justify_qc` = `locked_qc` seed — but the predicate **does not read `justify_qc`**, so this one does not reach it; (2) **a leader self-proposed block's `parent_id` = `locked_qc().block_id`** (`on_leader_step` basic:2244–2250, production when leader, §26.2a) — and the predicate **does** read `parent_id`. So a lock-derived **value** (the leader block's parent) *can* be an input the predicate reads. **The negative is therefore re-grounded on the `own_qc`/quorum gate, not on "no lock value reaches the predicate":** the predicate commits grandparent `G` only if `B`, `P`, `G` **each** carry `own_qc` (quorum QCs) and the strict height floor holds; a leader self-proposed block forms **no `own_qc` on a fresh key** (single self-vote < `two_thirds_vp`; inbound votes Required-rejected; §26.2b) — **but A19.8 correction: on a COLLISION key it DOES acquire `own_qc`** (the re-formed forged QC's `on_qc` re-attaches it, state:1008–1009), so the negative is **not** "never acquires `own_qc`"; rather, its lock-derived `parent_id` never participates in a **commit** because on a fresh key there is no `own_qc` and on a collision key the overwritten self/`B_k`-parent chain makes `try_commit`'s `g_view<p_view<b_view` fail (§26.4). The lock-derived parent sets only **chain topology**, which the commit gate (`own_qc` on all three + floor) does not accept without quorum. **A19.2 — the residency channel, previously unaddressed:** the predicate additionally requires the **resident** nodes `B`, `P`, `G` and their parent links (every `blocks.get(...)` must hit); residency is governed by `is_block_safe_to_evict` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:596), whose **clause 2** (`:607` — the locked block and its ancestors are not evictable) **IS lock-dependent**. So the lock can in principle influence *which* nodes stay resident, hence predicate availability — identifying the fields the predicate reads does **not** by itself close this. The channel is **discharged for the catch-up 3-chain** by **clause 3** (`:627` — any block whose `own_qc.is_some()`, and the ancestors of any own_qc block, are not evictable): catch-up `B/P/G` each acquire `own_qc` once their `q` replayed votes reach quorum, so they are retained **independent of the lock** *once `own_qc` is attached*. **A19.3 — the temporal window before `own_qc`, previously not checked:** `register_block` calls `evict_blocks_if_needed()` at its end (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:762), i.e. **before** the per-block `on_vote` loop attaches `own_qc` (basic:2186 register → 2192 vote loop), so clause-3 protection is *not yet* in force at that eviction pass. The bounded ordering check closes this for the §24.4b sufficient case on the **capacity ground, which is the load-bearing one: the trigger never fires** — `evict_blocks_if_needed` evicts only `while self.blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks` (:661) and the default `max_pending_blocks` is **4096** (:40), whereas the freshly-restored sufficient case holds `anchor + m` nodes with `m ≤ 128` (the accumulator `max_tracked_views` bound, §24.4b) ⇒ `blocks.len() ≤ ~129 ≪ 4096`, so the `while` guard is false and **no eviction runs at all** through the whole catch-up loop. (**A19.4 — FIFO-last is NOT relied on as the guarantee:** the just-registered block is `push_back`ed (:758) and eviction pops **front-first** (:664), but FIFO-last placement alone does **not** guarantee preservation in general — if every earlier queue entry is unevictable the inner loop drains the order queue and breaks with nothing evicted (the block then survives only incidentally, while the cap stays violated), and conversely a safe earlier entry is the one evicted; so the *preservation guarantee* for the fresh-state case rests on the **no-eviction capacity argument** above, not on FIFO position.) So the required nodes **remain resident through the stated catch-up sufficient case** — the fixed-resident premise is **discharged for that explicitly-bounded fresh-state case**. For an **arbitrary near-cap state** (`blocks.len()` already ≈ 4096 from prior traffic), the pre-`own_qc` window is real and neither the capacity argument nor FIFO position is a universal proof, so the **fixed-resident premise is retained there, not claimed fully discharged**.
- **(c) No production state-transition (commit / view / vote) consequence — PREMISED/SCOPED negative, with lock-replacement separated from view-advancement (A19.3-corrected).** Enumerating all lock consumers (table above): `safety_decision` (vote gate, **latent**), the **leader proposal parent/justify** read (production-reachable when leader, but no QC/commit without quorum — §26.2a), outbound `high_qc` (basic:3081, propagation), eviction floor (retention), `on_qc` replacement (lock-self-update), catch-up seed (stored, read only by latent `safety_decision`). None produces a production **commit** transition on the single wired node. The consumer that is not purely outbound is the **outbound `high_qc` → later local Timeout/TC consumption**. **A19.2 attributed the harmless outcome to `high_qc.view == locked.view` equality; A19.3 separates the two distinct `on_timeout_certificate` effects (basic:3256–3296), because the earlier reasoning conflated them:**
  - **Local sequence (source-exact).** View `V` times out → `create_timeout_msg` sets `high_qc = self.state.locked_qc().cloned()` (basic:3081), i.e. the node's **own lock** `L` (view `v_L`). Peers' timeouts accumulate (`on_timeout`, basic:3211–3214; stale if `timeout.view < current_view`, :3206). A TC forms when `maybe_tc_for` reaches quorum (basic:3222–3229 scan `current_view..=current_view+10`); `TimeoutCertificate::new` sets `view = timeout_view + 1` (timeout.rs:318) and `high_qc = max` over included timeouts (timeout.rs:306). Then `on_timeout_certificate(tc)` runs **four separable branches**:
  - **(1) forward-target-view admission guard (basic:3263–3267):** `if tc.view <= self.current_view { return Ok(self.current_view); }` — a TC whose target view is not ahead is **ignored entirely** (no lock, no view change). **If a later TC application is redundant, THIS guard is the cause** (the view already advanced via a preceding transition), **not** `high_qc` equality.
  - **(2) conditional lock replacement (basic:3271–3281):** `should_update = match locked_qc() { None => true, Some(locked) => tc_high_qc.view > locked.view }; if should_update { set_locked_qc(tc_high_qc) }`. Re-consuming the node's **own** `high_qc` gives `tc_high_qc.view == v_L == locked.view` ⇒ `should_update = false` ⇒ **lock unchanged**. *This* is the equality-based no-op — but it is a no-op **for the lock only**.
  - **(3) view assignment (basic:3284–3292):** `self.current_view = tc.view` (= `timeout_view + 1`). So an **admitted** TC **does advance the view** — the TC application is **NOT a complete no-op**; the view moves (a pacemaker/liveness effect = A1-F2's unbound-`tc.view` surface, E02), independent of whether the lock changed.
  - **(4) per-view flag resets (basic:3293–3295):** `proposed_in_view = voted_in_view = timeout_emitted_in_view = false` and the accumulator view is cleared (:3299).
  - **Quorum / configuration prerequisite — equal-high_qc is NOT the same as N=1 (A19.4-corrected).** Forming any TC requires `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp()` timeout signers (`TimeoutCertificate::validate`, timeout.rs:380). The lock-replacement **no-op** (branch 2, `should_update` false) fires whenever `tc.high_qc.view ≤ locked.view` — and this can arise in **two distinct ways** that A19.3 conflated: **(i)** a TC built from **only one validator's evidence** (`two_thirds_vp(1)=1` ⇒ **N=1 configuration**), where `tc.high_qc` is necessarily the sole contributor's; and **(ii)** a genuine **quorum TC in an `N=3f+1` set with multiple contributors** whose selected `max` high_qc happens to **equal the receiving node's lock view** — e.g. several timeouts carry the same high_qc, or the max among them equals `L.view`. Case (ii) gives `should_update = false` (no replacement) **without any N=1 assumption** — *equal high_qcs do not require a single contributor*. So branch 2 is driven by the **value** (`tc.high_qc.view` vs `locked.view`), independent of **who** contributed. The case where lock replacement **does** fire — a multi-contributor TC whose `max` high_qc is **strictly higher** than the receiver's lock (e.g. another node's unendorsed A1-F3 lock) — is the A1-F3 install rule itself (logical-`validate`-only, view-gated), **no new in-tree source edge**, its multi-node runtime manifestation tracked as **EXEC (E03)** within the **multi-node-agreement limit OBL-CONS-8** (SR-PARTIAL, TC-aggregation question assigned, §25.2) — **not** a universal negative.
  - **Net (one node's state, any `N`):** when the incoming TC's `max` high_qc has `view ≤ locked.view` (whether via N=1 or an equal-high_qc quorum TC), the TC leaves the **lock unchanged** (branch 2) and **advances the view** (branch 3) or is **ignored** if the view already advanced (branch 1) — in neither case a commit/vote consequence; the "no lock change" is attributed to branch 2 (value comparison), the "redundant application" to branch 1 (forward-guard), **not** to a blanket no-op and **not** to an N=1 assumption. A strictly-higher `max` (multi-contributor) **does** replace the lock → OBL-CONS-8/E03. *(The lock-self-update and eviction retention are lock-internal/memory effects, not consensus-progress transitions.)*

**Dispatch-site reconciliation (A19).** The production loop `run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io`→`handle_inbound_consensus_msg` **does** contain the engine dispatch sites `on_verified_proposal_event` (binary:6281) and `on_proposal_event` (binary:6312) that reach `ingest_proposal`→`safety_decision`. But both sit **after** the verification-context gate: in production `effective_pv = None` (because `current_auth=None` and `pv_authority=None`), so the Proposal handler takes the `None =>` arm and, under `Required` (`requires_context()` true), **increments `inbound_proposal_verification_context_unavailable_total`, logs "REJECTED … policy=Required — fail-closed, not delivered", and `return`s at ~6090-6104 — before 6281/6312**. So the dispatch sites are reached only under the test-only `LocalFixtureUnsigned` passthrough or a wired verification context, **not** the production config (§6L.1). A corroborating trace that located 6281/6312 without the preceding `None`/`Required` early-return would wrongly read the voting rule as production-reached; the gate makes it **latent**.

**A1-F3 downstream conclusion (bounded; OBL-CONS-3 **SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)** — A19.11 (§26.2f) WITHDREW A19.10's SR-DONE: its γ-exclusion invariant is **circular** with the no-leader-commit claim, and its retained-lock no-commit proof used a false node-invariance implication, a wrong cursor=`committed_height` identity, and a wrong anchor-non-residency step. **Established (non-circular):** the conditional view-advance (A19.7), the lock-non-replacement for the retained-lock collision (`qc.view=cv≤v_L`), and the **illustrated** no-commit sub-cases (D-eq self-parent; anchor-as-`G` by `own_qc=None`; non-resident `B_pre`); and the reduction **γ ⟹ ¬(per-view catch-up-id uniqueness)**. **Open (named edge):** the coupled lineage invariant **J** (uniqueness + general retained-lock commit) + the TC-admission posture sub-edge — both OBL-CONS-3 source residuals; collision reachability upstream OBL-STO-1b/A1-F3 + EXEC(E03)).** On the **wired production binary**, the unendorsed TC-installed lock's **safety-relevant consumer (the safe-voting rule `safety_decision`) is NOT reached** — but the correct reason (A19.3) is that `safety_decision` is reached only on the **inbound** proposal path (via `ingest_proposal`←`on_proposal_event`, Required-rejected at ~6090-6104 before the 6281/6312 dispatch), **not** that the leader path is unreachable: **`on_leader_step` IS production-reached** (via `try_propose` basic:3040 ← `do_leader_tick` binary:3360, §26.2a), and it votes for its own block directly via `state.on_vote`, **bypassing `safety_decision`**. The lock's **production-reachable reads** are now: (a) the **leader self-proposal's parent + `justify_qc`** when the node is leader (basic:2244–2255) — the leader registers a block built on the lock and self-votes, **but** forms no COMMIT: on a fresh key a single self-vote gives `Ok(None)` (quorum only at N=1; inbound votes Required-rejected) ⇒ no commit; on a **collision** key (D-eq / `C[0:16]=P_{h+k}`, §26.2c) the self-vote returns `Ok(Some(qc))` at N=3f+1 (pre-forged co-resident quorum) and `on_leader_step` fires `advance_view()` — a **conditional view advance, still no commit** (lock not replaced, self-chain fails strict-increase); emission is Required-gated either way, so **no production commit/finality consequence** (the view advance is a pacemaker effect, conditional on the anchor-form premise); (b) propagation of the attacker-chosen `high_qc` as the node's own `high_qc` in its outbound Timeout/NewView (basic:3081) — whose later **local** re-consumption via the node's own TC leaves the **lock unchanged** (branch 2, `should_update` false by view equality) while **advancing the view** (branch 3) or being **ignored by the forward-target-view guard** (branch 1) if the view already advanced — **not a complete no-op**, §26.2(c); and (c) eviction-floor retention of the locked block/ancestors (:607). **The commit predicate does not read `locked_qc`**, and — under the fixed-resident premise **discharged for the §24.4b sufficient case** (block count ≪ the 4096 cap; §26.2(b)) — the lock changes neither commit nor finalization **on the single wired node**. No **single-node** production commit/finalization consequence of the unendorsed lock is established; the **safe-voting-rule** harm is **latent** (inbound-only, would activate only if inbound Proposal/Vote authority is ever wired — cf. OBL-CONS-11); the **multi-node** TC-aggregation lock-propagation (another node's strictly-higher `high_qc` installed here) is the runtime manifestation of A1-F3 itself, tracked as **EXEC (E03)** + the multi-node-agreement limit **OBL-CONS-8 / T-A18-4**, not claimed negative here. This is a source-established **negative on the single-node wired path** plus the latent-inbound and multi-node scopes; **no new finding, A1-F3 disposition unchanged** (STATIC-SUPPORTED, OPEN). Runtime reproduction remains **EXEC (E03)**.

### 26.2a Local leader-proposal path — `do_leader_tick` traced separately from `on_leader_step` (A19.3)

v0.48 treated the whole proposal/vote/leader path as latent on the strength of "`on_leader_step` has no production caller (all four direct callers in `mod tests`)." That is **incomplete**: `on_leader_step` has an **indirect** production caller. Each stage is classified separately below; a cached header does **not** prove an emitted proposal or a vote, and the inbound `Required` rejection is **not** transferred to the local path without an actual call chain.

**Production entry chain (source-exact, `ef99e29`):**
- `run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` fires `do_leader_tick(...)` on **every `ticker.tick()`** — in both the has-inbound-io branch (binary:2899–2902) and the no-io branch (binary:3053–3056); there is **no leader-only guard at the call site** (the leader test is inside the engine):
  > binary_consensus_loop.rs:2899–2902 — `_ = ticker.tick() => { ticks = ticks.saturating_add(1); let tick_started = Instant::now(); do_leader_tick(`
- `do_leader_tick` calls `engine.try_propose()` (binary:3360):
  > binary_consensus_loop.rs:3360 — `let actions = engine.try_propose();`
- `try_propose` **is** `on_leader_step` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3039–3041):
  > `pub fn try_propose(&mut self) -> Vec<ConsensusEngineAction<ValidatorId>> {` / `    self.on_leader_step()` / `}`
- `on_leader_step` early-returns unless the node is leader and has not proposed (basic:2229–2235):
  > `if !self.is_leader_for_current_view() { return Vec::new(); }` … `if self.proposed_in_view { return Vec::new(); }`

So when the node **is leader for `current_view`** (which recurs ~1/N of views, `leader_for_view(current_view) == local_id`, basic:1747–1748) and has not yet proposed, `on_leader_step` runs **in production**. Per-stage classification:

| Stage | Source (ef99e29) | Runs in production? | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry guard: leader & not-yet-proposed | basic:2229 `is_leader_for_current_view`, :2233 `!proposed_in_view` | **YES** when leader for the view | Gate; passes for ~1/N of views |
| Reads lock for parent | basic:2244–2250 `parent_id = locked_qc().map(block_id).or_else(committed_block())` | **YES (when leader)** | **Production lock read** (A1-F3 consumer) |
| Reads lock for justify | basic:2255 `let justify_qc = self.state.locked_qc().cloned();` | **YES (when leader)** | **Production lock read** |
| **Local block registration** | basic:2258–2259 `self.state.register_block(block_id, view, parent_id, justify_qc.clone());` | **YES (when leader)** | **Local state mutation** — the self-proposed block enters the block tree |
| Header-cache insertion | binary:3378 `reconfig_detector.record_observed_proposal(p)` (inside the `BroadcastProposal` arm) | **YES (when leader & a `BroadcastProposal` action is produced)** | **Local cache write**, keyed by `compute_block_id` (§26.3) — a *cached header*, not an emitted proposal |
| `proposed_in_view = true` | basic:2329 | **YES (when leader)** | Local flag |
| **Leader self-vote (local)** | basic:2332 `let result = self.state.on_vote(self.local_id, view, &block_id);` | **YES (when leader)** | **Local vote** applied directly to state — **bypasses `safety_decision`** |
| Self-vote → QC-result → `advance_view` (NOT commit) | hotstuff_state_engine on_vote:979 `maybe_qc_for` (**unconditional**, needs `two_thirds_vp`); on_leader_step:2360–2372 `if let Ok(Some(_qc)) = result { … self.advance_view(); }` | **QC-result branch reachable at N=3f+1 (A19.7/.8), not only N=1** | On a **fresh** key a single self-vote (one voter, deduped) gives `Ok(None)` ⇒ no `advance_view` (quorum-1 only at N=1). On a **collision** key (the self-proposal id equals a catch-up block already holding the forged `2f+1`, §26.2c/.2d) `maybe_qc_for` returns `Some(qc)` ⇒ `Ok(Some(qc))` ⇒ **`advance_view` fires (VIEW advance, h→h+1)** — reachable at **N=3f+1** via the forged co-resident quorum. **Either way NO commit** (lock not replaced by equal/lower-view qc; overwritten/self-parent chain fails `try_commit`'s strict increase). Inbound producers (`ingest_proposal` :2911, `on_vote_event` :2983) are Required-rejected |
| Re-emission-cache population | binary:3391 `*last_leader_proposal = Some(CachedLeaderProposal { … provenance: capture(current_auth) })` | **YES (when leader)**; provenance `None` in production | **Cached bytes**; re-emission later **fails closed under `Required`** (B9, binary:3379–3395) |
| Outbound encode/enqueue of Proposal/Vote | the action-forwarding boundary consumes `current_auth`/`signer_ctx`/`journal` — all **`None`** in production (do_leader_tick doc, binary:3342–3356) | **NO (latent)** | **Outbound emission rejected fail-closed under `Required`** — proposal/vote never reach the wire |

**Disposition (A19.3).** The **local** leader stages — lock-read for parent/justify, `register_block`, self-vote, header-cache + re-emission-cache writes — **do run in production** when the node is leader; this corrects "no production caller / entirely latent." What is **latent/contained** is narrower and separately grounded: (i) the **safe-voting rule `safety_decision`** (reached only on the inbound path, Required-rejected — the leader self-vote does not consult it); (ii) **QC/own_qc/commit from the self-vote** (no quorum from one vote under `N=3f+1`; inbound votes Required-rejected); (iii) **outbound emission** of the proposal/vote (Required, `signer_ctx`/`journal` `None`). A **cached header** (binary:3378) therefore does **not** imply an emitted proposal or a formed QC. **No new finding** — the A1-F3 negative (no production commit/finality consequence of the unendorsed lock) holds, but by quorum + inbound-`Required` + emission-`Required`, **not** by the leader path being unreachable. The header-cache write being production-reachable is exactly what makes the epoch-consumer association question (§26.3) a real, bounded edge rather than a vacuous one.

### 26.2b Local-leader self-vote vs catch-up — accumulator interaction (A19.4, completes OBL-CONS-3)

A19.3 rested the "no production commit from the leader self-vote" negative on the isolated arithmetic *one unit-weight vote < `two_thirds_vp` for `N=3f+1`*. That alone is **not** a universal production-path negative, because **catch-up is another producer of votes and QCs**. A19.4 traces the shared vote-accumulator state across both producers from pinned source.

**Vote-accumulator mechanics (`ef99e29`).** The accumulator is keyed by `VoteKey { view, block_id }` (vote_accumulator.rs:322); `on_vote` rejects non-members (:309), dedups (`entry.insert(voter)` → `false` if already present, :342), and drops over the per-(view,block_id) cap `max_votes_per_view = 256` (:328–337). `maybe_qc_for(view, block_id)` forms a QC **only for that exact key** once its signer set meets `two_thirds_vp` (:377). The engine `on_vote` adds an **equivocation** gate first (a second vote by the same voter at the same view for a *different* block_id → `Ok(None)`, suppressed, hotstuff_state_engine.rs:959). There is **no clear on view change** — `on_timeout_certificate` clears the **timeout** accumulator (`timeout_accumulator.clear_view`, basic:3299), not the **vote** accumulator; vote entries persist (bounded by `max_tracked_views = 128`, evicting oldest, :314–320).

**Two producers, by (view, block_id) key:**
- **Local leader self-vote** (`on_leader_step` → `state.on_vote(self.local_id, view, block_id)`, basic:2332) writes **one** vote at `(current_view, D(local_id, current_view, lock))`.
- **Catch-up** (`apply_restore_catchup_blocks` → `on_vote(signer, block.view, block.block_id)` per forged signer, basic:2192–2195) writes `qc_signers` votes at `(block.view, block.block_id)`, where admission **enforces `block.height == block.view`** (basic:2155) and `block.height == expected_height` is **contiguous** `committed_height + i` (:2141), and `block.block_id == D(leader_for_view(block.view), block.view, parent)` (:2169–2179).

**Can a local self-vote encounter previously-populated state at its own key?** For the self-vote's `(current_view, X)` entry to already hold `≥ two_thirds_vp − 1` other votes, some producer must have written at **exactly** that key:
- Inbound Votes — **Required-rejected**, never ingested (§6L.1), so contribute nothing.
- Catch-up — writes at `(block.view, block.block_id)` with `block.view = committed_height + i` (height==view, contiguous), all **≤ `committed_height + m`**, i.e. **strictly below the post-catch-up `current_view = committed_height + m + 1`** at which the node next proposes; and the node's view is **monotonic** (`advance_view`/`set_view` never decrease), so each `current_view` is visited once and the leader's self-proposal key is **fresh**. The only way a catch-up write lands on a leader-proposal key is the **(α) association** (a forged catch-up block reproducing `D(local_id, V, ·)` at a view `V` the victim led) — and in that case the QC at that key is formed from catch-up's **own replayed `qc_signers`** (the A17-F1 forged QC), **independently of** and **not needing** the single self-vote (which is deduped/equivocation-gated if present). 

| Scenario | Accumulator at the leader key `(current_view, D(local_id,·,lock))` | QC? | Attribution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Steady-state leader, empty start | 1 (self-vote only); inbound rejected | **No** (1 < `2f+1`, N=3f+1) | §24.4b empty-accumulator case |
| Leader key after prior catch-up (lower views) | 1 (self-vote); catch-up wrote only at `view ≤ committed_height+m < current_view` | **No** | general reachable state — catch-up keys disjoint from the leader key |
| (α) forged catch-up block reproduces the leader key | `2f+1` forged `qc_signers` (± the deduped co-resident self-vote) | **Yes — via catch-up's forged signers** | QC is **forged (A17-F1 / OBL-CONS-4b)**, not a self-vote QC; **but (A19.7) the leader self-vote path still observes `Ok(Some(qc))` and fires `advance_view` — a VIEW advance (no commit), §26.2b/.2c** |
| N=1 degenerate | 1 self-vote = quorum | Yes | single-validator config, not BFT |

**Same-ID registration semantics (A19.5, `insert_block_node` hotstuff_state_engine.rs:568–577).** When catch-up registers a block whose `block_id` equals a victim's earlier self-proposed id (the (α) case), `self.blocks.insert(id, node)` (:576) **unconditionally overwrites** the existing `BlockNode`: the **new** node's `parent_id`, `view`, `height` (recomputed from the parent, :739–742) and `justify_qc` (= catch-up's `previous_qc`) **replace** the self-proposal's, and `own_qc` is **reset to `None`** (register_block builds a fresh node, then the per-block `on_vote` loop re-forms it). What **persists across the overwrite** is only the map **key** (`block_id`) — and, separately, the **`header_cache` entry** (`detector.header_cache`, binary:8392) and the **vote-accumulator entry** `(view, block_id)` (vote_accumulator.rs), which are **not** in `self.blocks` and are **not** touched by `insert_block_node`. So one must distinguish three objects: **(1) the `block_id`** (the stable cache/accumulator key, unchanged by re-registration); **(2) its current `self.blocks` map entry** (overwritten — parent/height/justify/own_qc all come from the latest `register_block`); **(3) the producer of each accumulator vote** (the victim's self-vote and the forged `qc_signers` co-reside under the same key, each tagged by its voter id). **Effect on the (α) transition:** the forged `qc_signers` (2f+1) alone meet `two_thirds_vp`, so `maybe_qc_for` forms the QC and `on_qc` sets `own_qc` **regardless** of the co-resident self-vote; the self-vote is **not an equivocation** (same `block_id`, so `record_vote_history` → `FirstVote`/`DuplicateSameBlock`, not `Equivocation`) and **dedups** if `local_id ∈ qc_signers` — it neither blocks nor is necessary. The map-entry overwrite does **not** break the association, because the epoch consumer keys on the **`block_id`** (object 1), which the overwrite preserves. So the QC's **attribution is the forged signers (A17-F1)**, established on the mechanics above — **not** merely by naming A17-F1.

**Bounded transition table across all return branches (A19.5; fresh-restore case, entry committed height `h`, `committed_height = h`, `committed_block = C`, engine `current_view = h+1`, `locked_qc = None` per §24.4b; `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` basic:2140–2210).** The per-block loop `return Err(..)`s on any failed check **before** `register_block` (:2141/2147/2155/2161/2174) or on a `qc.validate`/`on_vote` error (`?`/`map_err`, :2184/2195); the post-loop `set_view(expected_height)` (:2205–2207) runs **only on `Ok`**:

| Branch | `current_view` | `proposed_/voted_in_view` | lock-selected parent next `on_leader_step` uses | block-map entry (for the affected id) | effective accumulator contributions | `own_qc` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **(A) successful catch-up (non-saturating, `m≥3`, `h+m+1 ≤ u64::MAX`)** | `set_view(h+m+1)` runs → **`h+m+1`** | reset by no path here (flags are leader-step state; unchanged by catch-up) | `locked_qc` (now the last catch-up QC, view `h+m`) → parent prefix `P_{h+m}` | B₁…B_m each registered (justify = prior qc), own_qc set | forged `qc_signers` at each `(h+i, Bᵢ)` | set on each Bᵢ once its `2f+1` replayed |
| **(B) pre-registration rejection (first block fails a check)** | **unchanged `h+1`** (loop `return Err` before any mutation) | unchanged | `committed_block = C` (lock still None) → prefix `C[0:16]` | **none created** | **none** | none |
| **(C) accepted prefix `B₁…B_k` then `B_{k+1}` rejected** | **NOT advanced** — `set_view` skipped on `Err`; stays **`h+1`** (A17.1/A17.2, §24.4) | unchanged | `locked_qc` = last accepted qc (view `h+k`) → prefix `P_{h+k}`; `committed_block` = `B_{k-2}` if `k≥3` | B₁…B_k **persist** (registered, own_qc); B_{k+1} absent | forged signers at `(h+i, Bᵢ)`, `i≤k` **persist** | set on B₁…B_k; `committed_height` advanced to `h+k-2` if `k≥3` |
| **(D-ineq) subsequent leader step, key distinct** (`C[0:16] ≠ P_{h+1}`) | as left by (A)=`h+m+1` or (C)=`h+1` | leader & `!proposed_in_view` | parent = `locked_qc` (= B₁, view `h+1`) → self-id `= D(local_id, h+1, B₁) = P_{h+1}‖B₁[0:16] = P_{h+1}‖P_{h+1}` | a **distinct** self-proposed node (id `P_{h+1}‖P_{h+1} ≠ B₁`); single self-vote at a **fresh** key | **1** self-vote at `(h+1, P_{h+1}‖P_{h+1})` | **none** (1 < `2f+1`) |
| **(D-eq, `k=1`) subsequent leader step, key COLLIDES** (`C[0:16] = P_{h+1}`, A19.6; **caller transition completed A19.7**) | **`h+1` → `h+2`** — `advance_view()` **FIRES** (see outcome) | leader & `!proposed_in_view(h+1)`; after advance: proposed/voted reset to **false** | parent = `locked_qc` = B₁; self-id `= P_{h+1}‖B₁[0:16] = P_{h+1}‖P_{h+1} = B₁` (**since** `B₁ = P_{h+1}‖C[0:16] = P_{h+1}‖P_{h+1}`) | `register_block(B₁…)` **overwrites** B₁'s map entry → parent=B₁ (self), height=`h+2`, justify=lock, **own_qc reset** | self-vote lands on `(h+1, B₁)` which **already holds the forged `2f+1`** (catch-up); same-id ⇒ `DuplicateSameBlock`/`FirstVote` (no equivocation), dedups if `local_id ∈ qc_signers` | `maybe_qc_for` returns **`Some(qc)`** (entry has quorum) → `state.on_vote` returns **`Ok(Some(qc))`** → `on_qc`: **no lock change** (`qc.view h+1 ≯ locked h+1`, state:1000), **no commit** (self-chain `g_view=p_view=b_view` fails strict increase, §26.4); **BUT `on_leader_step`'s `if let Ok(Some(_qc)) = result` (basic:2361) → `advance_view()` (view h+1→h+2), NOT a commit** |

**Row (D) — the key-inequality is NOT assumed (A19.6-corrected).** A19.5 wrote "a fresh self-proposed block … 1 self-vote" for row D, silently assuming the subsequent leader key is **fresh**. It is not fresh in general. After an accepted first catch-up block `B₁ = P_{h+1} ‖ C[0:16]` whose forged QC becomes the lock (on_qc, state:1003–1004), a subsequent eligible leader step at the **unchanged** view `h+1` (branch C skipped `set_view`) builds on parent `B₁`, so its id is `D(local_id, h+1, B₁) = P_{h+1} ‖ B₁[0:16] = P_{h+1} ‖ P_{h+1}` — which **equals `B₁` exactly when `C[0:16] = P_{h+1}`**. The fresh-restore premises do **not** exclude that equality, and it does **not** require the anchor to satisfy the (γ) `C = D(P_{h+1}, C)` fixed point: taking `C = P_{h+1} ‖ R` with `R ≠ P_{h+1}` keeps `B₁ ≠ C` yet gives `C[0:16] = P_{h+1}`. So two cases: **(D-ineq)** `C[0:16] ≠ P_{h+1}` → the leader key `P_{h+1}‖P_{h+1}` is genuinely fresh → 1 self-vote → `state.on_vote` returns `Ok(None)` → the `on_leader_step` QC-result branch is **not** taken → no `advance_view`, no QC, no commit, no view change. **(D-eq)** `C[0:16] = P_{h+1}` → the leader key **collides with `B₁`**, which already carries the forged `2f+1`; the self-vote's `maybe_qc_for` (called unconditionally, state:979) returns **`Some(qc)`** → `state.on_vote` returns **`Ok(Some(qc))`**. This has **two distinct consequences that A19.6 conflated** (§26.2c completes the caller trace): **(i)** `on_qc` gives **no lock change** (`qc.view h+1 ≯ locked.view h+1`, state:1000) and **no commit** (`register_block`'s self-parent overwrite makes `try_commit`'s `g_view<p_view<b_view` degenerate to `h+1<h+1<h+1`, §26.4); **BUT (ii)** `on_leader_step`'s result handler `if let Ok(Some(_qc)) = result { … self.advance_view(); }` (basic:2360–2372) **fires `advance_view()`**, so **the view DOES advance `h+1 → h+2`** (flags reset). **A19.7 correction: D-eq is NOT a "no view transition" case — it produces a VIEW ADVANCE without a commit.** The earlier "no new leader-path commit/view transition holds in both cases" is **withdrawn**: only the **commit** negative holds in D-eq; the **view advances**. Eligibility: (D-eq) needs `!proposed_in_view` at the current view (else `on_leader_step` returns early at :2233). **Scope repair (A19.7):** the `parent = B₁`, `current_view = h+1` derivation is the **one-block (`k=1`) partial-rejection** case; it does **not** describe successful catch-up or a longer prefix — see the finite case table (§26.2c), where branch (A) (successful, `current_view = h+m+1`, lock `= B_m`) gives a **fresh** leader key `P_{h+m+1}‖P_{h+m}` (no collision, no view advance), and a `k`-block partial rejection leaves lock `= B_k` so the leader key is `P_{h+1}‖P_{h+k}`, colliding with `B₁` iff `C[0:16] = P_{h+k}` (the anchor-form condition generalizes to `P_{h+k}`). **The reachability of the equality `C[0:16] = P_{h+1}` is an UPSTREAM anchor-form premise** (the restored `snapshot_block_id`'s first 16 bytes encoding `(local_id, h+1)`), **owned by OBL-STO-1b / E22** (restore-acceptance / anchor form) — **not assumed reachable and not assumed excluded here**; this is an algebraic check of the proof, not an established runtime consequence. **Committed-vs-view (benign-inconsistency claim withdrawn, A19.6):** in branch (C) the first commit fires at `B₃` (commits `B₁`) giving `committed_height = h+1`; `committed_height = h+k−2` for `k` accepted blocks, so `committed_height` **exceeds** the unchanged `current_view = h+1` **only when `k ≥ 4`** (not at `k = 3`, where they are equal). The earlier "benign inconsistency" label is **withdrawn** (unsupported); the state is simply "committed height can exceed `current_view` for `k ≥ 4`", a consequence of the skipped `set_view`, recorded without a benign/non-benign characterization. **A self-vote never produces a new COMMIT in (A)/(C)/(D)** (fresh key → no QC; collision → self-referential/overwritten-parent chain fails the strict-increase commit check; lock never replaced since `qc.view ≤ current lock view`) — **but D-eq DOES produce a new VIEW transition** (`advance_view` via `Ok(Some(qc))`); the QCs the self-vote "sees" are the **forged** catch-up ones (A17-F1) co-resident at the collision key.

**Monotonicity / fresh-key scope (A19.5; A19.6-qualified).** The "each `current_view` visited once ⇒ fresh key" heuristic is **not** backed by an unconditional non-decrease in `advance_view`/`set_view`: **`advance_view` (basic:1794) is an unconditional `current_view + 1`** (monotone by construction but performs **no guard**, and resets `proposed_/voted_in_view`); **`set_view` (basic:1857) assigns the passed value unconditionally — it has NO non-decrease guard and can decrease the view** (its doc warns "only during startup/restart" but enforces nothing). The **only** method that fail-closed-enforces non-decrease is **`try_advance_to_view` (basic:3105, `if target_view <= current_view { … return false }`)**. In the wired paths monotonicity therefore rests on the **callers' guards**: catch-up's post-loop `if self.current_view < expected_height { set_view(..) }` (basic:2205) and `on_timeout_certificate`'s forward-target-view guard `tc.view <= current_view → ignore` (:3264); `advance_view`'s `+1`. So the fresh-key heuristic holds **only where a caller guard makes the view strictly increase**, and **crucially fails in branch (C)** where `set_view` is skipped and the view stays at `h+1` — which is exactly why row (D) must handle the key-collision case above rather than assume freshness. The **non-saturating regime** (`h+m+1 ≤ u64::MAX`) and the **preserved E02 saturating-band exception** `[M−9, M]` (A1-F2 `tc.view` overflow / `saturating_add` pinning, §23.5/§24.4b) stand as before — not re-proved, not claimed closed.

**Conclusion (OBL-CONS-3 → SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03); status history: SR-DONE A19.3–A19.5, SR-PARTIAL A19.6–A19.7, SR-DONE A19.8, SR-PARTIAL A19.9, SR-DONE A19.10, **SR-PARTIAL A19.11** — A19.11 §26.2f withdrew A19.10's SR-DONE because its invariant/commit proofs were circular/unsupported; both named obligations reduce to the coupled lineage invariant J, not discharged in this pass).** The **COMMIT negative is established** (single-node, the cases traced in §26.2c): a leader self-vote produces **no new commit** — fresh key → no QC; collision key → re-formed QC but no lock replacement (`qc.view ≤ current lock view`) and no commit (self-referential/overwritten-parent chain fails the strict-increase predicate); inbound votes Required-rejected; §26.2(b)'s leader block never commits for want of `own_qc`. **A19.7 CORRECTION — the view negative does NOT hold:** in the collision case (**D-eq / the generalized `C[0:16] = P_{h+k}` cases**, §26.2c) `state.on_vote` returns `Ok(Some(qc))` and `on_leader_step` then fires **`advance_view()`** (basic:2360–2372), so **a VIEW TRANSITION occurs without a commit**. So CONS-3's supported **predicate facts** are "no self-vote-induced commit" + "a self-vote-induced **view advance** IS reachable in the collision cases" — the earlier blanket "no commit/view transition" is **withdrawn**. **A19.8 OPENED the two remaining lock states and claimed completion → SR-DONE; A19.9 WITHDREW that completion** after repairing three defects (field binding, arithmetic, effective count, §26.2d). The vote-producer **inventory** (`state.on_vote` four callers — catch-up :2194 + leader self-vote :2332 production, `ingest_proposal` :2911 + `on_vote_event` :2983 Required-rejected) is complete, **but the inventory is not the determining condition**: the self-vote returns `Ok(Some(qc))` **iff `acc_vp(S ∪ {local}) ≥ two_thirds_vp`** — a **voting-power** predicate with four cases (single-node self-quorum α; entry-already-quorum β; **completing-quorum γ**; below-threshold δ), **not** the A19.8 "iff the key already holds a catch-up `2f+1`." A19.8 traced a **retained A1-F3 TC lock** (`on_timeout_certificate`) and **repeated partial batches**, but (i) it substituted the opaque lock prefix `B_pre[0:16]` with `P_{v_L}` — an unenforced binding (`TimeoutCertificate::validate` never validates `high_qc`, timeout.rs:358–388; `set_locked_qc` registers no node, state:1144–1146) — now withdrawn; (ii) its arithmetic exclusion (`v_L=h+m` ⇒ `current_view>v_L` "impossible") is false; (iii) the commit negative for the retained lock does **not** transfer from the fresh-restore self-parent mechanism. So **across the local states**: the self-vote **never induces a COMMIT in the fresh-restore/single-node cases** (resident-chain / self-parent mechanisms, §26.2c), and **induces a VIEW advance exactly on a collision** — an **established conditional transition**, preserved. **Remaining OPEN local source branches (why SR-PARTIAL):** the **completing-quorum γ** reachability (`acc_vp(S)=q−1`, local absent, via equivocation-suppression + repeated batches) and the **retained-lock collision** (opaque-prefix reachability + the resident-`B_pre` commit sub-case). **Genuinely non-local residuals:** anchor-form `C[0:16]=P_{h+k}` (**OBL-STO-1b / T-A18-2**), A1-F3 TC-prefix provenance (**A1-F3 / EXEC E03**), execution (E03). CONS-3's available-source scope was SR-PARTIAL at A19.9; A19.10 (§26.2e) claimed to resolve the two named obligations, but **A19.11 (§26.2f) WITHDREW that resolution** — the γ-exclusion invariant is circular with the no-leader-commit claim, and the retained-lock no-commit proof used a false node-invariance implication, a wrong cursor=`committed_height` identity, and a wrong anchor-non-residency step. Both obligations reduce to the **coupled lineage invariant J** (per-view catch-up-id uniqueness + general retained-lock commit), not discharged in A19.11, so OBL-CONS-3 stays **SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)**. Established (non-circular): the conditional view-advance; the lock-non-replacement (`qc.view=cv≤v_L`); the illustrated no-commit sub-cases (D-eq self-parent, anchor-as-`G` by `own_qc=None`, non-resident `B_pre`); and the reduction **γ ⟹ ¬uniqueness**. Residuals: the J edge + the TC-admission posture sub-edge (OBL-CONS-3 source), anchor-form upstream (OBL-STO-1b/T-A18-2), execution (E03). No full HotStuff safety proof is required, and none is claimed.

### 26.2c D-eq complete caller transition + finite composition case table (A19.7)

**(1) D-eq through the complete `on_leader_step` caller chain (pinned, separated outcomes).** The chain `state.on_vote → accumulator insert/dedup → maybe_qc_for → on_qc → returned Result → on_leader_step result-handling → advance_view` (basic:2332, state:952–987, basic:2360–2372):
> state (on_vote):952–987 — `record_vote_history` → `FirstVote`/`DuplicateSameBlock` (no equivocation, same id); `let _is_new = self.votes.on_vote(..)?;` (:974) **then unconditionally** `let qc = self.votes.maybe_qc_for(..)?;` (:979); `if let Some(ref qc) = qc { self.on_qc(qc)?; }` (:981–983); `Ok(qc)` (:986)
> basic (on_leader_step):2360–2372 — `if let Ok(Some(_qc)) = result { … self.advance_view(); }` (the **only** condition; no further guard)

Because the collision key `(h+1, B₁)` already holds the forged `2f+1`, `maybe_qc_for` returns `Some(qc)` **whether or not** `local_id`'s vote was new or a duplicate (it is evaluated after the insert regardless of `_is_new`). Reporting the outcomes **separately** (per the review's requirement — do not infer one from another):

| Outcome dimension | D-eq result (pinned) |
| --- | --- |
| **Map replacement** | `register_block(B₁, view=h+1, parent=lock, justify=lock)` overwrites B₁'s node (`insert_block_node` :576) — parent←lock (B₁ for `k=1`; B_k for `k≥2`), height←parent.height+1, justify←lock, `own_qc`←None |
| **Effective accumulator contents** | `(h+1, B₁)` held forged `2f+1` from catch-up; + `local_id` (new or dup). **NOT "one total vote."** `≥ 2f+1` |
| **QC return / re-attachment** | `maybe_qc_for` → `Some(qc)`; `on_qc` re-attaches `own_qc` to B₁'s (overwritten) node |
| **Lock replacement** | **NO** — `replace_lock = qc.view(h+1) > locked.view` is false (`k=1`: `h+1>h+1` false; `k≥2`: `h+1>h+k` false), state:998–1004 |
| **Committed-state change** | **NO** — `try_commit`'s `g_view<p_view<b_view` fails (overwritten self/`B_k` parent makes the 3-view chain non-increasing), state §26.4 |
| **View change** | **YES** — `state.on_vote` returns `Ok(Some(qc))` ⇒ `on_leader_step` runs `advance_view()` ⇒ `current_view: h+1 → h+2` (basic:1794–1811) |
| **Flag changes** | `on_leader_step` set `proposed_in_view=true` (:2329), `voted_in_view=true` (:2333); then `advance_view` **resets both to false** (and `timeout_emitted_in_view=false`) |
| **Returned actions** | `[BroadcastProposal(B₁), BroadcastVote(B₁)]` (basic:2375–2377) — returned regardless |
| **Outbound admission** | both actions are **Required-gated** at the forwarding boundary (`signer_ctx`/`journal` None → fail-closed, §26.2a) — **not emitted** |

**So D-eq establishes a VIEW transition (not a commit).** The "D-eq cannot change the view because it cannot commit" inference is **withdrawn**: commit and view are decided by **different** branches (`try_commit` vs the `Ok(Some(qc))` result-handler), and only the former fails. The view-advance is reachable at **`N = 3f+1`** (the forged `2f+1` co-reside at the collision key) — **not only `N=1`**; the `on_leader_step` comment "(e.g., single node)" names one way to reach the branch, not the only way. The transition remains **conditional** on the upstream anchor-form premise `C[0:16] = P_{h+k}` (OBL-STO-1b / T-A18-2), held conditional until that acceptance is reviewed.

**(2) Finite composition case table (CONS-3 local cases).** Preconditions / retained state / immediate `state.on_vote` return / caller effect:

| Case | Executable precondition | Retained state at the leader key | `state.on_vote` return | `on_leader_step` caller effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Successful catch-up (branch A), then leader** | m≥3 accepted; `current_view = h+m+1`; lock `= B_m` (view h+m); leader for `h+m+1` | leader key `P_{h+m+1}‖P_{h+m}` — **fresh** (no catch-up block at view h+m+1) | `Ok(None)` (1 vote) | no `advance_view`; no QC/commit/view change |
| **Partial rejection (branch C), `k=1`, leader** | B₁ accepted, B₂ rejected; `current_view = h+1`; lock `= B₁`; leader for `h+1`; `!proposed_in_view`; **`C[0:16] = P_{h+1}`** | leader key `= B₁` — **populated** (forged `2f+1`) | **`Ok(Some(qc))`** | **`advance_view` (h+1→h+2)**; no lock change; no commit |
| **Partial rejection (branch C), `k≥2`, leader** | B₁…B_k accepted, B_{k+1} rejected; `current_view = h+1`; lock `= B_k`; leader for `h+1`; `!proposed_in_view`; **`C[0:16] = P_{h+k}`** | leader key `P_{h+1}‖P_{h+k} = B₁` — **populated** | **`Ok(Some(qc))`** | **`advance_view` (h+1→h+2)**; no lock change; no commit |
| **Any branch, collision condition FALSE** (`C[0:16] ≠ P_{h+k}`) | lock `= B_k`; leader for `h+1`; `!proposed_in_view` | leader key `P_{h+1}‖P_{h+k} ≠ B₁` — **fresh** | `Ok(None)` | no `advance_view`; nothing |
| **Leader already proposed this view** (`proposed_in_view = true`) | e.g. victim self-proposed at `h+1` before catch-up | — | n/a (early return :2233) | `on_leader_step` returns `Vec::new()`; **no self-vote at all** |
| **Local vote new vs duplicate** at the collision key | `local_id ∉` vs `∈` forged `qc_signers` | `≥ 2f+1` either way | `Ok(Some(qc))` either way | `advance_view` either way (dedup does not change the quorum already present) |
| **Local vote suppressed (equivocation)** | victim previously voted at `h+1` for a **different** id than the leader's current proposal | prior id's entry unaffected; the new id's entry per above | `record_vote_history` → `Equivocation` → `Ok(None)` for the *new* vote (state:959–966) | the leader's self-vote at the **new** id is suppressed → no QC *from the self-vote*; but if the new id collides with a pre-forged entry, `maybe_qc_for` is **not reached** for a suppressed vote (on_vote returns early at :966) ⇒ no `advance_view` on that path |

The commit column is uniformly **no** (no case yields a self-vote-driven commit); the **view** column is **yes** precisely in the collision cases (`C[0:16] = P_{h+k}`), each conditional on the anchor-form premise. These are the available local cases for CONS-3's fresh-restore-derived scope; the broader non-fresh quantifier (pre-existing unrelated lock / pre-accumulated non-catch-up votes / repeated partial batches) remains the SR-PARTIAL residual (§26.2b conclusion).

### 26.2d Retained-lock + repeated-batch cases, effective-count predicate, field-binding repair (A19.8 opened; A19.9 corrected; the two named obligations are RESOLVED in §26.2e, A19.10)

A19.7 preserved the distinction that a QC-result return can advance the view independently of commit; **A19.8 opened** the two remaining local states (retained lock, repeated batches) and the vote-producer enumeration, but **over-claimed on three load-bearing points that A19.9 repairs from pinned source**: (1) it substituted the opaque lock block-id prefix `B_pre[0:16]` with `P_{v_L}` (an unenforced field binding); (2) it mis-stated an arithmetic exclusion (`v_L=h+m` actually permits `current_view>v_L`); (3) it reduced the self-vote QC condition to "iff the key already holds a catch-up-forged `2f+1`," collapsing the distinct **effective-count** cases. With these corrected, the leader self-vote's local trace is **not** exhausted — a named reachability sub-case remains — so **OBL-CONS-3's available-local reasoning stays SR-PARTIAL** (A19.8's move to SR-DONE is withdrawn).

**Vote-producer inventory (pinned — preserved from A19.8).** Every write to the vote accumulator goes through `state.on_vote`; it has exactly **four** callers at `ef99e29` (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs):
> :2194 `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` → `on_vote(*signer, block.view, &block.block_id)` — **catch-up forged signers, PRODUCTION-reachable** [A17-F1]
> :2332 `on_leader_step` → `on_vote(self.local_id, view, &block_id)` — **leader self-vote, PRODUCTION-reachable** (one voter)
> :2911 `ingest_proposal` → `on_vote(self.local_id, view, &block_id)` — reached only via `on_proposal_event` (inbound proposal) → **Required-rejected (binary:6090-6104), LATENT**
> :2983 `on_vote_event` → `on_vote(from, view, &block_id)` — inbound vote via binary:6584, **Required-rejected before `on_vote_event`** (binary:6546–6562: "missing context under Required … rejection BEFORE engine ingestion, vote aggregation, QC formation … return;")

So in production only **catch-up** and the **leader self-vote** populate the accumulator. But the **inventory is not itself the determining condition** — the condition is the effective voting-power count at the exact key, which splits into distinct cases A19.8's "iff" conflated.

**Effective-count predicate (A19.9 — the determining fact, corrected).** `state.on_vote(voter, view, bid)` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:952–987): after an **equivocation gate** keyed by `(view, voter)` — a voter may back only one `block_id` per view, else the vote is suppressed and returns `Ok(None)` (record_vote_history, state:908–931 / 959–966) — it inserts **one** voter into accumulator key `(view, bid)` via a single `entry.insert(voter)` (vote_accumulator.rs:338–343; the accumulator does **not** replay any signer list — the catch-up caller loops over `qc_signers`, one `on_vote` per signer, basic:2192–2196), then `maybe_qc_for` forms a QC **iff the distinct-signer set `S′` at that key has `acc_vp(S′) ≥ two_thirds_vp`** (vote_accumulator.rs:366–392 → qc.rs:83–114; `two_thirds_vp = ceil(2·total_vp/3)`, validator_set.rs:491–495 — a **voting-power**, not raw-count, threshold). So for a leader self-vote at key `K = (current_view, block_id_self)`, with `S` the distinct set already resident at `K`, `local_id ∉ S`, `local_id` eligible, the call returns `Ok(Some(qc))` **iff `acc_vp(S ∪ {local_id}) ≥ two_thirds_vp`**. This is **not** "`S` already holds a catch-up `2f+1`"; it is four distinct cases:
- **(α) single-node self-quorum (`N=1`):** `total_vp=1 ⇒ two_thirds_vp=ceil(2/3)=1`, so the lone self-vote (`S=∅`) forms a QC **with no catch-up at all** — the `on_leader_step` "(e.g., single node)" case (basic:2360). Benign, but it **falsifies** "iff collides with a catch-up `2f+1`."
- **(β) entry already at quorum (`acc_vp(S) ≥ q`):** the self-vote is redundant; `maybe_qc_for` **re-evaluates** the existing quorum → `Some(qc)` (dedup if `local ∈ S`). [key match + entry already at quorum → re-evaluation]
- **(γ) invocation completing quorum (`acc_vp(S) = q − acc_vp(local)`, `local ∉ S`, eligible):** the self-vote **itself completes** quorum (unit weight: `|S| = q−1` non-local). A19.8's "iff already holds `2f+1`" **omitted this path**. [key match + invocation completing quorum]
- **(δ) below threshold → `Ok(None)`.**

**Reachability of (γ) with `q ≥ 2` — retained as a named obligation, NOT excluded.** Catch-up admits a block only after `qc.validate(qc_signers)` passes (`acc_vp(qc_signers) ≥ q`, basic:2183) and then replays **all** its signers, so one catch-up block delivers `acc_vp ≥ q` to **its own** key `(h+j, B_j)` — never exactly `q−1` — **unless** the engine's equivocation gate drops some of those signers at a key where they already voted for a different `block_id` that view (state:959–966), which can leave the key below the listed power. Whether suppression across **repeated/overlapping catch-up batches** can drive a **leader self-vote key** to exactly `q−1` non-local power with `local` still eligible (so the self-vote completes quorum by path γ rather than merely re-evaluating an existing one) is an **intricate multi-batch reachability question, not a one-line invariant**. A19.9 **does not assert either its reachability or its exclusion** (per the task constraint); it is **retained as a local source obligation** on OBL-CONS-3. This open γ-edge — together with the field-binding and consequence corrections below — is why CONS-3's available-local reasoning is **not** complete.

**Case 1 — a pre-existing lock that catch-up does not replace (field binding repaired, A19.9).**
- **Producer / admission (pinned, not invented):** the retained lock `L_pre = tc.high_qc` (block `B_pre`, view `v_L`) is installed by **`on_timeout_certificate`** (basic:3259–3281, **A1-F3**): `tc.validate(...)` then, when `tc.view > current_view` and `tc_high_qc.view > locked.view`, `self.state.set_locked_qc(tc_high_qc.clone())`. **Field facts (decisive):** `TimeoutCertificate::validate` checks only the TC's **own `signers`** (membership / distinct / quorum voting power, timeout.rs:358–388) — it **never validates `high_qc`** and enforces **no** relationship between `high_qc.view` and `high_qc.block_id` (the high_qc is carried verbatim, timeout.rs:231–238); `on_timeout_certificate` performs **no** check on `tc_high_qc`; and `set_locked_qc` is just `self.locked_qc = Some(qc)` (state:1144–1146) — it **registers no block node**. So the lock is `{view: v_L, block_id: B_pre, signers}` with **`B_pre` an opaque, attacker-chosen 32-byte value whose prefix `B_pre[0:16]` is NOT bound to `v_L`.**
- **Non-replacement by catch-up:** catch-up's per-block `on_qc` replaces the lock only if `qc.view(=h+i) > locked.view(=v_L)` (state:997–1000); if **`v_L ≥ h+m`** the lock stays `L_pre` through the whole batch.
- **Field-binding repair (withdraws the A19.8 substitution).** `on_leader_step` takes `parent = locked_qc().block_id` when the lock is `Some` (basic:2244–2250), so the subsequent leader key is `D(local_id, current_view, B_pre)`. By `D` = `encode(proposer)‖encode(view)‖parent[0:16]` (basic:2043–2058) this is `P_{current_view} ‖ B_pre[0:16]`. A19.8 continued "`= P_{current_view} ‖ P_{v_L}`"; the **second equality is withdrawn** — `B_pre[0:16] = P_{v_L}` would require `B_pre = D(leader_for_view(v_L), v_L, ·)`, but nothing binds the opaque lock block-id to `v_L` (above). **`B_pre[0:16]` is retained symbolically.**
- **Collision condition (re-derived without `P_{v_L}`).** The key collides with an admitted catch-up block `B_j = P_{h+j}‖P_{h+j−1}` (view `h+j`, id checked at basic:2169–2179) **iff** `current_view = h+j` (first-16 match) **and** `B_pre[0:16] = P_{h+j−1}` (second-16 match). The second is a **16-byte equality on the attacker's opaque lock prefix** — a degree of freedom in the forged TC, **independent of `v_L`**. Distinguish the **first** suffix block (anchor parent `C` ⇒ second-16 `= C[0:16]`) from an **interior** block (`j≥2`, parent `B_{j−1}` ⇒ second-16 `= P_{h+j−1}`).
- **Arithmetic repair (Error 2).** A19.8 claimed "`current_view = h+m+1 > v_L` is impossible when `v_L ≥ h+m`." **Withdrawn:** `v_L = h+m` makes `current_view = h+m+1 > v_L` **true** (branch A). And the collision does not turn on `v_L` at all (it turns on `B_pre[0:16]`); `v_L` governs only (i) whether catch-up already replaced `L_pre` (needs `v_L ≥ h+m`) and (ii) whether the self-vote QC later **replaces** the lock (below). The A19.8 `v_L = current_view − 1` step conflated the lock **view** with the lock **block-id prefix** and is withdrawn; this inconsistency is **resolved from source/arithmetic**, not reclassified as execution uncertainty.
- **Consequence (Error 4 — no automatic transfer).** If the key is **fresh** (no collision): single voter → `Ok(None)` at `N≥2` (`Ok(Some)` only at `N=1`, case α) → no QC, no `advance_view`, no commit, lock unchanged. If the key **collides** (entry at quorum, case β): `state.on_vote → Ok(Some(qc))` → `on_leader_step` fires `advance_view()` (basic:2360–2372) — a **VIEW advance**. For the **lock**, `on_qc` replaces it **iff `qc.view (= current_view) > locked.view (= v_L)`** (state:997–1000) — so in **branch A** (`current_view = h+m+1 > v_L = h+m`) the self-vote QC **DOES replace** the lock (A19.8's blanket "no lock change" withdrawn); in **branch C** (`current_view = h+1 ≤ v_L`) it does not. For a **commit**, `register_block(block_id_self, current_view, parent = B_pre, …)` (state:731–760) sets the self-block's parent to `B_pre`, and `try_commit` then needs `P = blocks.get(B_pre)` **resident with `own_qc`** and a resident `own_qc`-bearing grandparent, with `g_view < p_view < b_view` and the strict height floor (state:1047–1137). Since `set_locked_qc` registered **no node** for `B_pre`, `B_pre` is **non-resident unless independently registered** (prior catch-up/proposal) ⇒ `P = None` ⇒ `try_commit` **early-returns (no commit)** — a **different mechanism** from the fresh-restore self-parent-loop of §26.2c (where the overwrite made the block its own parent, failing strict increase). **The earlier self-parent/non-increasing-view no-commit result does NOT transfer** to this independently-specified block id. **Exact unresolved condition:** if `B_pre` *is* resident with a resident `own_qc`-bearing grandparent and strictly-increasing views above the committed floor, this trace does **not** exclude a commit of `B_pre`'s grandparent; whether such a resident chain is reachable for an attacker-opaque `B_pre` is **not established here** (depends on A1-F3 lock provenance + prior block-tree state → EXEC(E03)/upstream), and is part of why CONS-3 stays SR-PARTIAL.

**Case 2 — repeated partial catch-up batches.**
- **Second response anchor-equality vs the ACTUAL current tip:** each `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` re-derives `expected_height = committed_height().saturating_add(1)` and `expected_parent = committed_block()` (basic:2130–2137). After batch 1 (branch C, `k` accepted, first commit at `B₃`), `committed_block = B_{k−2}` (for `k≥3`) at height `h+k−2`; so batch 2's first block must have `parent = B_{k−2}`, `height = view = h+k−1` (:2141/2147/2155). It anchors on the **batch-1-advanced** tip, not the original `C`.
- **Surviving state:** map entries `B₁…B_k` (with `own_qc`), accumulator entries `(h+i, B_i)` with the forged signers, vote-history records, lock `= B_k` (or `L_pre`), `committed_height = h+k−2`, and `proposed_/voted_in_view` **persist** (catch-up touches none of the view flags).
- **Re-registration of an existing key:** if batch 2 re-sends `B_{k−1}` (same `(proposer,view,parent)` ⇒ same id), `register_block` **overwrites** that node (`insert_block_node` :568; `own_qc` reset — `BlockNode::new` carries no `own_qc`) and the per-signer `on_vote` loop replays the forged signers into the **existing** `(h+k−1, B_{k−1})` entry → each insert **dedups** (`entry.insert`→false, the distinct set `S` already present) ⇒ **`acc_vp(S)` unchanged**; `maybe_qc_for` **re-evaluates** and still returns `Some(qc)` (case β, entry already at quorum) → `on_qc` re-attaches `own_qc`, **no lock replacement** (`qc.view = h+k−1 ≤ locked.view`). Equivocation suppression applies only if a signer is replayed at `(h+k−1)` for a **different** id (then that vote returns `Ok(None)`, state:959–966); capacity drop only past `max_votes_per_view=256`.
- **Commit vs view — traced to separate callers (not merely "named A17-F1").** A commit during repeated batches arises inside `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` itself: for each extending block it calls `state.on_vote(signer, …)` per forged signer (basic:2192–2196), and once a key reaches quorum that **same `on_vote`** runs `on_qc → try_commit_with_qc` on the forged 3-chain (state:981–983 → 1029–1137). This is the **catch-up caller's** `on_vote` (basic:2194), a distinct call site and distinct key from the **leader's** self-vote `on_vote` (basic:2332); the two are separated **by their callers and keys in source**, not by invoking the label "A17-F1." The leader step **after** batch 2 is then evaluated on its own key by the effective-count predicate above → `advance_view` iff that key is at/completing quorum, else nothing. **"Pre-accumulated non-catch-up votes" have no production producer** other than prior leader self-votes (one voter each, `local_id`), so they never add a second distinct voter toward a non-local quorum (dedup); the inbound producers (:2911/:2983) are Required-rejected.
