**CONS-3 local-source result (A19.9 snapshot — SR-PARTIAL with two named open branches; A19.10 RESOLVES both in §26.2e → SR-DONE available local source · EXEC(E03)).** As of A19.9 the vote-producer inventory was complete and the fresh-restore/single-node commit-and-view outcomes established, but two local branches were open: (i) the **completing-quorum (γ)** reachability and (ii) the **retained-lock collision** commit sub-case. **A19.10 (§26.2e) settles both from pinned source** — (i) by an **invariant excluding γ** at any leader self-vote key (the capacity refusal + unique-id-per-view), and (ii) by a **complete-predicate no-commit trace** for the retained lock (non-resident `B_pre`, or grandparent `G` already committed / below the strict height floor) — plus the TC-admission posture precision (item 4). With no remaining locally-available source branch, **OBL-CONS-3's available-local source review is complete (SR-DONE, derived)**; the view-advance on a collision remains an **established conditional transition** (preserved, not generalized), and the only residuals are **upstream** (anchor-form `C[0:16]=P_{h+k}` → OBL-STO-1b/T-A18-2; A1-F3 TC-prefix provenance, an in-tree surface whose deployment posture is EXEC) and **execution** (E03). No full HotStuff safety proof is required, and none is claimed.

### 26.2e Resolution of the two named CONS-3 obligations — formal transition arguments (A19.10) — ⚠️ SUPERSEDED BY §26.2f (A19.11): four load-bearing defects (circular uniqueness proof, false node-invariance implication, cursor≠committed_height, anchor-residency) invalidate this section's SR-DONE derivation; retained below as the dated A19.10 record

A19.9 left OBL-CONS-3 SR-PARTIAL with exactly two named open local branches. A19.10 resolves both from the pinned baseline `ef99e29`, in formal state-transition terms, and reconciles the joint collision/lock-transition conditions (item 1) and the TC-admission precision (item 4). Reachability of no proposed state is assumed — each production precondition is traced.

**Preliminary — the complete joint collision + leader-eligibility condition (item 1, pinned).** The leader self-vote key is `K = (current_view, bid_self)` with `bid_self = D(local_id, current_view, parent)`, `parent = locked_qc().block_id` if the lock is `Some` else `committed_block()` (basic:2244–2250), and `D(p,v,par) = encode(p)‖encode(v)‖par[0:16]` (basic:2043–2058). A catch-up block admitted at view `v` has `block_id = D(leader_for_view(v), v, expected_parent)` with `expected_parent` the running chain parent (anchor `C` for the first suffix block, `B_{j−1}` for interior `j≥2`; basic:2141–2179). Therefore `K` coincides with a catch-up entry **iff ALL of**:
- **view equality** `current_view = h+j` for some admitted suffix block `j` — and `current_view` equals a *processed* view only when the batch **partially rejected** (the post-loop `set_view(expected_height)` runs **only on full success**, basic:2207–2209; a rejected block returns `Err` earlier and leaves `current_view` unchanged). After **successful** catch-up `current_view = h+m+1`, **outside** `[h+1, h+m]`, so **no entry from that batch** sits at `K` (confirms item 1);
- **leader eligibility** `leader_for_view(current_view) = local_id` and `!proposed_in_view` (basic:2229–2235) — else `on_leader_step` returns early, no self-vote;
- **prefix equality** `bid_self[16:32] = B_j[16:32]`, i.e. **first suffix block** `current_view=h+1 ∧ B_pre[0:16] = C[0:16]`; **interior** `current_view=h+j ∧ B_pre[0:16] = P_{h+j−1}` (where `parent = B_pre` for the retained lock). A **prefix equality alone is insufficient** — the view and leader-eligibility conjuncts are required, and the exact retained entry `(current_view, bid_self)` must already hold the forged `2f+1`.

---

**Obligation A — can a leader invocation encounter `q−1` effective non-local contributions while the local voter remains eligible (the completing-quorum γ path)?**

*Decisive pinned source.* The engine `on_vote` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:952–987):
> `match self.record_vote_history(voter, view, block_id) { Equivocation { .. } => { … return Ok(None); } FirstVote | DuplicateSameBlock => {} }` (state:958–971) — equivocation is keyed by `(view, voter)` (state:908–931): a voter already recorded at `view` for a **different** `block_id` is suppressed **before** QC evaluation.
> `let _is_new = self.votes.on_vote(&self.validators, voter, view, block_id)?;` (state:974) then **unconditionally** `let qc = self.votes.maybe_qc_for(&self.validators, view, block_id)?;` (state:979).

The accumulator `on_vote` (vote_accumulator.rs:307–343) inserts **exactly one** voter and enforces the per-key cap:
> `if let Some(existing_votes) = self.entries.get(&key) { if existing_votes.len() >= self.limits.max_votes_per_view { if existing_votes.contains(&voter) { return Ok(false); } self.dropped_votes += 1; return Ok(false); } }` (:328–337) — **capacity refusal**; then `Ok(entry.insert(voter))` (:342).

`maybe_qc_for` forms a QC iff the distinct signer set meets the **voting-power** threshold:
> `let qc = QuorumCertificate::new(block_id.clone(), view, ids); match qc.validate(validators) { Ok(()) => Ok(Some(qc)), Err(InsufficientQuorum{..}) => Ok(None), Err(e) => Err(e) }` (:377–392) → `acc_vp = Σ voting_power(signers); if acc_vp < two_thirds_vp() { Err(InsufficientQuorum) }` (qc.rs:96–110); `two_thirds_vp = ceil(2·total/3)` (validator_set.rs:491–495).

Catch-up admission requires the forged QC itself to meet quorum before any replay:
> `let qc = QuorumCertificate::new(block.block_id, block.view, block.qc_signers.clone()); qc.validate(self.validators()).map_err(RestoreCatchupError::InvalidQc)?;` then `for signer in &block.qc_signers { self.state.on_vote(*signer, block.view, &block.block_id) … }` (basic:2183–2196) — so an admitted block contributes a signer set of `acc_vp ≥ q` to **its own** key.

*Transition argument (invariant I, excluding γ).* Let `w_local` be the local voting power, `q = two_thirds_vp`, `cap = max_votes_per_view = 256`. Define the **leader self-vote key** `K = (cv, bid_self)`.

1. **Unique id per view.** A catch-up block at view `v` has `block_id = D(leader(v), v, expected_parent)`, and `expected_parent` is the deterministic running chain anchored at the per-height-immutable `committed_block` (`committed_height` is strictly monotone via the `g_height > committed_height` floor, state:1097–1100; `committed_block` at each height is set once). Hence **at most one** catch-up `block_id` is ever admitted at a given view, across all batches (repeated/overlapping batches re-derive the identical id). *Consequence:* a signer recorded at `(v, id_v)` can never have an earlier `(v, ·)` record for a **different** id via catch-up, so **no equivocation suppression ever prunes a catch-up key** `(v, id_v)`; its effective set is the full union of replayed `qc_signers`, hence `acc_vp ≥ q` (subject only to the cap, below).
2. **Catch-up keys are never in `(0, q)` in a way the leader self-vote can complete.** For `q ≤ cap`: a catch-up key holds `acc_vp ∈ {0} ∪ [q, W_total]`. For `q > cap`: the key saturates at `cap < q` and **every further vote is capacity-refused** (:328–337) — including a would-be completing leader self-vote, which returns `Ok(false)` and leaves the set at `cap`, so `maybe_qc_for` still yields `acc_vp = cap < q ⇒ Ok(None)`.
3. **The leader self-vote key specifically.** `K = (cv, bid_self)` is populated by catch-up **only** by a block whose id `= bid_self`, i.e. `leader(cv)=local` and the prefix equality above — a **collision**. Such a block shares `bid_self`, so the leader's own later self-vote at `K` is `DuplicateSameBlock`/`FirstVote` (no self-pruning), and `K` already holds `acc_vp ≥ q` (β) — **not** `q−1`. If **no** catch-up block has id `bid_self`, `K` holds only the local self-vote `{local}`, `acc_vp = w_local` (`< q` for `N ≥ 2`; `= q` only at `N=1`, case α). A catch-up key `(v, id_v)` with `id_v ≠ bid_self` can be left at `q−1` (e.g. local pruned there), **but that key is not the leader self-vote key and no production producer casts the completing vote into it** (the leader self-votes only at `bid_self`; inbound producers are Required-rejected).
4. **Retention operations preserve the invariant.** Eviction removes **whole** keys (`entries.retain(|k,_| k.view != oldest)`, vote_accumulator:294–305) → `acc_vp = 0`, never `q−1`. `remove_entry` likewise clears a key. Capacity refusal only blocks growth (never reduces a key below `q` once reached, and refuses the completing vote when `q > cap`).

*Preservation across the two production producers.* (catch-up) delivers `{0}∪[q,·]` to its own unique-per-view key, never prunable to `(0,q)` by equivocation; (leader self-vote) delivers `{local}` to `bid_self`. No composition yields a leader self-vote key at exactly `q−1` with the local vote still able to complete it. In the **weighted library** the same holds: the completing band `W(S) < q ≤ W(S) + w_local` requires `0 < W(S) < q` at the self-vote key, which (1)–(3) exclude (a catch-up key is `{0}∪[q,·]` or capacity-saturated-and-refusing); equality `W(S)=q−w_local` is **not** assumed. No arbitrary-weight audit is performed or needed.

*Conclusion (Obligation A — RESOLVED, γ excluded).* A leader self-vote returns `Ok(Some(qc))` **iff (α)** `N=1` (`q=w_local`, self-vote alone) **or (β)** its key collides with a catch-up key already at `acc_vp ≥ q`. The **completing-quorum (γ)** transition is **unreachable** at any leader self-vote key through the enumerated production producers and retention operations. This is an **invariant exclusion** (option b of the obligation), not an inference from `q−1+w_local=q`.

---

**Obligation B — does the retained-lock leader block produce a new commit (the resident-parent commit obligation)?**

*Exact question.* With the retained lock `L_pre` (`v_L ≥ h+m`), the leader registers `B = bid_self` at view `cv`, parent `= B_pre`. Define `P = B_pre` (B's parent) and `G = B_pre`'s parent — **the committed node is `G`, the leader block's grandparent, equivalently `B_pre`'s parent** (correcting the earlier "`B_pre`'s grandparent" wording). Does `try_commit_with_qc` commit `G`?

*Decisive pinned source.* `register_block` (state:731–760) sets `B.parent_id = Some(B_pre)` and `own_qc = None` (own_qc is attached only by `on_qc`). `set_locked_qc` (state:1144–1146) is `self.locked_qc = Some(qc)` — it creates **no** node, but this says nothing about whether `B_pre` already exists from another producer. `try_commit_with_qc` (state:1029–1137):
> `let b_view = match self.blocks.get(&qc.block_id) { Some(node) => { if node.own_qc.is_none() { return; } node.view } None => return };` (:1047–1060)
> `P = blocks.get(b.parent_id)`; `if p.own_qc.is_none() { return }` (:1063–1083) — **P must be resident with own_qc**;
> `G = blocks.get(p.parent_id)`; `if g.own_qc.is_none() { return }` (:1086–1104) — **G must be resident with own_qc**;
> `if !(g_view < p_view && p_view < b_view) { return; }` (:1107–1109); `height_ok = committed_height.is_none() ∨ g_height > committed_height` (:1112–1115, **strict** floor); `should_commit` three-way (:1117–1133).

*Transition argument.* For `B` to reach `try_commit`, `on_qc` must run, which requires a QC at `K=(cv,bid_self)` — by Obligation A this needs **(α)** `N=1` or **(β)** a collision, i.e. a catch-up block at `(cv, bid_self)`. In the `N≥2` forged scenario (β):
- The collision block at view `cv` was admitted with `expected_height = cv`, which required `committed_height = cv−1` at that point of the loop; after the batch, `committed_height = max(anchor_h, cv−2)` (the 3-chain commits lag the tip by 2) — in all cases `committed_height ≥ cv−2`.
- **Case (i): `B_pre` non-resident** (the generic case — the opaque TC block-id is not a registered block). `P = blocks.get(B_pre) = None ⇒ try_commit returns at :1065 ⇒ NO commit.`
- **Case (ii): `B_pre` resident with `own_qc`.** By Invariant I, `own_qc` at `(B_pre.view, B_pre)` requires a catch-up quorum there ⇒ `B_pre` is itself an admitted catch-up block at view `w = p_view`, and strict increase needs `w = p_view < b_view = cv`, so `w ≤ cv−1`. Then `G = B_pre`'s parent at height `w−1 ≤ cv−2 ≤ committed_height` ⇒ `height_ok = (g_height = w−1 > committed_height)` is **FALSE** ⇒ `try_commit` does not commit `G`. (Sub-case `w = h+1`: `G = C`, the restore anchor, which is **not** registered ⇒ `G = blocks.get(C) = None ⇒` return at :1090 ⇒ no commit.)

In both cases the retained-lock leader self-vote produces **no new commit**. Any commit present in the trace is the catch-up **A17-F1** 3-chain, driven by the catch-up caller's own `on_vote → on_qc → try_commit` (basic:2194 → state:981–983 → 1029), a **separate caller and key** from the leader self-vote (basic:2332) — their independence is **traced to distinct call sites and keys**, not asserted by naming.

*Lock transition (item 1, corrected).* `on_qc` replaces the lock iff a QC is formed, execution reaches `on_qc`, **and** `qc.view > locked.view` (state:997–1000). For the retained lock a collision requires `cv ∈ [h+1, h+m]` (partial-rejection) and `v_L ≥ h+m`, so `qc.view = cv ≤ h+m ≤ v_L ⇒` **no replacement**. The A19.9 claim "branch A DOES replace the lock" is **withdrawn**: branch A (successful catch-up) has `current_view = h+m+1` outside the processed interval ⇒ no collision ⇒ **no QC** ⇒ `on_qc` is never reached ⇒ no replacement. The three premises (QC formed; `on_qc` reached; `qc.view > v_L`) never hold jointly for the retained lock.

*Conclusion (Obligation B — RESOLVED).* For `N ≥ 2`, the retained-lock leader self-vote: forms a QC only on a collision (β), **does not replace the lock** (`qc.view ≤ v_L`), **produces no new commit** (P non-resident, or `G` already committed / below the strict height floor), and **advances the view** (`advance_view`, the established conditional transition). The `N=1` configuration is **normal single-node consensus** (self-votes form QCs and commit the node's **own** resident chain); the no-commit result is confined to the `N≥2` forged-collision scenario and is **not** extended to all single-validator executions — "one node's local trace in an `N≥2` set" ≠ the `N=1` configuration.

---

**TC-admission precision (item 4).** `B_pre` remains **symbolic** — no enforced view-to-ID binding exists — but its *availability* is posture-gated, and both postures are in-tree **source** questions (not EXEC):
- **`verification_ctx = None`:** the inbound `NewView(TC)` handler runs the binding-gate origin admission (fail-closed only if a gate is installed; "legacy behavior" when none) and then calls `engine.on_timeout_certificate(&tc)` **unconditionally**, with **no** cryptographic/high-QC check (binary:6931–6936 the `if let Some(ctx)…` guard is skipped) — so `tc.high_qc` (hence `B_pre`) is constrained only by the TC's logical `tc.validate` (its own signer quorum), **not** its block-id. This is the A1-F1 fail-open posture.
- **`verification_ctx = Some`:** `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` runs before ingestion and requires `tc.high_qc == select_max_high_qc(verified signed-timeout evidence)` (`HighQcMismatch` else, timeout_verify.rs:419–422). This binds `B_pre` to a **signed, self-reported** high_qc carried by some timeout-signer with the max view — but **does not independently endorse that high_qc's own quorum** (it matches a signed self-report, exactly the A1-F3 core). So `B_pre` is still attacker-influenceable under a single malicious/colluding timeout-signer supplying the max-view high_qc; there is **no** structural view-to-ID constraint in either posture.

So the field-binding repair (R1, §26.2d) stands in both postures; the *availability* of a specific `B_pre[0:16] = C[0:16]` is an **in-tree admission source question** on the A1-F3 surface (kept as a source obligation, **not** moved to EXEC), while the deployment posture + validator-collusion reachability is **EXEC(E03)**, and the anchor form `C[0:16]` is the separate **OBL-STO-1b/T-A18-2** anchor-acceptance work (not begun).

**Bounded completion (A19.10) — ⚠️ WITHDRAWN BY A19.11 (§26.2f).** A19.10 concluded both named obligations were resolved (γ by an exclusion invariant; the retained-lock commit by a no-commit trace) and moved OBL-CONS-3 to SR-DONE. **A19.11 (§26.2f) found this derivation rests on four defects** — the γ-exclusion invariant's uniqueness lemma is **circular** with the no-leader-commit claim; the retained-lock proof used a **false** "resident ⟹ unchanged catch-up node" implication, a **wrong** cursor-vs-`committed_height` identity, and a **wrong** "anchor non-resident" step (the anchor is resident with `own_qc=None`). Both obligations reduce to a **coupled lineage invariant J** not discharged here, so **OBL-CONS-3 is SR-PARTIAL**, not SR-DONE. The conditional **view-advance** and the **illustrated** no-commit sub-cases (D-eq self-parent; anchor-as-`G`; non-resident `B_pre`) survive as established; the general retained-lock commit and per-view uniqueness/γ remain the open edge. See §26.2f. *[A19.10 text retained above as the dated, superseded record.]*

### 26.2f A19.11 — repair of the §26.2e invariant/commit proofs; the two obligations are NOT discharged (coupled lineage invariant); OBL-CONS-3 → SR-PARTIAL

A19.11 verified §26.2e's two proofs against pinned source and found **four load-bearing defects** that invalidate its SR-DONE derivation. The defects are repaired below; the solid partial results are stated; and the residual is named precisely. Because the two obligations reduce to a **coupled invariant that §26.2e established only circularly**, A19.11 **withdraws the SR-DONE conclusion** and returns **OBL-CONS-3 → SR-PARTIAL** with the open edge named. State quantities are tracked **independently** (item 1): wire `block.height`/`block.view`; `BlockNode.view`/`.height`/`.parent_id`/`.own_qc`; accumulator key `(view, block_id)` + effective signer set; vote-history `votes_by_view[(view, voter)]`; `committed_height`/`committed_block`; `current_view` and the catch-up cursor `expected_height`.

**Defect 1 — "resident QC-bearing node = unchanged catch-up node at height=view" is FALSE (invalidates §26.2e Obligation B step (ii)).** `register_block` (state:731–760) computes `height = blocks.get(parent_id).height + 1` and `insert_block_node` (state:568–577) **overwrites** any existing node for that id. The **D-eq row (§26.2c)** is a concrete counterexample: the leader step registers `B₁` with `parent = B₁` (the lock), so `B₁`'s map entry is **overwritten** — `view` stays `h+1` (the passed `current_view`) but `height` becomes `(old h+1)+1 = h+2`, `parent_id = B₁` (self), `own_qc` reset then reattached by the collision QC. So a resident `own_qc`-bearing node can be a **leader-overwritten self-parent node**, not necessarily a catch-up node at `height=view`. §26.2e's inference "`B_pre` resident with `own_qc` ⟹ it is an admitted catch-up block at view `w` with its catch-up-forced parent" is **withdrawn**. (This does **not** establish a new commit — the D-eq self-parent still fails strict-increase, §26.2c — but it invalidates the unrestricted implication.)

**Defect 2 — "unique admitted catch-up id per view" was asserted, not proven, and the proof is CIRCULAR (invalidates §26.2e Invariant I).** Deterministic `D` (basic:2043–2058) gives identical output for identical input, but that does **not** prove `expected_parent` has the same prefix across every admissible history. The connection §26.2e needed is an invariant linking: `committed_block`'s immutability-per-height, the block-id prefix, the current map-entry view/height, and the registration/replacement history. §26.2e argued "`committed_block` at each height is immutable and on the deterministic chain" — but `committed_block` is set by `try_commit`, which **could** be driven by a leader self-vote commit (Obligation B), so the uniqueness proof **assumes no leader-driven off-chain commit**, while §26.2e's no-leader-commit proof (Obligation B) **assumes uniqueness**. This is the exact **circularity** the review flagged. Strictly-increasing `committed_height` (state:1112–1115) does **not** by itself connect the prefix/lineage. *Per the review:* incompleteness of the uniqueness proof does **not** imply multiple ids are reachable — it leaves uniqueness **open**, to be settled only by a **joint induction** over the consensus-loop handlers (catch-up admit/commit, leader register/self-vote/commit, TC install, retention), not carried out in this bounded pass.

**Defect 3 — the catch-up cursor is not `committed_height` (invalidates §26.2e Obligation B's "`committed_height ≥ cv−2`").** The cursor `expected_height` is a **local counter**: initialized `committed_height().saturating_add(1)` once (basic:2130–2133) and incremented `expected_height.saturating_add(1)` **per block** (basic:2201), independent of `committed_height`, which advances separately via intermediate `on_qc → try_commit` **inside** the per-signer `state.on_vote` loop. So an **interior block at view `cv` can be admitted while earlier blocks have not produced a commit** — `expected_height = cv` means `cv − (batch-start committed_height)` blocks were processed, **not** that `committed_height = cv−1`. §26.2e's "`expected_height=cv required committed_height=cv−1`" and the derived "`committed_height ≥ cv−2`" are **withdrawn**; the floor relationship must be established per-case from the actual intermediate QC/commit predicates, not assumed.

**Defect 4 — the restore anchor IS resident (invalidates §26.2e's "G = anchor non-resident").** `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` (state:1254–1283) **inserts** the anchor node: `BlockNode::new(committed_block_id, committed_view, parent_id=None, justify_qc=None, committed_height)` with **`own_qc = None`** (insert at :1277). The source comment states it directly: *"own_qc remains None, which means this block can never be the G of a 3-chain (the commit rule requires `g.own_qc.is_some()`), preserving safety."* So the anchor-as-`G` no-commit holds by the **`g.own_qc.is_none()` predicate** (state:1104), **not** by non-residency. (`own_qc = None` at installation ≠ non-resident; a later QC for the anchor's exact `(view, id)` would mutate `own_qc` — but no catch-up block sits at `(committed_view, C)` since the first admitted block is at `committed_height+1`, and a self-vote id `= C` needs `C`'s prefix to encode `(local, committed_view)`, a coincidence — so the qualification is retained, not relied upon.)

---

**Obligation A (completing-quorum γ) — observation boundary fixed; reduced to the uniqueness edge; NOT discharged.**
- *Claim & scope.* At the QC-evaluation point of a **leader** self-vote `state.on_vote(local, cv, bid_self)` (inside `on_leader_step`, basic:2332 — a `do_leader_tick` handler invocation, **run to completion separately** from the catch-up handler, so no mid-catch-up-loop intermediate sub-quorum set is observed here), can the effective set `S_after` at key `K=(cv, bid_self)` be exactly one `local`-contribution short of quorum with `local` eligible?
- *Source.* `record_vote_history` equivocation gate keyed `(view, voter)` (state:908–931, 958–966); accumulator one-voter insert + **capacity refusal** by **signer count** `existing_votes.len() >= max_votes_per_view` (vote_accumulator:328–337, a **count** limit); `maybe_qc_for` → `qc.validate` **voting-power** threshold `acc_vp < two_thirds_vp` (vote_accumulator:366–392, qc.rs:96–110) — **`cap` is a signer-count limit; `q` is a voting-power threshold; these are different units.** Catch-up admission requires `acc_vp(qc_signers) ≥ q` **then** replays signers (basic:2183–2196).
- *Argument (non-circular reduction).* For `local`'s current self-vote to be *inserted* (not suppressed) it must not have a prior `(cv, local)` history entry for a different id (else early suppression → `Ok(None)`, item 3's "other producer" point). Given insertion, `K` completes iff its pre-existing effective set is exactly `q − w_local`. Catch-up cannot deliver a sub-`q` set to `K` **except** by equivocation-suppression of some of an admitted block's `qc_signers` (admission forces `acc_vp(qc_signers) ≥ q`). A **non-local** signer `s` is suppressed at `(cv, bid_self)` only if `s` has a prior `(cv, s)` entry for a **different** id — and the only producer of a non-local vote at view `cv` is **another catch-up block at `cv` with a different id** (self-votes are `local`-only). Therefore **γ-reachability at the leader key ⟺ two distinct admitted catch-up ids exist at a single view** — i.e. **exactly the Defect-2 uniqueness question**. 
- *Conclusion & named edge.* **Unit-weight configuration only** (the verified production scope; `acc_vp` = signer count there, so `cap`/`q` units coincide). The **general weighted extension of §26.2e is withdrawn** (not separately justified; the deferred arbitrary-weight review is out of scope). γ is **neither asserted reachable nor excluded**. **[A19.12 §26.2g correction:** the A19.11 wording "equivalent to the open uniqueness edge" is downgraded — only the **necessity** `γ ⟹ ¬uniqueness` is proven (γ requires a second catch-up id at the view to suppress a non-local signer); the **reverse** `¬uniqueness ⟹ γ` is **not** proven (two ids alone give neither exactly `q−1` at the leader key, nor local eligibility, nor insertion success, nor a matching eligible leader invocation). So γ-**exclusion** would follow from per-view uniqueness (Lemma U), but uniqueness is unproven, and γ-**reachability** is not shown either.**] Remaining named source edge:** the per-view catch-up-id uniqueness invariant (Lemma U, §26.2g).

**Obligation B (retained-lock resident-parent commit) — evaluated at the `try_commit` moment; illustrated cases hold; general case NOT discharged.**
- *Claim & scope.* With retained lock `L_pre` (`v_L ≥ h+m`), the leader registers `B = bid_self` (view `cv`, `parent_id = B_pre`); `P = blocks.get(B_pre)` (B's parent); `G = blocks.get(P.parent_id)` — **the committed node is `G`, the leader block's grandparent = `B_pre`'s parent** (wording corrected). Does a leader self-vote QC on `B` drive a **new** commit of `G`?
- *Source.* `try_commit_with_qc` (state:1029–1137), evaluated on the **map entries as they stand at that moment** (after registration/overwrite/eviction and `own_qc` attachment): `B.own_qc.is_some()` (:1047–1060); `P` resident ∧ `P.own_qc.is_some()` (:1063–1083); `G` resident ∧ `G.own_qc.is_some()` (:1086–1104); `g_view < p_view < b_view=cv` (:1107–1109); `g_height > committed_height` strict floor (:1112–1115); `should_commit` three-way (:1117–1133).
- *Established (non-circular) sub-cases.* **(a)** D-eq self-parent (`parent = B₁`, §26.2c): `P = G = B₁`, `g_view = p_view = b_view = h+1` ⇒ strict-increase fails ⇒ **no commit** (confined to this self-parent / non-increasing-view topology, not generalized). **(b)** `G` = the restore anchor: resident with `own_qc = None` ⇒ `g.own_qc.is_none()` at :1104 ⇒ **no commit** (Defect 4; source-documented). **(c)** `P = B_pre` **non-resident** (the opaque TC lock id was never registered) ⇒ `blocks.get(B_pre) = None` at :1065 ⇒ **no commit**.
- *NOT discharged (general case).* For a **resident, `own_qc`-bearing `B_pre`** with a resident `own_qc`-bearing grandparent at strictly-increasing views above the floor, a new commit of `G` is **not excluded** by any non-circular argument available here: whether such a `(B_pre, G)` chain with `g_height > committed_height` is reachable depends on (i) node-provenance vs accumulator-quorum-origin (Defect 1 — `B_pre` may be leader-overwritten), and (ii) the `committed_height`-vs-chain relationship (Defect 3 — the cursor does not pin `committed_height`), both of which reduce to the **same coupled lineage invariant** as Obligation A. §26.2e's blanket "no new commit in any `N≥2` case" is **withdrawn**.
- *Lock transition (separate from commit).* Retained-lock collision requires `cv ∈ [h+1, h+m]` (partial-rejection; the guarded `set_view` gives `current_view_after = max(current_view_before, h+m+1)`, basic:2207–2209, so a view inside the interval needs the partial-rejection path *and* the matching initial-view premise) and `v_L ≥ h+m`, so `qc.view = cv ≤ v_L` ⇒ `on_qc` (state:997–1000) **does not replace the lock**. "Branch A replaces the lock" stays **withdrawn** (branch A = successful catch-up ⇒ `current_view = h+m+1` outside the interval ⇒ no collision ⇒ no QC ⇒ `on_qc` unreached). **A retained entry from an EARLIER partial batch** at the resulting view is **not excluded** by the "no batch entry at `h+m+1`" fact alone — it is governed by the same lineage invariant, recorded here rather than omitted. QC formation / lock replacement / commit / caller-driven view-advance are kept as **separate transitions**.

**TC-admission (item 5) — named source obligation, not EXEC.** The `verification_ctx = None` / `Some` distinction is retained (§26.2e item 4): `None` ⇒ no high_qc check before `on_timeout_certificate` (A1-F1 fail-open); `Some` ⇒ `tc.high_qc == select_max_high_qc(signed evidence)` (`HighQcMismatch` else, timeout_verify.rs:419–422) binding to a signed self-report but **not** an independently-endorsed quorum (A1-F3). Whether a production admission configuration yields the collision-enabling `B_pre[0:16]` is an **in-tree source question** assigned to **OBL-CONS-3** (sub-edge: "TC-admission reachability of a lock block-id prefix equal to the anchor/interior prefix under each `verification_ctx` posture") — **not** moved to EXEC merely for being upstream of `on_leader_step`; the deployment **posture** + validator-collusion reachability is the EXEC(E03) tail.

**Named remaining source edge (both obligations).** The **coupled invariant J** = *"(the `committed_block` lineage is a single deterministic `height=view` chain) ∧ (no leader self-vote has produced an off-chain commit)"*. Obligation A's uniqueness/γ-exclusion and Obligation B's general no-commit **both reduce to J**, and J is **not** establishable by a single-direction argument (circular, Defect 2); it requires a **joint induction over the consensus-loop handler invocations** tracking the six state quantities above — explicitly **not performed in A19.11**. Plus the TC-admission posture sub-edge (item 5). These keep **OBL-CONS-3 at SR-PARTIAL**.

**Established in A19.11 (kept, non-circular):** the four defect repairs; the D-eq node-mutation fact; the anchor `own_qc=None` no-`G` mechanism; the leader-invocation observation boundary; the **γ ⟹ ¬uniqueness** reduction; the cursor/`committed_height` decoupling; the unit-weight scoping (weighted extension withdrawn); the conditional view-advance (preserved from A19.7, not generalized); and the lock-non-replacement for the retained-lock collision. **Not established:** per-view uniqueness, the general retained-lock commit predicate, and γ-reachability/exclusion — all reduced to invariant **J**. **No new finding, no closure; A1-F3/A17-F1 dispositions unchanged.** SR-DONE (A19.8, A19.10) is **withdrawn**; OBL-CONS-3 is **SR-PARTIAL**.

### 26.2g A19.12 — corrected γ implication (necessity only) + traced vote-history/accumulator retention; OBL-CONS-3 stays SR-PARTIAL

A19.12 corrects the γ logical claim to a **one-directional necessity**, supplies the contiguous pinned-source retention evidence A19.11 referenced, tabulates the retention transitions, and states the bounded γ result and the smallest missing lemma. It does **not** change CONS-3's status (SR-PARTIAL) or the obligation counts; it makes the γ reasoning sound and inspectable. Obligation B stays open except the two wording corrections in §26.2f (restated below). Scope: the **verified production unit-weight configuration**; the weighted-library review stays deferred.

**(1) Corrected logical implications.** Let `K = (cv, bid_self)` be the leader self-vote key, `q = two_thirds_vp`, `w_local` the local voting power, `S_before` the effective signer set at `K` **immediately before** the leader's completing insertion, `S_after` the set **at the `maybe_qc_for` evaluation** (i.e. after the insertion). γ (completing-quorum) is: `local ∉ S_before`, `local` eligible, the insertion **succeeds**, and `W(S_before) < q ≤ W(S_before) + w_local`.
- **Observation-point correction.** `S_before` is one `local`-contribution short of quorum (unit weight: `|S_before| = q−1` non-local); upon successful completion `S_after = S_before ∪ {local}` **reaches quorum** (`W(S_after) ≥ q`). The A19.11 phrasings that described the set *at QC evaluation* as still `q−1` are corrected: `q−1` is `S_before`, not `S_after`.
- **Necessity (proven), unit-weight:** `γ ⟹ ¬uniqueness` — a non-local signer is absent from a catch-up-admitted `K` (which is admitted only with `W(qc_signers) ≥ q`, basic:2183) only if it was **equivocation-suppressed** at `K` (`record_vote_history` → `Equivocation` → `Ok(None)`, state:958–966); suppression requires a **prior `(cv, that-signer)` history entry for a different id**; the only producer of a *non-local* vote at `cv` is a catch-up block at `cv` (self-votes are `local`-only; inbound Required-rejected), so the different id is a **second admitted catch-up id at `cv`** ⇒ `¬uniqueness`. (For `q ≤ max_votes_per_view = 256` — the unit-weight small-N scope — the capacity-refusal path to `q−1` does not arise, since reaching `cap` needs `len ≥ 256 > q−1`; it is listed as a separate case in the table.)
- **Reverse (NOT proven):** `¬uniqueness ⟹ γ` does **not** hold. Two admitted ids at a view do **not** establish (i) exactly `q−1` effective non-local at `K`, (ii) `local` eligibility (not already a different-id voter at `cv`), (iii) successful insertion within capacity, (iv) the retained accumulator/history state at the leader-invocation instant, or (v) that `K` matches an eligible leader invocation (`leader_for_view(cv)=local ∧ !proposed_in_view`). So A19.11's "equivalent" / "⟺" is **downgraded to the necessity `⟹`**. γ is therefore **neither excluded nor shown reachable** here.

**(2) Contiguous pinned-source retention appendix (`ef99e29`).**
> **vote-history structures** (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:192–207): `votes_by_view: HashMap<(u64, ValidatorId), BlockIdT>` (:192); `votes_by_view_tracked_views: BTreeSet<u64>` (:195); counters `equivocations_detected`, `evicted_votes_by_view_entries` (:207).
> **record_vote_history** (state:897–931): `let key=(view,voter); match self.votes_by_view.get(&key) { None => { self.votes_by_view_tracked_views.insert(view); self.evict_votes_by_view_if_needed(); self.votes_by_view.insert(key, block_id.clone()); FirstVote } Some(prev) => { if prev==block_id { DuplicateSameBlock } else { Equivocation{previous_block: prev.clone()} } } }` — an entry is **written once per `(view,voter)`** and **never overwritten** to a different id (a different id returns `Equivocation` without mutating the stored id).
> **evict_votes_by_view_if_needed** (state:683–694): `while self.votes_by_view.len() >= max_votes_by_view_entries { if let Some(&lowest)=self.votes_by_view_tracked_views.iter().next() { self.votes_by_view.retain(|(v,_),_| *v!=lowest); self.votes_by_view_tracked_views.remove(&lowest); self.evicted_votes_by_view_entries+=1 } else break } }` — whole-**lowest-view** eviction at the **16384-entry** limit (default `max_votes_by_view_entries`).
> **update_validators** (state:333–341): `self.votes = VoteAccumulator::with_limits(limits); self.votes_by_view.clear();` — resets **both** accumulator and vote-history together; sole production caller `transition_to_epoch` (basic:1723, sequential-epoch-gated, reached only on the operator-RECONFIG epoch path §26.3a).
> **accumulator on_vote** (vote_accumulator.rs:307–343): membership `if !validators.contains(voter) { return Err(NonMemberSigner) }`; view tracking + `if self.tracked_views.len() >= max_tracked_views { self.evict_oldest_views() }` (**128-view** default); capacity `if existing.len() >= max_votes_per_view { if existing.contains(&voter) {Ok(false)} else {dropped_votes+=1; Ok(false)} }` (**256-count** refusal); else `Ok(entry.insert(voter))`.
> **evict_oldest_views** (vote_accumulator:264–271): `while self.tracked_views.len() >= max_tracked_views { if let Some(&oldest)=…next() { self.entries.retain(|k,_| k.view!=oldest); self.tracked_views.remove(&oldest); self.evicted_views+=1 } else break }` — whole-oldest-view eviction; **only caller is `on_vote` itself** (:317).
> **maybe_qc_for** (vote_accumulator:366–392): builds `QuorumCertificate::new(block_id, view, ids)` from the key's signer set; `match qc.validate(validators) { Ok(())=>Ok(Some(qc)), Err(InsufficientQuorum{..})=>Ok(None), Err(e)=>Err(e) }`.
> **engine on_vote → on_qc** (state:952–1016): equivocation gate → `self.votes.on_vote(..)?` → `self.votes.maybe_qc_for(..)?` → `if Some(qc) { self.on_qc(qc)? }` → `on_qc` lock-replace (`qc.view > locked.view`) + `node.own_qc=Some` + `try_commit_with_qc`.
> **remove_entry** (vote_accumulator:388–398): per-key removal — **⚠️ A19.12 claim CORRECTED by A19.13 §26.2h-C:** the A19.12 search was scoped to `crates/*/src/*.rs` (which excludes `tests/`) and wrongly read as "no caller / library-only." The full-tree search (`crates/**`) finds **test callers** (`tests/consensus_memory_limits_tests.rs:600,605`; `tests/hotstuff_qc_aggregation_tests.rs:333`) and **no production caller**; positive control `.maybe_qc_for(` confirms the search reaches `tests/`. Corrected claim: **no production (non-test) caller; test-exercised** (not intrinsically unreachable).
> **timeout-accumulator `clear_view`** (basic:3299): clears the **timeout** accumulator on TC admission — does **not** touch the vote accumulator or vote-history.

**(3) Retention-operation table** (effect on: a = vote history `votes_by_view`, b = accumulator `entries`, c = local eligibility at `(cv,local)`, d = QC evaluation/return):

| Operation (production caller) | (a) vote history | (b) accumulator | (c) local eligibility | (d) QC eval / return |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_vote_history` FirstVote (engine `on_vote`) | writes `(view,voter)→id` | — | sets `(cv,local)→id` on a local vote ⇒ future different-id local vote suppressed | proceeds to accumulator insert |
| `record_vote_history` DuplicateSameBlock | unchanged | — | unchanged | proceeds (dedup) |
| `record_vote_history` Equivocation (different id) | **unchanged** (keeps original id) | **not inserted** | n/a | `Ok(None)` — **QC eval skipped** |
| accumulator insert (new) | — | adds voter to `(view,id)` | — | `maybe_qc_for` runs; `Some` iff `W ≥ q` |
| accumulator insert (duplicate) | — | `Ok(false)` | — | `maybe_qc_for` still runs on existing set |
| **capacity refusal** (`len ≥ 256`) | — | voter **not** added | — | `maybe_qc_for` on the capped set (`<q` if cap `<q`) ⇒ `Ok(None)` |
| `evict_oldest_views` (accumulator, inside `on_vote`, `>128` views) | **unchanged** | removes **all** entries for the oldest view | — | that key now empty until replay |
| `evict_votes_by_view_if_needed` (history, inside `record_vote_history`, `≥16384` entries) | removes **all** `(lowest,*)` entries | **unchanged** | eligibility at an evicted view is **forgotten** (next vote is FirstVote) | — |
| `update_validators` (`transition_to_epoch`, epoch change) | **clear()** | **full reset** | all forgotten | fresh |
| `remove_entry` (accumulator) | — | per-key remove | — | — — **unreachable (no caller)** |

**History/accumulator desynchronization (established).** The two evictions use **different structures and thresholds** (accumulator: 128 **views**, inside `on_vote`; history: 16384 **entries**, inside `record_vote_history`) and are **not** jointly maintained except by `update_validators` (which resets both). Therefore: (i) the accumulator can evict a view `v` (128-view pressure) while **history for `(v,·)` survives** (history's 16384-entry limit not hit) — so a later replay at `v` is still **suppressed** per surviving history; and (ii) history can evict `v` (16384-entry pressure) while **accumulator entries for `v` survive** — so a later vote at `v` is **FirstVote** (suppression forgotten) though the accumulator key persists. Both desync directions are reachable in principle; neither is a per-key accumulator removal (that API is uncalled).

**(4) Bounded γ result from the transitions.** Per case (upstream admission reachability kept explicitly conditional where noted):
- **First admitted catch-up block at a view:** delivers `W(qc_signers) ≥ q` to its own key; no suppression (first voter at that `(view,·)`); `K` ends `≥ q` (β), not `q−1`.
- **Prior local vote at `cv` for the same id (`bid_self`):** DuplicateSameBlock; the later self-vote dedups; no completion created.
- **Prior local vote at `cv` for a different id:** the current self-vote at `K` is **Equivocation → `Ok(None)`** — QC eval skipped; **not** a completing path.
- **Repeated same-key replay:** same id ⇒ DuplicateSameBlock, union/dedup; `W` non-decreasing; cannot drop to `q−1`.
- **Conditional different-key replay** (a second id at `cv`, parent-prefix different): **upstream admission reachability is conditional on Lemma U being false** (not established here); *if* admitted, it writes `(cv, s)→id'` history that can suppress `s` at `K` on a later `bid_self` replay ⇒ the only traced route to a `q−1` non-local `K`.
- **Accumulator eviction then replay:** whole-view eviction empties `K`; replay rebuilds it; the rebuilt effective set is `≥q` **unless** surviving history suppresses a signer (same different-id requirement) or capacity refuses (`q>256`). Eviction alone does **not** create `q−1`.
- **History pruning/reset then replay:** pruning forgets suppression ⇒ replay is FirstVote ⇒ `K` rebuilds toward `≥q`, moving **away** from `q−1`. `update_validators` resets both ⇒ fresh.
- **Capacity refusal:** can leave `K` below `q` only when `cap < q` i.e. `q > 256` (outside the unit-weight small-N scope); and it **refuses the completing self-vote** too, so it does not *enable* γ.

**Determination:** the retention mechanics establish the **necessity** `γ ⟹ ¬uniqueness` (every traced route to a `q−1` non-local `K` requires a second admitted catch-up id at `cv`, in the unit-weight `q ≤ 256` scope), **but do not exclude γ** — exclusion needs **Lemma U**. No production-reachable completing *schedule* is exhibited (a local transition example would not by itself be production-reachable), and no failed example is treated as a proof.

**Smallest necessary lemma for γ-exclusion.**
- **Lemma U (per-view catch-up-id uniqueness):** over the whole execution, `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` admits **at most one** distinct `block_id` at any given view. ⟨**A35 — REFUTED**⟩ this admission-sense U is **false**: §26.2u exhibits a bounded counterexample (`B6=P_7‖P_6` and `X=P_7‖P_3` both **admitted/registered** at view 7 across two responses). So the γ-exclusion route "prove U" is **unavailable**; ¬U does **not** establish γ (the relation is one-directional necessity `γ ⟹ ¬U`). The distinct **effective-vote / QC-bearing** per-view uniqueness (only `B6` bore votes/`own_qc`; `X` was equivocation-starved) is **not** refuted by that candidate and is **not** silently substituted for U.
- **Precise missing preservation step:** an admitted block at view `v` has `block_id = D(leader_for_view(v), v, expected_parent_v)` (basic:2161/2169–2179) with `expected_parent_v` the running chain parent anchored at `committed_block()` (basic:2134/2201). Uniqueness fails only if two admissions at `v` see **different** `expected_parent_v` prefixes, which requires `committed_block` (the anchor of the running chain) to have been moved onto a block **off the single catch-up chain** between the two admissions. The missing step is exactly: *"`committed_block` is only ever advanced along the deterministic catch-up chain (no leader-self-vote commit moves it off-chain)."*
- **Owner:** **OBL-CONS-3** (this is the coupled dependency on Obligation B's commit behavior, not an undefined global requirement; Lemma U's missing step is a property of the commit transitions, and Obligation B is itself open).

**Obligation B — two bounded corrections (item 4), otherwise open.**
- **Anchor result (restated precisely):** *"If `G` is resident and `G.own_qc` **remains `None` when `try_commit` evaluates it**, the `own_qc` check (state:1104) rejects the commit."* The previously-withdrawn **lifetime** claim (that the initializer comment guarantees `own_qc` stays `None` forever) is **not** reinstated — `own_qc` is a mutable field (set by `on_qc` on any formed QC for that id), so the result is stated at the evaluation instant only.
- **J as a candidate strategy, not an established equivalence:** "lineage" is defined to mean the **chain of current mutable `blocks` map entries via `parent_id`** reachable from `committed_block` at the instant `try_commit` runs (distinct from the *history of registrations* and from the *set of admitted ids*). The claim "both obligations ⟺ J" is **withdrawn**: Obligation A needs **Lemma U** (about admitted ids per view), Obligation B needs a property of the **current map-entry chain** (residency + `own_qc` + strictly-increasing views + height floor at `B_pre`/`P`/`G`); these are **different domains** linked only through the commit transitions. Also "**no off-chain commit**" alone does **not** prove "**no new leader-driven commit**" — a leader-driven commit could in principle commit an **on-chain** grandparent; the general resident-parent obligation therefore stays **open** and no full consensus induction is undertaken here.

**(5) A19.12 outcome.** γ's implication is corrected to the necessity `γ ⟹ ¬uniqueness` (unit-weight, `q ≤ 256`); the retention mechanics are pinned, tabulated, and shown to permit history/accumulator desync without a per-key accumulator removal; γ is **neither excluded nor shown reachable**; γ-exclusion reduces to **Lemma U** with the precise missing preservation step named and owned by OBL-CONS-3. Obligation B keeps the two wording corrections and stays open. **OBL-CONS-3 remains SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)**; counts unchanged (26 unfinished source; 54 obligations; findings 12/4/22). No new finding, no closure; established conditional transitions (A19.7 view-advance) and superseded history preserved.

301     pub fn on_vote(
302         &mut self,
303         validators: &ConsensusValidatorSet,
304         voter: ValidatorId,
305         view: u64,
306         block_id: &BlockIdT,
307     ) -> Result<bool, QcValidationError> {
308         // Reject non-members early.
309         if !validators.contains(voter) {
310             return Err(QcValidationError::NonMemberSigner(voter));
311         }
312
313         // Handle view tracking and eviction
314         if !self.tracked_views.contains(&view) {
315             // New view - check if we need to evict old views
316             if self.tracked_views.len() >= self.limits.max_tracked_views {
317                 self.evict_oldest_views();
318             }
319             self.tracked_views.insert(view);
320         }
321
322         let key = VoteKey {
323             view,
324             block_id: block_id.clone(),
325         };
326
327         // Check per-view vote limit
328         if let Some(existing_votes) = self.entries.get(&key) {
329             if existing_votes.len() >= self.limits.max_votes_per_view {
330                 // Check if this is a duplicate (already present)
331                 if existing_votes.contains(&voter) {
332                     return Ok(false); // Duplicate, not dropped
333                 }
334                 // Drop the new vote due to limit
335                 self.dropped_votes += 1;
336                 return Ok(false);
337             }
338         }
339
340         let entry = self.entries.entry(key).or_default();
341         // Returns true if the voter was newly inserted, false if already present
342         Ok(entry.insert(voter))
343     }
