**B. Ordering / tracking table (both structures).**

| Question | Accumulator (`on_vote`, vote_accumulator.rs) | Vote-history (`record_vote_history`, hotstuff_state_engine.rs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When does the view enter the tracked set? | **after** eviction, only if the view was **not** already tracked (`:319`, guarded by `:314`) | **before** eviction, only on the `None` (first `(view,voter)`) branch (`:908`) |
| Eviction before or after the tracked-view insert? | **before** (`:316–318` then `:319`) | **after** (`:908` then `:911`) |
| Eviction trigger operator | `len >= max` (`:316`, and the `while len >= max` loop `:265`) — executable condition is `>=`, pre-insert-of-the-new-view; the set is held at ≤ `max_tracked_views` (128) after the insert | `votes_by_view.len() >= max` (`:685`) — `>=` on the entry count, checked after the tracked-view insert but **before** the map-entry insert |
| Runs for an already-tracked view? (**A19.14-corrected**) | **No** — guarded on the **view** (`:314` `!tracked_views.contains(&view)`); any vote at an already-tracked view triggers no accumulator eviction | **Can run** — guarded on the **`(view,voter)` map entry** (`:904`), not the view: a **new voter** at an already-tracked view takes the `None`/FirstVote branch (`:905–914`), so `evict_votes_by_view_if_needed` (`:911`) **can run** at an already-tracked view. Only a repeat of the **same `(view,voter)`** takes the `Some` branch (Duplicate/Equivocation) with no eviction/write. The earlier blanket "does not run for an already-tracked view" is withdrawn |
| Can the currently-processed view be selected for eviction (within this call)? | **No** — the view is inserted (`:319`) **after** `evict_oldest_views` (`:317`), so it is absent from `tracked_views` during eviction | **Yes, possible** — the view is inserted into `votes_by_view_tracked_views` (`:908`) **before** `evict_votes_by_view_if_needed` (`:911`); if it is the **lowest** tracked view and `votes_by_view.len() >= 16384`, `:687–691` can remove it |
| Does the subsequent insert restore tracked-view membership? | n/a (view inserted before the entry; both consistent) | **No** — `:913` inserts only into `votes_by_view` (the `HashMap`), **not** back into `votes_by_view_tracked_views`; so if the current view was just self-evicted at `:911`, the entry exists in `votes_by_view` while the view is **absent** from `votes_by_view_tracked_views` (an **intra-structure desync**) |
| Map entry inserted relative to eviction | after (`:340`, accumulator `entries`) | after (`:913`, `votes_by_view`) |
| Do duplicate / suppressed votes bypass these ops? | capacity branch returns before the entry insert (`:331–337`); a duplicate voter re-insert is a no-op (`:342`) — **but** a history `DuplicateSameBlock` still **reaches** the accumulator (`:968–976`), and if that view was previously whole-view-evicted from the accumulator, the accumulator takes its **new-view** branch (`:314`) and re-inserts the voter — so an accumulator duplicate and a history duplicate are **independent** (A19.14) | Duplicate/Equivocation (`:916–926`) take the `Some` branch → **no** tracked-view insert, **no** eviction, **no** write; Equivocation additionally makes engine `on_vote` return `Ok(None)` at `:966` **before** the accumulator is touched |

Reconciliation of the earlier "≥128 vs >128" wording: the executable condition is **`>=`** (`:316`, `:265`), evaluated on the length **before** the new view is inserted; the accumulator therefore holds **at most 128** tracked views after the insert (when `len == 128`, a new view evicts down to 127 then inserts → 128). The history limit is **`>=` 16384 entries** (`:685`), evaluated after the tracked-view insert and before the map-entry insert.

**C. Corrected `remove_entry` caller claim (A19.12 scope error).** A19.12 wrote "`remove_entry` has no caller (library-only)"; that search was scoped to `crates/*/src/*.rs` and **wrongly excluded `crates/*/tests/`**. A19.13 re-ran `git grep -n "\.remove_entry(" ef99e29 -- 'crates/**'` (full tree, including `tests/`, `benches/`): callers found are **tests only** — `crates/qbind-consensus/tests/consensus_memory_limits_tests.rs:600,605` and `crates/qbind-consensus/tests/hotstuff_qc_aggregation_tests.rs:333`. **Positive control:** the same full-scope search for `.maybe_qc_for(` returns hits in both `src/` (hotstuff_state_engine.rs:979) and `tests/` (consensus_memory_limits_tests.rs, hotstuff_qc_aggregation_tests.rs), confirming the search reaches test directories. **Corrected claim:** `remove_entry` has **no production (non-test) caller** — its only callers are integration tests — so accumulator **per-key** removal does not occur on any production path; this is **"no production caller within the full `crates/**` search scope"**, *not* "intrinsically unreachable" and *not* "no caller." (Accumulator removal on production paths is therefore limited to whole-view `evict_oldest_views` and the `update_validators` full reset.)

**D. Intra-replay composition (catch-up signer loop, `:2192–2196`).** Admission validates `qc_signers` for quorum (`:2183`) then calls engine `on_vote` once per signer (`:2194`); `Err` aborts the whole batch (`?`), while `Ok(None)` (equivocation) and `Ok(Some)` continue. Tracing the effective target-key set:
- **Replay without eviction:** each signer passes the engine equivocation gate (first vote at this `(view, signer)`) and the accumulator insert; the key `(h+j, B_j)` accumulates all `qc_signers` ⇒ `W ≥ q` (β), never `q−1`.
- **Eviction of another (older) view** (accumulator `:317` or history `:911` hitting a lower view): removes that other view's entries; the current key is untouched (current view not the evicted one) ⇒ unchanged.
- **Possible eviction of the currently-processed view:** in the **accumulator** this cannot happen within the call (view inserted after eviction, `:319`); in **history** it can if the current view is the lowest tracked and `len≥16384` (`:687`), producing the intra-structure desync (B) — but this removes the history *entry/membership*, it does **not** place a non-local signer into the accumulator key, so it does not by itself build a `q−1` accumulator set.
- **Replay after accumulator eviction while history survives:** `evict_oldest_views` empties the key (whole-view) ⇒ set = ∅ at that instant; a later replay (same batch processes each view once, so this is a **repeated/different batch**) rebuilds the key; the rebuilt set is `W ≥ q` **unless** a surviving history entry `(h+j, s)→id'` with `id' ≠ B_j` suppresses `s` (which requires a **second admitted id `id'` at view `h+j`**) or capacity refuses (`len ≥ 256`, i.e. `q > 256`, out of scope). Whole-key eviction alone leaves ∅, not `q−1`; the later-call composition reduces to the suppression (second-id) or capacity path.
- **History pruning while accumulator survives:** removes `(h+j, s)→id'` ⇒ on the next replay `s` is a `FirstVote` ⇒ **inserted** ⇒ the accumulator key moves **toward `≥q`**, away from `q−1`.
- **Early suppression:** a signer with a prior `(h+j, s)→id' (id'≠B_j)` history entry → engine `on_vote` returns `Ok(None)` at `:966`, `s` not inserted ⇒ the key can land at `q−1` **iff exactly one** non-local unit is so suppressed; the prior `id'` is a **second admitted id at `h+j`** (= `¬U`).
- **Capacity refusal:** `:329–337` refuses once the key holds 256 signers; relevant only when `q > 256` (outside the unit-weight small-set scope) and it also refuses the completing self-vote, so it does not *enable* γ.

**Determination:** across the full composition, the **only** way the leader self-vote key `(cv, bid_self)` holds exactly `q−1` non-local with `local` eligible (for `2 ≤ q ≤ 256`, `N ≤ 256`) is **equivocation-suppression of one non-local signer**, which requires a **second admitted catch-up id at `cv`** (`¬U`); whole-view eviction gives ∅ (not `q−1`), history pruning moves toward `≥q`, and capacity is out of scope. So the earlier "only suppression can leave a sub-quorum set" is now **resolved through the composition** (not assumed): sub-`q` non-∅ at the leader key ⟹ suppression ⟹ `¬U`.

**E. Leader invocation (separate handler).** The subsequent `on_leader_step` self-vote (`basic:2332`) calls engine `on_vote(local, cv, bid_self)`: `record_vote_history` (history check + possible eviction + insert) → if not Equivocation, accumulator `on_vote` (insert `local`) → `maybe_qc_for`. **Pre-insertion set** `S_before` (effective non-local at the key) and **set at QC evaluation** `S_after = S_before ∪ {local}` are distinct: γ needs `S_before = q−1` (local absent/eligible), and `S_after` **reaches quorum** (`W ≥ q`). If `local` already has a `(cv, local)→id'` (`id'≠bid_self`) entry, the self-vote is Equivocation → `Ok(None)` (not a completing path).

**F. Evidence classification (item 4).** For each divergence direction, distinguished as **(op)** operation-level possibility / **(lim)** a sequence satisfying the configured limits / **(prod)** production-caller reachability:
- *Accumulator evicts a view while history retains it:* **(op)** yes (independent structures); **(lim)** requires `> 128` distinct tracked accumulator views with the shared old view still under the 16384-entry history bound — describable; **(prod)** requires a production schedule tracking `>128` voting views — **premises not established here**; narrowed to the structural fact.
- *History evicts a view while accumulator retains it:* **(op)** yes; **(lim)** requires `≥ 16384` `(view,voter)` entries with ≤128 accumulator views for the shared view — describable (needs large validator sets / many views); **(prod)** **not established**; narrowed to structural fact.
- *Intra-structure history desync (current-view self-eviction, B):* **(op)** yes (`:908` before `:911`, re-insert at `:913` into the map only); **(lim)** requires the current view to be the minimum tracked view at the instant `votes_by_view.len() ≥ 16384`; **(prod)** requires voting at a view below all views spanning 16384 entries — **not established**; recorded as an operation-level structural possibility, **not** a new finding or defect.

**G. Reassessed logical disposition.** After the ordering/composition analysis (D), within unit-weight, `q ≥ 2`, `q ≤ 256`, `N ≤ 256`: **`γ ⟹ ¬U`** is **retained as established** — every route to a `q−1` non-∅ leader-self-vote key requires a second admitted catch-up id at that view (`¬U`); all alternative retention paths (older-view eviction, current-view history self-eviction, whole-view-eviction-then-replay, history-pruning-then-replay, capacity) have been checked and none produce `q−1` without `¬U` in scope. By **contraposition, `U ⟹ ¬γ`**: per-view catch-up-id uniqueness **U** is therefore a **candidate sufficient route** to exclude γ — **not** shown to be a *necessary* or *smallest* requirement (other exclusion routes, e.g. the leader-eligibility or leader-invocation-match conditions failing independently, are not ruled out). **Not claimed:** that `¬U ⟹ γ` (A19.12: the reverse is unproven — two ids give neither `q−1` at the specific key, nor local eligibility, nor insertion success, nor a matching eligible leader invocation), nor that disproving U establishes γ, nor that the intra-structure desync (F) is a defect. **Remaining exact premise** for γ-exclusion via this route: **U** = "`apply_restore_catchup_blocks` admits at most one distinct `block_id` per view over the whole execution," ⟨**A36** — SUPERSEDED⟩ **this admission-sense U is now REFUTED (§26.2u); the "prove U" exclusion route is CLOSED.** γ-exclusion is instead approached through the **no-eviction** argument (§26.2v Part B, a *scoped* exclusion) with the accumulator-eviction defeat route **production-rejected** (§26.2v Part C); γ stays open, R independent. — (dated) the former open preservation step was "`committed_block` advances only along the deterministic catch-up chain" (coupled to the still-open general resident-parent obligation, OBL-CONS-3). γ is **neither excluded nor shown reachable**; **OBL-CONS-3 remains SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)**. No new finding, no closure; established conditional transitions (A19.7) and superseded history preserved.

### 26.2i A19.14 — local-vote-suppression sequence excluded by leader eligibility; γ⟹¬U reassessed and retained

A19.14 addresses the one route A19.13's `γ ⟹ ¬U` did not cover: the suppressing different-id at a view could be the **leader's own prior self-vote** (not a second catch-up id), so `¬U` (two *catch-up* ids) might not be necessary for γ. The abstract sequence is: **(a)** a local leader invocation records a self-vote at view `v` for id `A`; **(b)** catch-up at `v` admits id `B≠A` whose signer list includes `local`, so `local` is equivocation-suppressed at `K=(v,B)` and an effective sub-`q` non-local set may remain; **(c)** history pruning forgets the `(v,local)→A` record while `K=(v,B)` survives in the accumulator; **(d)** a later leader invocation at `v` selects `B` and attempts the completing insertion. Only **one** catch-up id (`B`) is used; `A` came from the leader. A19.14 traces each step's production predicates. Scope: unit-weight, **`q ≥ 2`** (N=1 self-quorum separate), the stated limits; ordinary non-wrapping execution kept separate from the E02 arithmetic band.

**A. Flag/view writer inventory (positive-controlled, `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs`).** Search `git grep` over `crates/**`; writers verified by reading each site (positive control: the inventory is nonempty and each assignment was read in context).
- **`proposed_in_view` writers:** `=true` at **`:2329`** (`on_leader_step`, set **before** the self-vote at `:2332`); `=false` at `:1805` (`advance_view`), `:1866` (`set_view`), `:1941` (`initialize_from_restart` wrapper), `:2014` (`initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` wrapper), `:2738` (`ingest_proposal`), `:3123` (`try_advance_to_view`), `:3293` (`on_timeout_certificate`); read at `:2233` (the `on_leader_step` guard `if self.proposed_in_view { return Vec::new() }`). (`:1396` is a `Debug` field print.)
- **`current_view` writers** with production direction: `:1804` `advance_view` → `+1` (forward); `:1865` `set_view` → `= view` (unconditional) but its **only production caller is catch-up `:2208`**, called `if self.current_view < expected_height` ⇒ **forward** (other `set_view` callers are `mod tests` `:3505/:3511`, `tests/*`, and the **sim** `hotstuff_node_sim.rs:2550` — none on the wired binary path); `:1940` / `:2013` startup initializers (`committed/snapshot_height + 1`, once at node start); `:2737` `ingest_proposal` → `if view > self.current_view` ⇒ **forward**, and `ingest_proposal` is **latent** (inbound Required-rejected, §26.2a); `:3122` `try_advance_to_view` → after `if target_view <= self.current_view { return false }` (`:3106`) ⇒ **forward** (fail-closed); `:3292` `on_timeout_certificate` → after `if tc.view <= self.current_view { return }` (`:3264`) ⇒ **forward**.

**Two source facts follow (production, wired-binary path):**
1. **View non-decrease (established within the non-wrapping interval; A19.15-scoped).** Every production writer of `current_view` is forward/non-decreasing with the cited guard; the only unconditional-assignment writer (`set_view`) has a single production caller that is forward-guarded. **Interval assumption (explicit):** this holds in **ordinary non-wrapping execution after initialization**. Note `advance_view` performs an **ordinary** `current_view + 1` (`:1796`), *not* a saturating add; at the `u64` boundary that add would wrap (and the E02/A1-F2 saturating-band concerns `tc.view`/`saturating_add`, §23.5/§24.4b, a *separate* arithmetic regime). A19.15 **does not** claim E02/wraparound cannot return the running view to a lower value and **does not** establish any wrap schedule; the wrap/E02 case is **explicitly excluded from this lemma's scope** (to be treated, if ever, under E02, not here). The saturating-vs-`+1` distinction is preserved. **Exceptions (explicit):** the one-time startup initializers (`:1940/:2013`, run before the consensus loop processes votes) and the excluded wrap/E02 regime. This is a per-production-path reading of the writers over the non-wrapping interval, **not** a global view-monotonicity proof.
2. **Flag clears only with a forward view change.** Every production writer that sets `proposed_in_view=false` (`:1805/:1866/:2738/:3123/:3293`) **simultaneously** moves `current_view` to a strictly higher value (per the guards above); the startup setters (`:1941/:2014`) run once. **No production path clears `proposed_in_view` while leaving `current_view` unchanged.**

**B. Transition table for steps (a)–(d).**

| Step | Required production predicate | Source | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (a) leader self-votes at `v` for `A` | `leader_for_view(v)=local`, `!proposed_in_view`, then `proposed_in_view=true` (`:2329`), records `(v,local)→A` via `on_vote`→`record_vote_history` (`:2332`,`:913`) | basic:2229–2332 | **reachable** (the ordinary first leader step at `v`) |
| (b) catch-up at `v` admits `B≠A`, `local` suppressed at `(v,B)` | a catch-up block id `B` at view `v` with `local∈qc_signers`; engine `on_vote(local,v,B)` sees `(v,local)→A≠B` ⇒ `Equivocation`⇒`Ok(None)` (`:959–966`), `local` not inserted; non-local signers inserted | basic:2192–2196; state:959–966 | **operation-level possible**; requires `B` admitted at `v` (a distinct id from `A`) |
| (c) history forgets `(v,local)→A` while `(v,B)` survives | `evict_votes_by_view_if_needed` removes the **whole lowest view**; to drop `(v,local)` it must evict view `v` ⇒ `v` is the **lowest** tracked history view **and** `votes_by_view.len() ≥ 16384` (`:685–691`); the accumulator `(v,B)` is a separate structure and can survive | state:683–696 | **operation-level possible** (desync, §26.2h); **(prod)** not established (needs `v` = min history view at the 16384-entry limit) |
| (d) later leader invocation at `v` selects `B`, completing insertion | a **second** `on_leader_step` at view `v` ⇒ needs `current_view=v` **and** `!proposed_in_view` **again** | basic:2229–2233,2329; writer inventory A | **EXCLUDED (production)** — see C |

**C. No second leader *self-vote* at `v` within the non-wrapping interval (A19.15-scoped).** The supported result concerns a **second leader invocation reaching its self-vote stage** at the same view — `on_leader_step` can be *called* repeatedly and simply **return early** at the `:2233` guard; the exclusion is of a second execution past `:2233` to the self-vote at `:2332`. After step (a), `proposed_in_view=true` at view `v` (`:2329`). By fact B.2, the flag returns to `false` only together with a strictly-forward `current_view` change; by fact B.1 (within the non-wrapping interval, startup-init and the excluded wrap/E02 regime aside), `current_view` does not decrease back to `v`. Therefore, once the leader has proposed at `v`, **no second `on_leader_step` reaches its self-vote at `v`**: either `current_view ≠ v` (the view has moved on; the self-id/key differ) or, if still `v`, `proposed_in_view=true` forces the early return at `:2233`. Step (d) cannot occur **in the non-wrapping interval**. **This excludes sequence (a)–(d) at step (d) via leader eligibility + production view non-decrease (non-wrapping interval), independently of whether step (c) is reachable.** Consequently the **leader's own prior self-vote cannot be the suppressing different-id for a *completing* leader self-vote.** *(Correction to the earlier "before the first self-vote `local` has no record": that is withdrawn — catch-up calls `state.on_vote` for every listed signer including `local_id` (basic:2192–2196), so a `(v,local)` history entry can be written by **catch-up** before the leader's first self-vote. What C actually establishes is producer-specific: **no earlier leader-produced self-vote at `v`** within the non-wrapping interval. The consequences of a catch-up-written `(v,local)` entry are enumerated in C′ below.)*

**C′. History-state × accumulator-state product at the leader's first self-vote at `v` (A19.16-corrected).** *History outcome and accumulator membership are **independent**:* engine `on_vote` returns early **only** on `Equivocation` (`:966`); **both** `FirstVote` and `DuplicateSameBlock` fall through to `self.votes.on_vote` (`:974`), and the accumulator's own `entry.insert(local)` returns *new* vs *duplicate* based on **accumulator-key membership** (`:342`), **not** on the history outcome. So a `DuplicateSameBlock` history record does **not** by itself establish that `local` is already in the accumulator key (the earlier C′(ii) "accumulator dedups `local`" is **withdrawn** — history and accumulator retention are separate; e.g. a whole-view accumulator eviction (§26.2h) can leave `(v,local)` in history while `local` is absent from the accumulator key). The product (history outcome × local accumulator membership × insertion result × effective power before→after × `maybe_qc_for`):

| History outcome (`record_vote_history`) | reaches accumulator? | `local ∈ K`? | accumulator insert | `W(K)` before → after | `maybe_qc_for` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FirstVote` (no live `(v,local)`) | yes (`:974`) | no | **new** (`:342`→true) | `S_before` → `S_before+1` | completes iff `S_before = q−1` |
| `FirstVote` | yes | yes (acc. has `local` though history forgot it) | duplicate (`:342`→false) | unchanged | re-evaluate (no new) |
| `DuplicateSameBlock` (`(v,local)→bid_self`) | yes (`:974`) | yes | duplicate | unchanged | re-evaluate (β if `≥q`) |
| `DuplicateSameBlock` | yes | **no** (acc. key evicted since catch-up wrote it) | **new** | `S_before` → `S_before+1` | **completes iff `S_before=q−1`** |
| `Equivocation` (`(v,local)→B'≠bid_self`) | **no** (early `Ok(None)` `:966`) | — | — | unchanged | not reached |
| capacity-refused (`len≥256`, `q>256` only) | yes | no | refused (`:336`) | unchanged | not completed |

So a **completing** first leader self-vote occurs iff the accumulator key `K=(v,bid_self)` holds effective power **exactly `q−1`** before the insert, `local ∉ K`, and the insert is accepted (not Equivocation, not capacity-refused). Whether `local ∈ K` or `local` is Equivocation-suppressed is driven by the **history/accumulator product**, not by either alone.

**C″. `q−1` at `K` does not require a *non-local* suppression (A19.16-corrected Part A2).** The no-second-*leader*-self-vote lemma (C) excludes an earlier **leader-produced** local vote at `v` (non-wrapping scope) — it does **not** exclude an earlier **catch-up-produced** `(v,local)` record (catch-up calls `on_vote(local,…)`, basic:2192–2196). So the route to a `q−1` `K` need **not** suppress a non-local signer; it can suppress **`local`**. Conditional sequence: **(1)** catch-up admits id `A` at `v` listing `local` ⇒ `(v,local)→A` written (history) and `local∈(v,A)` (accumulator); **(2)** catch-up admits id `B≠A` at `v` listing `local` ⇒ at `(v,B)`, `local` is `Equivocation`-suppressed (`A≠B`) while `B`'s non-local signers insert — **and reaching exactly `q−1` there requires its own premises (A20): `B`'s listed non-local effective power is exactly `q−1`, and all of those non-local signers successfully insert (none itself `Equivocation`-suppressed by a prior `(v,s)→id'`, none capacity-refused, the key not whole-view-evicted). Two admitted ids `A,B` alone do NOT establish exactly `q−1` contributions**; **(3)** history prunes `(v,local)` (whole-view eviction) while the accumulator `(v,B)` survives (§26.2h desync); **(4)** an **eligible first** leader self-vote at `v` targets `bid_self=B` ⇒ `FirstVote` (pruned) ⇒ `local` inserted ⇒ `(v,B)` reaches `q` ⇒ completes. **Here the suppressed signer is `local`, not non-local** — yet the sequence uses **two distinct admitted catch-up ids `A,B` at `v`** (step 1 and step 2), i.e. **`¬U`**. 

**Established vs unresolved (do not assert production-reachability):** steps (1),(2) are **operation-level established** given two admitted catch-up ids at `v` (the per-`on_vote` equivocation + insert behavior, pinned); step (3) is an **operation-level** desync possibility (§26.2h), **production-reachability not established** (needs `v`=min history view at the 16384-entry limit while the accumulator retains `v`); step (4) needs the **first** leader step at `v` to target `B` with `bid_self=B` (a parent/anchor-prefix premise). The **binding premise for the whole sequence is `¬U`** (two admitted catch-up ids `A,B` at the same view `v`), which is **unresolved** (the open per-view uniqueness question). **So `γ ⟹ ¬U` survives** — but via *"any suppression at `K` (local **or** non-local) requires a prior different-id vote for that signer at `v`, and the only non-leader producer of a vote at `v` is a catch-up block, so a second admitted catch-up id at `v` = `¬U`"*, **not** via "the suppressed signer must be non-local." The earlier C′/D phrasing "the pre-existing `q−1` must be non-local" is **withdrawn**; replaced by: the pre-existing `q−1` at `K` requires **some** suppression (of `local` via a catch-up-written `(v,local)→A`, or of a non-local via a prior `(v,s)→id'`), each ⇒ a second catch-up id ⇒ `¬U`. Unit-weight, `q≥2`, pre-insertion observation point, non-wrapping scope preserved; this is a **conditional state transition** (premised on `¬U` + pruning + scheduling), **not** an established production sequence; the full U proof is not reopened here.

**D. Effective-count statement corrected (item 3).** Catch-up admission requires `W(qc_signers) ≥ q` **voting power** (not exactly `q` listed signers; basic:2183, qc.rs). So "a key is `q−1` iff **exactly one** non-local signer was suppressed" is **withdrawn**. At the defined observation point (the key's effective **distinct** signer set `S_before`, just before the completing insertion), for the **first** leader self-vote at `v` to complete `K=(v,bid_self)`: `S_before` must be exactly `q−1` (unit weight), and — because the completing insert requires `local ∉ K` — those `q−1` **pre-existing contributions are non-local** (A20.1: this is the *existing-count* claim, distinct from the *suppressed signer* below). The completing insert is a **new accumulator insert**, which occurs in **case C′(i)** (`FirstVote` — no live `(v,local)` record, never written by catch-up or pruned) **or case C′(iv)** (`DuplicateSameBlock` where `local ∉ K` because the accumulator key was evicted since catch-up wrote it) — **A20.1 corrects the earlier "`FirstVote` insertion" to "a new insert via C′(i) or C′(iv)"**; the non-completing cases C′(ii)/(iii) (where `local ∈ K`, a duplicate) are excluded. `S_before` is the union over catch-up block(s) with id `bid_self` of their admitted signers, **minus** equivocation-suppressed signers, **minus** capacity-refused (`≥256`, i.e. `q>256`, out of scope), after any whole-view-eviction/replay (which gives ∅ then rebuilds). With admitted power `W_list ≥ q`, reaching `S_before = q−1` requires suppressing `W_list − (q−1) ≥ 1` units **(A19.16-corrected: not necessarily non-local)** — at least one signer `s` (local **or** non-local) with a prior `(v,s)→id'`, `id'≠bid_self`. For a **non-local** `s`, `id'` is a second admitted catch-up id at `v`; for `s = local`, `id'` is a **catch-up-written** `(v,local)→A`, `A≠bid_self` (C″) — a second admitted catch-up id at `v` as well. Either way ⇒ **a second admitted catch-up id at `v` = `¬U`** (the leader-produced local-vote route is excluded by C within the non-wrapping scope, but the catch-up-produced local route is **not**, so the suppressed signer may be `local`). Duplicates dedup (no effect); prior non-catch-up contributions do not exist (inbound Required-rejected).

**E. Reassessed implication (item 4).** With the local-suppression route excluded at step (d) (C), the suppression enabling a **completing** leader self-vote requires a prior different-id vote at the view for the suppressed signer — **of a non-local signer OR of `local` (via a catch-up-written `(v,local)→A`, A19.16 C″)** — and either way a second admitted catch-up id at the view: **`γ ⟹ ¬U` is retained** (the suppressed signer need **not** be non-local) within unit-weight, `q ≥ 2`, `q ≤ 256`, `N ≤ 256`, with the view non-decrease exception set (startup-init, E02) stated. The supporting exclusion (C) is a **source-based exclusion with explicit scope** — the invariant is: *"after a leader proposes at `v` (`proposed_in_view=true`), no production path returns `current_view` to `v` with `proposed_in_view=false`,"* with production preconditions = the writer inventory (A) + guards (B). By contraposition `U ⟹ ¬γ`, so **U remains a candidate *sufficient* exclusion strategy** (its own preservation step — per-view catch-up-id uniqueness — is still open, OBL-CONS-3); U is **not** shown necessary/smallest. **Not claimed:** γ reachability (the reverse `¬U ⟹ γ` is unproven, A19.12; and exclusion remaining unfinished does not imply reachability), nor a global lineage proof, nor any new implementation defect (the history desync of §26.2h and the step-(c) possibility remain operation-level, not production-established).

**F. Bounded conclusion.** The local-vote-suppression sequence (a)–(d) is **excluded** (production-unreachable at step (d), by leader eligibility + production view non-decrease, scope stated). `γ ⟹ ¬U` is **retained** on this firmer basis; the effective-count statement is corrected (A20.1) to "**≥1 suppression, of a local *or* non-local signer**," not "≥1 non-local suppression" and not "exactly one" — the **pre-existing `q−1` at a completing key are non-local** (because `local ∉ K`), but the **suppressed signer that explains why the key sits at `q−1`** may be local (via a catch-up-written `(v,local)→A`, C″) or non-local; either way the suppression requires a second admitted catch-up id at `v` (`¬U`). **Remaining exact premise** for γ-exclusion via this route: **U** (per-view catch-up-id uniqueness), whose open preservation step ("`committed_block` advances only along the deterministic catch-up chain") is coupled to the still-open general resident-parent obligation (OBL-CONS-3). γ is **neither excluded nor shown reachable**; **OBL-CONS-3 remains SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)**; counts unchanged. No new finding, no closure; established conditional transitions (A19.7) and superseded history preserved.

**C‴. β (already-quorate key, re-evaluated) is separate from γ (invocation completing quorum); a matching catch-up key does NOT by itself establish `¬U` (A20, Part A item 3).** The leader-self-vote `Ok(Some(qc))` outcomes are enumerated α/β/γ (§26.2e, §26.2b). These are *distinct* branches and must not be conflated:
- **γ (completing)** is the branch §26.2i-C′..F is about: the accumulator key `K=(v,bid_self)` holds effective power **exactly `q−1`** before the leader's own insert, `local ∉ K`, and the leader's insertion is the `q`-th that crosses the threshold. Only γ carries the C″/D derivation above (existing `q−1` ⇒ non-local; the *shortfall-causing suppressed* signer local-or-non-local; each suppression ⇒ a second admitted catch-up id ⇒ `¬U`). `γ ⟹ ¬U` is asserted **only** for this completing branch and **only** within the stated scope (unit-weight, `q≥2`, `q≤256`, `N≤256`, non-wrapping, exception set stated); no reverse (`¬U ⟹ γ`) and no reachability.
- **β (collision / already-quorate)** is the branch where the self-vote key is **already at `≥q`** (a catch-up key at `(v,bid_self)` reached `q` from catch-up signers alone, independently of the leader's vote) and the leader invocation merely **re-evaluates** `maybe_qc_for`, which re-reports the existing QC. The leader's own insert here is a *duplicate or a redundant member of an already-quorate key*; it does **not** cross the threshold. **β does not invoke the C″/D suppression argument at all** — a key that is already `≥q` needs **no** suppression to explain its count, so β is **not** evidence of `¬U`, and conversely `¬U` is **not** a premise β requires. A single catch-up id `bid_self=B` at view `v` whose own signers already reach `q` suffices for β; that is a *matching catch-up key*, and a matching catch-up key is consistent with **U** (per-view uniqueness) holding. Therefore: **"the leader's self-vote key matches a `≥q` catch-up key" (β) does not establish `¬U`.**
- **β decomposed into five distinct aspects (A20.1, item 5) — do not conflate them.** For a leader invocation at `(v, bid_self)`: **(1) matching id** — the leader's self-proposed `bid_self = D(local_id, v, parent)` equals an existing accumulator key id (this depends on the **parent** the leader selects = `locked_qc().block_id` else `committed_block`, basic:2245, §26.2N); a mere *prefix* coincidence is **not** an id match. **(2) retained quorum** — that key `(v, bid_self)` already holds effective power `≥ q` from prior (catch-up) voters, still retained (not evicted). **(3) history eligibility** — the leader's own `on_vote(local_id, v, bid_self)` is not `Equivocation`-suppressed (no live `(v,local)→id'≠bid_self`), so it reaches `self.votes.on_vote` (it is then a duplicate/redundant member of the already-quorate key, or a new member that does not change the `≥q` status). **(4) QC return** — `maybe_qc_for(v, bid_self)` re-reports `Some(qc)` because the key is already `≥q`; the leader's own vote is not what crosses the threshold. **(5) caller view advance** — `on_leader_step` calls `self.advance_view()` **iff** the self-vote result is `Ok(Some(qc))` (basic:2359–2372, firsthand); **this is gated solely on the `Ok(Some(qc))` branch and does NOT consult the commit-floor / residency / `own_qc` 3-chain predicates** — the view advance happens whether or not `try_commit_with_qc` commits anything. So a β view advance is a **result-branch** consequence, not a commit consequence; the earlier phrasing "β view-advance if its downstream residency/own_qc/floor predicates are met" is **withdrawn** (those predicates gate a *commit*, not the view advance).
- **Consequence for the anchor-form premise (OBL-STO-1b, §26.2L below).** Part B resolves that the restored-anchor prefix/first-16 can be made to equal `P_v` by an operator-supplied opaque `block_hash` (so a leader block id at a restored view *can* coincide with a catch-up/anchor prefix). That resolves the **anchor-form** premise that a β *collision* was waiting on — i.e. β's "matching key" input (aspect 1) is **constructible** — but it does **not** convert β into γ and does **not** supply `¬U`. **Crucially (A20.1/§26.2N):** whether aspect 1 actually holds depends on the leader's **parent selection** (`locked_qc().block_id`), so a prefix-only anchor plus intervening catch-up does **not** automatically yield a β id-match — §26.2N traces a concrete case-B configuration where the leader builds on the lock `B2`, derives `bid_self = C` (the anchor), and lands in a **fresh** key `(v,C)` at `W=1` (no retained quorum, no QC, no view advance). So "matching prefix" ⇏ β, and anchor acceptance does **not** discharge the γ⟹¬U scope and does **not** close OBL-CONS-3 (§26.2L/§26.2N return the resolved premise explicitly; `¬U` — two admitted catch-up ids at one view — remains **unresolved**).

**Summary of the existing-vs-suppressed distinction (A20, Part A item 1).** At a *completing* (γ) insertion: the **q−1 contributions already present in `K`** are necessarily **non-local** (because the completing case requires `local ∉ K` before the leader's own insert — C′(i)/(iv), D); the **signer whose suppression explains why `K` sits at `q−1` rather than `q`** (the shortfall cause) **may be local or non-local** (C″/D). These are two different signers and were previously (A19.15) conflated under "the suppression must be non-local"; that conflation is withdrawn. Both facts hold only for γ; neither applies to β.

```
568     fn insert_block_node(&mut self, node: BlockNode<BlockIdT>) {
569         let id = node.id.clone();
570         if let Some(old) = self.blocks.get(&id) {
571             let old_bytes = Self::evidence_bytes_of_node(old);
572             self.retained_evidence_bytes = self.retained_evidence_bytes.saturating_sub(old_bytes);
573         }
574         let new_bytes = Self::evidence_bytes_of_node(&node);
575         self.retained_evidence_bytes = self.retained_evidence_bytes.saturating_add(new_bytes);
576         self.blocks.insert(id, node);
577     }
```

```
1029    fn try_commit_with_qc(&mut self, qc: &QuorumCertificate<BlockIdT>) {
1031        let b_view = match self.blocks.get(&qc.block_id) {

1036                }
1037                node.view
1038            }

1040        };

1049                Some(id) => {
1050                    let p = match self.blocks.get(id) { Some(node) => node, None => return };
1055                    if p.own_qc.is_none() { return; }
1058                    (id.clone(), p.view)
1059                }
1060                None => return,
1061            }
1062        };

1084        };
```

```
995     fn on_qc(&mut self, qc: &QuorumCertificate<BlockIdT>) -> Result<(), QcValidationError> {
996         // Minimal HotStuff-style locking:
997         // - Update locked_qc to the highest-view QC.
998         let replace_lock = match &self.locked_qc {
999             None => true,
1000            Some(existing) => qc.view > existing.view,
1001        };
1002
1003        if replace_lock {
1004            self.locked_qc = Some(qc.clone());
1005        }
1006
1007        // Record QC on the block node itself.
1008        if let Some(node) = self.blocks.get_mut(&qc.block_id) {
1009            node.own_qc = Some(qc.clone());
1010        }
1011
1012        // Attempt 3-chain commit logic.
1013        self.try_commit_with_qc(qc);
1014
1015        Ok(())
1016    }
```

```
2043    fn derive_block_id_from_header(proposer: ValidatorId, view: u64, parent_block_id: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {
2048        let mut id = [0u8; 32];
2050        let proposer_bytes = proposer.0.to_le_bytes();
2051        id[..8].copy_from_slice(&proposer_bytes);
2053        let view_bytes = view.to_le_bytes();
2054        id[8..16].copy_from_slice(&view_bytes);
2056        id[16..32].copy_from_slice(&parent_block_id[..16]);
2057        id
2058    }
2061    fn make_block_id(&mut self, parent_block_id: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {
2062        Self::derive_block_id_from_header(self.local_id, self.current_view, parent_block_id)
2063    }
```

**B-4. Map state at `try_commit`, tracked independently.** The qc passed is the leader self-vote's collision QC at `(cv, bid_self)`, so `qc.block_id = B = bid_self`. The leader's `register_block(bid_self, cv, Some(B_pre), justify)` (basic:2259) **overwrote** any prior node for `bid_self` (e.g. a catch-up block that supplied the quorum): afterward `B.view = cv`, `B.parent_id = B_pre`, `B.height = blocks.get(B_pre).height + 1` (or `0` if `B_pre` absent) — **the current node fields come from this registration, not from the quorum's origin.** `P = blocks.get(B_pre)`; `G = blocks.get(P.parent_id)`. For each of `B`, `P`, `G` the independent quantities are: id; current resident entry; stored `view`/`height`/`parent_id`; `own_qc`; registration/replacement provenance; accumulator-quorum provenance; and `committed_block`/`committed_height` at evaluation. Cases:
- **Required node absent:** `B` absent (`:1039`), `P = blocks.get(B_pre)` absent (`:1052`), or `G = blocks.get(P.parent_id)` absent (`:1074`) ⇒ `return` ⇒ **no commit**. (The opaque `B_pre` not being a registered id is the generic instance.)
- **Required `own_qc` absent:** `B.own_qc` (`:1034`), `P.own_qc` (`:1055`), or `G.own_qc` (`:1077`) `is_none` ⇒ `return` ⇒ **no commit**. (`register_block` never sets `own_qc`; only `on_qc` does, for an id whose key reached quorum. The restore anchor is resident with `own_qc=None`, §26.2h-D4, so an anchor `G` fails here — stated at the evaluation instant, not as a lifetime claim.)
- **Alias among `B`/`P`/`G`** (apply the **actual** strict-view predicate `:1087`, not an imported topology): `B=P` ⇒ `p_view=b_view` ⇒ `p_view<b_view` false; `P=G` ⇒ `g_view=p_view` ⇒ `g_view<p_view` false; `B=G` ⇒ needs `cv<p_view<cv`, impossible. **Every alias ⇒ `:1087` returns ⇒ no commit.**
- **All three distinct, resident, `own_qc`-bearing:** the remaining case — B-5.

**ID-prefix-to-stored-view lemma `I_pv` (bounded; established with its anchor exception).** *Statement:* for every resident node registered via `register_block` on a production path, `node.view = decode(node.id[8:16])`. *Init/preservation:* `derive_block_id_from_header` writes `id[8:16] = encode(view)` (`:2053–2054`); the two production `register_block` callers both pass `view` equal to that embedded view — catch-up `register_block(block.block_id, block.view, …)` (basic:2186) under admission that enforces `block.block_id = D(proposer, block.view, parent)` (basic:2169–2179), and the leader `register_block(make_block_id(parent), current_view, …)` (basic:2259, `make_block_id` uses `current_view`, `:2062`). `insert_block_node` overwrites but every production registration re-establishes the equality. `ingest_proposal`'s `register_block` (basic:2806) is **latent** (inbound Required-rejected). *Exception, stated by **current-entry provenance** (A19.16):* `I_pv` is a property of each id's **current** resident entry, classified by **how that entry was last written**. An entry last written by the **restore-anchor initializer** (`insert_block_node` directly, `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` `:1277`, opaque `snapshot_block_id` + separately-supplied `committed_view`) is **exceptional** — `anchor.id[8:16]` need not equal `encode(committed_view)`, so `I_pv` need not hold for it. **But** a **subsequent validated replacement** of that id via `register_block` (e.g. a catch-up block admitted with the same id, basic:2186 under the `block_id = D(proposer,view,parent)` check, or a leader `make_block_id`) **overwrites** the entry (`insert_block_node`) and the new entry is assessed on **its** provenance — which satisfies `I_pv`. So the exception is per-current-entry and ceases once the opaque entry is replaced by a validated registration; an id that is *only ever* the opaque anchor is the lasting exception. `I_pv` does **not** assume `height=view` (height is `parent.height+1`, independent of the id). *Use:* under `I_pv`, for non-anchor `P=B_pre` and `G`, `p_view=decode(B_pre[8:16])` and `g_view=decode(G.id[8:16])` — tying the strict-view predicate to the ids' embedded views; but since `B_pre` is the attacker-chosen TC-lock id, `decode(B_pre[8:16])` is attacker-influenced (subject to `B_pre` actually being a resident admitted id), so `I_pv` **constrains but does not exclude** the distinct case.

**B-5. The distinct-resident-parent case → exact remaining source dependency (result type (c)).** For a **new** leader-driven commit of `G` in the all-distinct case, the complete predicate requires a production-reachable state with: (1) `B_pre` resident **with `own_qc`** — i.e. the opaque `tc.high_qc.block_id` **coincides with the id of an admitted block whose `(view,B_pre)` key reached quorum**; (2) `G = B_pre.parent_id` resident with `own_qc`; (3) `g_view < p_view < cv` (with `I_pv`: `decode(G.id[8:16]) < decode(B_pre[8:16]) < cv`); (4) `g_height > committed_height` (strict floor `:1093–1095`); (5) `should_commit` — `g_id ≠ committed_block` and (committed node resident) `g_view > committed_node.view` (`:1098–1117`). ### 26.2k A19.16 Part B — the d1 TC-admission sub-edge: inbound TC → lock install (resolved as conditional admission)

| 4d | Resulting view/flag mutations | `current_view ← tc.view`; `proposed_/voted_/timeout_in_view ← false`; `timeout_accumulator.clear_view(tc.timeout_view)` | same | basic:3292–3299 |

**Four precise answers.**
1. **Constraints on `high_qc.block_id` / `.view` / relationship.** `on_timeout_certificate` constrains only `high_qc.view` — via `should_update` (`tc_high_qc.view > locked.view`, a **view comparison**, 4c) and, separately, `tc.view > current_view` (4b). **(A20 correction: these are two independent executable checks; there is NO executable check relating `high_qc.view` to `tc.view` — the earlier "TCs normally carry `high_qc.view < tc.view`" editorial claim is withdrawn as not a source check.)** It places **no** constraint on `high_qc.block_id` and **no** `block_id↔view` structural binding (`tc.validate` ignores `high_qc` entirely). Under **`None`** that is the whole story — `high_qc.block_id` and `.view` are otherwise free. Under **`Some`**, step 3 additionally forces `tc.high_qc` to **equal the deterministic max-view high_qc carried by the cryptographically-verified signed evidence** (`high_qc_eq` compares block_id and view); so `high_qc.block_id` = some signer's **signed, self-reported** high-QC block id (the max-view one) and `high_qc.view` = that QC's view — still **no** re-derivation of `block_id` from `(leader,view,parent)` and **no** independent quorum-endorsement of that high_qc (the A1-F3 core).
2. **Is block-map residency or existing `own_qc` checked before lock installation?** **No.** 4c calls `set_locked_qc` which is `self.locked_qc = Some(qc)` (state:1144–1146) — it reads neither `self.blocks` nor any `own_qc`. The named `high_qc.block_id` is not looked up at all.
3. **Under which premises can the installed lock name an already-resident QC-bearing block `B_pre`?** The lock names `tc.high_qc.block_id`. It equals a resident `own_qc`-bearing `B_pre` iff: **(None)** the attacker sets `tc.high_qc.block_id = B_pre` (free) with `tc.high_qc.view > locked.view`, `tc.view > current_view`, and the TC admitted (origin gate at 1 + ≥2/3 TC `signers` at 4a); **(Some)** **some validator's signed timeout in the evidence carries, as the deterministic max-view high_qc, a QC for `B_pre`** (i.e. ≥1 signer reports `B_pre` as its high-QC and it is the maximum by view), with the same 4a/4b/4c view conditions. If `B_pre` is a genuine high QC a validator holds, the `Some` premise is ordinary honest behavior; the A1-F3 gap is that this high_qc is **not independently quorum-endorsed** at install.
4. **What changes / does not change at lock installation (4c).** **Changes:** `self.locked_qc ← tc.high_qc` (and, at 4d, `current_view`, the view flags, and the timeout accumulator). **Does NOT change:** the **block map** (no node is created or modified for `high_qc.block_id` — `set_locked_qc` does not touch `self.blocks`), the **vote accumulator**, and **any node's `own_qc`** (`on_timeout_certificate` never calls `on_qc`). Therefore `B_pre`'s block-map residency and `own_qc` are left **exactly as they were**: if `B_pre` was already resident with `own_qc`, it stays so; if absent, it stays absent — lock installation neither creates nor certifies the named block.

**QC-producer inventory for `B`, `P`, `G` (A19.16 — correcting §26.2j(d1)'s collision/`U` restriction).** `own_qc` is set only by `on_qc` (`:1008–1009`), for a resident block whose accumulator key `(view, id)` reached quorum (`maybe_qc_for`):
- **`B` = `bid_self`** (the leader's just-registered block): `own_qc` ← the **leader self-vote QC** at `(cv, bid_self)` — this is the collision/`U` question (`B`'s key reaches quorum only via a pre-populated collision, §26.2h/i). **This is the only producer for `B`, and it is the γ/`U` edge** (not part of d1).
- **`P` = `B_pre`**: `own_qc` ← a QC at `(B_pre.view, B_pre)`. Primary producer: **ordinary catch-up QC formation** — a catch-up block admitted at `(B_pre.view, B_pre)` whose forged `qc_signers` meet quorum (the standard A17-F1 path), `on_vote → maybe_qc_for → on_qc`. **No collision/`U` required.** (A leader-collision could also produce it, but ordinary catch-up is the common case.)
- **`G` = `B_pre`'s parent**: same as `P` — **ordinary catch-up QC formation** (A17-F1), no collision/`U` required.

So **§26.2j(d1)'s claim that the parent QC must arise from "collision/`U` mechanics" is withdrawn**: `P` and `G` acquire `own_qc` by ordinary catch-up; only `B`'s own QC is the collision/`U` edge.

**d1 disposition — conditional admission RESOLVED; full commit NOT.** The **admission half of d1 is resolved** as an available-source fact: the TC path **installs the lock as `tc.high_qc` without any block-map residency or `own_qc` check**, so the lock **can** name an already-resident `own_qc`-bearing `B_pre` (own_qc via ordinary catch-up), under the step-3/4a/4b/4c premises above (free block_id under `None`; a signed max-view high_qc for `B_pre` under `Some`); and lock installation **does not alter** `B_pre`'s residency/own_qc. This is **conditional admission of an existing resident identifier** — it is **not** a complete leader/QC/commit sequence: the resident-parent **commit** still requires (i) `B`'s own QC = the **collision/γ/`U`** edge (open), (ii) **d2** committed-floor/lineage (`g_height > committed_height`, `should_commit`) — **not** resolved by d1 (A19.16 does **not** infer d2 from d1), and (iii) **d3** anchor acceptance where `B_pre`/`G` is the restore anchor = **OBL-STO-1b / T-A18-2** (unstarted). **Separately reported:** *completed sub-edge* — d1 admission half (lock-installs-a-resident-id, QC-producer = ordinary catch-up); *remaining available-source* — `B`'s collision QC (γ/`U`) and d2 committed-floor/lineage, plus which resident `{B_pre, G}` own_qc states and `Some`-posture signed-evidence are reachable; *upstream prerequisite* — `U` (per-view uniqueness) and d3 anchor acceptance (T-A18-2); *execution gap* — deployment posture (`None`/`Some`) and validator collusion (A1-F3/E03). **OBL-CONS-3 remains SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)**; the general resident-parent obligation stays open; counts unchanged (d1 is a sub-edge of OBL-CONS-3's trace, not a separate obligation). No new finding, no closure; conditional view-advance (A19.7) and CONS-4b preserved.

### 26.2L A20 Part B — OBL-STO-1b: restore-anchor acceptance + same-key registration (available-source trace; block_hash is operator-supplied opaque)

A20 Part B traces, firsthand from the pin `ef99e29`, the baseline restore path from snapshot-metadata decode through the startup guards, `RestoreBaseline` construction, and engine init, to determine **what constrains the snapshot `block_hash`** (= the anchor id `C`) and then traces **same-key registration** over `C`. It resolves the two anchor-form premises (case **A** `C=P‖P`, case **B** `C=P‖R, R≠P`) that the §26.2d CONS-3 case table left as an **upstream OBL-STO-1b/T-A18-2** dependency. Scope: read-only; **no snapshot is created and no restoration is executed**; the crafted-snapshot realization and deployment posture remain **EXEC(E22)**.

**L-1. Ordered acceptance → mutation path (production binary, firsthand excerpts).**

| # | Step | Executable check / effect | `block_hash` touched? | Source (`ef99e29`) |

**L-2. What constrains `C = block_hash` (the decisive available-source fact).** Representation: `StateSnapshotMeta.block_hash: [u8; 32]` (32 bytes; state_snapshot.rs:103). The **only** check applied to it on the entire restore path is `from_json`'s `if block_hash_hex.len() != 64 { return None }` followed by hex-parse of 32 bytes (state_snapshot.rs:533–544). `validate_snapshot_dir` (step 4) checks chain_id/height/state-dir and **never reads `block_hash`**; `snapshot_restore.rs` uses `block_hash` **only** to hex it into the audit marker (step 8) and to populate `RestoreBaseline.snapshot_block_id` (step 9). There is **no**: (i) comparison of `block_hash` to the height, chain, materialized state, authority marker, or epoch; (ii) derivation of `block_hash` from any of those; (iii) canonical-ID / structural check (it is **not** required to equal `D(proposer,view,parent)` of anything); (iv) integrity/signature binding over it. The `StateSnapshotMeta.block_hash` **doc-comment** ("Used to verify the snapshot corresponds to the expected chain state. During restore, nodes **can** verify this matches the block at `height`") describes a **documented capability that this restore path does NOT execute** — firsthand-confirmed by the absence of any such comparison in steps 1–11. **Therefore `C` is an operator-supplied opaque 32-byte value**, settable to any bit pattern that is valid 64-hex. **(Absence of a snapshot signature / per-record authenticity is a *documented* "operator-honest, local-storage-trusted" assumption, E22 — restated, not elevated: absence of snapshot signatures alone is NOT a finding.)**

**L-3. `P` is not unconstrained — it is bound to the restored height and the deterministic leader schedule (with explicit bounds + leader/event premises, A20.1).** The first production proposal after restore is at **view `h+1`**, where `h = meta.height` and `current_view = snapshot_height.saturating_add(1)` (basic:2011). **Explicit arithmetic bound (A20.1 — saturation vs ordinary-add kept distinct):** the step-4 `InvalidHeight` gate forces `h ≥ 1`; the restore initializer uses `saturating_add(1)`, so for `h = u64::MAX` the start view **saturates to `u64::MAX`** (it does **not** wrap); for `1 ≤ h < u64::MAX` the start view is exactly `h+1`. This is a **`saturating_add` at the restore seed**, a different operator from `advance_view`'s ordinary `current_view + 1` (basic:1796, which *would* wrap at the `u64` ceiling); the two are not conflated, and the saturating case (`h = u64::MAX`) is set aside as a degenerate boundary (restored start view `= u64::MAX`, no further ordinary increment representable). For `1 ≤ h ≤ u64::MAX − 1` (the case analysed below), view `= h+1` exactly. **Leader-eligibility + event-order premises (A20.1 — stated, not assumed):** the first-post-restore leader *action* at `v=h+1` fires only when (i) `is_leader_for_current_view()` holds — `leader_for_view(v) = local_id` — and (ii) `!proposed_in_view` (reset to `false` by the restore initializer, basic:2012), and (iii) `on_leader_step` is actually invoked by the loop (the tick path), i.e. no earlier forward view change or proposal intervened. Under those premises the proposer is **`leader_for_view(v)`** (public deterministic schedule), parenting on the lock-or-committed block (L-6/§26.2N), and the block id is `D(leader_v, v, parent) = encode(leader_v)‖encode(v)‖parent[0:16]` (derive_block_id_from_header, basic:2043–2058, firsthand). Define **`P_v := encode(leader_v)‖encode(v)`** (16 bytes). `P_v` is **fixed** by `(h, schedule)` — its two halves are the LE-encoded leader id and the LE-encoded view `v`; it is **not** a free symbol. What is free is **`C` itself** (L-2), including `C[0:16]` and `C[16:32]` independently.

**L-4. Case A — fixed-point anchor `C = P‖P` (pure fresh restore, no intervening catch-up).** Premise: `C[0:16] = C[16:32] = P_v` (i.e. `C = P_v‖P_v`), `v=h+1`, and **no catch-up has run** (so the lock is still `None` — see L-6). Then (L-6/§26.2N) the first leader block builds on `committed_block = C` (lock `None`) and its derived id is `D(leader_v, v, C) = P_v‖C[0:16] = P_v‖P_v = C` — a **self-id collision**: the first post-restore leader block's id **equals the anchor id**. *Jointly-satisfiable symbolic inputs + prerequisites (the latter constrain the attacker; they are NOT free choices — A20.1/item 3):* the operator supplies `meta.block_hash = P_v‖P_v` (computable before restore from the chosen `meta.height = h` and the public schedule — this half **is** free, L-2) together with inputs that must satisfy the executable guards: `meta.chain_id` **must equal** the node's configured chain id (`ChainIdMismatch` else, state_snapshot.rs:1214); `meta.height = h ≥ 1` (`InvalidHeight` else); a present state dir (`MissingStateDir` else); the target VM state dir **must be empty** (`TargetStateNotEmpty` else); the snapshot authority-state block **must be consistent** with the locally-persisted authority marker (`enforce_authority_marker_check`, Run 124 v1 + Run 140 v2, else `AuthorityMarkerConflict{,V2}`); and `meta.epoch` **must be consensus-epoch-compatible** with `<data_dir>/consensus` (`epoch_precheck`, Run 422 D7-D5, else `ConsensusEpochConflict`). **No guard constrains `block_hash` beyond the 64-hex-length parse; the other fields are prerequisites a crafted snapshot must be made consistent with (bounding the attacker to a chain-id/authority/epoch-consistent forgery), not automatically operator-controllable.** **Residual = EXEC(E22):** crafting+placing such a snapshot requires **local write access** to the snapshot/data directory, and realization requires a DevNet restore-enabled deployment — neither created nor executed here. (The leader-step outcome of this overwrite is traced in §26.2N; it is a self-vote into a fresh key, **not** a commit.)

**L-5. Case B — prefix-only anchor `C = P‖R, R≠P` (scoped to the exact transition — A20.1).** Premise: `C[0:16] = P_v`, `C[16:32] = R ≠ P_v`. **Two different transitions must be distinguished, and the v0.63 wording conflated them:**
- **(B-pure) First leader proposal with no intervening catch-up** (lock `None`): the leader builds on `committed_block = C`, so its id is `D(leader_v, v, C) = P_v‖C[0:16] = P_v‖P_v ≠ C` (since `C[16:32]=R≠P_v`) — a **distinct** block; `N_C` is **not** overwritten by this transition, and the self-vote lands in the fresh key `(v, P_v‖P_v)` (W=1, no QC). So in B-pure there is no same-key registration and no QC.
- **(B-catchup) After an intervening origin-admitted catch-up** that locks a block `B2` with `B2[0:16] = P_v` (the full §26.2N sequence): the leader builds on `lock = B2`, and `D(leader_v, v, B2) = P_v‖B2[0:16] = P_v‖P_v`... — **correction:** with the §26.2N anchor `C = P_v‖P_{v+1}`, `B2[0:16] = P_{v+1}`, so the leader id is `P_v‖P_{v+1} = C` and the anchor **IS** overwritten. The exact derivation, which depends on the lock's prefix, is traced in §26.2N; it still ends in a **fresh self-vote key `(v,C)` at W=1 — no QC, no commit, no view advance**.

So the "`C[16:32]` supplies a β-collision prefix input" claim is **scoped**: a prefix coincidence alone does **not** produce a β collision at the leader's own key — whether the leader's self-vote key collides with a quorate catch-up key depends on the **lock/committed parent** selected (L-6/§26.2N), which these transitions resolve explicitly. *Jointly-satisfiable:* same prerequisites as L-4 (chain_id/height/authority/epoch consistency) with `C[16:32]=R`. **No L-1 guard constrains `block_hash`.** **Residual = EXEC(E22)** as in L-4. *(Both A and B resolve to "available-source satisfiable; no `block_hash` rejecting check exists; the remaining dependency is EXEC(E22) + the downstream commit/QC, which §26.2N shows this transition does not reach, and which otherwise is CONS-3's.")*

**L-6. Same-key registration over `C` (the five operations distinguished).** The anchor entry after step 10 is `N_C = {id=C, view=h, parent_id=None, justify_qc=None, own_qc=None, height=h}`, eviction-protected while `height ≤ committed_height`. A subsequent production registration with **the same id `C`** overwrites it via `register_block → insert_block_node` (the overwrite choke point, state:744/568; `BlockNode::new` always sets `own_qc=None`, block_state.rs:106; register_block's own comment: "A legacy/unverified registration replaces any prior node for this id, including any earlier verified designation"). Production `register_block` callers: catch-up (basic:2186), leader (basic:2259), ingest_proposal (basic:2806, latent). The five operations are **distinct**:
- **Acceptance** (step 10): `N_C` inserted at init with `own_qc=None` — the anchor is *accepted into the block map* but carries **no QC**.
- **Registration (same-key)** — *scoped to the exact transition examined (A20.1); this is NOT an inventory of all later registrations.* In the **B-pure/A pure fresh-restore first proposal** (lock `None`), the leader calls `register_block(block_id, v, parent_id=Some(C), justify_qc=None)` with `parent = committed_block = C` — note **`justify_qc = locked_qc = None`** here (on_leader_step binds `justify_qc = self.state.locked_qc().cloned()`, basic:2255; at fresh restore the lock is `None`), **correcting** the v0.63 "`justify_qc=Some(…)`". The block id equals `C` **only in case A** (`D(leader_v,v,C)=P_v‖P_v=C` when `C=P_v‖P_v`) → same-key overwrite with `parent_id=Some(C)` (self-parent), height `blocks.get(C).height+1 = h+1`. In **case B-pure** the id `≠ C` → a distinct new node, `N_C` unchanged. **After intervening catch-up (§26.2N)** the lock is non-`None` and the same-key overwrite recurs with a **non-self** parent and `justify_qc=Some(lock-QC)` — so "same-key registration reached only in case A" holds **only for the pure first transition**, not in general.
- **Replacement**: a case-A pure-fresh-restore same-key registration **overwrites** `N_C` to `{id=C, view=v, parent_id=Some(C) [SELF-PARENT], justify_qc=None, own_qc=None [reset], height=h+1}`; `is_new=false` so `pending_block_order` is not re-pushed. The anchor's original `view=h`/`parent_id=None`/`height=h` are **gone**; `own_qc` is (re)set to `None`. (In the §26.2N catch-up variant the overwrite instead has `parent=B2`, `justify_qc=Some(qc_B2)`, `height=v+2`.) **Note:** `committed_block`/`committed_height` are **not** touched by `register_block`, so after the overwrite the block-map entry for the committed id `C` no longer records `height=h` — the anchor-entry-preservation premise (A16.3) is concretely **not** maintained across a same-key re-registration.
- **QC-attachment**: `own_qc` is set **only** by `on_qc` (state:1008–1009), and only if the key `(view, id)` reaches quorum (`maybe_qc_for`); registration itself never attaches a QC. Whether the post-overwrite `C`-node ever gets `own_qc` depends on its self-vote key reaching `q` — §26.2N shows it does **not** (fresh key, W=1).
- **Commit** — *five predicates evaluated separately (A20.1); withdrawing one exclusion does NOT establish a commit.* `try_commit_with_qc` (state:1029–1137) commits the grandparent `G` of a 3-chain `B←P←G` only if **all** hold at **evaluation time**: (1) `B.own_qc.is_some()` **and** `P.own_qc.is_some()` **and** `G.own_qc.is_some()` — each checked when `try_commit` runs (state:1034/1055/1077); (2) strict views `g_view < p_view < b_view` (state:1087); (3) height floor `g_height > committed_height` (state:1093–1096); (4) `should_commit`: `g_id ≠ committed_block` **and** (committed node resident) `g_view > committed_node.view` (state:1098–1117). **Corrections (A20.1):**
  - **"`own_qc=None` ⇒ never the G" is withdrawn as an over-claim.** `own_qc=None` is an **initialization-time** property of the anchor; the predicate's `if g.own_qc.is_none() { return }` is an **evaluation-time** check. So the precise statement is: *while `C.own_qc` is `None` at the moment `try_commit` evaluates `C` as `G`, that check returns (no commit via `C`-as-`G`)*; a later `on_qc` on `C`'s key would set `C.own_qc` and remove **that** particular barrier — the other predicates (strict views, floor, `should_commit`'s `g_id ≠ committed_block`) would then be evaluated on their own.
  - **A self-parented node excludes only the `B`/`P` roles, not the `G` role by its parent pointer.** `try_commit` does **not** inspect `G.parent_id`. A self-parent (`parent_id = Some(self)`) makes the node alias itself when used as `B` or `P` (then `P==B` or `G==P`, so the strict-view chain `g_view<p_view<b_view` collapses to equal views and fails). As `G` the node's own parent pointer is irrelevant to the predicate; a self-parented `G` is excluded (if at all) only by its `own_qc`/view/floor/`should_commit`, evaluated separately.
  - Therefore "no commit follows from acceptance or same-key registration alone" holds **because predicates (1)–(4) are not *jointly* satisfied** (A21 — individual predicates such as the strict-view or height-floor condition may well hold on their own; the point is the conjunction fails): at the relevant evaluation the required `own_qc` is absent (no QC attached by registration), and `committed_block` still names the anchor so `should_commit`'s `g_id ≠ committed_block` fails when `G=C`. This is **not** a blanket "never G" and **not** "none of the predicates is individually satisfiable" — it is "the conjunction is not met" — and §26.2N confirms the concrete transition reaches no QC, hence no commit.

**L-7. Return of resolved premises to CONS-3 (explicit; no closure).** The §26.2d case-table rows "Fresh restore, branch C, collision" (anchor-form premise `C[0:16]=P_{h+k}`, rows at lines ~2836/2838) cited this as an **upstream OBL-STO-1b/T-A18-2** dependency. A20 Part B **discharges that upstream premise at available-source level**: `C[0:16]` (and `C[16:32]`) are operator-settable (L-2, only the 64-hex parse touches `block_hash`), so the β-collision prefix input `C[0:16]=P_{h+k}` is **constructible** — **the `block_hash` rejecting check the earlier rows were waiting on does not exist.** The chain_id/height/authority/epoch checks are **prerequisites that constrain the crafted snapshot** (it must be chain-id/authority-marker/epoch *consistent* with local state — §26.2L L-4/item 3, A21), **not** automatically operator-controllable fields; they bound the attacker to a consistent forgery rather than permitting an arbitrary one. **This does NOT yield a commit and does NOT close OBL-CONS-3**, for reasons kept strictly separate:
1. The β branch produces a **view-advance only** (an established *conditional* transition, §26.2d/§26.2b) — **not** a commit.
2. At evaluation time the anchor's `own_qc` is `None`, so a `try_commit` evaluating the anchor as `G` returns at that check (A16.3/A19.11-D4) — an **evaluation-time** fact, not a permanent "never G" (L-6, A20.1); and case-A's self-parent overwrite makes the replaced node alias itself when used as `B`/`P` (strict-view chain fails), while as `G` its parent pointer is not inspected — so the no-commit result rests on the separately-evaluated predicates (no `own_qc`, `should_commit`'s `g_id ≠ committed_block` failing when `G=C`), per §26.2N.
3. **γ** (completing-quorum) and the **general resident-parent / d2 committed-floor-&-lineage** obligation remain **open** (§26.2f/j); anchor-form reachability does not bear on them.
4. Realization is **EXEC(E22)** (crafted snapshot + local-write + deployment).
So the resolved item is **the upstream anchor-form premise only**; **OBL-CONS-3 stays SR-PARTIAL · EXEC(E03)**. The d3 reference in §26.2j/§26.2k ("where `B_pre`/`G` is the restore anchor → OBL-STO-1b/T-A18-2") is now answered with the corrected (evaluation-time) phrasing: the anchor is **accepted opaquely with `own_qc=None`**, so **while that holds at evaluation** a `try_commit` with `G =` the anchor returns at the `g.own_qc.is_none()` check; and even were a QC later attached to the anchor's key, `should_commit`'s `g_id ≠ committed_block` would fail for `G =` the still-committed anchor id — so a *new* commit would require a **distinct resident `own_qc`-bearing** `G` (d1+d2), not the anchor itself. This is a per-predicate conclusion, not a blanket "never G."

**L-8. OBL-STO-1b disposition.** The available-source deliverable ("L3 restore-acceptance of a `P‖P` block_id + general same-key reachability — available source read") is now **performed**: restore-acceptance of any opaque `C` (including `P‖P` case A and `P‖R` case B) is **source-established** (L-1/L-2, no rejecting check), and the same-key registration/replacement semantics are **source-established** (L-6). The anchor-entry-preservation premise (A16.3) is characterized precisely: `N_C` is preserved **until** a same-key `register_block(C, …)` overwrites it, which resets `own_qc=None` and recomputes `height` from the registration's parent. **Two established overwrite transitions (A21 — not "case A only"):** (i) **pure fresh-restore case A** (`C=P_v‖P_v`, lock `None`) → the first leader proposal builds on `committed_block=C`, derives id `C`, and overwrites `N_C` to a **self-parent** (`parent=Some(C)`, height `h+1`); (ii) **catch-up-then-leader case B** (`C=P_v‖P_{v+1}`, lock `=qc_B2` after catch-up, §26.2N) → the leader builds on the lock `B2`, derives id `C`, and overwrites `N_C` to a **non-self parent** (`parent=Some(B2)`, `justify_qc=Some(qc_B2)`, height `v+2`). So preservation holds against *eviction* (height floor) but **not** against a same-key re-registration, and that re-registration arises in **both** case A (self-parent) and case B (non-self-parent) — the v0.64 "case A only / self-parent" characterization is **corrected** to include the case-B replacement. Residuals are **EXEC(E22)** (crafted-snapshot realization, deployment) and the **downstream commit**, which is **CONS-3's** (returned in L-7, not owned here). **A20.1 scope note (so SR-DONE is not inflated):** what is source-complete is (i) restore-**acceptance** of an opaque `C` (any form, no `block_hash` rejecting check), (ii) the same-key registration/replacement **mechanics** (overwrite, `own_qc` reset, self-parent, height recompute), and (iii) the **specific examined transitions** — the pure fresh-restore first leader proposal (case A/B-pure) and the catch-up-then-leader case-B sequence (§26.2N) — each traced to **no commit / no QC / no view advance**. What is **NOT** claimed here and stays an open question routed to **CONS-3**: a **general multi-batch same-key reachability induction** and whether *any* reachable same-key sequence yields a commit — A20.1 deliberately did **no** lineage induction or later-batch expansion (per task scope), so this remains CONS-3's general resident-parent/`U` obligation, **not** silently converted to EXEC. **OBL-STO-1b → SR-DONE source · EXEC(E22)** for the acceptance + registration-mechanics + examined-transitions slice (available-source complete; crafted-snapshot execution = EXEC); the general-reachability commit consequence is **explicitly left open under CONS-3**, not absorbed into this SR-DONE. **No new finding, no closure of CONS-3 or C4/C5; RS1 unchanged; baseline not re-pinned; counts recomputed in §25 without forcing.**

**M-2. Four responder questions, dispositioned.**
1. **Production caller + origin/config gates.** The sole production caller is the inbound `RestoreCatchupRequest` arm (binary:6998), reached for every inbound consensus frame. Admission gate = **Run 418 transport-origin binding** (`binding_gate.authorize(origin, claimed_requester)`), fail-closed in production; **the responder is NOT gated on the node's own restore-mode** — the request arm does not even receive `restore_mode` (contrast the response arm, which does). So a node that is **not** itself catching up still answers origin-bound requests. The outbound facade must be present (step 4).
2. **Request validation + returned-block source/selection.** The request carries only `{requester_validator_index, from_height, from_block_id}` (no signatures). Validation beyond the origin bind is the self-request guard (step 3). Returned blocks come from the **responder's own local block tree**, filtered to an **`own_qc`-bearing** contiguous chain above the requested anchor, **lowest-view-first**, ≤128. **Supported property (A20.1, narrowed):** the responder **exports locally stored nodes that carry a logical `own_qc`** — nothing more is established. "`own_qc` present" is the **logical-QC** condition (set by `on_qc` when a key reaches logical quorum, A17-F1 class); it does **not** establish independent (cryptographic) endorsement of those blocks, and a responder whose own `own_qc` blocks were themselves formed from forged logical signers (A17-F1) would export exactly those. The earlier "does not fabricate or forward unverified material" wording is **withdrawn** as over-strong — the precise statement is "exports its own locally-`own_qc`'d nodes; independent endorsement is not established by that condition."
3. **Signer-index + endorsement-evidence source.** Signer indices = the exported block's `own_qc.signers` (logical validator indices), transmitted as `qc_signer_indices: Vec<u16>`. **No endorsement evidence (signatures/QC bytes) is included** — consistent with A17-F1 (the wire carries no signatures; the applier's `qc.validate` is logical-only). The `proposer_index` is **re-derived by the responder** from `leader_for_view(view)`, not copied from the stored node.
4. **Bounds / empty / error outcomes / state mutations.** Bound = 128 blocks/response. Empty export (no matching `own_qc` chain) → **no reply** (step 6). Self-request or missing facade → no reply (steps 3–4). Send error → logged, no retry. **No engine/consensus-state mutation occurs on the responder path** — supported by the callee bodies (`export_restore_catchup_blocks`/`committed_height` only read; no interior-mutability wrapper over the engine's consensus fields), not by the `&` type alone (step 10); only local `stats` counters change; the broadcast enqueue is a transport effect separate from engine state. Response **audience is all connected peers** (broadcast), not the requester alone (step 9).

- **`handle_restore_catchup_response`** (def binary:7865): sole caller = **binary:7017** (production inbound `RestoreCatchupResponse` arm), reached after the Run 418 responder-origin bind.

- **Production restore-mode** is `active = cfg.restore_baseline.is_some()` (binary:2048, via `RestoreCatchupModeState::from_config`), **immutable except the one-way active→inactive exit** (`maybe_exit_after_response`, binary:2065–2104: exits once `local_committed_height ≥ peer_max_observed` and strictly above the snapshot baseline; `if !self.active { return None }` makes it monotone).
- **Request broadcasting** is gated by `restore_catchup_enabled = cfg.restore_baseline.is_some()` (binary:2619) **plus** a tick cadence (binary:7780) — so only a restore-baselined node *emits* requests.

OBL-CONS-10 disposition (A20.1-narrowed).** The responder construction/trust and the restart/sim caller boundary are **source-dispositioned**: the responder is **read-only on engine state** (supported by the callee bodies — `export_restore_catchup_blocks`/`committed_height` only read, and the engine's consensus fields carry no interior-mutability wrapper — not by the `&` type alone; mutates only `stats`), **origin-gated** (Run 418), **broadcasts** its response **to all registered peers** (not a requester-only reply — wired `TcpKemTlsP2pService::broadcast` iterates `self.peers` and per-peer `try_send(msg.clone())`, best-effort drop-on-full, p2p_tcp.rs:2106–2115; `send_to` not used; request-origin admission gates the trigger, not the audience), **exports only its own locally-`own_qc`'d** blocks (≤128, lowest-view-first) — a **logical**-QC condition that does **not** establish independent endorsement (A17-F1 class) — and carries **logical signer indices with no endorsement evidence**; there is **no sim/restart production caller** of export/apply (only the two inbound handlers in production, plus unit tests whose admission is non-production). The **remaining question is EXEC/deployment (E20)**: whether, in a DevNet catch-up-enabled configuration with a given validator set, a malicious origin-bound requester can usefully harvest a responder's broadcast blocks, or a malicious responder's logical-signer response drives a victim's applier (the latter is the already-recorded **A17-F1** surface; the responder side adds no new finding — it discloses, to all peers, blocks it already holds with a logical `own_qc`, and independent endorsement of those is not claimed). **OBL-CONS-10 → SR-DONE source · EXEC(E20)** — the available-source responder/caller trace is complete; the one remaining item is genuinely EXEC/deployment, not an unperformed available-source trace. **No new finding, no closure of C4/C5/CONS-3; RS1 unchanged; counts recomputed in §25 without forcing.**

### 26.2N A20.1 — the finite prefix-only (case-B) replacement candidate, traced to its exact outcome; + case-A direct-catch-up admission

A20.1 checks the specific proposed symbolic trace in the task. **This is a proposed source trace, not an established production sequence or an execution result;** it is traced to either a jointly-admissible transition or an exact rejecting condition, firsthand at `ef99e29`. Premises (all as given): `v=h+1`; `P_x = LE64(leader_for_view(x))‖LE64(x)`; `N=4`, uniform unit weights, `q = two_thirds_vp = ceil(2·4/3) = 3`; `local_id = leader_for_view(v)`; `1 ≤ h` and `h+4 ≤ u64::MAX`; fresh restored state; stable membership; no relevant prior votes; no eviction; no earlier leader self-vote at `v`. **Prefix-only anchor** `C = P_v ‖ P_{v+1}` (case B: `C[16:32] = P_{v+1} ≠ P_v = C[0:16]`).

**Block-id algebra (firsthand, derive_block_id_from_header basic:2043–2058):** `D(proposer, view, parent) = LE64(proposer) ‖ LE64(view) ‖ parent[0:16]`.
- `B1 = D(leader_v, v, C) = P_v ‖ C[0:16] = P_v ‖ P_v` (parent `C`, since `C[0:16]=P_v`).
- `B2 = D(leader_{v+1}, v+1, B1) = P_{v+1} ‖ B1[0:16] = P_{v+1} ‖ P_v` (parent `B1`, since `B1[0:16]=P_v`).
