### 26.2o A33 — resume OBL-CONS-3: the all-distinct resident-parent commit case via β (read-only source at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review. Resumes OBL-CONS-3 under T-A18-1; reuses the §26.2j predicate packet and the completed sub-edges below. **Bounded; no new finding; no SR-DONE claimed; counts derived.** Does not reopen the completed §37.13 receiver trace, the N=4 emission witness, or attempt the general CONS-3 lineage (J) proof.

**Current CONS-3 dependency table (from the latest supported results).**

| Sub-edge | Latest result | Status for the commit question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CONS-1 / §37 — inbound Timeout/TC admission, signed-field limits, immediate mutations | **source-reviewed (§37.13, SR-DONE source)**; `tc.view` (target) and high_qc endorsement unsigned (A1-F2/A1-F3) | provides how a lock/`own_qc` can be installed via inbound TC; admission is not the open edge |
| §26.2k — inbound TC lock install | **resolved (conditional admission):** `set_locked_qc(tc.high_qc)` names an **existing resident** block id; **creates no block node and attaches no `own_qc`** | a TC lock alone does **not** give any block an `own_qc` |
| STO-1b / §26.2L — restore-anchor acceptance | **source-reviewed:** opaque operator-supplied anchor; anchor `own_qc=None` is an **evaluation-time** property, **not** a permanent guarantee (same-key registration can mutate it) | if `B`/`P`/`G` is the anchor, its `own_qc` may be absent *then* but is not permanently fixed |
| §26.2j — resident-parent predicate case split | **absent-node, absent-`own_qc`, alias** cases → bounded **no-commit**; **all-distinct** case = the exact remaining dependency (B-5) | the case under review here |
| §26.2i — β / γ / α QC-return mechanisms | **β** = re-evaluation of an already-quorate `(view,block_id)` key; **γ** = completing insertion; **α** = the separate N=1 self-quorum | this review uses **β** (no γ/U premise needed to obtain `B`'s QC) |
| §26.2N — case-B anchor replacement | documented **map overwrite + `own_qc` reset**, but **no** self-vote QC or commit *in that particular sequence* | same-key `register_block` resets the overwritten node's `own_qc` to `None` |

The completed admission/anchor sub-edges are kept **separate** from the unresolved question of whether all required state conditions **coexist**. Invariant **J** is **not** carried forward as proved, and **not** as an equivalence over both obligations; **γ⟹¬U** is preserved only within its established scope (reverse implication and γ-reachability unestablished, §26.2g).

**Commit definition (precise).** A **new leader-driven commit** = a commit of `G` caused by *this* `on_leader_step` self-vote invocation's `on_vote→on_qc→try_commit_with_qc` path (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2351` → `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:983→995→1029`), distinct from any commit already produced by catch-up. It is **not** equated with "off-chain commit".

**Map entries at evaluation** (tracked independently): `B` = the just-registered leader block (`id = derive_block_id_from_header(local_id, current_view cv, parent)`, `make_block_id` basic:2061–2063); `P` = `B.parent_id` entry = `locked_qc.block_id` (else `committed_block`), per `on_leader_step` basic:2246–2250; `G` = `P.parent_id` entry; plus `committed_block`/`committed_height` at that instant. Each entry carries its own id, stored view/height/parent, `own_qc`, last-registration provenance; the retained accumulator quorum's provenance is tracked **separately** from map-entry fields.

**β trace (the all-distinct case), conditions traced together.**
1. **Caller / eligibility.** `on_leader_step` runs only if `is_leader_for_current_view()` and `!proposed_in_view` (basic:2229–2235); production-reached via `do_leader_tick`→`try_propose` (§26.2a). It registers `B` with `parent_id = locked_qc.block_id | committed_block` and `justify_qc = locked_qc` (basic:2246–2256), then self-votes `state.on_vote(local_id, cv, &B)` (basic:2351).
2. **`register_block(B,cv,parent,justify)`** (state:731–760) computes `height` from the parent entry, **inserts/overwrites** `B`'s node with **`own_qc = None`** (own_qc never set here), **and then calls `evict_blocks_if_needed()`** (state:760). ⟨**A33.1**⟩ All-distinct ⇒ `B∉{P,G}`, so the **overwrite** does not touch `P`/`G`; but residency of `P`/`G` must be established through the **complete** operation including eviction (`evict_blocks_if_needed` can drop other nodes under the slot cap). The load-bearing property at `try_commit` is **`P`/`G` *present with `own_qc`* at evaluation**, **not** the stronger "`G` was never overwritten" — an overwritten entry can later receive a QC again via a subsequent `on_qc`. (The alias/same-id `own_qc` reset is the separate §26.2j/§26.2N case, excluded in the all-distinct configuration.)
3. **Derived-id equality with the retained quorum key.** β requires the **vote** accumulator (`VoteAccumulator`, not `TimeoutAccumulator`) to already hold a `≥two_thirds_vp` quorum at the key `(cv, B)` *before* the self-vote. ⟨**A33.1 producer correction**⟩ those prior votes are **not** necessarily genuine cryptographically-authenticated consensus votes: the **catch-up** path (`apply_restore_catchup_blocks`, basic:2122) validates a *logical signer-id list* (`QuorumCertificate::new(block_id, view, qc_signers).validate(validators)` — membership/quorum/dup only, **no signatures** — this is the **A17-F1** posture) and then calls `state.on_vote(signer, view, &block_id)` for each listed id, writing those votes into the `VoteAccumulator` and the local vote-history. So the retained `(cv,B)` quorum can be catch-up-written from a logical list; A17-F1's origin/admission prerequisites are preserved and **no** consensus-signature requirement is added (the earlier "genuine, unforgeable-without-keys votes" claim is **withdrawn**). `VoteAccumulator::maybe_qc_for((cv,B))` (vote_accumulator.rs:357–382) returns `Some(qc)` **iff** that key's signer set validates to quorum; `two_thirds_vp = (2·total).div_ceil(3)` (validator_set.rs:491–495) = **3** for N=4 unit weight. So β needs ≥3 prior votes retained at the leader's **own derived id** `B` at `cv`, **not** supplied by this invocation. ⟨**A33.3** — the surviving "genuine / unforgeable-without-keys votes" requirement is **removed**⟩ those retained votes need **not** be cryptographically-authenticated consensus votes: the catch-up path writes them from a **logical signer-id list** (`QuorumCertificate::new(...).validate` — membership/quorum/dup only, **no signatures**, the **A17-F1** posture), so the premise is **logical-signer catch-up provenance** (A17-F1's own origin/admission prerequisites preserved), not a key-authentication premise. This invocation supplies only the self-vote.
4. **`on_vote(local_id,cv,&B)`** (state:952–986): ⟨**A33.1**⟩ `record_vote_history(local_id,cv,B)` is a **real guard**, not discharged by the no-second-self-vote lemma: catch-up writes vote-history for the *listed signer ids* (e.g. {1,2,3}), so the leader's **own** id may already have a view-`cv` entry from some other path — the outcome is `FirstVote` (no prior local entry), `DuplicateSameBlock` (prior entry for the **same** B ⇒ proceeds), or `Equivocation` (prior entry for a **different** block id at `cv` ⇒ `Ok(None)`, vote ignored, **no** QC via this call). Only `FirstVote`/`DuplicateSameBlock` reach `votes.on_vote` → `maybe_qc_for((cv,B))`. ⟨**A33.2** — β does **not** require a successful insert⟩ `votes.on_vote` returns `Err` **only** on non-membership (the `?` then aborts *before* `maybe_qc_for`); a **duplicate/per-view-capacity `Ok(false)`** does **not** abort — `on_vote` proceeds to `maybe_qc_for` regardless. So the sufficient condition for β is: **not `Equivocation`** and **local_id a current member** (no `Err`); the self-vote's own insert succeeding (`Ok(true)`) is **not** required. Under β, `maybe_qc_for` returns `Some(qc_B)` from the **already-retained** quorum (the self-vote's weight is not needed — **no γ/U premise**).
5. **`on_qc(qc_B)`** (state:995–1016): ⟨**A33.1 corrections**⟩ its **lock-replacement branch and its resident-node attach are independent**. Lock replace tests `qc_B.view > v_L` where **`v_L` = the retained `locked_qc.view` before this self-vote** (not `P.view`; a TC-reported lock view can be arbitrary, e.g. 100, so replacement may **not** occur). Separately and unconditionally, `B.own_qc ← Some(qc_B)` **iff B is a resident node** (the attach is guarded by `blocks.get_mut(&qc.block_id)`, independent of whether the lock was replaced). Then `try_commit_with_qc(qc_B)`. (`set_locked_qc` used by the TC path attaches **no** `own_qc`; only `on_qc`'s attach sets one — these are distinct.)
6. **`try_commit_with_qc(qc_B)`** (state:1029–1090): `B.own_qc` Some ✓ (just set); `P = B.parent` must be resident with `P.own_qc` Some (else `return`, no commit); `G = P.parent` must be resident with `G.own_qc` Some (else `return`); **strict views** `G.view < P.view < B.view(=cv)` (`:1087`); then the **complete `should_commit` branches** (⟨A33.1⟩ preserved in full): `committed_block == None` ⇒ **true**; else `committed_id == g_id` ⇒ **false** (already committed); else `blocks.get(committed_id)` present ⇒ `g_view > committed_node.view`; else (committed node **absent** from tree) ⇒ **true** ("allow commit to move forward"); **AND** the height floor `height_ok` = `committed_height==None || g_height > committed_height`. Commit of `G` only if `should_commit && height_ok`. (Earlier shorthand `G.view > committed_node.view`) ⇒ commit `G`, advance tip.

```rust
// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:952-986  on_vote (⟨A33.1⟩ normalized: method-chains collapsed to one line; guards/returns unchanged)
    pub fn on_vote(&mut self, voter: ValidatorId, view: u64, block_id: &BlockIdT)
        -> Result<Option<QuorumCertificate<BlockIdT>>, QcValidationError> {
        match self.record_vote_history(voter, view, block_id) {
            VoteHistoryOutcome::Equivocation { previous_block: _ } => {
                self.equivocations_detected += 1;
                self.equivocating_validators.insert(voter);
                return Ok(None);
            }
            VoteHistoryOutcome::FirstVote | VoteHistoryOutcome::DuplicateSameBlock => {}
        }
        let _is_new = self.votes.on_vote(&self.validators, voter, view, block_id)?;
        let qc = self.votes.maybe_qc_for(&self.validators, view, block_id)?;
        if let Some(ref qc) = qc { self.on_qc(qc)?; }
        Ok(qc)
    }
```

```rust
// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1246-1270  initialize_from_snapshot_baseline (contiguous; comment lines retained)
    pub fn initialize_from_snapshot_baseline(
        &mut self, committed_block_id: BlockIdT, committed_view: u64, committed_height: u64,
    ) {
        self.committed_block = Some(committed_block_id.clone());
        self.committed_height = Some(committed_height);
        // Insert the snapshot anchor block into the tree at the recorded height.
        // parent_id = None, justify_qc = None, own_qc = None (never a 3-chain G).
        let node = BlockNode::new(
            committed_block_id.clone(), committed_view, None, None, committed_height,
        );
        let is_new = !self.blocks.contains_key(&committed_block_id);
        self.insert_block_node(node);
        if is_new {
            // `is_block_safe_to_evict` refuses to evict any block whose
            // height ≤ committed_height.
            self.pending_block_order.push_back(committed_block_id);
        }
    }
```
⟨**A33.2** — the v1.14 excerpt stopped at `BlockNode::new(`; the contiguous body through insertion is supplied above (`hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1269–1283`, verbatim, comment lines retained). The anchor is inserted (`insert_block_node`, a same-id-replacing `blocks.insert`) at `height=committed_height`, `own_qc=None`, and is **eviction-protected** by `is_block_safe_to_evict` rule #1 (`height ≤ committed_height`); see §26.2q.

```rust
// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:596-653  is_block_safe_to_evict  ⟨A33.5 label fix⟩ NORMALIZED (multi-line `if {…}` bodies collapsed to one line; `//`-comment and blank lines dropped) — NOT line-for-line verbatim; the genuine line-numbered verbatim body is in §26.2s's evidence packet
    fn is_block_safe_to_evict(&self, block_id: &BlockIdT) -> bool {
        if let Some(committed_height) = self.committed_height {
            if let Some(block) = self.blocks.get(block_id) {
                if block.height <= committed_height { return false; }
            }
        }
        if let Some(locked_qc) = &self.locked_qc {
            let locked_block_id = &locked_qc.block_id;
            if block_id == locked_block_id { return false; }
            let mut current_id = locked_block_id;
            while let Some(current) = self.blocks.get(current_id) {
                if let Some(parent_id) = &current.parent_id {
                    if parent_id == block_id { return false; }
                    current_id = parent_id;
                } else { break; }
            }
        }
        if let Some(block) = self.blocks.get(block_id) {
            if block.own_qc.is_some() { return false; }
        }
        for (other_id, other_block) in &self.blocks {
            if other_block.own_qc.is_some() {
                let mut current_id = other_id;
                while let Some(current) = self.blocks.get(current_id) {
                    if let Some(parent_id) = &current.parent_id {
                        if parent_id == block_id { return false; }
                        current_id = parent_id;
                    } else { break; }
                }
            }
        }
        true
    }
```

**(Part 3+4) The bounded overwrite→eviction case, reusing §26.2N.**

§26.2N (A20.1) already traced a **jointly-admissible** source sequence (restore at `(h,C)` → two catch-up blocks → a rejected 3rd → one leader step) whose leader self-proposed block's derived id resolves to the anchor id `C` (block-id algebra `D(local_id,v,B2)=P_v‖B2[0:16]=P_v‖P_{v+1}=C`), so `register_block` **overwrites the committed anchor's own map entry**. This is the same-id re-registration of a committed id — **not wholly unestablished**; §26.2N supplies its exact admissible end-state. (It is distinct from overwriting a node *previously committed by `try_commit`*: here `C` is the restored snapshot anchor, committed only in the sense `committed_block=C`.) The §26.2N end-state (verbatim from §26.2N):

- `committed_block = C`, `committed_height = h` — **unchanged scalars**.
- `C` node overwritten to `{view=v, parent=Some(B2), justify_qc=Some(qc_B2), own_qc=None, height=v+2}` (since catch-up applied `B1` at `height=v=h+1`, the overwrite height is `v+2=h+3 > h`).
- `C.parent=B2`, `B2.parent=B1`, `B1.parent=C` — the **3-cycle `C→B2→B1→C`**.
- `B1`,`B2` resident **with `own_qc`** (`qc_B1`,`qc_B2`); `locked_qc=qc_B2` (names `B2`, view `v+1`).

**All four eviction protections for `C`, evaluated in this actual state** (`is_block_safe_to_evict(C)`, state:596–653):

| Protection | Clause (source) | Outcome for `C` in the §26.2N state | Terminates? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#1 committed-height** | `committed_height` set ∧ `C.height <= committed_height` (L597–601) | **LOST** — `C.height = v+2 = h+3`, `committed_height = h`; `h+3 <= h` is **false** ⇒ #1 does not protect | yes |
| **#2 locked block / ancestor** | `C == locked_id`? else walk parents from `locked_id=B2` (L603–620) | **PROTECTS** — walk `B2`→parent `B1`→parent `C`; at `B1`, `parent_id == C` ⇒ `return false` | yes (matches before the cycle repeats) |
| **#3 own_qc** | `C.own_qc.is_some()` (L623–627) | **ABSENT** — overwrite set `own_qc=None` ⇒ #3 does not protect | yes |
| **#4 ancestor of `own_qc`-bearer** | for each `own_qc` block, walk parents (L630–645) | **PROTECTS** — `B1` has `own_qc`; walk `B1`→parent `C`; `parent_id == C` ⇒ `return false` (also via `B2`→`B1`→`C`) | yes |

⇒ **`is_block_safe_to_evict(C) = false`** — `C` remains protected by **#2 and #4**, independently of the lost #1 and absent #3. **The loss of the height protection and the absence of `C.own_qc` do NOT remove `C`'s protection**, exactly because the lock and the `own_qc`-bearing descendants (`B1`,`B2`) still cover it.

**Subsequent lock-changing TC — re-evaluated.** If an admitted inbound TC later installs a new lock naming a block off the `C`/`B2` chain, protection **#2** may drop for `C`. But a TC lock install (`on_timeout_certificate`→`set_locked_qc`, §26.2k) **changes only `locked_qc`**; it **creates no node, attaches no `own_qc`, and deletes nothing**. So `B1`,`B2` remain resident with `own_qc`, and `C` remains their ancestor ⇒ **#4 still protects `C`**. Defeating `C`'s eviction therefore requires, in addition, **changing the current `own_qc`-ancestry relation that makes `C` an ancestor of a QC-bearer** — ⟨A34⟩ `own_qc` removal from `B1`/`B2` is **one** possible way (not necessary; parent replacement, path disconnection, or QC reattachment would also change it); note `B1`/`B2` are themselves protected (`own_qc` ⇒ #3, and each is the locked block or its ancestor). No inspected transition does this.

**Queue (`pending_block_order`) and traversal mechanics (Part 4, exact).**

- **Enqueue sites** (verbatim source): `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` `push_back(committed_block_id)` **iff `is_new`** (state:1281); `register_block` `push_back(id)` **iff `is_new`** (state:758); `register_block_with_verified_justification` `push_back(id)` **iff `is_new`** (state:881). A **same-id overwrite re-enqueues nothing** — all three guard on `is_new = !blocks.contains_key(&id)`, which is **false** for an existing id. So in the §26.2N state `C` sits in `pending_block_order` **once** (from restore); the leader step's `register_block(C,…)` has `is_new=false` and does **not** re-enqueue it. Queue after Step A+leader ≈ `[C, B1, B2]` (all resident).
- **What `evict_blocks_if_needed` does with a protected id** (state:659–678; ⟨A34⟩ **normalized** in §26.2q, **line-for-line verbatim in §26.2s**): the inner `while let Some(block_id) = pending_block_order.pop_front()` **pops** an id; if it is not (`contains_key ∧ is_block_safe_to_evict`) the body does nothing and the loop **pops the next** — the popped protected id is **discarded from the queue and never re-queued**. ⟨**A33.4 correction** — two ordering caveats⟩ **(a)** the inner pop loop runs **only** inside the outer `while self.blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks` (state:661); in a state **below** the cap nothing is popped at all. **(b)** "no safe id ⇒ the queue drains and the loop `break`s" holds **only if every `is_block_safe_to_evict` call terminates**. When the `blocks` map holds a parent **cycle** and a popped id is **off** that cycle, the `#2`/`#4` parent-walk is **non-terminating**, so the next `pop_front` and the final `break` are **never reached** — execution ceases mid-check rather than draining. When all resident ids are **on** the cycle (`{C,B1,B2}`), each `is_block_safe_to_evict` **does** terminate (returns `false` by matching the cycle), so *if* the cap were exceeded the loop would pop-and-drop `C`,`B1`,`B2` and `break`; but §26.2N's small end-state is **below** the cap, so this never runs here (§26.2s checks the finite capacity-trigger that does). Net in the small state: **nodes `C`,`B1`,`B2` stay in `blocks` and `C` stays queued** (no eviction ran).
- **"Becoming safe later" does not imply revisiting.** Once `C`'s single queue entry is popped-and-dropped, even if `C` later became safe (e.g. `B1`/`B2` removed), `evict_blocks_if_needed` would **not** revisit `C`: it only pops from `pending_block_order`, and only a fresh `is_new` registration re-enqueues an id. Since `C` is resident, `register_block(C,…)` has `is_new=false` ⇒ no re-enqueue. So the legacy path cannot later evict `C` without an intervening removal + re-add.
- **`reserve_block_slot_for_new` classified by actual callers.** Its **only** caller is `register_block_with_verified_justification` (state:860, the Run-422 verified-ingestion path). The **legacy `register_block`** path calls `evict_blocks_if_needed` (state:762), **not** `reserve`. So `reserve`'s **up-front `Err(SlotCapacityUnavailable)`** (admissibility decided by `count_safe_to_evict_excluding(id) < deficit`, no eviction on shortfall) must **not** be transferred to the legacy path — that caller composition does not exist. (⟨A33.3 correction⟩ v1.15 attributed `reserve`'s up-front refusal to the committed-node protection generally; the legacy path's protection comes from `evict_blocks_if_needed`'s safe-gate, not from `reserve`.) Note `reserve` additionally has a **full-scan fallback** (state:546–561) over `blocks.keys()` filtered by `is_block_safe_to_evict`, independent of `pending_block_order`; it still evicts **only** `is_block_safe_to_evict` blocks, so it **never** evicts the protected `C`.

**Ancestry-walk termination against the `C→B2→B1→C` cycle (Part 4).** `is_block_safe_to_evict`'s clauses #2 (L603–620) and #4 (L630–645) walk the parent chain with `while let Some(current) = self.blocks.get(current_id)` and **no visited-set / depth bound**. Distinguishing the cases:

| Checked id | On the cycle? | #2/#4 parent-walk behaviour | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `C` | yes | `B2`→`B1`→`parent==C` matches | **returns `false`** (terminates) |
| `B1` | yes | `B2`→`parent==B1` matches | **returns `false`** (terminates) |
| `B2` | yes (locked) | caught by `block_id==locked_id` (L605) | **returns `false`** (terminates) |
| unrelated `U` | **no** | `B2`→`B1`→`C`→`B2`→… never matches `U`, every node has a present parent ⇒ never breaks | **does not terminate** (unbounded loop) — ⟨A34⟩ **only** once the preceding guards pass (`U` survives #1; `locked_qc=Some` and `U≠locked`; the walk from the locked id reaches the cycle without an earlier `parent==U` match or a missing-parent `break`), per the full conjunction above |

So for the committed-node question the walk **terminates and returns `false`** (C protected). The **non-termination arises only** when `is_block_safe_to_evict` is called with a `block_id` **not on the cycle** while the cycle is resident **and the full conjunction below holds** — ⟨A35⟩ an off-cycle target is **necessary but not sufficient**: the target must also survive the #1 height check, the lock (for #2) must name a node whose `parent_id` chain **reaches** the cycle, and no earlier `parent==target` match or missing-parent `break` occurs (see the itemized guards (i)–(v) next).

```rust
// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:596-653  is_block_safe_to_evict — VERBATIM (comment + blank lines retained; nothing collapsed)
    fn is_block_safe_to_evict(&self, block_id: &BlockIdT) -> bool {
        // 1. Check if block is committed
        if let Some(committed_height) = self.committed_height {
            if let Some(block) = self.blocks.get(block_id) {
                if block.height <= committed_height {
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }

        // 2. Check if block is locked block or its ancestor
        if let Some(locked_qc) = &self.locked_qc {
            let locked_block_id = &locked_qc.block_id;
            if block_id == locked_block_id {
                return false;
            }
            // Walk up from locked block to see if this block is an ancestor
            let mut current_id = locked_block_id;
            while let Some(current) = self.blocks.get(current_id) {
                if let Some(parent_id) = &current.parent_id {
                    if parent_id == block_id {
                        return false;
                    }
                    current_id = parent_id;
                } else {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        // 3. Check if block has own_qc (part of a QC chain)
        if let Some(block) = self.blocks.get(block_id) {
            if block.own_qc.is_some() {
                return false;
            }
        }

        // 4. Check if block is an ancestor of any block with own_qc
        for (other_id, other_block) in &self.blocks {
            if other_block.own_qc.is_some() {
                // Walk up from this block to see if block_id is an ancestor
                let mut current_id = other_id;
                while let Some(current) = self.blocks.get(current_id) {
                    if let Some(parent_id) = &current.parent_id {
                        if parent_id == block_id {
                            return false;
                        }
                        current_id = parent_id;
                    } else {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        true
    }
```
The two `while let Some(current) = self.blocks.get(current_id)` loops (#2 at :614, #4 at :638) advance `current_id` only along `parent_id` and exit **only** by (a) `parent_id == block_id` → `return false`, (b) `parent_id == None` → `break`, or (c) `self.blocks.get(current_id) == None` → loop end.     pub fn apply_restore_catchup_blocks(
```rust
        &mut self,
        blocks: &[RestoreCatchupBlock<[u8; 32]>],
    ) -> Result<usize, RestoreCatchupError<[u8; 32]>> {
        if blocks.is_empty() {
            return Ok(0);
        }

        let mut expected_height = self
            .committed_height()
            .ok_or(RestoreCatchupError::MissingLocalAnchor)?
            .saturating_add(1);
        let mut expected_parent = *self
            .committed_block()
            .ok_or(RestoreCatchupError::MissingLocalAnchor)?;
        let mut previous_qc: Option<QuorumCertificate<[u8; 32]>> = self.locked_qc().cloned();
        let mut applied = 0usize;

        for block in blocks {
            if block.height != expected_height {
                return Err(RestoreCatchupError::NonContiguousHeight {
                    expected: expected_height,
                    actual: block.height,
                });
            }
            if block.parent_block_id != expected_parent {
                return Err(RestoreCatchupError::AnchorMismatch {
                    expected_height,
                    actual_height: block.height,
                    expected_block_id: expected_parent,
                    actual_parent_block_id: block.parent_block_id,
                });
            }
            if block.height != block.view {
                return Err(RestoreCatchupError::HeightViewMismatch {
                    height: block.height,
                    view: block.view,
                });
            }
            let expected_proposer = self.leader_for_view(block.view);
            if block.proposer != expected_proposer {
                return Err(RestoreCatchupError::WrongProposer {
                    view: block.view,
                    expected: expected_proposer,
                    actual: block.proposer,
                });
            }
            let expected_block_id = Self::derive_block_id_from_header(
                block.proposer,
                block.view,
                &block.parent_block_id,
            );
            if block.block_id != expected_block_id {
                return Err(RestoreCatchupError::BlockIdMismatch {
                    height: block.height,
                    expected: expected_block_id,
                    actual: block.block_id,
                });
            }

            let qc = QuorumCertificate::new(block.block_id, block.view, block.qc_signers.clone());
            qc.validate(self.validators())
                .map_err(RestoreCatchupError::InvalidQc)?;

            self.state.register_block(
                block.block_id,
                block.view,
                Some(block.parent_block_id),
                previous_qc.clone(),
            );
            for signer in &block.qc_signers {
                self.state
                    .on_vote(*signer, block.view, &block.block_id)
                    .map_err(RestoreCatchupError::InvalidQc)?;
            }

            previous_qc = Some(qc);
            expected_parent = block.block_id;
            expected_height = expected_height.saturating_add(1);
            applied = applied.saturating_add(1);
        }

        // After replaying a valid certified suffix, resume at the first
        // height/view not covered by the learned material so the restored
        // node does not re-propose or re-vote below its new committed floor.
        if self.current_view < expected_height {
            self.set_view(expected_height);
        }

        Ok(applied)
    }
```
The per-block loop has **no `current_view` gate** and the vote replay uses `.map_err(RestoreCatchupError::InvalidQc)?` — which aborts **only** on an `Err` from `on_vote`, **not** on an equivocation (`Ok(None)`); the post-loop `set_view` only **advances** the view (`current_view < expected_height`), never rejects.

```rust
// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:952-987  on_vote — VERBATIM (equivocation → Ok(None); FirstVote/Dup → accumulator → maybe_qc_for → on_qc)
    pub fn on_vote(
        &mut self,
        voter: ValidatorId,
        view: u64,
        block_id: &BlockIdT,
    ) -> Result<Option<QuorumCertificate<BlockIdT>>, QcValidationError> {
        // 1. Equivocation detection.
        match self.record_vote_history(voter, view, block_id) {
            VoteHistoryOutcome::Equivocation { previous_block: _ } => {
                // Record metrics and ignore this vote for QC formation.
                self.equivocations_detected += 1;
                self.equivocating_validators.insert(voter);
                // For now we silently ignore; later we may want to expose this
                // via a separate error or event.
                return Ok(None);
            }
            VoteHistoryOutcome::FirstVote | VoteHistoryOutcome::DuplicateSameBlock => {
                // Proceed to feed vote into accumulator.
            }
        }

        // 2. Ingest vote into accumulator (membership & duplicate checks).
        let _is_new = self
            .votes
            .on_vote(&self.validators, voter, view, block_id)?;

        // 3. Attempt to form QC for this (view, block_id).
        let qc = self.votes.maybe_qc_for(&self.validators, view, block_id)?;

        if let Some(ref qc) = qc {
            // 4. Apply locking logic with the new QC.
            self.on_qc(qc)?;
        }

        Ok(qc)
    }
```

```rust
// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:897-928  record_vote_history — VERBATIM (key (view,voter); different block ⇒ Equivocation; prior entry NOT overwritten)
    fn record_vote_history(
        &mut self,
        voter: ValidatorId,
        view: u64,
        block_id: &BlockIdT,
    ) -> VoteHistoryOutcome<BlockIdT> {
        let key = (view, voter);
        match self.votes_by_view.get(&key) {
            None => {
                // First time we see this (view, validator) pair.
                // Track the view for eviction purposes
                self.votes_by_view_tracked_views.insert(view);

                // Evict old entries if we're over the limit
                self.evict_votes_by_view_if_needed();

                self.votes_by_view.insert(key, block_id.clone());
                VoteHistoryOutcome::FirstVote
            }
            Some(prev_block) => {
                if prev_block == block_id {
                    // Same block as before: benign duplicate.
                    VoteHistoryOutcome::DuplicateSameBlock
                } else {
                    // Different block: equivocation.
                    VoteHistoryOutcome::Equivocation {
                        previous_block: prev_block.clone(),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
```

### 26.2v A36 — the no-eviction γ exclusion (scoped) and the conditional accumulator-eviction route (production-rejected) (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review. Proposed arguments to **verify or reject** against the complete production composition, not adopted on their face. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected upstream `olivexo28/qbind`; no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.** `γ` = a **leader self-vote that COMPLETES a quorum** at its own key `(cv, bid_self)` (the self-vote is the `q`-th effective vote, forming the QC via `on_leader_step`→`on_vote`→`maybe_qc_for`).

**Four uniqueness properties, defined separately (⟨A36⟩ — producer universe + observation interval; not merged).**
1. **Catch-up admission uniqueness** — `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` registers ≤1 distinct `block_id` per view over the whole execution. Producer: the catch-up applier only. **REFUTED** (§26.2u: `B6`,`X` at view 7). (This was the register's "Lemma U".)
2. **Nonempty-effective-key uniqueness** — ≤1 `block_id` per view has a **nonempty** accumulator key (≥1 effective vote). Producers: **all** vote callers (catch-up replay **and** leader self-vote; inbound Proposal/Vote are `Required`-rejected on DevNet). **FALSE in general** (§26.2u view 6: `A6`={2} from the leader, `B5`={0,1} from catch-up — two nonempty keys).
3. **Quorum-bearing-key uniqueness** — ≤1 `block_id` per view reaches `≥q` effective votes (an `own_qc`-forming key). Producers: all vote callers. Observed to **hold in the §26.2u trace per view**, but **not** proven in general and **not** a lemma; crucially it **does not** exclude a *second* key holding `q−1` effective votes.
4. **Resident `own_qc`-node uniqueness** — ≤1 resident node per view bears `own_qc`. Producer: `on_qc`. Not proven; distinct from (3).
These are kept distinct; none is silently substituted for another, and (3)∧(4) are **not** combined into one "stronger" lemma. The γ question concerns whether a **second** key can hold exactly `q−1` votes that the leader self-vote then completes.

**Part B — the no-eviction γ exclusion (scoped; ACCEPTED under its assumptions).** ⟨**A38 scope marker (§26.2x)**⟩ **this exclusion is now explicitly confined to the no-eviction regime: with retention-pressure *history* eviction (`evict_votes_by_view_if_needed`), γ IS source-reachable** — §26.2x rebuilds a `q−1` key at a target view by evicting that view's history so the completing leader self-vote forms a QC. Part B's premise "no `votes_by_view` history eviction for `v` in the window" is exactly what §26.2x breaks; it is **not** refuted, only **scoped**. *Scope:* stable unit-weight membership, `2 ≤ q`, `N ≤ 256`, default limits, non-wrapping, no reconfig/reinit, and the first leader invocation reaching its self-vote at target view `v`; from the first vote-producing op at `v` until that invocation, **no** `votes_by_view` history **and no** accumulator entry for `v` is evicted or reset. Checked against the composition: before the first leader self-vote at `v`, the only vote producer at `v` is **completed catch-up signer replay** (inbound Proposal/Vote are `Required`-rejected before engine dispatch, §6L.1; the leader has not yet self-voted). Each admitted catch-up block carries a **≥q supplied signer list** (`qc.validate` quorum, basic:2183) whose non-suppressed members enter the accumulator (engine `on_vote` state:974). Let `A` be the first catch-up block at `v` whose signer replay completes:
- **If `A`'s supplied quorum includes `local`:** catch-up already wrote `local`'s history `(v,local)→A` **and** its accumulator membership at `(v,A)`. ⟨**A37**⟩ so **"no earlier *leader* self-vote at `v`" does NOT mean catch-up never recorded `local`** — a catch-up replay can write `(v,local)→A` (A17-F1 posture). The later leader self-vote for `A`: `record_vote_history` ⇒ `DuplicateSameBlock`; the **accumulator** `VoteAccumulator::on_vote` returns a **bool** `Ok(false)` (already present, `(v,A)` membership unchanged). ⟨**A37 caller-distinction**⟩ **"no new contribution" is NOT "no caller effect":** the **engine** `on_vote` (returns `Option<QC>`) still runs `maybe_qc_for`, may call `on_qc`, a `try_commit` evaluation, and a caller `advance_view`. But since `(v,A)` was **already ≥q**, this is **β** — a QC re-forms / the view may advance, yet **no new `q`-th completing vote** crosses a `q−1` threshold ⇒ **not γ**. A leader vote for any id `≠A` ⇒ **Equivocation** ⇒ `Ok(None)`, suppressed. Either way the self-vote adds **no completing vote to a `q−1` key** ⇒ no γ.
- **If `A` excludes `local`:** ≥`q` **non-local** validators are tied to `(v,A)` (already quorate). Any **other** key `(v,B≠A)` can receive at most `N−1−q` non-local contributions (the `q` tied to `A` cannot re-vote `B` without equivocating; `local` has not voted). Since `q = ⌈2N/3⌉` ⇒ `2q > N` ⇒ `N−1−q < q−1`. So no second key reaches `q−1`, and the single leader self-vote (adding 1) cannot complete a quorum at any `B` ⇒ no γ.
- ⟨**A37** — zero-prior-catch-up case⟩ **If no catch-up has voted at `v`:** the accumulator `(v,·)` is empty; the single leader self-vote has weight 1, and `1 < q` (since `q ≥ 2`), so `maybe_qc_for` returns `None` ⇒ no QC ⇒ no γ. (One self-vote can never reach `q ≥ 2` alone.)
*Guard checks:* admission (contiguity/anchor/`h==v`/proposer/id/`qc.validate`, basic:2141–2184); signer-loop returns (`on_vote` `Err`⇒abort, `Ok(None)` equivocation⇒continue-no-insert, `Ok(false/true)`⇒inserted); membership/capacity (`validators.contains`, `max_votes_per_view=256`); handler atomicity (a **later** response error does **not** roll back an already-completed block replay — A34/§26.2t). **Result:** under the stated **no-eviction** assumptions this is a **scoped γ exclusion** — it is **not** a global exclusion, **not** a proof of any uniqueness property above, and **not** a resolution of R. Its load-bearing premise is precisely "no accumulator/history eviction or reset for `v` in the window," which Part C probes.

**Part C — ⚠️ WITHDRAWN by A37/§26.2w. the conditional accumulator-eviction route (operation-level feasible in isolation; production embedding REJECTED).** ⟨**A37**⟩ **the "production embedding REJECTED" conclusion below is DISPROVED** (§26.2w countercandidate): the rejection conflated the **set-cardinality** condition on `tracked_views` (a 128-wide window of **wire** views) with a **chronological** advance of the scalars. When the catch-up chain is built on an **overwritten anchor whose stored height is 0** (a nonresident lock target, §26.2w Step 1), the blocks' stored heights stay **below `committed_height`** so **no 3-chain commits** advance it, and a **partial-response error skips `set_view`** so `current_view` does not advance — so view `v`'s accumulator keys are evicted with **both scalars below `v`**. The text below is retained as **dated history**. The accumulator (`VoteAccumulator`, vote_accumulator.rs) is **separate** from the engine's equivocation history (`votes_by_view`): `entries: HashMap<VoteKey{view,block_id}, HashSet<ValidatorId>>` + `tracked_views: BTreeSet<u64>`; `on_vote` (vote_accumulator:301–343) evicts via `evict_oldest_views` (:264–275) **only when tracking a NEW view with `tracked_views.len() ≥ max_tracked_views(128)`**, removing **all entries of the smallest tracked view** (`entries.retain(key.view != oldest)`). The history is evicted separately (`evict_votes_by_view_if_needed`, lowest-view-first, `max_votes_by_view_entries=16384`). *Operation-level sequence* (`N=4, local=2, q=3`, leader(`v`)=2, no earlier leader self-vote at `v`): (1) catch-up admits `A` at `v`, signers `{0,1,2}` ⇒ `(v,A)={0,1,2}` quorate, history `(v,2)→A`; (2) catch-up admits `B≠A` at `v`, `{0,1,3}` ⇒ `0,1` DuplicateSameBlock... — **no**: `(v,0)→A`,`(v,1)→A` already, so `0,1` are **Equivocation-suppressed** for `B`; `3` FirstVote ⇒ `(v,B)={3}`; (3) **whole-view accumulator eviction of `v`** removes `(v,A)`,`(v,B)` while history `(v,0..3)` survives; (4) catch-up re-admits `A` with `{0,1,3}` ⇒ `0,1` DuplicateSameBlock ⇒ rebuild `(v,A)={0,1}`, `3` Equivocation-suppressed (history `(v,3)→B`); (5) first leader self-vote at `v` derives `A` (if `lock=A.parent`, §26.2N prefix-alignment): history `(v,2)→A` ⇒ **DuplicateSameBlock**, but `local 2` is **absent** from the rebuilt `(v,A)={0,1}`, so `votes.on_vote(2,v,A)` **inserts** ⇒ `(v,A)={0,1,2}` = quorum ⇒ `maybe_qc_for`⇒`qc_A`⇒`on_qc`⇒`own_qc`, `advance_view`. The self-vote **completes** `{0,1}→{0,1,2}` ⇒ **γ at operation level.**

**Production embedding — ⚠️ claimed EXACT SOURCE REJECTION (DISPROVED by A37/§26.2w; dated history).** [former claim:] Step 3's whole-view accumulator eviction of `v` is **not production-reachable together with** steps 4–5:
- `evict_oldest_views` removes the **smallest** tracked view; so evicting `v` requires `v` to be the smallest among **≥128 tracked views**, i.e. **≥127 tracked views `> v`**.
- Views are tracked in the accumulator **only** by `on_vote` reaching `votes.on_vote` (state:974) — for **non-suppressed** signers. The only bulk producer is catch-up; the leader self-vote is one per view; inbound Proposal/Vote are `Required`-rejected. So tracking ≥127 views `> v` requires admitting catch-up blocks at ≥127 views `> v`.
- Those higher-view catch-up blocks each carry a **≥q supplied list** at **fresh** views (no prior history ⇒ no equivocation) ⇒ `≥q` effective votes ⇒ `own_qc`, and contiguous `height==view` blocks form a **3-chain** ⇒ `try_commit` fires, advancing **`committed_height`** (height_ok `g_height > committed_height`, state:1095 — **monotonic non-decreasing**), and the applier's post-loop `set_view` advances **`current_view`** (also monotonic; `on_timeout_certificate`/`try_advance_to_view` reject `≤ current`, A14/§21).
- But steps 4–5 require `committed_height = v−1` (so the applier's `expected_height = committed_height+1 = v` admits `A` **at** `v`, basic:2130/2141) **and** `current_view = v` (so the first leader step is **at** `v`, `is_leader_for_current_view`). After the ≥127-view advance both scalars are `≫ v`, and **neither can return** (monotone). So the applier can no longer admit at `v` (contiguity `block.height==expected_height` fails for `v ≠ committed_height+1`) and the leader step is at `current_view ≫ v`, deriving `D(leader(current_view),current_view,·) ≠ A`.

⇒ **The accumulator-eviction-of-`v` and the per-view-`v` operations (re-admit `A` at `v`; first leader self-vote at `v`) cannot co-occur under the monotonicity of `committed_height` and `current_view`.** [former claim:] This is an exact source-based rejection of the proposed route. ⟨**A37 — DISPROVED (§26.2w)**⟩ the premise "evicting `v` ⇒ a scalar advanced past `v`" is false: §26.2w evicts view 262 with `committed_height=256` and `current_view=258` (both below `v`), because the catch-up chain on a height-0 overwritten anchor has stored heights `1..134 < committed_height` (no commit) and the partial-response error skips `set_view` (no view advance); re-admission of `v` as an **interior** block and an eligible first leader self-vote at `v` then both occur. The co-occurrence **does** happen; this rejection is **withdrawn**.

**Transition sketch (operation-level steps 1–5, N=4, q=3; the embedding being rejected, this is the isolated-op trace only).**

| Op | actor | history outcome(s) | accumulator `(v,·)` after | `own_qc` | lock | commit / view |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | catch-up `A{0,1,2}` | `(v,0/1/2)→A` First | `(v,A)={0,1,2}` quorate | `A.own_qc` | per `on_qc` | per 3-chain |
| 2 | catch-up `B{0,1,3}` | 0,1 **Equiv**(→A); `(v,3)→B` First | `(v,B)={3}` | none | — | — |
| 3 | **accumulator evict view `v`** | history `(v,0..3)` **retained** | `(v,A)`,`(v,B)` **removed** | (nodes keep `own_qc`) | — | — |
| 4 | catch-up `A{0,1,3}` | 0,1 **Dup**(=A); 3 **Equiv**(→B) | `(v,A)={0,1}` (rebuilt) | — | — | — |
| 5 | **leader self-vote `A`** | `(v,2)` **Dup**(=A) | insert 2 ⇒ `(v,A)={0,1,2}` **quorum** | `A.own_qc`←qc | `on_qc` | **γ**: QC via self-vote; `advance_view` |

**register_block — one complete body (⟨A36⟩ `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:731–763`, line-for-line verbatim; this is the canonical registration body A35's §26.2t referenced):**
```rust
    pub fn register_block(
        &mut self,
        id: BlockIdT,
        view: u64,
        parent_id: Option<BlockIdT>,
        justify_qc: Option<QuorumCertificate<BlockIdT>>,
    ) {
        // Compute height: 0 if no parent, otherwise parent.height + 1
        let height = match parent_id.as_ref() {
            None => 0,
            Some(pid) => self.blocks.get(pid).map(|p| p.height + 1).unwrap_or(0),
        };

        let node = BlockNode::new(id.clone(), view, parent_id, justify_qc, height);

        // Check if this is an update to an existing block
        let is_new = !self.blocks.contains_key(&id);

        // A legacy/unverified registration replaces any prior node for this id,
        // including any earlier *verified* designation: the new node carries no
        // `verified_justification`, and `insert_block_node` reclaims the old
        // node's retained-evidence bytes. An unverified block therefore never
        // inherits an earlier verified certificate.
        self.insert_block_node(node);

        // If it's a new block, add to pending block order for eviction
        if is_new {
            self.pending_block_order.push_back(id);
        }

        // Evict blocks if we're over the limit
        self.evict_blocks_if_needed();
    }
```
`evict_oldest_views` — verbatim (`vote_accumulator.rs:264–275`):
```rust
    fn evict_oldest_views(&mut self) {
        while self.tracked_views.len() >= self.limits.max_tracked_views {
            if let Some(&oldest_view) = self.tracked_views.iter().next() {
                // Remove all entries for this view
                self.entries.retain(|key, _| key.view != oldest_view);
                self.tracked_views.remove(&oldest_view);
                self.evicted_views += 1;
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
```
The `on_vote` view-tracking/eviction trigger (vote_accumulator.rs:314–319) and `maybe_qc_for` (357–382) are reused by reference (§26.2o/§26.2u); engine `on_vote`/`record_vote_history` are in the §26.2u packet; `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` in the §26.2t packet; `try_commit_with_qc` height_ok/should_commit at state:1093–1121 (§26.4/§26.2t).

**Disposition (§1; no forced promotion/grouping/closure).**
- **Part B:** a **scoped γ exclusion** holds under the explicit **no-eviction + stable-membership + `2q>N`** assumptions — **not** global, **not** a proof of any uniqueness property (1)–(4), **not** a resolution of R.
- **Part C (⟨A37 update⟩):** the accumulator-eviction defeat of Part B is operation-level feasible, and its production embedding **REJECTION is WITHDRAWN** (A37/§26.2w): eviction of a target view **does coexist** with `committed_height`/`current_view` **below** `v`, interior re-admission of `v`, and an eligible first leader self-vote at `v`. However, the §26.2w countercandidate rebuilds a **full `{0,1,3}` quorum** (one id per view, no suppressing second id), so its leader self-vote is **β (redundant to an existing quorum), not γ** — it does **not** itself produce γ.
- **Net on γ:** γ is **excluded in the no-eviction regime** (Part B). ⟨A37⟩ the eviction-based **defeat of that exclusion is no longer rejected** — eviction + re-admission + eligible leader self-vote **coexist** (§26.2w) — but the A37 route is **β, not γ** (it rebuilds a full quorum, one id per view). ⟨**A38 — SUPERSEDES "not shown reachable" (§26.2x)**⟩ **the exact open construction is now completed: γ IS source-reachable.** §26.2x composes the **`q−1` rebuild** (a second distinct id `B=D(2,2354,T_2353)≠A` at target view 2354) with retention-pressure **history** eviction of that view and a completing **leader self-vote** that crosses `q−1→q`, forming `qc_B`. So γ is **no longer "open / not shown reachable"** — it is **reachable in source**. It remains **independent of R** and forms **no commit, no R, no honest-node safety violation** (catch-up producers are the A17-F1 posture; TCs are A1-F1/A1-F2 None-context; anchor overwrite is A16.3/§26.2N — no crypto break, no honest-node equivocation), so it is **not a new finding** and forces **no count change**. **A35's ¬U (admission) result is preserved unchanged.** OBL-CONS-3 stays **SR-PARTIAL** (**R** remains the open commit-safety question; γ-reachability does not resolve it).

### 26.2w A37 — finite retention-pressure countercandidate: accumulator eviction of a target view coexists with re-admission and an eligible leader self-vote there (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review. A construction to **verify or reject at the first failing guard**; no initial map/accumulator state is assumed. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected upstream `olivexo28/qbind`; no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.** Purpose: test A36/§26.2v-Part-C's claim that accumulator eviction of a view `v` cannot coexist with later catch-up re-admission and an eligible first leader self-vote at `v`. **This is not yet A36's two-distinct-ID γ construction.**

**Setup (verified, not assumed).** N=4 unit-weight `{0,1,2,3}`, `local=2`, `q=3`, default limits (`max_tracked_views=128`, `max_pending_blocks=4096`, `max_votes_by_view_entries=16384`), `verification_ctx=None`, non-wrapping, no reconfig, established P2P/restore/origin-admission prerequisites. `P_v = LE64(leader(v)) ‖ LE64(v)`, `leaders=[0,1,2,3]`; `D(proposer,v,parent)=LE64(proposer)‖LE64(v)‖parent[0:16]`. Snapshot height `H=256`; nonresident `L=P_3‖P_0`; opaque anchor `C=P_258‖P_3`. **Restore** (`initialize_from_snapshot_baseline`, state:1254; caller binary:2517–2528; `current_view = snapshot_height+1`, binary:327): committed `(C,256)`; `C` resident `{view=256, height=256, parent=None, own_qc=None}`; `current_view=257`; `lock=None`. ✓

**Step 1 — overwrite the resident anchor, committed scalar unchanged.** None-context TC: `timeout_view=257`, `tc.view=258`, logical quorum `{0,1,3}`, `high_qc=Some(L, view 257)`. `on_timeout_certificate` (basic:3256): `tc.validate` admits the logical list (A1-F1 posture); `258 > current_view 257` ✓; `high_qc=Some` ⇒ lock-update `should_update` = (`locked_qc None` ⇒ true) ⇒ `set_locked_qc(L, 257)` — **installs a lock naming `L`; creates no block node, so `L` stays nonresident**; `current_view←258`, flags reset. First leader step at 258 (`leader(258)=leaders[2]=2=local`, `!proposed_in_view` ✓): parent = `lock.block_id = L`; `make_block_id(L) = D(2,258,L) = P_258‖L[0:16] = P_258‖P_3 = C`. `register_block(C,258,Some(L),·)`: `is_new=false` (C resident) ⇒ **overwrite**; height `= blocks.get(L)…unwrap_or(0) = 0` (**`L` absent**); `view←258`, `parent←L`, `own_qc←None`. Committed scalars **stay `(C,256)`** (`committed_height` is the scalar, not re-read from the node). Self-vote `on_vote(2,258,C)`: FirstVote `(258,2)→C`; accumulator `(258,C)={2}`, weight 1 < 3 ⇒ no QC ⇒ no advance. `current_view=258`. ✓ (No guard rejects: the leader-step proposal build and gates pass; the overwrite is the §26.2N mechanism with a nonresident lock target.)

**Step 2 — accumulator pressure while the commit floor blocks commits.** Response anchored at `(C,256)`: 134 valid blocks `T_1…T_134` then one invalid block failing a pre-registration **height** check. For `i=1…134`: wire `height=view=256+i`; `proposer=leader(256+i)`; `parent = C` (i=1) else `T_{i−1}`; `id = D(proposer,view,parent)`; supplied `{0,1,3}`. Applier (`apply_restore_catchup_blocks`, basic:2122): `expected_height` starts at `committed_height+1 = 257`, `expected_parent=C`, **incrementing per block from the batch-start committed height, independent of any commit mutation**.
- **Stored heights:** `register_block` computes from the **resident parent**: `T_1.height = C.height+1 = 0+1 = 1`; `T_i.height = i`. So `T_i.height = i ∈ {1..134}`, **independent of wire height/view `256+i`**.

```rust
    fn evict_votes_by_view_if_needed(&mut self) {
        let max_entries = self.limits().max_votes_by_view_entries;
        while self.votes_by_view.len() >= max_entries {
            // Find the lowest view to evict
            if let Some(&lowest_view) = self.votes_by_view_tracked_views.iter().next() {
                // Remove all entries for this view
                self.votes_by_view
                    .retain(|(view, _), _| *view != lowest_view);
                self.votes_by_view_tracked_views.remove(&lowest_view);
                self.evicted_votes_by_view_entries += 1;
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust
// crates/qbind-consensus/src/timeout.rs:353-392  TimeoutCertificate::validate — VERBATIM (quorum gate)
    pub fn validate(
        &self,
        validators: &ConsensusValidatorSet,
    ) -> Result<(), TimeoutValidationError> {
        use std::collections::HashSet;

        let mut seen = HashSet::new();
        let mut acc_vp: u64 = 0;

        for id in &self.signers {
            // Check membership
            if !validators.contains(*id) {
                return Err(TimeoutValidationError::NonMemberSigner(*id));
            }

            // Check for duplicates
            if !seen.insert(*id) {
                return Err(TimeoutValidationError::DuplicateSigner(*id));
            }

            // Accumulate voting power
            let idx = validators.index_of(*id).expect("contains check passed");
            let entry = validators.get(idx).expect("index_of should be valid");
            acc_vp = acc_vp.saturating_add(entry.voting_power);
        }

        // Check quorum threshold (2/3)
        let required = validators.two_thirds_vp();
        if acc_vp < required {
            return Err(TimeoutValidationError::InsufficientQuorum {
                accumulated_vp: acc_vp,
                required_vp: required,
            });
        }

        Ok(())
    }
```

### 26.2y A39 — bounded OBL-CONS-3 R source review: can a first leader self-vote write a new commit? (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. **R** (the open commit-safety source question, §26.2p/§26.2q) is: does a **production-reachable first leader self-vote** cause `on_qc → try_commit_with_qc` to **write a new commit state**, with the §26.2q evaluation-time predicates `(r1)–(r5)` all holding at the self-vote? **R is addressed on its own; it is NOT inferred from γ** (a γ QC is a QC-formation event — §26.2x/§26.2x.1 — and proves no commit). One finite source-derived candidate is traced through the production callers and **rejected at its first failing transition**; the exact remaining source question is stated. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.** **Result: R is neither reached nor excluded — R stays OPEN (available-source).** ⟨**A39.1**: the specific "candidate fails at the height-floor/strict-view coupling" claim is **WITHDRAWN** (§26.2y.1) — for an interior construction the height floor can pass; one concrete interior construction's actual first failing guard is `should_commit`, but that is construction-specific, not a general exclusion.⟩

**The `(r1)–(r5)` predicates (verbatim-pinned, `try_commit_with_qc`, `hotstuff_state_engine.rs:1029–1137`).** For a QC on block `B`: (r1) `B` resident with `own_qc` (`:1031–1038`), `P=B.parent` resident with `own_qc` (`:1043–1062`), `G=P.parent` resident with `own_qc` (`:1064–1084`) — three independent `own_qc.is_none() ⇒ return` gates; (r2) folded into (r1) as the three `own_qc` checks; (r3) **strict stored views** `g_view < p_view < b_view` (`:1087`, on the `BlockNode.view` fields); (r4) **height floor** `g_height > committed_height` (`:1093–1096`, on `BlockNode.height`); (r5) **should_commit** (`:1098–1117`): `committed_block == g_id ⇒ false`; else `g_view > committed_node.view` (or committed absent/not-resident ⇒ true). Commit writes iff `should_commit && height_ok` (`:1119`). All fields are the **stored** `BlockNode` values set by `register_block`, not wire fields.

**Why v1.24's γ end-state fails R (precise).** At the Step-4 self-vote, `qc_B` forms on `B` (view 2354, stored height 2354), `P = lock = T_2353` (stored height 2353, stored **view 4698**), `G = T_2352` (stored height 2352, stored view 4697); committed `(T_2353, 2353)`.
- **(r4) FAILS:** `g_height = 2352 > committed_height = 2353`? **No.** `G` sits **below** the committed tip — `T_2353` was committed during Step 2, raising `committed_height` to 2353 ≥ `G.height`.
- **(r3) FAILS:** `g_view 4697 < p_view 4698 < b_view 2354`? `4698 < 2354` is **false.** `B` was reattached at the **low** view 2354 while its resident parent `T_2353` carries the **high** stored view 4698 (the A16.3 stored-height≠view artifact). The applier forces `B.view = B.height = committed_height+1 = 2354` (`h==v` + contiguity, `basic:2141/2155`), strictly below its parent's stored view.
These are **structural**, not incidental: the very reattachment that let γ rebuild a `q−1` key put `B` below its ancestors in both height and view. γ ⇏ R.

**Candidate R-α (finite, source-derived): a contiguous monotonic catch-up chain with an equivocation-starved tip `B`, completed by the first leader self-vote.** Goal: a chain `… ← G ← P ← B` with **stored height == stored view** (so views increase with heights), `G` and `P` bearing `own_qc`, `G.height > committed_height`, and `(cv, B_id)` pre-loaded with exactly `q−1` effective votes so the leader self-vote at `cv = B.view` is the **completing `q`-th vote** (= γ) whose `try_commit` then commits `G` (= R). Registration/reattachment and full-ID-vs-16-byte-prefix correspondence are the levers. Default limits; N, local, q as in §26.2x; `verification_ctx=None`; `leader(cv)=local`.

*Production-guard trace and the first rejecting transition.*
1. **Catch-up admits only ≥`q`-signer blocks.** Every catch-up block is gated by `qc.validate(self.validators())` on its supplied `qc_signers` (`basic:2182–2184`), which requires `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp` (= `q`). So a block reaches **fewer than `q` effective** accumulator votes **only** by **equivocation-suppression** during the ordered `on_vote` replay (`basic:2192–2196`): a supplied signer `s` with a pre-existing `(view, s) → X` history entry, `X ≠ B`, hits `Equivocation ⇒ Ok(None)` (`state:960`) and is not inserted. (This is the §26.2u/§26.2x mechanism and the **only** source of a `q−1` key under these callers.)
2. **Equivocation-starving `B` at view `cv` requires a second admitted id at view `cv`.** The pre-existing `(cv, s) → X` entry needs a **distinct** block `X ≠ B` admitted at the **same view** `cv` (¬U, §26.2u). The applier fixes exactly one `(height, view, parent)` per contiguity step (`block.height == expected_height`, `block.height == block.view`, `block.parent_block_id == expected_parent`; `basic:2141/2147/2155`), and `expected_height` is strictly increasing within a response (`:2200`). So a **second** admitted id at view `cv` must come from a **separate response**, whose cursor `expected_height = committed_height+1` (`:2130–2133`) must **equal `cv`** — i.e. **`committed_height = cv − 1` at that response's start.**
3. ⟨**A39.1 — WITHDRAWN as unproved; see §26.2y.1**: this rests on the false general cursor premise `committed_height = cv−1` (true only when B is the *first* response block, k=1; §26.2w admits an interior target at k=6 with committed_height 256) and on a generic `G.height = cv−2`. For an interior construction the height floor can PASS; a concrete interior construction's actual first failing guard is `should_commit` (committed-tip stored view), not the height floor — and even that is construction-specific, not a general exclusion. R is OPEN.⟩ **⟐ FIRST REJECTING TRANSITION — the height-floor coupling.** With `committed_height = cv − 1`, `B` is registered at **stored height `cv`** (off the committed tip, `h==v` + contiguity), so its grandparent `G` sits at stored height **`cv − 2`**. Then at the leader self-vote, `(r4)` evaluates `g_height = cv − 2 > committed_height = cv − 1` ⇒ **`cv − 2 > cv − 1` is FALSE** (`basic:1093–1096`). `try_commit` returns at the height floor: **no commit.** (Equivalently, `(r3)` also fails whenever the committed tip used as `B`'s parent carries a stored view ≠ `cv−1`, as in the reattached case.) The candidate is **rejected here** — the same floor that blocked γ.
4. **The 16-byte-prefix reattachment does not rescue it.** One might try to keep `B` at a high `cv` while pointing `B.parent` at a resident `P`/`G` chain above `committed_height`, using `D(local, cv, lock) = LE64(local)‖LE64(cv)‖lock[0:16]` (`basic:2043–2058`) to land the self-vote on a `q−1` key that catch-up pre-loaded via a block whose derived id collides on `lock[0:16]`. But the leader's `register_block(B_id, cv, parent = lock, …)` (`basic:2253–2259`) **rebinds `B.parent` to the FULL `lock` id and recomputes `B.height = resident(lock).height + 1`** (`state:register_block`, height from the **full** parent node). So the commit chain's `P`/`G` and their heights/views are **`lock`'s full-id resident chain**, never the colliding catch-up parent's — the prefix collision governs only **which accumulator key** the votes accrue to, not the commit-chain geometry. And `B.own_qc` is reset to `None` by the overwrite, set only when `qc_B` later forms. So the collision cannot smuggle a grandparent `G` with `G.height > committed_height` and `g_view < p_view < cv` into the chain.

**Transition table (candidate R-α; decisive points).**

| Step | guard (source) | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| catch-up block admission | `qc.validate ≥ q` (basic:2183) | every admitted block carries ≥q signers ⇒ `q−1` only via equivocation-suppression |
| build second id `X` at view `cv` | contiguity `expected_height=committed_height+1`, `h==v` (basic:2130/2141/2155) | needs a second response with `committed_height = cv−1` |
| register `B` at `cv` | height from resident parent = committed tip (state:register_block) | `B.height = cv`, `G.height = cv−2` |
| leader self-vote `qc_B` | **`height_ok`: `g_height = cv−2 > committed_height = cv−1`** (basic:1093–1096) | **FALSE ⇒ no commit — FIRST REJECTING TRANSITION** |
| (prefix-collision variant) | `register_block` rebinds `B.parent = full lock`, `B.height = resident(lock).height+1` (basic:2259) | commit chain = lock's full-id chain; collision cannot supply a floor-clearing `G` |

**Four separate claims (§1).** (1) **γ QC formation:** unchanged — source-reachable (§26.2x/§26.2x.1), proves nothing here. (2) **New commit by a first leader self-vote (R):** **NOT shown** — candidate R-α is rejected at the height floor; no production-reachable leader-self-vote new-commit is exhibited. (3) **R excluded:** **NOT established** — no non-circular invariant yet links "a second admitted id at view `v`" to "`committed_height ≥ v−1`" across all producers/eviction paths, so R is **not** proven impossible either. (4) **Honest-node safety violation:** none is established by this review (it exhibits no commit at all).

**Exact remaining source question (R, carried forward).** Does there exist a production-reachable catch-up/leader interleaving in which simultaneously **(a)** `B`'s accumulator key holds exactly `q−1` effective votes immediately before the first leader self-vote at `cv = B.view`; **(b)** `B`'s resident parent `P` and grandparent `G` both bear `own_qc` with strictly increasing stored views `G.view < P.view < cv`; and **(c)** `G.height > committed_height` at the self-vote — **without** the `committed_height ≥ cv−1` advance that producing `B`'s `q−1` deficit (a same-view second id via a second response) appears to force past `G.height`? A **complete source exclusion** of R is acceptable only with a **non-circular invariant** that, over **every production writer of effective `(view,id)` votes** (catch-up replay `basic:2192`; leader self-vote `basic:2332`) and **every eviction/overwrite path** (history `evict_votes_by_view_if_needed` 16384-cap; accumulator `evict_oldest_views` 128-cap; `register_block` overwrite), ties a second admitted id at view `v` to `committed_height ≥ v−1`. That invariant is **not** established. R therefore stays **OPEN**.

```rust
// crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2043-2058  derive_block_id_from_header — VERBATIM (16-byte-prefix D)
    fn derive_block_id_from_header(
        proposer: ValidatorId,
        view: u64,
        parent_block_id: &[u8; 32],
    ) -> [u8; 32] {
        let mut id = [0u8; 32];
        // Encode proposer id in the first 8 bytes
        let proposer_bytes = proposer.0.to_le_bytes();
        id[..8].copy_from_slice(&proposer_bytes);
        // Encode view in bytes 8-15
        let view_bytes = view.to_le_bytes();
        id[8..16].copy_from_slice(&view_bytes);
        // Copy first 16 bytes of parent_block_id for uniqueness
        id[16..32].copy_from_slice(&parent_block_id[..16]);
        id
    }
```

### 26.2y.1 A39.1 — corrections to R-α's source inference and §26.2x.1/§26.2y framing fields (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. This corrects three over-/mis-statements in the A39/A38.1 records: **(A)** the catch-up framing byte fields (wire struct uses `u16` indices, not 64-bit `ValidatorId`s); **(B)** §26.2y's general cursor implication "a second id at view `cv` requires `committed_height = cv−1`" (false for interior response blocks); **(C)** §26.2y's claimed "first rejecting transition = height floor" for candidate R-α (it rested on (B) and on a generic `G.height = cv−2` substitution). **R remains OPEN** — neither a complete source construction nor a non-circular exclusion is established; **γ's revised source result (§26.2x/§26.2x.1) is unaffected and not reopened.** Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — framing record corrected (wire fields are `u16` indices).** The actual wire declaration is `p2p.rs:200–208` (verbatim below): `RestoreCatchupBlock { height: u64, view: u64, parent_block_id: [u8;32], block_id: [u8;32], proposer_index: u16, qc_signer_indices: Vec<u16> }`. §26.2x.1/§26.2y wrongly sized `proposer` and the signer list as 64-bit `ValidatorId`s — that is the *engine* type (`basic:1177`, `RestoreCatchupBlock<BlockIdT>` with `ValidatorId`), **not** the serialized p2p type. **Exact field byte arithmetic (fixed-width fields only, from the inspected declaration):** per block = `height 8 + view 8 + parent_block_id 32 + block_id 32 + proposer_index 2 = 82 B` of fixed fields, plus the `qc_signer_indices` payload `2·n B` (n = signer count). Envelope fixed fields: `responder_validator_index 2 + request_from_height 8 + request_from_block_id 32 = 42 B`, plus `responder_committed_height: Option<u64>` payload and two sequence-length prefixes. **Separately, bincode serialization semantics (NOT re-derived from bincode source here, stated as its documented default):** default `bincode::serialize`/`deserialize` (p2p:651/664/700/725) uses fixint little-endian with **8-byte `usize` sequence-length prefixes**, a 1-byte `Option` discriminant (+8 B payload when `Some`), and a variable enum discriminant for `ConsensusNetMsg`/`P2pMessage`. Under those defaults: envelope = `42 + (1+8) + 8 (blocks len) = 59 B`; per block = `82 + 8 (signer-vec len) + 2n = 90 + 2n B`, i.e. **100 B (n=5), 102 B (n=6), 104 B (n=7)**. **Conservative payload upper bound** (every block `n=7`, `≤104 B`): `2355·104 + 59 = 244,920 + 59 = 244,979 B ≈ 0.24 MB`. **Exact (the §26.2x candidate's mix: 22 blocks n=5, 1 block n=6, 2332 blocks n=7):** `2332·104 + 22·100 + 1·102 + 59 = 242,528 + 2,200 + 102 + 59 = 244,889 B ≈ 0.24 MB`. **Single-frame admission conclusion REAFFIRMED and strengthened:** `≈0.24 MB` (both figures) `+ AEAD tag (16 B) + enum/wrapper bytes` is `≪ MAX_TRANSPORT_CIPHERTEXT = 16,777,216 B` by ≈ **68×** (vs the ≈47× recorded with the wrong 0.35 MB). Robust to the uninspected bincode-prefix widths: even a 10× larger encoding stays under the cap. **The withdrawn multiple-response fallback stays withdrawn** (not relied upon). This supersedes the `0.35 MB`/`358,019 B`/`357,659 B` figures in §26.2x.1/§26.2y.

**Part B — §26.2y's general cursor implication WITHDRAWN.** §26.2y asserted that producing a second admitted id at view `cv` forces `committed_height = cv−1`. **That is false in general.** `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` sets `expected_height = committed_height()+1` as the cursor **for the first block of a response**, then increments by 1 per block (`basic:2130–2133, 2200`); the target can be an **interior** block at cursor position `k`, with `cv = committed_height + k` and so `committed_height = cv − k`. **Reconciliation (source-established elsewhere):** A37/§26.2w admits its target at **view 262 as response block six** (`k=6`) while `committed_height = 256` (`256 = 262 − 6 ≠ 262 − 1`); A35/§26.2u admits **two distinct ids at one view** across responses. So interior/multi-id admission is reachable and does **not** require `committed_height = cv−1`. **Narrow condition (the only case where the implication holds):** `committed_height = cv−1` **iff** the id at `cv` is the **first block of its response** (`k=1`). The §26.2x γ witness is exactly that `k=1` case (B first block of the second response, `committed_height = 2353 = cv−1` with `cv=2354`); it is **not** general. **No claim is made that an interior two-id composition succeeds** — only that the cursor does not force `committed_height = cv−1`.

**Part C — R-α's claimed height-floor rejection WITHDRAWN; a concrete interior construction fails at a *different* guard.** §26.2y's "first rejecting transition = `g_height = cv−2 > committed_height = cv−1` false" is **withdrawn as unproved**: it inherited the false (B) premise and used a generic `G.height = cv−2`. The evaluation-time commit chain must be read off the **actual overwritten node**: the leader's `register_block(B_id, cv, parent = lock, …)` (`basic:2253–2259`) sets `B.parent = lock` (full 32-byte id) and `B.height = resident(lock).height + 1`; at `try_commit`, `P = lock` (the full-id resident node) and `G = P.parent` (that node's resident parent). So `(r3)/(r4)` must be evaluated on the concrete `lock`-chain, not a formula.

### 26.2y.2 A39.2 — the W-chain IDs collide with the first-response blocks: §26.2y.1's interior R-α construction is incoherent (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. §26.2y.1 claimed a concrete interior construction (a second-response chain `W_1,W_2,…` off the committed tip `T_2353`, with an equivocation-starved target `W_k`, `k≥3`) whose `try_commit` first-fails at `should_commit`. **That construction is incoherent at the producer step and the `should_commit` first-failing-guard claim is WITHDRAWN**: computing the **full 32-byte** derived IDs shows `W_k = T_{8+k}` for all `k≥2`, so the interior target is **not a distinct block** and **cannot be equivocation-starved** by `T_{8+k}`'s history. **Full-ID algebra (`derive_block_id_from_header`, basic:2043–2058).** `D(p,v,parent) = LE64(p)[0:8] ‖ LE64(v)[8:16] ‖ parent[0:16]`. Write `P_v := LE64(leader(v)) ‖ LE64(v)` (16 B); for `p=leader(v)`, `D(p,v,parent)=P_v ‖ parent[0:16]`, so a block's **first 16 bytes are `P_v` (its own leader+view) and its last 16 bytes are its parent's first 16 bytes `P_{parent.view}`.** First-response blocks: `T_i` at view `2345+i`, `T_i = P_{2345+i} ‖ T_{i−1}[0:16] = P_{2345+i} ‖ P_{2344+i}`. Second-response blocks off `T_2353` (committed tip, **view 4698 = 2345+2353**): `W_j` at view `2353+j`, `W_j = P_{2353+j} ‖ W_{j−1}[0:16]` with `W_0 = T_2353`.
- **`W_1` vs `T_9` (view 2354): DISTINCT.** `W_1 = P_2354 ‖ T_2353[0:16] = P_2354 ‖ P_4698` (since `T_2353` is at **view 4698**). `T_9 = P_2354 ‖ T_8[0:16] = P_2354 ‖ P_2353`. `P_4698 ≠ P_2353` ⇒ **`W_1 ≠ T_9`.** (`W_1` is exactly §26.2x's `B = D(2,2354,T_2353)`.)
- **`W_2` vs `T_10` (view 2355): EQUAL.** `W_2 = P_2355 ‖ W_1[0:16] = P_2355 ‖ P_2354`. `T_10 = P_2355 ‖ T_9[0:16] = P_2355 ‖ P_2354`. ⇒ **`W_2 = P_2355‖P_2354 = T_10`.**
- **Induction, `k≥2`: `W_k = T_{8+k}`.** Both are at view `2353+k` (first 16 = `P_{2353+k}`), and both parents (`W_{k−1}` and `T_{7+k}`) are leader blocks at view `2352+k`, so both last-16 = `P_{2352+k}`. Hence `W_k = P_{2353+k} ‖ P_{2352+k} = T_{8+k}`. Only `j=1` escapes, because `W_0=T_2353` sits at view **4698**, giving `W_1`'s parent-prefix `P_4698 ≠ P_2353 = T_8[0:16]`.

**Consequence 1 — `register_block` overwrites, it does not create a new interior block.** For `k≥2`, `W_k`'s id **is** `T_{8+k}`'s id, which is already resident from the first response. `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` calls `register_block(W_k, 2353+k, Some(W_{k−1}), prev_qc)` (basic:2186), and `register_block` builds a **fresh** `BlockNode::new(…)` with **`own_qc: None`** (block_state.rs:106) and `insert_block_node` **replaces** the prior node (state:731–763). So the overwrite **rebinds the node's parent to `W_{k−1}`, recomputes its height from `resident(W_{k−1})`, and resets `own_qc` to `None`** — discarding `T_{8+k}`'s original parent (`T_{7+k}`), height, and any `own_qc`. Equal id ⇒ one node; the parent/height/own_qc fields are whatever the **last** registration wrote.

**Consequence 2 — the interior target cannot be equivocation-starved.** §26.2y.1 needed `W_k` (`k≥3`) to carry only `q−1` effective votes by equivocation-suppression against a retained `(2353+k, s)→T_{8+k}` entry. A retained entry therefore does **not** suppress `W_k`'s signer; an **evicted** entry yields `FirstVote` and a plain insert. **Neither path produces a `q−1` equivocation-starved key.** The premise is void.

**Re-run of the producer steps (`record_vote_history → on_vote → maybe_qc_for`), no QC assumed.**

### 26.2y.3 A39.3 — corrected producer-neutral R definition; bounded β-route evaluation (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. **Part A** corrects the active R statement: §26.2y.2's "R needs a `q−1` equivocation-starved target and a distinct same-view block" is a **γ-route condition, not a necessary condition for R** — a duplicate leader self-vote on an **already-quorate** key (the **β** route) also drives `maybe_qc_for → on_qc → try_commit_with_qc` and can write a commit, with no `q−1` key and no distinct same-view block. **Part B** re-evaluates the two already-recorded β candidates (A33.1/§26.2p, A37/§26.2w) against their actual evaluation-time `B`/`P`/`G` and establishes that **neither writes a new commit**, while **source does not establish a general exclusion of β-driven R**; the exact remaining premise is named. §26.2y.2's **W-chain collision result** (`W_2=T_10`, `W_k=T_{8+k}` for `k≥2`) and the γ witness (§26.2x/§26.2x.1) are **preserved**; only the γ-only necessary-condition framing is withdrawn. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — the pinned `on_vote → votes.on_vote → maybe_qc_for → on_qc → try_commit_with_qc` flow (producer-neutral).** Engine `on_vote` (state:952–987): `record_vote_history` returns `Equivocation` ⇒ `Ok(None)` (abort); **`FirstVote` OR `DuplicateSameBlock` both fall through** (state:968–971) to `votes.on_vote` (accumulator), whose `Ok(false)` (duplicate already-present signer) **does not early-return the engine** — `maybe_qc_for` then runs **unconditionally** (state:974–979). `maybe_qc_for` (vote_accumulator:357–382) is **idempotent**: it reads the key's signer set and returns `Ok(Some(qc))` whenever that set meets quorum — it is **not** gated on "first time" and **does not remove the entry** (its own doc, :349). So on an **already-quorate** key it returns `Some(qc)` **every** call. `on_qc(qc)` (state:995–1016) then updates the lock, sets `node.own_qc = Some(qc)` for `qc.block_id`, and **unconditionally calls `try_commit_with_qc(qc)`** (state:1013). **Therefore a duplicate leader self-vote re-forms the QC and re-enters the commit path even when it adds no new effective vote.**

**Corrected R definition (producer-neutral).** **R** (per §26.2q) is purely an **evaluation-time** property: *does a production-reachable first leader self-vote reach `try_commit_with_qc` with `(r1)` resident `B`/`P`/`G` each bearing `own_qc`, `(r3)` strict stored views `g_view<p_view<b_view`, `(r4)` `g_height > committed_height`, and `(r5)` `should_commit` — and thereby write `committed_block`/`committed_height` to a value they did not already hold?* The QC may arrive at that self-vote by **either producer route**:
- **γ route:** the self-vote is the **completing `q`-th vote** on a `q−1` key (needs a distinct same-view block to suppress one signer; §26.2x/§26.2x.1). 
- **β route:** the key is **already quorate** (`≥q`) from catch-up **before** the self-vote; the self-vote is a `DuplicateSameBlock`/`Ok(false)` (or a `FirstVote` onto an already-quorate key), and the **idempotent `maybe_qc_for`** re-forms the QC ⇒ `on_qc` ⇒ `try_commit`. **No `q−1` key and no distinct same-view block are required.** Critically, `on_leader_step` runs `register_block(B, cv, parent=lock, …)` **before** the self-vote (basic:2253–2259), which **overwrites `B`'s node** (own_qc→None, then re-set by `on_qc`; `B.parent ← lock` full id; `B.height ← resident(lock).height+1`), so at `try_commit` the chain is `B ← lock ← lock.parent` evaluated on the overwritten node.
**Neither a QC nor `on_qc` alone proves R; only a new commit-state write with `(r1)–(r5)` satisfied does.** ⟨**A39.3**⟩ §26.2y.2's "R needs a `q−1` equivocation-starved target and a distinct same-view block" is **WITHDRAWN as a necessary condition for R** (it is the γ-route condition only). The header, §26.2y.2, the CONS-3 cell, and the mapping are updated to this producer-neutral statement; the γ-only phrasing is kept as dated history, marked superseded.

**Part B — the two existing β candidates, re-evaluated at their actual evaluation-time nodes.**

**(1) A33.1 / §26.2p (clean resident anchor, N=4).** Catch-up Step A admits `[G@2, P@3, B@4]` each `{1,2,3}` off resident anchor `C` (height 1); stored height == view (clean chain). When `B`'s catch-up QC forms, `try_commit(qc_B)` **commits `G` during Step A** (`g_height 2 > committed_height 1`, strict views `2<3<4`, should_commit true) ⇒ `committed_block=G, committed_height=2`.
