**(2) A37 / §26.2w (overwritten height-0 anchor, N=4).** Step 1 overwrites anchor `C` to **stored height 0** (nonresident-lock target), so Step-2 catch-up blocks `T_i` off `C(h0)` get **stored heights `1..134`, all below `committed_height=256`** ⇒ **no catch-up 3-chain commits** (floor), `committed` stays `(C,256)`. Step 4 leader self-vote at view 262 (`lock=T_5`, `D(2,262,T_5)=T_6`): `register_block` overwrites `T_6` (height `= T_5.height+1 = 6`, own_qc→None), self-vote `FirstVote` for id 2 onto the **already-quorate** `(262,T_6)={0,1,3}` ⇒ `{0,1,2,3}` ⇒ **β** QC; `on_qc` re-sets `T_6.own_qc`, `try_commit`: `B=T_6,P=T_5,G=T_4` own_qc ✓, strict views `260<261<262` ✓, **but `(r4)` `g_height(T_4 stored height 4) > committed_height(256)` false** ⇒ **NO commit**. **Accepted steps:** eviction+re-admission+β self-vote coexist (§26.2w's purpose); QC re-forms; own_qc/strict views hold. **Rejected step (first failing R predicate):** `(r4)` height floor — the **overwrite that prevented catch-up commits also pinned `G`'s stored height (4) far below `committed_height` (256)**.

**Does source establish a general exclusion of β-driven R? NO.** The two candidates expose a **coupling**, not a proof: in the **clean-anchor** regime the catch-up 3-chain that confers `own_qc` on `G` **also advances `committed_height` to ≥ `g_height`** (A33.1), so the later β self-vote finds `G` committed / the floor at equality; in the **overwritten-anchor** regime catch-up commits are suppressed but `G`'s stored height is then **below `committed_height`** (A37), so the floor fails. ### 26.2y.4 A39.4 — the evaluation-time commit chain, and the committed-node-absent eviction premise (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. **Part A** names the exact IDs/fields `try_commit_with_qc` reads at a leader self-vote and corrects §26.2y.3's "`G = lock.parent`" to the **pre-vote lock's block**, distinguishing it from the possibly-replaced **live** `locked_qc`. **Part B** reads `evict_commit_log_if_needed` in full (it touches **only** `commit_log` — **not** a committed-absent lever, correcting §26.2y.3's lever (b)) and gives a **scoped exclusion** of the block-map committed-absent `(r5)` arm under the `is_block_safe_to_evict` protections, naming the one residual unread premise. **R stays source-OPEN**; the producer-neutral β/γ definition (§26.2y.3), the W-chain collision (§26.2y.2), and the γ witness (§26.2x/§26.2x.1) are preserved. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — ordered evaluation-time states of one leader self-vote.** Let `L` be the **pre-vote lock snapshot** (`locked_qc` at entry to `on_leader_step`): `L.block_id`, `L.view`.
1. **Parent selection (basic:2244–2250):** `parent_id = locked_qc().block_id = L.block_id` (else committed_block, else `[0xFF;32]`). **Reads `L.block_id`.**
2. **Derive + register B (basic:2253–2259):** `B = make_block_id(L.block_id) = D(local, cv, L.block_id)` (basic:2061→2043: `LE64(local)‖LE64(cv)‖L.block_id[0:16]`); `justify_qc = L`; `register_block(B, cv, Some(L.block_id), L)`. The node for `B` is (re)written: **`parent_id = L.block_id` (full 32-byte), `view = cv`, `height = resident(L.block_id).height + 1`, `own_qc = None`** (block_state.rs:106). ⟨if `B` collided with a resident id, this overwrites it — §26.2y.2⟩.
3. **Self-vote (basic:2332 → on_vote state:952):** `record_vote_history(local,cv,B)`; `votes.on_vote`; `maybe_qc_for((cv,B))` → `qc_B` by **γ** (completes a `q−1` key) **or β** (key already `≥q`; idempotent, §26.2y.3). `qc_B.block_id = B`, `qc_B.view = cv`.
4. **on_qc (state:995–1013):** `replace_lock = (locked_qc None) ∨ (qc_B.view(cv) > locked_qc.view)`; if so **`locked_qc ← qc_B`** — the **live lock is now `qc_B`**; then `blocks.get_mut(B).own_qc = qc_B`; then `try_commit_with_qc(qc_B)`.
5. **try_commit_with_qc (state:1029–1096) — the chain lookup:** `b = blocks.get(qc_B.block_id) = B`, `b_view = B.view = cv`; `p_id = B.parent_id = L.block_id`, `P = blocks.get(L.block_id)`, `p_view = P.view`; `g_id = P.parent_id = parent(L.block_id)`, `G = blocks.get(g_id)`, `g_view = G.view`, `g_height = G.height`. **`try_commit` never reads `locked_qc`** — the structural chain is fixed at step 2 as **`B → L.block_id → parent(L.block_id)`**, where `L` is the **pre-vote** lock. The step-4 lock replacement to `qc_B` is **irrelevant** to the chain.

**⟨A39.4 — correction⟩** §26.2y.3 wrote "`G = lock.parent`". Precisely: **`G = parent(L.block_id)` where `L` is the pre-vote lock snapshot** (whose `block_id` `register_block` captured as `B`'s parent), **not** the live post-`on_qc` `locked_qc` (which may already be `qc_B`). **Residency/overwrite premises for the chain to even reach `(r3)–(r5)`:** `L.block_id` must be **resident** with `own_qc` (else `P = None` ⇒ `try_commit` returns at state:1050–1053 — a TC-installed lock may name a **nonresident** block, §26.2s, giving `P=None` and no commit); `parent(L.block_id)` must be **resident** with `own_qc` (else `G=None` ⇒ return at 1072–1075); `B.height = resident(L.block_id).height+1`; `g_height = G.height` (stored). **Neither the lock replacement (step 4) nor the `own_qc` attachment proves a commit** — only `(r1)` resident `B/P/G` with `own_qc`, `(r3)` strict `g_view<p_view<cv`, `(r4)` `g_height>committed_height`, `(r5)` `should_commit` do.

**Part B — the two eviction mechanisms, separated.**

**(i) `evict_commit_log_if_needed` (state:704–712, VERBATIM below).** It compares `commit_log.len()` to `max_commit_log_entries` and, if over, `commit_log.drain(0..excess)` (removes the oldest `excess` `CommittedEntry` records from the front) and bumps `evicted_commit_log_entries`. **It touches ONLY the `commit_log` Vec.** It does **not** read or write `blocks`, `committed_block`, or `committed_height`. Its sole caller is inside `try_commit_with_qc` (state:1135), after a commit-log push. **⟨A39.4 — correction⟩ `evict_commit_log_if_needed` cannot make `blocks.get(committed_id)` absent**; §26.2y.3's lever (b) must **not** list "commit-log eviction" as a committed-absent route (its name includes "evict" but the mechanism is a bounded history-Vec trim). `commit_log` is an append-only audit history; draining it loses old *records*, never a block node or the committed scalars.

// hotstuff_state_engine.rs:704-712  evict_commit_log_if_needed — VERBATIM (commit_log Vec only; no blocks / committed_* touch)
    fn evict_commit_log_if_needed(&mut self) {
        let max_entries = self.limits().max_commit_log_entries;
        if self.commit_log.len() > max_entries {
            let excess = self.commit_log.len() - max_entries;
            // Remove the oldest `excess` entries from the front
            self.commit_log.drain(0..excess);
            self.evicted_commit_log_entries += excess as u64;
        }
    }

### 26.2y.5 A39.5 — correcting §26.2y.4's committed-node eviction quantifier against §26.2r (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. §26.2y.4 asserted the committed node is **always** at `height == committed_height`, hence **always** protected by `is_block_safe_to_evict` rule #1, hence the `should_commit` committed-absent `(r5)` arm is **unreachable** (unconditional eviction-table "NO"). **That over-claims.** §26.2r (A33.3) already establishes a jointly-admissible state (`committed_block=C`, `committed_height=h`) in which a **same-ID `register_block` overwrite leaves resident `C.height = h+3`** — so rule #1 **does not** protect `C` there; it is protected instead by rules **#2 (locked-ancestor) and #4 (ancestor of an `own_qc`-bearer)**. This pass corrects §26.2y.4's quantifier to its supported **conditional** scope and names the genuinely unresolved transition. Part A's pre-vote-lock chain and the finding that commit-log trimming removes **no block node** are retained; β/γ (§26.2y.3), the W-chain collision (§26.2y.2), and the γ witness (§26.2x/§26.2x.1) stay separate and unchanged. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Correction 1 — writer-time equality vs preserved equality.** The equality `committed_block.node.height == committed_height` is established **at the instant a committed-block writer runs**: `try_commit` sets `committed_block=g_id` and `committed_height=g_height` together (state:1120–1121); `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` inserts the anchor at `height=committed_height` (state:1197/1261). It is **not** an invariant **preserved across later registrations**: `committed_height` is a scalar that only those writers change, whereas the resident node at `committed_id` can be **re-registered** (same-ID `register_block` overwrite, §26.2N/§26.2r) to a **different stored height** computed from a new parent. §26.2r's established end-state: `C` overwritten to `{parent=B2, height=v+2=h+3, own_qc=None}` while `committed_block=C, committed_height=h` stay fixed. So **`C.height (h+3) > committed_height (h)`** — the writer-time equality is **not preserved**. §26.2y.4 conflated the two; corrected here.

**Correction 2 — rule #1 is conditional; in the §26.2r state protection is #2 ∧ #4.** `is_block_safe_to_evict` returns `false` (protected) if **any** of rules #1–#4 holds (state:596–652). In the §26.2r end-state (verbatim-sourced there): **#1 LOST** (`h+3 ≤ h` false); **#3 ABSENT** (`C.own_qc=None` after the overwrite); **#2 PROTECTS** (`locked_qc=qc_B2`; parent-walk `B2→B1→parent==C`); **#4 PROTECTS** (`B1` has `own_qc`; walk `B1→parent==C`). So `is_block_safe_to_evict(C)=false` there — **but via #2/#4, not #1.** §26.2y.4's "always protected by rule #1", "committed-absent arm unreachable (unconditional)", and the eviction-table "**NO**" entries for the committed node are therefore **narrowed**: they hold **only while `C.height ≤ committed_height` (rule #1 in force)**; once a same-ID overwrite raises `C.height` above `committed_height` (established, §26.2r), **rule #1 lapses** and the committed node's protection rests **entirely on #2 and #4** (and transiently #3 until the overwrite clears `own_qc`). (The §26.2y.4 point that a same-ID overwrite keeps the id **present**, not absent, stands — but its significance is **defeating rule #1**, not irrelevance.)

**Correction 3 — `evict_commit_log_if_needed` finding RETAINED.** Unchanged and correct: `evict_commit_log_if_needed` (state:704–712) drains only the `commit_log` Vec; it removes **no block node** and cannot make `blocks.get(committed_id)` absent. The committed-absent `(r5)` arm can only be reached by **block-map** removal of `committed_id`.

**The genuinely unresolved transition (exact remaining source premise).** Removing `C` from `blocks` (⇒ the `(r5)` committed-absent arm) requires an admissible sequence that:
1. **(established, §26.2N/§26.2r)** same-ID-overwrites `C` to `height > committed_height`, defeating rule #1, and clears `C.own_qc` (defeating #3);
2. **(open)** also defeats **rule #2** — a later TC installs a lock **off** the `C`/`B2` chain so `C` is neither the locked block nor a locked-ancestor (a TC lock install changes only `locked_qc`; it creates no node, attaches no `own_qc`, deletes nothing — §26.2k);
3. **(open)** also defeats **rule #4** — `C` must cease to be an ancestor of **every** resident `own_qc`-bearer. In the §26.2r state `B1`,`B2` bear `own_qc` and have `C` as a parent-chain ancestor; `own_qc` is only ever **set** by `on_qc` and **cleared** only by a full same-ID re-registration (`BlockNode::new` ⇒ `own_qc=None`), so stripping `C`'s QC-ancestry means **re-registering `B1` and `B2`** (or otherwise disconnecting `C` from their parent chains) — and `B1`,`B2` are themselves protected (#3 `own_qc`, and #2 as the locked block / its ancestor), so each such re-registration is its own guarded step; ⟨**A39.6 — CORRECTION (§26.2y.6)**: this over-states the necessary steps. A **single** same-ID re-registration of `B1` with a new parent `X` (ancestry avoiding `C`) re-points `B1.parent` away from `C` **and** clears `B1.own_qc`, which drops **both** #2 (the lock `B2`'s ancestry walk `B2→B1→X` no longer reaches `C`) **and** #4 (the sole remaining `own_qc`-bearer `B2` no longer has `C` as an ancestor) — so `is_block_safe_to_evict(C)=true` after one `B1` re-registration, with **no** `B2` re-registration and **no** TC lock change. That is graph reasoning only; its production admissibility is **rejected on the catch-up path** (anchor guard forces `parent==C`) and **unread on the leader path**, and `C`-removal needs a further capacity trigger — §26.2y.6.⟩
4. **(open)** reaches a removal path: the legacy `register_block` → `evict_blocks_if_needed` (runs its pop loop **only** when `blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks`, state:661), or the Run-422 `register_block_with_verified_justification` → `reserve_block_slot_for_new` (admits only when `count_safe_to_evict_excluding(id) ≥ deficit`, else `Err(SlotCapacityUnavailable)` with no eviction); **both remove only `is_block_safe_to_evict` blocks.**

**Two inferences explicitly NOT drawn (task caveats).** (i) **Absence is not inferred from the loss of rule #1 alone** — losing #1 (and #3) leaves #2∧#4, which protect `C` in the established state; absence requires defeating those too (open). (ii) **R is not inferred from absence alone** — even a reachable absent committed node only makes the `(r5)` "committed id absent ⇒ true" arm available; R still **independently** requires the β (or γ) producer, resident `B/P/G` with `own_qc`, strict views `(r3)`, the height floor `(r4)` `g_height > committed_height`, and a resulting **new** commit-state write.

### 26.2y.6 A39.6 — the single-B1 re-registration route to an evictable committed node (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. §26.2y.5 said defeating the committed node `C`'s protections #2 **and** #4 requires **"re-registering `B1` and `B2`"**. **That over-states the necessary steps.** By graph reasoning on the recorded §26.2r state (`C→B2→B1→C`, `lock=B2`, `own_qc` on `B1`/`B2`, `C.height=h+3`), a **single** same-ID re-registration of `B1` with a new full parent `X` (ancestry avoiding `C`) makes **`is_block_safe_to_evict(C)=true`** — no TC lock change and no `B2` re-registration. **But** that re-registration is **not established production-admissible**, and even if it were, `C`'s removal is a separate, unmet capacity step. **`blocks.get(committed_id)=None` ⇏ R.** R stays source-OPEN; the commit-log distinction, the pre-vote-lock chain, the γ witness (§26.2x/§26.2x.1), and the W-chain collision (§26.2y.2) are preserved. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part 1 — conditional graph reasoning: one `B1` re-registration drops #2 and #4 together.** Starting state (§26.2r, established): `C.parent=B2`, `B2.parent=B1`, `B1.parent=C`; `locked_qc=qc_B2`; `B1.own_qc`,`B2.own_qc` set; `C={height=h+3, own_qc=None}`, `committed_block=C`, `committed_height=h`. Apply **one** same-ID re-registration `register_block(B1, view_B1, parent=X, …)` where `X` is resident with **ancestry avoiding `C`**. Effect (state:731–763 + block_state.rs:94–111): `B1.parent←X`, `B1.height←resident(X).height+1`, **`B1.own_qc←None`** (`BlockNode::new`); `B2` is **not** touched (`B2.parent=B1`, `B2.own_qc` intact); `C` untouched. New graph: `C→B2→B1→X→…(avoids C)` — the `C→B2→B1→C` cycle is **broken** at `B1`. Now evaluate all four `is_block_safe_to_evict(C)` clauses (state:596–652):
- **#1 (`C.height ≤ committed_height`)**: `h+3 ≤ h` false ⇒ **does not protect** (lost already via the §26.2r overwrite).
- **#2 (C==locked_id ∨ C is locked-ancestor)**: `locked_id=B2≠C`; parent-walk `B2→B1→X→…` never reaches `C` (X avoids C) ⇒ **does not protect**. ⟨B1's re-pointed parent severs the lock→…→C path⟩
- **#3 (`C.own_qc.is_some()`)**: `None` ⇒ **does not protect**.
- **#4 (C is ancestor of any `own_qc`-bearer)**: the `own_qc`-bearers are now `{B2}` (B1 cleared; C none; X/ancestors only if they bear it, and they avoid C). Walk from `B2`: `B2→B1→X→…` — `C` not found ⇒ **does not protect**. ⟨the single re-registration both (i) clears `B1`'s `own_qc` and (ii) removes `C` from `B2`'s ancestor chain — so the one `own_qc`-path to `C` is gone⟩
⇒ **`is_block_safe_to_evict(C)=true`.** **So §26.2y.5's "re-register `B1` and `B2`" is corrected: a single `B1` re-registration (new parent `X`, ancestry avoiding `C`), on top of the already-established `C`-overwrite-to-`h+3`, defeats #1/#2/#3/#4 jointly — `B2` need not be re-registered and no TC lock change is needed.** This is **conditional graph reasoning**; its production admissibility is Part 2.

**Part 2 — source prerequisites for re-registering the *same full `B1` id* with parent `X`; first rejecting / unread guard.** `B1`'s id is fixed: with its original parent `C`, `B1 = D(proposer_{B1}, view_{B1}, C) = P_{view_{B1}} ‖ C[0:16]` (basic:2043–2058). To re-register **the same id** `B1` with parent `X`, the derivation must reproduce it: `D(proposer, view, X) = P_{view} ‖ X[0:16] = B1` ⇒ **`proposer=proposer_{B1}`, `view=view_{B1}` (= `h+1` in the §26.2r trace), and `X[0:16] = C[0:16]`** (block-ID **prefix equality**). So `X` must be a resident block sharing `C`'s 16-byte prefix (a `view(C)`/`leader(view(C))` block distinct from `C`) whose ancestry avoids `C`. Admission paths:
- **Catch-up (`apply_restore_catchup_blocks`, basic:2122–2160): REJECTED at the anchor guard.** The cursor is `expected_height = committed_height()+1 = h+1` and `expected_parent = committed_block() = C` (basic:2130–2136). `B1` has `view_{B1}=h+1` and `h==v` ⇒ `height=h+1`, admissible **only** at cursor 1 (first block), where `block.parent_block_id` must `== expected_parent = C` (basic:2147). Our required `parent = X ≠ C` ⇒ **`AnchorMismatch` `Err`** — the **first rejecting guard**. (An interior cursor `k>1` has `expected_height=h+k` and `h==v` forces `view=h+k≠h+1`, so `B1` cannot sit there.) The catch-up route cannot give `B1` any parent other than the committed anchor `C`.
- ⟨**A39.7 — now DECIDED: leader route SOURCE-REJECTED (not unread); see §26.2y.7**: §26.2i's writer inventory + A14/§21 monotonicity decide it. After the overwrite leader step `proposed_in_view=true, current_view=v`; a second `on_leader_step` at `v` returns at `if self.proposed_in_view { return }` (basic:2233), and every path that clears `proposed_in_view` also advances `current_view` forward past `v` (restart/reinit excluded), so `make_block_id` never re-derives `B1`'s id. All three production registrars (catch-up/leader/ingest_proposal) reject the single-`B1` route ⇒ that route is CLOSED (scoped).⟩ **Leader (`on_leader_step`, basic:2228–2259): prerequisites UNREAD/unmet.** The leader derives `B = make_block_id(lock.block_id) = D(local, current_view, lock.block_id)` (basic:2253→2061). For `B=B1`: `current_view = h+1`, `local = leader(h+1)`, and `lock.block_id = X` with `X[0:16]=C[0:16]`. Obstructions: (i) **one proposal per view** — `if self.proposed_in_view { return }` (basic:2233); the §26.2r overwrite leader step already proposed at the relevant view, so a second leader proposal there is blocked; (ii) **view monotonicity** — `current_view` returns to `h+1` only if it never advanced past it (`on_timeout_certificate` admits only `tc.view > current_view`; `advance_view` increments), so once past `h+1` the leader can never re-derive a `view_{B1}=h+1` id; (iii) the **lock must already name `X`** (`X[0:16]=C[0:16]`, `X` resident, ancestry avoiding `C`) at that step. Whether a production sequence presents `current_view=h+1 ∧ proposed_in_view=false ∧ locked_qc=X` with those properties is **not traced** — this is the **unread guard**; I stop here and do **not** construct it.

**Part 3 — even if `B1` were re-registered, `C`'s removal is a separate, unmet step (do not infer removal from the predicate).** `C` sits in `pending_block_order` **once** (from restore; same-ID overwrites don't re-enqueue — all enqueue sites guard on `is_new`, §26.2r). The single `B1` re-registration (same-id, `is_new=false`) enqueues nothing. Removal happens only inside `evict_blocks_if_needed`'s pop loop, which runs **only while `blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks` (=4096)** (basic:661), or via `reserve_block_slot_for_new` at capacity. The §26.2r state holds a handful of blocks — **far below the cap** — so **no eviction runs** even though `is_block_safe_to_evict(C)` now returns `true`; `C` stays resident. Driving `blocks.len()` past 4096 (with `C` still queued and the ancestry walks terminating now that the cycle is broken — note A33-F1/§26.2s's non-termination applied to the *cyclic* state) is a **separate large construction, not traced here**. ⟨A39.6⟩ a `true` from the eviction predicate is **necessary, not sufficient** — removal requires the capacity trigger to actually fire and pop `C`.

**Part 4 — `blocks.get(committed_id)=None` is not R.** An absent committed node changes **one** branch of `(r5) should_commit` (the `blocks.get(committed_id)=None ⇒ true` arm, state:1109–1112). R still **independently** requires: the **β (or β/γ) producer** forming `qc_B` at a leader self-vote; resident `B`,`P`,`G` each with `own_qc`; strict stored views `g_view<p_view<cv` `(r3)`; the height floor `(r4)` `g_height>committed_height`; and a resulting **new** commit-state write. None of those is supplied by `C`'s absence.

**Reassessed status.** §26.2y.5's necessary-step claim is **corrected**: defeating `C`'s #2∧#4 needs only a **single** `B1` re-registration (graph-theoretically), not `B1`+`B2`. But that re-registration is **not established production-admissible** — the catch-up route is **rejected** at the anchor guard (parent must be the committed anchor `C`), and the leader route's prerequisites (`current_view=h+1`, `proposed_in_view=false`, `lock=X` with `X[0:16]=C[0:16]`) are **unread**. Even granting it, `C`'s removal needs a **separate, unmet** capacity trigger. So the committed-absent `(r5)` arm remains **neither established reachable nor excluded**, and — being only one `(r5)` branch — would not establish R even if reached. **R stays source-OPEN.**

**Separation of results.**
- **Source-established (this pass):** the single-`B1`-re-registration graph result (one re-registration defeats #1/#2/#3/#4 for `C`); the block-ID prefix-equality requirement `X[0:16]=C[0:16]`; the **catch-up anchor-guard rejection** (parent must `== committed_block = C`, basic:2147); that `C` is enqueued once and no eviction runs below the `max_pending_blocks` cap.

### 26.2y.7 A39.7 — the single-B1 route decided against the proposal-flag / view-writer inventory and the full `register_block` caller set (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. §26.2y.6 left the **leader-route** admissibility of a same-ID `B1` re-registration "unread." Using §26.2i's positive-controlled proposal-flag / view-writer inventory (reused, not re-derived) and A14/§21 view-monotonicity, that route is now **source-REJECTED**, not unread. A positive-control of **all** in-tree `register_block` / `register_block_with_verified_justification` callers finds exactly three production callers; **all three reject** re-registering `B1` with an off-`C` parent `X`. **This closes the specific single-`B1` route** — **not** the whole committed-absent `(r5)` arm, **not** the capacity-trigger question, **not** producer-neutral R. The **conditional graph fact** (one *admissible* off-`C` `B1` re-registration would defeat #2 ∧ #4, §26.2y.6) is preserved and kept distinct from whether any production caller can perform it. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — leader route SOURCE-REJECTED (proposal flag + forward-only view writers).** The §26.2N/§26.2r continuation's leader step at `v=h+1` already proposed the block whose id is `C` (via `on_leader_step` → `register_block(C,…)`), setting **`proposed_in_view=true`** (basic:2329) and leaving **`current_view=v`**. Positive-control of the two state fields (⟨reuses §26.2i⟩):
- **`proposed_in_view` writers (8, exhaustive):** set **true** only at `on_leader_step` (basic:2329); set **false** at `advance_view` (1805), `set_view` (1866), `initialize_from_restart` (1941), `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` (2014), `ingest_proposal` (2738), `try_advance_to_view` (3123), `on_timeout_certificate` (3293). **Every `false`-writer writes `current_view` on the immediately preceding line** (1804/1865/1940/2013/2737/3122/3292) — the flag is never cleared without a concurrent `current_view` write.
- **The `current_view` writers partition into forward-advance vs restart/reinit:** `advance_view` (to_view = current+1, forward), `try_advance_to_view` (rejects `target ≤ current_view` with "ignoring to preserve safety", basic:3105–3113 — forward only, A14/§21), `on_timeout_certificate` (requires `tc.view > current_view`, basic:3264 — forward), `set_view` (unconditional, but its production caller `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` guards `if current_view < expected_height` — forward, basic:2207), `ingest_proposal` (sets to the proposal's view — forward, and Required-rejected on DevNet, Part B); versus **restart/reinit** `initialize_from_restart` (`current_view = committed_height+1`) and `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` (`current_view = snapshot_height+1`) — these **can** move `current_view` backward but are **process restart / reinitialization**, kept **separate** (not a within-execution revisit; arithmetic wrap likewise excluded).
⇒ **In one non-wrapping, non-restarting execution:** a second `on_leader_step` while `current_view=v` returns immediately at `if self.proposed_in_view { return }` (basic:2233) — **first rejecting guard**, before parent/lock `X`. Clearing `proposed_in_view` requires one of the forward writers, which moves `current_view` strictly past `v` (monotone); thereafter `on_leader_step` derives `make_block_id(parent) = D(local, current_view, parent)` with `current_view > v`, whose view-bytes ≠ `v`, so the derived id is **never** `B1` (`B1`'s view-bytes are `v`) for any parent. **So no leader invocation ever re-registers `B1`'s id with any parent — the route is source-rejected by the flag + forward-view inventory, not "unread."**

**Part B — bounded caller completeness (positive control).** The **only** production callers of the two registrars (all other call sites are in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, basic:3315+, and binary test modules at 21xxx–22xxx):
- `register_block`: **(1)** `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` (basic:2186), **(2)** `on_leader_step` (basic:2259), **(3)** `ingest_proposal` (basic:2806, the `verified_evidence=None` arm);
- `register_block_with_verified_justification`: **(3′)** `ingest_proposal` (basic:2798, the `Some(evidence)` arm).

First rejecting guard, per caller, for re-registering the **same full `B1` id** with parent `X≠C`:
- **(1) Catch-up** — **REJECTED at the anchor guard** (retained from A39.6): `expected_parent = committed_block = C`, and `B1` (`h==v`, view `h+1`) is admissible only at cursor 1, where `block.parent_block_id` must `== C` (basic:2147); `X≠C` ⇒ `AnchorMismatch`.
- **(2) Leader** — **REJECTED at the proposal-flag / forward-view inventory** (Part A), before parent/lock `X`.

Only the **test-only `LocalFixtureUnsigned`** policy passes it through. So `ingest_proposal` is **not production-reachable on DevNet**, and cannot re-register `B1`. (Were it reached, `block_id=B1` would additionally require the header to carry `parent=X` with `X[0:16]=C[0:16]` and pass the safe-to-vote/view gates — but the authority gate rejects first.)

**Net on the single-`B1` route — CLOSED (scoped).** Across **all three** production registrars, re-registering `B1` with an off-`C` parent `X` is source-rejected at the first guard (anchor / proposal-flag / Proposal-Vote-authority). **The specific single-`B1` re-registration route to make `C` evictable is therefore CLOSED** under the scoped assumptions (non-wrapping `u64` views; no restart/reinit via `initialize_from_restart` / `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline`; DevNet `Required` policy). **Explicitly NOT closed:** (i) the **whole committed-absent `(r5)` arm** — other mechanisms to orphan or remove `C` from `blocks` (e.g. re-registering `C` itself differently, multi-block reconfigurations, or other decoupling levers) are **not** enumerated here; (ii) the **capacity-trigger** removal step (`blocks.len() > max_pending_blocks`) — still a separate open question even granting an evictable `C`; (iii) **producer-neutral R** — the β/γ producer, resident `B`/`P`/`G` with `own_qc`, strict views `(r3)`, the height floor `(r4)`, and a **new** commit-state write remain independent, open requirements.

**Preserved distinction (conditional graph fact vs production admissibility).** §26.2y.6's graph result stands: *if* some admissible caller re-registered `B1` with a parent `X` whose ancestry avoids `C`, it would clear `B1.own_qc` and re-point `B1.parent`, defeating `C`'s protections #2 **and** #4 in one step. ### 26.2y.8.1 A39.8.1 — QC restoration is signer-history/accumulator-conditional, but C's #2/#4 are independent of `B1.own_qc` (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. §26.2y.8 claimed an admitted same-id `B1` re-registration **always** re-forms its QC and restores `B1.own_qc`. **That is over-general.** Separating the replay by signer-history and accumulator state shows restoration is **conditional**: it holds in the recorded §26.2r state (retained quorate `(v,B1)`), but a **persistent** QC loss is possible under a conjunction (accumulator key evicted **and** a crafted logically-quorate list whose equivocating signer is suppressed below `q`) — whose eviction premise is **not established** to coexist with the §26.2r cycle state. **Decisively, this does not change §26.2y.8's eviction conclusion:** `C`'s protections #2 and #4 are **independent of `B1.own_qc`** (anchored by `B2` via the intact `B2→B1→C` chain), so QC restoration is **moot** for `C`'s eviction. R stays source-OPEN; γ (§26.2x/§26.2x.1), the W-chain result (§26.2y.2), C4/C5 OPEN, RS1, and the RUN-422 boundary are preserved. Audit-only; baseline from the ONDRAT object store; selected `olivexo28/qbind` separate, no transfer. **Public-DevNet scope, execution deferred.**

**§26.2N state recap (verbatim-sourced there).** `C` and `B1` are **both at view `v=h+1`** (`C` overwritten to `{view=v, parent=B2, own_qc=None, height=v+2}`; `B1 = P_v‖P_v`, view `v`). Vote-history at `v`: `(v, s)→B1` for the **3 non-local** `B1` signers, and **`(v, local_id)→C`** (the leader self-vote, step d). Accumulator: `(v,B1)` at `W=3` (quorate), `(v,C)` at `W=1`, `(v+1,B2)` at `W=3`. So the only `(v,·)` history naming a block `≠B1` is `(v, local_id)→C` — **`local_id` is the sole signer that can equivocate against a `B1` re-replay.**

**Replay order per the pinned callers: `qc.validate` → `register_block` → {`record_vote_history` → `votes.on_vote` → `maybe_qc_for`} per signer.** `qc.validate` (`QuorumCertificate::new(B1,v,list).validate`, basic:2183) checks only **membership + no-duplicate + ≥q voting power** over the **supplied list** — it does **not** read vote-history or the accumulator, so any list of ≥q distinct members is admitted regardless of their `(v,·)` histories.

**Case (1) — retained quorate `(v,B1)` (the recorded §26.2r state).** `register_block(B1,v,Some(C))` clears `B1.own_qc` but **does not touch the accumulator** (separate structure); key `(v,B1)` stays `{3 non-local}` at `W=3`. Replay of the supplied ≥q list: any **non-equivocating** signer (`DuplicateSameBlock` for a `B1`-original, or `FirstVote`) falls through to `votes.on_vote` then **`maybe_qc_for(v,B1)`**, which reads the **retained** `W=3 ≥ q` ⇒ `Some(qc_B1)` ⇒ `on_qc` **restores** `B1.own_qc`. An admitted list has ≥q=3 distinct members, of which **at most one (`local_id`) equivocates** (returning `Ok(None)` before `maybe_qc_for`), so **≥2 non-equivocating signers remain and at least one triggers `maybe_qc_for`** on the retained quorate key. ⇒ **QC restored, for every admitted list.** (`on_qc`: lock-replace `v>v+1`? no; `try_commit`: `P=C`, `C.own_qc=None` ⇒ no commit.) **Established in the §26.2r state.**

**Case (2) — `(v,B1)` evicted before the replay.** If the accumulator key `(v,B1)` were evicted (whole-view eviction, `evict_oldest_views`, at `tracked_views ≥ 128`), the replay rebuilds `(v,B1)` from empty; only the **non-suppressed** supplied signers insert. **Premise check:** the §26.2N end-state tracks exactly **two** accumulator views (`{v, v+1}`), far below the 128 cap, so `(v,B1)` is **retained, not evicted**. ⟨**A40 threshold correction (§26.2z)**: the exact trigger is the **insertion of the 128th distinct accumulator view above `v`** — `on_vote` evicts the lowest (`v`) when a new view finds `tracked_views.len() >= 128` before insertion (vote_accumulator:314–320/264–275) — not "> 128 tracked views."⟩ Evicting it from `{v, v+1}` requires admitting catch-up at **126 further higher views (filling the set to 128), whereupon the 127th further view — the 128th distinct view above `v` — is the insert that evicts `v`** (⟨A41 wording fix⟩ 126 further *fill* to 128; the *127th* further evicts), while **preserving** the exact §26.2r cycle state (`C`,`B1`,`B2` resident, `lock=qc_B2`, `committed=(C,h)`, catch-up mode active). **That coexistence is NOT established** — such a multi-view response is a separate construction (cf. the retention-pressure machinery of §26.2x, built for a different target) and is not shown to leave the §26.2r cycle intact. So case (2) is **conditional on an unestablished eviction construction**, not a property of the recorded state.

**Case (3) — evicted `(v,B1)` + a logically-quorate list with an equivocating signer.** Given case (2), a crafted list `{local_id, s1, s2}` (3 distinct ⇒ `qc.validate` ✓): `record_vote_history(local_id,v,B1)` finds `(v,local_id)→C`, `C≠B1` ⇒ **Equivocation ⇒ `Ok(None)`** (suppressed, before `maybe_qc_for`); `s1,s2` (`B1`-originals) insert ⇒ rebuilt `(v,B1)={s1,s2}`, `W=2 < q=3` ⇒ `maybe_qc_for` ⇒ `Ok(None)` ⇒ **no QC ⇒ `B1.own_qc` NOT restored (persistent loss).** But this depends on **both** (2) [eviction] **and** (3) [≤ q−1 non-equivocating supplied signers] — and only `local_id` can equivocate (sole `(v,·)→C` entry), so a response simply supplying the **3 non-local `B1`-originals** would restore the QC even after eviction. ⇒ **persistent QC loss is possible only under the case-(2)∧(3) conjunction, which is not established in the §26.2r state.**

**Corrected statement (replacing "always restores").** In the recorded §26.2r state (retained quorate `(v,B1)`), an admitted same-id `B1` re-registration **re-forms `qc_B1` and restores `B1.own_qc`** (case 1). The **universal** "always restores" is **withdrawn**: a **persistent** QC loss is reachable **iff** the accumulator key `(v,B1)` is evicted (case 2 — requiring a >128-view construction **not established** to coexist with the §26.2r cycle) **and** the crafted list's non-equivocating members number `< q` (case 3 — limited by the single `(v,local_id)→C` equivocation source). This is stated as the **conditional** result; neither (2) nor (2∧3) is established here.

**Reassessing `C`'s #2/#4 independently of `B1.own_qc` (the decisive point).** `is_block_safe_to_evict`'s clauses #2 and #4 **walk parent-chains and test `own_qc` on OTHER nodes**, not `B1`'s:
- **#2** (lock-ancestor): `locked_qc=qc_B2`; walk `B2 → B1 → C` (`B1.parent=C`) matches `C` ⇒ protects — **reads `B1.parent`, not `B1.own_qc`.**
- **#4** (ancestor of an `own_qc`-bearer): `B2.own_qc` is set (unchanged — `B2` not re-registered); walk `B2 → B1 → C` matches `C` ⇒ protects — **the walk follows `parent_id` links and depends on `B2.own_qc`, not `B1.own_qc`.**
So **whether `B1.own_qc` is restored (case 1) or persistently lost (case 2∧3), `C` remains protected by #2 and #4 via `B2` and the intact `B2→B1→C` chain.** Moreover, losing `B1.own_qc` does **not** make `B1` itself evictable: `B1` is independently protected by #2 (ancestor of locked `B2`) and #4 (ancestor of the `own_qc`-bearer `B2`), so `B1` is not removed and the `B2→B1→C` chain stays intact. **Therefore QC restoration is moot for `C`'s eviction: `C` is not evictable in either case.** §26.2y.8's eviction conclusion stands; only its "always restores" sub-reasoning is corrected — and the conclusion no longer rests on restoration at all, but on the `B2`-anchored, `B1.own_qc`-independent protection of both `C` and `B1`.

**No inference drawn.** No eviction is inferred from a (conditional) `B1.own_qc=None` (the §26.2y.8 route stays inert — `C`/`B1` protected via `B2`); no R is inferred from eviction; no new finding. The committed-absent `(r5)` arm remains **neither reachable nor excluded** via other mechanisms (re-registering `C`, `B2` changes + lock change, multi-block), unchanged from §26.2y.5–§26.2y.8.

**Separation of results.**
- **Source-established (this pass):** `C.view = B1.view = v` and the `(v,local_id)→C` history entry (§26.2N); `qc.validate` reads only the supplied list (no history/accumulator) (basic:2183); the retained-quorate `(v,B1)` re-forms `qc_B1` on any admitted list (case 1); a persistent QC loss needs the case-(2)∧(3) conjunction; **#2/#4 (and `B1`'s own protection) are independent of `B1.own_qc`**, anchored by `B2` — so `C` is not evictable in either case.
- **Unresolved available-source:** whether a >128-view accumulator-eviction construction can coexist with the §26.2r cycle state (case 2) — **not** pursued, and **moot** for `C`'s eviction; plus the unchanged R work (other committed-absent mechanisms, capacity trigger, independent producer/commit requirements).

### 26.2aa A41 — the resident-committed-node β route for CONS-3 R: controls excluded by monotonicity; reattachment route reduced to a named unread premise (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. This evaluates **only** the **resident-committed-node** branch of R via **β** (a first leader self-vote whose derived `(cv,B)` key is already quorate). It (A) corrects the §26.2y.8.1/§26.2z accumulator-eviction threshold wording, then (B) uses the two failed β candidates (§26.2y.3) as controls and tests the remaining partial-overwrite/height-recomputation / mixed-regime route against the exact registration, catch-up, QC, and committed-state writers. **Result: the no-reattachment controls are source-EXCLUDED by committed-scalar monotonicity; a new commit requires a prefix-collision reattachment whose joint catch-up-admissibility is a precisely-named UNREAD source premise — neither a witness nor a complete scoped exclusion.** R stays **SR-PARTIAL**. The committed-absent `(r5)` branch, γ, runtime, and remediation are **out of scope** this pass. The A40 cross-revision content observation is kept separate (provenance only). Audit-only; the new external register is the sole write. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — threshold wording corrected.** From `tracked_views = {v, v+1}`: **126 further higher views fill the set to 128** (`v` + `v+1` + 126 = 128); the **insertion of the 127th further view** then finds `tracked_views.len() = 128 ≥ 128` and `evict_oldest_views` removes the lowest (`v`) before inserting (vote_accumulator:314–320/264–275). **That 127th further view is the 128th distinct view above `v`.** (§26.2z/§26.2y.8.1's "126 further … reaching the 128th distinct view above `v`" is corrected: 126 further reach the **127th** distinct view above `v` and fill to 128; the **127th further = 128th distinct above `v`** is the one whose insertion evicts `v`.)

**Part B — the resident-committed-node β route.** Evaluation-time chain (§26.2y.4): at the first leader self-vote at `cv`, `register_block(B = D(local,cv,lock), cv, parent = lock)` runs **before** the vote, fixing `B.parent = lock` and `B.height = resident(lock).height+1`; `on_qc` may replace the live lock with `qc_B` but `try_commit` reads `qc_B.block_id → B.parent_id → P.parent_id`, i.e. the chain **`B → P=lock → G=lock.parent`** off the **pre-vote** lock. A **new resident-committed-node commit** needs, together: `(r1)` `B`,`P=lock`,`G=lock.parent` resident with `own_qc` at evaluation; `(r3)` strict stored views `G.view < P.view < cv`; `(r4)` `G.height > committed_height`; `(r5)` `should_commit` with a **resident** `committed_block ≠ G` and `G.view > committed_block.view`; then a commit write `committed_block:=G, committed_height:=G.height`.

**Controls (§26.2y.3) — EXCLUDED by committed-scalar monotonicity.** ⟨**A41.1 (§26.2ab)**: the two controls A33.1/A37 are **RETAINED** as specific reachable end-states (each a genuine `committed_height`-monotone latch); but the **general** latch bullet below and the "only non-excluded path" claim are **WITHDRAWN** — only `committed_height` is monotone, the `own_qc`/stored-view/stored-height guards are mutable. See §26.2ab.⟩ When `B`'s catch-up parent **equals** its commit-chain parent `P=lock` (no reattachment; `p_c = lock`), catch-up's own `qc_B` (via `B←P←G`) and the leader self-vote's `qc_B` (same `B←P←G`) target the **same** `G`:
- **A33.1 (clean anchor):** catch-up's `qc_B` already committed `G` (predicates held) ⇒ at the leader self-vote `committed_id = G` ⇒ `(r5)` false **and** `g_height = committed_height` ⇒ `(r4)` false.
- **A37 (overwritten h0 anchor):** catch-up stored heights pinned `< committed_height` ⇒ `G.height < committed_height` ⇒ `(r4)` false.
- ⟨**A41.1 (§26.2ab) — WITHDRAWN**: this bullet treats `(r1)` `own_qc` and `(r3)` stored views as static; firsthand they are **mutable** (set by `on_qc`, reset/overwritten by same-ID `register_block`), so an intervening writer can flip the first-failing catch-up guard (g2)/(g3)/(g4) FAIL→PASS before the leader self-vote. Only `committed_height` is monotone. The general exclusion does **not** follow; see §26.2ab.⟩ **General no-reattach latch:** `(r1)` holds (B/P/G have `own_qc`); `(r3)` is static; `committed_height` is **monotonic non-decreasing** (only `try_commit` raises it; restore/reinit are a separate scenario). So if catch-up's `qc_B` did **not** commit `G`, the predicate that blocked it — `(r4)` `G.height > committed_height` (committed only rises) or `(r5)` (`committed_id=G`, or `g_view ≤ committed.view` with `committed.view` only rising) — **still** blocks it at the leader self-vote; and if it **did** commit `G`, `(r5)` is false at the leader self-vote. **⇒ A non-reattached β self-vote never writes a new resident-committed-node commit. The controls are source-excluded.**

**The only non-excluded path — prefix-collision reattachment.** ⟨**A41.1 (§26.2ab)**: "**only**" is **WITHDRAWN** — reattachment remains **a** valid open route, but a **no-reattachment** interleaving whose catch-up `qc_B` is blocked at a non-monotone guard flipped by an intervening `on_qc`/same-ID `register_block` is **also** non-excluded. See §26.2ab.⟩ The latch breaks **iff** `B`'s catch-up parent `p_c ≠ lock=P` while `D(local,cv,p_c) = D(local,cv,P)` — i.e. `p_c` and `P` are **distinct** blocks sharing the 16-byte prefix `P_{P.view}` (both at view `P.view` by `leader(P.view)`), differing only in their parent-prefix: `p_c.parent = G_c` with `G_c[0:16] ≠ G[0:16]`. Then catch-up's `qc_B` (via `B←p_c←G_c`) commits a **different** grandparent `G_c`, while the leader self-vote's reattached `qc_B` (via `B←P←G`) targets `G=lock.parent` — so the monotonicity latch (which assumed a single `G`) does not apply.

**Why the clean reattachment is still blocked.** Under strict contiguity (`block.parent_block_id == expected_parent`, `block.height == block.view`, `block.block_id == D(proposer,view,parent)`, basic:2140–2180), `p_c` and `P` both at view `P.view` force their parents `G_c`,`G` to be the **immediately-lower** wire-height = view `P.view−1`; in a **clean** chain (stored height = view) `G.height = G_c.height = P.view−1`, so catch-up's `qc_B` committing `G_c` sets `committed_height = P.view−1 = G.height` ⇒ `(r4)` `G.height > committed_height` **fails** for the leader self-vote. So a NEW commit of `G` additionally requires a **mixed-regime height-decoupling**: `G.stored_height > G_c.stored_height` (so committing `G_c` leaves `committed_height < G.height`), and/or `G_c` lacking `own_qc` so catch-up's `qc_B` commits nothing (returning at the `G'=G_c` `own_qc` gate, state:1077) while `committed_height` stays `< G.height`.

**Why this is not a witness — the determinism/¬U obstruction.** Assembling a **distinct** sibling `G_c ≠ G` (both at view `P.view−1`, different parents) is constrained by catch-up determinism: a response anchored at a given `committed_block` admits a **deterministic** chain (each block's id is `D(leader(h), h, previous)`, previous fixed by contiguity), so **two responses anchored at the same `committed_block` produce identical ids** — a distinct `G_c` sibling of `G` requires the two responses to anchor at **different** `committed_block` values (the §26.2u ¬U mechanism), hence `committed_block` must take distinct values (via intervening commits) when `G` vs `G_c` are admitted. Composing **that** (distinct-anchor ¬U siblings at the `G`/`p_c` levels) with (i) `P=lock` and `G` carrying `own_qc` with `G` **un-committed** and `G.stored_height > committed_height`, (ii) the **mixed-regime height-decoupling** `G.height > G_c.height`, and (iii) `(cv=P.view+1, B=D(local,cv,P))` quorate while catch-up's `qc_B` commits nothing — all under one reachable `committed_block`/`committed_height` trajectory with monotonic commits — is **not traced to an admissible sequence**. 

**Why this is not a complete exclusion.** The monotonicity latch that excludes the controls **does not apply** once the leader self-vote's grandparent `G=lock.parent` differs from catch-up's committed grandparent `G_c=p_c.parent`; and the clean-height blocker is defeatable in principle by the A16.3 stored-height≠view mechanism (mixed regime). No single guard rejects **all** reattachment constructions, and no non-circular invariant tying "a resident `own_qc`-bearing `G=lock.parent` with `G.height > committed_height` and `G` un-committed at a first leader self-vote" to its own impossibility is established.

**Precise unread source premise (R, resident-committed-node β route).** *Does there exist a production-reachable catch-up/leader interleaving — under the strict contiguity/anchor/`h==v`/`qc.validate` admission guards and monotonic `committed_block`/`committed_height` — in which, at a first eligible leader self-vote at `cv`: the pre-vote `lock=P` and `G=P.parent` are resident with `own_qc`; `G` is un-committed with stored `G.height > committed_height`; `committed_block` is a resident block `≠ G` with view `< G.view`; strict stored views `G.view < P.view < cv` hold; and the key `(cv, D(local,cv,P))` is already quorate via a prefix-collision sibling `p_c ≠ P` (`p_c[0:16]=P[0:16]`, `p_c.parent = G_c`, `G_c[0:16] ≠ G[0:16]`) whose own catch-up `qc_B` commits only `G_c` (or nothing) at a height `< G.height` — the latter requiring the §26.2u ¬U distinct-anchor sibling mechanism together with a mixed-regime stored-height-decoupling `G.height > G_c.height`?* This joint admissibility is the **open available-source question**; it is **source work, not EXEC** (it concerns the registration/catch-up/QC/commit writers, not runtime reproduction), and it is **neither witnessed nor excluded** here.

**Three claims kept separate.** **(1) β forms a QC: YES** — a first leader self-vote on an already-quorate `(cv,B)` key re-forms `qc_B` via the idempotent `maybe_qc_for → on_qc` (established, §26.2y.3). **(2) New commit: NOT established** — excluded for the no-reattachment controls (monotonicity); for the reattachment route it reduces to the unread premise above (clean reattachment blocked by equal `G`/`G_c` heights; mixed-regime decoupling + ¬U-sibling admissibility untraced). **(3) Honest-node safety consequence: NOT analyzed this pass** — a commit-state write is not, by itself, a proven honest-node safety violation; that is a separate question deferred here.

### 26.2ab A41.1 — repairing the no-reattachment β argument: the general exclusion and the "only reattachment" claim are WITHDRAWN; the two concrete controls are retained; R's resident-committed-node β route stays OPEN under a broadened unread premise (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. This repairs §26.2aa's **no-reattachment β argument**. §26.2aa claimed the no-reattachment controls are *source-EXCLUDED by committed-scalar monotonicity* and that *prefix-collision reattachment is the only non-excluded path*. Re-reading the ordered `try_commit_with_qc` guards and the catch-up replay **firsthand** shows that generalization rests on treating `own_qc`, stored views, and stored heights as static/monotone, when **only `committed_height` is monotone**; `on_qc` (an `own_qc` writer) and a same-ID `register_block` (an `own_qc`-reset + stored-field overwriter) can flip the other guards between catch-up's `qc_B` and the later leader self-vote's `qc_B`. **Result: the general no-reattachment exclusion and the "only reattachment" claim are WITHDRAWN; the two concrete no-commit controls (A33.1, A37) are RETAINED as specific reachable end-states; R's resident-committed-node β route is OPEN via a broadened, precisely-named premise — neither witnessed nor excluded.** R stays **SR-PARTIAL**; no count change. The committed-absent `(r5)` branch, γ, runtime, and remediation stay **out of scope**. Audit-only; the new external register is the sole write. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Ordered guard record of `try_commit_with_qc(qc_B)` (source order, state:1029–1117 — firsthand this pass).** Each `return` is a guard; evaluation reaches a guard only if all earlier ones passed:
- **(g1)** `B = blocks.get(qc_B.block_id)` resident **and** `B.own_qc = Some` (else return). Record `b_view = B.view`.
- **(g2)** `B.parent_id = Some(P_id)`, `P = blocks.get(P_id)` resident **and** `P.own_qc = Some` (else return). Record `p_view = P.view`.
- **(g3)** `P.parent_id = Some(G_id)`, `G = blocks.get(G_id)` resident **and** `G.own_qc = Some` (else return). Record `g_view = G.view`, `g_height = G.height`.
- **(g4)** strict stored views `g_view < p_view < b_view` (else return).
- **(g5)** `height_ok`: `committed_height = None ⇒ true`; `Some(h) ⇒ g_height > h`.
- **(g6)** `should_commit`: `committed_block = None ⇒ true`; `Some(cid)`: `cid == g_id ⇒ false`; else `blocks.get(cid)`: `Some(n) ⇒ g_view > n.view`, `None ⇒ true`.
- **commit** `committed_block:=g_id, committed_height:=g_height` **iff** `(g5) ∧ (g6)` (state:1118–1121).

Each of (g1)–(g6) reads the resident nodes' **mutable stored fields** (`own_qc`, `view`, `height`, `parent_id`) and the `committed_block`/`committed_height` scalars **as they are at the evaluation instant**.

**The two evaluation instants (no reattachment, `p_c = P = lock`).** Both are `try_commit_with_qc(qc_B)` on the **same** block id `B`; the chain `B → B.parent_id → (B.parent).parent_id` is read from the resident map **at each instant**.
- **I₁ = catch-up's first `qc_B`** — inside `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` (basic:2122–2211): blocks replay in **ascending contiguous order**; for each block the **full** `qc_signers` set is replayed (`on_vote` per signer, basic:2192–2196) **before** the next block; when a block's replayed quorum completes, `on_vote → maybe_qc_for → on_qc` **writes that block's `own_qc`** and calls `try_commit` (state:970–1013). So `qc_B`'s `on_qc→try_commit` fires within B's own replay iteration.
- **I₂ = the first leader self-vote's `qc_B`** — at `on_leader_step` (basic:2228–2379): `register_block(B = D(local,cv,lock), cv, Some(lock_id), …)` runs **before** the self-vote (fixing `B.parent_id = lock_id = P_id`, §26.2y.4 pre-vote lock), then the self-vote re-forms the already-quorate `(cv,B)` key ⇒ idempotent `maybe_qc_for → on_qc(qc_B) → try_commit(qc_B)`.

**I₁ — the clean contiguous no-reattachment chain (the A33.1 geometry).** B's parent `P` is the catch-up block one iteration earlier; `G = P.parent` two iterations earlier; each has a `qc` (`qc.validate ≥ q`, basic:2183) whose quorum completed in its own earlier iteration ⇒ `on_qc` already wrote `P.own_qc` and `G.own_qc`. At I₁:

| field | value at I₁ (clean chain) |
| --- | --- |
| B resident / `own_qc` | yes / `Some(qc_B)` (just written by `on_qc`) — **(g1) PASS** |
| P = B.parent resident / `own_qc` | yes / `Some(qc_P)`, `P.view = cv−1` — **(g2) PASS** |
| G = P.parent resident / `own_qc` | yes / `Some(qc_G)`, `G.view = cv−2`, `G.height = anchorH + k` — **(g3) PASS** |
| strict views | `cv−2 < cv−1 < cv` — **(g4) PASS** |
| committed_height | ⟨**A41.2 CORRECTION**: for the actual A33.1 construction the floor is the **restore anchor** (`committed_height=1`); `qc_P`'s `try_commit` **did NOT commit** (grandparent is the `own_qc=None` anchor), so catch-up's **`qc_B` is the first commit** (commits `G`, 1→2). The "raised by `qc_P`" cascade holds only in a deeper all-`own_qc` chain. See §26.2ac Part 1.⟩ `G.height > committed_height` — **(g5) PASS** |
| committed_block / its view | `= G.parent (≠ G)`, `g_view > committed_node.view` — **(g6) PASS** |

⇒ **catch-up's `qc_B` COMMITS `G`** (writes `committed_block:=G, committed_height:=G.height`). **There is NO "first failed guard" in the clean chain** — catch-up itself performs the commit. (§26.2aa's framing "*if catch-up's `qc_B` did not commit `G`, the predicate that blocked it is (r4)/(r5)*" mis-describes this case: nothing blocked it.)

**I₂ — same clean chain (nothing re-registered B/P/G).** B/P/G still resident with `own_qc`; chain and stored views unchanged; (g1)–(g4) still pass. `committed_block = G` (from I₁; or a strictly-higher catch-up block if B was interior and later blocks committed past G), `committed_height = G.height` (or higher).
- **(g6)** `committed_id == G ⇒ false` (or, if moved higher, `g_view ≤ committed_node.view ⇒ false`).
- **(g5)** `g_height = G.height = committed_height ⇒ not >` ⇒ `false` (or committed_height already higher).
⇒ **no new commit. The A33.1 control holds** — and it holds **because catch-up's `qc_B` SUCCEEDED** (wrote `committed_block=G` / `committed_height=G.height`) and `committed_height` is monotone (only `try_commit` raises it, state:1120–1121; never falls), so it cannot drop back below `G.height`. This is a genuine committed-scalar-monotonicity latch — **for the clean geometry where catch-up already committed `G`.**

**The configurations where catch-up's `qc_B` does NOT commit `G` — and whether the block is monotone-latched.** Catch-up's `qc_B` fails to commit `G` iff some guard fails at I₁ ((g1) cannot fail — `on_qc` just wrote `B.own_qc`). Per-guard, at I₂:

| first-failing guard at I₁ | field(s) it reads | monotone-latched to I₂? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **(g2)** `P.own_qc = None` | stored `own_qc` of `P = lock` | **NO.** `own_qc` is written by `on_qc`, reset to `None` by a same-ID `register_block` (block_state.rs:106). It usually holds for the lock (locking writes `P.own_qc`=`locked_qc` in the same `on_qc`), but a same-ID re-registration of the lock node after locking resets it. |
| **(g3)** `G.own_qc = None` | stored `own_qc` of `G = P.parent` | **NO.** If `G = lock.parent` is a resident node that never received, or lost (same-ID overwrite), a `qc`, (g3) fails; an intervening `on_qc(qc_G)` between I₁ and I₂ sets `G.own_qc = Some` ⇒ flips **FAIL→PASS**. |
| **(g4)** strict stored views fail | stored `view` of B/P/G | ⟨**A41.2 CORRECTION**⟩ **QUALIFIED — for a DERIVED block, NO flip.** The derived id `D=LE64(proposer)‖LE64(view)‖parent[0:16]` **binds the view**, so any same-ID registration of a derived B/P/G carries the **same stored view** — a plain same-ID `register_block` **cannot** change it. Only the **opaque anchor** (id not a `D`-derivative) has a settable stored view, and only via the §26.2r **prefix-collision** overwrite `D(local,v,·)=anchor-prefix` — which is the **reattachment** mechanism (route A), not a no-reattachment flip. So in the strict no-reattachment setting (g4) is **not** flippable for derived blocks; the available non-monotone flips are **(g3) `own_qc`** and **(g5) stored height** (height is not id-bound). See §26.2ac Part 2. |
| **(g5)** `height_ok` false (`G.height ≤ committed_height`) | `G.stored_height` vs `committed_height` | **PARTIAL only.** `committed_height` is monotone (never falls), **but `G.stored_height` is mutable** — a same-ID `register_block` recomputes `G.height = resident(parent).height + 1` (state:744–747), which can RAISE it above a fixed `committed_height` ⇒ flips **FAIL→PASS**. Latched only if `G` is never re-registered upward (the A37 control's end-state). |
| **(g6)** `should_commit` false | `committed_id`, `g_view`, `committed_node.view` | **PARTIAL only.** `committed_id == G` persists unless a higher commit moves it — and that raises `committed_height` past `G.height`, so (g5) then fails (**this branch is monotone-protected**). But the `g_view ≤ committed_node.view` branch reads the **mutable stored views** of `G` and the committed node, which a same-ID `register_block` can change ⇒ not monotone. |

**Intervening writers (I₁ → I₂), exhaustive (firsthand).**
- **`on_qc`** (state:995–1016): sets `locked_qc` if `qc.view` higher; **writes `node.own_qc = Some(qc)`** for `qc.block_id`; calls `try_commit`. ⇒ can flip **(g2)/(g3) own_qc FAIL→PASS** for `P`/`G`. (It does **not** rewrite a node's stored `view`/`height`/`parent_id`.)
- **same-ID `register_block`** (state:731–763; `insert_block_node` replaces the node, `BlockNode::new` sets `own_qc = None`, block_state.rs:94–111): ⇒ can flip **(g3) own_qc PASS→FAIL**, change **(g4)** stored views, **raise/lower (g5)** `G.stored_height`, and **change the identity of `G`** by overwriting `P.parent_id` (so `G = P.parent` at I₂ need not be `G` at I₁). Not excluded in general between the two instants.
- **committed-state writes** — only `try_commit` (state:1120–1121): `committed_height` strictly **rises** (`height_ok` requires `>`), `committed_block` moves to a strictly-higher-height block. **MONOTONE.** (`initialize_from_restart`/`initialize_from_snapshot_baseline`, state:1197/1261, are restart/reinit — a **separate** scenario, no active-mode intervening write.)

**Preservation result.**
- **Proven where it holds:** if catch-up's `qc_B` **commits `G`** (clean chain / A33.1), or is blocked **purely** by `committed_height ≥ G.stored_height` with **no** intervening same-ID re-registration of the B/P/G chain or of `G` (A37's overwritten-h0 anchor pins `G.height` low and never re-registers `G` upward), then committed-scalar monotonicity **latches** the no-commit to I₂. These are exactly the **two retained controls**: **A33.1 (§26.2p)** — catch-up committed `G` ⇒ `(r5)`∧`(r4)` false at I₂; **A37 (§26.2w)** — `G.height < committed_height` monotone-latched ⇒ `(r4)` false at I₂.
- **Does NOT hold in general:** for a no-reattachment configuration whose **first-failing guard at I₁ is (g2)/(g3) `own_qc`, (g4) strict stored views, or the mutable-stored-field part of (g5)/(g6)**, an intervening `on_qc` (giving `P`/`G` its `own_qc`) or a same-ID `register_block` (overwriting stored views/heights/parents) can flip that guard **FAIL→PASS** before I₂. `committed_height` monotonicity alone does **not** latch these. **No full guard-preservation argument succeeds.**

**Withdrawals (§26.2aa).**
1. The **"General no-reattach latch"** (§26.2aa line *"if catch-up's `qc_B` did not commit `G`, the predicate that blocked it — (r4) … or (r5) … — still blocks it"*) and its conclusion *"a non-reattached β self-vote never writes a new resident-committed-node commit / the controls are source-excluded"* (read as a **general law**) are **WITHDRAWN** as over-claimed. The generalization silently assumed the I₁ first-failing guard is the monotone one and that `own_qc`/stored-views/stored-heights are static; firsthand they are mutable, and the two mutating writers above can change them. **What survives is the two specific controls, not a general exclusion.**
2. The claim *"**reattachment (prefix-collision `p_c≠lock`) is the only non-excluded path**"* (§26.2aa, incl. the "Source-established" bullet) is **WITHDRAWN**. Reattachment remains **a** valid open route, but it is **not the only** one: no-reattachment configurations whose I₁ first-failing guard is a non-monotone guard flippable by an intervening `on_qc`/same-ID `register_block` are **also** not excluded.

The §26.2aa results that **stand**: the Part-A eviction-threshold correction; the pre-vote-lock evaluation-time chain `B→P=lock→G=lock.parent` (§26.2y.4); the **clean-reattachment block** (`G.height=G_c.height` ⇒ `(r4)` fails for the reattachment route); the determinism/¬U constraint on distinct sibling grandparents; and the two controls A33.1/A37 as concrete **no-commit** end-states. Only the **generalization beyond the two controls** is withdrawn.

**Encoded ID prefix vs mutable stored view (reiterated — load-bearing here).** A node's identity `B_id = D(proposer,view,parent) = LE64(proposer)‖LE64(view)‖parent[0:16]` (basic:2043–2058) encodes the **derivation-time** view into the id bytes, but a resident node's **stored** `view`/`height`/`parent_id`/`own_qc` are **mutable**: a same-ID `register_block` keeps the id and overwrites the stored fields, resetting `own_qc = None` (block_state.rs:106). This is sharpest for the **restored anchor**: §26.2N/§26.2r (A16.3) re-registers the committed/anchor node under its own id to a stored `height`/`view` that **differs** from the id-encoded view (resident `C.height = h+3` while `committed_height = h`). So "`G = lock.parent` at view `P.view−1`" is a statement about the **id-encoded** derivation. ⟨**A41.2 CORRECTION**: sharpen — for a **derived** block the stored **view** IS pinned by its id (`D` binds proposer+view; a same-ID registration carries the same view), so (g4) is **not** mutable for derived blocks; only the **stored height** (not id-bound) and **`own_qc`** are mutable, and the stored **view** decouples only for the **opaque anchor** via a prefix-collision overwrite (= reattachment, §26.2r/§26.2ac Part 2). So the non-static, no-reattachment-flippable guards are **(g3) `own_qc`** and **(g5) height** — not (g4). The general latch still fails via (g3)/(g5); the claim is narrowed, not reversed.⟩

**Did this exhibit a witness? No.** Showing the guards are mutable and that `on_qc`/same-ID `register_block` **can** flip them **defeats the exclusion proof**; it does **not** construct a production-admissible interleaving that actually flips a guard and commits. No new commit, no safety violation, is inferred from this unresolved route.

**Precise (broadened) unread source premise (R, resident-committed-node β route).** *Supersedes §26.2aa's "only prefix-collision reattachment."* R's resident-committed-node β route is open via **EITHER** route, both reducing to the **same** underlying question:

> Is there a production-reachable catch-up/leader interleaving — under the strict contiguity/anchor/`h==v`/proposer/`qc.validate` admission guards (basic:2141–2184) and monotone `committed_block`/`committed_height` — such that at a **first** eligible leader self-vote at `cv`, evaluating `try_commit_with_qc(qc_B)` for `B = D(local,cv,lock)`: the pre-vote `lock = P` and `G = P.parent` are **resident with `own_qc`**; strict stored views `g_view < p_view < cv` hold; `G` is **un-committed** with stored `G.height > committed_height`; and `committed_block` is a **resident** block `≠ G` with stored view `< g_view` — **reached without** catch-up's own `qc_B` having already committed `G` **and without** `committed_height` already latched `≥ G.stored_height`?
>

**Part 1 — A33.1 commit provenance corrected (§26.2ab clean-chain table).** §26.2ab's clean-chain cell read `committed_height = G.parent.height` "**raised by `qc_P`'s earlier commit**". Firsthand against §26.2p (A33.1) this is **wrong**. In the A33.1 construction: `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` sets the opaque anchor `C` resident at `height=1, view=1, own_qc=None` with `committed_block=C, committed_height=1` (state:1246–1270); catch-up applies `[G@2, P@3, B@4]`. Then:
- `on_qc(qc_G)` → `try_commit(qc_G)`: `G`'s parent is `C`, `C.own_qc=None` ⇒ **returns at (g2), no commit**.
- `on_qc(qc_P)` → `try_commit(qc_P)`: grandparent is `C`, `C.own_qc=None` ⇒ **returns at (g3), no commit**.
- `on_qc(qc_B)` → `try_commit(qc_B)`: `B→P→G` all `own_qc`, strict views `2<3<4`, `should_commit` (`committed_id=C≠G`, `g_view 2 > C.view 1`), `height_ok` (`g_height 2 > committed_height 1`) ⇒ **COMMIT G** (1→2).

So **`qc_P` did not raise `committed_height`** (its `try_commit` returned no-commit because the grandparent chain bottoms out at the `own_qc=None` anchor); **the restore established `committed_height=1`, and catch-up's `qc_B` later committed `G`**. The general "clean cascade" where an intermediate `qc_P` commits `G.parent` holds **only** in a deeper all-`own_qc` chain; near a freshly-restored opaque anchor the **first** commit is `qc_B`. §26.2ab's table cell and its "clean cascade" wording are corrected by inline ⟨A41.2⟩ markers; the §26.2ab I₁/I₂ no-commit *conclusion* for A33.1 is unchanged (at I₂ `committed_id==G ∧ g_height==committed_height`).

**Part 2 — same-ID stored-view claim qualified; the opaque anchor is a separate case.** §26.2ab's (g4) row claimed "stored views are overwritten by a same-ID `register_block`." Firsthand this is **wrong for an ordinary derived block**: a block's identity is `B_id = D(proposer,view,parent) = LE64(proposer)‖LE64(view)‖parent[0:16]` (basic:2043–2058), which **encodes proposer and view into the id**. To register `id = B` the caller must pass a `(proposer, view, parent)` that derives `B`, so **any** same-ID registration of a derived block carries the **same view** (and proposer); a plain same-ID `register_block` therefore **cannot change a derived `B`/`P`/`G`'s stored view**. What `register_block` **can** change on a same-ID overwrite is the **stored height** (recomputed `resident(parent).height + 1`, state:744–747 — height is **not** id-bound) and `own_qc` (reset to `None`, block_state.rs:106).
- **The opaque restored anchor is the exception.** Its id is **not** a `D`-derivative, so it encodes no view; the §26.2N/§26.2r (A16.3) mechanism re-registers the anchor's id via a **prefix-collision** `D(local,v,B2) = anchor-prefix` and the overwrite then sets the anchor node's stored `view = v` and recomputes its stored `height` (resident `C.height = h+3` while `committed_height = h`). **But that overwrite is a prefix collision — the reattachment mechanism (A41.1 route A), not a plain no-reattachment re-registration.**
- **Consequence for A41.1.** In the **strict no-reattachment** setting the non-monotone guards an intervening writer can flip are **(g3) `own_qc`** (set by `on_qc`, reset by same-ID `register_block`) and **(g5) stored height** (not id-bound); **(g4) stored view is id-pinned for derived blocks** and decouples **only** through the opaque anchor via a prefix collision (= reattachment). The A41.1 **withdrawal of the general exclusion still stands** (via the live (g3)/(g5) routes); it is only **narrowed** — (g4) is not a no-reattachment flip. §26.2ab's (g4) row and the "encoded ID prefix vs mutable stored view" paragraph are corrected by inline ⟨A41.2⟩ markers.

### 26.2ae A41.2.2 — bounded derived-`G` source review for CONS-3 R: §26.2ad qc_P guard corrected in place; one derived-`G` no-reattachment β candidate tested through the vote producers and REJECTED at its first guards; the route is not generalized (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. (Part 1) corrects §26.2ad's `qc_P` guard label in place; (Part 2) tests **one** derived-`G`, no-reattachment β route — catch-up's first `qc_B` fails `(g3)` because a **derived** resident `G` lacks `own_qc` (its supplied logical quorum produced **fewer than `q` effective** votes), and then asks whether a production-reachable later operation can attach `G.own_qc` before the first eligible leader self-vote re-evaluates the already-quorate `(cv,B)` key. **Result: the tested candidate is REJECTED.** Starvation by a **catch-up sibling** makes `G` permanently uncompletable (ceiling `≤ N−q < q`); starvation by the **local leader self-vote** (the only sub-`q` pre-lock, §26.2u's `A6→B5`) leaves `G` completable by counting but blocks the **completion** (re-admission is cursor-rejected once `committed_height ≥ G.view`) and the **β step** (leader-eligibility conflict `local = leader(G.view) ≠ leader(B.view)` for consecutive views, `n ≥ 3`). No new QC for `G` ⇒ no new commit ⇒ no safety consequence. The route is **not** generalized: a variant that keeps `committed` at `G`'s parent (so `G` stays re-admittable) with a **leader-produced** non-adjacent-parent `P` aligning leadership — which entangles the **height-decoupling** route — is **untraced and not excluded**; it is named remaining source work. R stays **SR-PARTIAL / open**; no count change (18/4/27/11). Height-decoupling, prefix-collision reattachment, and committed-absent routes are kept **separate**. **Part 1 — §26.2ad `qc_P` guard corrected in place.** §26.2ad's catch-up bullet stated `try_commit(qc_P)` "grandparent is `C`, `C.own_qc = None` ⇒ returns at **(g3)**." Firsthand the geometry there is `P.parent = C` (anchor), so for `qc_P` the chain is `P → C → C.parent`: `C` is `P`'s **parent**, caught at the **(g2)** gate (`P.parent = C` resident but `C.own_qc = None`), not `(g3)`. The corrected reading: **`try_commit(qc_P)` returns at `(g2)`** (P's parent `C` lacks `own_qc`); **`try_commit(qc_B)` returns at `(g3)`** (B's grandparent `G = C` lacks `own_qc`). This is a guard-label fix; §26.2ad's no-commit result and the `G = anchor` rejection are unchanged. (Marked by an inline ⟨A41.2.2⟩ correction in §26.2ad.)

**Part 2 — the derived-`G` no-reattachment β candidate.**
