### 26.2af A41.2.3 — repair and reassess the derived-`G` review: §26.2ae's sibling-starvation proof, cursor claim, producer set, and I₁ grounding corrected; A41.2.2's general rejection WITHDRAWN; the `B5` instance dispatched non-generalizably; the derived-`G` route is OPEN (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. ⟨**A41.2.4 CORRECTIONS (§26.2ag)**: three statements below are corrected — (1) "re-admission admissible whenever `committed_height < G.view`" over-claims: that only furnishes a **cursor position** `k=G.view−committed_height`; admission requires the full anchor/parent/proposer/id/`qc.validate`/handler guard chain for `G` **and every preceding block**. (2) "completing `G` by a leader self-vote folds into the general β R question" is mislabeled: completing `G` from `q−1` by a leader supplying the `q`-th is **γ for `G`** (§26.2x), while a self-vote on an already-quorate `B` is **β for `B`** (§26.2y.3) — distinct events at distinct views. (3) "the (g5)/(g6) pass leans on stored-height≠view" / "entangled with height-decoupling" is **withdrawn**: with anchor `C@view=height=1` and `G@view=height=2`, (g5)/(g6) pass on **clean heights** — the obstruction is the leader-eligibility conflict (§26.2ag), not the commit predicates.⟩ §26.2ae over-claimed. This pass corrects four points in place and reassesses: **(E1)** the catch-up-sibling "ceiling" proof confused a supplied quorum with `q` effective non-`G` votes; **(E2)** the re-admission cursor is `committed_height = G.view − k` at response position `k`, not uniformly `G.view − 1`; **(E3)** the producer set wrongly excluded the **leader re-deriving an existing block id and self-voting it** (the β mechanism itself); **(E4)** the I₁ step — a first `qc_B` for a block `B` above `P = B6` — was never constructed. **Result: A41.2.2's general "derived-`G` REJECTED on two grounds" is WITHDRAWN. The specific `B5` instance is dispatched (I₁ unestablished; and even granted, `B5` uncompletable) but for `B5`-specific reasons that do NOT generalize. The general derived-`G` no-reattachment β route is NEITHER witnessed NOR excluded — its completion folds into either the already-open general β-self-vote R question (leader re-derivation) or a cursor-constrained catch-up re-admission, and composing a starved-yet-completable `G` with a built `B→P→G` chain and a locally-led β remains the open premise, entangled with height-decoupling.** R stays **SR-PARTIAL / open**; no count change (18/4/27/11). Audit-only; the new external register is the sole write. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**(E1) Sibling-starvation proof corrected — `qc.validate` is a supplied-list quorum, not `q` effective votes.** §26.2ae's "(A)" claimed any catch-up sibling `Y@G.view` forces `E_other ≥ q` (so ceiling `≤ N−q < q`). That is **unsound**: `qc.validate(supplied_Y)` only checks that the **supplied** list has `≥ q` members (vote_accumulator:357–382 / timeout-style membership+quorum); the **effective** votes `Y` contributes are only those of its supplied signers that are `FirstVote` at `G.view`. Partition the **actual first-vote histories** at `G.view` into `E_G` (first-voted `G`), `E_other` (first-voted some non-`G` id), and `F` (never voted at `G.view`): `E_G + E_other + F = N`, and `G`'s attainable ceiling is `E_G + F = N − E_other`. **Permanent inability to complete `G` requires `E_other > N − q`** — a statement about **effective** first-votes, which **cannot** be inferred from a sibling's supplied list. **Overlap case (as the brief requires):** if a sibling `Y`'s supplied signers include validators who **already first-voted `G`**, their vote for `Y` is `Equivocation → Ok(None)` (state:960–966) — they stay in `E_G`, do **not** join `E_other`, and `Y` gets no effective vote from them. So a `≥q`-supplied sibling can leave `E_other ≤ N − q` (even `E_other = 0` if all its supplied signers are `G`-voters or free-but-suppressed), keeping `G` **completable**. The ceiling rejection is therefore **withdrawn**; uncompletability is a construction-specific property (`E_other > N − q`), not a consequence of a sibling existing.

**(E2) Catch-up cursor corrected — position `k`, not only `k = 1`.** §26.2ae's "(B).1" claimed re-admitting `G@G.view` "requires `committed_height = G.view − 1`." That holds **only** at response position `k = 1` (first block). The applier cursor is `expected_height = committed_height + 1` and increments per admitted block (basic:2141/2155), and `h == v`, so a target at **position `k`** has `G.view = committed_height + k`, i.e. **`committed_height = G.view − k`**. Re-admitting `G` is therefore admissible whenever **`committed_height < G.view`** (choose `k = G.view − committed_height ≥ 1`, supplying the `k−1` contiguous ancestors ahead of `G`). **`B5` rejection retained, not generalized:** for `G = B5` (view 6) with `committed = (B2, 6)`, `committed_height = 6 ≥ B5.view = 6`, so `G.view − committed_height = 0` ⇒ **no valid position `k ≥ 1`** — every response position is at height `≥ 7 > 6`, so `B5` can never be a re-admission target. That `B5`-specific block stands; it does **not** extend to a general derived `G` with `committed_height < G.view`.

**(E3) Producer set corrected — the leader can re-derive an existing id and self-vote it.** §26.2ae claimed the "only" producer that can add an effective vote to an **existing** block's `(view, id)` is a catch-up re-admission, excluding leader/`do_vote` self-votes as targeting "the node's own freshly-derived proposal." But the **β mechanism itself** (§26.2p/§26.2ad) is precisely the leader **re-deriving an existing block id** and self-voting it: at `on_leader_step`, `make_block_id(lock) = D(local, current_view, lock)` can equal an already-resident id, `register_block` overwrites it, and `on_vote(local, current_view, id)` adds `local`'s vote. So a **leader self-vote at `G.view`** — with `local = leader(G.view)`, `current_view = G.view`, `!proposed_in_view`, and `lock` sharing `G`'s parent-prefix so `make_block_id(lock) = G` — **adds `local`'s effective vote to `(G.view, G)`** (if `FirstVote`) and can complete `G`'s quorum. Its guards, tested: **leader** `local = leader(G.view)`; **view** `current_view = G.view` (view writers are forward-only, §26.2i — a node at `current_view > G.view` cannot return); **proposal-flag** `!proposed_in_view`; **history** `local` must not have a prior `(G.view, ·)` entry (else `Equivocation`, suppressed); **parent/overwrite** `register_block(G, G.view, Some(lock), ·)` resets `G.own_qc := None` and rebinds `G.parent := lock` (so `lock = G.parent` exactly, else the parent changes — prefix-collision/reattachment territory, kept separate). This producer was wrongly excluded and **keeps the route open**. Note it is itself a β self-vote **at `G.view`**, so completing `G` this way is the **general β-self-vote R question one level down**, not a new mechanism.

**(E4) I₁ grounding — the `B` above `P = B6` is UNESTABLISHED.** §26.2ae posited "a block `B` above `B6`" whose first `qc_B` fails `(g3)`, but never constructed `B`'s admission. Firsthand, in §26.2u's end-state (`committed = (B2, 6)`, `current_view = 8`, `B6{v7,h10,qc_B6}`), `B6` is the **top** of the Step-2 chain (nothing is built on it; `X@7` is a separate leaf with parent `B2`). A **catch-up** `B` with parent `B6` cannot be admitted: a response anchored at `(B2, 6)` has `expected_parent = B2` and a forced contiguous chain `B2 → D(leader(7),7,B2) → …`; `B6 = D(3,7,B5)` (parent `B5`) is **off** that chain, so no admitted block can have `expected_parent = B6`. A **leader-produced** `B = D(leader(8),8,B6)` at `current_view = 8` needs `local = leader(8) = 0`, conflicting with the view-6 starvation's `local = 2`; and such a `B` would be a fresh `{0}` key, **not** already-quorate (no β). **So the §26.2u-based I₁ step is unestablished** — the derived-`G` setup there never reaches a first `qc_B` above `B6`.

**Reassessment of the `B5` instance.** With (E1)–(E4): A41.2.2's general rejection is **withdrawn**. The `B5` instance is still dispatched, but non-generalizably: **(i)** its **I₁ is unestablished** (E4 — no `B` above `B6`); and **(ii)** even granting a chain, `B5` is **uncompletable** — catch-up re-admission is cursor-blocked (E2: `committed_height = 6 ≥ B5.view = 6`, no valid `k`), and the leader-self-vote producer (E3) fails because `current_view = 8 > 6` is forward-only (cannot return to view 6) **and**, even if it could, `local = 2` already first-voted `A6` at view 6 ⇒ `Equivocation`, suppressed. Both `B5` blocks are specific to this construction (its starvation used `local`'s own view-6 self-vote, locking `local`; and `committed` advanced to 6); neither generalizes.

**Reassessment of the general derived-`G` route — OPEN.** No general rejection survives:
- Starvation to `q−1` effective with `E_other ≤ N − q` (so `G` completable) is **not excluded** (E1); the overlap case shows a `≥q`-supplied sibling need not raise `E_other`.

- The composition that would yield R — a derived `G` starved-yet-completable, with `B → P → G` built above it (`B` already-quorate, `P` with `own_qc`, `P.parent = G`), the β self-vote at `B.view` **locally led**, `committed` positioned so the ordered commit guards pass at I₂, and the completion producer not disturbing the needed `B/P/G`/lock state — is **untraced and not excluded**. ### 26.2ag A41.2.4 — the clean-height derived-`G` route: three §26.2af statements corrected; one finite clean-height candidate tested through the production callers; the leader-self-vote-driven (R) commit REJECTED at β leader-eligibility, the only reachable commit being the established catch-up-driven (non-R) one (read-only at `ef99e29`)

**Part 1 — three §26.2af statements corrected.**
1. **Cursor permits, does not establish, admission.** §26.2af said catch-up re-admission "is admissible whenever `committed_height < G.view`." Corrected: `committed_height < G.view` only furnishes a **cursor position** `k = G.view − committed_height`; **admission** still requires the full guard chain for `G` **and every preceding block** of the response — the handler anchor gate (`committed == request_from`, binary:7893), then per block the applier's contiguity (`height == expected_height`), anchor/parent (`parent_block_id == expected_parent`), `h == v`, proposer (`== leader_for_view`), derived id (`== D(proposer,view,parent)`), and `qc.validate` (basic:2141–2184). A cursor slot is necessary, not sufficient.
2. **γ for `G` vs β for `B`, labeled separately.** §26.2af said completing `G` by a leader self-vote "folds into the general β R question." Corrected: if `G` holds `q−1` effective votes and a **leader supplies the `q`-th** (a completing-quorum leader self-vote), that event is **γ for `G`** (the §26.2x sense). A later leader self-vote on an **already-quorate** `(cv,B)` key is **β for `B`** (§26.2y.3). They are distinct events at distinct views and are labeled so here.
3. **(g5)/(g6) can pass on CLEAN heights — height-decoupling entanglement withdrawn.** §26.2af/§26.2ae tied the `(g5)`/`(g6)` pass to stored-height≠view inflation. Corrected and **withdrawn**: with the committed anchor `C` at **view = height = 1** and `G` at **view = height = 2** (clean), `(g5)` `G.height 2 > committed_height 1` ✓ and `(g6)` `committed_id = C ≠ G`, `g_view 2 > committed_node(C).view 1` ✓ **both pass on clean heights**, no inflation needed. The remaining obstruction is therefore **not** the commit predicates but whether the late `G`-QC and the subsequent `B` re-evaluation can coexist.

**Part 2 — the finite clean-height candidate (production-caller state).**

Restore `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline(C, 1, 1)` ⇒ anchor `C` resident `view = height = 1`, `own_qc = None`; `committed = (C,1)`; `current_view` left at the restore value `v₀ = 2`.

**Step 1 — local leader self-vote at view 2 (the only sub-`q` pre-lock).** At `current_view = 2`, `leader(2) = 2 = local`, `!proposed_in_view`: `on_leader_step` proposes `Z = make_block_id(lock₀) = D(2, 2, lock₀)` with `lock₀ ≠ C` (restore lock), so `Z ≠ G = D(2,2,C)`; self-vote `on_vote(2, 2, Z)` ⇒ `record_vote_history(2,2,Z)` = `FirstVote`, writes **`(2,2) → Z`**; accumulator `(2,Z) = {2}` < 3 ⇒ no QC, no view advance. This is the **only** producer of a non-`G` vote at view 2: a second distinct id at view 2 is impossible off the fixed anchor (`D(leader(2),2,C) = G` is unique; a second would need `committed` to differ — ¬U — but `committed = (C,1)` is fixed here), and inbound votes are `Required`-rejected (binary:~6547–6553). **So starving `G` at view 2 forces `local = leader(2) = 2`.**

**Step 4 — re-evaluating the `B → P → G` chain to a commit.** `try_commit(qc_B)` re-runs only on a fresh `on_qc(qc_B)`, i.e., a new vote forming `qc_B`. Two producers:
- **(i) leader β self-vote on `B` (the R trigger).** A TC installs `lock = P` and `current_view = 4` (`high_qc = {P, view 100}`, `tc.view = 4`, `timeout_view = 3`, `verification_ctx = None`; `on_timeout_certificate`: `4 > current_view 2` ✓, `100 > lock.view 4` ⇒ `set_locked_qc(P)`; `current_view ← 4`). Equivalently — the dichotomy — had we set `local = leader(4) = 0` to pass this guard, then `local ≠ leader(2) = 2`, so the Step-1 self-vote could not occur, `G` would be the first id at view 2 and receive a full quorum, `qc_G` would form **during catch-up**, and the `(g3)` starved-`G` premise would **not** hold. It is **not R** (R is the **leader-self-vote-driven** new commit), and it is **not a new finding** — it is exactly the already-recorded catch-up-driven commit (and the starvation/re-admission detour is gratuitous: admitting `[G,P,B]` once with `G` given a full non-equivocating quorum commits `G` at `qc_B` directly, which is ordinary §26.2p catch-up behaviour).

So with the correct restore lock, the leader self-vote completes `G`'s quorum (via `DuplicateSameBlock` + the catch-up pair), and the chain is committed **by ordinary catch-up** at `qc_B` — the established §26.2p / A17-F1 catch-up-driven commit. So catch-up produces only `G`-votes at view 2.
- **Inbound votes.** `Required`-rejected fail-closed before `on_vote_event` (binary:~6547–6553).

So a non-`G` view-2 vote exists only if `locked_qc` already names some `X ≠ C` at the leader step. **Obtaining such a lock, while preserving `current_view = 2` / `committed = (C,1)` / the clean chain, is impossible:**

Every route is circular (needs a starved `G` to produce the lock that would starve `G`), names `G` itself (so no non-`G` view-2 vote), or advances the view past 2. **The `lock₀ ≠ C` premise is unreachable for this candidate.** ⟨**A41.2.6 CORRECTION (§26.2ai)**: this categorical conclusion is **WRONG and withdrawn**. ### 26.2aj A41.2.7 — correcting the lock-owner and catch-up-outcome claims: a non-`C` lock can name `P` (not "only `qc_G`"); and a clean-height prefix long enough to evict view 2 provably advances `committed_height` past 1 (first commit at view 4), while a trailing invalid block does NOT advance `current_view` (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. Two corrections to §26.2ai. (Part A) §26.2ai's scope "a non-`C` lock is installable **only** as `qc_G`" is too narrow: a catch-up prefix `[G@2, P@3, invalid]` installs `locked_qc = qc_P` (naming `P`), and the leader then derives `D(2,2,P) ≠ G`. (Part B) §26.2ai's Part-B obstruction conflated two effects of a long partial-error prefix: a trailing invalid block skips the post-loop `set_view` **regardless of prefix length** (so `current_view` is **not** advanced — correcting §26.2ai's "advances `current_view` past 2"), while the admitted blocks' `on_vote→on_qc→try_commit` calls **do** commit; and on clean heights a prefix long enough to evict the view-2 accumulator key provably advances `committed_height` past 1 (first unavoidable commit at view 4). **Result: "only as `qc_G`" is WITHDRAWN (the lock-owner can be any quorate admitted block); the clean-height eviction obstruction is re-grounded on the COMMIT (not a view advance), with the first unavoidable commit named; and "height-decoupling is the only low-commit eviction route" is NOT asserted (not exhaustively argued) — the open premise is stated instead.** Both traces leave `G` (and `P`) quorate; neither is starvation or R. R stays **SR-PARTIAL / open**; no count change (18/4/27/11). Audit-only; the new external register is the sole write. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — the lock-owner is not "only `qc_G`" (tested; ACCEPTED).** From the v1.44 fresh restore (`committed=(C,1)`, `current_view=2`, `locked_qc=None`, `local=2`), choose the opaque anchor prefix with `C[0:16] ≠ LE64(3)‖LE64(3)` so that `D(2,2,P) ≠ D(2,2,C) = G` (since `P = D(3,3,G)` has `P[0:16] = LE64(3)‖LE64(3)`, and `D(2,2,P) = LE64(2)‖LE64(2)‖P[0:16]` vs `G = LE64(2)‖LE64(2)‖C[0:16]`). Catch-up `[G@2 {0,1,3}, P@3 {0,1,3}, invalid third block]`:
- **`G = D(2,2,C)@2`** — anchor gate `committed=(C,1)` ✓; parent `C` ✓; proposer `leader(2)=2` ✓; id `D(2,2,C)` ✓; `h==v` ✓; `qc.validate({0,1,3})` ✓ ⇒ `register_block`; `on_vote(0/1/3,2,G)` FirstVote ⇒ `(2,G)={0,1,3}` ⇒ **`qc_G`** ⇒ `on_qc`: `locked_qc = None → qc_G` (view 2); `G.own_qc = qc_G`; `try_commit(qc_G)`: `G→C→None`, `C.own_qc=None` ⇒ **(g2)** return, no commit. **State:** `committed=(C,1)`, `lock=qc_G`, `current_view=2`.
- **`P = D(3,3,G)@3`** — contiguity `height 3 == expected 3` ✓; parent `== G` (expected_parent after `G`) ✓; proposer `leader(3)=3` ✓; id `D(3,3,G)` ✓; `h==v` ✓; `qc.validate({0,1,3})` ✓ ⇒ `register_block`; `on_vote(0/1/3,3,P)` FirstVote ⇒ `(3,P)={0,1,3}` ⇒ **`qc_P`** ⇒ `on_qc`: `qc_P.view 3 > lock.view 2` ⇒ `locked_qc = qc_P` (**names `P`**); `P.own_qc = qc_P`; `try_commit(qc_P)`: `P → G → C`; `G.own_qc` is **attached** ⇒ (g2) passes; grandparent `C.own_qc = None` ⇒ **(g3)** return, **no commit**. **State:** `committed=(C,1)`, `lock=qc_P` (view 3, names `P`), `current_view=2`.
- **Invalid third block** fails a pre-registration guard ⇒ `Err` **before** `register_block` and the post-loop `set_view` (basic:2141–2208) ⇒ `current_view` stays `2`, `proposed_in_view=false`.
- **First leader step at view 2** (`leader(2)=2=local`, `!proposed_in_view`): `parent_id = locked_qc.block_id = P` (basic:2246–2248); `Z' = make_block_id(P) = D(2,2,P) ≠ G` (by the prefix choice). `register_block(Z',2,Some(P),qc_P)`; self-vote `on_vote(2,2,Z')` ⇒ `record_vote_history(2,2,Z') = FirstVote`, writes `(2,2) → Z'`; `(2,Z')={2}` < 3 ⇒ no QC. **No rejecting guard.**

**⇒ "a non-`C` lock is installable only as `qc_G`" is WITHDRAWN.** The lock-owner is the **highest-view quorate block in the admitted prefix** ⟨**A41.2.8 SCOPE (§26.2ak)**: this holds because the trace starts from `locked_qc=None` and views strictly increase; in general `on_qc` replaces the lock only when the new QC's view strictly exceeds the current (state:997–1004), so from a higher non-`None` lock a lower-view catch-up QC would not take it⟩ — here `P` (and it could be `B` at view 4, etc.). Every such owner is **quorate** (has a QC); the lock-install still leaves `G` (and `P`) **quorate, not starved**. The non-`G` leader vote `(2,2) → Z'` does nothing to the already-formed `qc_G`/`qc_P`. **Not starvation, not R** (per the brief).

**Part B — the two effects of a long catch-up prefix, separated.**
- **(1) A trailing invalid block does NOT advance `current_view` — regardless of prefix length.** The per-block guards run before `register_block`/`on_vote`, and the post-loop `set_view` runs only after the loop, guarded by `if self.current_view < expected_height` (basic:2206–2208). A block failing a guard propagates `Err` via `?` and returns **before** `set_view` — even after many admitted blocks. Nothing inside the loop (`on_vote`/`on_qc`/`try_commit`) advances `current_view`. **So §26.2ai's "admitting ~128 views advances `current_view` past 2" is WRONG and withdrawn: `current_view` stays `2`.** (A view advance must **not** be inferred from the length of a partially-rejected response.)
- **(2) But the admitted blocks DO commit — a clean-height prefix long enough to evict view 2 provably advances `committed_height` past 1.** The accumulator key `(2,G)` is evicted only when the vote-accumulator reaches its tracked-views cap (`evict_oldest_views` at `tracked_views.len() >= max_tracked_views`, default 128; vote_accumulator:264–275/314–320) — i.e. ≥ ~128 distinct **accumulator** views must carry votes. In catch-up each admitted block is supplied `≥ q` signers (`qc.validate`), and in a **contiguous clean-height** prefix each view appears once, so every block's supplied signers are `FirstVote` ⇒ every block **forms a QC**. ⟨**A41.2.8 SCOPE (§26.2ak)**: "each view appears once in this response" alone does **not** prove `FirstVote` — vote history persists across responses and leader self-votes, and `qc.validate` checks the supplied list, not effective votes. The `FirstVote` step (hence the view-4 commit) holds only under the premises: (1) no prior conflicting `(w,s)→Z` history at `w∈{2,3,4}`, (2) clean accumulator keys, (3) no interleaving writer at those views. The concrete commit stands scoped to (1)–(3), not as a universal claim.⟩ Trace the ordered `on_vote→on_qc→try_commit` for the contiguous prefix `[B_2@2, B_3@3, B_4@4, …]` off `(C,1)`:
  - `qc_{B_2}@2`: `try_commit`: `B_2 → C → None` ⇒ (g2), no commit.
  - `qc_{B_3}@3`: `try_commit`: `B_3 → B_2 → C`, grandparent `C.own_qc=None` ⇒ (g3), no commit.
  - `qc_{B_4}@4`: `try_commit`: `B_4 → B_3 → B_2`, all `own_qc`; strict views `2<3<4` ✓; `should_commit` (`committed_id=C≠B_2`, `g_view 2 > C.view 1`) ✓; `height_ok` (`B_2.height 2 > committed_height 1`) ✓ ⇒ **COMMIT `B_2`** ⇒ `committed = (B_2, 2)`, `committed_height = 2`.
  **First unavoidable commit: `qc_{B_4}` (the third admitted block, view 4) commits `B_2@2`, raising `committed_height` 1 → 2.** Commits then cascade (`qc_{B_5}` commits `B_3`, …), so by the time ~128 views are tracked `committed_height ≈ 126`. Since evicting the view-2 accumulator key requires ~128 tracked views, and the first commit fires at the **third** admitted block, **a clean-height prefix long enough to evict view 2 cannot leave `committed_height = 1`** — the obstruction to §26.2ai Part B is this **commit cascade**, not a (non-existent) view advance.
- **No "only height-decoupling" assertion.** Whether some route — height-decoupling (§26.2w, which holds `committed` low via a height-0 overwritten anchor) **or any other mechanism** — can evict the view-2 accumulator key while keeping `committed_height = 1` is **not** settled here, and is **not** claimed to be height-decoupling-exclusive (no exhaustive enumeration of low-commit eviction routes is given). **Exact unresolved source premise:** *does any production-reachable sequence evict the view-2 accumulator key `(2,G)` while `committed_height` stays `1`?* The clean-height contiguous catch-up route provably cannot (first commit at view 4); other routes are open.

**Reassessment of §26.2ai / §26.2ah.** §26.2ai's **starved-`G`-unestablished** result **stands**, and its two supporting statements are corrected: (i) the lock-owner is any quorate admitted block, not "only `qc_G`"; (ii) the clean-height eviction obstruction is the **commit cascade** (first commit at view 4), not a view advance, and height-decoupling is **not** asserted to be the unique low-commit eviction route. §26.2ah's starved-`G` withdrawal likewise stands, via this corrected reasoning. The starved-`G` state (hence any derived-`G` `(g3)` R on this clean-height candidate) remains **not established reachable**; the sharpened open premise is the view-2-eviction-with-`committed_height=1` question above.

**Accepted / rejected steps.** Part A (lock = `qc_P`, leader votes `D(2,2,P) ≠ G`): **ACCEPTED** (no rejecting guard; "only `qc_G`" withdrawn). Part B(1) (`current_view` not advanced by a trailing invalid block): **ACCEPTED** (source-established). ### 26.2al A41.2.9 — correcting the vote-history and clean-height-parent implications of §26.2ak: FirstVote vs DuplicateSameBlock distinguished; "clean height ⇒ quorate parent" REFUTED (a TC can lock a resident non-quorate parent); "FirstVote ⇒ QC" removed for q>1; the all-clean-height `(2,G)`-eviction-with-`committed_height=1` question stays OPEN (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. Three corrections to §26.2ak. (Part A) its view-4-commit premise conflated **FirstVote** (absent `(view,signer)` entry — newly inserts into the accumulator) with **DuplicateSameBlock** (an existing entry for the **same** block — proceeds but the accumulator dedups, adding no weight) ⟨**A41.2.10 CORRECTION (§26.2am)**: this ties weight to the **history** label, which is wrong — the history map and the accumulator are **independent** structures with independent eviction. A vote adds a distinct accumulator voter iff (not Equivocation) ∧ (voter **absent** in the accumulator entry `(view,block)`), regardless of the FirstVote/Dup label: a FirstVote whose accumulator voter is already present (history was evicted) **dedups** (no weight); a DuplicateSameBlock whose accumulator entry was evicted **inserts** (adds weight). Weight is an accumulator-presence property, not a history-class property. See §26.2am Part A.⟩; re-stated via the actual `record_vote_history → votes.on_vote → maybe_qc_for` order, the commit needs the accumulator key to reach `q` **distinct** voters, not a "first vote" per supplied signer. (Part B) its claim that a clean-height leader block forces a **quorate** locked parent is **REFUTED**: `register_block` needs the parent **resident** at height `view−1`, not quorate, and a TC installs a lock naming a resident block **without** attaching `own_qc` — a one-step candidate produces a clean-height block whose locked parent lacks `own_qc`, with no commit. (Part C) the implication "a prior FirstVote ⇒ QC" is **removed** for `q>1` (one vote is not a quorum); the two-route discussion is reassessed **non-exhaustively**; the general all-clean-height `(2,G)`-eviction-with-`committed_height=1` question stays **OPEN**. R stays **SR-PARTIAL / open**; no count change (18/4/27/11). Audit-only; the new external register is the sole write. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — FirstVote vs DuplicateSameBlock (the view-4 commit, re-stated).** `on_vote` runs `record_vote_history(voter,view,block)` first (state:897–928): an **absent** `(view,voter)` entry ⇒ **FirstVote** (the entry is written); an **existing** entry for the **same** `block` ⇒ **DuplicateSameBlock**; a different block ⇒ **Equivocation → Ok(None)** (not fed to the accumulator). For FirstVote **and** DuplicateSameBlock, control proceeds to `votes.on_vote` (state:974), which inserts the voter into the accumulator entry `(view,block)` and **dedups** (returns `false` if the voter is already present); `maybe_qc_for` then forms a QC iff that entry holds `≥ q` **distinct** voters (vote_accumulator:357–382). So "no prior **conflicting** entry" (which rules out Equivocation) permits **both** FirstVote and DuplicateSameBlock, and a DuplicateSameBlock is **not** a first vote and **adds no accumulator weight**. **Sufficient premises for the view-4 commit, re-stated:** for each `w ∈ {2,3,4}`, the accumulator key `(w, B_w)` reaches `≥ q` **distinct** voters during the replay — i.e. `(prior distinct voters already in (w,B_w)) ∪ (supplied signers that are FirstVote) ≥ q`, with **no** supplied signer equivocating (no prior `(w,s) → Z`, `Z ≠ B_w`). In the fresh-restore trace specifically, each key `(w,B_w)` starts **empty** and the `q` supplied signers are **all FirstVote**, so the key reaches exactly `q` distinct voters ⇒ `qc_{B_2}`,`qc_{B_3}`,`qc_{B_4}` form ⇒ `try_commit(qc_{B_4})` commits `B_2@2` (`committed_height` 1→2). The commit is stated on **`q` distinct effective voters**, not on "each supplied signer is a first vote."

**Part B — "clean height ⇒ quorate parent" REFUTED (one-step candidate).** §26.2ak (Part B / route (ii)) claimed a clean-height (`stored height = view`) leader self-vote forces a **quorate** locked parent (so the sub-quorum route is "height-decoupled"). Firsthand this is **wrong**: `register_block` computes `height = resident(parent).height + 1` (state:744; `None`/non-resident parent ⇒ 0) — it needs the parent **resident** at height `view−1`, and reads **nothing** about the parent's `own_qc`; and `set_locked_qc` just stores `locked_qc = Some(qc)` (state:1144–1146) — a TC's `set_locked_qc(high_qc)` (basic:3271–3281) attaches **no** `own_qc` to the named block (§26.2k). So a lock can name a **resident, non-quorate** block. **Bounded one-step candidate (tested through the guards):**
- **Pre-state.** `P` resident at `view = height = v−1`, `own_qc = None` (e.g. a prior leader self-proposed clean block, or a catch-up block whose quorum was not reached); `current_view < v`; `committed = (C,1)`.
- **Admitted TC** — `tc.high_qc = {block_id = P, view = h_P}` with `h_P >` the current lock's view, `tc.view = v`, logical quorum signers (A1-F1 `None`-context posture): `on_timeout_certificate` — `tc.validate(validators)` (signer membership/power/dedup/quorum) ✓; `tc.view v > current_view` ✓ ⇒ proceed; `should_update` (`h_P > lock.view`) ✓ ⇒ `set_locked_qc(high_qc)` ⇒ **`locked_qc` names `P` (resident, `own_qc = None`)**; `current_view ← v`; flags reset. **No `own_qc` attached to `P`; no commit.**
- **Eligible leader step at view `v`** (`leader(v) = local`, `!proposed_in_view`): `parent_id = locked_qc.block_id = P`; `Z = make_block_id(P) = D(local, v, P)`; `register_block(Z, v, Some(P), high_qc)` ⇒ `Z.height = resident(P).height + 1 = (v−1) + 1 = v` ⇒ **`Z@(view v, height v)` CLEAN**, `own_qc = None`, parent `P` (resident, `own_qc = None`). Self-vote `on_vote(local, v, Z)` ⇒ FirstVote ⇒ `(v,Z) = {local}` = 1 `< q` ⇒ no QC, no `on_qc`, no `try_commit`, **no commit**.
- **First rejecting guard: NONE** — the one step passes. **⇒ "clean height ⇒ quorate locked parent" is FALSE.** A clean-height leader block can have a **resident, non-quorate** parent, locked via a TC.

**This does NOT build a 128-view eviction (not inferred).** Per the brief, the one successful step is **not** extended to a full sequence. The obstruction to extension (noted, not claimed closed): the next clean block `Z'@(v+1)` needs a **resident** parent at height `v`; local can self-vote only at views `≡ local (mod n)` (leaders is a distinct-id permutation, §26.2aj), and the intermediate (non-local-led) view-`v` blocks are not resident in local's state (remote proposals are `Required`-rejected; catch-up admission of them re-enters the commit-cascade analysis). Whether some interleaving supplies the needed resident parents across non-local-led views **without** committing is **unresolved** — it is **not** inferred from this one step, and **not** excluded.

**Part C — "FirstVote ⇒ QC" removed; routes reassessed non-exhaustively; exclusion OPEN.** §26.2ak's wording that "every first-at-view block is FirstVote ⇒ quorum ⇒ qc" conflated a **single** FirstVote with a **quorum** of them: for `q > 1`, one FirstVote is weight 1, **not** a QC; a QC needs `q` **distinct** effective voters. Corrected: a catch-up block forms a QC because it is supplied `≥ q` signers that are **all** FirstVote (q distinct), **not** because "a FirstVote ⇒ QC." With Part B, the two-route discussion is reassessed, and **neither route is claimed exhaustive**:

- **No exhaustiveness.** Routes (i)/(ii) are **not** asserted to be the only ways to track `≥ 128` accumulator views on clean heights.

Part B one-step clean block with resident-non-quorate parent: **ACCEPTED** (no rejecting guard; "clean ⇒ quorate parent" refuted). Part B 128-view extension: **NOT inferred / NOT established**. ### 26.2am A41.2.10 — reconciling vote history with accumulator state (two independent structures); grounding the TC-parent candidate's resident non-quorate `P` as the restored anchor; the 128-view eviction and R stay OPEN (read-only at `ef99e29`)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. Three items. (Part A) §26.2al's categorical "FirstVote adds accumulator weight; DuplicateSameBlock adds none" is **corrected**: `record_vote_history` (the history map `votes_by_view`) and `votes.on_vote` (the accumulator `entries`) are **two independent structures with independent eviction**, so whether a vote adds accumulator weight is governed by the **accumulator** voter-presence, not by the history label — the four history×accumulator combinations (incl. both evictions) are traced. (Part B) §26.2al's assumed resident `P@(view=height=v−1, own_qc=None)` is **grounded as the restored anchor** (a production restore produces exactly such a node); the one-step clean-height leader block off it is therefore production-reachable — but a **non-anchor** such `P` (needed to chain) has **no established producer** (remote proposals `Required`-rejected; a prior clean sub-quorum leader step recurses and breaks at non-local-led views; a starved catch-up block is the unestablished premise). (Part C) one clean-height sub-quorum leader step does **not** establish a 128-view `(2,G)` eviction; that eviction and R stay **OPEN**. R stays **SR-PARTIAL / open**; no count change (18/4/27/11). Audit-only; the new external register is the sole write. **Public-DevNet scope, RUN-422 separation, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1 unchanged, execution deferred.**

**Part A — history and accumulator are independent; weight is an accumulator property.** `on_vote(voter,view,block)` (state:952–987): step 1 `record_vote_history` classifies against the **history map** `votes_by_view[(view,voter)]` (state:897–928; its own eviction `evict_votes_by_view_if_needed` at `votes_by_view.len() >= max_votes_by_view_entries`, state:683–697, evicting the lowest tracked view's entries); step 2 (only if not Equivocation) `votes.on_vote` inserts into the **accumulator entry** `entries[(view,block)]` (vote_accumulator:301–343; its own eviction `evict_oldest_views` at `tracked_views.len() >= max_tracked_views = 128`). These are **separate maps with separate caps**, so the history class (FirstVote/DuplicateSameBlock) does **not** determine whether weight is added — the accumulator voter-presence does. All relevant combinations:

| history `(view,voter)` | accumulator voter in `(view,block)` | `record_vote_history` | `votes.on_vote` | net accumulator effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| absent | absent | **FirstVote** | insert (new) | **+1 distinct voter** |
| absent (history **evicted**) | present | **FirstVote** | dedup (already present) | **no weight** (desync: history evicted but accumulator kept) |
| present, same block | absent (accumulator **evicted**) | **DuplicateSameBlock** | insert (new) | **+1 distinct voter** (desync: accumulator evicted but history kept) |
| present, same block | present | **DuplicateSameBlock** | dedup | **no weight** |
| present, **different** block | (any) | **Equivocation → `Ok(None)`** | **not reached** (returns before `votes.on_vote`, state:960–966) | **no weight, no dedup** |

**Precise rule.** A vote **adds a distinct accumulator voter** iff it is **not** Equivocation (history absent, or present-same) **and** the voter is **absent** from the accumulator entry `(view,block)`. It **deduplicates** (no weight) iff not Equivocation and the voter is **present**. **Equivocation** (history present, different block) returns `Ok(None)` **before** the accumulator. So §26.2al's "FirstVote ⇒ +weight, Dup ⇒ none" is **false in general**: a FirstVote whose accumulator voter is already present (history evicted) **dedups**; a DuplicateSameBlock whose accumulator entry was evicted **adds weight**.

**Scoped view-4 commit, reassessed on distinct accumulator voters.** The commit needs each key `(w,B_w)` (`w∈{2,3,4}`) to hold **≥ q distinct voters in the accumulator** at `maybe_qc_for` time. In the fresh-restore trace **both** structures start empty, so every supplied signer is the (absent,absent) combination ⇒ each **inserts** ⇒ `q` distinct ⇒ `qc_{B_2}`,`qc_{B_3}`,`qc_{B_4}` ⇒ `try_commit(qc_{B_4})` commits `B_2@2`. The commit holds **under** the premises: no prior history or accumulator content at those `(w,·)`/`(w,B_w)` (so no desync, no equivocation), and `q` distinct supplied signers. Stated on the **accumulator distinct-voter count**, not on history labels.

**Part B — grounding the resident non-quorate `P`.** §26.2al's one-step candidate assumed a resident `P` with `P.height = P.view = v−1` and `P.own_qc = None`. Through the production callers:
- **`P` = the restored anchor (ESTABLISHED producer).** `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline(P, committed_view = v−1, committed_height = v−1)` (state:1254–1283) inserts `P` resident at `view = height = v−1`, `parent_id = None`, **`own_qc = None`**, and sets `committed = (P, v−1)`. So the assumed node is **exactly** a restored anchor. With `locked_qc = None` after restore, the first eligible leader step at `current_view = v` (`leader(v) = local`, `!proposed_in_view`) parents to `committed_block = P` (basic:2246–2248), derives `Z = D(local,v,P)`, and `register_block` gives `Z.height = resident(P).height + 1 = v` ⇒ **`Z@(view v, height v)` clean, parent `P` non-quorate**, self-vote sub-quorum ⇒ no QC, **no commit**. (A TC locking `P` is **not** required; `lock = None` already parents to the committed anchor. If used, a TC with `high_qc` naming `P` would lock it without attaching `own_qc`, same outcome.) **So the one-step clean-height-non-quorate-parent fact is PRODUCTION-REACHABLE** — `P` is simply the committed anchor (which is **always** `own_qc = None`). "clean height ⇒ quorate parent" is false, confirmed with a real producer.
- **A NON-anchor resident non-quorate `P` (for chaining) has NO established producer.** To extend past one step (a second clean block `Z'@(v+1)` parented to a resident node at height `v`), the parent must be a **non-anchor** resident block at `view = height = v`, `own_qc = None`. Producers: (i) a prior **leader self-vote** producing a clean `Z@v` — but that needs `local = leader(v)`, while the next step needs `local = leader(v+1) ≠ leader(v)` for `n ≥ 3` (distinct-id permutation, §26.2aj); a different (remote) leader's block is **inbound, `Required`-rejected**, not resident locally; (ii) a **catch-up** block at view `v` with `own_qc = None` — i.e. a **starved** catch-up block, which is the **unestablished** premise this whole thread is probing (and a non-starved catch-up block would carry `own_qc`, breaking the "non-quorate" requirement, and sit on a chain that commits). **No producer for a non-anchor resident non-quorate `P` is established.** Per the brief, beyond the anchor the result is retained **only as a conditional engine-state implication** ("*if* such a `P` were resident, a clean `Z@(v)` off it would register with no commit"), **not** a production-reachable witness.

**Part C — disposition (one step ≠ eviction; both questions OPEN).** The production-grounded result is a **single** clean-height sub-quorum leader step off the restored anchor. It does **not** establish a 128-view `(2,G)` eviction: the chain cannot be extended past the anchor without a non-anchor resident non-quorate parent, whose producer is unestablished (Part B). So:
- The **all-clean-height `(2,G)`-eviction-with-`committed_height=1`** question stays **OPEN** — neither a non-circular invariant (A41.2.9 removed the height-decoupling argument) nor a finite clean-height counterexample (the one grounded step does not extend) is established. It is **source** work over the restore / leader / catch-up / TC-lock / accumulator-eviction / commit writers — **not EXEC**.
- **R** (leader-self-vote-driven new commit) stays **OPEN**; no candidate reaches one. The grounded commits (view-4 catch-up; §26.2ah/§26.2aj control) are **catch-up-driven (A17-F1), non-R**.
- §26.2ai/§26.2ah's **starved-`G`-unestablished** results **stand** on the open `(2,G)`-eviction premise.

**Accepted / rejected steps.** Part A rule and four-combination table: **ACCEPTED** (source-established). View-4 commit on `q` distinct accumulator voters: **ACCEPTED** (under its premises). Part B `P` = restored anchor + one-step clean `Z@v`: **ACCEPTED, production-reachable** (no rejecting guard). Part B non-anchor `P` for chaining: **NO producer established** (conditional only). Part C 128-view eviction / R: **OPEN**.

**Source-established (this pass).** History map and accumulator are independent structures with independent eviction; a vote adds a distinct accumulator voter iff (not Equivocation) ∧ (accumulator voter absent), with the two eviction-desync cases; the view-4 commit on `q` distinct accumulator voters; the resident non-quorate `P` is production-reachable **as the restored anchor** (so the one clean step is grounded), but a non-anchor such `P` has no established producer.

**Remaining source work (R).** The all-clean-height `(2,G)`-eviction-with-`committed_height=1` composition (open; needs a non-anchor resident non-quorate parent chain or some other 128-view no-commit tracking); whether any interleaving supplies such parents across non-local-led views without committing; plus the still-open deeper-`G`/non-consecutive, height-decoupling, prefix-collision reattachment, and committed-absent routes.

**Deployment prerequisites (source/deployment).** Restore-from-snapshot (anchor at the chosen `view=height`); admitted/compromised responder (A17-F1); catch-up mode active; `None`-context TCs (A1-F1/A1-F2); local leadership at the relevant views; default limits; DevNet. **DEP reserved for external implementation properties** (none invoked).

**Deferred runtime (EXEC).** No execution/harness; occurrence/timing unobserved.

**Separate claims (kept distinct — stored height, own_qc, lock, effective votes, commit, safety).** **Stored height** = `resident(parent).height+1` (register-time; needs a resident parent). **`own_qc`** = attached by `on_qc` on `q` distinct accumulator voters; **never** by `set_locked_qc`, and `None` on a restored anchor / fresh register. **Lock** = a QC installed as `locked_qc` on a strictly higher view (via `on_qc` or a TC); a locked block need not be quorate or (for the lock itself) resident, though the leader-step parent-height needs residency. **Effective votes** = distinct accumulator voters after Equivocation suppression and subject to accumulator eviction (≠ supplied, ≠ history class). **Commit** = `try_commit` on a 3-chain of `own_qc`-bearers with strict views and the grandparent above the committed floor. **Honest-node safety** = not analyzed; no safety-exclusion proof claimed. These are not inter-derived here.

**Disposition (§1).** Vote history and accumulator state are reconciled as **two independent structures** (correcting §26.2al's categorical weight claim: weight is an accumulator-presence property, with history/accumulator eviction producing FirstVote-dedup and Dup-adds-weight desyncs); the scoped view-4 commit is re-stated on `q` **distinct accumulator voters**; the TC-parent candidate's resident non-quorate `P` is **grounded as the restored anchor** (one clean-height step production-reachable), while a **non-anchor** such `P` (needed to chain) has **no established producer** and is retained only as a conditional engine-state implication. One clean step does **not** establish a 128-view eviction; the all-clean-height `(2,G)`-eviction and R stay **OPEN**. No new QC for a starved `G`, no leader-self-vote-driven commit, no safety consequence. No finding, no commit/safety result ⇒ **no count change** (18/4/27/11). **OBL-CONS-3 stays SR-PARTIAL.** **γ source-reachable; admission-sense ¬U refuted; R open.** §26.2aa–§26.2al (with the inline §26.2al corrections), §26.2x–§26.2z, §26.2u, §26.2t, §26.2w, A40, A37, §26.2v Part B, C4/C5 OPEN, RS1, public-DevNet scope, and the RUN-422 boundary are preserved. ## 27. A22 — T-A18-4: validator membership, quorum arithmetic, and multi-node TC high-QC propagation (read-only source; v0.69)

A22 performs the **T-A18-4** substantive source review (OBL-CONS-6 / OBL-CONS-7 / OBL-CONS-8) after a bounded A21.3 carry-forward reconciliation (Part A, applied in place to §26.4b/§26.4c/§26.4d/§3B/§2 — summarized in §27.1). The review is a **scoped negative in the A12 sense**: it forces **no new finding** and **no count change** (13 static / 4 gaps / 22 evidence gaps), and it **extends the evidence** for **A1-F1** (missing-context Timeout/TC verification) and **A1-F3** (unendorsed high-QC becomes a lock) without re-counting them. All source was read firsthand at the pinned baseline `ef99e29` via read-only `git show`/`git grep` with a **nonempty search scope and positive controls**. OBL-CONS-3 is **not** reopened. Attribution: register/excerpt review plus firsthand pinned-source reads; not independent checkout/CI verification.

**Decisive production fact (positive-controlled; A22.1-corrected).** Every **reachable** production validator-set construction route uses **unit voting power (`voting_power = 1`)**: the engine membership `build_uniform_validator_set` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:711–719) reached by the wired loop `run_binary_consensus_loop_with_io` (binary:2491→2493 `BasicHotStuffEngine::new`), with `num_validators = static_peers.len()+1`; and the admissible P2P key-provider / timeout-verification-context set `build_validator_set_and_key_provider` (peer_key_provider.rs:432–442, `voting_power: 1`). The genesis authority `build_genesis_consensus_authority` (genesis_consensus_authority.rs:405–412, `voting_power: 1`) is **NOT a reachable production route** — it is built only inside `if args.consensus_authority_from_genesis` (main.rs:5812), a **statically-dead branch** gated by the startup refusal at main.rs:5405 (comment 5813: "unreachable in a normally built binary"); its unit-weight provenance is a **library** property established **without** implying activation. The production epoch transition **reuses the same set** — `let same_validator_set = engine.validators().clone(); engine.transition_to_epoch(new_epoch_id, same_validator_set)` (binary:8501–8502) — so, **within the inspected in-process transition**, production membership is unit-weight and invariant (reconfig advances only the epoch id; this is **not** extended across restarts/nodes/configs/authority objects). Consequently, in production **`W = total_voting_power = N = len`** (with `N < 2⁶³` a **retained representation/allocation premise**, §27.2); the weighted/degenerate edges below are **library-path**, recorded without transferring unit-weight safety to the arbitrary-weight code or vice versa.

### 27.1 Part A — A21.3 carry-forward corrections (applied in place)

Verified against source before adoption; each applied to the active text (not appended):
- **§26.4b allocation model.** `≤128` bounds `len(blocks)`, **not** `capacity(blocks)` (the "backing capacity ≤128 blocks worth" wording withdrawn). Backing storage counted **once per region**: outer `= capacity(blocks) × size_of::<RestoreCatchupBlock>()`; nested `= Σ_blocks capacity(qc_signer_indices) × size_of::<u16>()`. The owned **dynamic** fields are exactly `RestoreCatchupResponse.blocks: Vec<RestoreCatchupBlock>` (p2p.rs:213–219) and `RestoreCatchupBlock.qc_signer_indices: Vec<u16>` (p2p.rs:200–209) — **no other** owned dynamic field, so no further terms. The outer-element size already contains each block's inline `Vec<u16>` header (3×`usize`), so **headers are not added again**. Top-level `P2pMessage` storage is kept separate and counted **once** as `size_of::<P2pMessage>()` (the compiler-laid-out enum size, **not** hand-derived from headers + a discriminant). `H(m)` is defined per object and `H_max` over the **explicit message set** `M = {Timeout, NewView(TC), RestoreCatchup{Request,Response}}` (enqueue-eligible wired variants). The **necessity claim** "`cap == len` only if the source had no slack" is **withdrawn** — source and destination capacities require separate reasoning; the queued object is a **clone**, whose `cap` is governed by `Vec::clone`/`collect` library behavior (an **uninspected dependency premise**), not by the source layout. `P × 64 × S_max` retained **only** as serialized-equivalent queued volume.
- **§26.4d.** "unbounded function" corrected to "a function not bounded by any application-level resource check (bounded only by the field's finite `u32` representation, `tx_count ≤ u32::MAX`)".
- **§26.4c.** A21-F1's runtime consequence is **unmeasured/deployment-dependent (E13)** with the **decode production-wired** kept separate from the unobserved allocator/deployment outcome — **not** the register's LATENT applicability category.
- **§3B (A21-F1 row).** "before any of that" corrected: the reservation runs **after** the fixed-field reads (consensus.rs:728–755) and the optional nested-QC decode (:758–764), **before** the per-transaction loop (:767–771).
- **Exact thresholds.** `len_to_u16` panics at `len > u16::MAX` (65 535 B), not "> 64 KiB" (the outbound table corrected). Outbound: the unguarded demux `as u32` truncates at `len > u32::MAX`; **4 GiB = `u32::MAX + 1` strictly exceeds `u32::MAX`** (the "4 GiB boundary itself" wording corrected); the checked transport stage returns `Err` at `len > u32::MAX` (transport.rs:35); the emittable-but-receiver-rejected interval is **`(16 MiB, u32::MAX]`**, not `(16 MiB, 4 GiB]`; emission also requires `write_all`+`flush` progress (framed_io.rs:88).

**Degenerate / boundary cases (traced through the actual constructor + consumer checks):**
- **Empty set** → rejected at `::new` (:414–416) and at genesis (`EmptyValidatorSet`); fail-closed everywhere.
- **Zero individual weight** (`voting_power = 0`) → **NOT rejected** by `::new` (no `>0` check). `EpochState`'s doc claims it is enforced — **false** (mismatch recorded). Not production-reachable (all production weights are 1).
- **All-zero total** (`total_voting_power = 0`) → `two_thirds_vp = (2·0).div_ceil(3) = 0`. **A22.1 correction — "accepts any signer list" is wrong:** membership and duplicate checks **still apply**. Exact behavior, stated separately: **(logical `qc.validate`/`TimeoutCertificate::validate`)** every signer must be a member (`NonMemberSigner` on an unknown id) and distinct (`DuplicateSigner`), and only the *quorum threshold* is trivially met (`acc_vp = 0 ≥ 0`); so it accepts any list of **distinct members** (and an **empty** list, vacuously), but **rejects** any list containing a non-member or a duplicate. Note that at **unit weight with `W = N ≥ 1`** the threshold is `⌈2N/3⌉ ≥ 1`, so an **empty** or sub-threshold list is **rejected** (`InsufficientQuorum`); the empty-accepting behavior arises **only** in the all-zero-total degenerate case. **(signed-evidence `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`)** additionally **rejects** an empty evidence/signers set outright (`EvidenceMismatch`, timeout_verify.rs:366) before any threshold test. **Library-path degenerate only** (production total `= N ≥ 1`, unit weights); recorded, not a finding.
- **Duplicate ids in the set** → rejected at `::new` (:405–407). **In a signer list** → `qc.validate`/`tc.validate` reject (`DuplicateSigner`, via `HashSet`); the set-level `has_quorum` (:500) does **NOT** dedup its input iterator (double-counts repeated ids) — but `has_quorum` is reached only through `ValidatorContext` (sim/test), **not** the wired validation path.

**Four separated concerns (A22.1 — item 4):**
- **(a) Collection bounds safety (A22.2 — corrected; parser audit not reopened).** Separate **output length** from **backing capacity / pre-allocation**: on the receive side `resp.blocks.into_iter().map(..).collect()` (binary:7917–7932) produces a `Vec` whose **length** equals the decoded input block count, but its **backing capacity** and any pre-allocation are library behavior (not "exactly the input length"). The **upstream** step is the `bincode::deserialize` of the outer `P2pMessage` carrying `RestoreCatchupResponse.blocks: Vec<RestoreCatchupBlock>`; its untrusted-length pre-allocation/allocation-ordering is the **same unresolved bincode semantics preserved in E12**, and **A21-F1 stands** (this does not re-audit or resolve it). **The responder's `RESTORE_CATCHUP_MAX_BLOCKS_PER_RESPONSE = 128` is a RESPONDER-side construction cap only** (referenced solely at binary:7836); there is **no inbound acceptance guard** — `handle_restore_catchup_response` (binary:7865–7918) rejects only on anchor staleness/mismatch, and `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` (basic:2122) iterates `for block in blocks` (:2140) with **no `len ≤ 128` check** — so the inbound block count is **not** bounded by 128. The only applicable transport limit is the **≤16 MiB frame-byte bound** (`MAX_TRANSPORT_CIPHERTEXT`, a bound on **ciphertext/serialized bytes**, not a decoded-cardinality bound); translating that frame-byte bound into a decoded `blocks.len()` or an allocation bound needs its **own separate premises** about the bincode decoder's per-element consumption and pre-allocation — the **unresolved DEP/E12 bincode semantics**, which this note **preserves without reopening the parser audit** (A21-F1 stands). The earlier "blocks ≤ 128 on the catch-up apply" is **scoped to the responder**; inbound decoded cardinality is a DEP/E12 question, not a 128-bounded one.
- **(b) Validator-ID vs positional-index correspondence.** The wire `qc_signer_indices: Vec<u16>` and `proposer_index: u16` are converted to **ValidatorId VALUES** — `ValidatorId::new(v as u64)` (binary:7925/7929) — **not** used as positional indices into the set. Membership is then checked downstream (`qc.validate`/accumulator `contains` → `NonMemberSigner`/`UnknownValidator` on an unknown id). The set's positional `get(idx)` (bounds-checked `None` on OOB, :446–448) is **not** on this wire path; `index_of(id)` is a `HashMap` lookup. So "indices" is a misnomer here — they are id values, and an out-of-range/unknown id fails the membership check rather than indexing OOB. (QC decode in qbind-wire handles signer fields separately; not re-audited here.)
- **(c) Outbound ID-narrowing conversions (A22.2 opened; A22.3 — three fields traced separately, see the table below).** The **responder** applies `u64 → u16` narrowing at **three distinct sites with three distinct source values**, so they are **not** all "QC signer ids": `responder_validator_index` = the responder's own `local_validator_id` (binary:7842); `proposer_index` = `leader_for_view(node.view)`, a **computed leader** id (binary:7853; `leader_for_view` basic:1739/2098); and each `qc_signer_indices` entry = `own_qc.signers` (binary:7854; `export_restore_catchup_blocks` basic:2105). The low-16-bit truncation (`65 536 → 0`, …) loses identity only for ids `≥ 2¹⁶`; the four aspects — (i) ID preservation, (ii) membership of the converted id (a truncated id may be a **valid but different** member — the A22.2 "would surface as `NonMemberSigner`" is correct only when the truncated value is a non-member; **withdrawn** as a general claim), (iii) duplicate consequence (a mod-`2¹⁶` collision → `DuplicateSigner`; a lone truncation to a different member is **not** caught), (iv) production reachability — are resolved per field in the table below. **A22.4 — four separate *representabilities*, not one conclusion:** **(α) QC-signer representability** — bounded `< 2¹⁶` by the vote cap (`max_votes_per_view = 256`, default on the 2-arg `BasicHotStuffEngine::new` path, basic:1418/1424 → `ConsensusLimitsConfig::default()`): a QC forms only when `q = ⌈2N/3⌉ ≤ 256 ⟹ N ≤ 384`, so `own_qc.signers` ids are `< 2¹⁶` ⇒ **lossless** (the A22.2 "not source-excluded (uncapped `num_validators`)" is thereby **refined** — the cap, not `num_validators`, is decisive). **(β) computed-proposer representability** — `leader_for_view ∈ 0..N`; own_qc-bearing export ⇒ `N ≤ 384` ⇒ `< 2¹⁶` ⇒ **lossless**, and additionally **re-checked** at apply (`WrongProposer`/`BlockIdMismatch`, basic:2161–2179, §24.4 B4). **(γ) responder-local-ID representability** — **NOT source-bounded `< 2¹⁶`:** `local_validator_id` is the operator CLI `--validator-id` set with **no `< num_validators` / membership guard on *either* production route** (A23: LocalMesh `run_local_mesh_node` main.rs:5499; P2P `run_p2p_node` main.rs:6190–6191; the sole `LocalValidatorOutOfRange` check, genesis:396, is on the dead genesis route), so a `≥ 2¹⁶` id makes the cast **lossy** — the A22.3 "lossless on the production path" is **withdrawn for this field**. **(δ) receiver rejection after a narrowing** — a lossy narrowing is caught, per field, by: `ClaimedSenderMismatch` (responder id, the Run-418 dispatch binding, binary:7003–7013, §24.2 — **so `responder_validator_index` IS part of the origin binding**, correcting the A22.3 "not the origin binding, only a self-drop"); `WrongProposer`/`BlockIdMismatch` (proposer); `NonMemberSigner`/`DuplicateSigner` (qc-signers). **A23 — exact responder predicate:** `gate.authorize` applies the ordered checks `MissingOrigin → UnknownPeer → AmbiguousMapping → UnknownValidator(C) → ClaimedSenderMismatch(C vs A)` (peer_consensus_binding.rs:388–433); with the configured id `L ≥ 2¹⁶`, `C = L mod 2¹⁶ ≠ A (= L)` under a consistent map, so binding fails via `UnknownValidator` **or** `ClaimedSenderMismatch` (whichever fires first — not one promised error). An **accepted** lossy responder id requires the binding map to independently map the origin to `C` (i.e. `A = C ≠ L`), a **separate configuration prerequisite**, not an automatic consequence of truncation (§27.2 table). The per-field detail, source lines, and the "not a benign liveness no-op" note are in the table; the vote-cap **override** (`with_state_limits`, basic:1448) is **test-only** at the baseline (binary:21178–22247), a forward re-audit note, not an open edge.
- **(d) Engine vs verification-context membership agreement.** The engine set (contiguous `0..N`) and the ctx set (configured/effective vids) are built independently; the source enforces only a **partial** peer-coverage check (`PeerMissingKey`), not full equality — and the two **threshold** checks can use **different totals** — **traced in §27.5** (available-source), with deployment divergence an EXEC matter and a difference not automatically a defect.
- **Sparse / non-contiguous ids** → supported by the `HashMap<ValidatorId, usize>` (:384); `index_of` returns `None` for unknown ids. The wire path (b) uses **id values** (not the positional `get`), so sparse ids are consumed as ids and membership-checked; no contiguity assumption **inside the set**, though the engine's `build_uniform_validator_set` *does* construct contiguous `0..N` (relevant to (c)/(d)). The earlier "index-conversion safe (bounds-checked `get`)" basis is **withdrawn** — the wire path does not use positional `get` at all.

**Three ID-narrowing traces (A22.3 — one row per field, each with its own source/prereq/cast/receiver-check/consequence).**

| Wire field | Source value | Construction / admission prerequisites | Cast | Receiver checks | Supported consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `responder_validator_index` | the responder's own `local_validator_id` (**not** a QC signer) = operator CLI `--validator-id` (`args.validator_id.unwrap_or(0)`). **A23 — both production routes, no guard:** LocalMesh `run_local_mesh_node` main.rs:5499 and **P2P `run_p2p_node` main.rs:6190–6191** (`num_validators = static_peers.len()+1`, :6194) both set `local_validator_id` with **no `< num_validators` / membership guard** (`.with_local_validator` consensus_net_p2p.rs:250 is a plain setter; `BinaryConsensusLoopConfig::new` binary:562 only `.max(1)`); the sole `LocalValidatorOutOfRange` check (genesis:396) is on the **statically-dead** genesis route | response is built only if `!blocks.is_empty()` (binary:7838); a blocks-bearing export needs own_qc blocks (⇒ **signer/leader** ids `< 2¹⁶`), but `local_validator_id` is **independent** of that bound | `local_validator_id.0 as u16` (binary:7842) | **(1) origin binding (ordered predicate, A23)** — dispatch sets `claimed = C = ValidatorId::new(resp.responder_validator_index as u64)` (binary:7003) → `bind_sender(C) → gate.authorize(origin, C)` (binary:7004/5819). `authorize` (peer_consensus_binding.rs:388–433) checks, in order: absent origin→`MissingOrigin`; `map.validator_for_node(origin.node_id())` None→`UnknownPeer`; `mapped != origin.validator_id()`→`AmbiguousMapping`; **`map.node_for_validator(C).is_none()`→`UnknownValidator` (:424)**; **`C != origin.validator_id() (=A)`→`ClaimedSenderMismatch` (:431)**. **(2)** then the handler drops `responder_validator_index == local_validator_id` as a **self-response** (binary:7872) | **A23 — exact binding predicate (replaces the vague "collision"):** let `L` = the responder's configured id, `C = L mod 2¹⁶` the widened wire value, `A = origin.validator_id()` the authenticated origin's id. **Where `A = L` and `L ≥ 2¹⁶`:** `C = L mod 2¹⁶ ≠ L = A`, so binding **cannot pass** — it is rejected by `UnknownValidator` (if `C` is not a mapped validator) **or** `ClaimedSenderMismatch` (if `C` is some other mapped validator), whichever check fires first (do **not** promise one specific error); membership of `C` alone does not change the reject, only which error. The **`A = C ≠ L`** scenario (binding passes with the truncated id) is **not** an automatic consequence of truncation — it requires the binding map to independently map this authenticated origin to `C`, a **separate configuration prerequisite** (and then `A ≠ L`, itself a map/config disagreement). So a lossy responder id (`L ≥ 2¹⁶`) under a consistent map (`A = L`) is **receiver-rejected**, not silently misattributed. Whether `L ≥ 2¹⁶` is configured, and the binding-map population, are **config/EXEC**. Available-source result: **no `local_validator_id < N` guard** on either production route (owner: `--validator-id` → `run_local_mesh_node`/`run_p2p_node` → `BinaryConsensusLoopConfig::new`/`BasicHotStuffEngine::new`). A dropped catch-up response is **not** asserted a "benign liveness no-op" (no progress argument is made) |
| `proposer_index` | `leader_for_view(node.view) = leaders[view % N]`, a **computed leader** id from the sorted validator-id schedule (basic:1739/1419–1427) — **not** a QC signer | exported **only** for an **own_qc-bearing** node (export predicate `own_qc.is_some()`, basic:2089) ⇒ a QC exists ⇒ `N ≤ 384` | `proposer.0 as u16` (binary:7853) | widened `ValidatorId::new(as u64)` → `EngineRestoreCatchupBlock.proposer` (binary:7925); **A22.4 — the apply loop DOES re-check it:** `block.proposer != leader_for_view(block.view) ⇒ WrongProposer` (basic:2161–2168, §24.4 B4), and the proposer is bound into `derive_block_id_from_header(proposer, view, parent)` so a mismatch also triggers `BlockIdMismatch` (basic:2169–2179). The A22.3 "not independently re-checked" is **WITHDRAWN** | **lossless** (leader id `< N ≤ 384 < 2¹⁶`) **and** independently re-checked — a (hypothetical) lossy proposer would be rejected by `WrongProposer`/`BlockIdMismatch` |
| `qc_signer_indices` | `own_qc.signers` (basic:2105) = the QC formed by `VoteAccumulator::maybe_qc_for` (vote_accumulator:374) from accumulated voters — QC signer ids | a QC forms only if ≥ `q = ⌈2N/3⌉` distinct **member** votes accumulate (`qc.validate` quorum, vote_accumulator:377); votes capped at `max_votes_per_view = 256` (default; production `new` path) ⇒ `q ≤ 256 ⟹ N ≤ 384`. The catch-up **attach** path (basic:2182) also runs `qc.validate` + replays each signer via `on_vote` (256-capped), and received ids are already `< 2¹⁶` (wire `u16`) — **no cap bypass** | `v.0 as u16` per signer (binary:7854) | widened `ValidatorId::new(as u64)`, assembled into a QC and **`qc.validate(local set)`** (membership + dedup + quorum, basic:2183) + replayed via `on_vote` (basic:2192–2195); a non-member truncation → `NonMemberSigner`, a mod-`2¹⁶` collision → `DuplicateSigner` | **lossless under the default 256 vote cap** (`N ≤ 384 ⇒ ids < 2¹⁶`). "num_validators uncapped" alone does **not** establish high-ID exportability — the vote cap bounds the QC-signer count, hence `N`, for any QC to exist/attach. **Caveat (named; resolved for the baseline, forward-looking only):** the vote-cap **override** `with_state_limits` (basic:1448) has **no production caller** at `ef99e29` (its only callers are test modules — binary:21178/21650/21957/22247, all `#[cfg(test)]`); the production path is the 2-arg `new` (binary:2493, default 256). So the lossless conclusion is **source-resolved** for the baseline; the override is a **re-audit note** if a future build wires a large cap (owner: the QC/own_qc producer `hotstuff_state_engine::on_qc` + the `VoteAccumulator` config), **not** an open available-source edge and **not** EXEC |

**Composition note (QC export precondition × accumulator cap).** Under unit weights and non-overflowing arithmetic, `q = ⌈2N/3⌉ > 256` exactly when `N > 384`; since the production vote accumulator drops votes beyond `max_votes_per_view = 256`, no `(view, block_id)` ever accumulates `> 256` voters, so no QC can reach `q` for `N > 384` ⇒ **no own_qc attaches for `N > 384`** ⇒ the export yields no blocks and no high **signer/leader** ids. **A22.4 scope:** this bounds only the **(α) QC-signer** and **(β) computed-proposer** ids (`< 2¹⁶` ⇒ their narrowings lossless); it does **NOT** bound **(γ) the responder's own `local_validator_id`** (operator CLI `--validator-id`, no `< N` production guard), which is dispositioned separately (receiver-rejected via `ClaimedSenderMismatch` on a lossy value; see the table). The bound is also **separate** from the `N < 2⁶³` arithmetic-overflow premise of the Overflow note (different `N`-bound, different purpose), and it does **not** rely on "num_validators has no cap". It is contingent on the production config using the **default** `ConsensusLimitsConfig` (verified: the 2-arg `BasicHotStuffEngine::new` does, binary:2493/basic:1418–1424; the override `with_state_limits` is **test-only** at the baseline, binary:21178–22247) — so it is source-resolved for `ef99e29`, with the override a forward re-audit note. TC **lock installation** (`on_timeout_certificate` → `set_locked_qc`) is kept **separate** from **own_qc attachment** (`on_qc` → `node.own_qc`, hotstuff_state_engine:1009): only the latter feeds `export_restore_catchup_blocks`.

**Overflow bound (A22.1 opened; A22.2 — usize/isize corrected).** `W = N` does **not** by itself establish `N < 2⁶³`. Per-route: the **genesis** route caps `N ≤ MAX_GENESIS_CONSENSUS_VALIDATORS = 4096` (genesis:86) — a **source-enforced** bound (but the route is statically dead). The **uniform/binary** route has **no explicit numeric cap**: `num_validators = config.network.static_peers.len() as u64 + 1 (saturating)` (main.rs:5503/6194). **A22.2 correction:** `static_peers.len()` is a `usize`, and on a 64-bit target **`usize::MAX = 2⁶⁴−1`** (not `2⁶³−1`) — the earlier `usize ≤ isize::MAX` identity was **wrong**. The relevant restriction is a **separate library contract**: a `Vec<T>` with `T` non-zero-sized can allocate at most `isize::MAX` **bytes**, so `static_peers.len() ≤ static_peers.capacity() ≤ isize::MAX / size_of::<T_peer>()` where `T_peer` is the static-peer spec element type (a non-trivial struct/string, `size_of ≥ 1`). This is a documented Rust **library** contract (supplied docs are **external semantic evidence, not pinned-toolchain verification**). We do **not** perform the exact derivation here (it depends on `size_of::<T_peer>()` and the `+1`), so — per the task's alternative — **`N < 2⁶³` is retained explicitly as a premise**, now **without** the incorrect `usize = 2⁶³−1` argument and **without** substituting "finite memory" for a derivation: it is a stated premise that a production deployment's static-peer count (hence `N`) stays below `2⁶³`, whose exact source-contract justification (via the Vec allocation-byte limit and `size_of::<T_peer>()`) is named but not fully derived. Under this premise `2·total = 2N` does not overflow `two_thirds_vp`. The **weighted-library** arithmetic (`2·total` for arbitrary `voting_power`) is kept **separate**: there `total` can approach `u64::MAX` and `2·total` can overflow (debug panic / release wrap); this remains ordinary library code in the audit even though no production caller constructs a weighted set.

**Negative-caller search scope + positive controls (A22.1 — item 3).** The "no production caller" / "zero callers" claims were established by `git grep` over **all `*.rs` at baseline `ef99e29` (production `src`, library, sims, and `tests/`)**, distinguishing **declaration** (`struct`/`impl`/`pub fn`), **re-export** (`pub use` in `lib.rs`), **construction** (`::new`/struct-literal), and **method call**. Positive controls that the search reaches the relevant consensus wiring: `with_consensus_handler` **is** found at main.rs:6341 (builder used), `build_uniform_validator_set` **is** found called at binary:2491, and the Run-035 spawn site **is** found at main.rs:8756 — so a true caller would appear. For `StakeFilteringEpochManager`: the type is **declared** (validator_set.rs:1167) and has an `impl`/`transition` (:1222) but **no construction site anywhere** (no `::new`/literal in `src`, sims, or tests) — it is dead as to construction, distinct from merely "unreferenced".

**OBL-CONS-6 disposition (A22.1):** production membership is unit-weight and (within the inspected in-process epoch transition, binary:8501) invariant; the genesis-authority route is **statically dead** (not production — strengthening containment); the weighted builders + `StakeFilteringEpochManager` are **constructed nowhere**; `authority.validators`/ctx weight provenance resolved (unit-weight). The `N < 2⁶³` overflow bound is a **retained explicit premise** for the uniform path (source cap only on the dead genesis path). The weighted-library arithmetic stays in scope as ordinary library code. **Status: SR-DONE source** for the membership/weight-provenance question (production-contained; the one premise is named, not an untraced source edge) — re-audit if a future build wires the weighted path or `StakeFilteringEpochManager`.
