The **count-based `2f+1`** helper and the **non-dedup set-level `has_quorum`** are **not** on the wired validation path (test/sim only) — their looser behavior is **not** transferred to the production predicates. **Unit-weight explicitness:** with `W = N` the threshold is `⌈2N/3⌉`, which still requires the **cardinality bound `N = len`** (a valid signer set of distinct members has `acc = |S| ≤ N`); nothing here infers arbitrary-weight safety from the unit-weight production constructors. **SR-NONE → SR-DONE source** (degenerate reachability dispositioned per constructor; the `2*total` overflow recorded as a **library/weighted-path** edge, bounded in production only by the **retained `N<2⁶³` premise** of §27.2 — **not** asserted source-unreachable; the non-dedup set-level `has_quorum` is a test/sim-only edge; no finding forced).

### 27.4 Intersection reasoning (assumptions stated first) — OBL-CONS-7/8 boundary

**Assumptions (stated before any conclusion):** (i) a **single validator universe and weight snapshot** (one `ConsensusValidatorSet`); (ii) **nonnegative weights** (`u64`); (iii) **distinct members** (enforced at `::new`); (iv) **arithmetic without overflow of the mathematical total `W`** — i.e. `W = Σ voting_power` fits in `u64` so the stored `total_voting_power` equals `W` with **no saturation loss** (§27.3); the `2·total` computation in `two_thirds_vp` additionally requires `W ≤ u64::MAX/2`, which for the unit-weight production set reduces to the `N < 2⁶³` **bound of §27.2** (a representation/allocation premise for the uniform path, a source cap `N ≤ 4096` for the dead genesis path), retained **explicitly** rather than asserted as "small". **Mathematical vs stored total (A22.1):** the inclusion–exclusion below uses the **mathematical** `W`; it is valid **only where `W = stored total_voting_power`** (no saturation). If `Σ voting_power` overflowed `u64`, the saturating stored total is **strictly less** than `W` and the exact bounds do not hold — **saturation loss is excluded** from the exact argument (a weighted-library edge, not production-reachable at unit weight). **Derived threshold:** `q = two_thirds_vp = ⌈2W/3⌉` (from source, validator_set.rs:491).

For two signer sets `S₁, S₂` each with weight `≥ q` on the **same snapshot**, inclusion–exclusion gives intersection weight `≥ 2q − W`, i.e. **`≥ max(0, 2q − W)`** (retained). **A22.2 — scope of `2q − W > F`:** this is a **sufficient guarantee**, obtained **from the intersection lower bound**, that **every** pair of quorums intersects in more than a faulty-weight budget `F` (since intersection `≥ 2q − W > F`). It is **not** a **necessary** condition for a fixed weighted membership: the **actual** minimum pairwise intersection can **exceed** `2q − W` (the inclusion–exclusion bound is not tight for every weight distribution), so quorums may still intersect in `> F` even where `2q − W ≤ F`. **A22.1 correction — the equivalence "`2q − W > F` iff `F < W/3`" is WITHDRAWN.** `F < W/3` is **sufficient but not generally necessary** for `2q − W > F`, because `2q − W` is the **exact rounded** value of `⌈2W/3⌉`-arithmetic, which can exceed `W/3`:
- `W = 3k` → `q = 2k`, `2q − W = k` (`= W/3`);
- `W = 3k+1` → `q = 2k+1`, `2q − W = k+1` (`> W/3`);
- `W = 3k+2` → `q = 2k+2`, `2q − W = k+2` (`> W/3`).
**Mathematical counterexample (no protocol claim):** `W = 5` (`= 3·1+2`, so `k=1`) ⇒ `q = ⌈10/3⌉ = 4`, `2q − W = 3`. With `F = 2`: `2q − W = 3 > F = 2` **holds**, yet `F < W/3 ⇔ 2 < 1.667` is **false**. So `F < W/3` is not necessary for the intersection inequality. This is a **pure arithmetic** observation about the rounded threshold; it does **not** assert a protocol failure, nor greater supported Byzantine fault tolerance (the supported fault model is unchanged — this only shows the equivalence was overstated).
**Quorum-availability (stated separately; A22.2-scoped):** `W − F ≥ q` is the condition under which a quorum can form from the `≥ W − F` weight that **remains when up to `F` weight is unavailable or faulty** (under the relevant responsiveness/participation assumptions). It is **not** necessary for *any* quorum ever to form — if those `F` members also participate, a quorum can form without it (for `W=5, q=4, F=2`: `W−F = 3 < q = 4`, so a quorum cannot form from the honest 3 alone, but **can** form once the other 2 also sign). The intersection guarantee and the availability condition are **independent**. **Neither `2q − W > F` (a sufficient intersection guarantee) nor `W − F ≥ q` (an availability condition) is, alone or together, a full safety/liveness proof;** no full BFT proof is asserted.

**Boundary / degenerate:** all-zero total ⇒ `q = 0` ⇒ the bound is vacuous (any two "quorums", including empty, "intersect" in `≥ 0`) — library-path only (§27.3). **Membership-change caveat (scoped):** the above is a **within-snapshot** statement; it does **NOT** establish intersection **across** membership changes. The only membership behavior established here is the **inspected in-process epoch transition** (`engine.transition_to_epoch(.., engine.validators().clone())`, binary:8501), which reuses the same set; this is **not** extended across process restarts, across nodes, across other configurations, or to other authority objects (e.g. the separately-built verification-context set, §27.5). For a hypothetical rotating/weighted set the cross-epoch intersection and the epoch-admission rules are **unproved** (library path; recorded, not claimed). No full BFT safety/liveness proof is asserted.

### 27.5 Multi-node TC high-QC propagation — OBL-CONS-8

**Three distinct roles (A22.1 — kept separate throughout).** (R1) the **TC message sender** — the peer whose frame delivers the `TimeoutCertificate` (NewView); (R2) the **authenticated Timeout evidence signers** — the distinct validators whose individually-signed `TimeoutMsg`s constitute `tc.signed_timeouts`; (R3) the **selected high-QC reference** — the value chosen by `select_max_high_qc` (the max-`view` non-`None` one) that becomes `tc.high_qc`. R1, R2, and R3 are generally different parties; a TC with `r = |tc.signers|` evidence entries has `r` R2 signers. **A22.3 — R3 is not "exactly one reporter":** `select_max_high_qc` picks a *reference* (view, block_id), not a unique party — **(i)** if **all** evidence `high_qc` fields are `None`, there is **no** selected reference (R3 is empty; `tc.high_qc = None`); **(ii)** several reports may carry the **same** max reference (a **tie**), so more than one R2 signer can be an R3 "carrier"; selecting the reference proves **neither** a unique carrier **nor** that a quorum carried it. R1 may be any relaying peer that clears the NewView origin-admission boundary.

The assigned chain, source-traced end to end: **local lock/high_qc → Timeout construction/signing → origin-admission + per-message verification → accumulation → max-high_qc selection → TC verification → receiving-node lock/view transition.**

1. **Local high_qc + Timeout signing (emission).** `maybe_emit_view_timeout` (binary:7119) fires only after its gates (primitive enabled; not in restore-catchup; outbound facade present; `!timeout_emitted_in_view`; tick window elapsed, :7152–7174). It calls `engine.create_timeout_msg()` (basic:3080–3082), which sets **`high_qc = self.state.locked_qc().cloned()`** — i.e. the local Timeout's reported high-QC **is the node's own lock** (`locked_qc`), not an arbitrary value — and `TimeoutMsg::new(current_view, high_qc, local_id)`. Under `verification_ctx = Some` with a wired signer, `signer.sign_timeout_with_chain_id(view, high_qc, …)` (binary:7234) signs the canonical preimage `timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id(chain_id, view, high_qc, validator_id)` (timeout_verify.rs:284–289); on signer error the timeout is **not** broadcast (fail-closed). So the signature authenticates the reported `high_qc` **reference** (view+block_id as encoded), **not** that `high_qc` carries a valid quorum.
2. **Origin admission + per-message verification (inbound), then accumulation.** The inbound Timeout arm (binary:6645–6736) runs, in order: (a) `bind_sender(claimed)` (binary:6672) — Run-418 **transport-origin admission** binding the authenticated transport identity to the claimed `validator_id` (Err ⇒ reject, both None/Some); (b) **under `Some(ctx)` only**, `verify_timeout_msg(timeout, ctx.validators, …)` (binary:6698–6700) — per-message membership+suite+**signature** gate (Err ⇒ reject, not delivered); (c) `engine.on_timeout_msg(from, timeout)` (basic:3195): `from == validator_id` (:3201), stale-view ignore (:3206), `timeout_accumulator.on_timeout(validators, timeout)` (:3214). **A22.1 correction:** the accumulator's own lack of signature verification (timeout.rs:537) is only step (c); it does **not** describe the whole inbound path — under `Some` each accumulated timeout was already origin-bound (a) and signature-verified (b). Under `None`, (b) is skipped, so the accumulator holds origin-bound-but-unverified timeouts.
3. **TC formation.** `maybe_tc_for` (timeout.rs:594–633) forms a TC once `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp` (:613): `signed_timeouts = all per-view entries`, `signers = their ids` (⇒ `A = E = r ≤ 256`), `high_qc = select_max_high_qc(entries)` (R3 selection: max by `view`; equal view ⇒ first kept, timeout.rs:410–425). The logical QC's membership is its **`signers: Vec<ValidatorId>`** field (qc.rs:29–38) — **not a signer bitmap**.
4. **Receive-boundary verification (binary:6858–6931) — None vs Some:**

| Step | `verification_ctx = None` | `verification_ctx = Some(ctx)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| crypto gate | **skipped entirely** (the `if let Some(ctx)` block, binary:6858, is not entered) | empty `signed_timeouts` rejected (:6869); `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence(tc, tc.signed_timeouts, ctx.validators, …)` (:6892) |
| evidence↔signers | not checked | **permutation** required (no extras/missing/dups) (timeout_verify.rs:380–391) |
| per-evidence view | not checked | `== tc.timeout_view` else `MixedView` (:396) |
| per-evidence signature | not checked | `verify_timeout_msg` (membership+suite+**signature**) (:402) |
| quorum | not checked here | `acc_vp ≥ two_thirds_vp` over verified evidence (:411) |
| reported high_qc | not checked | `high_qc_eq(select_max_high_qc(evidence), tc.high_qc)` — **compares (view, block_id) ONLY**, NOT the high_qc's own `signers` list / endorsement (the logical QC carries a `signers: Vec<ValidatorId>` field, **no bitmap**; :420–424, explicit :432–434) |
| on Err | n/a | **return** — `on_timeout_certificate` not reached, no view advance (:6913–6927) |

5. **Receiving-node transition** `engine.on_timeout_certificate(&tc)` (basic:3256–3302), reached in **both** paths after the (None: absent / Some: passed) gate:
   - `tc.validate(validators)` (:3261) — membership + dedup + `⌈2W/3⌉` on **`tc.signers` only** (never the high_qc, never signatures).
   - **target-view admission:** `tc.view ≤ current_view ⇒ return current_view` (no-op) (:3264–3267).
   - **lock update:** if `tc.high_qc = Some`, `should_update = locked_qc.is_none() ∨ tc_high_qc.view > locked.view`; if so `set_locked_qc(tc_high_qc.clone())` (:3271–3281). **Equal high_qc view ⇒ `should_update = false` ⇒ lock unchanged** while the view still advances.
   - **view advance:** `current_view = tc.view`; reset `proposed/voted/timeout_emitted` flags; `clear_view(tc.timeout_view)` (:3292–3299).

**Jointly-supported conditional transitions (no multi-node execution result, no safety/liveness proof):**
- **(None ctx, reachable on a multi-validator P2P deployment with `io = Some` and timeout verification not activated):** a TC whose `tc.signers` pass logical `tc.validate` (membership + dedup + `⌈2W/3⌉`) and `tc.view > current_view` advances the receiver to `tc.view` and installs `tc.high_qc` as the lock when `tc_high_qc.view > locked.view` — **with no signature and no endorsement verification of any kind.** This is precisely the **A1-F1** fail-open surface on the TC path (extends A1-F1 evidence; not a new finding).
- **(Some ctx) — A22.1 corrected:** the transition occurs only after `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` succeeds, which requires `r = |tc.signers|` **distinct** evidence entries that are a **permutation** of `tc.signers`, each individually **signature-verified** (R2), each at `view == tc.timeout_view`, with `acc_vp ≥ ⌈2W/3⌉`, and `tc.high_qc` **equal to `select_max_high_qc(evidence)` by (view, block_id)** (R3 selection rule). So successful Some-verification establishes **(1)** a quorum of **distinct, authenticated** Timeout signers (R2), and **(2)** that the TC's high-QC reference is the correct max over *that* evidence per the selection rule — it does **NOT** establish that a **quorum reported the same selected high-QC**: **at least one** report (R3) carried the selected max, but **ties are possible** (several reports may carry the same max reference), so selecting it proves **neither** a unique carrier **nor** that a quorum carried it; the remaining signers may carry the same, a different, or a `None` reference. It also does **NOT** verify the selected high-QC's **own endorsement quorum** (`high_qc_eq` compares (view, block_id) only; `tc.validate`/`on_timeout_certificate` never validate the high-QC's `signers`). **"Single configured validator" is WITHDRAWN for the Some path:** for `q > 1`, one validator (one R1 sender) cannot by itself supply the required `r ≥` quorum of **distinct signatures** (unless it holds multiple validators' signing keys); an **aggregator forwarding genuinely-signed evidence** from distinct R2 signers is a **different role** from a forger. The residual A1-F3 surface under Some is therefore: *a validator that is a legitimate member of a real timeout quorum can carry an unendorsed/forged high-QC reference, and if it is the max-view report (R3) it is adopted as the receiver's lock without endorsement verification* — this needs a genuine `q`-quorum of distinct signed timeouts to exist, not a single-party forgery. (The **None** path is where a single party can fabricate the whole `tc.signers` list + high-QC with no signatures — the A1-F1 surface; "single configured validator" is retained **only** for None.)
- **Authentication ≠ endorsement (the OBL-CONS-8 distinction; A22.2-scoped):** **None** performs **no Timeout/TC *evidence* (signature) verification** — but the **transport authentication** and the **Run-418 origin admission** still apply and are **separate** checks (for a Timeout, `bind_sender`, binary:6672; for a TC/NewView, the "inbound NewView REJECTED (origin admission)" gate, binary:~6800–6807 — the R1 sender must satisfy this NewView admission boundary before the crypto gate). **Some** authenticates the *distinct signed reports* (R2) and the *selection* of R3's reference, but neither path verifies the reported high-QC's own endorsement quorum. If **all** evidence `high_qc` fields are `None`, `select_max_high_qc` returns `None` ⇒ `tc.high_qc = None` ⇒ **there is no selected high-QC reporter and no lock-update branch runs**. Equal-selected-high_qc-view (selected view `≤` locked view) leaves the lock unchanged while the view still advances, in both paths.

**One jointly-supported conditional propagation case (explicit premises; source-supported transitions separated from unobserved scheduling/deployment).** *Premises (both totals stated explicitly; A22.3):* `verification_ctx = Some`; **two unit-weight sets, each of cardinality 4** — the receiver's **engine set** `E` (total `W_E = 4`, threshold `q_E = ⌈2·4/3⌉ = 3`) and its **ctx set** `C` (total `W_C = 4`, threshold `q_C = ⌈2·4/3⌉ = 3`) — **both containing `{a,b,c}` and every member named in `Qₐ`** (membership of `{a,b,c}` in both is **not** by itself sufficient: the two **thresholds** are what must be met, and they coincide here only **because** both totals are 4; e.g. a ctx of cardinality 5 would give `q_C = ⌈10/3⌉ = 4 > 3` and **fail** — so equal cardinality is assumed, not inferred from common membership); the TC sender **R1 passes the Run-418 NewView origin-admission gate** (binary:~6800); a receiver `v` with `current_view = 5`, `locked_qc = Some(L)` with `L.view = 2`; three **distinct** validators `{a,b,c}` each emit a genuinely-signed `TimeoutMsg` for `timeout_view = 5`, with `a.high_qc = Qₐ (view 7)`, `b.high_qc = None`, `c.high_qc = Q_c (view 4)` — not identical high-QCs (no such premise is imposed); `Qₐ` is well-formed and names members of the set but its own endorsement is **not** checked anywhere on this path. *Source-supported transitions:* each of `{a,b,c}` passes `bind_sender` + `verify_timeout_msg` (R2 authenticated); an aggregator forms `tc` with `signers = {a,b,c}` (`r = 3`), `tc.timeout_view = 5`, `tc.view = 6`, `high_qc = select_max_high_qc = Qₐ` (R3 = `a`, the unique max here at view 7); at `v`, `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (against **ctx** `C`) succeeds — permutation holds, 3 distinct signatures verify, `acc_vp = 3 ≥ q_C = 3`, `high_qc_eq(Qₐ, Qₐ)`; **then** `on_timeout_certificate → tc.validate` (against **engine** `E`) succeeds — `acc_vp = 3 ≥ q_E = 3` (the **two separate threshold checks**, both met here only because `W_E = W_C = 4`); it admits `tc.view = 6 > 5`, and since `Qₐ.view = 7 > locked.view = 2` sets `locked_qc ← Qₐ` and advances `current_view` to `6`. *Not established (unobserved):* whether a real deployment schedules `{a,b,c}` to time out together, whether `Qₐ` is actually unendorsed in a live run, and any resulting honest-node disagreement — all **EXEC (E03)**. *Variant (equal-view, NO lock replacement) — recomputed (A22.2):* for the lock to be left unchanged, the **selected max** must have `view ≤ locked.view = 2`, so **all** evidence high-QCs must be `≤ 2`: set `a.high_qc = Qₐ (view 2)`, `b.high_qc = None`, `c.high_qc = Q_c (view 1)`. Then `select_max_high_qc = Qₐ` (R3 = `a`, max view 2), `tc.high_qc = Qₐ`, `high_qc_eq(Qₐ, Qₐ)` holds, `tc.view = 6` is still admitted (`> 5`), but `tc_high_qc.view = 2 > locked.view = 2` is **false** ⇒ `should_update = false` ⇒ **lock unchanged**, while `current_view` advances to `6`. *(The earlier v0.70 variant — changing only `Qₐ.view` to `2` while keeping `Q_c.view = 4` — was **wrong**: `select_max` would then pick `Q_c` at view 4 (> locked 2), which **would** replace the lock, and retaining `tc.high_qc = Qₐ` would instead **fail** `high_qc_eq`.)*

**Membership-source edge (A22.1 opened; A22.2 — completed provenance, §6J-reconciled).** Three sets are kept distinct: **(1) configured entries** = `config.network.static_peer_consensus_keys` (each decoded; **empty set rejected** before insertion, `NoConfiguredKeys`, peer_key_provider.rs:334–336; duplicate configured ids rejected, :362–366); **(2) effective ctx entries** = configured entries **plus** a conditionally **inserted signer-derived local entry** when the local id is absent and a signer is present (:384–387); when the local id **is** configured and a signer is present, the configured key is **compared byte-for-byte to the signer's key** (`configured_pk.as_slice() != signer_pk ⇒ LocalKeyMismatchesSigner`, :372–379) — a fail-closed local-key/signing-key cross-check, preserved here — so the ctx membership is **configured ⊆ effective**, *not* "exactly the configured vids" (v0.70 wording withdrawn); the effective set becomes `LoadedValidatorKeyProvider.validators` → `TimeoutVerificationContext.validators` (unit weight); **(3) engine set** = `build_uniform_validator_set` contiguous `0..N`, `N = static_peers.len()+1`. The source enforces a *partial* agreement: every `--p2p-peer vid@addr` in `config.network.static_peers` must have a configured key (`PeerMissingKey` fail-closed, :404–417; bare `addr` fails closed, :424) ⇒ effective ctx **⊇** the static-peer vids. It does **NOT** enforce full engine≡ctx **equality**. **Acceptance predicates against each set:** the Some-path `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` checks membership + quorum against the **ctx** total `W_ctx = |effective ctx|` (`acc ≥ ⌈2·W_ctx/3⌉`); the subsequent engine `on_timeout_certificate → tc.validate` checks membership + quorum against the **engine** total `N` (`acc ≥ ⌈2N/3⌉`). **A22.2 — withdraw the blanket "mismatches surface as `UnknownValidator`/`NonMemberSigner`":** a signer set `S ⊆ (effective ctx) ∩ (engine set)` passes **both** membership checks, yet the **two threshold checks use different totals** (`W_ctx` vs `N`), so `S` can be a quorum under one total and not the other — a membership *difference* need not surface as a membership *error*. The only in-tree compatibility checks are the empty-set reject, the local-entry insert, and `PeerMissingKey` (traced — available-source); **no `|effective ctx| = N` equality check exists** on the admissible path (the genesis path's full count-agreement, main.rs:5847, is **statically dead**, §27.2). Whether a deployment's effective-ctx total equals `N` — and any consequence of their differing — is a **configuration/EXEC** property; a difference is **not automatically a defect**; no missing in-tree check remains untraced here. **OBL-CONS-8 → SR-DONE source · EXEC(E03):** the propagation chain (emission→admission→per-message verify→accumulate→select→TC-verify→transition), the three-role separation, the None/Some gate table, the configured/effective/engine provenance with its two acceptance predicates and the enforced compatibility checks, and the bounded intersection review (§27.4) are source-complete; the **multi-node runtime manifestation** (does an adopted unendorsed lock produce honest-node disagreement / a safety violation; do the ctx and engine totals actually diverge in a deployment) remains **EXEC (E03)**, and no full BFT proof is claimed.

### 27.8 A22.1 — bounded reconciliation of §27 (v0.70; register/excerpt review + firsthand pinned-source at `ef99e29`)

A22.1 reconciles the A22 §27 completion claims; each correction was verified against source before adoption, and mathematical corrections are distinguished from source questions. **No new finding, no closure, no count change (13/4/22); OBL-CONS-3 not reopened; T-A18-5 not begun.** The CONS-6/7/8 statuses are **reaffirmed** after independent reassessment — the corrections refine substance without opening a new untraced available-source edge; no status was forced and no available-source question was reclassified to EXEC.

1. **Quorum mathematics (§27.4) — exact.** Retained `intersection-weight ≥ max(0,2q−W)` and (for exceeding a faulty-weight budget `F`) `2q−W>F`. **WITHDREW the equivalence "`2q−W>F` iff `F<W/3`"**: `F<W/3` is **sufficient, not generally necessary**. Exact rounding of `q=⌈2W/3⌉`: `W=3k⇒2q−W=k`; `W=3k+1⇒k+1`; `W=3k+2⇒k+2`. Counterexample **`W=5, q=4, F=2`**: `2q−W=3>F=2` holds while `F<W/3 ⇔ 2<1.667` is false (pure arithmetic; **no** protocol-failure or increased-fault-tolerance claim). Stated the **quorum-availability** requirement `W−F≥q` separately; neither inequality alone is a full safety/liveness proof. Distinguished the **mathematical total `W`** from the constructor's **saturating stored total**: equal iff `Σ voting_power ≤ u64::MAX`; saturation loss is excluded from the exact inclusion–exclusion.
2. **Production arithmetic bound (§27.2) — grounded.** `W=N` alone does not give `N<2⁶³`. Traced each route's count type/cap: genesis `N ≤ MAX_GENESIS_CONSENSUS_VALIDATORS = 4096` (source cap, but the route is statically dead); uniform/binary `num_validators = static_peers.len() as u64 + 1` (saturating, `.max(1)`), **no explicit numeric cap**, bounded by the `static_peers` `Vec` length (`usize ≤ 2⁶³−1` on 64-bit). Replaced "N small"/"production-unreachable" with an **explicit retained representation/allocation premise** (`N<2⁶³` on a 64-bit target with finite memory) for the uniform path. Kept weighted-library arithmetic (`2·total` overflow for arbitrary weights) separate and in scope as ordinary library code.
3. **Caller/configuration classifications (§27.2) — repaired.** **Genesis authority** reclassified from "PRODUCTION" to **compiled library code with a textual call site in a statically-dead branch** (`if args.consensus_authority_from_genesis`, main.rs:5812, gated by the 5405 startup refusal; `genesis_authority` always `None` in production; the 6016–6036 consumption never reached) — unit-weight provenance kept **without** implying activation. **Run 035 harness** reclassified: **compiled into the binary** (not `#[cfg(test)]`-excluded), **runtime-gated** by CLI `--devnet-forged-inject` (non-empty) + DevNet environment + `FORGED_INJECTION_ENV_VAR` (fail-closed `exit(1)` otherwise) — a comment + spawn site do not establish compile-time exclusion. **Negative-caller claims**: recorded the search scope (all `*.rs` at `ef99e29` incl. tests) + positive controls (`with_consensus_handler`, `build_uniform_validator_set`, Run-035 spawn all found), and distinguished declaration / re-export / construction / method call (`StakeFilteringEpochManager`: declared + `impl`, **no construction site**). **Unchanged-membership** scoped to the inspected in-process epoch transition only (not restarts/nodes/configs/other authority objects).

### 27.14 A22.4 — bounded reconciliation of the narrowing proof and receiving predicates (v0.73; register/excerpt review + firsthand pinned-source at `ef99e29`)

A22.4 resolves two receiver-description contradictions against source, proves (and bounds the scope of) the responder local-ID premise, and reconciles the summaries. Each observation was verified before adoption. **No new finding, no closure, no count change (13/4/22); OBL-CONS-3 not reopened; T-A18-5 not begun.** Attribution: register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. The corrections **tighten** the narrowing disposition (removing two over-claims); they do not force a status.

1. **Two receiver descriptions resolved from source (§27.2 table).** **(responder_validator_index)** §27.2's "only a self-response drop, **not** origin binding" is **WRONG** and is reconciled to §24.1–24.2: the complete route is `ConsensusNetMsg::RestoreCatchupResponse(resp)` dispatch → `claimed = ValidatorId::new(resp.responder_validator_index as u64)` (binary:7003) → `bind_sender(claimed) → gate.authorize(origin, claimed)` (binary:7004/5819) → **`ClaimedSenderMismatch` ⇒ response not applied** (binary:7013) → only then `handle_restore_catchup_response`, whose `responder_validator_index == local_validator_id ⇒ return` (binary:7872) is a **separate handler-local self-drop**. So the field **is** bound to the authenticated transport identity (the self-drop is an additional, narrower check). **(proposer_index)** §27.2's "not independently re-checked" is **WRONG** and is reconciled to §24.3/§24.4-B4: `apply_restore_catchup_blocks` rejects `block.proposer != leader_for_view(block.view)` with **`WrongProposer`** (basic:2161–2168) and binds the proposer into `derive_block_id_from_header` so a mismatch also fails **`BlockIdMismatch`** (basic:2169–2179). Both corrections follow the **pinned source**, not version recency. Decisive excerpts below.
2. **Responder local-ID premise proved independently; unconditional losslessness WITHDRAWN.** The accumulator argument (unit weights + non-overflowing `q = ⌈2N/3⌉` + the enforced 256 vote cap ⇒ QC formation needs `N ≤ 384`) bounds **member signer ids** and **computed leader ids** `< 2¹⁶` — but it does **not** bound the separately supplied `local_validator_id`. Tracing local-ID config → engine construction: `local_validator_id = ValidatorId::new(args.validator_id.unwrap_or(0))` (main.rs:5499), passed to `BinaryConsensusLoopConfig::new` (binary:562, only `num_validators.max(1)`) and `BasicHotStuffEngine::new` — **no executable `local_validator_id < num_validators` (or membership) guard** exists on the production uniform path (the sole `LocalValidatorOutOfRange` check, genesis_consensus_authority.rs:396, is on the **statically-dead** genesis route; it is an enforced check only there, not a comment/debug assertion elsewhere). **Therefore the responder-local-ID narrowing is NOT unconditionally lossless** — the A22.3 responder "lossless" conclusion is **withdrawn** and dispositioned separately. The nonempty-export guard (`!blocks.is_empty()`, binary:7838) is preserved. Four representabilities are kept distinct: **(α) QC-signer** and **(β) computed-proposer** — source-bounded `< 2¹⁶` (lossless; β also re-checked); **(γ) responder-local-ID** — **not** source-bounded (no guard), lossy if `--validator-id ≥ 2¹⁶`; **(δ) receiver rejection after a narrowing** — `ClaimedSenderMismatch` (responder) / `WrongProposer`+`BlockIdMismatch` (proposer) / `NonMemberSigner`+`DuplicateSigner` (signers), unless a truncation collides with a valid/mapped id. A dropped catch-up response is **not** called a "benign liveness no-op" (no progress argument is made).
3. **Assumptions attached; summaries reconciled.** The **no-overflow** premise is kept on every `q = ⌈2N/3⌉` conclusion (the `N ≤ 384` formation bound is **conditional**, not an unconditional configured-size limit). The corrected TC example (engine and ctx cardinalities both **4**; §27.5) and its completed arithmetic are **not** reopened; CONS-3's lineage/commit obligation is **not** touched.
4. **Statuses (reassessed on the merits).** The source disposition of the narrowing is now **complete**: all three fields traced to their receiver checks, and the `local_validator_id < N` guard established **absent** on the production path (a definitive source negative, not an open edge). **OBL-CONS-7 → SR-DONE source** and **OBL-CONS-6 → SR-DONE source** are retained **on the merits** (not automatically): the only residual is the **config/EXEC** reachability of a `--validator-id ≥ 2¹⁶` (owner: the `--validator-id` → `BinaryConsensusLoopConfig::new`/`BasicHotStuffEngine::new` construction path; the binding-map population that decides a `ClaimedSenderMismatch` vs a collision), which is a deployed-value question, **not** an available-source question transferred to EXEC. **OBL-CONS-8 → SR-DONE source · EXEC(E03)** unchanged. ### 28.1 Trace 1 — Canonical identity

CHECK (in `verify_boot_time_genesis`, genesis.rs:1802–1855, ordered): (1) `GenesisConfig::validate_for_environment(env)` = `validate()` [chain_id non-empty → allocations → per-alloc amount/addr/dup/supply-overflow → total_supply>0 → validators non-empty → per-validator addr/pqc_public_key/dup → council.validate, genesis.rs:1393–1465] then authority-present for Main/Test (DevNet tolerates `None`); (2) **chain/env substring check** (Main/Test only): `config.chain_id.to_lowercase().contains("mainnet"|"testnet")` else `ChainEnvironmentMismatch` (genesis.rs:1813–1827, firsthand-verified); (3) `compute_canonical_genesis_hash(config, env)` (genesis.rs:1831); (4) **supplied-vs-computed compare** — `expected (= config.expected_genesis_hash, operator `--expect-genesis-hash`, default None) != canonical_hash ⇒ CanonicalHashMismatch`; Mainnet+None ⇒ `ExpectedCanonicalHashMissing`; Test/DevNet+None allowed (genesis.rs:1834–1852, firsthand-verified). ACCEPTED: the computed canonical hash → `boot_accepted_canonical_hash`. FAILURE: any `Err` → main.rs:2416 `exit(1)`.
- **Canonical pre-image (firsthand, genesis.rs:1527/1580–1621).** `SHA3-256` over a **manual length-prefixed** buffer (NOT serde-canonical / sorted-key JSON), domain-tagged `CANONICAL_GENESIS_HASH_DOMAIN_V1 = b"QBIND:GENESIS:v1"` (:1527). **Included, in declaration order:** `env.scope()` ("DEV"/"TST"/"MAIN" — so **environment IS bound into the hash**, :1582), `chain_id` (:1583), `genesis_time_unix_ms` BE (:1584), each allocation, each validator, council, monetary (`serde_json::to_vec`, length-framed), and the authority block (`encode_authority_block`: policy_version, authority_sequence, authority_epoch?, pqc_transport_roots[], bundle_signing_authority_roots[]) (:1619). Optionals use a 0/1 discriminator (None ≠ Some("")). **Excluded:** `GenesisConfig.extra` — a **doc/impl divergence** (the :1569–1575 docstring claims `extra` is hashed; the body :1580–1621 does not encode it; `extra` defaults to `Null`) — recorded as a **named minor source residual**.
- **Parsing vs canonicalization vs consistency vs authentication (the decisive distinction).** Parsing = `serde_json`; canonicalization = manual re-serialize → SHA3-256 (so compact vs pretty JSON yield the same canonical hash, different raw-byte hash); consistency = the `expected != canonical_hash` operator-pinned-value check; **authentication = NONE** — there is **no PQC signature** over the genesis file or its canonical hash (positive control: no `verify…genesis…sig` construction; the authority block is validated *structurally* only, and the ledger docstring itself says the authority is "hash-bound … Not consumed for live bundle-signing-key ratification").
- **Supported invariant:** production startup proceeds past genesis verification **only if** the parsed `GenesisConfig` passes env-aware structural + authority validation, the genesis `chain_id` contains the env token on Main/Test, and (Mainnet always / when `--expect-genesis-hash` is supplied) the recomputed canonical hash equals the operator-pinned value; else `exit(1)`. **Scoped negative:** genesis authenticity is **not** established by any signature — a DevNet/TestNet node with no `--expect-genesis-hash` accepts any structurally-valid genesis; the canonical hash binds env+fields but is **self-consistency + operator-pinned, not a cryptographic trust anchor**.
- **Remaining:** source — the `extra` doc/impl divergence (minor); dependency — `qbind_hash::sha3_256` not opened (assumed standard SHA3-256, DEP); execution — the operator's actual `--expect-genesis-hash`/genesis file is a deployed value (EXEC). **DevNet applicability:** with **no `--genesis-path`**, `run_boot_time_genesis_verification` returns `SkippedNoExternalGenesis` (pqc_boot_genesis.rs:229) and the embedded path continues with **no canonical-identity enforcement**; with an external genesis, DevNet tolerates missing authority + missing expected-hash and **skips** the chain/env substring check (Main/Test only). So on DevNet the canonical hash is computed but self-consistency-only unless `--expect-genesis-hash` is pinned.

So the runtime `ChainId` (u64) is a **fixed per-environment constant**, **distinct** from the genesis file's `chain_id` String (which is only hash-bound + substring-checked). `map_environment` (pqc_boot_genesis.rs:69–75) is a 1:1 `NetworkEnvironment → NetworkEnvironmentPolicy`, and the two `scope()` functions agree byte-for-byte.

- **chain_id consumers in the reviewed runtime:** (crypto preimage, PROD) `timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id` → `domain_prefix(chain_id, Timeout)` (timeout.rs:163) = `format!("QBIND:{scope}:{kind}:v1")` where `scope = chain_scope(chain_id)` ∈ {DEV,TST,MAIN,UNK} (domain.rs:131–178, firsthand) — **the preimage uses the env-derived SCOPE TAG, not the raw `chain_id` u64 and not the genesis `chain_id` String**; (periodic snapshot, PROD) `config.chain_id().as_u64()` (main.rs:96); (trust-bundle/ratification, PROD-when-configured) `chain_id_hex(config.chain_id())` as the `expected_chain_id` string.
- **Enforced vs operator-config vs disabled.** *Enforced:* genesis `chain_id` must contain the env token on Main/Test; env scope bound into the canonical hash; Mainnet requires `--expect-genesis-hash`; crypto domain separation by scope is applied+verified on every timeout signature (timeout.rs:163–167 / timeout_verify.rs:284). *Operator-config:* `environment` itself is operator-chosen (default Devnet); **all** runtime chain separation flows **from** `environment` — there is **no** independent check that the operator's `--environment` is "correct"; the genesis substring check only couples the genesis *file* to the chosen environment, not vice-versa. *Disabled/library-only:* the dead `GenesisAuthorityValidationError::ChainEnvironmentMismatch`; the genesis-authority route (refused); the record-correspondence domain checks (unwired).

A matching label alone is **not** cryptographic domain separation; the separation is by env-scope, with exactly one `ChainId` per environment. **Remaining:** dependency — the `chain_scope` "UNK" fallback is unreachable for runtime signing (config.chain_id() is always a known constant) but would weaken isolation if a custom `ChainId` were ever passed (not exercised on the reviewed path; noted); execution — deployed `--environment`/`--chain-id` values (EXEC). **DevNet applicability:** DevNet `ChainId` → scope "DEV" in every timeout preimage; DevNet is exempt from the genesis chain/env substring check; Test/Main differ only where shared code forces it (the substring check and Mainnet's mandatory expected-hash).

### 28.6 A23.1 — Reconciliation of §28 genesis/bootstrap evidence (firsthand `ef99e29`; v0.75)

A23.1 re-traced the §28 evidence firsthand. **Central correction:** v0.74 §28.2 wrongly concluded that "none of the four identity sets consume genesis authority on production … the record-correspondence module is library-only … [transport] remains a Run 102+ topic (not wired)." That rested on the **stale Run-101 docstrings** (`GenesisAuthorityConfig`, genesis.rs:599–600/768–776, and the `authority` field doc, genesis.rs:1349–1355 — all still saying "Not yet consumed by any live ratification verifier … Run 102+") rather than a caller trace of the pinned **Run-105+/Run-422** binary. A **live, fail-closed production path does consume** the genesis authority block. Register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification.

**1. Genesis-authority consumer trace (item 1).**
- **The live consumer.** `apply_run_105_ratification_gate_at_startup` (main.rs:135) is the production **Run-105/106 bundle-signing-key ratification gate**. It re-loads the operator `--genesis-path` (`load_external_genesis`, main.rs:193), extracts `genesis_cfg.authority` (fatal if absent, main.rs:201–214), recomputes the canonical hash, and calls `qbind_ledger::enforce_bundle_signing_key_ratification(RatificationEnforcementInputs { ratification, authority, expected_chain_id, expected_environment, expected_genesis_hash: &canonical_hash, candidate_bundle_signing_public_key, policy })` (main.rs:274–282). Production caller: **main.rs:6837**, inside the startup `--p2p-trust-bundle` surface, after Run-050/051/053/057 bundle validation + the activation gate and **before** the Run-055 sequence write and **before** bundle roots merge into `trusted_roots`. On `Err` → `[run-105] FATAL` + `std::process::exit(1)` (main.rs:6846–6852) — **fail-closed: no root merge, no sequence write, no P2P start**. (`build_run_105_reload_check_context`, main.rs:458, is the sibling reload used by the reload-check / peer-candidate / v2-marker preflights at main.rs:3055/3460/4508/6733/7872/8291/8968.)
- **Config gates.** Surface: operator supplies `--p2p-trust-bundle`. Invocation: `pqc_ratification_policy::ratification_gate_decision(config.environment, args.p2p_trust_bundle_ratification_enforcement_enabled)` — **MainNet and TestNet invoke by default** (the `…enforcement-enabled` flag can neither enable nor disable MainNet); **DevNet** is Run-105 operator-opt-in. v1 body: an external `--genesis-path` with an authority block is required, else **MainNet FATAL** / **DevNet·TestNet** require `--p2p-trust-bundle-allow-unratified-testnet-devnet` to take the explicit legacy-unratified verdict. A v2 (`schema_version=2`) sidecar diverts to `preflight_run_136_v2_marker_decision_for_startup` (the v1 gate is SKIPPED on that branch).
- **Which of the three relationships.** This is **(2) authorizing acceptance of a supplied trust bundle** (a ratification gate) — **not (1) directly constructing a root/validator set** and **not (3) merely validating/hashing**. The live transport-root set still comes from CLI (`--p2p-trusted-root` / `--p2p-trust-bundle` + leaf certs); genesis authority does **not** become the root set. It **gates** whether the supplied bundle's signing key is accepted: `enforce_…` (bundle_signing_ratification.rs:1150) delegates the crypto/chain/env/genesis/authority-root binding to the Run-103 verifier `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification` (:1202), then binds the verified ratification to the **exact** candidate signing key (`RatifiesDifferentKey` guard, :1215). A Strict surface with **zero** `bundle_signing_authority_roots` fails closed (`NoBundleSigningAuthorityConfigured`, :1170); a missing ratification under Strict fails closed (`Missing`, :1181); `AllowLegacyUnratified` on MainNet is refused defense-in-depth (:1160). The authority-root lookup consults **`authority.bundle_signing_authority_roots` only**; `pqc_transport_roots` is explicitly **rejected** as a ratification anchor (bundle_signing_ratification.rs:26/592/688/889/1861).
- **Do not transfer the disabled consensus-authority flag.** The `--consensus-authority-from-genesis` route (`load_verify_and_build_genesis_authority`, genesis_consensus_authority.rs:1404 / main.rs:5852) remains statically dead (refused at main.rs:5405; branch guard `if args.consensus_authority_from_genesis` at main.rs:5812 is documented unreachable). That deadness is **specific to consensus-signing authority** and must **not** be read onto the independently-wired Run-105 trust-bundle ratification path, which is live. The two genesis-authority sub-blocks thus have **different dispositions**: `pqc_transport_roots` — hash-bound only; **not** a live root source (its only non-test production write is the embedded-genesis constructor, pqc_boot_genesis.rs:344) and **not** a ratification anchor; `bundle_signing_authority_roots` — hash-bound **and** a live, fail-closed trust-bundle ratification anchor.
- **`boot_accepted_canonical_hash` correspondence (item 1).** Created at boot (`Some(canonical_hash)`, main.rs:2399), threaded `run_p2p_node` (main.rs:6183) → `run_p2p_consensus_security_preflight` (sig :5648; call :8131) → `load_verify_and_build_genesis_authority` (:5856). Its **only** equality consumer — "requires equality with the boot-accepted identity (reject a file swapped after boot)" (main.rs:5845–5850) — is inside the `if args.consensus_authority_from_genesis` branch, i.e. the **dead** route. On the **live** Run-105 path the gate re-loads the same `--genesis-path` and **recomputes `compute_canonical_genesis_hash` independently**, and does **not** compare the reload against `boot_accepted_canonical_hash`. So: **the only genesis-reload correspondence check against the boot-accepted identity is on the statically-dead route; the live reload trusts the same pathname** — a swap between the Run-102 boot read and the Run-105 reload within the same process start would not be caught by a boot-hash comparison (the Run-105 recompute is internally consistent but not cross-bound to the boot-accepted value). Recorded as a precise observation, **not a forced finding** (same-process / same-path reload; the on-disk TOCTOU surface is an EXEC/operational concern, named). *Do not infer object equality from the shared pathname.*

**2. Trust model + startup quantifiers (item 2).**
- **"No embedded genesis-signature verification" ≠ "no authentication."** v0.74 §28.1's blunt "**authentication = NONE**" is **withdrawn**. Correct: there is **no embedded PQC signature** over the genesis file or its canonical hash (no `verify…genesis…sig` construction). But a **trusted, out-of-band-provisioned `--expect-genesis-hash`** authenticates **every field covered by the canonical encoding** (env scope, chain_id, genesis_time, allocations, validators, council, monetary, authority), **conditional on** (a) SHA3-256 collision/preimage resistance and (b) **trusted provisioning of that pin** — which **this audit does not establish** (the pin is an operator input; its provenance is EXEC). No new signature requirement is asserted.
- **Expected-digest type / source / route.** Type `config.expected_genesis_hash: Option<GenesisHash>`, `GenesisHash = [u8;32]` (node_config.rs:3985). Source CLI `--expect-genesis-hash <String>` (cli.rs:1583) → `parse_genesis_hash(hex)` → `[u8;32]` → `config.expected_genesis_hash` (cli.rs:2373; CLI doc cli.rs:1710 names it "canonical Run 101 genesis hash"). Route `run_boot_time_genesis_verification` passes `config.expected_genesis_hash.as_ref()` as `expected_canonical_hash` to `verify_boot_time_genesis` (pqc_boot_genesis.rs:244), compared against `compute_canonical_genesis_hash` — the **structured canonical** hash (genesis.rs:1831–1846). (The `compute_canonical_genesis_hash` docstring's claim that the **file-bytes** hash `compute_genesis_hash_bytes` backs `--expect-genesis-hash` is **stale legacy T233 wording**: at `ef99e29` the boot comparator is the canonical hash; `compute_genesis_hash_bytes` has **no boot caller** — its only non-test use is the `--print-genesis-hash` compact/pretty demonstration, pqc_boot_genesis.rs:503/506.)
- **Startup matrix** (env × external-genesis × expected-digest, at `run_boot_time_genesis_verification` → `verify_boot_time_genesis`):

| env | ext-genesis | `--expect-genesis-hash` | behaviour at the caller boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| any | absent | — | MainNet → `GenesisPathMissing` **exit(1)**; DevNet/TestNet → `SkippedNoExternalGenesis` (**embedded path continues; NO canonical-identity enforcement**) |
| MainNet | present | absent | `ExpectedCanonicalHashMissing` **exit(1)** (also pre-empted by `validate_mainnet_invariants` T233 shield) |
| MainNet | present | present | validate → substring needle "mainnet" → canonical → `expected≠canonical ⇒ CanonicalHashMismatch` **exit(1)**; else Verified |
| TestNet | present | absent | validate (authority **required**) → substring "testnet" → canonical computed, **no pin compare** (documented partial-positive); Verified |
| TestNet | present | present | as MainNet-present-present, needle "testnet" |
| DevNet | present | absent | validate (authority **optional**) → **substring exempt** → canonical computed, no pin compare; Verified |
| DevNet | present | present | validate → substring exempt → pin compared (`CanonicalHashMismatch` on mismatch); Verified |

- **Mainnet mandatory-pin — qualified.** Mandatory **only on the external-genesis branch**, enforced in two places: `NodeConfig::validate_mainnet_invariants` (T233 `MainnetConfigError::ExpectedGenesisHashMissing`) **before** the boot verifier, and `verify_boot_time_genesis` step 4 `(Mainnet, None) ⇒ ExpectedCanonicalHashMissing`. On the **no-external-genesis** branch the pin check never runs — MainNet fails earlier on `GenesisPathMissing` (nothing to hash). So "MainNet always compares a pin" holds only once an external genesis is present.
- **Loader fallback vs serde field defaults.** The **loader** `load_external_genesis` does **no whole-config fallback/defaulting**: a missing/unreadable/malformed file is a typed fatal error and the required top-level fields (`chain_id`, `genesis_time_unix_ms`, `allocations`, `validators`, `council`, `monetary`) must be present (no embedded `GenesisConfig::default`). **Serde field-level defaults do exist**: `extra` `#[serde(default)] → Null` (genesis.rs:1339), `authority` `#[serde(default)] → None` (genesis.rs:1356; then required by `validate_for_environment` on Main/Test), plus nested optionals (`authority_sequence`/`authority_epoch`/`pqc_transport_roots`; alloc `memo`/`lockup`; validator `name`/`metadata`). So "**no defaults**" is correct **only in the loader-fallback sense** and is narrowed here — it does **not** contradict `extra`'s recorded serde default.

**3. Repository-owned canonical-hash trace (item 3).**
- **`sha3_256` is in-tree, not DEP.** `qbind-ledger` depends on `qbind-hash` by **path** (qbind-ledger/Cargo.toml:18). `qbind_hash::sha3_256` (crates/qbind-hash/src/hash.rs:5–12) is a thin wrapper — `Sha3_256::new(); update(data); finalize()` — over the RustCrypto **`sha3 = "0.10"`** crate (qbind-hash/Cargo.toml). **The wrapper is opened and confirmed standard SHA3-256 (FIPS-202)**; v0.74's "`sha3_256` not opened (assumed standard, DEP)" is **withdrawn**. DEP narrows to the external **`sha3` 0.10 Keccak permutation internals only**, not the wrapper.
- **Field-to-encoding table** (`compute_canonical_genesis_hash`, genesis.rs:1576–1621; counts/lengths big-endian `u32`, **declaration order**, not sorted):

| # | field | framing |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | domain | literal `b"QBIND:GENESIS:v1"` (no length prefix) |
| 1 | `env.scope()` | `u32_be(len)‖bytes` ("DEV"/"TST"/"MAIN") |
| 2 | `chain_id` | `u32_be(len)‖UTF-8` |
| 3 | `genesis_time_unix_ms` | `u64_be` |
| 4 | allocations | `u32_be(count)`, per alloc: `address(len‖bytes)`, `amount be`, `memo` opt (0/1 disc), `lockup_until_unix_ms` opt-u64 (0/1 disc) |
| 5 | validators | `u32_be(count)`, per validator: `address`, `pqc_public_key`, `stake be`, `name` opt, `metadata` opt |
| 6 | council | `u32_be(threshold)`, `u32_be(member_count)`, each member `len‖bytes` |
| 7 | monetary | `u32_be(len) ‖ serde_json::to_vec(monetary)` (serde_json **without** `preserve_order`) |
| 8 | authority | `encode_authority_block(authority.as_ref())` — empty framed block if `None`; else policy_version, sequence, epoch(opt), `pqc_transport_roots[]`, `bundle_signing_authority_roots[]` |
| — | **`extra`** | **OMITTED** (not encoded) |

  Optionals use a `0`/`1` discriminator (`None` ≠ `Some("")`). Normalization is **structural re-serialization** → compact-vs-pretty source JSON and map-order differences yield the **same** canonical hash (a different raw-byte hash).
- **`GenesisConfig.extra` — doubly inert.** (a) **Excluded** from the canonical encoding (body omits it) while the docstring (genesis.rs:1569–1575) claims it is hashed — a **doc/impl divergence** (documentation bug). (b) **Zero production consumers** (`git grep '\.extra' crates/*/src` outside tests = none). Documented role "Reserved for future extensions" (genesis.rs:1337). **Exact property:** changing `extra` leaves the canonical encoding (hence the canonical hash and the `--expect-genesis-hash` comparison) unchanged, **and — because no production code reads it — also leaves accepted runtime behaviour unchanged.** Omission alone forces no finding, and the consumer trace confirms there is none. (Digest equality, encoded-field identity, and complete runtime-config identity kept distinct: two files differing only in `extra` are digest-equal, encoded-field-identical, and — here — runtime-identical.)

**4. Chain-separation bounded to inspected bytes/callers (item 4).**
- **Complete timeout preimage** (`timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id`, timeout.rs:157–187 — inspected end-to-end, not only `domain_prefix`): `domain_prefix(chain_id, Timeout)` = `b"QBIND:{scope}:TIMEOUT:v1"` ‖ `view` (`u64` LE) ‖ [`high_qc.block_id` (32 B) ‖ `high_qc.view` (`u64` LE)] or [32 zero bytes ‖ `0u64` LE] ‖ `validator_id.0` (`u64` LE). **Exactly what appears:** the **env-derived scope tag** ("DEV"/"TST"/"MAIN"/"UNK") via `domain_prefix`; **not** the raw numeric `chain_id` (`u64`), **not** the genesis `chain_id` String, **not** the canonical genesis digest.
- **Verification reconstruction.** `timeout_verify.rs:284` reconstructs the identical preimage via `timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id(chain_id, timeout.view, timeout.high_qc.as_ref(), timeout.validator_id)` then `backend.verify_vote(…)` (step 5). It requires a `key_provider` + `backend_registry` — i.e. it runs **only under an activated `TimeoutVerificationContext`**; per A22.2 the `None`-ctx `on_timeout_certificate` path (basic:3256) runs **`tc.validate` only** (no signature reconstruction). **Incoming timeout-signature verification is therefore conditional, not unconditional** (verification-context condition preserved).
- **`chain_scope` UNK branch = repo-owned source (not DEP).** `chain_scope` (qbind-types/src/domain.rs:131–141, **in-tree**) returns "UNK" for any `chain_id` ∉ {DEV,TST,MAIN} — **repository-owned code with known behaviour**, an **answered** source question (reclassified from v0.74's "dependency"). **Caller applicability:** on the reviewed signing/verification path `chain_id = config.chain_id() = NetworkEnvironment::chain_id()` is always a known env constant (primitives.rs:114–120), so the UNK arm is **unreachable there**; it is reachable only if the public `chain_scope`/`domain_prefix` is called with a custom `ChainId` (doc: UNK "provides weaker isolation"). Named as a scoped observation.
- **No `--chain-id` CLI option exists.** v0.74 §28.3/§28.5's "deployed `--chain-id` values (EXEC)" is **withdrawn**: the CLI exposes **no** `--chain-id` arg (cli.rs long-args include `--network-mode`, `--genesis-path`, `--print-genesis-hash`, `--expect-genesis-hash`, `--consensus-authority-from-genesis`; none is `--chain-id`). The runtime `ChainId` is derived **solely** from the environment, chosen by **`--env`/`-e`** (default `devnet`, cli.rs:92) or `--profile`/`-P` (cli.rs:82). The remaining EXEC item is the deployed **`--env`/profile** choice (and the operator-provisioned genesis/pin), **not** a chain-id flag.

**5. Completion reassessment + ledger (item 5).**
- **Answered vs unfinished (kept distinct).** **Answered** source questions (behaviour/absence established): the `extra` exclusion + no-consumer disposition; the `sha3_256` in-tree wrapper; the complete timeout preimage; the `chain_scope` UNK behaviour; the no-`--chain-id` fact; the `boot_accepted_canonical_hash` correspondence being dead-route-only. **Unfinished** source work (available in-tree, **production-active**, not fully read): the **live Run-105/106 ratification verifier** — the Run-103 crypto core `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification` (signature verification + preimage reconstruction + authority-root lookup) and the entire **v2 (Run-130/131/136) ratification + authority-marker** path — a consumer of genesis `bundle_signing_authority_roots` that A23 never traced (it was wrongly called "not wired"). ### 28.8 A23.2 — Substantive GEN-1 startup-ratification trace completed (firsthand `ef99e29`; v0.76)

A23.2 completes the live production edge A23.1 §28.6 left open: the inner ratification verifiers (`verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification` v1, `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2`), the startup-selected v2 Run-130/131/136 route, and the provenance of every expected value. The genesis→startup-ratification **acceptance chain** is now traced end-to-end. Register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification.

**A. Startup ordering + §28.6 conflict resolution (item 1).** Two independent layers enforce the MainNet pin; §28.6's two statements describe different layers — no contradiction:
- **Config layer** `NodeConfig::validate_mainnet_invariants` (node_config.rs:5577), ordered: step 31 `genesis_source.validate_for_mainnet()` (external genesis required) → `GenesisMisconfigured` (:5862); **then** step 32 `expected_genesis_hash.is_none()` → `ExpectedGenesisHashMissing` (:5869). So MainNet-without-external-genesis fails at **step 31, before step 32** — the pin check is ordered *after* the genesis-presence check.
- **Boot-verifier layer** `run_boot_time_genesis_verification` (pqc_boot_genesis.rs:215): Path 1 (`!use_external || genesis_path.is_none()`) returns `GenesisPathMissing` (MainNet) / `SkippedNoExternalGenesis` (Dev·TestNet) **before** Path 2 calls `verify_boot_time_genesis` (whose step-4 `(Mainnet,None) ⇒ ExpectedCanonicalHashMissing` is the verifier-layer pin check).
So "`validate_mainnet_invariants` checks the pin before the boot verifier" (true — the config shield runs first and *contains* a pin check at step 32) and "no external genesis fails before the pin check runs" (true — both layers order the genesis-presence refusal ahead of their pin check) are **consistent**: a **helper branch** (step 32 / verify step 4) vs **the complete path** (step 31 / Path 1 precede it).
- **Supplied expected digest + no external genesis — explicit disposition:** `expected_genesis_hash` is read only inside Path 2 (`verify_boot_time_genesis(…, config.expected_genesis_hash.as_ref())`, pqc_boot_genesis.rs:244). On Path 1 it is **never consumed**: MainNet → refused (GenesisPathMissing / config step 31); **Dev·TestNet → `SkippedNoExternalGenesis`, so a supplied `--expect-genesis-hash` has NO effect** (embedded path continues, pin silently unused).

**B. First-applicable outcome, by (env × external-genesis × pin):** see the §28.6 startup matrix; A23.2 confirms the *first* applicable refusal/comparison/continuation at each boundary: config step 31 (MainNet no-genesis) → boot Path 1 (GenesisPathMissing / Skipped) → `validate_for_environment` (structural) → chain/env substring (Main/Test) → canonical-hash **compute** → pin **compare** only if present (**TestNet-no-pin computes but does NOT compare** — documented partial-positive) → Verified / `exit(1)`.

### 28.10 A23.3 — v2 startup acceptance, candidate-key binding, handoff ownership (firsthand `ef99e29`; v0.77)

A23.3 traces the v2 startup path **independently of v1** and finds a **source-established defect**: the v2 `--p2p-trust-bundle` startup ratification path **does not bind the genesis-ratified target key to the key that actually signed the accepted bundle** — the v1 `RatifiesDifferentKey` check has **no v2 analogue**. Register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification.

**1. v2 candidate-key binding — the defect A23-F1 (item 1).**
- **Normative basis.** `docs/protocol/QBIND_TRUST_ANCHOR_AUTHORITY_MODEL.md` §5.4 condition **1**: "A bundle-signing key K is authorized to sign a bundle B … iff … **There exists a ratification R such that `R.bundle_signing_public_key == K`**" (K = the bundle's actual signing key).
- **v1 enforces it.** `apply_run_105_ratification_gate_at_startup` resolves K from `loaded.signature_status = Verified{signing_key_id}` → `bundle_signing_keys.lookup` (main.rs:234–249), passes it as `candidate_bundle_signing_public_key`, and `enforce_bundle_signing_key_ratification` checks `ratified.public_key == candidate` else `RatifiesDifferentKey` (ratif.rs:1215). The v1 Run-120 preflight also takes `&loaded, &bundle_signing_keys` and re-derives K (main.rs:1400/1432–1463).
- **v2 omits it — positive-controlled.** The startup v2 path `preflight_run_136_v2_marker_decision_for_startup(config.environment, config.chain_id(), ctx_data, data_dir, now_secs)` (main.rs:1176; dispatched main.rs:6808) receives **neither `loaded` nor `bundle_signing_keys`** (confirmed: no such token in its body). ### 28.12 A23.4 — A23-F1 disposition (STATIC-SUPPORTED / OPEN) + bounded acceptance case (firsthand `ef99e29`; v0.78)

A23.4 applies the §1 classification standard to the A23.3 evidence and **withdraws** the A23.3 framing ("source-established defect, promotable at discretion; headline 13/4/22 kept"). On the reported evidence A23-F1 is **STATIC-SUPPORTED / OPEN** and is counted as the **14th static-supported finding**; runtime/exploit confirmation is **E23** (new). The C4 cross-reference does **not** replace the finding record. Classification authorizes no implementation or execution. Register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification.

**Finding record — A23-F1 (full §1 shape; evidence status / C4 relationship / wiring+deployment / severity+priority+release-consequence / reproduction+remediation kept separate).**
- **Violated invariant.** Model §5.4 ("Activation semantics") condition **1**: a bundle-signing key K is authorized to sign a bundle B only if there exists a ratification R with `R.bundle_signing_public_key == K`. For a **Ratify** action this is the authorization requirement for the signer of an accepted bundle.
- **Callable path (source-established).** Startup `--p2p-trust-bundle` surface → v2 dispatch when `ctx.ratification_v2.is_some()` (main.rs:6796–6808, v1 gate SKIPPED) → `preflight_run_136_v2_marker_decision_for_startup(config.environment, config.chain_id(), ctx_data, data_dir, now_secs)` (main.rs:1176) → `verify_bundle_signing_key_ratification_v2` (ratif.rs:1808) + `decide_marker_acceptance_v2` (pqc_authority_marker_acceptance.rs:1590) → on `Ok`, `loaded.active_roots` merge into `trusted_roots` (main.rs:7201–7207) + P2P start. The preflight inputs are `{environment, chain_id, ctx_data, data_dir, now_secs}` — **neither** `loaded` **nor** `bundle_signing_keys`; `RatificationV2VerifierInputs`/`MarkerAcceptanceV2Inputs` carry no candidate key; `derive_authority_state_v2_from_ratification` binds the target only to the verifier's own output (`ratification.target_bundle_signing_key_fingerprint == ratified.fingerprint`, :1969). `bundle_signing_keys` ← CLI `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-key` (main.rs:2901), independent of the ratification.
- **Explicit prerequisites (distinct capabilities, not collapsed).** (1) select a v2 (`schema_version=2`) sidecar + a bundle; (2) a bundle signed by **K ∈ the configured `--p2p-trust-bundle-signing-key` set** (`loaded.signature_status = Verified{K}`); (3) possession of a **valid genesis-authority-signed** v2 ratification for some **T** (the authority-root ML-DSA-44 signature over the v2 preimage must verify against a `bundle_signing_authority_roots` entry in the **reloaded** genesis authority — the Run-105 reload used by the verifier, **not** the boot-accepted identity; **equality with the boot-accepted genesis is not enforced on this live reload route**, A23.2/A23.3 — so the signature is **not forgeable** but is checked against the reloaded authority); (4) **K ≠ T**; (5) ratification-enforcement selected (Main/TestNet default; DevNet only under `--p2p-trust-bundle-ratification-enforcement-enabled`); (6) `--data-dir` present. These are **separate** from the strictly higher capabilities of **changing trusted config** or **changing genesis authority**. **Premise of the sufficient case:** the Run-105-reloaded genesis file is byte-identical to the boot-verified one (no on-disk swap between the Run-102 boot read and the Run-105 reload — not enforced in-source; such a swap is a **deployed / on-disk (EXEC) question owned by OBL-GEN-1** itself, **not E22** — E22 is the snapshot-restoration trust boundary, a different surface).
- **Source-established consequence (conditional).** When prerequisites (1)–(6) hold **and the complete successful-path conjunction of the symbolic table below succeeds** — the v2 verifier accepts the Ratify ratification of T (step 5), the anti-rollback marker accepts (step 7), governance policy is NotRequired/satisfied (step 8), and the Run-055 sequence check passes (step 9) — the v2 route accepts the bundle: `loaded.active_roots` merge into `trusted_roots` **with no further K/T check (the merge is unconditional only at that post-gate point, reached after the preceding checks succeed)** and P2P starts, **without establishing the §5.4-cond-1 authorization relationship for the actual signer K** — the genesis-authority ratification it checks is for T, not K. K's membership in the configured signing-key set is the *pre-ratification* trust level the Run-105/106 gate is designed to **augment** with genesis-authority ratification; on v2 that augmentation binds T, so for K≠T it is absent for K. **Not** "every valid v2 ratification suffices" — the specific conjunction above.
- **Evidence status / lifecycle:** **STATIC-SUPPORTED · OPEN** (source-level; high confidence on the control-flow absence, positive-controlled against v1; runtime/exploit **unexecuted** = E23). **C4 relationship:** concrete source instance of C4 (cross-reference, not a substitute). **Wiring / deployment:** production-WIRED on the v2 startup path; **observed deployment unestablished**. **Severity / priority / release consequence:** priority **P2**; severity unassigned pending E23; **not asserted a launch blocker** (C4 OPEN ≠ blocker; DevNet must-have is a documented-decision item). **Reproduction / remediation:** E23 (runtime); remediation = add the v2 candidate binding (target == bundle signer K) analogous to v1 `RatifiesDifferentKey` — **owned by OBL-GOV-2 as audit owner, not authorized here**.

**Symbolic acceptance table — one jointly-supported Ratify case (K ≠ T).** K = the configured key whose bundle signature verifies; T = the verified v2 ratification target. Read top-to-bottom from the actual caller guards; control-flow continuation is distinguished from persistence invocation / successful persistence / root merge / node startup:

## 29. A24 — T-A18-6 / OBL-OPS-1: operational configuration, metrics endpoint, diagnostic data flow (read-only; v0.80)

A24 performs the **OBL-OPS-1 portion** of T-A18-6 (the other T-A18-6 transport obligations retain their own statuses). Firsthand pinned-source at `ef99e29`; register/excerpt review, **not** independent checkout verification. **No new finding** (one scoped availability observation, §29.4); **no count change (14/4/23)**. OBL-CONS-3, C4/C5, RS1, coverage, baseline, execution all unchanged.

### 29.1 Production caller / configuration inventory

| control | production entrypoint | config source / precedence | enablement predicate | default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Metrics HTTP server | `main` → `MetricsHttpConfig::from_env()` (main.rs:4991) → `spawn_metrics_http_server_with_crypto(node_metrics, cfg, CryptoMetricsRefs::new(), shutdown_rx)` (main.rs:5003) | **env var only** `QBIND_METRICS_HTTP_ADDR` (`METRICS_HTTP_ADDR_ENV`, metrics_http.rs:62); **no CLI flag, no profile layer** | `cfg.enabled` true iff the env var is **set and parses as `SocketAddr`** | **disabled** (`MetricsHttpConfig::disabled()`, bind `127.0.0.1:0`, enabled=false) |
| Build/chain context (metric labels) | `node_metrics.set_build_context(env_label, chain_id_hex)` (main.rs ~4984); `set_data_dir(dir)` when `--data-dir` set | derived from `config.environment` + `config.chain_id()` (+ `--data-dir`) | always set pre-spawn (labels only) | env/chain = fixed vocab; data_dir path stored, **not emitted** |
| Diagnostics / "logs" | **stderr `eprintln!`** throughout | **no** `tracing`/`env_logger`/`RUST_LOG`/`log` init in `main.rs` (no level/sink config) | always on stderr | — |
| (established, not recounted) connection-rate limiter | main.rs:8096–8111 (A4) | CLI-installed | **default-off** (abuse_dos_config.rs:258) | off |
| (established, not recounted) timeout pacer | binary_consensus_loop.rs (A14) | config | invalid config → **disabled pacer, startup continues** (fail-closed-to-disabled) | base 50 / ×2 / cap 800 |

**Callers (positive-controlled).** `spawn_metrics_http_server_with_crypto`: **one production caller** (main.rs:5003); a thin lib wrapper `spawn_metrics_http_server` (metrics_http.rs:244) + the re-exports (lib.rs:2401–2402) are **library interface**; `spawn_metrics_http_server_with_addr` (returns the bound addr) is **test-only** (binary_path_b1_b2_b4_tests.rs, metrics_http_tests.rs). `MetricsHttpConfig::from_env` production caller = main.rs:4991.

### 29.2 Precondition → check → output/state effect → failure outcome

| # | precondition | check (source) | accepted output / state | failure outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `QBIND_METRICS_HTTP_ADDR` set | `std::env::var` + `parse::<SocketAddr>()` (metrics_http.rs:137–141) | enabled cfg bound to the parsed addr + `[metrics_http] Enabling…` | **set-but-invalid → warn + `disabled()`** (fail-closed to disabled, NOT fail-open; :148–151); **unset → `disabled()`** (:159) |
| 2 | cfg enabled | `if !config.enabled { return no-op task }` (metrics_http.rs:265–268) | spawn the server task | disabled → **no-op task** (never binds) |
| 3 | bind | `TcpListener::bind(config.bind_addr)` (metrics_http.rs:338) | `[metrics_http] Listening on {addr}` | bind error → `MetricsHttpError::Bind` → logged `[metrics_http] Server error`; task ends; **node startup continues** (handle independent) |
| 4 | accept loop | `tokio::select!{ listener.accept() / shutdown_rx.changed() }` (metrics_http.rs:353–380) | per-connection **detached** `tokio::spawn(handle_connection)` (handle discarded; no read deadline → **not duration-bounded**, "short-lived" withdrawn A24.2 §29.9) | accept error → logged + **continue**; shutdown → `[metrics_http] Shutting down` + break |
| 5 | request parse | `read_line` request-line; header-skip loop reads until blank/EOF (metrics_http.rs:393–412) | request line split; `parts.len()<2` → **400** | **no request-size / header-count / line-length cap** (repo-owned bounds observation §29.4) |
| 6 | method / route | `method != "GET"` → **405**; `path ∈ {/metrics,/metrics/}` → 200; else **404** (metrics_http.rs:420–470) | 200 + `format_metrics_output(...)` body (`text/plain; version=0.0.4`) | non-GET → 405; other path → 404 |
| 7 | response | `send_response` fixed `HTTP/1.1` + `Content-Length` + `Connection: close` (metrics_http.rs:491–518) | response written + flushed | write/flush io error → `MetricsHttpError::Io` → conn-task logs `[metrics_http] Connection from {peer} error` |

**Task ownership.** The server task is the `metrics_handle` returned to `main` (driven by the node shutdown `watch`). Each **connection** is a **detached** `tokio::spawn` (handle dropped; **"short-lived" withdrawn A24.2 §29.9 — no read deadline, so duration is not source-bounded**), with **no cap on concurrent connection-handler tasks** (§29.4). Reuses the A15/OBL-SUP-1b supervision posture without recounting.

### 29.3 Diagnostic field-to-output table

| source value | sink | representation | secret? |
|---|---|---|---|
| env (devnet/testnet/mainnet) | `/metrics` `qbind_node_build_info{env=…}` | fixed vocab, `sanitize_info_label` (metrics.rs:5779 applied at :10561) | public identifier |
| chain_id hex | `qbind_node_build_info{chain_id=…}` | canonical hex, sanitized | public identifier |
| crate version / `QBIND_BUILD_ID` / `QBIND_GIT_COMMIT` | `qbind_node_build_info{version,build_id,git_commit}` | sanitized (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, ≤64, empty→`unknown`) | public build metadata |
| data-dir path | `qbind_node_data_dir_free_bytes` | **free bytes (numeric) only — the path is NEVER emitted** (`data_dir_free_bytes` metrics.rs:5811; emission :10589; path stored in `set_data_dir` :9735 but not formatted) | path **not** exposed; free-bytes is benign |
| configured bundle-signing keys | `qbind_p2p_pqc_trust_bundle_signing_keys_configured` | **count** (metrics.rs:7265) | count, not key material |
| consensus-sig / KEMTLS / DAG-mempool metrics | `/metrics` crypto section | counters/timings; docstrings assert "**No secrets, key IDs, passphrases, or key material**" (metrics.rs:4963 / 5227) | no secrets (by design) |
| bind_addr / peer_addr / io errors | **stderr** `eprintln!` (startup/accept/conn-error/shutdown) | operator config + connection source + `io::Error` text | network metadata / error text — not secret |

**Conclusion (secret-free, with a stated limit). [A24.1 §29.7 SUPERSEDES this universal phrasing with the precise per-output-group properties — the production output is `NodeMetrics::format_metrics()` only (crypto_refs not activated), module-wide no runtime-string labels [**further corrected A24.2 §29.9** — "module-wide no runtime-string labels" is WITHDRAWN: runtime-interpolated labels DO exist (peer/validator/block-id/env/op), all public identifiers, none secret], and the "data-dir path never emitted" claim is scoped to the demonstrated sinks.]** On the reviewed path the metrics endpoint and stderr diagnostics expose **public identifiers, sanitized build labels, numeric gauges/counters, and network/error metadata** — **not** keys, passphrases, key-ids, or the data-dir path. Basis: the two decisive emitters read firsthand (`qbind_node_build_info` via `sanitize_info_label`; `qbind_node_data_dir_free_bytes` numeric-only, "never the path"), the configured-key **count** emitter, and the framework's explicit secret-free docstrings; a type name / `Debug` derive is **not** relied on. **Bounded-review limit:** the ~25 per-subsystem `format_metrics` implementations were **not** each enumerated line-by-line (available in-tree edge, §29.5).

### 29.4 Scoped availability observation [SUPERSEDED by A24.1 §29.7 → reassessed under the §1 standard as finding **A24-F1** (STATIC-SUPPORTED/OPEN); the "not a finding" disposition below is withdrawn]

The metrics request reader applies **no request-size bound** — the request line and the header-skip loop use `read_line` with no cap on line length or header count (metrics_http.rs:393–412) — and the accept loop spawns an **unbounded number of concurrent detached** connection-handler tasks (no occupancy gate). On an **enabled** endpoint this is a per-connection memory-growth / task-growth availability surface. **Recorded as a scoped observation, not a finding**, because the endpoint is **default-disabled**, **operator-opt-in**, bound to the **operator-chosen** address (documented/example default `127.0.0.1` localhost), **GET-only**, and non-tx; reachability/severity depend on the operator enabling it, choosing a non-localhost bind, and allocator/runtime behaviour — all deployment/EXEC, unmeasured. Kin to A4-F1 (accept-path occupancy) but a **distinct owner/surface** (operator-opt-in metrics listener), **not merged**.

Server disabled.` → `disabled()`; **`Ok` + parse `Ok(addr)`** → enabled bound to **that supplied addr**. Separated: *disabled config* carries an **unused** sentinel addr `127.0.0.1:0` and yields a **no-op task** (never binds, metrics_http.rs:265–268); *enabled config* uses the **operator-supplied** addr; *actual listener binding* = `TcpListener::bind(supplied addr)` (metrics_http.rs:338); *configured bind scope* = whatever the operator supplied; *observed deployment exposure* = **unobserved**. **A24's "enabled default localhost" is WITHDRAWN** — `127.0.0.1` is only the **disabled sentinel** and a **doc example**; an **enabled** endpoint has **no default bind** (it is exactly `QBIND_METRICS_HTTP_ADDR`, which could be loopback, a LAN addr, or `0.0.0.0`). Invalid config establishes **listener non-activation**; separately, **startup continues and metrics monitoring is unavailable** (the from_env returns disabled; `main` proceeds) — this is **not** a general operational fail-closed *security* guarantee (it fails the observability feature closed, nothing more).

**(3) Request-resource + handler-lifecycle — completed; "short-lived" withdrawn.** `handle_connection` (metrics_http.rs:388–472): request line read into `request_line: String::new()` via `read_line` (grows unbounded until `\n`); headers read into `header_line: String` **reused** (`.clear()` each iteration) but each `read_line` is unbounded and the loop runs until a blank line / EOF. **Bounds, separately:** per-line length = **unbounded**; total request bytes = **no accumulator / no cap**; header count = **unbounded** (loop has no max); processing-work per request = O(1) route match. **Ordering:** the handler reads the **request line and all headers first**, **then** checks `parts.len()<2` (400) / `method!="GET"` (405) / route (404) — i.e. the full (unbounded) request is consumed **before** any method/route rejection. **Application admission/concurrency limit:** **none** (no semaphore/permit/max-conn; the accept loop `tokio::spawn`s each connection unconditionally, metrics_http.rs:357–366). **Read/write deadline:** **none** (no `set_*timeout`/`tokio::time::timeout` in metrics_http.rs — unlike the P2P path's socket timeouts). **Listener shutdown vs in-flight handlers:** `drop(metrics_shutdown_tx)` (main.rs:5462) → `shutdown_rx.changed()` → the accept loop `break`s; `metrics_handle.await` (main.rs:5463) awaits the **server task** only; the detached per-connection `tokio::spawn` handlers are **not** awaited or aborted — they run independently (and with no read deadline a stalled one is unbounded in duration). **Handle ownership/cleanup:** server task = `metrics_handle` (awaited once at shutdown); connection tasks = **detached** (handle dropped); each handler returns `Ok(())` on 200/400/404/405 after writing a response, or `Err(MetricsHttpError::Io)` (logged by the spawn wrapper) — the `TcpStream` is dropped (closed) on return either way. **`Connection: close`** expresses per-response connection-handling policy, **not** a deadline. **"Short-lived" is withdrawn** (no duration bound is established). The absence of application bounds is **not** the same as unlimited physical resources, measured memory growth, or demonstrated process failure. The A15 consensus-task supervision conclusion is **not** imported — the metrics server/connection tasks have their own owners/signals (traced here: `metrics_shutdown_tx`/`metrics_handle`).

143                    );
144                    MetricsHttpConfig { bind_addr: addr, enabled: true }
148                }
149                Err(e) => {
150                    eprintln!(
151                        "[metrics_http] WARNING: Invalid {} value '{}': {}. Server disabled.",
152                        METRICS_HTTP_ADDR_ENV, addr_str, e
153                    );
154                    Self::disabled()
155                }
156            },
157            Err(_) => {
158                // Not set - disabled by default
159                Self::disabled()
160            }
161        }
162    }

`handle_connection` (complete):
```rust
388 async fn handle_connection(
389     mut stream: TcpStream,
390     metrics: &NodeMetrics,
391     crypto_refs: &CryptoMetricsRefs,
392 ) -> Result<(), MetricsHttpError> {
394     let mut reader = BufReader::new(&mut stream);
395     let mut request_line = String::new();
398     reader.read_line(&mut request_line).await.map_err(MetricsHttpError::Io)?;
404     let mut header_line = String::new();
405     loop {
406         header_line.clear();
407         let bytes_read = reader.read_line(&mut header_line).await.map_err(MetricsHttpError::Io)?;
411         if bytes_read == 0 || header_line == "\r\n" || header_line == "\n" { break; }
414     }
417     let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
418     if parts.len() < 2 { /* 400 Bad Request */ send_response(&mut stream, 400, ...).await?; return Ok(()); }
431     let method = parts[0]; let path = parts[1];
435     if method != "GET" { /* 405 */ send_response(&mut stream, 405, ...).await?; return Ok(()); }
448     if path == "/metrics" || path == "/metrics/" {
450         let body = format_metrics_output(metrics, crypto_refs);
451         send_response(&mut stream, 200, "OK", "text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8", body.as_bytes()).await?;
459     } else { send_response(&mut stream, 404, "Not Found", "text/plain", b"Not Found").await?; }
464     Ok(())
465 }
```
(**abridged** at the `send_response(...)` argument lists 420–427 / 436–443 and the comment lines, preserving control-flow order; the reads 394–414 and the ordering 417→418→435→448 are verbatim.)

488 }
