### 35.3 Plaintext equality / difference (to actual fields)

⟨**A30.2 — the differing `Timeout.view` case alone, traced to the actual `seal` input.**⟩ The plaintext passed to `seal` is **not** merely the bincode payload — it is the output of `encode_frame` (p2p_tcp.rs:146): `discriminator(1 B) || len(u32 BE) || payload`, where `payload = bincode::serialize(&P2pMessage::Consensus(ConsensusNetMsg::Timeout(bytes)))` and `bytes = bincode::serialize(&TimeoutMsg{view, high_qc, validator_id, suite_id, signature})` (binary_consensus_loop.rs:7266). So the nesting is: **inner** `create_timeout_msg` (sets `view = engine.current_view()`) → **inner serialize** `bincode(TimeoutMsg)` → **outer** `bincode(P2pMessage enum)` → **frame** `encode_frame` (adds the discriminator + length prefix) → **plaintext to `seal`** = that frame. Under the §35.2 schedule the two emissions carry `view = V` and `view = V′`, **V ≠ V′**.

**Precise encoding premise (not "determinism"):** ⟨**A30.3 — sufficiency, not "iff":**⟩ a **distinguishable `view` encoding is a sufficient basis** for the selected content difference — if the distinct `u64` values V and V′ produce distinct `view`-field bytes at a stable position, the two framed plaintexts differ. The property relied on is that bincode's encoding of a `u64` field is **injective** (distinct `u64` ⇒ distinct 8-byte encodings) and that this field occupies a **stable position** given the rest of the message, so that changing only `view` changes the frame bytes. (This is stated as a sufficient condition for *this* witness's difference; it is **not** offered as a general "the plaintexts differ exactly when…" biconditional over all possible field combinations — other fields could also differ, and the witness does not need them to.) ⟨A30.2: **determinism alone is insufficient** — a deterministic-but-lossy encoding could map V and V′ to equal bytes; the claim rests on **injectivity/distinguishability of the `view` encoding**, which is a property of bincode's fixed-width integer encoding.⟩ Repository-owned construction (`create_timeout_msg` writing `current_view` into the `view` field; `encode_frame`'s layout) is kept **separate** from the external `bincode` encoding semantics: that the `view` byte-encoding is injective and position-stable is the **`bincode` dependency boundary** (nameable as fixed-width LE integer encoding; not re-derived). Given that premise, the two frames **differ** → a **source-supported content difference via the `view` field alone**, independent of signature randomness.

⟨A30.2: the `high_qc` and message-variant alternatives are **removed** — the `view`-difference alone suffices and is the cleanest source-admissible witness; neither alternative is separately relied on here.⟩ fips204 signing determinism is relevant **only** to the narrower sub-case where `view` (and all other fields) are **identical** and the sole candidate difference is the signature — a `fips204`/signer-adapter **dependency** question (the signer is `signer.sign_timeout_with_chain_id(...)`, binary_consensus_loop.rs:7238), not reached by the chosen witness. If all fields are equal **and** unsigned (`verification_ctx = None`), the two plaintexts are **identical** — still a reused (key, nonce) pair, but leaking nothing from the XOR. We do **not** infer a difference from two separate connections, elapsed time, or two `seal` calls — only from the distinguishable `view` encoding above.

The **recorder/replayer does not hold the session key** (distinct from a peer that already knows its own session key). | general consequence (repeated keystream+MAC key; ciphertext-XOR = plaintext-XOR) = DEP (crypto) ; key-recovery/useful-forgery = DEP + EXEC + structure premise (separate) ; **downstream acceptance → owner below** |

⟨A30.1⟩ We do **not** infer practical recovery, forgery, or consensus acceptance solely from two encryptions or the general nonce-reuse property; A11-F1's established finding is preserved with **no** claimed demonstrated recovery/forgery/acceptance.

⟨**A30.4 — the handoff's verification premise, corrected to the actual branches (reviewer item 2).**⟩ The receive-side gate for inbound `TimeoutMsg`/`NewView(TC)` is the **`verification_ctx` posture**, **not** the Proposal/Vote policy. The earlier "forged invalid-signature Timeout/NewView rejected under `Required`" wording is **withdrawn** (it transferred the `Required` Proposal/Vote-authority policy onto the Timeout/TC family, which it does not govern — Run 422 D5 split the two; `Required`/`proposal_vote_authority` bear only on Proposal/Vote, main.rs:8684–8709). The actual branches (binary:6698–6736, 6860–6926):
- **`Some(ctx)`** — `verify_timeout_msg` (timeout_verify.rs:238) / `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (350) **execute**: membership in `ctx.validators`, governance `(suite, pk)` lookup, suite-id match, and backend signature verification over the canonical preimage `(chain_id, view, high_qc, validator_id)`; a failure returns **before** `engine.on_timeout_msg` (fail-closed). So a **forged (invalid-signature)** frame is rejected **here** — but only under `Some(ctx)`.
- **`None`** — the `if let Some(ctx)` block is **skipped**: no signature check runs (the **existing A1-F1 bypass**). Admission then rests on the **separate** controls that run regardless of posture — the inbound **origin / sender-binding** check (Run 418) and `engine.on_timeout_msg`'s own logical checks (`from == timeout.validator_id`; `timeout.view ≥ current_view` else stale-dropped; accumulator membership, basic:3195–3230). Origin admission and logical validation are **not** the signature gate.

Transport vs consensus signatures: an s2c frame is **AEAD-authenticated at the transport layer** (ChaCha20-Poly1305, server→client), which is **distinct** from the **consensus signatures embedded in the `TimeoutMsg`/TC evidence**. **Lacking the consensus signing keys does not imply every transport-level forgery invalidates those embedded signatures.** ⟨**A31.1 — replaces "a replayed genuine frame passes `verify_timeout_msg` even under `Some(ctx)`":**⟩ a replayed genuine frame carries a signature that was valid in its **capture** context, but **that does not automatically pass the current receiving-context verifier** — under `Some(ctx)` `verify_timeout_msg` re-checks membership in the receiver's **current** `ctx.validators`, the governance `(suite, pk)` for that validator, the suite-id, and the signature over a preimage that includes the receiver's **current `chain_id`**; a replayed frame passes **only if** those current inputs still match the capture context (e.g. same chain-id, same validator set and key, not rotated/revoked), and is rejected otherwise. The TC **target-view** boundary remains the separate **A1-F2** unsigned surface (the per-timeout signatures cover each timeout's own `view`, not an independent bound on the certificate's target view), classified as A1-F2. These receiving-context checks are **CONS-1's** to adjudicate once a message reaches the admission boundary; TRN-1b does not resolve them.

**Which cases existing traces answer vs. what remains assigned (reviewer item 2):**
- **Answered now (reused evidence):** **part (a) forged-invalid-signature** admission — rejected by `verify_timeout_msg`'s signature step **under `Some(ctx)`**; **under `None`** the signature is not checked (A1-F1), and only origin + logical checks apply. The recorder/replayer **cannot mint** a new valid consensus signature (no keys).
- **Remains assigned to `OBL-CONS-1` (UNPERFORMED here):** **part (b) replayed valid-signature** admission. ⟨**A31 correction:** a signature that was valid in its **original** context does **not** establish validity under the **receiving** context — the receiving-side verification still re-applies, over the receiver's current inputs, the **key / suite-id / domain (`chain_id` in the preimage) / validator-set membership / signature** checks (`verify_timeout_msg`/`verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`, under `Some(ctx)`), which can reject a replayed frame if the current `ctx.validators`, governance key, suite, or chain-id differ from the capture context. So the admission question is admit-or-reject across the **full** set — those receiving-context crypto checks **together with** the non-crypto controls (origin/sender-binding; `from == validator_id`; `view`-staleness/bounds; accumulator dedup/membership; TC `two_thirds_vp` evidence; the A1-F2 unsigned target-view boundary) — **not** "the signature is already valid so only non-crypto controls remain." Determining that verdict is the handoff.⟩

**Downstream owner + audit handoff (not a remediation authorization):** one owner — **`OBL-CONS-1`** (A1-F1, §4; inbound Timeout/TC admission `verify_timeout_msg` / `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` + the `handle_inbound_consensus_msg` Timeout/NewView arms), gap **E01**, with **`OBL-TRN-1b`** (transport-level replay/freshness) and the A1-F1 finding as **dependencies** (not co-owners). **Stopping criterion:** reach an **admit-or-reject** determination from the full admission set above (signature/verifier dispatch where posture-applicable, suite-id, `view` bounds/monotonicity, validator-set membership, TC quorum/weight, dedup/freshness) — **not** solely the presence/absence of a freshness check. - `SecureChannelAsync::send` (verbatim, secure_channel.rs:830–849):

```rust
    pub async fn send(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<(), AsyncChannelError> {
        let (response_tx, response_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();

        let cmd = WriteCommand::Send {
            data: plaintext.to_vec(),
            response: response_tx,
        };

        // Send command to writer worker
        self.write_tx
            .send(cmd)
            .await
            .map_err(|_| AsyncChannelError::ChannelClosed)?;

        // Wait for completion
        response_rx
            .await
            .map_err(|_| AsyncChannelError::ChannelClosed)?
            .map_err(AsyncChannelError::Channel)
    }
```

```rust
    pub fn encrypt_app(&mut self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, NetError> {
        let session = match &mut self.state {
            ConnectionState::Established(ref mut sess) => sess,
            ConnectionState::Handshaking => {
                return Err(NetError::Protocol(
                    "encrypt_app called before handshake complete",
                ));
            }
        };

        let frame: TransportFrame = match self.side {
            HandshakeSide::Client => encrypt_app_frame(&mut session.c2s, plaintext)?,
            HandshakeSide::Server => encrypt_app_frame(&mut session.s2c, plaintext)?,
        };

        frame.encode()
    }
```

- `seal` + `next_nonce` (verbatim, session.rs:68–83; the counter advances in `next_nonce` **before** the backend `aead.seal`):

```rust
    fn next_nonce(&mut self) -> Result<[u8; 12], NetError> {
        let counter = self.counter;
        if counter == u64::MAX {
            return Err(NetError::NonceOverflow);
        }
        self.counter = self.counter.wrapping_add(1);
        Ok(make_nonce(self.flag, &self.session_id, counter))
    }

    pub fn seal(&mut self, aad: &[u8], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, NetError> {
        let nonce = self.next_nonce()?;
        self.aead
            .seal(self.key.as_bytes(), &nonce, aad, plaintext)
            .map_err(|_| NetError::Aead("encrypt failed"))
    }
```

pub fn encrypt_app_frame(
    direction: &mut AeadDirection,
    plaintext: &[u8],
) -> Result<TransportFrame, NetError> {
    let ciphertext = direction.seal(APP_FRAME_AAD, plaintext)?;

        msg_type: TRANSPORT_TYPE_APP_MESSAGE,
        ciphertext,
    })
}

- `encode_frame` (verbatim, p2p_tcp.rs:146–172 — the plaintext handed to `seal` is this framed buffer, not the bare bincode payload):

```rust
fn encode_frame(msg: &P2pMessage) -> Result<Vec<u8>, P2pTransportError> {
    let (discriminator, payload) = match msg {
        P2pMessage::Consensus(_) => {
            let payload =
                bincode::serialize(&msg).map_err(|e| P2pTransportError::Encoding(e.to_string()))?;
            (DISCRIMINATOR_CONSENSUS, payload)
        }
        P2pMessage::Dag(_) => { /* … DISCRIMINATOR_DAG … */ unreachable!() }
        P2pMessage::Control(_) => { /* … DISCRIMINATOR_CONTROL … */ unreachable!() }
    };

    let len = payload.len() as u32;
    let mut frame = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 4 + payload.len());
    frame.push(discriminator);
    frame.extend_from_slice(&len.to_be_bytes());
    frame.extend_from_slice(&payload);

    Ok(frame)
}
```
(**ABRIDGED** — the `Dag`/`Control` arms' bodies are elided to `/* … */ unreachable!()` placeholders; only the `Consensus` arm is exercised by the witness. The `discriminator` + `len`-prefix framing is complete.)

- `on_timeout_certificate` view transition + flag reset (verbatim, basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3256–3302):

```rust
    pub fn on_timeout_certificate(
        &mut self,
        tc: &TimeoutCertificate<[u8; 32]>,
    ) -> Result<u64, TimeoutValidationError> {
        // Validate the TC
        tc.validate(self.state.validators())?;

        // Only process TCs for views > current_view
        if tc.view <= self.current_view {
            return Ok(self.current_view);
        }

        if let Some(ref tc_high_qc) = tc.high_qc {
            let should_update = match self.state.locked_qc() {
                None => true,
                Some(locked) => tc_high_qc.view > locked.view,
            };
            if should_update {
                self.state.set_locked_qc(tc_high_qc.clone());
            }
        }

        let from_view = self.current_view;
        let to_view = tc.view;
        self.record_view_duration_internal(from_view, to_view);
        self.record_progress_view_change_internal(from_view, to_view);

        self.current_view = to_view;
        self.proposed_in_view = false;
        self.voted_in_view = false;
        self.timeout_emitted_in_view = false;
        self.last_view_start_instant = Some(Instant::now());
        self.timeout_accumulator.clear_view(tc.timeout_view);

        Ok(to_view)
    }
```

### 35.9 A30.3 — self-quorum witness resolution + receiving-obligation reconciliation (summary + git observations, START = END identical)

A30.3 resolves the self-quorum witness against the complete production leader tick and completes the OBL-CONS-1 handoff bookkeeping; firsthand `ef99e29`, register/excerpt review, not independent checkout verification. **Bounded; no new finding.**

**(1 witness tested against the real tick).** The full production tick is `do_leader_tick` → `try_propose` → `on_leader_step` (which internally self-votes via `self.state.on_vote`) → the immediate-QC check → `maybe_emit_view_timeout`, in that order (binary_consensus_loop.rs: `do_leader_tick` at 2902/3056 before `maybe_emit_view_timeout` at 2961/3108; `try_propose` at 3333). The validator-set size is **N = `static_peers.len() + 1`** (configured static peers + self). At **N = 1** one vote **is** the quorum: `on_leader_step` forms a QC and calls **`self.advance_view()` within the same tick, before the timeout check** (basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2359–2370, "If a QC was formed immediately (e.g., single node), record and advance view"); `advance_view` resets `timeout_emitted_in_view` (basic:1794–1807). The progress observation therefore always sees an advance and **no Timeout ever fires at N = 1** → the **N = 1 self-quorum witness is WITHDRAWN**. A11-F1 and the other nonce-reuse schedules are **not** withdrawn.

**(2 one sufficient alternative witness).** The installed witness is the **N ≥ 2** case: the leader self-vote returns `Ok(None)` (one vote < quorum ⇒ no QC ⇒ no `advance_view`), view V stalls, and after `threshold_ticks` the five Timeout gates pass → `Timeout(V)`. The view then advances **only** by a **validated quorum `TimeoutCertificate` built from the *other* validators' legitimate signed timeouts** (normal view-change machinery) via `on_timeout_certificate` (`tc.validate(self.state.validators())?` → `current_view = tc.view` + `timeout_emitted_in_view = false`, basic:3256–3302), reached by **local accumulation** (`apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view` :7339) or an **inbound verified `NewView(TC)`** (:6931); the local route then broadcasts `NewView(V)`. The replayed-transcript connection C2 registers **after** the `NewView(V)` broadcast and **before** `Timeout(V′)` (a non-empty ≥`threshold_ticks` window); V′ stalls → `Timeout(V′)`. Both emissions sit at a fresh s2c counter 0 under the reused key+`session_id` (precondition: no preceding counter-consuming `seal` attempt on each connection). Result: two s2c frames at the **same (key, nonce@0)** carrying `Timeout(V)` vs `Timeout(V′)`, V ≠ V′. The NewView of the transition and the catch-up/raw-0x05 producers are accounted as competing s2c producers; enqueue order is kept separate from async encryption/write; the unresolved edges are source-admissible ordering + runtime scheduling/I/O (EXEC E19), not unread source.

**(3 OBL-CONS-1 handoff bookkeeping).** The §35.4 downstream-acceptance handoff is split into **part (a)** — a **forged (invalid-signature)** s2c Timeout/NewView — which **corresponds to the existing A1-F1 verification trace** (such frames are rejected fail-closed under `Required`; the recorder/replayer lacks consensus signing keys), and **part (b)** — a **replayed valid-signature** frame recorded off the wire and re-injected — whose inbound **dedup / view-bounds / membership / TC-quorum / freshness** admission is **UNPERFORMED**. Part (b) is assigned to exactly one owner **`OBL-CONS-1`** (A1-F1, §4; gap **E01**; deps **`OBL-TRN-1b`** + A1-F1), with entrypoints `verify_timeout_msg` / `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` + the inbound Timeout/NewView handlers, and a **stopping criterion = reach an admit-or-reject determination from the full inbound check set, not merely confirm a freshness check's presence/absence**. The OBL-CONS-1 row no longer reads "remaining: none / SR-DONE": it is **SR-DONE (ctx-absence slice) · SR-PENDING (part-(b) sub-question, unperformed)**. `OBL-TRN-1b` keeps **only** the transport-level replay/freshness dependency; its earlier **freshness-only stopping criterion is REMOVED** (replaced by a transport admit-or-reject criterion). **No downstream review is started here** (the A30.3 scope bars beginning OBL-TRN-1b or the acceptance review).

**(4 evidence + current-claim reconciliation).** §35.5 now supplies the **tick-order / `on_leader_step` self-vote + `if Ok(Some(_qc)) advance_view` / `advance_view` flag-reset** excerpts (ABRIDGED where marked); `encode_frame` and the shortened `NewView` excerpt remain labeled **ABRIDGED**. ### 35.10 A30.4 — one concrete emission witness + coverage-ledger normalization (summary + git observations, START = END identical)

## 36. A31 — OBL-TRN-1b: dialer lifecycle, revocation propagation and remaining transport boundaries (read-only source; v1.04)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, register/excerpt review (read-only `git show`/`git grep`), not independent checkout verification. One bounded obligation (OBL-TRN-1b), reusing A2/A6/A11/A26/A27; governance/ratification **acceptance-gate internals** are kept with **OBL-GOV-2** and durable sequence/marker **persistence** with its existing owners (recorded as premises, not re-audited). **No new finding forced.**

### 36.1 Production caller / configuration inventory

**Outbound dial path (production, P2P mode `run_p2p_node`):** `start()` (p2p_tcp.rs:929) — for each `config.static_peers` spawns one task `dial_with_retry(peer_addr, policy)` (p2p_tcp.rs:951–957) → `dial_with_retry` (p2p_tcp.rs:2058) loops `dial_once` up to `policy.max_attempts`, backing off on `is_transient_dial_error`, **returning on the first success** or on give-up → `dial_once` (p2p_tcp.rs:1935): TCP connect → build per-peer `client_cfg` from `self.client_cfg` + `peer_kem_pk_overrides`/`peer_validator_id_overrides` (p2p_tcp.rs:1949–1975; absent override ⇒ WARN, single-validator/smoke only) → `connect_kemtls_async_with_server_identity` (KEMTLS handshake) → **Run 418 origin binding**: derive `AuthenticatedConsensusOrigin` from the **verified server cert identity** matched against `outbound_consensus_origins` (reject on `!authenticated || !node_match || !vid_match`, p2p_tcp.rs:1996–2024; `None` expected ⇒ origin `None`) → `spawn_peer_handlers` (p2p_tcp.rs:1362) which `peers.write().insert(node_id, conn)` (p2p_tcp.rs:1426).

**Inbound accept path:** `spawn_accept_loop` (p2p_tcp.rs:962) → per-accept connection-rate gate (`abuse_dos_runtime.should_admit`) → KEMTLS accept handshake → `spawn_peer_handlers` (same registry insert).

**Classification (positive-controlled construction/caller chains):**
| Path | Kind | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start`→`dial_with_retry`→`dial_once`→`spawn_peer_handlers` | **production (P2P)** | spawned from `start()` per static peer; `run_p2p_node` builds `TcpKemTlsP2pService` via `P2pNodeBuilder` (main.rs:6339) |
| `dial_peer` (p2p_tcp.rs:1225) | **dead** (superseded) | no non-doc caller in scope (A26 §31: production site is `dial_once`); textually mirrored by `dial_once` |
| `NetService`/`PeerManager`/`ConsensusNode`/`Peer::recv_msg` (net_service.rs:129, peer_manager.rs:90/113, peer.rs:90) | **sim/test-only** | constructed only in `NodeHotstuffHarness::new` (hotstuff_node_sim.rs:714/721); callers are `tests/async_runner_tests.rs` + `examples/*`; `main.rs` names `NodeHotstuffHarness` only in doc comments (5484/5568/5616) — **no production construction** |
| `LoopbackNetService` / `MockConsensusNetService` | test/harness | load_harness.rs / consensus_net_worker tests |
| SIGHUP live-reload task (main.rs:8868/9195/9209) | **production, runtime-gated** | gated on `--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-enabled` + `--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-path` (main.rs:8889–8890) |
| process-start reload-apply (main.rs:4222/4453) | **production, runtime-gated** | gated on `--p2p-trust-bundle-reload-apply-*`; wires the **no-op** evictor (runs before P2P start) |

**Lifecycle facts (A31; ⟨A31.1⟩ grounded in callers/ownership, not the scope comment alone):** (i) `dial_with_retry` is **initial-dial only** — the loop (p2p_tcp.rs:2061) `return`s once `dial_once` succeeds, it is **spawned exactly once per static peer** inside `start()` (p2p_tcp.rs:951–957), and **no inspected caller re-invokes `dial_with_retry`/`dial_once` on connection loss and no supervisor respawns the per-peer dial task** — this "no automatic redial" rests on the **caller/ownership evidence** (the single spawn site + the read/write loops that merely exit); the scope comment p2p_tcp.rs:264 ("reconnect/churn out of scope") is corroboration, not the basis. (ii) ⟨**A31.1 — separate the teardown events (A6-F1/A27 §32):**⟩ a `read_loop` `break` (p2p_tcp.rs:1519/1527/1531) ends only the **async read task**; it does **not** by itself establish `write_loop` termination, registry (`peers`) removal, or socket release. The blocking `reader_worker`/`writer_worker` (secure_channel.rs:631/637) each hold an `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>` strong reference; **local socket release follows destruction of the *final* strong `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>` owner** (both workers gone), and a **fatal reader's `blocking_send(Err(..))` error-delivery can block before that worker exits** (A29.1/A27 §32). So **cancellation request (`abort()`), async-task completion, blocking-worker destruction, and socket release are four distinct events**; a dropped/evicted peer is **not** re-dialed by this node (re-establishment would be the peer's inbound dial or a fresh connection).

### 36.2 Synchronous-path disposition (inherited §34.1 / A29.2 question — RESOLVED)

The synchronous `NetService` → `PeerManager::recv_from_any` → `Peer::recv_msg` path is **production-unreachable**: `NetService::new` has exactly one non-doc, non-mock construction (`hotstuff_node_sim.rs:721`, inside `NodeHotstuffHarness::new`), whose only callers are integration tests and examples; `main()`/`run_p2p_node`/`run_local_mesh_node` never construct it (doc-comment references only). **Bounded exclusion established with caller evidence.** For completeness, the inherited "`Peer::recv_msg` error propagation / caller continuation" question is answered on the sim path: `recv_msg` (peer.rs:90) = `channel.recv_app()?` then `NetMessage::decode_from_slice(..)?`, propagating `ChannelError`; the caller `recv_from_any`/`try_recv_from_any` (peer_manager.rs:162/191) maps any non-`WouldBlock`/`TimedOut` error to `PeerManagerError::Channel` ("fatal for now") — but this governs only the **sim** harness, not production transport (production uses the async `read_loop`→`inbound_tx` demux, §36.5).

### 36.3 Trust / revocation propagation (startup config + accepted live updates)

⟨**A31.1 — this subsection is substantiated per-direction; the A31 claim that "each dial/accept reads the live snapshot via the closures" is corrected: the two directions are ASYMMETRIC.**⟩ Active state: `LivePqcTrustState { inner: Arc<RwLock<Arc<LivePqcTrustSnapshot>>> }` (pqc_live_trust.rs:339, `#[derive(Clone)]` → a clone bumps the **one** `inner` Arc); the snapshot holds active roots + `revoked_root_ids` + `revoked_leaf_fingerprints`. The builder holds one `self.pqc_live_trust` (p2p_node_builder.rs:861, from `with_live_pqc_trust`, main.rs:7721) and **one** `inner` RwLock backs every live consumer below.

**Field-provenance table (per direction; construction → config field → capture → handshake lookup/check → refusal → live vs static):**
| Consumer | Direction (this node's role) | Config field | Builder construction / capture | Handshake lookup/check + refusal | Live-snapshot-backed? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **outbound server-ROOT** | **dial** (KEMTLS **client**) | `ClientHandshakeConfig.peer_root_network_pk: Vec<u8>` (handshake.rs:272) — **a single static key, NOT a resolver; the client cfg has no root-resolver field** | `root_network_pk = pqc_root_config.trusted_roots.first().root_pk` (p2p_node_builder.rs:1956–1964) → installed `peer_root_network_pk: root_network_pk.clone()` (:2165) — from `pqc_root_config`, **not** `pqc_live_trust` | `verify_delegation_cert(crypto, &delegation_cert, &self.cfg.peer_root_network_pk)` (handshake.rs:441–445). ⟨**A31.2 — correct the earlier "unknown/revoked root ⇒ signature-verify failure":**⟩ this verifies the cert's signature against the **single configured static key**; an **unknown** root (cert signed by a key ≠ the configured one) fails signature verification (`NetError::KeySchedule`), **but** a cert **validly signed under the configured root** still **passes** — a subsequent **live root-level revocation does NOT change `peer_root_network_pk`**, so such a cert is **not** rejected on the dial path (no "untrusted root"/`active_roots` branch exists on the client cfg) | **STATIC (construction-time) — NOT live; a root revoked by a live reload does NOT propagate to the dial direction (see §36.3a)** |
| **outbound server-LEAF revocation** | dial (client) | `ClientHandshakeConfig.leaf_cert_revocations: Option<LeafCertRevocationList>` (handshake.rs:296) | the **same** `LeafCertRevocationList` closure (below), cloned into the client cfg (p2p_node_builder.rs:2169) | `rev_list.is_revoked(fp)` → `Err(ClientCertInvalid("cert revoked"))` (handshake.rs:482–488) | **LIVE** (shared closure → `is_leaf_revoked`) |
| **inbound client-ROOT** | **accept** (KEMTLS **server**) | `ServerHandshakeConfig.trusted_client_roots: Option<TrustedClientRoots>` (handshake.rs:627) | `TrustedClientRoots::new(<closure over root_key_id → live.lookup_active_root_pk>)` capturing `self.pqc_live_trust.clone()` (p2p_node_builder.rs:2036–2044), installed into the server cfg | `roots.lookup(&cert.root_key_id)` → `Some(pk)` else `Err(ClientCertInvalid("untrusted root"))` (handshake.rs:1156–1165); `lookup_active_root_pk` checks `revoked_root_ids` then `active_roots` | **LIVE** (fail-closed `None`/untrusted on lock poison) |
| **inbound client-LEAF revocation** | accept (server) | `ServerHandshakeConfig.leaf_cert_revocations` (handshake.rs:642) | the same `LeafCertRevocationList::new(active_count, <closure over fp → live_for_closure.is_leaf_revoked>)` (p2p_node_builder.rs:2131–2138), installed into the server cfg | `rev_list.is_revoked(fp)` → `Err(ClientCertInvalid("cert revoked"))` (handshake.rs:1206–1212) | **LIVE** (fail-closed `true`/revoked on lock poison) |
| **per-peer KEM-key overrides** | dial (client) | `peer_kem_pk_overrides: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>>>` (p2p_tcp.rs:464) | setter `set_peer_kem_pk_overrides` (p2p_tcp.rs:636) — **only caller is `build()`** (p2p_node_builder.rs:1462) | read `.read().get(&peer_addr)` per dial, into `cfg.peer_kem_pk` (p2p_tcp.rs:1954–1962) | **construction-populated** (mechanism is `RwLock` so live-*capable*, but **no reload path rewrites it**) |
| **authenticated-origin / binding** | dial + accept | `outbound_consensus_origins` (p2p_tcp.rs:569) + `inbound_consensus_origin_resolver` (p2p_tcp.rs:559) | setters (p2p_tcp.rs:692/682) — **only caller is `build()`** (p2p_node_builder.rs:1682/1661) | dial reads `.read().get(&peer_addr)` → Run-418 verified-identity match, refusal `P2pTransportError::Handshake` (p2p_tcp.rs:1996–2024); accept reads the resolver at :1192 | **construction-populated** (live-capable mechanism, not reload-refreshed) |

**Key asymmetry (source-established, A31.1; dispositioned under §1 in §36.3a):** live trust-reload revocation propagates to **inbound client-root**, **inbound client-leaf** and **outbound server-leaf** (all read the shared snapshot on each new handshake), but **NOT to outbound server-root** (static `peer_root_network_pk`, refreshed only by a restart with a new `pqc_root_config`) nor to the per-peer KEM overrides / origin maps (construction-populated). "Revocation" = **static leaf-fingerprint set + active-root set** from the snapshot; **no CRL/OCSP/time-based** revocation. The evidence-derived classification of this asymmetry — invariant, same-anchor correspondence, callable path, remaining controls, bounded consequence — is in **§36.3a**; ⟨**A31.3**⟩ it is **resolved as a source-supported invariant violation and promoted to finding A31-F1** (the earlier "operator's call" and "not promoted pending a missing link" hedges are **withdrawn**).

**Snapshot coherence (source-established, A31.1 — an atomic swap does NOT give one coherent per-handshake snapshot):** the config captures the `LivePqcTrustState` **handle** (the RwLock), not a snapshot; every check re-enters `snapshot()` which takes its **own** `inner.read()` and clones a fresh `Arc` (`lookup_active_root_pk`/`is_leaf_revoked` wrappers, pqc_live_trust.rs:404–429 → `snapshot()` :389–396). So within one **inbound** handshake the root-lookup and the leaf-revocation check are **two independent reads** and can observe **different snapshots** if `swap_snapshot` interleaves; and the swap does **not** refresh the immutable config fields (outbound root, overrides, origins, suite ids) nor retroactively re-check a **handshake already in progress** (the checks already ran under whatever snapshot was current then). These are examined facts, not unread edges.

| state allocation affected | **constructs** the one `LivePqcTrustState` (initial snapshot) **and** the static handshake-config fields (`peer_root_network_pk` from `trusted_roots.first()`, overrides, origins) | ⟨**A31.3 — corrected:**⟩ builds a **fresh, throwaway** `Arc<LivePqcTrustState>` (`initialize_from_loaded_bundle`, main.rs:4450–4453) and `swap`s **that** (never the node's); **no node handshake config is constructed** | **`swap_snapshot`** on the **running node's** `LivePqcTrustState` (the one shared with the live verifiers); static config fields **not rebuilt** |
| continuation after apply (⟨A31.3⟩; ⟨A31.4⟩ exits made exact) | continues into normal node startup (`run_p2p_node`/`run_local_mesh_node`) | **`std::process::exit`** on every branch — success `exit(0)` main.rs:4781, failure `exit(1)` main.rs:4797/4808 (earlier fail-closed exits 4448/4543/4607/4655/4726/4744) — a **command mode that does NOT run the node**; the running node reaches any updated trust input only on a **subsequent restart** (route 1), which **reconstructs** `peer_root_network_pk` from its **actual startup inputs** (CLI `--p2p-trusted-root` + the bundle at the configured path) — reconstruction does **not** guarantee removal of R (⟨A31.4⟩; see §36.3a-2) | the node keeps running; no restart |
| config construction timing | this **is** the construction (the static outbound root / overrides / origins are frozen here) | **not applicable** — this command never constructs the node's handshake configs (it exits); only a later restart (route 1) does | configs were already constructed at the prior route-1 startup; this route mutates only the live snapshot |
| eviction | n/a (no sessions yet; nothing to evict) | evictor = **`NoActiveSessionsEvictor` NO-OP** (main.rs:4453) → `EvictionReport(0,0,0)`; and no sessions exist pre-start anyway | evictor = **real `TcpKemTlsP2pService`** (main.rs:8621) → `evict_all_sessions(TrustBundleReloadApply)` drains the **current `peers` registry** (`std::mem::take`, p2p_tcp.rs:1796–1800) |
| eviction requested vs completed (A27 qualifications) | n/a | n/a (no-op) | `abort()` is a cancellation **request**; socket release follows destruction of the **final strong `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>` owner** (both blocking workers gone), and a fatal reader's `blocking_send(Err)` can block first — so the `EvictionReport(failed=0)` does **not** establish completed revocation enforcement per live socket (A27 §32 EXEC(E14)). **A6-F1:** a same-NodeId-**displaced** session (prior `PeerConnection` discarded at the `peers.insert`, p2p_tcp.rs:1426) is not in `peers` and is **not reached**; a **handshake in progress** (not yet inserted) is likewise not evicted |
| effect on subsequent handshakes | sets the baseline for all three verifiers | **none in this process** — the command `std::process::exit`s (`main.rs:4781` on apply success / `4797`/`4808` on failure; earlier fail-closed exits `4448`/`4543`/`4607`/`4655`/`4726`/`4744`) **before any P2P listener or dialer is created** (no `run_p2p_node`); any later node start is a fresh **route (1)** startup from separately-selected inputs | the **live** verifiers (inbound client-root/leaf, outbound server-leaf) see the swapped snapshot on the next handshake **on the running node**; the **static** outbound server-root + overrides/origins are **unchanged** |
| reconnect after eviction | n/a | n/a | **none** (no reconnect-after-drop, §36.1); an evicted peer is not re-dialed |

Pipeline order for (2)/(3) (pqc_trust_reload.rs:1075–1100): validate → snapshot_active → **swap_trust_state** → **evict_sessions** (rollback on failure) → sequence commit. Durable sequence/marker persistence = **OBL-STO-2a (available-source handoff)**; candidate validation internals = **OBL-GOV-2 (available-source handoff)**.

**⟨A31.2⟩ "No stale cache" scoped:** the "each handshake reads the current snapshot" property holds **only for the live-backed fields** (inbound client-root via `lookup_active_root_pk`; inbound + outbound leaf via `is_leaf_revoked`) — each re-reads the snapshot per check (so these have no stale per-dial cache, but also no coherent per-handshake snapshot). It does **not** hold for the **static outbound `peer_root_network_pk`** or the construction-populated `peer_kem_pk_overrides` / `outbound_consensus_origins`, which are frozen at route (1) and are effectively a **stale (construction-time) trust input** with respect to a **route (3)** live apply (route (2) never reaches a running node — it `exit`s). The previous snapshot returned by `swap_snapshot` is retained only for rollback (pqc_trust_reload.rs:1091 on eviction failure).

### 36.3a Outbound-root revocation asymmetry — §1-standard disposition (⟨A31.2⟩ opened; ⟨A31.3⟩ resolved → **finding A31-F1 (OPEN)**)

Applying the register's §1 standard to the source result "outbound server-cert verification uses construction-time `peer_root_network_pk`, while live root revocation affects only the inbound root resolver (and leaf-revocation on both directions)":

**Applicable invariant.** (a) *Pinned requirement:* the trust-anchor model's §5.6 revocation semantics govern **bundle-signing keys** (the ratification layer, OBL-GOV-2), not the transport cert root, so it does not directly bind this path. (b) *Selected-configuration contract:* the **Run-074 live-reload** evidence states its design as "Run 071 `LivePqcTrustState` **shared with every handshake verifier (no second trust set, no parallel networking architecture)**" and the Run-070/072 apply pipeline's purpose is that a validated trust/revocation update **takes effect on the running node** (incl. Run-072 eviction of existing sessions). (c) *Implemented control's purpose:* live revocation is meant to stop the node trusting the revoked anchor for its handshake trust decisions. The derived invariant: **a live-applied root-level revocation should make the node stop trusting certificates chaining to that root for its handshake trust decisions.**

**⟨A31.3⟩ Exact contract location + scope.** `docs/devnet/QBIND_DEVNET_EVIDENCE_RUN_074.md:17`, inside the numbered list describing what the SIGHUP handler "Drives the validated candidate through" (item 3, "against the **running node's live handles**"): *"Run 071 `LivePqcTrustState` shared with every handshake verifier (no second trust set, no parallel networking architecture);"*. Scope: the live-reload applies to the **one** `LivePqcTrustState` that the node's handshake verifiers read — the evidence states this as an architectural property ("no second trust set") of the running node, with **no stated exception** for any particular verifier/direction. There is no documented carve-out for the outbound server-root.

**⟨A31.3⟩ Same-anchor identity correspondence (confirmed — the two "roots" are the same anchor).** `peer_root_network_pk` = `pqc_config.trusted_roots.first().root_pk` (p2p_node_builder.rs:1959–1964; `pqc_config.trusted_roots = trusted_roots.clone()`, main.rs:7628). That `trusted_roots` vec is the CLI `--p2p-trusted-root` specs **merged with the loaded bundle's `active_roots`**, deduped by `root_key_id` (main.rs:7201–7207: `for r in &loaded.active_roots { if !seen.contains(root_key_id) { trusted_roots.push(r) } }`). The live state is built from the **same** bundle: `LivePqcTrustState::initialize_from_loaded_bundle` sets `active_roots: loaded.active_roots.clone()` (pqc_live_trust.rs:199). A **root-level** revocation (Run 050) removes a root (by `root_key_id`) from a reloaded bundle's `active_roots` (and/or lists it in `revoked_root_ids`), so the live snapshot's `active_roots` no longer contains it (inbound `lookup_active_root_pk` → `None` → "untrusted root"). When the revoked `root_key_id` is the one at `trusted_roots.first()`, the static `peer_root_network_pk` retains that id's `root_pk` and is **not** rebuilt by `swap_snapshot`. ⟨**A31.4 scope correction** — supersedes the earlier general inference here⟩ The merge dedups **by `root_key_id` only** (key *bytes* are never compared, and a CLI entry sharing an id would win), so "same id" does **not** by itself imply "same key bytes / same bundle origin" — the earlier parenthetical to that effect is withdrawn. The **bit-exact** same-anchor correspondence (static R ≡ the initial live entry in both `root_key_id` **and** key bytes) is established only for the **sufficient configuration of §36.3a-2** (DevNet, `--p2p-trust-bundle` + **empty** `--p2p-trusted-root` ⇒ `trusted_roots.first() == loaded.active_roots[0]`); A31-F1 is stated on that sufficient case. In that configuration the outbound verify continues to accept certs under the **same anchor** the operator just revoked. (Scope note: `peer_root_network_pk` is only `first()` — the outbound dial path verifies against a **single** root regardless of the full `active_roots` set; the finding concerns live-revocation of that first anchor.)

**Source-supported deviation.** The **outbound** server-root decision is verified against the **static** `peer_root_network_pk` (handshake.rs:272/441–445), built once from `pqc_root_config.trusted_roots.first()` (p2p_node_builder.rs:1956–1964) and **not** rebuilt by `swap_snapshot`. So a cert **validly signed under the configured root** continues to pass the outbound verify **after** a live root-level revocation — this is a **"second trust set"** for the outbound-root decision, in tension with the Run-074 "no second trust set / every handshake verifier" wording. (The inbound root resolver and the bidirectional leaf-revocation **do** honor the live snapshot.)

**Callable path + prerequisites.** Path: a dial → `ClientHandshake::handle_server_accept` → `verify_delegation_cert(cert, &self.cfg.peer_root_network_pk)` → **pass** for a cert under the (now live-revoked) root. Prerequisites: (i) the **SIGHUP live-reload** route armed on the running node — `--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-path <PATH>` + `--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-enabled` (`main.rs:4838`; handler `spawn_run074_live_reload_task`, `main.rs:8868`), **not** the process-start reload-apply command flags (those exit before the node runs); (ii) a **root-level** revocation (`leaf_cert_fingerprint = None`, Run 050/052) delivered to the running node via that **route (3)** SIGHUP apply (route (2) cannot deliver a revocation to a running node — it `exit`s); (iii) this node **dials/retries** a configured static peer; (iv) the presented leaf is **not individually leaf-revoked**.

**Remaining controls on the root-only case (do NOT infer acceptance from the missing root lookup alone).** A root-only revocation where the presented leaf is not individually revoked is still subject to: `verify_delegation_cert`'s **validity-window + suite** checks; the **leaf-revocation** check (which **passes** here, leaf not listed); and the **Run-418 outbound origin binding** — ⟨**A31.3 — what Run-418 actually compares:**⟩ if `outbound_consensus_origins` is configured for the peer, `dial_once` requires the **verified server identity** (the `node_id` derived from the verified cert + the `validator_id` parsed from the cert's `validator_id` field) to **equal** the configured mapping's `node_id`+`validator_id`, else returns `Err` (p2p_tcp.rs:2002–2024). This is an **identifier-equality** check against the configured mapping; it is **not** an independent key-possession proof beyond what the KEMTLS handshake + the delegation-cert-signature-chain-to-`peer_root_network_pk` already establish. **A sufficient case for the revocation question does not need an impersonation attack:** the **configured peer itself**, whose root `root_key_id` was just live-revoked (e.g. its root key compromised), still presents a delegation cert that chains to that root (identifier matches, signature verifies under the static `peer_root_network_pk`) → the node **continues to establish/trust the outbound session with that peer** despite the live revocation. (The identifier-match does constrain which `node_id`/`validator_id` is accepted; it does not re-introduce the revoked-root check.)

**Initial-dial-only lifecycle route (source-supported; no invented reconnection).** For an **already-established** outbound session, route (3) **evicts** it; ⟨**A31.3 — corrected from "the connection stays down":**⟩ the inspected local caller schedules **no replacement dial** after eviction (the per-peer `dial_with_retry` task already returned on its initial success and is not re-spawned, §36.1) — registry eviction, cancellation completion, and final-socket-owner release remain **separate** events (A27), so "no re-trust there" means "no local caller re-dials," not a claim about the socket's teardown timing. The source-supported window where the static root is evaluated **after** a revocation is: (α) a `dial_with_retry` task **still retrying** an initial dial (peer unreachable at startup; each `dial_once` rebuilds `client_cfg` from the static `self.client_cfg`, so the retry re-reads the stale root), bounded by `policy.max_attempts`; and (β) a **handshake in progress** when the swap lands (its static-root check already ran / runs under the frozen field). No automatic reconnection is asserted.

**Coverage of the cited applicability constraints / possible controls.** `static_peers` bounds the **dial surface** to configured addresses (so this is not "trust an arbitrary server"); live **leaf-revocation** catches **individually-revoked leaves** outbound. **Neither establishes containment of every certificate authorized by a revoked root:** a leaf validly issued under a revoked root that is not itself on the leaf-revocation list is caught by neither (static root still verifies it; leaf not listed).

**⟨A31.3⟩ Process-start route does not change this (resolves the earlier route-2 framing).** The process-start `--p2p-trust-bundle-reload-apply-*` path is a **standalone command mode** that builds a **fresh throwaway** `LivePqcTrustState` (`Arc::new(LivePqcTrustState::initialize_from_loaded_bundle(&baseline_loaded))`, main.rs:4450–4453) with the `NoActiveSessionsEvictor` (main.rs:4454), applies + persists the sequence, and then **`std::process::exit`s** on every branch (⟨A31.4⟩ exact: success `exit(0)` main.rs:4781, failure `exit(1)` main.rs:4797/4808) — it **never runs the node** and never constructs the node's handshake configs. The running node reaches any updated trust input only on a **subsequent restart** (route 1), which **reconstructs** `peer_root_network_pk` from its **actual startup inputs** (CLI `--p2p-trusted-root` + the bundle at the configured path). ⟨**A31.4** — supersedes the earlier "after a restart the outbound root is consistent" claim⟩ Reconstruction is **not** removal: unchanged CLI roots can re-select R, and whether the on-disk bundle excludes R is an OBL-STO-2a question — so **post-restart rejection of R is not guaranteed and is left unestablished** here (see §36.3a-2 for the sufficient changes that would remove R from the selected outbound trust input). Therefore the live, no-restart deviation is specifically the **SIGHUP route (3)**.

**Classification under §1 (aspects kept separate).** *Source support:* **STATIC-SUPPORTED** — the same-anchor correspondence is source-confirmed and the outbound static verify vs the live inbound/leaf verifiers are both read from source; the Run-074 contract is pinned with no stated exception. *Evidence status / lifecycle:* STATIC-SUPPORTED / **OPEN**. *Severity:* **unassigned**. *DevNet applicability:* reachable when the operator **arms SIGHUP live-reload** (the two required flags) and applies a **root-level** revocation of the first-configured root, and the node then evaluates the outbound root in the (α) retrying-initial-dial or (β) in-progress-handshake window; the dial surface is the configured `static_peers`. *Release consequence:* requires a documented project decision (not asserted). *Accepted risk:* **NOT inferred**.

**⟨A31.3⟩ Disposition — promoted to a new finding (the "missing link / not a new weakness" hedges are withdrawn).** The §1 condition is met: the **same anchor** is revoked under an **applicable contract** (Run-074, no stated exception) and the bounded outbound path still accepts its certificate. Per the §1 standard this is a **source-supported invariant violation**, classified as a new **STATIC-SUPPORTED finding A31-F1** (OPEN): *the outbound (dial-side) server-certificate verifier retains a construction-time static root (`peer_root_network_pk`) that a SIGHUP live root-level revocation does not refresh, so the node keeps trusting delegation certs chaining to a live-revoked root for as long as the static field retains it* ⟨**A31.4**: the earlier "until process restart" is superseded — a later restart only **reconstructs** the field from its actual startup inputs, which does **not** guarantee removal of R; sufficient changes to remove R are in §36.3a-2, and post-restart rejection is otherwise unestablished. Absence of the exact field name in the Run-074 wording is **not** treated as an exemption; `static_peers`, operator-armed activation, unobserved deployment and absent runtime reproduction are applicability/EXEC facts, **not** reasons to deny source support. **Distinctness (mechanism / trust-decision / consequence / remediation compared):** vs **A23-F1** — A23-F1 is the bundle-signing-key **ratification** binding (who may sign a bundle; GOV layer); A31-F1 is the **transport dial-time** server-cert verifier retaining a stale root (different layer, different trust decision, different remediation). vs **A2-F1** (inbound client-cert PoP), **A6-F1** (session leak), **A11-F1** (key/nonce reuse) — different mechanisms and trust decisions. vs **C4** — A31-F1 is a **concrete source instance within the OPEN C4 gate** (trust-bundle hot-reload), like A23-F1, not "covered" by it. A broad assurance gap is not a substitute: A31-F1 is a concrete, source-supported defect. **Unexecuted runtime confirmation** (observing a live node accept a server cert under a SIGHUP-revoked first root in the retry/in-progress window) is a **distinct evidence gap E26** — **not** covered by E14 (which is the session-cleanup/socket-release scope).
**Reused findings (premises, not re-audited here):** A2-F1 (handshake admits a signed client cert without PoP) — the accept/dial handshake admission; A6-F1 (same-NodeId registry `insert` drops the displaced `PeerConnection`; socket release follows destruction of the **final strong `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>` owner** — the two blocking workers each hold an `Arc::clone` (secure_channel.rs:631/637), so release requires **both** to have dropped it (and a fatal reader's `blocking_send(Err)` can block before its worker exits); "both workers exit" is shorthand for that final-owner condition); A11-F1/§6K (KEMTLS key schedule — client encapsulates to the server's public KEM key and holds `shared_secret`, server decapsulates with its private key; directional AEAD counters; replayed-ClientInit **server-side** s2c reinstall); A26 §31 (production dial site = `dial_once`, dead `dial_peer`); A27 §32 (complete socket-release chain + limiter eviction/reconnect). **Cross-obligation handoffs (⟨A31.1⟩ these are *available-source* review owned by another obligation — NOT "genuinely unavailable dependency evidence"):** **OBL-GOV-2** owns the trust-bundle/ratification **acceptance-gate verifier internals** (the `try_trigger_with_activation` candidate validation); **OBL-STO-2a** owns the **durable sequence/marker persistence**. This pass states their premises explicitly and does not claim those reviews complete; it does not reclassify them as DEP.

### 36.3a-2 ⟨A31.4⟩ One sufficient same-anchor configuration, and the restart limitation

**Sufficient configuration (admitted by the actual guards — bit-exact same anchor).** The merge at `main.rs:7201–7207` is *CLI roots first*, then bundle `active_roots` appended, deduplicated **by `root_key_id` only** (`seen` is seeded from the CLI roots' ids; a bundle root is pushed only if its id is new — key *bytes* are never compared, so a CLI entry sharing an id would win). Static selection is `trusted_roots.first().root_pk.clone()` (`p2p_node_builder.rs:1956–1963`). A dedup-by-id merge does **not** by itself prove the first root came from the bundle or shares key bytes with the live entry — so the sufficient case pins a configuration where the first root provably **is** the live entry:

- Environment **DevNet**; `--p2p-mutual-auth` required + `--p2p-pqc-root-mode pqc-static-root` (⇒ `pqc_required`); a **`--p2p-trust-bundle <PATH>`** supplied; and **no `--p2p-trusted-root` flags**.
- Empty CLI roots **is admitted here** (verified, not assumed): `cli_trusted_roots_required = pqc_required && args.p2p_trust_bundle.is_none()` is **false** when a bundle is supplied (`main.rs:6390`), and `parse_pqc_trusted_root_specs` returns `Ok(vec![])` for `specs.is_empty() && !require_present` (`pqc_root_config.rs:272–285`). The post-merge empty-set guard (`main.rs:7341`) is satisfied by the bundle's ≥1 active root; the CLI+bundle conflict guard (`main.rs:6623`) does **not** fire (`!trusted_roots.is_empty()` is false, and it exempts DevNet regardless).
- With empty CLI roots the merge yields `trusted_roots == loaded.active_roots` (each `r.clone()`), so `trusted_roots.first() == loaded.active_roots[0] == R` and `peer_root_network_pk == R.root_pk`.
- The live state is `LivePqcTrustState::initialize_from_loaded_bundle(&loaded)` (`main.rs:7701–7704`), whose snapshot sets `active_roots: loaded.active_roots.clone()` (`pqc_live_trust.rs:199`). So the **initial live entry for R is the same `loaded.active_roots[0]`** — same `root_key_id` **and** same public-key bytes (bit-exact; the crate's own unit test asserts `snap.active_roots()[0].root_pk == loaded.active_roots[0].root_pk`, `pqc_live_trust.rs:503–520`).

→ In this configuration R (static) and R (initial live) are the **same anchor, bit-identical**. A **route (3) SIGHUP root-level** revocation of R (`leaf_cert_fingerprint = None`, Run 050/052) swaps the live snapshot so `lookup_active_root_pk(R.id)` → `None` (inbound rejects), while `peer_root_network_pk` retains `R.root_pk`. The remaining certificate checks (validity-window + ML-DSA suite), live leaf-revocation (both directions), and the Run-418 origin check are **preserved**. This is a **bounded** sufficient case; universal root correspondence is **not** claimed (a CLI root sharing R's id but different bytes would make `first()` a CLI root, not the live entry — excluded here by the empty-CLI shape).

**Restart limitation (reconstruction ≠ removal).** At a later startup `trusted_roots` is **rebuilt** from the then-current CLI `--p2p-trusted-root` flags and the bundle at the configured `--p2p-trust-bundle <PATH>`:
- If the CLI flags still name R, R wins the dedup regardless of the bundle (CLI-first), so `first()` can **still** be R.
- If the CLI roots are empty, `first()` tracks whatever the **on-disk bundle at the configured path** now lists as `active_roots[0]`.

Whether that on-disk bundle has been updated to exclude R is a **durable-storage** question (**OBL-STO-2a**, available-source handoff): the process-start command persists a *sequence* (`commit_sequence`), which does **not** by itself change the bundle pathname or the configuration selected at a later startup; the SIGHUP live apply mutates the *running node's in-memory* snapshot, not necessarily the file. Therefore **"restart rebuilds the root correctly" and "the outbound root is consistent after restart" are withdrawn.** Post-restart rejection of R requires **updated startup inputs** — a bundle file at the configured path whose `active_roots` no longer contain R (revocation set including it) **and**, if any CLI roots named R, flags that no longer name it. Absent evidence those inputs changed, **post-restart acceptance of R is left unestablished** (not expanded into storage/governance internals here).

**⟨A31.4⟩ Post-update vs pre-update root evaluation (kept distinct).** A31-F1 concerns a handshake whose **root verification occurs *after* the SIGHUP swap**, reading the stale static `peer_root_network_pk` (`verify_delegation_cert_at`, qbind-net handshake.rs:183/441–445) that the live apply did not refresh. A handshake whose root check **already completed *before*** the revocation was applied is **not** evidence of stale-root evaluation — it legitimately passed against a then-valid root; only a post-swap verify against the un-refreshed static field demonstrates the asymmetry. (Sessions established by pre-revocation handshakes are a separate matter: the live apply **evicts** them rather than re-verifying them — eviction-request / cancellation-completion / socket-release are §36.4, not this root-staleness point.)

### 36.5 Transport dependency for CONS-1 (hand back at the consensus-admission boundary)

⟨**A31.1 — this subsection is rewritten; the A31 "three receiving states" table and its wire-counter framing are withdrawn.**⟩ For an **s2c frame** to reach the consensus demuxer on a receiving node, the production async receive chain is: `read_loop` (p2p_tcp.rs:1448) → `channel.recv()` = `recv_app`→`decrypt_app`→`decrypt_app_frame`→`AeadDirection::open` → `0x05` peek → `decode_frame` → per-peer rate limiter → `InboundP2pEnvelope`(session-bound `consensus_origin`) → `inbound_tx.send` → demux → `ChannelConsensusHandler` → consensus-loop `inbound_rx` → `handle_inbound_consensus_msg` (= the CONS-1 admission boundary). A decode error or read error ⇒ `break`.

**Acceptance mechanics (corrected — ⟨A31.2⟩ control-flow, not an "iff"):** a `TransportFrame` is `{ msg_type: u8, ciphertext: Vec<u8> }` (transport.rs:21) — **it carries no counter**. The actual control flow: (i) **repository preconditions** gate whether the backend is even reached — `decrypt_app` errors if the session is not `Established` (connection.rs), the frame `msg_type` must be `TRANSPORT_TYPE_APP_MESSAGE` (transport.rs `decrypt_app_frame`), and `next_nonce` first applies the **nonce-exhaustion guard** `if counter == u64::MAX { return Err(NonceOverflow) }` **before** producing a nonce; (ii) once reached, the direction computes `nonce` from its **own local `counter`** and calls `aead.open(key, nonce, aad, ciphertext)`, whose **`Ok`/`Err` is the operative acceptance result** (`Err ⇒ NetError::Aead("decrypt failed")`). There is **no wire-counter equality check**. So acceptance is **tag verification under the locally-supplied key, nonce, AAD and ciphertext** at the receiver's current state — **not** inferred from the recorder's observation or the sender's completed write, and the frame does not announce the counter it was sealed at. ⟨A31.2: this is **not** rephrased as "`open` returns Ok iff key and nonce match"; it is the backend result under the named inputs — a **sufficient conditional** statement (below), not an exact historical-provenance equivalence, and **counter progress alone is not a universal rejection proof for every candidate** (a candidate forgery targets the current state, not a stale counter).⟩

**Key provenance (reconciled with §6A/§6K; the A31 "client KEM secret" prerequisite is withdrawn).** `ClientHandshake::start` (qbind-net handshake.rs:362) **encapsulates to the server's public KEM key** `peer_kem_pk` and stores `(kem_ct, shared_secret)` locally (handshake.rs:385/387); the **server decapsulates with its private key** `local_kem_sk` (handshake.rs:988). Both session keys (`k_c2s`, `k_s2c`) derive from that shared secret (§6K). So the shared secret is held by (i) the original client (which performed the encapsulation and holds `ss`) and (ii) the server (which decapsulates). A party replaying a recorded `ClientInit` obtains the `kem_ct` **bytes** but **not** the stored `shared_secret`; recovering the shared secret from `kem_ct` + the server's public key is the **KEM hardness assumption (DEP)**, not a "client secret" the replayer is missing.

**Four scenarios, per relevant receiver** (endpoint role · key provenance · session id · current local receive counter · prior receive attempts · candidate provenance · required delivery capability):
| Scenario | Relevant receiver | Role / key provenance / session_id | Receiver's local s2c receive counter | Candidate provenance | Backend outcome (operative) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **(1) unchanged-ciphertext replay** of a recorded s2c frame | an honest **client** of that server | client; **its own** s2c key from its handshake; its own `session_id` | whatever **its own** reads have advanced it to — **not assumed** past the recorded frame's original counter | the **unchanged** recorded ciphertext+tag | **Sufficient conditional case:** reusing an **unchanged valid ciphertext in the same cryptographic context** (same key, same local nonce as when it was sealed, same AAD) is one case under which `open` returns `Ok` (a ChaCha20-Poly1305 correctness property — a named **backend assumption**), *not* an exact historical-provenance equivalence. ⟨**A31.3 — stated purely conditionally:**⟩ this case's `open`-`Ok` holds **when** the receiver's local nonce coincides with the one the frame was sealed under (e.g. the receiver has not advanced past that counter — the **surviving client is not necessarily past** it); the review does **not** assert that rejection *necessarily* requires counter advance (other preconditions — not `Established`, wrong `msg_type`, nonce-exhaustion — also gate the backend, and counter progress alone is **not** a universal rejection proof and does not exclude scenario (2)). Only `open`'s `Ok`/`Err` under the locally-supplied inputs decides. **A successful transport `open` does not establish that the frame is legitimate or fresh at the consensus layer** (that is CONS-1's). |
| **(2) newly constructed candidate forgery** targeting the receiver's **current** state | same honest client | same | its current counter (the forger targets it) | a **new** ciphertext/tag crafted for the receiver's current (key, nonce) | requires forging a valid Poly1305 tag under the receiver's current session key — a **cryptanalytic capability (DEP)**; **rejecting one unchanged old ciphertext (1) does NOT exclude this** |
| **(3) legitimate retransmission / delayed delivery** | the intended client | same | at the matching counter in-order | a genuine in-order frame, merely delayed | `open` `Ok` on the in-order frame (normal operation; not an attack) |
| **(4) actor sending through a session whose key it already knows** | the actor's **own** peer endpoint, or any endpoint for which it holds the session key | that endpoint; key **already known** to the actor | that endpoint's counter | the actor **constructs** frames under the known key at the correct counter | `open` `Ok` at that endpoint — this is the "peer that already knows its own key" case, **distinct** from a recorder/replayer that does not hold the key |

**Boundary preserved (A11-F1):** replaying a recorded `ClientInit` reinstalls **server-side** state (the server re-derives `k_s2c` + counter 0 for that replayed session, A11-F1/§6K) — a **send-direction** fact that **does not reset an honest client's receive state**. **Neither successful injection nor its impossibility is an acceptance criterion** of this review; the point is only to classify which questions are transport (TRN-1b) and which are cryptanalytic (DEP) or consensus-admission (CONS-1).

**Four separable questions (⟨A31.2⟩ — do not collapse; (a) is not (b)):**
- **(a) the repository's receive/decode/routing behavior *once candidate bytes are presented* at a receiver** — **transport (TRN-1b), source-answered:** the receive chain above (`open` `Ok` → `0x05` peek → `decode_frame` → per-peer limiter → session-bound `InboundP2pEnvelope` → `inbound_tx` → demux), with the backend `Ok`/`Err` as the acceptance gate (no wire-counter check). This is about the **target** receiver's `open` + routing, so **forwarding** ciphertext does **not** require the forwarder's own endpoint to decrypt.
- **(b) the actor's ability to actually *deliver* those candidate bytes to the relevant endpoint/session at the required local-counter state and time** — **NOT established by the receive-chain trace.** This is a separate **explicit premise**: it needs a network position that reaches the target's socket and timing that hits the compatible counter state. Its classification: **source** supplies only the receive-chain's preconditions (endpoint must be a connected, `Established` session; the per-peer limiter); the actor's on-path delivery + timing is a **runtime/deployment premise (EXEC)**, not a repository guarantee. The receive-chain trace does **not** by itself establish (b).
- **(c) cryptanalytic capability** — **DEP:** (α) recover the shared secret / full session key from `kem_ct` + server public key (KEM/KDF hardness); (β) exploit repeated keystream / one-time-MAC-key reuse at a reused (key, nonce); (γ) construct a candidate ciphertext/tag the backend will `open` under the target's current key/nonce. Full-key **recovery** (α) and a **useful forgery** (γ) are distinct capabilities.
- **(d) consensus admission** — **CONS-1** (§35.4): the embedded Timeout/NewView key/suite/`chain_id`/membership/signature + origin/view/dedup/quorum checks once a message reaches `handle_inbound_consensus_msg`.

**Conditional handoff (sufficient):** given candidate bytes presented at a compatible receiver (b), the repository behavior (a) routes a successful `open` to the consensus boundary; whether the bytes are **obtainable** is (c) DEP, whether they can be **delivered** at the right state/time is (b) EXEC/deployment, and whether they are **admitted** is (d) CONS-1. **Neither a successful attack nor a universal exclusion is claimed. Stop at the consensus-admission boundary; the consensus handlers are not reviewed in this pass.**

The verifier itself (`verify_delegation_cert_at`, handshake.rs:183–224) is the decisive body — **verbatim, through its refusal branches**; it verifies the cert signature against the **single supplied `root_pk`** and has **no root-set/revocation lookup**:
```rust
pub fn verify_delegation_cert_at(
    crypto: &dyn CryptoProvider,
    cert: &NetworkDelegationCert,
    root_pk: &[u8],
    validation_time_secs: u64,
) -> Result<(), NetError> {
    let suite = crypto
        .signature_suite(cert.sig_suite_id)
        .ok_or(NetError::UnsupportedSuite(cert.sig_suite_id))?;
    let digest = network_delegation_cert_digest(cert);
    suite
        .verify(root_pk, &digest, &cert.sig_bytes)
        .map_err(|_| NetError::KeySchedule("signature verify error"))?;
    if cert.not_before > cert.not_after {
        return Err(NetError::ClientCertInvalid("cert invalid validity window"));
    }
    if validation_time_secs < cert.not_before {
        return Err(NetError::ClientCertInvalid("cert not yet valid"));
    }
    if validation_time_secs > cert.not_after {
        return Err(NetError::ClientCertInvalid("cert expired"));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
(`root_pk` is the static `self.cfg.peer_root_network_pk: Vec<u8>`, handshake.rs:272 — there is no root-resolver field on the client cfg. A cert validly signed under that key and inside its validity window returns `Ok` regardless of any live `active_roots`/`revoked_root_ids` state.) **Subsequent acceptance checks on the dial path:** leaf-revocation (handshake.rs:482–488, §36.6(iii) consumer) then, back in `dial_once`, the Run-418 origin binding (p2p_tcp.rs:2002–2024).

```rust
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<Arc<LivePqcTrustSnapshot>, LivePqcTrustError> {
        let guard: RwLockReadGuard<'_, Arc<LivePqcTrustSnapshot>> = self
            .inner
            .read()
            .map_err(|_| LivePqcTrustError::LockPoisoned)?;
        Ok(Arc::clone(&*guard))
    }
    pub fn lookup_active_root_pk(&self, root_key_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, LivePqcTrustError> {
        let snap = self.snapshot()?;
        Ok(snap.lookup_active_root_pk(root_key_id))
    }
    pub fn is_leaf_revoked(&self, fingerprint: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<bool, LivePqcTrustError> {
        let snap = self.snapshot()?;
        Ok(snap.is_leaf_revoked(fingerprint))
    }
    pub fn swap_snapshot(&self, new_snapshot: LivePqcTrustSnapshot) -> Result<Arc<LivePqcTrustSnapshot>, LivePqcTrustError> {
        let mut guard = self.inner.write().map_err(|_| LivePqcTrustError::LockPoisoned)?;
        let previous = Arc::clone(&*guard);
        *guard = Arc::new(new_snapshot);
        Ok(previous)
    }
```
(each lookup wrapper re-enters `snapshot()` ⇒ its own `.read()` ⇒ no coherent per-handshake snapshot.)

### 36.7 Disposition

⟨**A31.1 — reassessed on the corrected/substantiated basis.**⟩ **Separated:**
- **Established source results (available-source, answered):** the production outbound dialer lifecycle (initial-dial-only, **no reconnect-after-drop** grounded in the single spawn site + caller/ownership, not the scope comment; registry insert/replacement); the sync `NetService`/`PeerManager`/`Peer::recv_msg` production-exclusion (sim/test-only, caller-evidenced) — resolving §34.1; the **both-direction** live-trust field provenance (§36.3) including the **source-established asymmetry** (outbound server-root STATIC / not live-revocable; inbound root + bidirectional leaf LIVE; overrides/origins construction-populated); the **per-check (non-coherent) snapshot reads** and the "swap does not cover an in-progress handshake / does not refresh immutable config"; eviction operating **only on registered `peers` entries** with the A6-F1 displaced-session and A27 final-owner qualifications (an `EvictionReport` is not completed revocation enforcement on every live socket); the transport→CONS-1 receive chain and the four injection scenarios with the corrected AEAD-`open`/local-nonce mechanics and reconciled key provenance.
- **Cross-obligation handoffs (available-source, owned elsewhere — NOT "genuinely unavailable"):** the trust-bundle/ratification **acceptance-gate verifier internals** → **OBL-GOV-2**; durable **sequence/marker persistence** → **OBL-STO-2a**. Premises stated; not re-audited here, not reclassified as DEP.
- **Genuine dependency assumptions (DEP):** recovering the shared secret / session key from `kem_ct` + server public key (KEM/KDF hardness); exploiting repeated keystream / one-time-MAC reuse; forging a candidate ciphertext/tag the backend will `open` (ChaCha20-Poly1305 cryptanalysis) — the §36.5 (α)/(β)/(γ) layers.
- **Deployment facts:** whether an operator enables live-reload (`--p2p-trust-bundle-live-reload-enabled`) and configures a revocation bundle; whether `static_peers`/overrides are populated; the `pqc-static-root` profile selection.
- **Runtime observations (EXEC):** the A6-F1/A27 §32 socket-release-completion tail (E14); actual eviction/reconnect timing; whether a swap interleaves a live handshake's two checks.

- **Remaining available-source questions:** none for TRN-1b's own transport scope — the dialer lifecycle, the both-direction trust/revocation propagation (with its asymmetry), the snapshot/eviction ordering, the sync-path exclusion, and the transport→CONS-1 conditions are all answered from source. (The GOV-2/STO internals are owned elsewhere; the consensus-admission part (b) is CONS-1's; the crypto layers are DEP.)

**OBL-TRN-1b → SR-DONE (source)** on the corrected+substantiated basis — every required **repository-owned transport** question is answered, including the newly-substantiated both-direction provenance and the outbound-root/snapshot/eviction qualifications (these are source **results**, not gaps). Limits carried explicitly: **DEP** (KEM/KDF/ChaCha20-Poly1305 cryptanalysis, §36.5 α/β/γ); **deployment** (operator trust/revocation/static-peer config); **EXEC(E14)** (socket-release completion, eviction/handshake-interleave timing); **cross-obligation** (GOV-2 acceptance-gate internals, STO-2a persistence; CONS-1 the §35.4 consensus-admission part (b)). **No new finding forced** — ⟨**A31.2:** the outbound-root static/non-live-revocable asymmetry now carries a **§1-standard disposition (§36.3a)**: **STATIC-SUPPORTED** source observation in tension with the Run-074 "live `LivePqcTrustState` shared with every handshake verifier / no second trust set" contract; callable path, prerequisites (operator-armed live-reload + a root-level revocation), the root-only-case remaining controls (validity-window/suite, leaf-revocation-passes, Run-418 origin-binding limits impostors), and the bounded dial/retry/in-progress exposure window all traced; production-wiring / observed-deployment / severity / release-consequence / accepted-risk kept separate; the **"operator's call" phrasing is withdrawn**; **accepted risk is NOT inferred**; not promoted to a numbered finding** pending the one named missing link (an explicit source/spec statement that the outbound static server-root is in-scope of that Run-074 contract). A2-F1/A6-F1/A11-F1/A23-F1 cores unchanged⟩. ⟨**A31.3 — supersedes the "no new finding / not promoted" conclusion immediately above:** the same-anchor correspondence is source-confirmed and the Run-074 contract carries no stated exception, so the §1 condition is met and the asymmetry is **promoted to STATIC-SUPPORTED finding A31-F1 (OPEN)** (§36.3a); "absence of the exact field name" is not an exemption. TRN-1b's **source** questions remain answered, so it **stays SR-DONE (source) while now carrying the open finding A31-F1** — precedent: OPS-1 carries A24-F1, AVL-1b carries A28-F1; an open finding does not block SR-DONE, and this finding is a source-established weakness, **not** an unread source question (so it is not hidden in DEP/EXEC). **(1 §36.5 transport argument rebuilt).** Withdrew the A31 "three receiving states" table and its wire-counter framing. `TransportFrame` carries **no counter** (transport.rs:21); `open` reconstructs the nonce from the receiver's **local** counter and the backend `Ok`/`Err` is the **sole** acceptance gate (no wire-counter equality check). Four scenarios separated (unchanged-ciphertext replay; newly-constructed candidate forgery; legitimate retransmission/delayed delivery; an actor sending through a session whose key it already knows), each with endpoint role / key provenance / session id / current local receive counter / prior attempts / candidate provenance / required delivery capability. Corrected: an original surviving client is **not necessarily past** the recorded counter (rejection needs a stated progress premise); a fresh handshake **re-encapsulates** (repo fact) — different keys is a fresh-randomness/KEM/KDF **assumption**, not an unconditional guarantee; rejecting one unchanged old ciphertext does **not** exclude a candidate forgery at the receiver's current state; receiver progress is **not** inferred from the recorder's observation or the sender's completed write.

**(2 key provenance + ownership).** Reconciled with §6A/§6K: `ClientHandshake::start` **encapsulates to the server's public KEM key** and holds `shared_secret`; the **server decapsulates with its private key** — the **"client KEM secret" prerequisite is removed**. Six capability layers kept distinct (recover secret/key · exploit keystream/MAC reuse · construct candidate ciphertext/tag · deliver to a compatible receiver · pass transport decode/routing · pass consensus admission); forwarding ciphertext does **not** require the replayer's own endpoint to decrypt. Transport role / key-counter compatibility / delivery / routing = **TRN-1b (answered)**; cryptanalysis = **DEP**; embedded Timeout/NewView admission = **CONS-1**.

**(3 live-trust propagation substantiated, both directions).** §36.3 now carries a per-consumer field-provenance table and the **source-established asymmetry**: outbound server-root is a **static** `peer_root_network_pk` (not live-revocable; handshake.rs:272/441–445, built from `pqc_root_config.trusted_roots.first()`), while inbound client-root (`TrustedClientRoots`→`lookup_active_root_pk`) and the bidirectional leaf-revocation (`LeafCertRevocationList`→`is_leaf_revoked`) are **live** over the **one shared** `LivePqcTrustState` `inner` Arc; per-peer KEM overrides and origin maps are construction-populated. Each check re-enters `snapshot()` with its **own** `.read()` (no coherent per-handshake snapshot; a swap can interleave two checks and does not cover an in-progress handshake or refresh immutable config). Eviction drains **only the registered `peers` map** (`std::mem::take`); an A6-F1-displaced session is not reached, and the `EvictionReport` is not completed revocation enforcement per live socket (A27 final-owner / E14). GOV-2 (acceptance-gate internals) and STO-2a (persistence) are **available-source cross-obligation handoffs**, not "genuinely unavailable."

**(4 lifecycle distinctions restored).** A `read_loop` break ends only the async read task — not writer termination, registry removal, or socket release; a fatal reader's `blocking_send(Err)` can block before the worker exits; socket release follows destruction of the **final** strong `Arc<Mutex<SecureChannel>>` owner; cancellation request / task completion / worker destruction / socket release are four separate events; "no automatic redial" rests on the single spawn site + caller/ownership, not the scope comment. §36.6 excerpt labels corrected (abridged/paraphrase vs verbatim) and the outbound-static-root, key-provenance, per-check-snapshot and no-wire-counter excerpts added.

### 36.10 A31.2 — outbound-root disposition + transport-handoff/evidence completion (summary + git observations, START = END identical) — ⚠️ the "not promoted pending one named missing link" / "operator's call withdrawn-but-unpromoted" disposition below is **SUPERSEDED by §36.11 (A31.3)**, which resolved the named link and **promoted the asymmetry to finding A31-F1 (OPEN)**; retained as dated A31.2 history

Firsthand `ef99e29`, register/excerpt review (read-only), not independent checkout verification. **Bounded disposition + correction; no finding/closure/count forced.** Preserves v1.05; corrects §36.1/.3/.4/.5/.7 and the §35.2 event-order parenthetical, adds §36.3a and rebuilt §36.6 excerpts.

**(1 outbound-root asymmetry dispositioned under §1, §36.3a).** Invariant drawn from the **Run-074 contract** ("live `LivePqcTrustState` shared with every handshake verifier; no second trust set") + the Run-070/072 apply-pipeline purpose (a validated trust/revocation update takes effect on the running node). Source-supported deviation: the **outbound server-root** uses a **static** `peer_root_network_pk` not refreshed by `swap_snapshot`, so a cert validly signed under the configured root still passes the dial verify **after** a live root-level revocation — a "second trust set" for that decision. Corrected the earlier "unknown/revoked root ⇒ signature-verify failure": an **unknown** root fails the signature check, but a **valid cert under the configured key that the live state has since revoked** **passes** (no `active_roots` branch on the client cfg). Classification: **STATIC-SUPPORTED** observation; production-wiring (outbound verify always on; live-reload operator-armed) / observed-deployment (unknown) / severity (unassigned) / release-consequence (needs a documented decision) / accepted-risk (**NOT inferred**) kept separate; **"operator's call" withdrawn**; **not promoted to a numbered finding** pending one named missing link (explicit scope of the outbound static root under the Run-074 "every handshake verifier" contract).
