Firsthand `ef99e29`, register/excerpt review (read-only), not independent checkout verification. **Bounded resolution; one new finding promoted on the evidence (A31-F1); no closure forced.** Preserves v1.06.

**(1 outbound-root resolved under §1 → finding A31-F1).** The Run-074 contract is pinned exactly (`docs/devnet/QBIND_DEVNET_EVIDENCE_RUN_074.md:17`: live `LivePqcTrustState` "shared with every handshake verifier (no second trust set)"), with **no stated exception**. Same-anchor identity correspondence is **source-confirmed**: `peer_root_network_pk = trusted_roots.first().root_pk`, and `trusted_roots` is the CLI roots **merged with the loaded bundle `active_roots`** (deduped by `root_key_id`, main.rs:7201–7207) — the same bundle the live state is built from (`initialize_from_loaded_bundle`, pqc_live_trust.rs:199); a root-level revocation of that first `root_key_id` removes it from the live `active_roots` (inbound rejects) while the static `peer_root_network_pk` is unchanged, so the outbound verifier keeps accepting certs under the **same revoked anchor** for as long as the static field retains it (a later restart reconstructs it from separately-selected inputs — not automatic removal, §36.3a-2). Per §1 this is a **source-supported invariant violation → STATIC-SUPPORTED finding A31-F1 (OPEN)**. The "absence of the exact field name = exemption" hedge and the "cannot be a new weakness beyond A2-F1/…" assertion are **withdrawn**; distinctness was established by comparing mechanism/trust-decision/consequence/remediation (A31-F1 = transport dial-time static-root retention; A23-F1 = ratification-layer binding; different layer/decision/remediation). A31-F1 is a concrete source instance within the OPEN **C4** gate. `static_peers`, operator-armed activation, unobserved deployment and absent runtime reproduction are kept as applicability/EXEC facts, not reasons to deny source support.

**(2 process-start caller resolved).** The `--p2p-trust-bundle-reload-apply-*` path is a **command mode that `std::process::exit`s** (main.rs ~4365) after building a **fresh throwaway** `LivePqcTrustState` (main.rs ~4450) with the `NoActiveSessionsEvictor` and persisting the sequence; it **does not run the node** and never constructs the node's handshake configs. The running node reaches the updated bundle only via a **subsequent restart** (route 1), which rebuilds `peer_root_network_pk`. The matrix's earlier self-contradiction ("fields already built" vs "runs before run_p2p_node builds them") is resolved: neither — it exits. The live no-restart deviation is specifically the **SIGHUP route (3)**.

**(3 consequence bounded).** Run-418 is an **identifier-equality** check (verified `node_id`+`validator_id` vs the configured mapping), not an independent possession proof; a **sufficient** case is the **configured peer under its own revoked root** (no impersonation needed). "Connection stays down" is replaced by "**no replacement dial is scheduled by the inspected local caller**" (eviction / cancellation / final-socket-owner release separate, A27). §36.5's "rejection necessarily requires counter advance" is removed; the unchanged-valid-ciphertext case is stated purely conditionally, and a successful transport `open` does **not** establish consensus-layer legitimacy/freshness.

**(4 evidence).** §36.6(ii) now carries the full `verify_delegation_cert_at` body through its refusal branches (signature-verify-against-single-root + validity-window) and names the subsequent dial-path checks; §36.6(v) carries the real step-7 sequence-commit/rollback branch and the process-start `exit` fragments; the root-selection/merge and same-anchor evidence is in §36.3a.

## 37. A32 — OBL-CONS-1 part (b): replayed Timeout / NewView inbound admission (read-only source; v1.09)

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review, not independent checkout verification. Owner **OBL-CONS-1 / T-A18-1**. Answers the pending **part (b)**: under what receiving-context and state conditions does the **production** inbound path reject / ignore / accept / act on a **replayed** Timeout or NewView carrying previously-recorded signatures. Transport delivery is a **boundary premise** (OBL-TRN-1b SR-DONE, §36); this section claims no transport delivery, forgery, or actor capability.

### 37.1 Boundary and message cases

**Entry premise (not re-derived here).** Candidate bytes are assumed already past the required transport decode / routing / origin checks — i.e. a decrypted `ConsensusNetMsg` reaches the production dispatcher `handle_inbound_consensus_msg` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:5763`, `pub(crate) fn`). This does **not** demonstrate that an actor can produce such delivery; it is the stated OBL-TRN-1b premise.

**Message cases reviewed (kept separate):**
- **(T)** unchanged replay of an encoded `Timeout` (`ConsensusNetMsg::Timeout(bytes)`, `TimeoutMsg<[u8;32]>`).
- **(N)** unchanged replay of an encoded `NewView` / TC (`ConsensusNetMsg::NewView(bytes)`, `TimeoutCertificate<[u8;32]>`).
- **(U)** reuse/modification of authenticated evidence with **unsigned outer fields** — relevant only to the **existing A1-F2 boundary** (the unsigned outer `view`/target fields are not signed; this is A1-F2's surface, not re-opened here).

**Standing principle.** *Historical signature validity is not receiving-context validity.* The receiving-context checks that re-apply over the receiver's **current** inputs are: authenticated-origin / sender binding (Run 418); `from == validator_id` (Timeout); `verification_ctx` key/suite/domain(`chain_id`)/membership/signature (when `Some`); view-staleness/future bounds; accumulator membership + duplicate; TC signer-membership + `two_thirds_vp`. **Note (doc discrepancy):** the counter comment at `binary_consensus_loop.rs:5836` calls Timeout/NewView "received-but-unhandled on the binary path" — this is **stale**: the B14 arms (below) *do* decode, bind, gate, and route them to the engine. The comment is observational text, not a guard; the handlers are authoritative.

### 37.2 Ordered admission trace — Timeout `(T)` (executable order)

Dispatcher arm `ConsensusNetMsg::Timeout(bytes)` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6616`):
1. **inbound counter** `inc_inbound_other()` (5848) — observational only.
2. **size cap**: `bytes.len() > MAX_INBOUND_TIMEOUT_FRAME_BYTES` (= **64 KiB**, `:307`) → `inbound_decode_failures`+`view_timeout_decode_failures`++, **`return`** (no engine state). (6650)
3. **decode**: `bincode::options().with_limit(64 KiB).with_fixint_encoding().deserialize::<TimeoutMsg<[u8;32]>>(&bytes)` → `Err` ⇒ decode-fail counters, fall through to end (no engine state). (6663)
4. **Run 418 sender binding**: `claimed = timeout.validator_id`; `bind_sender(claimed)` ⇒ `Err` → `inbound_sender_binding_rejected_total`++, **`return`**. The authenticated transport `origin` (from the KEMTLS session, never the payload) must bind one-to-one to the claimed id. (6675)
5. **delivered counter** `inbound_timeouts_delivered`++ (6689).
6. **Run 030 crypto gate — ONLY if `verification_ctx` is `Some`** (6697): `verify_timeout_msg(&timeout, ctx.validators, ctx.key_provider, ctx.backend_registry, ctx.chain_id)` ⇒ `Err` → `inbound_timeout_verify_rejected_total`++, **`return`** (never reaches the engine). `Ok` → accepted-counter++. **If `verification_ctx` is `None` → step skipped entirely (no signature check).**
7. **engine** `engine.on_timeout_msg(from, timeout)` (6735): see §37.4. `Ok(Some(tc))` → `apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view(...)`; `Ok(None)` → nothing further; `Err` → `view_timeout_engine_rejects`++.

### 37.3 Ordered admission trace — NewView / TC `(N)` (executable order)

Dispatcher arm `ConsensusNetMsg::NewView(bytes)` (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6783`):
1. **Run 418 origin admission** — `NewView` carries **no single self-declared sender** (it is a multi-signer TC), so instead of claimed-sender binding: if `binding_gate` is `Some`, `gate.authorize_origin(origin)` ⇒ `Err` → `inbound_sender_binding_rejected_total`++, **`return`** (before the delivered counter, crypto, engine, and any mutation). If `None` (test-only) → legacy. (6800)
2. **size cap** 64 KiB → decode-fail counters, **`return`**. (6824)
3. **decode** `TimeoutCertificate<[u8;32]>` → `Err` ⇒ decode-fail, end. (6839)
4. **delivered counter** `inbound_new_views_delivered`++; `from_view = engine.current_view()` (6845/6847).
5. **Run 030 crypto gate — ONLY if `verification_ctx` is `Some`** (6857): (a) empty-evidence pre-check `tc.signed_timeouts.is_empty()` → reject (`inbound_newview_rejected_missing_evidence`), **`return`**; (b) `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence(&tc, &tc.signed_timeouts, ctx.validators, ctx.key_provider, ctx.backend_registry, ctx.chain_id)` ⇒ `Err` → reject, **`return`**. **`None` → step skipped (no signature check).**
6. **engine** `engine.on_timeout_certificate(&tc)` (6930): see §37.4. `Ok(to_view)` with `to_view > from_view` → advance counters + log; else no-op; `Err` → `view_timeout_engine_rejects`++.

### 37.4 Engine-side treatment (separate from the loop; `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs`)

`on_timeout_msg(from, timeout)` (`:3195`), executable order:
- `if from != timeout.validator_id` → `Err(InvalidSignature)` (sender/id consistency; `from` is the Run-418-authenticated id).
- **`if timeout.view < self.current_view` → `Ok(None)` — stale, silently ignored, NO accumulator mutation.**
- else `timeout_accumulator.on_timeout(self.state.validators(), timeout)?` — membership check (`validators.contains`) then **duplicate suppression by `validator_id` key**: an already-present `(view, validator_id)` returns `Ok(false)` (no insert); a per-view-limit overflow also returns `Ok(false)`; otherwise insert `Ok(true)` (`timeout.rs:539`). View tracking evicts oldest views past `max_tracked_views`.
- TC-formation loop `check_view in current_view..=current_view+10`: `maybe_tc_for(validators, check_view)` forms a TC when accumulated member voting power ≥ `two_thirds_vp()` (`timeout.rs:594`), carrying `signers` + exact `signed_timeouts` evidence.

`on_timeout_certificate(tc)` (`:3256`), executable order:
- `tc.validate(self.state.validators())?` (`timeout.rs:353`): each `signers` id must be a **member** (`contains`) and **non-duplicate** (HashSet); accumulated member voting power ≥ `two_thirds_vp()`. **No signature crypto at the engine level** — `validate` trusts the `signers` *list*.
- **`if tc.view <= self.current_view` → `Ok(self.current_view)` — old view, ignored, NO lock/view change.**
- else: if `tc.high_qc.view > locked_qc.view` (or no lock) → `state.set_locked_qc(tc.high_qc.clone())`; advance `current_view = tc.view`; reset `proposed/voted/timeout_emitted_in_view`; `timeout_accumulator.clear_view(tc.timeout_view)`; `Ok(to_view)`.

**Two membership/threshold sets kept separate (equality not assumed):** the engine uses `self.state.validators()` (for `on_timeout`, `validate`, `maybe_tc_for`); the `Some`-ctx crypto uses `ctx.validators` (in `verify_timeout_msg` / `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`). This review does **not** assert they are the same set; where a case depends on it, that is named.

### 37.5 Signed-field coverage (why crypto is not a replay defense)

`verify_timeout_msg` (`timeout_verify.rs:238`) verifies over the canonical preimage `timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id(chain_id, timeout.view, timeout.high_qc, timeout.validator_id)` after membership + governance suite/key + backend dispatch. `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` (`:350`) requires: non-empty evidence; `tc.signers` unique; evidence ↔ `tc.signers` exact permutation; every evidence `ev.view == tc.timeout_view`; per-signer `verify_timeout_msg`; accumulated VP ≥ `two_thirds_vp()`; and `select_max_high_qc(evidence)` matches `tc.high_qc` by **view + block_id only** (`high_qc_eq` — ⟨A32.2⟩ the carried `high_qc` is a **logical `QuorumCertificate` with `signers: Vec<ValidatorId>`**; its signers/endorsement are **NOT verified here** (no separate QC verifier is invoked on this TC path — `high_qc_eq` compares only view+block_id) → links to A1-F3 / CONS-3).

**⟨A32.1 corrected⟩ Exact preimage (`timeout_signing_bytes_with_chain_id`, `timeout.rs:157–185`):** `domain_prefix(chain_id, DomainKind::Timeout)` (8 LE) `view` ∥ (`high_qc.block_id` 32 ∥ `high_qc.view` 8 LE, else zeros) ∥ `validator_id` 8 LE. The domain tag is `format!("QBIND:{scope}:{kind}:v1")` where `scope = chain_scope(chain_id)` maps chain_ids to a **coarse environment class** `DEV`/`TST`/`MAIN`/`UNK` (`domain.rs:175–179`). So the signed material is **(env-scope tag, view, high_qc's block_id+view, validator_id)** — it does **NOT** sign the **raw `chain_id`**, **genesis identity**, or any **session identity**, and for the high_qc it signs only **block_id+view**, not its signer list or endorsement (reconciling with §28: the authenticated scope is the environment tag, not the full chain/genesis identity).

**Consequence (⟨A32.2⟩ — the earlier "re-verifies iff unchanged governance/key/signed-fields" is replaced by separated checks + one sufficient case; "binds `chain_id`" withdrawn).** The verifier is composed, in order (`verify_timeout_msg`):
- **(a) current repository checks (over the receiver's *current* inputs, not the sender's past state):** `ctx.validators.contains(validator_id)` (membership); `ctx.key_provider.get_suite_and_key(validator_id)` (key-provider lookup); wire `suite_id` == that governance suite (suite match); `ctx.backend_registry.get_backend(suite)` present (backend selection); plus the loop's size-cap + bincode decode (input validation).
- **(b) effective signed bytes reconstructed** from the receiver's `ctx.chain_id` and the message: `domain_prefix(ctx.chain_id,Timeout)` ∥ view ∥ (high_qc.block_id+view | zeros) ∥ validator_id. These are computed from *current* inputs, not carried from the signer.
- **(c) backend verification result:** `backend.verify_vote(validator_id, pk_bytes, preimage, signature)` → `Ok`/`Err` is authoritative.
- **(d) one sufficient replay case:** if the recorded message is re-presented when (i) `validator_id` is still a current member, (ii) the key-provider still returns the (suite, pk) corresponding to the signing key, (iii) the wire suite still matches and the backend is present, (iv) the receiver's `ctx.chain_id` is in the **same `chain_scope` class** that was used at signing, and (v) the signed fields are byte-identical — then the reconstructed preimage equals the signed preimage and, **under the stated backend assumption that `verify_vote` is a deterministic function of (pk, preimage, signature)**, (c) returns `Ok`. This is a **sufficient** case, not a biconditional: historical validity is **not** a substitute for current verification, and a changed key/suite/scope does **not** *unconditionally* reject (it changes an input to (a)–(c); the backend decides). So crypto is **not** a replay/freshness defense; **view-monotonicity + accumulator duplicate-suppression** are what bound replay. **Crucially, crypto does NOT bind:** the TC's **aggregate target `tc.view`** (A1-F2 — §37.6/§37.11), nor the **endorsement of the high_qc** it carries (A1-F3). Both apply **even under `Some(ctx)`**.

A **duplicate** (T2) adds no weight; because `on_timeout_msg` discards `_is_new` and scans unconditionally, it **can** produce a caller effect — **but only** if a ≥2/3 quorum is *retained* at a scanned view (T2b). ⟨**A32.2** supersedes the A32.1 "redundant re-broadcast" wording⟩ ⟨**A32.3** supersedes the A32.2 "consumed on completion / requires out-of-window" wording⟩ the scan returns the **first qualifying view**, so a completing timeout can form a TC for a **lower** retained quorum and leave a **higher** completed quorum retained **within** the window — so a within-window quorum **can** sit retained across calls (verified N=4 trace, §37.13), and a duplicate can later select it. When a qualifying quorum is retained, the result is a TC emission + optional `NewView` broadcast + view advance to `V+1`. For **that selected `V`** a subsequent same-`V` timeout is then stale (success advanced past `V` and `clear_view(V)`); this is **not** a claim that a duplicate can cause only one transition ever — a later duplicate can select a **different** retained `V'`. **No amplification is established** (the formed TC is genuine). The within-window retention is **source-admissibly reachable** (verified §37.13); full producer-schedule reachability is a **runtime** question (§37.13). A **new-to-receiver** message (T3, N2) is admitted; under `Some(ctx)` crypto re-checks membership/suite/key/env-scope over current inputs but **does not bind freshness, the TC target `tc.view`, or the high_qc endorsement**. So the fail-opens are **not** limited to the no-ctx case: **A1-F1** is the no-ctx skip (T4, N3); **A1-F2** (unconstrained target view, N8) and **A1-F3** (unendorsed high_qc, N2/N3) apply **even under `Some(ctx)`**. Acceptance of a genuine new-to-receiver timeout for its own `timeout_view` is not itself a replay vulnerability, but that observation **does not** establish that all replay-triggered progress is safe — the target-view (A1-F2) and endorsement (A1-F3) gaps remain, and the duplicate-triggered **single conditional transition** (T2b) remains an open **runtime** reachability question (§37.12), not a demonstrated amplification.

### 37.8 Bounded resolution and §1 assessment

**⟨A32.1 — this paragraph corrects the v1.09 over-claim.** The v1.09 statements "the sole fail-open is the no-ctx case" and "a genuine signed artifact for its own view ⇒ invariant upheld" are **withdrawn**; see §37.11 for the full corrected composition.⟩ **Part (b) is answered** (source level, on the corrected composition) for the production inbound path:

So the fail-opens are **A1-F1** (no-ctx skip, T4/N3), **A1-F2** (unconstrained target view, reachable even under `Some(ctx)` — N8), and **A1-F3** (unendorsed high_qc, N2/N3). What bounds *replay* specifically is **view-monotonicity + duplicate suppression**, not the signature.

Even if a repetition/fan-out question existed, its owner would **not** be **A28-F1/E25** (those concern cumulative *inbound* limiter-map retention; a per-prefix *input*-rate control does not bound node-wide *output* byte/fan-out). On the supported source consequence, §1 establishes **no new invariant violation** here (the retained quorum is genuine; the single transition is to a view ≥2/3 genuinely timed out at) — **but this is not a safety/liveness exclusion**; the retained-out-of-window reachability (T2b) is an open runtime question (§37.12). This subsection **supersedes** the v1.09/A32 claims corrected in §37.5/§37.6/§37.8; it adds the load-bearing branches the earlier short stale-view excerpt + prose crypto description did not substantiate. **Bounded; no new finding forced; count derived.**

**(1) Complete `on_timeout_msg` caller composition (abridged, `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3195–3231` — comment lines and the two dead `let view = from; let _ = view;` lines removed; the guards, the discarded `_is_new`, and the unconditional scan are intact and unmodified):**
```rust
    pub fn on_timeout_msg(&mut self, from: ValidatorId, timeout: TimeoutMsg<[u8; 32]>)
        -> Result<Option<TimeoutCertificate<[u8; 32]>>, TimeoutValidationError> {
        if from != timeout.validator_id {
            return Err(TimeoutValidationError::InvalidSignature(from));
        }
        if timeout.view < self.current_view {
            return Ok(None); // Stale timeout - silently ignore
        }
        let _is_new = self.timeout_accumulator
            .on_timeout(self.state.validators(), timeout)?;   // result DISCARDED
        for check_view in self.current_view..=self.current_view + 10 {   // UNCONDITIONAL scan
            if let Some(tc) = self.timeout_accumulator
                .maybe_tc_for(self.state.validators(), check_view) {
                return Ok(Some(tc));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }
```
The scan runs on **every** non-stale, membership-valid timeout — duplicate or not. `_is_new` (the add/duplicate/capacity outcome) is bound to `_` and never consulted. So the Option<TC> return is a function of the **retained accumulator contents in `[current_view, current_view+10]`**, not of whether this message was new.

**(2) Accumulator branches (⟨A32.2⟩ paraphrase of `timeout.rs:539–582`; verbatim in (11)):** membership `validators.contains(timeout.validator_id)` → `Err(NonMemberSigner)`; view-tracking + `evict_oldest_views()` when `tracked_views.len() >= max_tracked_views` (`tracked_views` is a **`BTreeSet`**, so `iter().next()` is the **smallest/oldest** view → a high retained view survives); per-view-limit overflow → `Ok(false)`; **duplicate** `view_entries.contains_key(&validator_id)` → `Ok(false)` (no insert); else `insert`, `Ok(true)`. A duplicate therefore adds **no signer weight**. "Not currently recorded" ≠ "never seen": entries are retained until a `clear_view` (see (4)) or eviction; a validator cleared/evicted then re-sent is treated as new again.

**(3) `maybe_tc_for` + locally-formed TC shape (paraphrase of `timeout.rs:605–627`; the constructor `new_with_evidence` is recorded **(⟨A33⟩ normalized, per §26.4b's own label) in §26.4b**, timeout.rs:**326**, and reused by reference — not re-quoted here):** the scan from `current_view` upward returns the **first** view whose summed member voting power is `≥ two_thirds_vp()` (`< two_thirds_vp()` → `None`); on a hit it builds `TimeoutCertificate::new_with_evidence(view, select_max_high_qc(values), signers, signed_timeouts)`, which sets `view = timeout_view.saturating_add(1)`. ⟨**A32.3 scoped**⟩ so a **locally-formed** TC has `tc.view = V+1`; **in the non-wrapping case** (`V < u64::MAX`, the only case considered — `saturating_add` is the boundary exception, E02) `V+1 > current_view` since `V ≥ current_view` in the scan, so **that** TC is non-stale at `on_timeout_certificate` and advances + `clear_view(V)`. This is **not** a claim that *every* TC always advances under every arithmetic/context condition (an **inbound** TC's `view` is a decoded wire field, unconstrained — see (6); the `u64::MAX` boundary is excluded).

**(4) The only accumulator clear (verbatim, `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3299`):** `self.timeout_accumulator.clear_view(tc.timeout_view);` — reached **only** inside `on_timeout_certificate` **after** the `tc.view <= current_view` early return, and it clears **only** `tc.timeout_view`. The six other `self.current_view =` assignments (`:1804/1865/1940/2013/2737/3122` — timeout-advance helper, commit `committed_height+1`, snapshot restore `snapshot_height+1`, and others) **do not touch the accumulator**. Hence a quorum retained at a view `V` not equal to a cleared `timeout_view` **survives** arbitrary view advances, and once `V ∈ [current_view, current_view+10]` the next `on_timeout_msg` (any timeout) scans and forms it.

**(5) Broadcast gating (⟨A32.2⟩ paraphrase of `binary_consensus_loop.rs:7384–7410`; ⟨A32.3 cross-ref fix⟩ the verbatim `apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view` caller is recorded in **§35.5** (the one TC-route caller excerpt) and reused by reference, not reproduced):** in `apply_local_tc_and_broadcast_new_view`, only the `Err(_)` arm of `engine.on_timeout_certificate(tc)` returns early; the `Ok(to_view)` arm records a counter **inside** `if to_view > from_view` but does **not** return, so control falls through to `let Some(facade) = outbound else { return; };` then `facade.broadcast_consensus_msg(&ConsensusNetMsg::NewView(tc))`. The broadcast is not syntactically gated on `to_view > from_view`; **however** (⟨A32.2⟩) a TC reaching this caller came from `maybe_tc_for` with `tc.view = check_view+1 > current_view`, so `on_timeout_certificate` **always advances** (`to_view = tc.view > from_view`) and `clear_view`s — the `to_view == from_view` "stale-but-still-broadcast" case is **not reachable for a locally-formed TC**. ⟨**A32.3**⟩ So a formed TC that reaches this caller is applied (advance + `clear_view(V)`) **always**, but the `NewView` broadcast is a **separate downstream gate** — it occurs only if `outbound` is `Some` **and** `bincode::serialize(tc)` succeeds **and** `broadcast_consensus_msg` is attempted; **application and clearing can occur with no broadcast attempted** (e.g. `outbound` None). "Exactly one broadcast" is **not** asserted; a formed TC consumes its own `V` but a later duplicate can select a different retained `V'`. This is why T2b is a single transition *for the selected V*, not a repeatable rebroadcast.

### 37.12 ⟨A32.2⟩ Duplicate-trigger disposition, verbatim branch packet, and reassessment — ⚠️ **PARTLY SUPERSEDED BY §37.13 (A32.3):** its claims that "a within-window quorum is consumed on completion" and that the duplicate-trigger "requires a quorum completed out of the scan window" are **WITHDRAWN** (the scan returns the *first* qualifying view, so a lower quorum shadows a higher completed one, leaving it retained within-window — verified N=4 trace in §37.13). The **verbatim branch packet** and the signed-field/`bind_sender` evidence below remain valid; read the disposition through §37.13

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review. This subsection **supersedes** the A32.1 "repeatable rebroadcast / A28-bounded amplification" wording and supplies the branch excerpts §37.11(2)(3)(5) paraphrased. **Bounded; no new finding; count derived.**

**Precise duplicate-triggered effect (the question in item 1).** Composing the unconditional scan (§37.11(1)) with the locally-formed TC constructor (3) and its immediate application:
- Let `W` = the incoming Timeout's view, `V` = a scanned quorum's view, `c` = `current_view`. The engine stale-gate drops `W < c` **before** the scan, so a triggering timeout has `W ≥ c`; the scan ranges `V ∈ [c, c+10]`; a formed `tc.view = V+1 > c` (saturating; `c+10` is the **scan** bound, E02, not reopened).
- A formed TC is therefore **never stale** at `on_timeout_certificate` ⇒ it **always** advances `c → V+1` and `clear_view(V)`. Hence a **second** Timeout for `V` is stale ⇒ **no repeatable same-TC rebroadcast**. A different retained quorum at `V'` would be its **own single** emission.
- ⚠️ **WITHDRAWN (A32.3):** ~~"A within-window quorum cannot sit retained-and-complete across calls … so the only way a duplicate finds a retained quorum is one that completed OUT of the scan window."~~ The scan returns the **first** qualifying view (`maybe_tc_for` over `current_view..=current_view+10`), so a completing timeout for view `V₁` can form a TC for a **lower** retained quorum `V₀` and leave `V₁` **retained within the window**. A within-window retained quorum is therefore reachable at the source-admissible level — see the verified N=4 trace in §37.13.
- ⚠️ **WITHDRAWN (A32.3):** ~~"Supported result: only a conditional single transition iff the retained-out-of-window schedule holds."~~ Corrected result in §37.13: a duplicate at `W` triggers the scan and, if any scanned view holds a quorum, applies the TC for the **lowest** such view (advance + `clear_view` of **that** view); this is source-admissible **within-window** (no out-of-window premise); it is still **not** a repeated same-TC emission and **not** an amplification.

**Retained-out-of-window schedule — reachability NOT established (exact missing link, not an exclusion).** A jointly-admitted sequence would need: (i) compatible engine vs `ctx` memberships/thresholds; (ii) origin + current-context signature prerequisites met for the far-view timeouts; (iii) a **genuine ≥2/3 quorum of distinct validators' timeouts for a view `V` with `V > c_old+10`** admitted and retained (each such timeout is non-stale so it is ingested, but the scan `[c_old, c_old+10]` does not reach `V`); (iv) a **production-wired, non-scanning, non-clearing** advance of `current_view` to some `c` with `V ∈ [c, c+10]` — e.g. the commit path `self.current_view = committed_height+1` (`:1940`) or snapshot restore (`:2013`), **neither of which scans or clears** `V`, and with `≤128` tracked views so the `BTreeSet` eviction (oldest-first) does not drop `V`; (v) **no intervening non-stale Timeout** between that advance and the duplicate (any such message would itself trigger the scan and consume `V`, making the *duplicate* not the decisive trigger); (vi) the duplicate (`W ≥ c`). **The honest-producer gap:** step (iii) requires a genuine ≥2/3 of validators to have timed out at a view this receiver is **>10 views behind**, while step (iv) requires this receiver to then reach `V−10` by **committing blocks** (not by consuming that very quorum's TC/NewView, which would clear it). Whether a production message schedule realizes (iii)+(iv)+(v) jointly is ⟨**A33**⟩ **not established in this review** (the end-to-end producer/delivery schedule is not traced here and its runtime occurrence is **unobserved**) — this is **not** a claim that source reasoning *cannot* establish such a schedule, only that it is not done here; **no accumulator fixture is asserted**, and reachability is **neither claimed nor excluded**. Owner/observables: a consensus **liveness/catch-up runtime** observation (a lagging node's accumulator retaining a far-view quorum across a commit-driven advance), observable as a `NewView` emitted on receipt of a duplicate/stale-looking Timeout with no new signer; **not** owned by A28-F1/E25 (inbound limiter-map retention) and **not** covered by E01/E02/E19/E03.

### 37.13 ⟨A32.3⟩ First-qualifying-scan resolution: verified N=4 trace and final CONS-1 disposition

Firsthand `ef99e29`, read-only source inspection; register/excerpt review. This subsection **supersedes** the A32.2 §37.12 claims that a within-window quorum is "consumed on completion" and that the duplicate-trigger "requires an out-of-window quorum". **Bounded; no new finding; count derived.**

**The decisive source fact.** `on_timeout_msg` scans `for check_view in current_view..=current_view+10 { if let Some(tc) = maybe_tc_for(check_view) { return Ok(Some(tc)); } }` (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3221–3229`): it returns the **lowest** scanned view that holds `≥ two_thirds_vp` (`validator_set.rs:491`, `(2*total).div_ceil(3)` = **3** for N=4 unit weight). `on_timeout_certificate` clears **only** `tc.timeout_view` (`:3299`); an inbound TC for `U` advances `current_view` while leaving any `V ≠ U` untouched — the relevant condition is **"does not clear V"**, not "no clear anywhere". A view advance can therefore come from the **inbound-NewView** path, not only commit/snapshot.

**Checked finite candidate (VERIFIED through the production handlers; N=4 unit-weight, quorum=3, `verification_ctx=Some`, stable compatible engine/ctx membership, keys/suite/scope/origin/size/decode/high-QC premises all held, views far from `u64` bounds).** This is a **source-admissible** trace given admissible signed inputs and their delivery — **not** an asserted runtime occurrence and **not** an arbitrary accumulator fixture. Start `current_view=0`, accumulator empty:

| Step | Admitted input | Verified consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | three distinct, currently-verifiable Timeouts for **view 20** | each non-stale (`20 ≥ 0`), ingested; after the 3rd the scan `0..=10` does **not** reach 20 → `Ok(None)`. **Quorum 20 retained** |
| 2 | two distinct, currently-verifiable Timeouts for **view 22** | ingested; scan `0..=10` → `Ok(None)`. View 22 holds 2 (`< 3`), below quorum |
| 3 | a valid inbound **NewView** TC, `timeout_view=11`, `target view=12` | origin-admitted + evidence-verified (3 signed view-11 timeouts); `on_timeout_certificate`: `12 > 0` → advance to **12**, `clear_view(11)`. **Entries 20 and 22 preserved; the NewView handler runs no timeout scan** |
| 4 | the **third** distinct Timeout for **view 22** | non-stale (`22 ≥ 12`), ingested → view 22 now holds 3. Scan `12..=22` checks 12…19 (none), **20 (quorum) → returns TC for 20 FIRST**. Apply: `tc.view=21 > 12` → advance to **21**, `clear_view(20)`. **Quorum 22 completes but is NOT consumed — it stays retained within the window** |
| 5 | an unchanged **duplicate** Timeout for **view 22** | non-stale (`22 ≥ 21`); accumulator `Ok(false)` (no weight); scan `21..=31` → 21 (none), **22 (quorum) → returns TC for 22**. Apply: `tc.view=23 > 21` → advance to **23**, `clear_view(22)`, then the broadcast gate. **A duplicate triggered a view transition from a within-window retained quorum** |
| 6 | another Timeout for **view 22** | `22 < 23` ⇒ **stale** at the engine stale-gate (before ingest/scan) → `Ok(None)`; no accumulator scan |

**No step was rejected.** Step 4 is the crux: the completing (3rd) timeout for view 22 forms a TC for the **lower** retained view 20, so view 22's quorum is left retained — refuting A32.2's "consumed on completion". Step 5 then shows a **duplicate** (zero added weight) selecting that within-window retained quorum. (The duplicate at `W=22` triggers a scan from `current_view=21`; it selected `V=22` here, but in general `W` need not equal the selected `V`.)

**Levels kept separate.**
- **Source-admissible transitions** (given admissible signed inputs + delivery): the table above, **established**.
- **Provenance/capabilities:** steps 1–4 require genuine signed timeouts for views 11, 20, 22 from distinct current members (unforgeable without keys; the step-5 "duplicate" is a replay of a genuine view-22 timeout). **No signing-key control is assumed.**
- **All-honest producer schedule:** would require honest validators to have emitted timeouts for views 11/20/22 while this receiver sits at 0–12 (a **lagging-receiver** configuration). The producer *mechanism* (a validator emits a signed timeout for its current view on timeout) is source-covered by the completed **§21 (pacemaker)** and **§35 (emission witness)** — not reopened here.
- **Runtime occurrence:** whether a production network schedule realizes steps 1–4 jointly (a ≥3-validator quorum at views 20 and 22 while one node lags, reached by inbound NewView/commit) is a **liveness/timing** question, **separate** and **not** required for the conditional admission result.

**Remaining source question.** None on the **receiver side**: the dispatcher, `on_timeout_msg` (scan + discard `_is_new`), the accumulator branches (membership/eviction/capacity/duplicate), `maybe_tc_for`+`new_with_evidence`, `clear_view`, `on_timeout_certificate`, `verify_timeout_msg`/`verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence`, `bind_sender`+`authorize`, and the broadcast gate are all read (verbatim in §37.12 / §26.4b / §35.5). The producer *mechanism* is the completed §21/§35. The one open item is the **producer-schedule reachability** above — a **runtime/liveness** question, explicitly **not** an unread receiver-side source link and **not** relabelled EXEC.

**Immediate consequence (exact scope).** For the selected non-wrapping `V`: a locally-formed TC has `tc.view = V+1 > current_view` ⇒ it advances to `V+1` and `clear_view(V)`, so a later timeout for **that** `V` is stale. This does **not** generalize to: every TC always advances (inbound `tc.view` is unconstrained, A1-F2; the `u64::MAX` boundary is excluded); every duplicate causes only one transition ever (a later duplicate can select a different retained `V'`); or every formed TC causes exactly one broadcast (the broadcast needs `outbound Some` + serialize `Ok` + attempt; application/clearing can occur with **no** broadcast). Attempt ≠ enqueue ≠ completed write ≠ receipt.

**§1 / findings.** The verified trace establishes **no new invariant violation**: every TC formed is a **genuine** ≥2/3 quorum; a duplicate contributes no weight and only *triggers* a scan that a subsequent honest non-stale timeout would also trigger. **No amplification** is established, and **A28-F1/E25** stays within its limiter-retention scope (not the owner of any consensus emission). Conversely, **no broad safety/liveness exclusion** follows from the quorum being genuine. The standing **A1-F2** (unsigned target `tc.view`) and **A1-F3** (unendorsed high_qc) apply under `Some(ctx)`; **A1-F1/A1-F2/A1-F3 remain distinct and none is newly discovered**.

**Status.** The bounded **admission + immediate-effect** source questions for CONS-1 part (b) are answered with supported dispositions and explicit premises/limits; no required receiver-side source link remains unresolved; the sole open item is a named **runtime** producer-schedule question. Therefore **OBL-CONS-1 = SR-DONE (source)**, carrying OPEN **A1-F1 / A1-F2 / A1-F3**, EXEC(E01); downstream lock/commit lineage = **OBL-CONS-3** (SR-PARTIAL, E03). **Unfinished-source = 11** (unchanged; status retained on corrected evidence, not re-moved — neither 11 nor 12 is targeted). **No finding-count change.**

| R3 | p2p + signer + **`--validator-consensus-key` set**, **default transport** (`MutualAuthMode::Disabled` + `TestGradeDummySig`) | **Starts**; timeout context ACTIVE | **Yes** | **None effective** — `DummySig.verify→Ok(())`, no client cert, `DummyAead` (no integrity) | **Yes** — decode precedes sender-binding/verify (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6192-6199`); **F001 reachable by effectively unauthenticated peers** | **Yes** (mandatory) |
| R4 | p2p + signer + `--validator-consensus-key` + **`--p2p-pqc-root-mode pqc-static-root` + `--p2p-mutual-auth required` + trusted root** | **Starts**; timeout context ACTIVE | **Yes** | **Real** KEMTLS mutual-auth + ML-DSA-44 (suite 100) cert verification; ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD | **Yes**, but **only for peers that pass KEMTLS mutual-auth** with a trusted-root-chained cert | **Yes** |
| R5 | `--consensus-authority-from-genesis` (any mode) | **FATAL `exit(1)`** via the `main` containment guard (`main.rs:5801-5809`); genesis activation DISABLED | No | n/a | No | No |
| R6 | Fixture/feature-gated: `ConsensusVerificationPolicy::LocalFixtureUnsigned`, `forged_injection` (hidden flag + env + `Devnet`) | Not reachable through normal production CLI (A1 §5; `forged_injection` triple-gated) | — | — | **UNRESOLVED** for Proposal/Vote *admission* (fixture passthrough exists; production constructors exclude it per A1) | — |

**Net reachability correction:** the only rows that reach `BlockProposal::decode` are **R3** and
**R4** — a purposely-configured P2P validator. R3 (default transport) exposes the decoder to
effectively unauthenticated peers; R4 restricts it to mutual-authenticated peers. A1's implication
that a *default* node is exposed to *anonymous* peers is withdrawn.

**Unresolved (R6):** whether any non-test production route can select `LocalFixtureUnsigned` or
`forged_injection` on DevNet was not fully re-traced in A2; A1 found production constructors exclude
them, but this remains an A3 confirmation item.

## 4. F001 deep analysis — allocation before proposal verification

### 4.1 Field-offset table (inner `BlockProposal`, little-endian; `qbind-wire/src/io.rs`)

`BlockProposal::decode` (`qbind-wire/src/consensus.rs:726-771`). All multi-byte integers LE
(`io.rs:39-66`). Offsets are within the **inner** proposal byte string (the `Vec<u8>` payload carried
by `ConsensusNetMsg::Proposal`, itself inside a bincode `P2pMessage` inside a transport frame).

| Offset | Field | Reader | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `msg_type` (must == `MSG_TYPE_BLOCK_PROPOSAL`, `:729`) | `get_u8` | 1 |
| 1 | `version` | `get_u8` | 1 |
| 2 | `chain_id` | `get_u32` | 4 |
| 6 | `epoch` | `get_u64` | 8 |
| 14 | `height` | `get_u64` | 8 |
| 22 | `round` | `get_u64` | 8 |
| 30 | `parent_block_id` | `get_bytes(32)` | 32 |
| 62 | `payload_hash` | `get_bytes(32)` | 32 |
| 94 | `proposer_index` | `get_u16` | 2 |
| 96 | `suite_id` | `get_u16` | 2 |
| **98** | **`tx_count`** | **`get_u32`** | **4** |
| 102 | `timestamp` | `get_u64` | 8 |
| 110 | `payload_kind` | `get_u8` | 1 |
| 111 | `next_epoch` | `get_u64` | 8 |
| 119 | `batch_commitment` | `get_bytes(32)` | 32 |
| 151 | `qc_len` | `get_u32` | 4 |
| 155 | *(qc bytes if `qc_len>0`; else none)* | — | `qc_len` |
| **155** (qc_len=0) | **`Vec::with_capacity(tx_count)`** (`consensus.rs:766`) | — | — |

**Minimum prefix consumed before the allocation = 155 bytes** (with `qc_len=0`). Your independent
figure is confirmed; A1's "~20 bytes" is corrected. `tx_count` is an attacker-controlled LE `u32` at
inner offset 98. (If `qc_len>0`, the prefix grows by the QC bytes, which are themselves bounded —
`QuorumCertificate::decode` uses a u16 `sig_count`.)

### 4.2 The four distinct effects (separated as requested)

1. **Attacker-controlled allocation request:** `Vec::<Vec<u8>>::with_capacity(tx_count as usize)`;
   `size_of::<Vec<u8>>() == 24` on 64-bit ⇒ request up to `4_294_967_295 × 24 ≈ 1.03 × 10¹¹ bytes
   (~103 GB)` for the vector spine. CONFIRMED (code read first-hand).
2. **Virtual address-space reservation:** `with_capacity` asks the allocator for that many bytes;
   glibc routes a >128 KiB request to `mmap`. On a 64-bit host there is ample VA; whether the request
   **succeeds** depends on the allocator and the kernel overcommit policy.
3. **Resident memory (RSS) growth:** `with_capacity` **does not write** the buffer, so **no pages are
   faulted** — RSS does **not** grow from the reservation alone. To grow RSS the `Vec` would have to be
   populated, which requires the attacker to actually supply `tx_count` encoded tx entries; those are
   bounded by the enclosing transport frame cap (`qbind-net` 16 MiB), so a huge `tx_count` cannot be
   backed by real entries in one small frame.
4. **Failure / panic / abort / termination:** if the allocator returns null (e.g. overcommit disabled
   — `vm.overcommit_memory=2` — or a per-process/cgroup commit limit, or a 32-bit/limited host), Rust
   calls `handle_alloc_error` → **process abort (SIGABRT)**. If the reservation **succeeds**
   (common with default Linux heuristic overcommit), see §4.3.

### 4.3 What happens if allocation succeeds but the first tx length is absent

The loop at `consensus.rs:767-771` does `for _ in 0..tx_count { let tx_len = get_u32(input)?; … }`.
On the **first** iteration `get_u32` runs against the remaining input; if the attacker supplied the
155-byte prefix and **no** tx bytes, `input` is empty ⇒ `get_u32` returns `WireError::UnexpectedEof`
⇒ `?` propagates ⇒ `decode` returns `Err` ⇒ the just-reserved `txs` `Vec` is **dropped** and its
(unbacked) reservation released. Net effect in that case: a transient large **VA reservation** that is
immediately freed, **no RSS growth, no crash**. The damaging outcome (abort) therefore occurs **only**
when effect (4) fires at reservation time.

**Conclusion (corrected disposition):** the defect — an unbounded `with_capacity` driven by an
untrusted `u32`, executed before authentication — is **CONFIRMED**. The **impact is conditional**: a
denial-of-service **abort** on hosts/allocators that reject the ~103 GB request (overcommit disabled,
constrained cgroup/container memory, or small hosts), and a transient VA spike (freed on the ensuing
decode error) where overcommit is permissive. A1's unconditional "guaranteed crash" is withdrawn.
**Assumptions:** 64-bit target, glibc/jemalloc-style allocator, Linux overcommit policy as the decisive
variable. No execution evidence was gathered (static inspection only).

### 4.4 Attacker prerequisites by configuration

- **R0/R1/R2/R5:** unreachable (no listener).
- **R3 (default transport):** any peer that completes the **server-authenticated** KEMTLS handshake —
  no client authentication (`MutualAuthMode::Disabled`) and `DummySig` accepts any server/cert path, so
  effectively **any network peer** reaching the port. `decode` precedes sender-binding and signature
  verification (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6192-6199`), and precedes the fail-closed Proposal/Vote
  rejection (`pv_authority=None`) — so the allocation happens even though the proposal is ultimately
  rejected.
- **R4 (static-root + mutual-auth required):** only a peer presenting a **trusted-root-chained,
  mutual-authenticated** KEMTLS cert; effectively a provisioned validator/seed, which narrows the
  attacker set substantially (but a single misbehaving/compromised authenticated peer still triggers it).

### 4.5 Adjacent count/length allocations (defense-in-depth sweep)

- Per-tx body: `get_u32(tx_len)` then `get_bytes(input, tx_len)?.to_vec()` (`:768-769`) — `get_bytes`
  checks `input.len() < len` **before** slicing, so an oversized `tx_len` errors without over-allocating;
  `.to_vec()` copies only validated bytes. **Bounded.**
- `QuorumCertificate::decode` (`consensus.rs:351`): `sig_count` is **u16** ⇒ `with_capacity` ≤ 65535
  entries (~1.5 MB spine); each signature via `get_bytes`. **Bounded** (finite width is the only bound —
  acceptable here only because it is u16, not u32).
- `Vote::decode`, `Transaction::decode` (u16 counts), `PeerList::decode` (explicit
  `> MAX_PEER_LIST_SIZE` check, `net.rs:513`). **Bounded.**
- **`BlockProposal.tx_count` (u32) is the sole unbounded pre-size.** A finite integer width (u32) is
  **not** an acceptable bound here (~103 GB), and the outer 16 MiB frame cap bounds only the *byte
  length*, never the embedded `tx_count` value. Confirmed outlier.

### 4.6 Proposed reproduction (bounded, isolated; **NOT executed**)

In an isolated unit harness, call `<BlockProposal as WireDecode>::decode` on a 155-byte buffer whose
bytes 98..102 are `0xFFFFFFFF` (LE) and `qc_len=0`, with no tx bodies; observe the `with_capacity`
request size and the subsequent `UnexpectedEof`. To observe the abort branch, run under a constrained
memory cgroup / `vm.overcommit_memory=2`. Do **not** target any running node or network.

---

## 5. F002 deep analysis — distinct council authorization

### 5.1 Trace result

- `verify_envelope` (`qbind-gov/src/verify.rs:95-124`) iterates `envelope.council_approvals`,
  incrementing `valid_count` for each approval that (a) names a `member_id` present in the keyset
  (`:133`), (b) carries a `public_key` byte-equal to the keyset's key for that id (`:156`), and (c)
  produces a valid ML-DSA-44 signature over the digest. **No set of already-counted `member_id`s is
  maintained** — confirmed by re-read and by grep (no `HashSet`/`seen`/dedup over approvals in
  `verify.rs`). `is_valid()` = `valid_count >= threshold` (`:56-58`).
- The signed digest excludes `council_approvals` **by design** (`hash.rs:38-63`, to allow incremental
  signing); it **includes** `network_environment` (`hash.rs:121-122`).
- `CouncilKeySet::validate` dedups the **keyset** member ids and enforces `0 < threshold <= keys.len()`
  (`council.rs:166-205`) — but the keyset is **trusted operator config**, not the attacker-controlled
  approvals list.
- The only caller is the standalone CLI `qbind-envelope verify` (`bin/qbind_envelope.rs`), which prints
  `result.is_valid()` as the PASS/FAIL verdict and maps it to exit code 0/1 (`:304-352`,
  `exit_codes` `:42-46`). **No caller dedups approvals before counting.** `qbind-gov` is **not** a
  dependency of `qbind-node` (confirmed in its manifest in A1) — it is an **offline operator tool**.

### 5.2 Disposition (unchanged core finding; corrected remediation)

**CONFIRMED** duplicate-approval quorum bypass: an actor holding **one** valid `(member_id, public_key,
signature)` triple can append it `threshold` times; each copy independently passes
`verify_single_signature` and increments `valid_count`, so `is_valid()` returns true with a single
distinct signer. Duplicate **public keys under different member ids** would similarly each count (the
check is per-approval `member_id`→keyset-pk match, not cross-approval key distinctness), but that
requires the keyset (trusted config) to contain the duplicate — lower concern.

**Corrected remediation (replacing A1's):** do **not** fold the completed signature list into the
signed digest (that breaks intentional incremental signing). The correct fix is to **count distinct
authorized signers** — e.g. maintain a `HashSet<member_id>` (and reject duplicate `member_id` /
duplicate public key across approvals) so each authorized member contributes at most one toward the
threshold — together with keeping the decision-relevant fields (already in the digest, incl.
`network_environment`) bound. No cryptographic redesign is warranted.

**Scope separation:** this is an **offline-tool** defect (operator relying on `qbind-envelope verify`
to decide an upgrade is misled); it is **not** a live on-chain consensus bypass (the node does not link
`qbind-gov`). No additional reachable on-chain scenario was found.

---

## 6. Reassessed dispositions — F003 and F004

### F003 — live timeout-signing path: durable / cross-restart double-sign protection
- **Timeout signer reachability (resolved):** on the P2P path the signer is **mandatory** — the node
  **cannot start** without it (`main.rs:5699-5768` fatal on signer-load failure; `:6115-6134` fatal if
  the context is absent). So whenever a P2P validator runs (R3/R4), timeouts **are** signed
  (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:7701`). A1's open question is answered: the live signing path **is**
  exercised on any running P2P validator.
- **Which signed fields can vary after restart:** the timeout preimage binds `chain_id, view, high_qc,
  validator_id` (`timeout_verify.rs:292-297`). In production the embedded QC authority snapshot
  (`current_auth`/`AuthorizedProposalVoteSnapshot`) is `None`, so the F7 retained-QC admission refuses
  any `high_qc`-bearing timeout (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:1556`); emitted timeouts therefore carry
  `high_qc=None`. Two timeouts at the same `view` are then **byte-identical** (same chain_id, view,
  None, validator_id).
- **Identical re-sign vs conflicting message:** producing the same timeout bytes twice is a **repeated
  identical signature**, not a protocol-defined conflicting message. The slashing taxonomy's O1
  "Double Sign" (M-series M9; `slashing/mod.rs`) targets **conflicting** votes/blocks at the same
  height/view — it is **not** triggered by identical re-signs. So the current configuration produces
  **no slashable equivocation** from the timeout path.
- **Crash / rollback / clone (separated):** within one process, the in-memory
  `timeout_emitted_in_view` flag (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4959`) prevents a second timeout in a view;
  it **resets on restart** (seed via `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline`, not the locked-state
  `initialize_from_restart`, `:2654-2677`). The `SigningReservationJournal` (durable-before-sign) is
  **not initialized in production** (its own header, `signing_reservation_journal.rs:26-28`) and, even
  if wired, provides **no anti-rollback/anti-clone** anchor (`:22-25`). So: (a) **crash recovery** — no
  durable highest-signed-view is restored; (b) **disk rollback** — undetectable from local state; (c)
  **concurrent key clone** — two data dirs with the same key are not mutually aware. Ordinary durable
  local storage would address (a) only.
- **Disposition:** **design risk; CONFIRMED code facts; exploitability CONDITIONAL and currently
  NON-slashable.** Because emitted timeouts are forced to `high_qc=None`, there is **no** reachable
  conflicting-content timeout today, so this is **not** a live equivocation at HEAD. The risk would
  become a slashable equivocation vector only if a future activation lets the timeout (or Proposal/Vote)
  signer emit **content-varying** messages **without** a wired durable, rollback/clone-aware journal.
  **Severity:** Medium (latent). **Confidence:** High (code facts) / the equivocation scenario is a
  stated hypothesis, not demonstrated. **Reachability:** signer reachable on any P2P validator;
  conflicting-content emission not reachable at HEAD. **Not closed** (conditional impact).

### F004 — insecure-by-default transport authentication
- **Provider selection & compile-time guards:** `make_test_crypto_provider` (wiring `DummySig` +
  `DummyKem` + `DummyAead`) is **ordinary `src/` code, not `#[cfg(test)]`** (`p2p_node_builder.rs:278-380`),
  and is selected at runtime whenever `mode != PqcStaticRoot` (`:1307-1309`). Default mode is
  `PqcRootMode::TestGradeDummySig` (`pqc_root_config.rs:63-72, 451`) and default mutual-auth is
  `MutualAuthMode::Disabled` (`handshake.rs:33`). So the always-accept provider **ships in the release
  binary** and is the **default** — A1's inference here is confirmed, and the "test-grade"/"test-only"
  comments do **not** mean compiled-out.
- **Separated crypto assessment (default R3 mode):**
  - **Signature verification:** `DummySig::verify → Ok(())` unconditionally — transport cert/identity
    verification is absent.
  - **KEM secrecy:** `DummyKem` (test-grade) — not real ML-KEM-768 encapsulation; no PQ secrecy
    guarantee.
  - **AEAD integrity:** `DummyAead` — single-byte XOR with an xor-fold "tag"; no confidentiality or
    integrity.
- **Reachability (corrected with §3):** reaching a listener requires a configured P2P validator
  (R3/R4). In **R3** the transport is wholly unprotected (sig/KEM/AEAD all dummy, no client auth); in
  **R4** real ML-DSA-44 cert verification + ML-KEM-768 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 apply. The documented DevNet
  seed/validator checklist mandates R4, but the binary's **default** is R3.
- **Disposition:** **CONFIRMED insecure default that ships in release.** **Severity:** Medium-High (a
  P2P validator left at default transport has no real transport authentication/secrecy/integrity and
  widens F001's attacker set to unauthenticated peers). **Confidence:** High. **Reachability:**
  configured P2P validator with default transport (R3). **Not closed.**

---

## 7. Post-quantum / classical-crypto dependency & trust-boundary assessment

A1's blanket assurances are **withdrawn and replaced** with the bounded classification below.

**Classical cryptographic dependencies present (`Cargo.lock`):** `ecdsa 0.16.9`, `elliptic-curve
0.13.8`, `k256 0.13.4` (secp256k1), `p256 0.13.2`, `secp256k1 0.31.1`, reached via `revm 34.0.0` /
`revm-precompile 32.0.0` (EVM precompiles — `ecrecover`, `p256verify`, bn128/modexp, etc.).

| Dependency role | Classification | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Recorded in lockfile only | No — they are **selected by build config** | `qbind-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `default=["evm"]`, `evm=["revm"]`; `qbind-node` depends on `qbind-runtime` ⇒ `revm`+precompiles compile into the node binary |
| Selected by a relevant build configuration | **Yes** | default feature `evm` |
| Reachable through execution / interop | **NOT demonstrated** on the deployed path | `RevmExecutionEngine` (`qbind-runtime/src/revm_engine.rs`) runs during block execution; A1 established block/tx execution (`apply_block`) is invoked only by sim/tests on the deployed path (no network tx ingress; empty proposals). So EVM precompile crypto is **compiled-in but not demonstrably reached with untrusted input** on the DevNet node. |
| Used to authorize consensus / transport / governance / trust-root | **No** | consensus/transport/governance/trust-root authorization uses ML-DSA-44 / ML-KEM-768 only (`qbind-crypto`, `genesis_consensus_authority.rs`, `timeout_verification_bridge.rs`); the classical primitives are **EVM-layer** (user-contract precompiles) and independent of native trust |
| Unresolved | EVM execution reachability **if/when** tx ingress is enabled; exact precompile set exposed by this `revm` build; whether any native QBIND tx path calls EVM precompiles | not traced to completion in A2 — A3 item |

**Corrected PQ statements:**
- `qbind-crypto` contains **no** classical signature/KEM primitives (ML-DSA-44 / ML-KEM-768 /
  ChaCha20-Poly1305 / SHA3 only) — this narrower A1 claim stands.
- "**No classical crypto anywhere in source**" — **WITHDRAWN**: classical ECC crypto is present and
  compiled-in via the EVM layer.
- "**All PQ-relevant deps reachable-and-sound** / per-message verifiers **cryptographically sound**" —
  **NARROWED** to: the specific ML-DSA-44 verify wrapper, the QC verifier, and the timeout verifier
  that were read are **individually consistent with their intent** (length checks, result checked, no
  cross-suite fallback); this does **not** establish end-to-end cryptographic soundness, and the EVM
  classical surface is explicitly outside that review.
- **Dependency presence ≠ native-trust vulnerability.** No reachable scenario was found in which the
  classical EVM crypto authorizes consensus, transport, governance, or trust-root changes; conversely,
  inspecting selected PQ wrappers does **not** prove the whole system sound.

---

| ID | Title | Severity | Confidence | Reachability | Evidence status | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F001** | Unbounded `with_capacity(tx_count)` pre-auth in `BlockProposal::decode` | Medium (High where overcommit disabled / memory-constrained) | High (defect) / Medium (crash outcome) | **R3/R4 only** — configured P2P validator; R3 = unauthenticated peers, R4 = mutual-auth'd peers; **not** default/anonymous | Static source; offsets/encoding confirmed first-hand; **not executed** | **OPEN**, corrected (prefix 155B; impact conditional, allocator/OS-dependent) |
| **F002** | Council quorum bypass via duplicated approval (`verify_envelope`) | High (within tool) / Medium (overall) | High | **Offline `qbind-envelope` CLI only**; not linked by `qbind-node` | Static source; confirmed first-hand (no approval dedup) | **OPEN**, remediation corrected (distinct-signer counting, not digest redesign) |
| **F003** | Live timeout signing lacks durable / cross-restart double-sign protection | Medium (latent) | High (code facts); equivocation scenario hypothetical | Signer reachable on any P2P validator; **conflicting-content emission NOT reachable at HEAD** (`high_qc` forced `None`) | Static source first-hand | **OPEN** (design risk); **not** a live/slashable equivocation today |
| **F004** | Insecure-by-default transport (`DummySig`/`DummyKem`/`DummyAead`, mutual-auth disabled); ships in release | Medium-High | High | **R3** — configured P2P validator left at default transport | Static source first-hand (not `cfg(test)`) | **OPEN**, confirmed; reachability tied to R3 |
| **F005** | Tx-auth fail-open (empty auths; no threshold/weight/dedup) | High if tx ingress enabled; Low as-deployed | High | **Unreachable on deployed path** (no tx ingress; `apply_block` sim/tests only) | Static source (A1, first-hand) | **OPEN** (reachability-mitigated); unchanged |
| **F006** | Documentation overstates deployed posture | Low-Medium | High | Docs | Static | **OPEN**; A2 additionally records that **A1 itself** overstated (classical-crypto "anywhere"; "off by default" timeout verification) — corrected here |

No finding is closed solely because its impact is conditional. No new finding is opened: the EVM
classical-crypto surface (§7) and the `sha3_256_tagged` length-framing / `nodeid` tag-reuse
observations (A1 §9) remain **observations**, not findings, absent a reachable exploit scenario.

   `with_capacity` request size and confirm the abort-vs-reserve behavior under a constrained-memory
   cgroup; and a full `qbind-wire` sweep for any other `u32`/`usize` pre-size on untrusted counts.

# QBIND Audit — A1: Baseline, Trust Model, and Initial Deep Source Review

**Target:** `olivexo28/QBIND` · **Scope:** Public DevNet (incl. shared components used by DevNet)
**Audited commit (pinned):** `18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b`
**Branch:** `claude/exciting-keller-a05rwc` · **Root tree:** `5b6c543435ac017dd8372c93f48be397899db14a`
**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Pass:** A1 (first pass; NOT the whole audit) · **Names preserved as-is.**
**Non-mutating inspection only; no builds/tests/nodes/network were run. No repository file was modified.**

---

## 1. Executive assessment (with explicit limitations)

QBIND is a Rust post-quantum L1 (ML-DSA-44 / FIPS-204 signatures, ML-KEM-768 / FIPS-203 KEM,
KEMTLS + ChaCha20-Poly1305 transport, SHA3-256, HotStuff-style BFT, RocksDB state). The workspace
is large (321 `src/*.rs`, 491 test files, 117 examples) and extraordinarily documentation-heavy
(e.g. `docs/whitepaper/contradiction.md` ≈ 2.5 MB; 746 DevNet evidence files).

**Central structural finding (not a vulnerability per se, but the key to reading everything else):**
there are effectively **two consensus code paths**, and they must never be conflated:
- a feature-rich **simulation/harness + library engine** (`hotstuff_node_sim.rs`, `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs`, the M-series mitigations), and
- the **deployed binary consensus loop** (`crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs`, spawned by `main.rs`).

On the **deployed DevNet path at this commit**, the production node is wired **fail-closed to the
point of non-participation** in authenticated consensus: `proposal_vote_authority: None` and
`ConsensusVerificationPolicy::Required` (`main.rs:6148`, `main.rs:8682`) cause **all inbound
Proposal/Vote to be rejected** and **all outbound Proposal/Vote to be suppressed**; genesis
authority activation is DISABLED and the release binary refuses `--consensus-authority-from-genesis`.
This matches the project's own self-declared posture: **RS1 OPEN / launch-blocking, C4/C5 OPEN,
public DevNet NO-GO** (`docs/release/public-devnet/LAUNCH_GO_NO_GO.md`). The underlying PQ primitives
and the per-message verifiers that *would* run are individually **cryptographically sound**; they are
simply **not activated end-to-end** in the release build.

A1 nonetheless identifies concrete defects, most of which live **before or beside** that fail-closed
gate, or in components not covered by it:
- a **confirmed, remotely reachable pre-authentication allocation DoS** in the proposal wire decoder (QBIND-A1-F001);
- a **confirmed council-quorum-bypass logic defect** in the governance upgrade-envelope verifier (offline tool; QBIND-A1-F002);
- a **design risk**: the only production-live signing path (timeout emission) has **no durable-before-sign / cross-restart double-sign protection**, and the machinery that would provide it is unwired (QBIND-A1-F003);
- an **insecure-by-default transport posture** (always-accept `DummySig` + disabled mutual-auth are the defaults) (QBIND-A1-F004);
- a **confirmed fail-open transaction-auth** primitive, currently unreachable on the deployed path (QBIND-A1-F005);
- **documentation that overstates the deployed security posture** in places (QBIND-A1-F006).

**Limitations of this pass.** A1 reviewed the crypto core, the verification wiring, the two mandated
traces, genesis/trust-root establishment, and governance verification first-hand, with read-only
subagents mapping the full inbound and signing-safety paths. **Not reviewed in depth:** ledger
execution / gas / EVM (`revm`), monetary engine, slashing engine/ledger, snapshot/restore & epoch
atomicity on the deployed path, the ~40 near-duplicate `pqc_governance_durable_completion_*`
modules, metrics, and the large audit documents. Nothing here was executed; all reproduction
procedures are **proposed, NOT executed**. Documentation and prior "run" verdicts are treated as
**claims to evaluate**, not conclusions to adopt.

## 6. Threat model, trust assumptions, security invariants

**Adversary capabilities (DevNet):** network adversary able to TCP-connect and complete the
server-authenticated KEMTLS handshake (default `MutualAuthMode::Disabled` ⇒ effectively anonymous
inbound); can send arbitrary consensus frames; Byzantine validators up to the BFT bound; operator
mis-configuration; local attacker with access to a validator data directory (clone/rollback).

**Stated trust assumptions (from `task/RUN_422_TASK.txt` §3, evaluated not adopted):** operator
accepts a specific genesis/network identity via a trusted bootstrap; all validators share the accepted
authority commitment; OS + signer custody protect private keys; three authority roles are **separate**
(KEMTLS transport roots ≠ trust-bundle ratification roots ≠ consensus validator keys), and none may
substitute for another.

**Security invariants an auditor should hold the code to, and A1 status:**
- INV-A (message authenticity): inbound Proposal/Vote/Timeout/NewView and imported QCs are
  cryptographically authenticated over domain-separated, replay-bound preimages. — *Verifiers sound;
  **not activated** for Proposal/Vote on deployed path (fail-closed-by-unavailability); timeout
  verification **off by default** (`--require-timeout-verification false`).*
- INV-B (sender binding): authenticated transport peer ⇒ authorized consensus sender (F6). — *Gate
  exists (`PeerConsensusBindingGate`); not reachable to prove in prod because messages reject earlier.*
- INV-C (no double-sign incl. across restart/clone): — **Not provided on the live path** (F003).
- INV-D (suite integrity, no downgrade/fallback): — *Sound: no classical primitive, no "none" suite,
  strict `wire_suite == governance_suite` with no cross-suite retry.*
- INV-E (bounded resource use on untrusted input before auth): — **Violated** by F001.
- INV-F (trust-root replacement authenticated by prior root + quorum): — *Production fail-closed; the
  only realized (fixture) path authenticates by a recomputable commitment + self-asserted quorum (§7).*

**Security chain (source → … → governance), with evidence status:**
`source/build` (reproducible-build scripts, package-integrity manifests — *not reviewed A1*) →
`release artifact` (`.github/workflows/public-devnet-*` — *not reviewed A1*) →
`node startup` (genesis boot-verify fail-closed — *mapped*) →
`peer identity` (KEMTLS; **insecure default** F004) →
`consensus` (fail-closed-by-unavailability; verifiers sound) →
`durable state` (RocksDB synced writes exist; **signing-safety state not persisted on live path** F003) →
`restart` (no locked_qc/vote/timeout history restored on deployed path, F003) →
`validator/gov evolution` (epoch-0-only; governance replacement not cryptographically authenticated on the realized path, §7).

## 7. Post-quantum trust-path assessment

**Primitives — sound, no classical fallback.** `qbind-crypto` depends only on `fips204`
(ML-DSA-44), `fips203` (ML-KEM-768), `chacha20poly1305`, `pbkdf2`, `sha2`, `sha3`. No
ed25519/ecdsa/secp256/rsa/x25519 anywhere in source. `MlDsa44Backend::verify_internal`
(`ml_dsa44.rs:536-573`) checks pk length (1312), **signature length (2420)** — so empty/truncated
sigs are rejected before verify — and returns `Ok` **only** when `public_key.verify(...)` is true.
ML-DSA is used with an **empty context string**, so all domain separation is carried in the preimage.

**Domain separation / replay binding — present (two schemes).**
- Legacy v1 (`qbind-types/src/domain.rs`): `QBIND:<SCOPE>:<KIND>:v1`, SCOPE ∈ {DEV,TST,MAIN,UNK}.
  Vote body binds version/chain_id(u32)/epoch/height/round/step/block_id/validator_index/suite_id
  (`qbind-wire/src/consensus.rs:206-220`). Timeout binds chain_id/view/high_qc/validator_id.
- v2 (`qbind-wire/src/pv_signing_domain.rs`, tag `QBIND:PVDOMAIN:v2`): binds a **message-family byte**
  (Proposal=1/Vote=2), the full 64-bit chain id, 32-byte genesis identity, and 32-byte authority
  commitment; rejects all-zero genesis/commitment. **v2 is implemented but production-DISABLED.**
- No tag collision found among Proposal/Vote/Timeout/QC/governance.

**Weaker spots (evidence, not demonstrated exploits):** `sha3_256_tagged(tag, body)` concatenates
`tag || body` with **no length separator** (`qbind-hash/src/hash.rs:16-24`) — safe only because tags
are fixed constants and bodies begin with fixed-width fields; `derive_node_id_from_{cert,pubkey}` reuse
the **same** tag `QBIND:nodeid:v1` over different body shapes (`qbind-hash/src/net.rs:112,134`).
Timeout binds only the SCOPE *string* (DEV/UNK), not the full chain id / genesis / authority
commitment that v2 binds (asymmetry). Legacy `Vote/BlockProposal::signing_preimage()` **hard-code**
`QBIND_DEVNET_CHAIN_ID` (`consensus.rs:246,968`), consumed by the legacy `MultiSuiteCryptoVerifier`
(suite-0-slot) — a latent hazard **if** that legacy verifier is ever on a non-DevNet node path
(reachability unresolved — A2).

**Trust-root establishment (genesis) — sound, fail-closed.** Consensus authority is derived **only**
from `GenesisConfig.validators[].pqc_public_key` (strict-hex 1312-byte ML-DSA-44, duplicate-key/address
rejection, deterministic index→ValidatorId, authority commitment over chain-id+genesis-hash+per-validator
(index,suite,pk)); transport/bundle roots are never reinterpreted as consensus keys. Every validator
is assigned suite 100 (ML-DSA-44); the toy suite `0` is not the governance suite on this path.

**Trust-root replacement (governance) — the central PQ gap.** The **production** on-chain governance
verifier is an explicit fail-closed placeholder (`pqc_onchain_governance_verifier.rs:609-637,722-748` →
`ProductionVerifierUnavailable`; default kind `Disabled`; MainNet peer-apply always refused). The **only
acceptance path** is the DevNet/TestNet "fixture" verifier (`pqc_onchain_governance_proof.rs`), which
performs many binding checks but authenticates by (a) **self-asserted integer quorum/threshold fields**
(`is_met()` over proof-supplied numbers, `:782-793`) and (b) a **recomputable commitment**
(`proof_bytes == fixture_onchain_governance_proof_bytes(...)`, a plain public-field concatenation,
`:440-475,795-814`) — **no council public keys, no signatures**. So on the realized path the new trust
root is **not authenticated against the old root by any signature** (design risk; DevNet/TestNet-only,
MainNet fail-closed). See also QBIND-A1-F002 for the offline council verifier.

**Dependency classification:** all PQ-relevant deps are reachable-and-sound at the primitive layer;
end-to-end completeness is **not** realized because activation is DISABLED. Presence of PQ primitives
≠ end-to-end PQ security here.

---

## 8. Two detailed source traces

### Trace 1 — Untrusted inbound data → security-sensitive state change

Two inbound decode surfaces exist and do **not** share a decoder:
1. **KEMTLS handshake** (`qbind-net`): `framed_io.rs` caps payloads (16 MiB transport / 16 KiB
   handshake) **before** allocating; `cookie.rs` HMAC-SHA3-256 DoS cookie gates KEM decapsulation;
   `transport.rs`/`handshake_packet.rs` bounds-check length before copy. **Sound.**
2. **Post-handshake application plane** (deployed): `p2p_tcp.rs` read loop → `decode_frame`
   (`disc:u8 + len:u32`, bounds-checked) → `bincode` `P2pMessage` (opaque `Vec<u8>` payloads) →
   **hand-written `qbind-wire` decoders in the consensus loop**.

Ordering on the consensus plane (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6189-6258`): **decode → sender-binding
(F6) → signature/suite verification → (fail-closed) → engine mutation**. Decode precedes all crypto
(correct in principle for a cheap/safe decoder), and **state mutation is gated behind verification**
(production rejects before the engine). The exposure is therefore strictly the **pre-verification
decode allocation** — see QBIND-A1-F001.

Decoder bounds audit: `QuorumCertificate::decode` (`consensus.rs:351`, u16 `sig_count`, ≤~1.5 MB),
`Transaction::decode` (u16 counts), and `PeerList::decode` (explicit `> MAX_PEER_LIST_SIZE` check,
`net.rs:513`) are **bounded**. `BlockProposal::decode` is the outlier (F001). No narrowing `as`-casts,
recursion, or unchecked indexing on untrusted input in the decoders (slicing via checked `get_bytes`).

Admission controls (connection-rate limiter, per-peer message-rate limiter) are **opt-in / off by
default**, and a single message triggers F001 regardless.

### Trace 2 — Local consensus signing through restart (double-signing safety)

**Live signing path = timeout emission only.** In production, Proposal/Vote outbound signing is
**suppressed** (`Required` + `current_auth=None`/`journal=None`; `do_leader_tick`/`forward_actions_to_facade`
pass `None`, and `admit_outbound_action` rejects before the guarded journal path). The only
production-reachable `signer.sign_*` is **`sign_timeout_with_chain_id`** (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:7701`,
via `maybe_emit_view_timeout_with_auth:7542`), with a signer wired when a validator key is loaded
(`main.rs:6021/6045`).

**Durable-before-sign (INV-1):** implemented correctly **in the journal module**
(`signing_reservation_journal.rs`: reserve → one atomic **synced** write via `WriteOptions::set_sync(true)`
→ continuation → sign → record), with crash-recovery classifying a recovered reservation as
`PotentiallySigned` (refuse re-sign). **But the journal is not wired in production** — its own header
states "**Production startup never initializes a journal**" and "**no durable anti-rollback anchor**
… a whole-copy rollback or deletion of the local store cannot be detected" (`:22-28`). The
`safety_record_store` is likewise `SafetyBackendPolicy::Disabled`, MainNet-refused, and referenced only
by its `mod` declaration.

**The live timeout path has NO durable safety record and NO fsync-before-sign.** Its sole guard is the
**in-memory** `timeout_emitted_in_view` flag (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4959`), which **resets on
restart**: production restart seeds only `initialize_from_snapshot_baseline` (committed height/block_id,
`current_view = snapshot_height+1`, resets `voted_in_view`/`timeout_emitted_in_view`); the
`locked_qc`-restoring `initialize_from_restart` is **sim/test-only**. See QBIND-A1-F003.

**RUN 422 retained-QC admission (the HEAD change):** read-only projection matching a logical QC against
**already-verified** attached evidence; bounded scan `min(max_pending_blocks, 4096)` (`ScanLimitExceeded`
over-size), working-set ≤ 1 MiB; **admission (bounded scan + working-set) runs before reverification**,
so reverify CPU is not steerable by fresh attacker bytes; in production `snapshot=None` ⇒ any
`high_qc`-bearing Timeout/NewView is refused `AuthorityUnavailable`. The bound is sound and not a DoS.
