## 9. Findings with evidence

> Severity and Confidence are stated separately. Reproduction procedures are **PROPOSED, NOT EXECUTED.**
> "CONFIRMED" = defect demonstrated in source at the pinned commit; reachability is stated explicitly.

### QBIND-A1-F001 — Pre-authentication unbounded allocation DoS in `BlockProposal` wire decoder
- **Classification:** CONFIRMED source-level defect (verdict: CONFIRMED).
- **Severity:** High (remote, unauthenticated node crash / OOM-abort). **Confidence:** High.
- **Location:** `crates/qbind-wire/src/consensus.rs:747` (`let tx_count = get_u32(input)?;`) and
  `:766` (`let mut txs = Vec::with_capacity(tx_count as usize);`), function `impl WireDecode for
  BlockProposal`. Reached by the deployed loop at `crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs:6192`.
  Pinned: https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-wire/src/consensus.rs#L766
- **Violated invariant:** INV-E — untrusted length/count fields must be bounded against remaining input
  before allocation and before authentication.
- **Reachable trigger / mechanism:** `tx_count` is an attacker-controlled `u32` read directly off the
  wire with no bound relating it to remaining bytes. `Vec::<Vec<u8>>::with_capacity(tx_count)` requests
  up to `4_294_967_295 × 24 ≈ 103 GB` in one allocation **before** any tx byte is consumed (loop at
  `:767`) and **before** sender binding (`binary_consensus_loop.rs:6199`) and signature verification.
  A ~20-byte proposal frame carrying `tx_count = 0xFFFFFFFF` ⇒ allocation request ⇒ `handle_alloc_error`
  abort ⇒ node crash.
- **Attacker capability / scope:** any peer that completes the (DevNet-default `MutualAuthMode::Disabled`,
  server-auth-only) KEMTLS handshake to a node with P2P enabled and reachable. Affects availability of
  the targeted node.
- **Existing safeguards / counter-evidence considered:** transport frame cap is 16 MiB
  (`qbind-net/src/framed_io.rs`), but that bounds byte length, **not** the embedded `tx_count`; the
  1 MiB `MAX_NET_MESSAGE_BYTES` cap applies only to `NetMessage::decode_from_slice`, which the deployed
  consensus plane does not use; rate-limiters are off by default and one message suffices; the
  fail-closed verification gate sits **after** this allocation. Sibling decoders (QC u16, Transaction
  u16, PeerList explicit cap) are correctly bounded — the defect is specific to `tx_count` (u32).
- **Directly inspected vs inferred:** code read first-hand (both lines + handler ordering). Crash
  outcome inferred from Rust allocation semantics (not executed).
- **Proposed reproduction (NOT executed):** on a disposable DevNet node with P2P enabled, complete a
  KEMTLS handshake and send a `ConsensusNetMsg::Proposal` whose encoded `BlockProposal` sets
  `tx_count = 0xFFFFFFFF` with no tx bodies; observe abort/RSS spike before any verification counter
  increments.
- **Remediation direction (prose):** bound `tx_count` against remaining input (e.g. reject if it
  exceeds a protocol max or the bytes-left / min-encoded-tx-size ratio) before `with_capacity`, mirroring
  the existing `PeerList`/u16 patterns; prefer capacity-free incremental push or a sanity cap.
- **Verification required before closure:** demonstrate rejection of oversized `tx_count` before
  allocation on the deployed `binary_consensus_loop` path, with a bounded-rejection counter and no RSS
  spike; audit all other `with_capacity`/pre-sizing on untrusted counts across `qbind-wire`.

### QBIND-A1-F002 — Governance upgrade-envelope council quorum bypass via duplicated approval
- **Classification:** CONFIRMED source-level defect (verdict: CONFIRMED).
- **Severity:** High within the tool's purpose / Medium overall (no live on-chain consensus
  reachability). **Confidence:** High.
- **Location:** `crates/qbind-gov/src/verify.rs:95-124` (`verify_envelope` loop, no `member_id` dedup;
  `valid_count += 1` per valid approval; `is_valid()` = `valid_count >= threshold`, `:56-58`) and
  `crates/qbind-gov/src/hash.rs:38-63` (`envelope_digest` **excludes** `council_approvals`).
  Pinned: https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND/blob/18d71a549d868ed33d352e9fc70a9d060f75e03b/crates/qbind-gov/src/verify.rs#L110
- **Violated invariant:** INV-F (M-of-N council quorum must count **distinct** authorized signers).
- **Reachable trigger / mechanism:** because the signed digest excludes the approvals list, one council
  member's single valid approval can be **appended `threshold` times**; each copy independently passes
  `verify_single_signature` and increments `valid_count`, so `is_valid()` returns true with a single
  signer. `CouncilKeySet::validate` dedups the keyset but the **approval list is never deduped at verify
  time**. (`verify_envelope` also does not check `network_environment`.)
- **Attacker capability / scope:** anyone holding **one** valid council signature (or one malicious
  council member) can forge apparent M-of-N approval of an upgrade envelope evaluated by this tool.
- **Reachability:** `qbind-gov` is **not** a dependency of `qbind-node` (confirmed in its manifest); it
  is used by the standalone `qbind-envelope` CLI. Impact is **operational** (an operator relying on this
  tool to decide whether an upgrade meets council threshold is misled), not a live consensus bypass.
- **Safeguards / counter-evidence:** per-signature validity (keyset membership + pk match + signature
  verify) is enforced; only distinctness is missing.
- **Inspected vs inferred:** both functions read first-hand; bypass is a direct code reading.
- **Proposed reproduction (NOT executed):** build an envelope, attach one member's valid approval
  `threshold` times, run `qbind-envelope` verify, observe `is_valid()==true` / exit success.
- **Remediation direction (prose):** deduplicate by `member_id` (and reject duplicate member entries)
  before counting; optionally bind the approval set into the digest; validate `network_environment`.
- **Verification before closure:** add distinctness enforcement and a negative test proving duplicated
  approvals do not reach threshold; re-audit any node use of `qbind-gov` (none found at HEAD).

### QBIND-A1-F003 — Live timeout-signing path lacks durable / cross-restart double-sign protection
- **Classification:** Design risk + evidence gap (verdict: CONFIRMED code facts; exploitability
  CONDITIONAL). **Severity:** Medium now (latent; not presently exploitable), High if authority is
  later activated without the journal. **Confidence:** High (code facts).
- **Location:** live signing `crates/qbind-node/src/binary_consensus_loop.rs:7638-7720` (sign at `:7701`);
  in-memory guard `timeout_emitted_in_view` (`crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:4959`,
  reset `:2675`); restart seeding `binary_consensus_loop.rs:2838` →
  `basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:2654-2677` (no `locked_qc`/vote/timeout history); unwired durable machinery
  `signing_reservation_journal.rs:22-28` and `safety_record_store/mod.rs:1-12`.
- **Violated invariant:** INV-C (no conflicting signatures across restart/clone).
- **Mechanism:** the only production signing path (timeout) writes **nothing durable** before releasing
  the signature; its anti-double-sign guard is purely in-memory and resets on restart; no highest-voted/
  highest-timeout view is persisted or restored on the deployed path. The INV-1 journal and
  `safety_record_store` that would enforce durability are not initialized in production; even when wired,
  the journal provides **no anti-rollback/anti-clone** protection (per its own contract).
- **Why not a live equivocation today:** production forces `high_qc=None` on emitted timeouts
  (`snapshot=None` ⇒ `admit_f7_retained_high_qc` refuses `high_qc`-bearing timeouts), so two timeouts
  for the same view are **content-identical re-signs**, not conflicting signatures. The risk becomes a
  real equivocation vector **iff** the Proposal/Vote or timeout authority snapshot is later activated
  (enabling varying signed content) **without** also wiring the durable journal.
- **Attacker/scope:** a restarted or **cloned** validator (same key, two data dirs) could, once signing
  of content-varying messages is enabled, produce conflicting signatures the local state cannot prevent
  — a slashable equivocation / safety risk.
- **Safeguards / counter-evidence considered:** RocksDB synced-write durability (`set_sync(true)`) is
  real but used by the *journal*, not the live timeout path; the project's own `task/RUN_422_TASK.txt`
  §10/§17 explicitly says not to claim cross-clone/restart double-sign protection — consistent with this
  finding. Currently mitigated by the `high_qc=None` constraint above.
- **Inspected vs inferred:** signing path, restart seeding, journal/store contracts read first-hand;
  the "activation-without-journal" exploit path is a stated hypothesis, not demonstrated.
- **Proposed reproduction (NOT executed):** in a harness that activates a timeout snapshot (enabling
  `high_qc`-bearing timeouts) without a journal, emit a timeout at view V, kill+restart (or clone the
  data dir), re-enter view V, emit a differing timeout; show two conflicting signatures for V.
- **Remediation direction (prose):** persist highest-signed (view, message-family, content-binding)
  durably before releasing any signature on the live path (reuse the INV-1 journal), and gate activation
  of any content-varying signing on a wired durable journal; document the clone/rollback limitation.
- **Verification before closure:** prove, on the deployed path, that a restart/clone cannot produce a
  second differing signature at an already-signed view.

### QBIND-A1-F004 — Insecure-by-default transport authentication (`DummySig` always-accept + mutual-auth disabled)
- **Classification:** Design risk / insecure default (verdict: CONFIRMED defaults; exploitability
  config-dependent). **Severity:** Medium (experimental DevNet; secure config is documented and
  operator-selectable). **Confidence:** High (code), reachability config-dependent.
- **Location:** `crates/qbind-node/src/p2p_node_builder.rs:278-305` (`DummySig::verify` → `Ok(())`),
  `:369-380` (`make_test_crypto_provider` wires `DummySig`+`DummyKem`+`DummyAead`), `:1307-1309`
  (provider selection by mode); default mode `PqcRootMode::TestGradeDummySig`
  (`pqc_root_config.rs:63-72, 451`); default `MutualAuthMode::Disabled` (`qbind-net/src/handshake.rs:33`;
  CLI `p2p_mutual_auth`/`p2p_pqc_root_mode` default `None`, `cli.rs:220-231,314`).
- **Violated invariant:** INV-D/INV-B at the transport layer (peer/transport authenticity).
- **Mechanism:** with defaults, transport certificate "verification" accepts **any** signature
  (`DummySig`), there is **no client authentication** (`Disabled`), and the `DummyAead` provides no real
  confidentiality/integrity (single-byte XOR + xor-fold "tag"). A node that enables P2P without the M4
  security flags (`--p2p-mutual-auth required --p2p-pqc-root-mode pqc-static-root --p2p-trusted-root …`)
  runs with no meaningful transport peer authentication, widening exposure (e.g. who can reach F001).
- **Counter-evidence considered:** the documented DevNet seed/validator posture (`LAUNCH_GO_NO_GO.md`
  §4 M4 checklist, operator QUICKSTART) **mandates** `pqc-static-root` + mutual-auth `required`, under
  which real ML-DSA-44 (suite 100) verification and the production-honest provider
  (`make_pqc_static_root_crypto_provider`) are used. So a correctly-configured node is not affected; the
  risk is an **insecure default** for a misconfigured/omitted-flag node. Public DevNet is explicitly
  experimental/NO-GO.
- **Inspected vs inferred:** DummySig/provider/defaults read first-hand; operator-config dependence noted.
- **Proposed reproduction (NOT executed):** start a node with `--enable-p2p true` and a public listen
  address but without the static-root/mutual-auth flags; connect with an arbitrary/forged
  `NetworkDelegationCert`; observe handshake acceptance.
- **Remediation direction (prose):** make the secure mode the default (or refuse to start a P2P-enabled,
  externally-bound node in `TestGradeDummySig`/`Disabled`), and ensure `DummySig`/`DummyKem`/`DummyAead`
  are compiled out of release/non-test builds.
- **Verification before closure:** prove a release node bound to a non-loopback address cannot run with
  always-accept transport auth.

### QBIND-A1-F005 — Transaction authentication fail-open (empty auths; no threshold/weight/dedup)
- **Classification:** CONFIRMED source-level defect; currently **unreachable** on the deployed DevNet
  path (verdict: CONFIRMED code; reachability-mitigated). **Severity:** High if tx ingress is enabled;
  Low-as-deployed (no ingress). **Confidence:** High.
- **Location:** `crates/qbind-ledger/src/auth.rs:31-33` (`if tx.auths.is_empty() { return Ok(()) }`) and
  `verify_single_auth` (`:44-103` — verifies each present auth against "at least one key"; **no**
  threshold/weight enforcement, **no** signer/key dedup). Called via `ExecutionContext`
  (`qbind-ledger/src/context.rs:50`) → `apply_block` (`qbind-node/src/lib.rs:2595`).
- **Violated invariant:** transaction authorization must require ≥1 valid auth meeting keyset
  threshold/weight with distinct signers (with explicit genesis exemption).
- **Reachability:** `apply_block` is invoked only by `hotstuff_node_sim.rs:3156` and `execution_adapter`
  tests — **no transaction ingress on the deployed binary** (empty proposals). So this is currently a
  **reachability mitigation, not cryptographic closure** (matches the project's F1/F2).
- **Inspected vs inferred:** `auth.rs` read first-hand; reachability confirmed by caller grep.
- **Proposed reproduction (NOT executed):** once tx ingress is wired, submit a transaction with empty
  `auths` (or sub-threshold/duplicated signers) and observe acceptance.
- **Remediation direction (prose):** require ≥1 auth and enforce keyset threshold/weight with signer
  dedup (explicit genesis exemption) **before** enabling any transaction ingress.
- **Verification before closure:** negative tests for empty/sub-threshold/duplicate-signer auths on the
  path that will actually ingest transactions.

### QBIND-A1-F006 — Documentation overstates deployed security posture in places (stale prose)
- **Classification:** Evidence gap / documentation-accuracy (verdict: CONFIRMED). **Severity:** Low-Medium
  (misleading; not a runtime vuln). **Confidence:** High.
- **Location / examples:** `QBIND_FOUNDATIONAL_RUNTIME_SECURITY_RECONCILIATION.md` §2.2 present-tense
  "proposals/votes accepted without signature … VERIFIED-FAIL-OPEN" is **stale** vs HEAD (Run 420+ made
  the deployed Proposal/Vote path fail-closed under `Required`); `QBIND_M_SERIES_COVERAGE.md`
  (2026-02-16) asserts "all pre-testnet critical issues mitigated … residual risk Low", which the later
  RS1 record (OPEN/launch-blocking) contradicts, and which largely describes **harness/engine**
  mitigations rather than the deployed `binary_consensus_loop`.
- **Impact:** an auditor or operator reading the whitepaper/M-series triad in isolation would overestimate
  deployed guarantees. The project *does* maintain a reconciliation + contradiction ledger acknowledging
  much of this; the gap is residual stale/optimistic prose.
- **Remediation direction (prose):** reconcile present-tense "mitigated/fail-open" prose with HEAD,
  consistently distinguishing harness/engine from deployed-binary behavior.
- **Verification before closure:** a doc-vs-code pass confirming each present-tense security claim matches
  the deployed path at the audited commit.

**Additional observations (sub-finding; lower confidence / defense-in-depth, not full findings):**
- `sha3_256_tagged` lacks a length separator between tag and body (`qbind-hash/src/hash.rs:16-24`); same
  `QBIND:nodeid:v1` tag over two derivation shapes (`qbind-hash/src/net.rs:112,134`). No demonstrated
  collision; recommend explicit length framing / per-derivation domain byte.
- Legacy `CryptoConsensusVerifier`/`MultiSuiteCryptoVerifier` hard-wire the suite-`0` slot and the
  DevNet-hardcoded chain-id legacy preimage (`crypto_verifier.rs:670-672,747-782`;
  `consensus.rs:246,968`); node reachability unresolved — **A2**.
- DevNet "fixture" governance trust-root replacement authenticated by recomputable commitment +
  self-asserted quorum (`pqc_onchain_governance_proof.rs:440-475,782-814`); production fail-closed. A2.

## 11. Prioritized A2 work (exact areas + unresolved questions)

1. **F001 exhaustive pass:** confirm the `BlockProposal` `tx_count` DoS end-to-end and enumerate every
   pre-verification `with_capacity`/pre-size on untrusted counts across `qbind-wire` (and the
   `NetMessage`→`BlockProposal` path if ever wired). Files: `qbind-wire/src/{consensus,net,tx}.rs`.
2. **F003 activation-without-journal:** determine whether any operator-opt-in or test-utils path can
   activate a Proposal/Vote or timeout authority snapshot (enabling content-varying signatures) **without**
   a wired durable journal, and assess clone/rollback equivocation. Files: `binary_consensus_loop.rs`
   (signer/journal/snapshot wiring), `main.rs` signer construction, `signing_reservation_journal.rs`,
   `safety_record_store/*`.
3. **Legacy verifier reachability:** resolve whether `CryptoConsensusVerifier`/`MultiSuiteCryptoVerifier`
   (suite-0 slot + DevNet-hardcoded chain-id preimage) is reachable on any node path. Files:
   `qbind-consensus/src/crypto_verifier.rs`, `qbind-wire/src/consensus.rs:246,968`.
4. **Governance trust-root replacement:** evaluate the DevNet fixture verifier's reachability (peer-driven
   trust apply / `pqc_live_trust*`) and the quorum-by-integer + recomputable-commitment design (C4/C5).
   Files: `pqc_onchain_governance_proof.rs`, `pqc_live_trust*.rs`, `pqc_trust_bundle.rs`.
5. **Insecure-default hardening (F004):** confirm release builds can run externally-bound in
   `TestGradeDummySig`/`Disabled`, and whether DummySig/DummyKem/DummyAead are compiled into release.
6. **KEMTLS deep-dive:** transcript binding, v1/v2 downgrade, cookie/IP binding, KEM
   encap/decap handling, `DummyAead` vs real ChaCha20-Poly1305 selection. Files: `qbind-net/src/*`.
7. **Untouched subsystems:** ledger execution/gas/monetary overflow & determinism, slashing engine/ledger
   restart safety (M9/M11/M13/M19), snapshot/restore & epoch atomicity (M16) on the deployed path.
8. **Supply chain:** `.github/workflows/public-devnet-*`, reproducible-build & package-integrity scripts,
   `Cargo.lock` dependency review.

**Open questions:** Does production ever wire a timeout signer when no genesis authority is active (i.e.
is the live timeout path exercised at all on a default DevNet node)? Is there any operator flag that
activates Proposal/Vote authority without the journal? Does any deployed path reach the legacy
suite-0 verifier?
